The staff here is pretty inconsistent. Very few vets remain from visit to visit, turnover is frequent. Sometimes you get a good vet, more times you get an average/bad one.

It sounds bad, but we still go here. Mostly because they try to take good care of us after all of this has happened. The excessive charging on EVERYTHING is annoying and if we had more than 3 cats then we probably couldn't afford it. I really would look into other places first.

I am so disappointed with this hospital. This was the second time I came here, and each time was a HUGE disappointment. I am never returning. EVER. The vet's name is Melissa Schupp. 

 First, I arrived around 2:35 on a Sunday afternoon. I called two hours ahead of time to schedule an appointment because I knew Sundays would be busy; this is because many other animal hospitals are not open on Sundays. My dog was suffering from unknown allergic reactions with skin rashes left and right. I had just adopted him, and his skin had recently become infected and rotten-smelling.
 I called ahead of time, gave my details , a $77 quote and they reserved a room for me. When I arrived  the room was already reserved and I was led straight in. I initially thought I was going to have a great experience because of the quick room preparation but BOY was I wrong. When I was led into the room that was "prepared," there was water all over the floor and the front desk lady hastily used paper towels to clean it up. I waited the standard 30 minutes in the smelly room until the nurse came into to check details, run temperature and give my dog a general physical. Then she left for AN HOUR. By this time it  was already 3:35, and my dog was whining from pain and discomfort in a closed off room. When the nurse returned and began to write down symptoms, my dog actually started peeing on floor. I didn't know what to do because I had no cleaning materials with me, so the nurse stepped into action and dropped a few paper towels on the ground. She didn't manage to soak up all the urine, so when she moved around, my dog was pushed into it and it ended all over my clothes when she asked for my to carry my dog onto the checkup table.

To make things worse, she left again for another hour, and checked in after the 40 minute mark to tell me the veterinarian would be with me after 1 minute. Ten more minutes passed and no one came. My dog was whimpering more and more at this point. Finally at 4:30, the vet comes in, smiling and kind, and asking me for doggie symptoms. I ask her about fleas, but I swear, this place was so profit driven that the VET DID NOT EVEN CHECK MY DOG FOR FLEAS BEFORE GIVING ME A PRESCRIPTION ON MY FLEA MEDICATION. The mere mention of "I think my dog might have fleas but I don't know how to check for them" initiated a conditioned response "I'll prescribe flea medication" WITHOUT LOOKING AT THE DOG. I asked kindly to hint to her that my dog might not have fleas because the itchiness could be a symptom of allergies. She then shows me how to check for fleas, but doesn't find any as she shows me. She continued to write down a prescription for fleas on my bill without my knowing. Is this a professional business? How can they cheat people like this!
As I continued to ask questions to make sure what my dog had, the nurse seemed to reply with more things to run up my medical bill. She gave my dog a unnecessary skin scrape for mites TWICE even though SHE SAID that it didn't seem like my dog had mites, she performed and charged me for the scrape all the same. Because I had never needed to have these operations performed, I did not know that it was an extra $30 to have skin scraped. She went to look at the scrapes under the microscope, and returned another hour later. By this time, it was 5:30 and my patience was running low. For three hours, I sat in a stuffy room, covered in urine and staring at my miserable dog scratching his skin to bloody scabby bits as the doctors and nurses neglected the both of us. Honestly, I was so frustrated, I didn't even know what to do.  I had never experienced such a horrible medical visit. 

Around 5:35 when she returned, she apologized for being gone for an hour, and she said she had to look over a pet with a "real emergency." I'm not here to disqualify her statement, because I understand that this is a real animal hospital and that other people may have pets who are dying. But I also understand that this is a FOR-PROFIT animal hospital, and if they don't even have enough vets to go around that I have to wait three hours for something that takes less than 50 minutes, I truly will never EVER recommend this place or ever set foot near this place again.
 After she came back, she confirmed my dog had no mites, and gave me a pet "cone of shame" that I had asked for earlier. She told me it was $15 cone, and gave me flea medication and antibiotics for the infection. She hardly looked at my pet. The only part of the visit that was clear to my mind was that she kept saying "ow" when my dog nibbled at her fingers.
I excitedly hurried out and paid my bill. EXCEPT IT WAS $207. I let the vet CUT MY DOG for $32, the flimsy cone was $30 in addition to the $29 un-needed flea meds. I cried.
I think my only mistake was coming to this hospital. Be wary of coming here as the more questions you ask to get a better idea of your dog's condition, the more services and products they try to shove down your throat to earn revenue.

Our dog was attacked by another dog and our usual vet was closed.  Thank God for places like this.  The staff was nice and the vet was extremely attentive to our dog and to us.  The vet and the staff took the time to update us on her status and walk us through what we needed to do for her recovery.  I love my vet, but I definitely recommend this place for emergencies or after hour visits.

I was a bit skeptical about Animal Medical Hospital at first because of its size.  It's so big that when you walk in, there are anywhere from 3-5 people at the service counter waiting to assist.  And with 13 veterinarians on staff, I was afraid that it was the Walmart of veterinary clinics.  

Last fall, however, we had to take one of our senior cats to Animal Medical Hospital for emergency treatment of his failing kidneys.  He stayed overnight in the hospital, and we could easily make daily visits.  Dr. Tammy Evans was fantastic.  She was compassionate, honest, and very informative.  We eventually brought our cat home and he survived another couple of months before inevitably passing away.  Dr. Evans called to check up on him several times.  I was so impressed with her "bedside manner."  

Soon after that, it was time to take my other senior cat in for his next exam and shots.  I continued to take him to his regular vet clinic that he had been going to for a few years just because of the history there.   Unfortunately, that clinic had a massive turnover of staff (never a good sign), including my favorite vet, and they "diagnosed" that something was wrong with my kitty that wasn't and started to "treat" him.  That's when I decided to take him to Animal Medical Hospital for a second opinion.  Dr. Evans wasn't available, so I took the first appointment with the first veterinarian that I could.  After examining my cat and getting back the blood test results, Dr. Angela Abendroth immediately took him off the meds the other clinic prescribed and did a full exam.  I was so impressed with how friendly she was, the thoroughness of her examination, and the detailed information/diagnosis she gave me that when it was time to return for my cat's next senior wellness exam (every 6 months), I specifically picked a time when the (apparently very busy) Dr. Abendroth was available.  

We recently visited Dr. Abendroth again for that appointment and I was so pleased to see her give such good care again to my cat and do such a thorough examination.  She doesn't rush through things; she takes her time with patients and their "parents."  She really loves animals, and it shows.  Following the exam, I received a "report card" in the mail with my cat's blood test results (all normal -- yea!).  Additionally, Dr. Abendroth personally called me and reiterated that everything was A-OK.   We'll go back in another six months for an appointment, and it will definitely be with Dr. Abendroth again.

Don't be fooled by Animal Medical Hospital's size.  Going to a smaller clinic doesn't mean that you'll get more personalized service.  It's all about the quality of the staff, and I've gotten a lot of quality from Animal Medical Hospital.

Let me start by saying WOW! If I could give more than 5 stars, I would! This place is awesome. I adopted my dog from the Humane Society and was given a $200 credit.
We went for an initial checkup back in March when I got her and that went extremely smooth. We made the appointment and got in on time, maybe even early! 
The facility is super clean and welcoming. Everyone on the staff at this place, from the front desk people to the vet and everyone in-between is amazing. They are all so warm and welcoming, always with a smile on their face. You can really tell the employees here love animals what they do and it shows. 
Being this is my first dog, I feel like I have had a lot of silly questions and no one has ever seemed too bothered to answer and help me. From calling at 1130pm with minor concerns to setting up appointments, it is an absolute pleasure to be a patient here. It is wonderful to have confidence in knowing I don't have to look any further for a vet in Charlotte, my dog will be continuing to get great care from this group of amazing people at AMH.

Love this place! The staff is very courteous and attentive. Facility is always clean and the animals are cared for so well.  They email notifications and reminders which is really helpful. They also have great weekend hours! Thankful for the awesome work these guys do!

The only reason I've visited this hospital is because there was a $150 credit to, my cat, Elaine's account there after I adopted her.

MAH is a very nice facility. However, your bill will be a tall one with every visit. 

My cat swallowed a foreign object and the vet claimed it would not pass on its own - that it would need to be surgically removed. I left her over night - I work night shift and had to drop her off on the way. They placed an IV and gave fluids. Animals can receive fluids subcutaneously (this is cheaper) but they charged me for the actual IV placement, monitoring, etc. When I arrived in the morning they repeated X-rays and stated that the object had not moved. It would cost $3000 for surgery. 

I checked her out and took her to my home town - this doctor said she could do it for less than $1000 the next day. Elaine pooped out the object the next morning - after reviewing the X-rays the object had actually made progress in the bowel despite what the MAH vets claimed.

The surgery would not be necessary and a lot of the things they did (iv placement, etc) just racked up a charge. 

Needless to say I won't visit again.

Last night I had the pleasure of taking an introductory group class here under the tutelage of studio owner Caroline. 

The studio, which can be a tad tricky to find (and really the only drawback), is located on the second floor of the building towards the right hand side. My suggestion is to just look for the unit number which is on the same door as their logo. 

Once our group arrived we were asked to fill in information forms and then pay for our class which would start soon. 

Once completed we were swiftly brought out into the studio and we began. Caroline is a consummate professional and employs staff of the same caliber. Her and her staff seem to have a unique way of explaining the counts and steps in a way that's easy to understand for even the most 2 left footed individual (like me). Breaking each dance down into manageable chunks, we learned the basics of traditional Cuban Salsa and a Merengue. 

The Salsa is a slightly more difficult dance once you get into it but I really enjoyed the Merengue especially as we were taught different spins and locks. Not gonna lie, as the rust fell off my hips I felt super sexy - not unlike a much younger Saturday Night Fever John Travolta!

Before we knew it our 45-minute class was over and we all looked around wanting more! That's a good thing - always leave-em wanting more!

Can't wait to shake-ma-groove-thang at Blueheel again soon.

I took a trial lesson here and they were very patient.  As a result of their patience, I decided to take a few paid lessons.  While the studio is quite small, there is enough parking (at least during the evening and on Saturdays), 

I've taken a few private lessons with them and the instruction style is a good balance between making sure you have the proper steps and making you do them right and also patience (since people are bound to make mistakes).  She makes you feel comfortable as well and you don't feel the least bit intimidated even though there are all levels of dancers around you.

Overall, so far a pretty good experience.

After the Yelp event here with instructor Caroline, I decided to be serious about learning Tango. We didn't do Tango at all during our Yelp event, but it's a dance I've been looking into (I even know the studios in downtown Toronto that are teaching it!)

Blueheel in Mississauga is just a short drive away.... so I signed up! And I specifically asked for Kalan. 

During the Yelp event (which was fantastic, you can read more in Kris's review), we met Kalan as he was the male partner for Caroline. He taught the men, Caroline taught the ladies. He has a gentle demeanour, very patient, and he dances beautifully. I love his posture!

With group classes, you have to follow their monthly class schedule. This is published based on demand, and Tango isn't always there.

With private, you can schedule whenever is convenient for you. And that's what we did! We bought a package of 3? classes, which includes a free Group and a free "Dance with everybody with today's theme" class (Friday evenings).

The staff are friendly and approachable. The studio is quite small. Private classes are often held DURING the group classes, so yes we were at the corner avoiding the people as we moved across the dance floor. And yes, we had people watching us during our private class. It's really just one room (reception area, coat check, dance floor)

But no, we didn't mind at all. Kalan was amazing. He taught depending on how comfortable we are and how fast we'd like to go. He watched and he knew what we were struggling with, etc. He read our minds!

I stopped going due to family problems and we have some lessons left. He hasn't bothered us about coming back after I explained to him about my family, and this was a year ago! A YEAR!! They have not bothered me about coming back, they know it's my schedule, my time, but they didn't forget me! Thanks Blueheel!!! 

I need to reschedule and finish our lessons!

I purchased a great deal from them while they were promoting at Lifetime Athletic's latin night event. For only $20 I am able to attend 10 drop in classes. So far I've only been to three and I can't wait to attend the next one. I also won $500 worth of dance classes which is awesome!

I've had a chance to learn from several instructors who are all friendly and patient. My sister and I don't have any dance experience so they started us off with some basic steps. They ensure we have the steps down correctly before moving onto the next move.

The studio has just one dance floor so there can be multiple classes running at the same time. They have to share the music so sometimes you'll be learning salsa but tango music will be playing because of the other private lesson.

Blueheel is great and I will most likely purchase some more sessions when I finish all of mine up.
Mindy is a superior photographer with great customer-service skills.  I am glad I came across her business.
We had a great experience with Doug as our photographer. The photos look great and now we can always look back and be reminded of the wonderful time we had in Vegas getting married.

I am grateful for all the helpful reviews that led us to Mindy Bean. We had Doug as our photographer and he seemed to be everywhere at once, getting from one shot to the next faster than what seemed humanly possible. He was flexible, yet made sure that he got the shots he knew we would want, which was great since I'm clueless. Doug's professionalism stood not only to the bride and groom, but to guests and family members. Choosing Mindy Bean photography was a great decision!

Mindy and Doug are the consummate professional photographers!  They are locals who know every part of the city and surrounding areas and you can get the best photo shoots and therefore the best pictures.  

They have done a few family photo sessions for us and anyone with kids knows they are tough but somehow we always get amazing photos!

They are quick to get everything to us in a disc and then are kind enough to give us the rights so we can do with the pictures as we please.  Surprisingly, this makes them much cheaper than those specialty photo places because you print only what you choose!!!

I cannot say enough about them but give them a try; you WILL NOT be disappointed!

We are customers for life!

My husband and I found Mindy and Doug at the bridal show. I felt a connection with Mindy immediately and we liked what the packages had to offer. The engagement shoot was so much fun and Mindy shot some beautiful photos. We used Doug and Mindy for the ceremony and reception they worked so well together. Honestly they made my husband and I fell comfortable and we had a blast working with them. I couldn't tell you witch picture is my favorite because I love them all. I recommend them to all my friends and family getting married.

Doug Bean was our wedding photographer and we cannot praise him enough. Leading up to the day he was always available by text or email, and as he had never been to our unique venue before, he met us there a few weeks before the wedding for us to scope out shooting locations. On the big day, he helped my inexperienced groom tie his tie and arrange his tie clip and cuff links. After that Doug set up our First Look and it's a moment we will never forget. Throughout our entire day he was kind, courteous, patient, and made sure we only focused on each other and our love. He took shots we never would have thought of and for the specific shots we did ask for he made them even better than what we had in our heads. He was very careful about taking wonderful detail shots of my bouquet, our shoes, my groom's Green Lantern tie clip and cuff links, etc. He was creative and resourceful and together we took advantage of every nook and cranny of our beautiful 1930s Mission style Historic Fifth Street School venue. My husband and I really felt like Doug was part of our team! During the ceremony and reception he was both unobtrusive and everywhere at once! I know he got all the classic shots but I was never aware of him. All my guests and our family couldn't stop gushing about him. He was so fun during the reception too! There were a few times when he took our wedding rings away from us and I can't wait to see the photos to find out what creative things he did with them. I also saw him with our custom cake topper that was painted to look like us! He's a sneaky one! We haven't seen the photos yet but I have absolutely no doubt they will be gorgeous. We would hire Doug again in a second for any special occasion. He was the one vendor for our wedding that we appreciated the most and can't stop talking about. THANK YOU DOUG!!!

For the reviewer here who gave Doug one star, I think you must have just caught him at a busy moment because that is so far away from my experience with Doug that it's hard to believe we could be talking about the same person.
Doug was wonderful to work with! He made our wedding so much fun and memorable with his awesome photos. When is Las Vegas I highly recommend Mindy Bean Photography!!!

Finding Mindy Bean Photography was easily the best google search we ever made. My wife and I are so incredibly fortunate that we were able to have Mindy and Doug photograph our engagement session, as well as our wedding day. Not only are they the epitome of professionalism, but they are fun, energetic, and display a true passion for their craft. In my opinion, there is no reason to shop around when searching for a qualified wedding photographer in Las Vegas. If Mindy is available book her immediately before someone else is lucky enough to secure a spot in her already busy schedule. She will accommodate your every need, and you will be blown away by the results.

After seeing some of these bizarre one-star reviews, I need to chime in. I don't know where those people are getting "rude" from. Doug was super cool, down to earth, and really responsive, and so was Mindy. If you aren't down to earth (which I'm betting money these people aren't), then go find some uptight, snooty photographer for a whole lot more money who'll suck up to you. However, if you want a competent photographer who will make you feel relaxed and jive with what you're wanting, then go with Mindy or Doug. And believe me, it wasn't that I wasn't picky and just let him do whatever; I had a long list of ideas and things I didn't want, and Doug was totally understanding and made sure to get all the shots I wanted.

My wedding was on a tight budget, but I still wanted great photographs. Doug was, by far, the best option that I could find in town. C-Shack, a new venture by the owners of Port of Siam (originally in this location, now moved closer into town) is a fresh look at a seafood restaurant in Newhaven. Sure, it utilises stereotypes (oh I do like to be beside the seaside white and blue decor) and it's name alone is a natty little play on words (sadly, no crab though when we visited) in more than one way, but we enjoyed our visit there last night, and enjoyed it more in all honesty than our visit to it's predecessor, which hadn't delivered on a tempting promise. 

C-Shack promises to serve up whatever is brought into dock, along with some more staple offerings. We tried out the Isle of Mull crab spring rolls (the home made sweet chilli dip was the outright winner on this plate) and Vietnamese salmon with orange (flavours drowned out by some dried onion, but the salmon itself was fresh and tender and was still tasty). We followed this up with the Surf & Turf burger (burger with a side of prawns and a portion of skinny fries) and the special - bream with tomatoes and samphire. The burger was a winner - a solid pice of beef, although skinny fries are forgettable at best. The bream, for me, was a little on the disappointing side - overloaded with butter (nay, drowned) and the tomatoes (cherry) roasted and placed on top - for me, the flavours were too separate and as a dish didn't gel together super well - but the fish itself was beautifully cooked, and I'll have samphire any day of the week. 

Overall, C-Shack is a a newbie, some of it's dishes could do with a little improvement but it has good ownership running it and overall, it's a welcome addition to the neighbourhood and I'm sure we will be back again.

Vedett and San Miguel on tap and other beers by bottle. Nice wine selection. Sat at a table with a view of a lighthouse. Small and cozy place. We saw the fish monger deliver the seafood, beer distributor the kegs and another delivery of maybe homemade ice cream or something else.  Needless to say everything is fresh and prepared by the chef!!!

Best meal in months.  Great from start to finish.  Yummy starters (we tried the scallops and goat cheese), delicious and well  proportioned mains (lobster and sea bass) and the desserts were sweet and tasty without being too rich (raspberry trifle and brownie with peanut butter ice cream).  

The locations in lovely directly across from the harbor and the interior is quaint and comfortable.  Small, so recommend advance booking.

After relocating to PV I had a hard time finding a stylist. I thought Groupon is a good gateway for trying out new hair salons. One day I received a hair salon promotion email from Groupon. Chateau D'tour Salon was on the top of the list. Later I found out its only 4 miles away from my house. After read all these 5-star reviews on Yelp I decided to give this place a try. I bought this Groupon without hesitation. That was 3 month ago. 

1st Red Flag: Booking
I tried calling a few times but no one ever answered the phone. I also left voice messages but no one ever bother to return my call. I also tried texting, same thing, and no response whatsoever. BTW, I told her I am a Groupon customer in both voice message and text message.  After a few attempts, I started having bad feelings... But I still have high hope for this place because of all those 5-star Yelp reviews. Finally, I booked my appointment through an online booking system (no one ever told me how to make an appointment).

2nd Red Flag: Poor Business Practice
I couldn't wait to try this place out so I took the first available opening. 9:00 A.M. in the morning, I believe I was her 1st customer on that day. I arrived 5 minutes before 9:00. No one was there so I called Stephanie. She told me she stuck in a car accident and she will late for at least 15 minutes. I said no problems. She arrived about 20 minutes later. I had a few unpleasant haircut experiences before so I thought it was necessary to spend a little time to communicate with my hairstylist. BTW, I have very long, thick, and natural curly hair. So I always chose v-shaped, long layered hairstyle in order to control frizzy. All I wanted just a beautiful haircut, which could make me look a little prettier. I guess that just too much to ask. 

3rd Red Flag: Lack of Experiences
After about 10 minutes discussion, Stephanie started washing my hair. The Groupon Promotion Haircut Package included shampoo, deep conditioning, haircut, and style. OK, now do the math, we were definitely running out of the time. So everything started speed up from this point. Her next customer showed up when she was still cutting my hair. Technically, she chopped my hair. She used the thinner shears (a special scissors for thinning hair) thinning my hair. A regular hair stylist could tell that was a huge mistake for my kind of hair. She started thinning my hair from the middle of my hair length, so my long layered hairstyle was totally ruined. After the cut, the shortest hair was only 3-4 inches long. It was the frizziest haircut I ever had. As a result my hair looked crazy frizzy from the root all the way to the end. My hair couldn't be frizzier. 

I trusted Stephanie because I thought we had good communication. So I wasn't paying attention. I was texting my friends. It was too late when I realized what she was doing. I think Stephanie also realized thinning my hair was a mistake so she tried to cover it up by flat-ironed my hair, which I hate the most. The funny thing was my hair looks even frizzier afterwards because the fly iron dry my hair out.

Since Stephanie was late for her next appointment so she was in rush to complete my haircut. My hair looked dull, dry, and crazy frizzy when I walked out the salon. My hair also stuck on my skull because too much styling products. I pointed out a couple obvious flaws and asked her to fix it but she was really impatient. In the end, I feel I wasn't welcome anymore. I had to leave because she gave me that "I am done" look. I went to Costco after my hair appointment. I saw my hair in big mirror. It's definitely a mess. I couldn't stand the look of my hair, so I went back to the salon and politely asked her to fix it. I was trying to offer her an opportunity to make things right but she ruined it. I am getting tired writing...

Long story short, I went to another Salon and tried to fix my hair. But the damage was too great; there is no quick fix but to wait for my hair to grow back. I had 2 haircuts in one day. I tried so hard to control my temper. I was beyond upset; not only because of the horrible haircut but also because of the way I've been treated in the end. It's been 3 months now I am still getting angry every time I look at my hair. Now, I am thinking to give my hair a Brazilian Blowout or a Keratin Treatment in order to reduce frizzy. I need at least another 5-6 months to recover from the damage, which Stephanie has caused. And NO, ABSOLUTELY NOT!! I WILL NOT RECOMMEND Stephanie TO ANYONE!!!! NEVER!!!!

Blueberry Basil
Lavender Love
Tropical Turmeric
Raspberry Goji Rose

[1]  I have found joy with these kombucha offerings!  Not only are these probiotics great for your gut health, but they're organic and contain only 80 calories per bottle (40 calories per serving, and two servings per bottle).  After I finish the contents, I plan on reusing the beautiful blue bottle as a water receptacle.

[2]  Visited WF today (6/27/16), and it does NOT carry Wild Tonic kombucha among the myriad brands of kombuchas inside their dedicated cooler (across the bakery).  I only know of one other restaurant/market that carries Wild Tonic's products, and that's The Market by Jennifer's in Phoenix.

Bought a brand new 2010 ford raptor.  Bought every warranty.  7 year 125000 miles. Bought the service plan. I even had a windshield, tire, and door ding warranty. It started to leak oil, So they took it in and made some repairs. Drove it for a week or two and problem returns. Finally there was a huge clunk every time I put it in reverse.  I physically had to drive the tech around to show him.  Truck was in the dealership for 2 months for transmission repair.  At the time my vehicle was 2 years old and had 20-30k miles. I was lucky I had the manufacturers warranty. 


Shocks - The raptor have high performance fox shocks which cost around $10,000. So to have problems with them is a big deal. I had my vehicle at a off road shop installing HID lights.  They drove it around at night to make sure the lights were pointed correctly.  The tech said I'm pretty sure your shocks are blown take it to ford.  He said you have bump steer and a lot of movement on uphill or downhill grades.  I take it to ford and as you can guess, nothing is wrong.  I failed to look at the paperwork. If I would have I would've seen the techs note that read, "unable to duplicate problem, checked for leaks or loose parts". There are several tests you can perform that will show if the shocks are shot, they looked at it and said no loose bolts or leaks, your good. Two months later I hit a bump on the freeway and almost crash with my family in the car.  I immediately take it to a shop, who performs a legitimate inspection, and he says your shocks are bad.  I told them it was just at ford and they said they were fine.  He's asked to see the paperwork for the tests they ran.  That's when he showed me they DIDN'T perform any tests.  I decide to take it to the other ford dealership, even though it's an hour away.  They said "your warranty expired on your shocks in October, but it shows you were at the other dealership for this issue before the warranty expired. They should cover this". They printed all the documents to take to team ford. Team Ford refused to do anything even after I had the original tech that found the problem call them and say it's the exact same issue as before, nothing has changed. 

Lesson learned, don't go to this service department or maybe buy a different brand. I spent $60,000 on a new vehicle and $10000 in warranties. Nothing but problems with the service team.  I had similar issues with my sync system, sunroof, and rear slider.

If someone could harness the power of Ansel Adams turning in his grave from this gallery, we could stop importing oil from the middle east tomorrow.

Passing this gallery and watching people talk about spending tens of thousands on a print of one of Jeff's pictures made me cry inside. And if at any point Jeff tried submitting his pictures to National Geographic or any reputable travel magazine, I'm sure I'm in good company. While some of his pictures aren't bad, the majority are derivative and bland. You can find similar (and better) quality shots on postcards or browsing flickr. The one feature that stands out best about this collection of cliche landscape pictures is the price: not even the masters would charge $30,000 for a reprint.

The worst part is that almost every picture suffers from amateur-hour post processing, resulting in extremely oversaturated colors and blown out highlights. Jeff clearly had thousands of dollars and entire months to spend on capturing his pictures in the first place, so it boggles the mind why he couldn't find the few hours necessary to correct minor technical issues like these. Ultimately, it speaks to the essence of what this gallery is about: not good photography, but extraordinary commercial exploitation.

Some examples of landscape photography done right: http://www.luminous-landscape.com/techniques/cycling.shtml

I had just concluded my tour of the pleasant little Monet Exhibit within the Bellagio Gallery. After you leave the Gallery, they funnel you past a tiny sales area and then deliberately into the Jeff Mitchum Gallery. What a lucky opportunity!

The Jeff Mitchum Gallery features a stunning and diverse collection of fine art photography of nature and dramatic landscape from around the world. Some have referred to him as the Ansel Adams of color. He also has his own line of eco-furniture that I relaxed in as I happily paged through his Seasons of Light (Volume II). At at $175 it's most probably worth every penny.

Bellagio is one of the finest hotels in all of Vegas, and Jeff Mitchum's work is right at home there. It's one thing to see his work, it's a whole other to meet the photographer! Jeff Mitchum's landscape photography is like Ansel Adams in color. Not only did he grow up a personal friend of Ansel (as he'll tell you), his style is reflected in Jeff's work. Jeff was even gifted Ansel's hiking boots by his family.

The gallery is beautiful and intimate. The work is stunning and there's a story behind every piece. If you get a chance to talk with Jeff he'll tell you that while Ansel didn't believe in limiting his work with edition sizes (all of his pieces are open editions), Jeff believes in protecting the pieces and the collectors; Jeff does sign and number each print. Most will fall in love with his art, at minimum a print or two, but some may feel they can't afford it. Jeff now has his book available as a set with a framed print - the collection is priced under $1,000 so those that want to own a piece of his work can afford to do so.

Jeff will have the grand opening of his second gallery in Vegas 4th of July weekend 2013. That gallery will show additional pieces, but will not have the intimate feeling that this current gallery does. Stop in and check it out!

I have been to the gallery several times since it's been at the Bellagio next to the Bellagio gallery of Fine Arts.  If you're going to/from the pool or to/from the Bellagio's Spa Tower, or attending a meeting at one of the conference rooms down the hallway, you've gone by and maybe noticed the photos but kept going to get to where you wanted to be.  Next time, stop, go in, and enjoy the photos.

I have been on two walking photo journeys with Jeff and I find his work to be outstanding!  It is great when you're able to hear from the photographer how they composed a particular photo, how long they had to study the area to know when was the best time, and other things that a layman such as myself never think of.

A reason to visit would be to see some of the original Masad photos which will  soon be going to the museum in Israel.  Hearing him describe how he discovered and used the metal from the bunkers on the Golan Heights for his frames was a fantastic story and put the photographs into an historical perspective.

I'll be sure when I go to the BGFA to see the Warhol exhibit that I'll once again stop in and see the photos.  They are good!
A very important photographer - Jeff Mitchum - and a great art gallery dealing with so many international artists.

In October of 2015, hubby and entered this gallery because of the furniture we saw through the display window.  They were so different, then we sat in them and they were so comfortable.  Being that we were remodeling a new home, we thought it might be fun to own a couple of these pieces.

We made our choices and put down our deposit.  We were told the chairs would take 8-9 months.  We waited.

Now it's September of 2016, there has been NO communication from the gallery.  No updates, nothing.  We tried calling to get information, at first they didn't know us, then when we started pressing they "found" our order and told us that Victor had to call us back.  A week went by and no phone call from Victor, so since we were in Vegas we decided to stop by the gallery and do this in person.

Gary, our original salesperson was working.  He remember us, we told him about our situation.  He obviously had no information to give us and told us Victor would have that information.  This conversation took place last Sunday.  I said, well not knowing is a horrible excuse and that if we didn't have a definitive answer by Tuesday I wanted our money back.

Gary called us on Tuesday (Victor is still in hiding, I'm starting to think he isn't real and they use that name to blow people off) and told us that the container ship with OUR chairs will be docking in Long Beach any day now, but definitely within September, but we don't have a date, but we know your chairs are on there.. etc.  

We gave them until October 1st to have our chairs in our home in San Diego or we want a refund.  

This gallery has beautiful items, but if you can't take it home with you when you purchase it, I would rethink buying here.  They have zero communication skills and ZERO f**ks are given by them.

Jeff s the man!  I first met Jeff a year ago ,I was working and he asked me about my weekend. I told him I just finished Mystery Canyon and he said he had been back there. I then started asking what other canyons he had completed in Zion. I then explained to him that I spent years teaching outdoor education and spend all my time climbing, camping, canyoneering, riding, or doing whatever it takes to the next adventure.  He laughed a little... I asked what he did for work and what brought him to Vegas. He told me to check out his website.  I did.  I came back later that afternoon and talked to him about his Teton images.  The rest is history, it was the beginning of a solid friendship through the things he captures- Nature.

Jeff's ability to capture these images are awesome, the world needs to see these places. His philosophy is simple and that is what I like about his images.  We all know pictures are powerful, but I believe that what Jeff does is different. He is able to take nature and present in a form that everyone can learn from.  One day these places won't be the same and images is all we will have to remember from. 

In the end, his traditional approach and influence from Adams is apparent in his images, it is a good thing.   The world needs to be reminded of places that he is capturing.  Most people will never walk off the beaten path or step foot in the back country; it is scary to think about in my opinion.  However, when Jeff releases images, it can plant a seed of thought, and that seed can lead to growth, and growth can lead to change.  When you look at the early times with Adams he was capturing the things that were important to him and his legacy.  Open spaces were sparred from development through Adam's work...Jeff honors that tradition.

 As for me, I am inspired by his work, particularly the Teton images.  I have spent years in the back country and teaching outdoor education; it is grounding to find someone who has the ability to reach the masses with one image.  In the end, we all have a responsibility to create a positive impact for society; Jeff is doing this and will continue to do it.  In my opinion, his images speak for themselves and each person can find a way to relate to it.  It is so easy to complicate things in life, these images are a reminder that nature is where the greatest reflection can occur.  

One day, I hope I can join him on one of his adventures or he can tag along with me on a climb, ride, or trip.  See you on the summit Grand Teton Traverse 2014 3 peaks 1 day!  

Dave

I am a Las Vegas native and have been to Jeff Mitchum's gallery multiple times. The first time I heard of this gallery I became excited because we have few here. As soon as I entered the gallery I was filled with misery, another photographer had jumped on to the Peter Lik bandwagon of charging far too much per print, the over use of bad HDR techniques and blowing up their mediocre, badly post-processed images as large as possible and selling them on gimmicky metallic photo paper. The only thing worse than the prints in this gallery are the salespeople. As I looked at each image I was approached by which ever salesperson that was present the multiple times that I have gone to the gallery. I was bombarded with a lack of knowledge about photography on their half. One time I was there I was looking at a very poorly done extremely large print of a pixelated HDR image of a sail boat, the salesperson approached me and started telling me the origin of the image. When I asked her about why Jeff had decided to make a post process High Dynamic Range of a moving image she could not answer me, I explained what I meant and she assured me that it was a single image and had not been manipulated by post processing. I let her finish her sales pitch and left. About a year later I found my self in the Bellagio and decided to visit again, as I looked at the image, Radiant Wonder, I was approached by a salesperson who said, isn't it wonderful how he was able to capture such a magnificent moment in a single image, if only that were true. I explained to her that there was no possible way that print is a single image, the bird was layered on in post process because the background (waterfall) had been taken in a slow exposure. She continued her sales pitch and assured me that Jeff was a master of his art. The thing that bothers me the most is that Jeff and other "artists" such as Peter Lik are taking advantage of buyers with big wallets and little knowledge and trick them in to thinking they are buying a masterpiece, when in reality they are lying and deceiving and selling a $500-1000 print for upwards of $40,000. These buyers find themselves in difficult positions later on when trying to sell. Thinking they will be able to sell them for more than the purchased price because of the lies the salespeople tell them, few are lucky enough to sell them for $1000. Plus many of your largest prints are pixelated. 


RESPONSE TO JEFF MITCHUM'S COMMENT:
I appreciate the response back to my comment. I strongly recommend that you do not tell someone how to spend their time, I was simply reviewing my experiences in your gallery, you as a gallery owner should look at my review as a way to improve yourself and be thankful that someone took the time to write a review about your business, even if it was a negative critique. I spend much of my time creating and shooting, I rarely critique anything, however your salespeople left me with such a bad taste in my mouth I felt it necessary to tell your future visitors about my experiences and heed them with warnings. From the tone of your comment I feel that you want me to apologize for the false information that your salespeople had relayed to me. The sail boat photo is the only photo in your gallery that I can recall being an HDR, knowing that it is not yours is refreshing. I apologize for not being aware that only your display prints have the digital signatures, it makes me happy to know that you sign and number each of your prints.

My first time at Jeff's gallery adjacent to the Bellagio Gallery of Fine Art was a result of the CYME photo walk. I did some research and found out Jeff has a renowned background, including being mentored by Ansel Adams. His work is beautiful and the chance to meet him and hear the story behind his work in his gallery was awesome! 
He surprised us by opening his suite at the Cosmo to all of us for a great evening of shooting from the suite's wrap around balcony. We had a full view of the fountains and also enjoyed snacks and drinks. A great evening!

I wandered into Jeff's gallery in the MGM during a trip to Vegas. As a pro photographer myself, I was interested in the techniques that Jeff uses to print these large scale images and spent time looking at each one, both at a normal viewing angle and close up.  The composition of the images is really good - Jeff manages to find the right light/time of day and viewing angle to provide a great perspective. His images have a very painterly feel to them - one of a country road (Appalachia?) had stalks of corn in just the right place, which I thought was a very nice touch. 

Beyond that, Jeff is using his darkroom/digital skills to the max to render these images. The colors are really brilliant - beyond what I would expect to find in nature. Another image - cowboys bringing in a herd - had the 'subjects' in sharp relief while the herd and background was more bokeh'ed and de-res'ed to heighten the subjects.  The shipwreck on the beach (mentioned by another Yelper) is in super-sharp detail but the water around it has been smoothed (this one is a double exposure?). It's not a photo journalistic style (which is what I shoot), but it makes for an image that minimizes the distractions and lets people see the beauty.  (BTW I didn't quite understand the 'fuzziness' of the flowers until I realized that Jeff is shooting film and likely long exposures, during which the wind will blow things around.)

I started out fairly critical (especially given Peter Lik's sales-driven focus) but came out more appreciative. The images are an artist's view of nature - not far from what Ansel Adams himself worked to capture. It was also nice to see some of Anthony Hopkins' work up close, hanging along side the photos.

Jeff Mitchum stands alone and at the top of my list of Fine Arts Photographers in America. His MOSSAD collection has NEVER been duplicated by ANY other artist.  His years of work with Ansel Adams shows in his Yosemite, Moab and Antelope Canyon images.  I have admired pieces of Jeff's California Coastlines - Mendocino and Marin County (Point Reyes), San Francisco to Monterey and down to my favorite Mitchum's La Jolla pier shot . His work strikes my senses more than other's in the field - values are higher than I paid because of such LIMITED release numbers.  I am targeting one of the MGM Hollywood pieces before they hit Harrods in London, by summer 2014?   Also love Jeff Mitchum Coffee Table Books collection - on my third in a series.

People love to claim that there is no culture in Vegas. I would challenge them to shoot on over to the Bellagio and check out Jeff Mitchum's gallery. I could sit here and spout a bunch of facts, such as the fact that he has been featured in both the Smithsonian and the Getty Museum; or that he was given advice at a very young age by the legendary Ansel Adams. If I do that, then I'd be no better than a Google search result. So I'll tell you why I feel that you need to check this gallery out for yourself.

In a relatively small space, you get an incredible history lesson and a trip around the world to some of the most beautiful views you've ever seen (from as far away as Israel, to as close as San Francisco and even the Vegas strip). It's basically like looking through a window to a world that you could only see by bending time. We could look at these locations at any given time of year, and not truly appreciate or even see what both Jeff's camera and his gifted vision had the ability to capture. That's the beauty of a long exposure, in some cases an extremely long exposure. If you're like me, you'll look at these pictures and keep saying to yourself "These aren't even photoshopped?!?". You'll enter with a hungry soul, and leave thoroughly satisfied. You should also pick up his awesome book, "Seasons of Light: Volume II". Every time you need inspiration or a pick me up, you can flip through and just escape to another world that Jeff proves exists, even if we don't  always see it.

I visit his gallery every time I am in Vegas. His work is incredible, including specifically designed frames for each piece. He is truly a great artist!! His work is the bright light for me, whenever I go, there are always new pieces to enjoy. Maybe someday I will own one or, at very least, one of his books. If you love nature, Mitchum takes you on a journey around the world to places you never knew about.  Awesome!

Last night was the first time I ever attended an event.  I was in awe when I entered Jeff Mitchum's Gallery.  His photo's are breathtaking! I was amazed how I felt when I looked at his photo's, I felt as though I was right there in the place where the photo was taken.  I highly recommend the Gallery, everyone who loves nature, landscape and art in general should take the time to browse through Jeff's Gallery.  

This man started talking to me during my visit.  He was so down to earth and a pleasure to talk to.  When I asked who he was, I was shocked to know that I was actually talking to Mr. Mitchum!!! Such a neat guy.  

When we finished looking at his beautiful photo's, he invited us up to his suite at the Cosmopolitan Hotel on the 37 floor.  He had snacks and beverages available for us as well as an open balcony with a beautiful view of the strip so we could take all the photo's we wanted to.   

Because I'm an armature with my camera, I needed lots of help with settings to get the photos I was hoping for.  Jeff and another guest was very helpful.  I learned a lot from them and I hope I can remember everything they taught me.  

I'm looking forward to seeing my photo's as soon as I get the free time to do so.

Also, a big thank you to Melissa who supported me all evening long by giving me advice on which view I should take photo's of and certain effects I should had to the photo such as causing the head/tail lights of vehicles to stream across the photo's!! You Melissa are a sweetheart!

Another nice thing about this event, I was able to meet some really super nice people!! Norm, thank you for being such a gentleman by introducing me to everyone.  You really made me feel comfortable.

I can't wait for the next Photo opportunity with Jeff Mitchum!!! Thank you Mr. Mitchum for your time and generosity!

On a prior trip, I asked a guard for directions to this gallery, but he could not help.  We found it this trip because it adjoins the Bellagio's Gallery of Fine Art.  Jeff is an obviously excellent photographer who specializes in panoramic nature photos.  Our visit was well worth out time.  I subsequently learned Jeff has opened a new gallery
a MGM which we will be visiting soon.

There needs to be more STARS than just 5!
Jeff Mitchum Gallery is one of the most beautiful galleries I've ever been to! His photographs are not photographs, they are pure ART! But Jeff is so much more than an amazing photographer. I've followed his work for over a year & unfortunately have never actually met this wonder man. However, Jeff is always so kind & generous to fellow photographers. Always willing to share photography tips & his knowledge of his work. He is SO encouraging & supportive to so many of us that follow him. It is a dream of mine to some day soon own one of his pieces and to meet the man behind the lens. Thank you Jeff for creating such beautiful pieces for the world to enjoy.

A nice gallery literally featuring some of the finest art landscape photographs captured over decades by one of the world's finest master landscape photographer, Jeff Mitchum.  With works recognized by the Smithsonian and also the Israel collection that will be featured in museum in Israel, Jeff has been described as the Ansel Adams of Color. 

The photos all look like it was back-lit, but it is actually printed on some special photo-paper with a special silver compound dye, which helps absorbs the light and disperse it throughout the photograph.  Making each print a museum quality works of art.

The gallery itself is not in a well traversed part of Bellagio, but it is totally worth the effort to locate and check out the displayed photos in the gallery.

If you are visiting the Bellagio, be sure to stop by and experience the lights as envisioned and captured by a truly world class photographer.  You will not be disappointed.

The price is relatively modest compared to other high end photography galleries, but the quality is second to none.

 It was finally received the last week of April!  My husband called Victor and told him it was received but it had been such a hassle and stress for me.  Victor said he spoke to the owner and was told to send another photograph of my choice for all the trouble.

WOW! 

I had an amazing experience walking into the Jeff Mitchum Gallery inside of the MGM Grand Casino in Las Vegas. 

I'm a huge fan of giant prints... I love the feeling of standing in front of a giant print and feeling like I could hike right into the scene! At the proper viewing distance, these prints came to life for me! 

Jeff has an amazing portfolio of images captured in some of my favorite locations in the world, as well as a number of locations that are on my bucket list. 

I thought the prints were amazing, and presented in frames that are as artful as the images themselves. I loved the use of alternative framing materials to create a spectacular presentation. 

My favorite print in the gallery was the 12' long, masterfully framed image of a bamboo forest! Felt like I could walk right up those stone steps and into the forest!

I walked out with a beautiful, weighty limited edition book called "The Dance of Light" to add to my photography book collection! Probably the highest quality printing I have seen! The book itself is a work of art!

Can't wait to get one of these images on my one of my walls!!
Potential new patient but put on hold every time I call.  First wait was over 15 minutes.  If I can't even set an appt. Then I don't want to go further than that.  Not recommended already.

I stopped in on a whim. Driving down 43rd Ave, I noticed a new sign and thought ?????Hot Dog?!! who does love a good hot dog?

This place is OUTSTANDING! I went here with my brother one day to try some Chicago style hotdogs. My parents are from Illinois, and I  was craving a taste of home. A MUST TRY hotdog joint!
I just had in the Sonoran hotdog and it has to be one of the best hotdogs I've had in many many years! Great location plenty of items on the menu go in and say hi to JR tell him Gary sent you
It was suggested by yelp...and was worth it! My favorite was the Carolina yummtastic!

Excellent grub!!!!! Mmmm mmm mmm!!! 
The staff are friendly and down too earth.
I couldn't decide between the Sonoran Hotdog or mushroom swiss burger I had both! And I loved them both. I'm happy I have a huge appetite so I can enjoy both. I will definitely be coming back here during my lunch breaks.

WE met the owners at a previous place of business and started talking. They told us they had a hot dog business and where it was. Very clean, good hours of operation and enough TV's to watch for entertainment and sports. We will make this place our new "honey hole". Thank you Hometown! 
P.S.  GREAT SALSA, TOO!
Outstanding selection of hotdogs! Their sonoran dog is something you'll want to order again -- very tasty and the bread is toasted just right.

Today I had the Sonoran hot dog combo with pinto beans and cheese. 
The hot dog itself was awesome. All beef, big, good flavor. Not the kind you can get in grocery store. The bun was good. My Sonoran toppings were awesome! Usually, you get bacon wrapped around the hotdog with mayo and salsa over. Not here, everything chopped up including the bacon. It was a huge mess (in a good way). 
The side dish of pinto beans with cheese were simple and delicious. I could just eat those beans for dinner. 
The service was attentive and polite. These are real people, wanting to succeed in what they do.
My only complaint was the Sonoran needed more heat. I told the owner, she said next time just ask....they have a ghost pepper mix they can add if asked for! Wahooo! 
This place is "expensive" for a hot dog, but the quality backs up the price. I can see this place getting a cult following with time. 
Can't wait to try out the burgers.

There's not much to say other than this place has some decent hot dogs with a lot of different options.  The only negatives that I can say we're the tater tots and the speed of the meal.

My husband ordered a classic brat with a side of potato bites (tater tots), son ordered a hot dog, ketchup only. I ordered a Philly baked potato, or I should say I wanted a Philly potato..out of potatoes. So I ordered loaded potato bites, I'm not much of a hot dog fan!

I always order the Carolina.. absolutely love how it's loaded with my favorites; which is macaroni salad and coleslaw. I always get potato salad on the side too. Reminds me of summer BBQ. Luv it!!!
Next time I'm going for pastrami. Yum!!!

Amazing. Absolutely amazing. 

My love of hotdogs has been fulfilled in this perfect neighborhood joint. They are so incredibly friendly, even going out of their way to give us a sample of their amazing tater tots. 

The menu has a wide selection for everyone, it is a MUST try.
Good people good service great hot dogs  awesome salsa great burgers and prices are very reasonable prices

You will never feel more American than when you eat a hot dog at Nana Tees!  The first thing I tried was the Sonoran Dog and it was great! Very friendly, easily conversational staff and reasonable pricing.   

08/01/16

Been going back since and found a new favorite... The Philly! very tasty with a brat.

This great restaurant is very well kept. I had the opportunity to meet the owners, one being Nana Tee.  They have a great variety from hot dogs that come in many different loaded formations.
