Tried them out this morning and was very satisfied.  Had a sausage, egg and cheese sesame bagel.  The bagel was great, chewy not tough like some.  The entire bagel was covered with sesame seeds not just the "top".  Tasted fresh.  They have plain and flavored coffees in pump urns so you can choose what you want.  The only reason they didn't get 5 stars from me is the cheese was a slice of American and I think a bagel this good should be paired with real cheese and because the bagel was barely toasted.  Those nit picky issues didn't stop me from buying a half dozen to go.  Oh and the prices are extremely reasonable.

Breakfast is freshly prepared and any choice of items looked delicious.   Hash browns are cubed with a nice seasoning.....  Try this place.   Definitely  get some bagels to go! Bagels are fresh and numerous options on flavored cream cheeses.   Quick friendly service.  Lots of salad options and sandwiches are filled with excellent high quality meats.   This place is a great addition to Fort Mill.

Wonderful Gourmet quality foods!
What a surprise to find such a gem in Tega Cay!
I will be back and bring my friends.
Just excellent!
Excellent salads and sandwiches, bagels are as good as it gets in SC...staff is very accommodating, prices are good, should make a trip. Breakfast of bacon, egg and cheese on bagel is definite get.
Love this place! So happy to have a good deli here finally. Friendly staff. Great food. I'm a regular.
One of our favorite lunch places.  We usually get some type of panini and have yet to be disappointed.  Sometimes it can be difficult to find a place to sit when it's busy, so that can be annoying.

I love the Tega Cay Deli! I work next to them, and I frequently go for my lunch. I love the owners, they are the nicest people! They have great food! Love their sandwiches! I will say it's a little on the pricier side for lunch items like sandwiches and salads, but over all I love it. Line is long during lunch time, and the place is pretty small inside, I wasn't able to sit inside because there was no room, but they do have outdoor seating, it was a little to cold to sit out there today so I just got it to go. But a great place overall, totally 5 stars!

I absolutely love this place! The bagel breakfast sandwiches are simply the best. One day I plan to try them for lunch but for now I'll share my enthusiasm for the bacon egg and cheese breakfast sandwich. I get it on the egg bagel as a combo with a cup of coffee which rings up to a little under $5. I'd be in serious trouble if this was on my way to work instead of the opposite direction. 

The owners are very friendly and service is always so quick. The pump your own coffee comes in a variety of flavors and is always hot and fresh. The price is good for the quality of the breakfast and the atmosphere is very inviting. This is a stop worth making!
Being from New York, i have high expectations for food. This place will not disappoint. Great Bagels, Great Staff. Awesome Owners. So glad your here!!
I have only heard great things from people who have been here.  Everything is fresh and delicious!
Very good. Staff was very friendly. Food was very tasty. Zero to complain about. I'll be back.

Bagels and sandwich ingredients = Bagels Sandwiches

My wife and I ate here for breakfast and she ordered a Bacon Egg Cheese on a bagel and I ordered the same, but on a roll.  Hers was better, get the bagel if you go.

Overall the taste was a bit on the bland side, both seemed to be missing a little something, although we could not put out finger on what it was missing.

The decor is kinda plain, and looks a bit unfinished. But that didn't take away from the experience.

The prices were very reasonable.  I will be going back.

I teetered between a 3 and a 4, becuase of the plain flavor. I went with 4 stars because the food was good overall, the service quick, and the prices were so reasonable.

A New Yorker and an egg sandwich is a love affair. It's the    one thing we miss the most and now it's here! They also have great coffee, chopped salads and sandwiches and bagels. At the front when you pay they have homemade crumb cake and desserts. It's always packed so call ahead to order if your picking up . You won't be disappointed.

This place recently opened this week. I have eaten there 2 times already with my mom and 2 small children. We tried many dishes from the hot bar and sanwiches as well. Chicken dishes, rice pilaf, mac and cheese and veggies were excellent. Everything is made in house by a skilled NY cook. They make their own bagels too. This spot is super clean and so adorable inside. Owners were warm and helpful to me and my family. If you like fresh quality yummy food, make a stop!

When I walked into the deli I got a huge smile on my face, because I recognized the owner from another bagel shop in Charlotte. My husband and I are from New York and have tried out every bagel shop in town. This deli is truly a New York deli, and will not disappoint. So glad they are open in Tega Cay!
Food and service were great. I had the Santa Fe and my wife had a cold sub. Quality was great and had a big selection to choose from.
Appreciate having a local "Deli" offering various regional foods!  Support local business owners!!

Best breakfast sandwich and bagels ive had since moving from NY! Fresh authentic and delicious-  not too heavy or doughy, the bacon crisp and high-quality and made to order eggs.   Quick, efficient and pleasant service.  The $3.99 special is a steal- bacon egg and cheese on a roll/bagel and a coffee!!  Also other yummy ny faves like taylor ham, strawberry creamcheese and buttery crumbcake!! Definitely recommend trying!
Taylor ham, egg and cheese on the freshest everything bagel! Staff was very pleasant. Quick service. Will be back! Great food!
This place makes it easy to support local business. Great food, great service and great prices. We'll be back again and again.

Stopped in for the bacon, egg, cheese bagel breakfast special and was surprised with made from scratch NY style bagels!! I got mine on the egg everything bagel and it was amazing-- also, bacon quality was well above the average breakfast sandwich.

Can't wait to go back and try their lox w/ the works bagel and more!

So fresh and tasty. The salads are amazing and so are the bagels and hashbrowns. I think the only item that wasn't impressive was a pasta salad. They've got a good thing going over there and I'm happy to support a local business.
Great place,  food is real good as far as the sandwiches go and the bagels and breakfast.   Finally a good place to get egg sandwiches.

Being from New York, I am thrilled to find a New York style deli here in South Carolina! I had the "Lox with the Worx" on a asiago cheese bagel, toasted. My mouth is still celebrating! Had to take half in a take out box because the portions were so generous. Where else are you going to Dina bagel with smoked salmon, red onions, tomatoes, CAPERS, and cream cheese. This place is friendly, clean, convenient, and oh so amazing w their bagels. Check it out!

This is my first time visiting this location. I had the Tega Cay omelette with ham onions and cheddar and I thought I'd add a bagel with cream cheese just to check out their bagels. Overall for a breakfast Deli not a bad selection however it was not my favorite breakfast. I'll file this under a potential maybe for my next Deli outing.
Great place! Small but wonderful food. A bit pricey but food is great! Love coming here whenever I can! Limited hours so get here early!
First visit for lunch today,carry out. Great sandwich (the Italian), with a side of egg salad. Friendly staff.Now that my office has moved down the street they will see me again.
TC Deli has the best bagels I've had since living in South Florida.  This has become our quick, go to breakfast place.  However, the chopped salads are amazing for lunch, too!

Good deli!  I've had the chopped salad and a few of the prepared salads.  Sandwiches are good too.  My Italian sub was really good but just a tad soggy due to a little too much oil.  Other than that I highly recommend this place!

I am not sure why there are so many great reviews. 

We ate there ordering two sandwiches; a Rueben and a Pastrami on Rye. 

The ingredients were fine and they were hot when they brought them out. 

The problem is the bread was soaked in greasy butter. Literally dripping from the bread. 

Not toasty as it should have been but soaking in grease. 

Mediocre at best.
A family staple for us.  We love the omelets, salads, bagels, & cookies are awesome.  The paninis are most likely the best we've ever had as a family.  We love this place!!!!

I'm here for the 3rd day in a row. Very excited this place is here  one thing the South lacks is good delis and this is it.   I do not consider Jason's deli or any big chains like that legit good delis. This is a good legit deli. If you are from up North you will love it..  food and service are great  15 minute drive and I'm happy to make it.

This place is okay... just a basic breakfast. Anything you get here you can do at your own house. I got a bacon egg and cheese on toast and it wasn't hot cheese wasn't even melted. Been here 3 or 4 times and service is just slow for breakfast/ bagel place.
Finally a place to buy a fresh chopped salad. I'd probably be here every day if I worked hereby. Will become a weekend regular. Great fresh bagels too.

Came in for a family breakfast once I heard about NY Bagels. Well we were so happy to have our beloved bagels right here in SC. Just moving from LI NY we were missing those perfect bagels. This place totally nails it. 

Clean and updated atmosphere, super family friendly. The outdoor seating was nice too, the mornings are still not too hot so we can sit outside. 

We will surely be back here for breakfast. I would have uploaded pics but we are everything too fast. :) 

YUM GUYS & GALS! Well done.
This deli is one of the best things to happen to Fort Mill this past year.  Quick service, reasonable prices, great coffee, and delicious bagels!

I saw this place and instantly thought a northern style deli. Looking at the menu, I noticed that all the "condiments" were extra: Cheese, lettuce, onions, pickles, tomato... all extra. So my $6 sandwich ends up being $2 extra when your done with topping it. Ive never heard of a deli place charging you for standard items on a sandwich. My sandwich, plus a side of mac salad and drink was $12. KInda steep. Food was good though, no issues there, and they were doing a good brisk business when I was there. The breakfast items seem priced better, so I may try that.
Best New York deli food here in Tega Cay!  So glad they are here, bagels are fantastic! Deli sandwiches love them!!

Great little deli with fresh salads, breads and sandwiches. I love their everything bagels. Friendly staff and it's always busy there. Minor pitfalls are their short hours the business is open. But then again it's just a breakfast and lunch spot.

Kept hearing about this place so finally decided  to give it a try. So glad that I did. I was stuck between giving a 4 and a 5 but after finishing my salad, definitely had to lean towards that 5. Walked in on a Saturday a little before they closed to get a to go order. Chopped salad for myself which was absolutely amazing. I had them mix my lettuce, so I got a mix of spinach, spring lettuce and romaine and added avocado, mushrooms, carrots, feta cheese and ranch dressing. They chopped it up for me and I'm here to tell you it was banging!!! I ordered my husband an Italian sandwich and asked for it to be on white bread instead of a sub roll. I also asked for no tomatoes or red peppers. Well I got home and it was on a sub roll instead of the white bread. And then they still added the red peppers. Not a big deal, I pulled the peppers off for him and he said it was good, he just obviously wished it was on the white bread like I asked and then wished it had more romaine lettuce on it. It had one teeny tiny piece of lettuce on it. Lastly, I got a pound of egg salad for a friend. It was good! I contemplated maybe keeping it for myself. I love how they have homemade pasta salads and such that they sell by the pound. I will be back!

Finally good NY bagels in Lake Wylie!  Don't fool around with any other place.  Fresh hot bagels made on site!  Boars Head meats.  Bacon, egg and cheese on a roll.  Deli style sandwiches!  They have it all.  You need to try this place!!!!

This place is great, greeted with smiling faces, the staff is friendly and fast.
The food is awesome, the select of bagels that are fresh and pastries are plentiful. I have a family of picky eaters and the menu selections they have has something for everyone
My choice is the omelet and home fries
Clean, friendly, and reasonably priced good food.  Can't ask,for much more.  Plus they have Taylor Ham sandwiches.
Awesome homemade bagels and a variety of salads made fresh every morning. Boar's Head meats and cheeses. Staff are amazingly friendly and helpful. Definitely a fine addition to Tega Cay!

Great spot to grab a bagel or breakfast sandwich. Used to live in the South End neighborhood of Charlotte and this filled the void of Owen's Bagels. Coffee is great, too. Expect a 5 minute wait during peak breakfast times, but it's well worth it.
As close to a NY/NJ deli as you will get in South Carolina.  Great food and good prices.  This is my new favorite lunch spot on Ft Mill

Tega Cay Gourmet Deli is located in Tega Cay, SC (near the Walmart Supercenter).  My manager (from work) has been raving about their breakfast rolls.  

I ordered Ham, Egg, and Cheese on a roll (with an extra egg).  YUM!!  Exactly as my manager mentioned, the rolls were delicious!  It did remind me of the breakfast sandwiches / rolls that my significant other and I used to get in New York City!  

ENJOY!!
Best real Turkish iskender doner kebab ,fantastic baklava and Turkish tea, nice management in Danforth .

Went to Efes last night for the first time. Went with wife and daughter. All 3 of us enjoyed (and shared) our entrees. We had the Adana Kabob, chicken shish and meatball platter.

Having been to Istanbul 4 times, I can honestly say the food here is authentically Turkish.  In my experience, that's easier said than done. 

I believe this place is family run. Nice people.

Wine selection was limited.  Raki was available. A true Turkish drink!!!

Very good experience overall!

Hands down, one of the best gyros in town. Seriously. 

As a native Turkish, I can say that this place offers authentic delicious food that won't make you miss the real thing. I tried the beef doner over rice, comes with a generous portion of fresh veggies, absolutely delicious. Iskender kebab was pretty good although it lacks a bit of a kick, maybe tiny bit too bland. Sish chicken was okay, again it could use some more spices. The soup is a good option for a light vegan choice. Adana kebab and kofte (meatballs) are both pretty good. Last but not least, baklava is a boost of pistachios that will make you want to have more. Don't forget your Turkish tea/coffee with it! 

The service could be better but l still want to round my 4,5stars to five in order to support this new business. Kudos for the cleanliness. Good for families, easy access for stroller & lots of room for babies, high chair. Live instrumental music on Fridays and Saturdays. Requires reservation on weekend.

Hands down the best Turkish food on the Danforth. This family run business really goes above and beyond. The dine-in meals are no joke. They don't skimp you on portions and everything is tasty. Our favorite meal is the lamb shish. They cook it so tender and juicy. With an order of cacik you're in heaven. Worth the price that you pay.

This restaurant has just opened and we are so happy it has! The food is delicious and authentic tasting and the atmosphere is great! They serve alcohol unlike many other Turkish restaurants in the city. It is a definite must place to come!

This place is in terrible shape. Avoid it at all costs. No grass left in the fairway and the rough is weed. Greens are the best feature and they are bumpy and inconsistent. I would like to buy it and do it all over.
Terrible fairways and kind of a boring course.
Golfed there today and must say it has to be in the worst shape of any golf course I have ever played. Which says a lot.  Absolutely terrible.

It is literally the bare minimum to be considered a bar.  A rectangular room with sticky floors and terrible music.  Filled with Bros and Hoes.  But they serve minors so I guess thats the whole point right?

A few years ago i would have given this bar 3 stars, but they have cleaned up a little and the crowd has changed since i graduated. When i went there, the bathrooms would flood about half way into the night and spill out into the actual bar. It's a little better now, but the bathrooms are still really gross, even for a campus bar. Take a friend in case there's no door.

This is where I had my first "party night" out back in 1989 (I was 18... not quite drinking age but I had a fake ID). I was pledging a local fraternity and they brought me here and got me wasted on Blue Hawaiians. Later in the evening, a Senior came in and pretended to bust me for underage drinking. 

This was where I met countless (and I really mean countless) women prior to questionable late night hookups. I still remember many faces but sadly, very few names. Such was the magic of COs.

COs is where on not one, but two, occasions my friends who later respectively became a successful doctor and a well-known physicist kicked off their 21st birthdays off (both of them ended the evening in the local ER to get treated for alcohol poisoning).

I haven't been there since maybe 1999 but I can still recall the sickly sweet smell of puke and stale beer that wafted past the place as I walked past to my morning classes.

Yes, so questionable, but the people you'll meet there eventually go on to do some remarkable things! Enjoy your time there... I'd give anything to have it back!

CO's is slightly classier than Kam's and has a slightly older crowd. Good specials, Mondays are $1 you call it's and Wednesdays are $5 ice bombs, which I believe are a CO's invention, because I've never heard of them anywhere else. They definitely get the job done. There are old school video games in the back, the bathrooms sometimes over flow all the way into the bar area, and it can be crowded. There's usually cover on weekend nights after 10 and a line, I think about $5. Honestly, it's a typical college bar.

I was actually in CO's two years ago, and they sure cleaned the place up.  I'd still pay never to have to go in there again, but that's only because of memories of a floor covered in vomit and backed-up toilet water.  It's much nicer now, or at least it was two years ago, but it's a college bar, which means that you should leave your sophistication and morals at the door.

When I went in it smelled overpoweringly like barf. Remembrance of the stomach bile stink still haunts me whenever I think of or pass by this eyesore. It was so strong I couldn't talk, listen or even think. I could hardly choke down the swill and nod to whatever crap music was playing or in rough acknowledgment of what I thought someone else was saying. WHAT DID SHE SAY? THIS PLAY DUCKLING BUCKS? Its pretty loud. 

Needless to say it was also too crowded, dark and dirty. I realize that I am not exactly in their target market, being over 21 and all, but this place is just horrifically bad. Those that characterize this bar as anything but an unmitigated crap-dungeon are either lying to themselves or have never been to a decent bar.

Name should be C.O. Daniel's.

Not that I would ever be comfortable in a bar like this again...but damn did I have fun here in college!

Competitor of KAM'S, which is right next door.  Oh, and btw, both of them are a stone's throw from the main quad.

I love UIUC.

For one, the name of this bar is "C.O. Daniel" - which stands for Cochrane On Daniel. It's a Cochrane bar - imagine that.

It is affectionately known as "C.O.'s" or "See Ho's".
It is a dirty dirty bar, full of underaged fratties and fratties to be, and their corresponding sorostitutes. 

You will not sit on any of the toilets (unless getting the clap sounds like a fun idea to you). You will not make out with any of the basketball players that show up and drink for free all night.

You will receive free shots from your frat brothers who work there. You will stick to the floor, which is covered in a sludge of booze, puke, broken glass, and old napkins which have been ground into a slime. You will be approached by a number of unsavory types. And you will see an exorbitant amount of striped shirts, popped collars, and nearly naked 19 year old girls who are way too excited about their vodka-crans.

Pork burrito with green salsa. I'm coming back for this. 

Coke in a glass bottle. Awesome

Very clean food and kitchen. The owner washed his hands then wore gloves.
Great food, very fast and for the price it is a must stop by and try!
Chicken burrito was delicious!!  Burrito was made exactly the way I wanted it.  Great customer service.

I had the 2 taco combo, a ground beef and pork taco to be exact.  The ground beef wasn't bad but it didn't have a lot of flavor. To pork taco was really good though, it was really tender and wasn't over seasoned. I didn't really care for the rice, the beans tasted like they came out of a can... but good canned beans at least. I had the red roasted chile and chips too. The chips were great, really thin and crispy. The chile needed a little salt and was fine. I will go back but just for the pork i think, if i just had pork tacos i would have given them 4 stars.

I stopped in and had lunch today. Had the burrito with a mix of chicken and steak. It was delicious! Everything was fresh and the right amount of heat. The burrito was so big I don't think that I'll need to have dinner. Definitely will be back!
I love this place. Mom and Pop business where they'll customize your plate with a lot of food for the money.

I am a fan. I usually wait for a few visits before I review just so I do not pass along un-trusting reviews. 

Well Jesters is much better then the reviews let up. The food is fresh and well made. The place is clean and the service is spot on. 

I had a burrito, filled with meat, beans, cheese, and killer hot salsa. (I was having stuffed head syndrome that day) Man was it good. 

The second time I had the ground beef enchilada's. While it seems really boring the meal was great. The flavor just kinda melted together in a symphony of yum. 

If you live/work near by stop in....tell em Daren C sent ya. If you don't like it tell em Nick B sent ya. LOL
My favorite place for lunch with my little man Rhett!! Best loaded Nachos in Phoenix!! Hands UP!! Super fast friendly service!!

I'm big on supporting local business owners to the fullest, but I'm also honest with my reviews.  

Jester's location is tough as is since the storefront is facing an airport and next door is a motorcycle shop and a MVD registration.  However, the good side is that it's the only Mexican restaurant within a 1 to 2 miles radius!  Most other places around the area are sandwich and burger shops.  The shop itself is very new -- matter of fact; think I was their first Yelper.  The decor to me is kind of cheesy with a Jester mascot in a jeep baja and the walls were splashed with some comical quotes of the day.  Needless, to say I wasn't here for that.

I ordered the 2 taco combo; my buddies ordered the cheese quesadilla and a beef burrito.  Fresh ingredients and made to your order, that's a plus in my opinion. However, my corn tortilla tacos were okay.  I thought overall it was pretty plain.  I had a beef and pork taco and there were no seasoning or spice except topped with your choice of sides.  I just had the pico de gallo, lettuce, and hot sauce.  Truthfully, the sauce was mild at best.  Nothing really popped on my plate.  My buddies thought their dishes were excellent.  I was told the burrito was real tasty and the cheese quesadilla was awesome!  Needless, to say I'm the one telling the story - wink!  

Service is real relaxed and inviting.  I think the owners of the place worked hard to get this place up and running.  Their welcoming and position attitude is much appreciated! - Enjoy!

I was really looking forward to eating here due to the recommendation of a coworker who knows what's up. Unfortunately I'm going to have to give it a 3 star "meh"...for now. 

The place is like a mom-n-pop Chipotle; you choose your meat and they build a taco/burrito etc. to your liking with their fixings. I had a carne asada burrito, it was tasty but it was cold. I've experienced this same problem at Chipotle and I assume it's due to the misuse of their steam tables. The chips and salsa that are included with each order were very good, and so are the prices and their service. The place is new, so I'll have to give this place another go and see if they've got some of the kinks worked out.

I will never go to another Bertos brothers establishment again for a breakfast burrito. These are fresh made and not greasy at all! Plus they let you pick more than one meat, my husband's favorite combo is bacon and chorizo. I'd like to try their other menu items but the breakfast burrito is so darn delicious!

When I am being lazy and don't really care about what I am shoving down my gullet I head down to the local super market and grab the following: Pork butt ( I then boil it in unseasoned water), canned black beans, clearance special leaf lettuce, store brand artificial cheese, roma tomatoes, and rice-a-roni  spanish rice, as well as some off-brand chips.... and some tomato sauce.
I get home have a few beers, cook the pork for 5 hours in boiling water, and then I throw all of the listed ingredients in a bowl and chow down.... at this point not caring about flavor, seasoning, or overall enjoyment from the meal other than to just plain eat.

If you like to get this type of food fast and from a restaurant! Go to Jester's. They are really killing it. Ragu based 'hot sauce', and the food city label to match. Do yourselves a favor and start buying your pork cooked at Food City, it will be a exponential improvement. 

I am pretty sure that when the statistics come out concerning restaurants and their 90% failure rate..... Jester's is the type of place they are talking about.

Start over. 

Seriously fellas...... Better get back to the drawing board.... People do not want what they can make themselves! That is the whole point of going out to eat... Set yourselves apart by doing something different and have someone to come in there to show you some good recipes. Would hate to see you fail but with this type of food, in this area, doom is in your near future if you dont get it together!

Love,
Concerned Local Citizen and Mexican Food Connoisseur.

Yay, I'm a fan. I'm a sucker for carnitas tacos and I sure did enjoy their tacos. The owner and staff are friendly and will customize your dish. I asked for Jalapenos for my taco and had about 10 Jalapenos put on to each of my tacos. A skosh too many but I turned the proverbial lemon into lemonade when I scouped up my Jalpenos with the nacho chips to give a little kick to the chips. The prices are reasonable and the seating is plentiful and inviting, they even have TV'S.

This place is average at best. Very friendly atmosphere and very friendly staff make up for the lack of imagination when it comes to the food. Like another reviewer stated this is a spin off of chipotle. Being from Texas I am a Mexican food snob and this place does not hold up. I would come here if I were in the area but it's not good enough to make a trip especially for here. In the end, it will make a turd.
Great food, great service, great prices! Recipe for success.

Vibrantly painted walls with circus patterns and jester hats & faces greet you at Jester's, along with a friendly welcome from the gentlemen running the show behind the counter. 

(NOTE: If you have an evil clown phobia, one of the paintings may be borderline, but just remember these are jesters, not clowns. Clowns are sad men who pretend to be happy in order to make you laugh because you feel sorry for them. Pitiful.
Jesters performed out of fear for their life, though. They weren't pretending, it was genuine and real. So real that if they weren't any good....KCHXXXSZ   "OFF WITH HIS HEAD! That's Brave. Big difference.)

You'll find a small but solid assortment of fixin's for your fully customized burrito, tacos, enchiladas, taco salad, or whatever you'd like to make from the ingredients they have, apparently!
In burrito form, both the chunked chicken and shredded carnitas pork were quite good. The meat is grilled fresh and simply seasoned, giving folks a chance to add heat from outside sources as desired. Considering the demographic of far north phoenix that Jester's serves, this is a much better idea than serving meat that is overspiced from the start. 

The mild fire roasted salsa was also quite mild. ( a hotter version is offered, no worries ) When i mentioned to my brother that it's flavor remined me in some way of a batch of salsa that i tried to make myself once, he asked "is that a good or a bad thing?" 
Well, it's not a bad thing, but although i rather enjoyed it's tasty flavor -- which tasted to me as if it may have red pepper pureed into it somehow, but i could be wrong -- i will say that this mild salsa's flavorful, interesting taste is different enough from what most people are used to that it may get some criticism for that. i enjoyed it.  I didn't taste the hotter red version this time, but their Verde tomatillo salsa was absolutely delicious - tangy with a roasted mild kick to it. 

I will enjoy trying some other menu items at Jester's. Carnitas tacos sounds like a good short term goal. I believe I will achieve it. I was trying to bring a tie back to the jester story here, but saying that i'd come back out of bravery or out of fear for my life, as opposed to pity, would seriously convey the entirely wrong idea! 

Go to Jesters, like i will go back, because of the good food and friendly service. No better reason needed. At the risk of getting my head cuttoff by the king, that's no joke. 
~*KCHXXXSZ *~

Went here last week with a co worker and this was really good! Like other users have posted it's a mom and pop Chipotle, but better. I had a chicken burrito with sour cream, guac, chicken, rice, pinto beans and the mild salsa on the side. The chicken was very tender and had a great flavor. The staff and owner were very friendly and very helpful in explaining the pricing, combo's, etc. Will be back again very soon.
Nice, quick, assembly-line style Mexican grill (like chipotle and qdoba). I hope this place stays open because it's great having casual quick food so close other than subway.

In Fear of new Mexican places and running to the bathroom 30-45 minutes after a Meal, I was hesitant to try out Jesters,, I was driving by and thought a "GOOD" chicken Quesadilla would suffice for lunch... 

On Entry, this place is immaculately CLEAN, seriously.. Nice Job. I arrived a tad early, 10:40 as they were still setting up for the day. 

When I Ordered, I was told the chicken wasn't ready yet, but other options available,, grr, but then one option was Red Chili Beef... Hmm, ok, since the Tamales i got on Christmas SUCKED, I could use a good fix of Red Chili Meat... SO got that to go.. 

Red Chili Beef Quesadilla. Preparation, consistent as they prepare in front of you, Flavors on the meat, Juicy, Tender, n flavorful.. Wow,, don't think I will EVER get the chicken version again.. The guy running the show was VERY courteous, and polite. 

Will be back there SOON to try more options,, Great first impression guys !!

FYI: 45 min later, no urge to run to the nearest bathroom... A++

This "restaurant" is, quite possibly, the worst place I have ever eaten - and I've traveled through Arkansas, so that's saying something.  

The waitress was only mildly interested in being there, and our dining experience only went downhill from there.  The food was among the most mediocre I have ever eaten.  The BBQ sliders (dry pork with a drop or two of sauce and some cole slaw) I got for an appetizer were barely appetizing.  My entree was an 8-oz sirloin (because, at 6:00 on a Tuesday, they were out of the only other cut of steak on the menu), which was completely without flavor.  Ordered with grilled onions, it arrived with mushrooms on it, and when I sent it back for grilled onions, it came out covered in raw onions that had been dropped on the grill for less than 10 seconds.  The accompanying beer-battered onion rings were uninspiring, as were the steak fries. 

And the atmosphere - it is very hard to describe.  The decor is ambitious and has some potential - but it needs people to liven it up.  It won't, however, get people with the lackluster food and service.  Generally, the place seemed like an old adult book store where someone decided to serve food.

Man, this place sucks. The service was awful. The server forgot my husband's drink. The food took a long time to come out. We ordered cheese sticks for $7.49, it came with only 5 cheese sticks. They charged us .50 cents for ranch even though it says on the menu that the cheese sticks come with ranch. Our server disappeared halfway through our dinner. Just as bad experience all together. Its a convenient place because its connected to the Best Western, but its overpriced. Avoid Hoot & Howl.
This place is bad all around, the food, the drinks, and the service. I saw the bartender go outside and smoke and make out with some guy and then come in without washing hands. Majorly gross!!

I love this place. I live in San Diego, but have to visit about once a year to deal with my rental properties,,,,,,,after driving around looking for a non chain dive bar, I spotted this place......it's more like a sports bar, micro brews,,,,,tv's and the food is pretty darn good.  Makes dealing with rentals almost something to look forward to. I don't classify it as a dive bar though,,,don't think that.....it's nice.

Don't even know where to start... I went here with my girlfriend, her sister and bother in law for a drink and food. We order our drinks and was told that one of the drinks the keg needed to be changed so it would be about 5 minutes. Which was fine.. The waitress then came back and took our order. She repeated it back to us which was correct.. I finished my drink and was ready for a refill, but the waitress is no where to be found. 20 minutes later she returns with our food which was WRONG she brings fish instead of chicken, onion rings instead of fries.. Hard to believe.. Mined you that we are still waiting on one drink (and a refill) my girlfriends sister asked about the hold up on her drink. Was told its out still waiting for the keg to get changed. We asked to speak with the manager. When the manager arrives shes rude. Doesnt even listen to whats being told to her she just keeps saying sorry. She then says can I bring you a different drink because I dont have time to hear this. At this point we say no just bring the check.. Now get this the order is ALL correct here they even charged us for the beer that was never brought out. We get up take the check over to the manager and tell her she says oh fixes it and says heres the new total. No discount, no apologie, no nothing. We paid and left. The girls were heated, furious. The sister went next door and asked for the person above the bartenders/manager. She had to write the complaint down because she was told he'll return on Tuesday.Shes still waiting a call 15 days later. I will NEVER go back

Hidden Treasure!  Fun atmosphere and huge menu.  There are different rooms that have themes like movies, music, and sports.  There is this really cool room that is kind of set up like a living room with a huge big screen.  The bugers and hot wings are the best.  They even have a Hot Wing challenge that I am considering.  They have their own signature microbrew - Hoot &  Howl Ale, which is fantastic.  Great spot for Happy Hour & Dinner.

This was my first and last time there. The service was horrible and no one knew how to make a mixed drink.. They had to look up recipes and to add to that, they were out of most everything, including most alcohol. When ordering food, they were out of mushrooms, onion rings... And my chicken tasted like it was cooked the day prior.

This review is for the drinkers!

If it wasn't for the $1 beers after 10pm I wouldn't be as big of a fan I must admit. Cheap drinks is always a huge plus for any bar for me. Sometimes you just want to go out and drink than to stay home and drink. This is the place for me when there's nothing else to do!  The bartender is a cool girl. Cute too. The place is pretty laid back so don't expect a club type bar, or to pick up chicks. My friends and I always seem to be the loudest but everyone seems to be cool with us, so don't be put off by the laid back feel. My drinker friends who like the mixed drinks say they are generous when it comes to the alcohol in the drink. ( That means "Damn that's good!" ) I've never tried the food. So I can't say much about that.
This place is ok.  The bartenders are friendly and the beer is cold.  The food is average at best.  It could really use some updating inside.

More bar than restaurant. The food is what you would expect from a bar. They have a dartboard. They have their own draft called hoot - available by pitcher. Interesting decor - movies, sports, etc. Excellent, friendly service.

The place was pretty empty.  Service was friendly.  I ordered a French Dip.  awful awful awful   The dip-I have no clue what it was.  Something was on the bottom and it was clear on top.  It tasted like water that had coloring in it.  The nasty "swiss cheese?"  I can assure you that it was not Swiss cheese.  pretty lousy

Hoot & Howl is an excellent / yet average place.  
This is NASCAR country!

Love the atmosphere.   We (the Sales & Marketing Staff from PIR and a few others) used to go every year to watch the Gatorade Duels (the qualifying race for the Daytona 500).

The top brass would be in Daytona for the race...   so we would head out and watch the races at Hoot & Howl.    They have  a cool room that looks like a living room.  Couch, chairs, TV & fireplace (I think)...   cool place to hang out.

Worth a try... go with some friends, you'll like it.

Tokyo Suishi is a nicely decorated restaurant. It has been closed for a long time, but recently reopened. It is a family run restaurant.

I ordered the yakitori chicken and the salmon dinner. I thought that the restaurant was an average Japanese restaurant. The yakitori chicken was very good, but too much sauce. The salmon came on a sizzling hot plate which was unexpected. It was very good.

Would I go back? The food was good, but rather expensive.

It may not be the cheapest sushi joint but I found I was paying just a little extra for some of the finest sushi I have ever tasted. That, and the chef and waitstaff were superfriendly and efficient.. Definitely worth a look.
Not the prettiest of places however it serves the best sushi I have ever had. Try the Spicy tuna crunch!

* Review is based on my take out experience and food only *

We planned a Japanese Lunch Party at work on Friday. In order to avoid confusion/mix-ups with the 'who ordered what' and 'you pay $5.83 and I pay 8.25,' we decided to order platters. I gave Tokyo Sushi the number of people, what we wanted, and a price - TS made it happen. I asked for everything to be ready by noon and it was. The food wasn't out of this world, but it also wasn't narsty.

Very accommodating place, I would definitely recommend this place if you want to order for a group.
The restaurant is kind of outdated but very good fresh sushi. The owners are very nice and generous for take out-ers. There are lots of regular and return customers.

Unbelievable find at the Las Vegas-NORTH food court. I always get my Subway, but decided to go a different route that day. To my surprise, this Las Vegas Great Steak & Potato was pretty good and super bang for the buck. I never really seen a Great Steak & Potato serve such a big sandwich. So, a LARGE great steak sandwich is $10, but it is like more than a foot long. So if you are resting your foot from a marathon day of shopping at the Las Vegas-NORTH outlet, you can re-energize with a LARGE great steak sandwich and order of fries. If you need more flavoring, you can sprinkle their extra seasoning.
Got a cheesesteak and regretted it immediately. The meat is tasteless and floppy. At least I didn't get sick!
Worst food ever! OMG can't imagine how bad it is. And overpriced AF! Omg this food doesn't worth a penny
Over 17.00 for a sandwich, and an order of fries. You tell me?? I mean, if Im going to pay that much, might as well head over to a dennys, or a sit down restuarant. It will probably be cheaper.
Bad service with very bad attitude. We don't own anything don't give me a strange look.

Excellent experience! We did the HHH Open bar, just at sunset , definitely breath taking view as you could still make out the various land marks & the vibrant city lights. Our bartender was extremely attentive & generous with the alcohol.

This is pretty similar to the London Eye in London (not that I've ever been but I've seen pictures).  We got the livingsocial deal so we got happy hour included for a pretty good price!  Its not that hard to find, you have to walk through the Linq Promenade (similar to 3rd street promenade in santa monica) and at the end you see this humongous wheel.  You can't miss it!  There's also "secret parking" behind the wheel.  

There were really no lines so we got through pretty quickly and were ready to board.  We boarded with about 6-7 other people.  Our bartender was awesome and made drinks so quick.  Since its happy hour and open bar, you get to drink all you can.  I was able to get in about 7-8 drinks in before our 30 minute tour was over.  The views are beautiful and great!  You get to be on top of Vegas!  The wheel goes fairly slow so take your time and enjoy the view with that special someone.  Drink up!

Don't pay full price. 

Check groupon, living social or travel zoo for deals. I lucked out and travelzoo had a cyber Monday special, and we got the nighttime happy hour for $18, normally $45 which is a 1/2 hour ride plus an open bar.

Drinks were not watered dow, as Stephen found out.  They had "almost" everything from beer to any mixed drink you want, and, of course pepsi products.  They did not have water, though, which was odd.

The ride was nice, but not worth full price.  I also dinged them for not cleaning up the mess made by the prior ride.  Someone spilled their drink and left a soppy mess and a wet rag on the seat.  The staff took the rag, but never cleaned up the mess.

I don't know if they couldn't see the mess (the capsule is dark) but it was clear there was a puddle on the bench.  I had to ask for the bartender to give me a stack of paper towels to wipe it down.
Greatest thing on The Strip. 550ft worth of greatness. It was worth 20 dollars. Tip: Buy your ticket on The Linq's website. Its cheaper right now.

I went on LINQ website and bought tickets for general admission for 2 in advance.
So I seen on Groupon the prices and I compared to the general admission. The general admission is best value at night is beautiful. We bought our drink LINQ bar before boarding. I suggest don't go for the open bar deal because it not worth it & as a30min ride was just enough time to enjoy and I didn't even finish my drink because I was too busy taking pictures and video and embracing the scene.
I would love to go on high Roller again my next visit.

The High Roller experience was amazing from mechanical to the view. 

What was really dissapointing was how rude the attendants were. Getting on they were fine, just like any ride being rushed to get in. Yet, there was no hurry keep in mind there was NO ONE. Me and my girlfriend went around 1 in the morning. The part that bothered me the most is my girlfriend had been drinking and I was sober. As we were getting if the sphere I was trying to figure out how to get her out safe she had pretty high heels and her balance was not all there. I was waiting for what it seemed to be the drop off point were there is carpet so she would not slip as she was getting out. A male attendant told us to get off when I hasitated and told him I was waiting for the carpet he raised his town and restated what he said with a firm voice Step Out now, then as I waited a little more less then a second he repeated come on out. It seemed he had no concern of what was going on. I get by the time we were done it was pretty much closing time, let me tell you if she would have fallen and trip or something happened he would have stayed there longer than 2 am... I work at a theme park as a general supervisor and I tell all my associates safety and costumer satisfaction is always the key. Seems like The famous "HIGH ROLLER" hasnt figured out costumer service and havent been trained of safety regulations.

other than that the view is amazing. but the reason its always so empty might be because of the bad attitude of the employees...

Jorge Mejia
mejij304@gmail.com

Considering the amount of money they spent on the ride, I was not as thrilled as I thought I would be however it is a good time and a must see for tourists.

The view to the north and north west is great, unobstructed, but with almost nothing to see.  The view to the west, sw, s, and se is partially obstructed by casinos and hotels leaving you with only a partial view.  A few feet higher would have made a big difference.  At the peak, you can see the bellagio fountain show which is really the highlight.  At night, the lights really make a difference and it is a much better experience.

The video is annoying and if the writer and the comedian/host ever gets another job I would be surprised.  There is almost nothing informative about the video nor is it remotely entertaining.  Even the quiz questions are too simple and at least one is a blatant plug for the Yardhouse.

The pricing is not bad, $19.99 during the day and $39.99 at night with $5.00 discounts to locals.  This summer locals were 1/2 off on Tuesdays, not sure if it is still going.

Helpful tip 1-if you prebook a time, book the daytime price but book your time at 6:45.  The daytime price for prebookings goes until 7 but if you show up after 6 without pre-booking you pay the full price.

Helpful tip 2 - the groupon and living social deals are deceiving.  They claim $20.00 for day or night but when you go to pay, the price jumps up to $34.99 for nighttime which is the same price you pay if you are local.

Helpful tip 3 - kids under 12 are free.

As is the norm in Vegas, you will have your photo taken and then they will try to gouge you if you buy the photo.  Those prices are way out of line.  Something I never understood, why charge a price most people won't pay when instead you can charge something more reasonable and make more money overall. (For those who can't do simple mathematics and economics if you charge 30 dollars and sell 100 you make $3000.  If you charge 20 dollars and sell 200 you make $4000.  

Anyway, If you are visiting, definitely do it.  If you are local, take advantage of the deals when you have friends in town.

I would say it makes for a romantic date but that is only if you manage to get a car to yourself.  When there are 20+ others, including people drunk and getting sick, it isn't very romantic.

I have been on the High Roller twice now.  Once with a friend at night and once during the day with my husband.  

Got lucky both times, they were not crowded.

Going at night is a treat.   Seeing the lights of Vegas is always beautiful against the black backdrop of the desert.  The only bad thing is that the observation wheel is behind a lot of the casinos, so you can't see all the way down the strip.

I also enjoyed seeing the view during the day. Las Vegas is in a valley and on a clear day you can see the beautiful red rock formations around the city.  We were also fortunate to catch the sunset.

The ride takes about 30 minutes, but that is long enough.  They have a pod with an open bar that you can pay extra for, but you only have thirty minutes to slam them drinks down!  Personally, I am more interested in the view.

The wheel is good to do once or twice, but not habit forming.  I think it is a little pricey, but everything in Las Vegas has gone up.  It is $39 for adults at night and $29 for the day without the bar.  They did have a summer special for locals - Two for One Tuesdays.  Check to see if they are still offering this great savings before you go.

Have fun!

I'm a local, I came here on a Friday night. I've done the helicopter strip tour and that was pretty amazing, I thought this would be a similar experience. I was expecting something breath taking or magical but this was not that. I was super bored in the capsule filled with a handful of drunk people from Ohio whose loud voices were echoing of the super acoustic interior of the capsule. They seemed impressed, I was miserable. I wish this would have had windows or something or some sort of wow factor. It moved so slowly that you almost felt like you were in a hotel room looking out at a view of the strip-not impressed. I wish we would have used the 80bucks towards another helicopter ride.

Save your money go to the stratosphere instead. We had dinner at "top of the world" the view was a million times better. 

Our pod had a group of middle age bachelors screaming and punching their way to the front of the bar to get second and 3rd drinks before we could get our first. 
Not to mention the drinks are horrible!!!! Cheap booze. The pineapple juice was vile!!! It was extremely watered down. This was for my birthday and all of us were very disappointed with it. We had a Groupon and still felt like it was a total waste of money. Save yours and do Paris or the stratosphere.

The newest must-experience in Vegas. What's not to like? Great views and a drink in your hand. It's an affordable, fun way to make a memory in sin city. Just hope you don't get stuck in a pod with a drunkard...or two drunkards making out...or two loud drunkards making out... ;)

While I'm generally loathe to do Ferris wheels, the honeybunny picked up tickets, and I'm glad she did!

Our night-time ride on the High Roller allowed us to see all the landmarks through which we'd walked during our week in Las Vegas. The vantage point at almost 170 m (550 ft) above the ground is really fabulous (over a city of blinky lights).

The half-hour ride was gentle, just the right length, and the floor-to-ceiling windows afforded us the perfect spot for taking pictures. Would do again.

Our friends wanted to try this, and even though I'm terrified of heights I said ok. We paid the extra for the open bar. We got lucky and it was only our party of four and only one other couple. I could see if it was a large group obviously you would have less opportunity to receive drinks and if your short like me less of a view. I think each pod holds 40 people, but I think that would be a tight fit. 

Our bartender was awesome. She was from Rhode Island. Sadly I have forgotten her name...uh we had already been drinking for quite some time before we got on the ride lol. Anyways she was very fast, personable with just the right amount of sass. She made sure everyone got drinks and made us some delicious shots. We enjoyed her company and her skills as a bartender. 

The view was pretty, but we had a great room on the 54th floor and I would say our view was just as good from there. It was worth doing once, but probably not something I would do again. The ride is a total of thirty minutes long. Drink fast to get your money's worth, if your lucky like us with a small party and a great bartender not too hard. A larger party....good luck.

I had high expectations. Next to none we're met. I was expecting a great view but instead all I saw was parking lots and hotels. I thought I was going to see. The cool streets but no. It went higher then I expected,  which was good. I would not go on it again.

We bought the $20 ticket and went on Wednesday December 23rd.  We took the advice of the ticket seller and went at 5pm.  There was no line up, we literally walked onto the 2nd pod, although the entire facility is set up to service long, long, LONG line ups.  Luckily, we just walked on.

So at 5pm it was dusk, the perfect time to go.  We saw so much of the strip - great views.  Entire experience was 30 minutes.  We enjoyed it.  I'm glad we got the $20 tickets - as a Canadian, and with the terrible exchange rate right now, full price tickets would have cost me approx $52 Canadian - and I wouldn't have paid that.

Got the Groupon. 75 bucks for two with 20% off at Brooklynn Bowl two for one drinks at the sky lounge and the all you can drink inside the High Roller itself.  I for one thought the High Roller was great.  I being a Vegas local try to avoid the strip but wanted to check this out.  It was great its a 30 minute ride with awesome views of the strip, the jewel of Southern Nevada.  The pod we was in had a bar and I think the bar tender was on a mission to get people F'd uped.  Now for the tourists that had to just stumble to their hotel rooms good for them. I had to drive home so I had just one Jack and Pepsi (No Coke on this trip).  But It was a good time, LiLMark Highly recomends this activity for all!

Disclaimer: This review is solely for the Open Bar pod.

My boyfriend and I went on the open bar pod and it's wasn't all that great. It was my second time going and my boyfriend's third. For some reason since the last time we'd gone, things have changed with the drinks. They are still unlimited, but barely have any alcohol in them. We both had 7 drinks each and I was barely buzzed when we got off and my boyfriend felt nothing and they don't offer shots of anything anymore. Also, the bartender seemed annoyed, it's advertised like a party pod but she was kind of a buzz kill, asking for tips but making weak drinks. The High Roller itself is pretty cool but if you're looking to get your money's worth of drinks from the open bar, I suggest you save your money.
Great views of the strip, I loved it. But to me overpriced. $34.95 a ticket at night. We did the family pack for $79.95 for 4. We still had a great time.

We went on the High Roller tonight for our date night.   I purchased the tickets on a Groupon deal and we had a great time.  There was no line, we each got a drink, the ride was fun and the view was beautiful.  My husband and I are so fortunate to live here in Las Vegas and have so many fun things to do on a date night.  I would recommend this to locals and visitors alike.  My only tip is to go right before sunset for better pictures.  We went right after sunset and our pictures turned out dark.

had a great time on the high roller. amazing review at night of the LV strip. it's not cheap but lucky for us we got in on comped tickets. worth a try at lease once. i would consider coming back again for it.

I'm not going to tell you the specifications of the High Roller since most reviews already have told you that the 550 foot observation wheel is currently the tallest in the world.
I recommend riding at night versus the day since you really get to see a stunning view of the entire Las Vegas Valley. For the people that love airplanes, at night you can see the landing and take-off patterns into and out of McCarran.

Before going, check if Groupon or Amazon Local has a ticket deal.

Also if you have a Platinum, Diamond, or Seven Stars Total Rewards card, be sure to first stop at the Concierge Desk.  Depending on your card level, you may be entitled to a larger discount or free tickets.

A word of advice for locals:  Present your Nevada ID and you get a $5 discount.

My wonderful last and I did the Groupon 2 for 1 half hour deal on the night ride. It is a fantastic deal for $72 us. You can get a night ride for two people and free drinks for half an hour on board the tallest observation wheel in the world. If you're lucky enough,  you'll have Cheryl as your on board bar tender.  She makes an amazing apex shot for everyone in the cabin and as Vegas goes...tips matter for your drink. Enjoy and have a great time in the world's most visited tourist destination.

OK, so true tourist trap BUT it was a blast and beautiful view.

We did the groupon happy hour and had a fun time. 30 miinute ride + 3 drinks each was fun. 

Would be great with a group. Not sure the drink car is that much of an addition, but did not seem to add much to the already high price.

Pretty neat addition to the Las Vegas strip. The high roller takes you up 550 feet to view the Las Vegas skyline in an air conditioned cabin. Don't worry...there are plenty of places to buy a drink before you go on your 30-minute journey. Each cabin holds about 35-40 people and it costs about $20 during the day and $35 at night.

Don't leave Las Vegas without taking a half-hour spin on the High Roller first. Simply put, there are very few places in the world where you can have this type of experience. It was so nice we did it twice.

I recommend riding at night so you can get a true appreciation of the lights of Las Vegas.
Sights are incredible! Don't forget your camera. Going during the day is cheaper and much less crowded!

Really cool. Definitely worth doing. We had purchased a groupon for the happy half hour and the bartender on the pod was great. We brought our own officiant on with us and got married! The bartender got everyone in the pod a round of shots after we said our 'I do's' and it was really sweet. Very memorable!

I've been on the London Eye so when I heard the High Roller is even taller, I just had to check it out! I was in Vegas with my fam and boyfriend and my boyfriend and I decided to do something "romantic" in Vegas so we set to try this out. It was a Tuesday night so there was no line, but there were quite a lot of people who wanted to go on. It was $37 per person without the bar and we were transported to another room for a photoshoot and a waiting section for our designated bubble. After a couple minutes of waiting, my boyfriend and I along with about 8 other people were moved into our bubble to start our long journey!

Although many people said the whole full circle takes 30 minutes, it seemed a lot shorter for me. The view was lovely and although my boyfriend and I are both scared of heights, we eventually got used to it that we were able to stand up and walk around and take pictures. After we made it back down to civilization, all the guests were able to look at their photoshoot pictures.There were three pictures with different background and they're all $45 including two frames which was a steal! 

I definitely recommend this because it's a very nice attraction and a very eye-opening experience for those who have a phobia of heights!

We LOVED THE HIGH ROLLER! :) I will say if you can - get your tickets on Groupon. We got the AYCD Happy Hour in the Evening - 2 tickets for like $60 (with a 25% off Groupon coupon) which was WAY WORTH IT! I believe it's $52 a person regular price for an evening AYCD HH - so we practically got it buy one get one. 

We decided to do our High Roller ride on Halloween Night around 11PM - there was a decent size line for the non AYCD HH - so between my group of 4 and another group of 3 girls - we were IT for our High Roller ride. I think they usually pack in 40 people usually! So we had a HUGE cabin to just the 7 of us, the bar and our bartender. Our bartender was great too - she was super nice and kept the drinks pouring - in our 30 minute ride, I think i got in at least 7-8 shots and 4-5 drinks - was it worth the money? SURE WAS - did it achieve the goal? SURE DID. We got some great pictures of Vegas at night - and i exited my cabin - drunk - just as i wanted so we could get our night going - and it was the cheapest way to drink and enjoy the party :)

Again - groupon is the best bargain!

PROS : 
clean, air-conditioned cabins
no lines (we went on a Thursday evening)
great views
friendly staff


CONS : 
tickets, drinks and photos are pricey (check Groupon for deals!)
seating is limited
bar area is a bit unorganized 
windows need to be cleaned (inside and out)


OVERALL : 

I'll echo what other reviewers have said, The High Roller is something you go on once just for the experience. I wouldn't go on it again unless the fare was comped. 

The best time to go is sunset/evenings during the weekday. There wasn't a line and the only hold up was the mandatory (very quick!) bag check.  The pods don't stop moving (unless someone in your group/party uses a wheelchair) so you literally will hop on/off - don't worry it goes slow.  If you do happen to fall (eep!), there's a net below to catch you (think of it like a trapeze net at the circus). If you have little kids with you (say 6 and under), please carry or take their hand as you board.

Yes, the views are pretty spectacular at 550 feet. You'll see the lights of the strip on one side and the parking lots/airport/valley/mountains etc. on the other. There are TVs above the pod to keep track of your elevation as well as learn the history of the ride. 

Your experience will highly depend on the other people in your group. If you're lumped in with drunk/obnoxious strangers well, then you're SOL for the next 30 minutes. ;)

Very fun! We had no line, walked right up. Before getting on, they have a nice bar area. Ordered 4 patron margaritas, YUM! Then they take your picture. Afterwards, you get on the ride. It's roughly about 30 mins, slow, steady, and nice view. Plenty of space on there. We went during the day; walked from Caesar Palace. Overall smooth process.

Got a good deal on Living Social.  Night ticket (after 6 pm) is $34.95.  I got in for $20 including free drink.  Much better deal.  Best at night, after sunset, to see all the pretty lights on the strip and the surrounding city.  

Nice upbeat music in the pod.  Pod moves so slowly you don't realize that you are moving and stopping so high up.  Not sure it's worth full price, but you should it is a great view.  

Not good for peeps with fear of heights or claustrophobic.  Pod has windows all around but they can put up to 40 peeps in during peak time.
Fun for family and friends. Recommend sunset as it is especially breathtaking view. Great staff and customer service.

I was really nervous about how I was going to handle riding on the High Roller since I am semi-afraid of heights.  I took advantage of a groupon that also offered open bar and it was great!  Our bartender was super nice and attentive to everyone, there was about 15 of us in the pod and we still had enough space to move around. 

Going up wasn't as terrifying as I had imagined, you can feel the pod moving at the beginning but after a few minutes you really can't tell.   Getting on and off is a little scary because it doesn't stop!  

There is a video playing the whole time that will tell you some information such as where you are at on the wheel and also how high you are currently.  It also has a part about the process that went in to building the High Roller which was pretty interesting.  

Go at night and hopefully you will luck out and catch a glimpse of the Bellagio fountain show!  It was spectacular!

A pricey gimmick, but truly an amazing view. Thankfully I went midweek and it was pretty empty; not sure it would have been as much fun after a long wait pressed in by dozens more people. My biggest criticism is the constant self-promotion and relentless reminders of HOW COOL it was!! It's a Ferris Wheel, guys. I'm not going to buy your overpriced drinks and I don't need the guy on the video screen to keep telling me how awesome it is. But still, that view!

We went Halloween night and we paid extra for it. It was supposed to be zombie themed but the bar tender was not dressed up at all. They pack the carts to the brim so I felt like a sardine. It was hard to get drinks and we were scolded for throwing away our cups after no one told us not to.

Worst experience, only reason I came was to be with my friends we walked up and told them we were all together, as a designated driver I did not purchase a drink also had a minor in the party. When we went to board our group was separated and I spoke to Manager Christina who said she couldn't refund us and our group could not ride together. WORST customer experience!

Great view of Las Vegas, right from the Strip!  And, it pays to be a local - it's literally half-price, I think.  The ride is a half hour long, but it flew by for me.  I enjoyed every second of it!  And, if you get on there late night, you might even get a whole cabin to yourself...

So much fun!!!! We opted for the High Roller Happy Hour, I bought the tickets online for $32. We took the last daytime ride of the day at 5:50 and we got great views of a Vegas sunset. Cheryl was our bartender and she was AWESOME! Very friendly and accommodating. She made a round of shots for everyone in the pod! She made our 30 mins a great experience. Definitely recommend!
I've included the as advertised photo and the as actual photo... we had a great time...

The biggest mistake I made this year. For starters the staff was rude and displayed poor customer service. The ride is mediocre, I would rather buy a timeshare in Louisville, Kentucky that pay to ride the "High Roller" again. Don't do it !!!!!
Awesome this is bad ass .... Phenomenal views !!! Great way to see it all without a helicopter ...... Reasonable price ... !!!

The High Roller doesn't appear to be bigger than the London Eye, and the capsule actually seems to be slightly smaller.  I had a better experience than most (from what I've read in other Yelp reviews), since my family and I rode by ourselves as part of a birthday celebration & surprise gift for my sister-in-law (her Navy husband came just for the week to surprise her & reunited with the family at the High Roller).  Our ride was at 6PM-ish, so I absolutely have to tell people, the view will most likely be more spectacular if you ride during the night.  The tickets aren't cheap, so make sure that you  ride under optimal conditions for your money!

This was a fun experience. It was neat to see the Vegas skyline from this view at night. We went on Saturday after dinner and didn't have to wait. They have a bar before you get on if you choose not to do the booze cart (we did not). I'm glad we didn't because we had more room. The cart was quite roomy and not full at all. We had a dance off on our way down! This is definitely something to do in Vegas at least once!

How anyone could give this less than 5 stars is beyond me. 

We got discounted tickets (discount = $8) at the discount ticket place (but there is an even better deal right now with a check in on Yelp (discount = $10). For a $10 upgrade you get a "bar car" - and well worth it.

We went around 4:30 on a Saturday - which was a perfect time - no line at all. We upgraded (of course) to the "bar car" they added a bar car right at the time we were in line. The 3 of us were in a car with another group of 3. At then of our ride - our car only reloaded with 2 people, so you can get very lucky!!! 

We had the absolute best bartender Francis, and you think if it is all you can drink in 35 mins, how good could it be?...strap on your extra liver folks and don't be a pussy. They have top shelf liquor (about 4 flavors of Skye vodka, a Ketel One, Patron tequila.. plus all the usual suspects...it was impressive!)

Francis was a fast and started us off with raspberry vodka cocktails, he then made everyone their drink of choice, at some point he handed out shots, he was going nuts.  Of course he made $60 in tips for his 35 min ride with us, so the better/faster these guys are the more they make...If a car had 12 or more people it would be more difficult to feel you got your money's worth. These were 35 of my favorite minutes in Las Vegas.  

The views are stunning. One of my friends was a little trepidations, but in the end - she agreed it was fantastic, the cars move so slowly you can barely tell.

Deja in the gift shop hooked us up too...There is some extra deal too, if you spend a certain amount in the gift shop (it was $20 or $30 I think) then you get some super great deal for another ride - I wanna say it was about $12-14 off the regular price for EACH of up to 4 people)

The high roller had great views.  I did the basic package so no booze.  Views from up top were so beautiful.  I would've done 5 stars if I wasn't annoyed by the repeating message on the tvs inside the pod.  I thought they'd play some nice music or something at least.  I went with 3 other people and thought it would just be us in the pod but there were two other people in there.  They were fine and it worked out so they could take our group picture.  I'd definitely recommend this as something to do on Vegas.  Night time is when I went but I'm sure anytime would be good.

Definitely a great experience, try it at night and is awesome the view, 30 minutes and 550ft hight. Also the prices are not bad: adults $37 at night 6pm and over and $27 at day kids under 12 free and also check for promotions; Mother day Was free for Mothers.
I ending paying only $37 at night for my family (4 members) was awesome!!!
Great time!  Go early and get a private trip. 30 minutes with fun music and great views. I'm sure the view at night is awesome.

You pay $35 (on the cheap side) for 30 minutes of open bar and a 30 minute ride. Didn't sound too bad. My dad who is in a wheelchair can't drink due to all of the meds he is on. Yet we still had to pay for the drink package. Because if we didn't we'd have to be in separate balls. So we bought it. Anyways the balls are crowded and loud if you want to see a good view it's nearly impossible because they slam up to 40 people in one of those balls. Plus they did last call which I thought was funny. I managed to get one beer out of the 30 minutes. After all of that we get off and guess what! The bartender called security on us. And by us my mean my 60 year old mom. My 65 year old dad in a wheelchair and my boyfriend. We asked to speak to the manager after because we were offended to say the least. He asked to get my mother free drink but that was about all... Awful customer service.

My partner and I did the High Roller Happy Hour Today and Scored a Private Ride.. Our bartender Phadra was amazing.. She is so nice and sweet. Your can request here and i would definitely recommend doing that...  She is there 5 days a week and totally amazing...

Thanks Phadra for the amazing conversations and great service...

Didn't know about this attraction before we got to Vegas. But walking down the strip we saw this massive wheel, tallest observation wheel in the world. We went at around 12.30 am. We were the only 2 people in our pod which was great, nobody jumping up and down or trying to rock the pod, which honestly I don't think could be rocked. It's the best way to get up over the city and see the lights apart from getting a chopper tour. We paid €50 for both of us which for something so spectacular is very reasonable. If you're in Vegas try it out you won't be disappointed!
What a great view of Vegas. Went during the day and we had our own car.  The ride gave some interesting facts and information through the ride. Would do again and want to try a night view.

This experience is definitely as good as it gets in terms of viewing the strip from above. While the price is a bit high, I do think that the experience is well worth it! The video that plays throughout is entertaining and the employees are good about not filling each pod with too many people at once. 

You are able to request a bar that provides unlimited drinks for your 30 minute ride. Of course, this option is a bit more expensive, but hey, it is what it is. 

The wheel moves very slowly so it's nothing to be afraid of. 

My favorite part was seeing the entire view while the Bellagio water show was going on!

I rode the night happy hour high roller through discount living social tickets. Worth the discount price. Great views for the 30 minute ride and an open bar (not sure how much you can reasonably drink in 30 minutes). The bartender was great and the drinks were great and top shelf. Word to the wise, this thing does not stop so you have to rush on and off. It moves super slow but still...there is a net under it if you fall (not sure how comforting that is). No one fell or almost fell but I took my heels off just in case!

The World's Tallest Ferris Wheel. 550 feet high. How can you not go on it? You can have a full bar in there too!

My initial reaction when I first heard the suggestion to do this, I was a bit skeptical because you're just sitting in a pod going slowly, drinking, and look at panoramic views of Las Vegas. It didn't seem to exciting to me. After a number of days, we decided to it one afternoon, and you know what? I was excited for it!

We did the $37 Happy Half Hour with the free open bar. As we were walking in, it felt like I was walking through the line to go on a ride at Disneyland, perhaps Space Mountain! When we reached outside, it wasn't busy at all. There was an engaged couple in front of us, and that was it. But we waited and watched pod after pod after pod go by. I suppose we were just waiting for the pod with the open bar inside. After around 20 minutes, we were able to hop on. Be careful though because the wheel doesn't stop, but it's slow enough that you shouldn't have a problem. Maybe when you get off after a few drinks. :)

The pod is pretty big, and can probably comfortably fit ten people with the portable bar inside, and uncomfortably twenty. The bar has your bare essentials, so don't expect any expensive stuff. Our bartender was super cool and very friendly, and made our time very enjoyable.

The only downer was the annoying guy speaking on the screen. "Oh, you're at 420 feet right now. You know what that means! .......You're high!" Haha, laaaaame.

Overall, it was a great experience. You are able to sit and relax out of the desert heat inside a cool air conditioned pod for 30 minutes with free drinks while you enjoy a magnificent 360-degree view of Las Vegas. I had a great time with my close friends and the couple that was with us was super cool. Shots all around! :) At only $37, it's a great deal with the free open bar. 4-5 drinks will definitely cost you over $40 elsewhere, and you don't get to ride the World Tallest Ferris Wheel.

I'm definitely coming here next time I visit, and try the nighttime views.

Totally awesome!! 
It takes 30 minutes for one ride and fits a good amount of people. Any spot in the pod is a good view but I prefer the strip view! 
I recommend going at night when the strip is lite up and the lights on the wheel are flashing!

We really enjoyed the experience on the High Roller. The views were spectacular and it was  very hassle free.

We had read that just after sunset was a nice time to schedule the ride so we purchased our tickets on the Vegas.com website for 8 p.m. The confirmation email told us to visit the box office inside the LINQ, which was a little confusing. We weren't sure if that meant the LINQ Hotel (the former Imperial Palace and The Quad) or the LINQ shopping area. We eventually went to the High Roller ticket office and were able to retrieve our actual tickets. 

We reported to the ride at 8:15 p.m. and essentially walked straight through all the way to the loading deck, even though it was prime time. So our total wait was only about five minutes. Our pod/cabin was loaded with about 20-25 people. We staked out the southwest view as we knew that was the best view from the top. Even though we moved around the cabin throughout the ride, we were always able to come back to that spot. The video narration was funny/cute/informative and the views were spectacular.

I feel this will definitely be something we do again especially when we are visiting with people who have never been to Las Vegas.

Had a chance to to ride the High Roller and let me tell you it was awesome!

I am not into heights but this was incredible! Got on around 10 minutes to 9pm and that was just in time to be in the perfect spot to watch the water show at the Bellagio from a great and beautiful view ! Smooth riding and our group had the pod to ourselves !! 

This was an amazing experience and would recommend to anyone and everyone!! Perfect to hit Mid week ( less crowded) and pick a time at night to take in the lights of Las Vegas !!!

This was so much fun! I don't know if I would recommend for couples but definitely for groups of friends. If there's not too big of a line you can request your own pod. The pods come equipped with ac, tv and radio. For an extra 5.00 per person you can get a bartender with drinks! The ride takes 30 mins. I loved it

Get the groupon deal and you got yourself a great time for a great price. The high roller gives you a great view of Vegas (on one side) and you get to have that amazing view some decent drinks. Its a lot of fun with friends and you do get to a see a different view of vegas. It is a quick 30 min ride but make it worth your while! Drink and enjoy. Fun experience and would recommend to those who are on the fence about it.

An iconic ferris wheel connected to the LinQ Hotel where we stayed at. We bought our tickets for the High Roller for a weekday night. Tickets are around $25 USD but you save about $5 if you buy it at a  Tickets and More kiosks. The Higher Roller is at the end of the LinQ Promenade and is lit up at night which is quite nice. It wasn't busy when we went as it was closer to around 11PM. We arrived to get scanned in and they do a quick security search. We brought own alcoholic drinks in which is allowed but they do have their own bar on the 2nd floor. The ride is about 30 minutes and is 1 full circle around as it goes very slowly. When you reach the top, it's quite the nice top view of the entire Vegas strip and you can see for quite the distance. We took quite a bit of pictures, selfies and even sang some karaoke along with the music being played inside. There is also a voice recorded audio person who gives you some history about the High Roller and about Las Vegas. Overall, it was a great experience and the view is quite nice. Highly recommend it!!

It is receiving a three start only because of bad timing. I recently went to Las Vegas and took my Mom for Mother's Day. For Mother's Day I bought her a night time 30 minute helicopter ride of the strip. it was wonderful and because I was spending over $100 I got the Highest Roller passes for free as part of the promotion. 
We did the helicopter ride in the evening (when it was dark) and then did the Big Roller during the day so that we can see Vegas at night and during the day from up high. It was good to see both. Therefore, if you can I would recommend the helicopter ride better but I realize not everyone can so in that case I highly recommend the High Roller :)
We really enjoyed our trip to Las Vegas. This was an amazing experience. Wish we had an opportunity to try this out at night.
