I'm glad I had the chance to ride the High Roller, but at $21.95 during the day & $36.95 at night, I find it to be too pricey for just a souped up ferris wheel.  I recommend the High Roller as something to take a pic of from a distance, with or w/o selfie.

BTW, I have a free ticket voucher for the High Roller, which expires Dec. 30, 2014.  If you're interested, I'll trade it for dinner ;)

Price with $5 off discount coupon given to me from the Flamingo hotel was $24.99, which the staff applied to my entire group, although it said one per customer, she didn't care! :) And we got there right as the prices changed from the Day admission to Night and she still gave us the day admission fare.

The views are amazing, even for someone like me who has a fear of heights.  The total time we were on the ride was about 33 mins.

My group had gotten a drink from the bar before heading up.  They do offer a HH deal that has a bartender in the Pod, but for the price and the time spent on the ride, I don't think it's a good deal, unless you are slamming the drinks down or just taking shots.

Those who haven't been on it, try it and then you can say you've done it.

I feel that certain things that Vegas offers have to be measured by the fact they're built for tourists, not locals. What I mean is that certain things will be pricier than they ought to be, more ostentatious than necessary, and there will be an overbearing need to deliver an amazing experience. Based on that, yeah, the High Roller delivers. 

We got tickets through one of those deal websites. I believe we paid like $60, which included two tickets, a Buy 1 Get 1 Free drink, and like a free photo thing (all of which was clearly advertised on the site and explained by the concierge). Yeah, the drinks were weaker than I'd like and served in smaller cups, but it's Vegas. The line to get into the place takes you through a number of rooms, kind of like when you're in line for a ride at Disneyland and you go from one room to next. At no point did we have to wait too long in line as it moves at a pretty good pace (more on this later). 

Once you're up near the pod and getting ready to board, they have two queues for going up. The pods themselves are always in motion; the pods do not stop for loading or offloading people. That, I thought, was pretty clever for keeping the line going as well as delivering a seamless experience once you're in the pod. The first few minutes of being in the pod you're gaining altitude. You don't have any cool views for the first bit, but then it gets awesome. After about 5 minutes, the photo ops do not stop. I took some awesome shots of the Bellagio fountains, the Vegas valley, and the greater Strip area. Also, the pods are pretty big. I mean, it doesn't feel cramped at all. There were a few minutes where you had to wait for people to finish taking their selfies with a nice backdrop, but other than that? Not an issue. Once you get to the apex of the ride at 550 feet, you get amazing shots. I really regret not taking my DSLR. 

Overall, the ride was amazing. The service was really good throughout, and really delivered what I feel ought to be Vegas-level quality. Is it pricey? Yeah, absolutely. But it's Vegas and you pay a premium for that kind of stuff. If you're a tourist, it's not a bad bet. If you're a local, keep in mind they sometimes have locals-only deals so I'd be on the lookout for one of those.

Great views and a full wet bar inside a monster ferris wheel. What's not to like?

We had a dozen people, not counting the bar tender and his bar, inside our capsule and had some great views while conversing and having a couple of drinks. Great idea for a networking activity and a great time by all who attended.

We had a nice view on a beautiful, clear night on the High Roller.  

Problems:
1) Drunk guy in our pod hogging the front part of the window and belittling his wife  (They probably should not be pushing the alcohol prior to the 30-minute ride)

2) $2 service fee per ticket purchased at the official ticket box office (that's a first for me, I usually buy tickets directly at a venue to AVOID ticket fees)

3) $70 for two people (A bit steep)

4) Oh yeah.... super confusing figuring out how to get there by car (no GPS updates yet for the reconfiguration) and only a small sign on Las Vegas Blvd.  Accidentally turned right instead of left near the wheel and ended up in the Quad lot instead of the Linq lot)

Next time, I will wait to go around closing and hope for a pod that is more empty.

P.S.  You can use Quick Rewards/comps if you have them on your Total Rewards card to pay for the High Roller.

This is a really fun activity to do with your friends when you are just out and about and want to have drinks with a view. 

Preface - I am a bit afraid of heights but this place wasn't intimidating. It has glass sides but the floor is solid. Also, the pods move really slowly and smoothly. So if you are a height-fearing individual, don't rule this out!

My friend brought our group here during my bachelorette week-end. She was able to get a happy-hour deal. I don't know the exact pricing but the admission definitely pays for itself if you plan on having a couple drinks. 

Here's the scoop:
You arrive, go through the line to be admitted inside, and then your group is loaded onto round glass pods which have a couple benches and a mini bar on wheels inside. Each pod fits about 10-15 people comfortably. The ride is 30 minutes during which you are able to drink at the open bar. 

Our waitress was funny and entertaining. She poured stiff drinks. Obviously don't expect top shelf stuff, but they have all the standard well liquors and mixers. I don't suggest getting wasted in a span of half-hour but you can definitely get a nice buzz and head off to your next destination.

PRO TIP:
We came here during the day and there was no wait at all. I would recommend trying this place after dark for a better view although I imagine it will be more crowded as well. 

Buy your tickets ahead of time and get deals/avoid lines!

If you are looking to bring your fun to a screeching halt then go get on the high roller. I can only hope the pods with alcohol are a lot more fun. We waited in line on a Saturday night and got in the pod with 15 other people. Going up and coming down most of your view is blocked by the building around you. After about 10 min everyone was sitting and yawning. They try to entertain you with a video of a guy making funny comments but it's not enough. Once you get to the top and look around you realize your only halfway home. I haven't done the happy hour pod but I recommend that over a standard one.

Buy your tickets before you go during the day or you'll be in line forever. The two ladies at the counter clearly we not people persons & were pretty rude to where we almost didn't go. 

Once getting on we enjoyed the sites & views of vegas. The seating is minimal and the guy on the video playing overhead can get annoying but otherwise again a great experience
Not worth the price. But if u will get free tickets go try it for once or twice ( day time and night time)
This is a great idea for anyone coming to las Vegas! We bought our tickets online and it was well worth the money to ride at night!! It's a 30 min ride, our pod was not full which I loved!

Amazing fun!  Best at night.  We walked right on and only had six in our pod. Don't think I would like the happy hour ride.  Might be way too distracting.  I wanted to do this sober and aware.  Cannot wait to go again when I come back in April!

Holy booze, batman! The Happy Hour is an incredible deal. We rode with a great group of people at 630pm and we had about six drinks each in the 30 minutes we were in there. They were ready to party. Views are great, especially as the sun is setting and it wasn't busy at all. It was a great way to start the night, and eventually I might remember how we spent the rest of the evening.

The high roller was really neat. Not sure it's worth the high price though. We got free tickets but probably wouldn't of done it otherwise. The pods are way bigger than I expected and the views are amazing. We did it at night but I think right around sunset time would be perfect- that way you still get to see the mountains in the distance and the lights of the city. Ride was exactly 30 minutes long.

If you come to Vegas this is one thing you must experience! I'm not a big fan of heights but doing this helps a lot. Plus, liquor is involved lol. To begin with I found it very cool that you have to actually hop onto this ride as it's moving and then the whole time while your in there (if you purchase a certain package I believe) you get to drink as much as you want the whole time. If I remember correctly the ride is about 30 minutes or a little less and the waiter I had was a very very very good host (Older Gentleman; forgot his name) but he was very welcoming and when we got to the exact top of the ride we took shots to celebrate it. This is a must for Every Vegas trip. I can't say that enough.

The High Roller offers a 30 minute ride on pod that circles high over the strip. This activity offers something that is fun for all ages during both the day time and night time. I recommend going during the day because it's cheaper and if you're lucky you'll get your own "pod" with your own party. If you're older and without children they also offer pods that have a bar inside. The High Roller is definitely something that you should do at least once while in Vegas and feel like doing something touristy.
Fun thing to do first thing in morning before it gets super crowded at night. Entire spin is 30 minutes. Reasonably priced. Great views  all around.

Dang! Tons of people have reviewed this hot new attraction since I went on it at the beginning of the year.

Though much has been said, we enjoyed the High Roller experience for what it is. As an observatory wheel, it offers a great view of the Vegas skyline since it's pretty much located above mid-Strip. If you're not getting to it by walking along Las Vegas Blvd, there is a large surface lot behind it to park at. As long as you follow signs or ask people, you'll find where to go.

We were here on a weeknight so there were absolutely no lines.The online coupon deal was a sweet value for two, especially since we used it for the Happy Hour pod. Though it was "open bar," 30 minutes passed by really quickly on the whole ride so each of the 8 or so people got an average of 2 drinks. Drink selection was fine and the bartender was cool. She made everyone Gummy Bear shots to toast together when we reached the peak (which is actually pretty anti-climactic and accompanied by a video narration on overhead screens). Interestingly, to keep with the flow of the videos and time limit in the pods, the wheel doesn't stop so you have to get on and off while it's moving.

The view itself is nice. It was past sunset so naturally the best time to see the sparkling lights and take night photos. If I had to pay full price to go again, I'd probably skip it, but the High Roller is a worthy Vegas attraction to go on at least once if you're into that sort of thing.

Do not waste your money!! Only about 5-6 different drinks to choose from which are all disgusting and the "free photo" is not accurate. They take a great group photo of you guys before, and after they already have them printed..that's awesome. As we were all admiring the photo we started walking away and told we had to pay for those. Even with the "free photo" stub that came with the tickets. We handed the photos back and said hope u enjoy the photos of us. Biggest waste of money, so disappointing.

I bought a pair of passes on groupon for the discounted happy hour day package ($66). We bought another ticket for our third friend when we got there, just a few minutes before 5. That one was $38.

The line wasn't too bad and moved really fast.

The happy hour cabin surprised me as being much smaller than I expected. But the bartending did not disappoint. Ours was fast, skilled, and served us any brand of liquor we wanted that she had available. We had a lot of individuals in our cabin, but none of us left without being satisfied with the drink quality or amount.

The ride itself was amazing. A half hour was perfect. It was slow enough to enjoy the view, but fast enough not to get bored. I got some great photos! This is a definite must-do activity for visiting Vegas!

We did a day time open bar trip and it was fantastic! It was only the 4 of us and another couple. Drinks were STRONG and were made fast! This was all of our favorite part of our trip. There wasn't much of a line and it all seemed well organized.

The High Roller, located at The Linq Promenade, is easily one of my favorite attractions in Vegas. You have a Birdseye view of the various hotels located along the Las Vegas Strip. You can also see some residential areas, and a clear view of the Ceasars Palace Coliseum. . 
It's a family friendly activity at a minimal cost. The average cost per persons is $20-25 depending on coupon availability. The ride is a solid 30 mins long with tons of space. If you choose to have a more adult time, you can actually have a small "party" mini bar and bartender included. It's well worth the cost, be it with family, or friends.
This was a fun but peaceful amusement ride. It's a great way to get to the top of the Vegas.

AWESOME! Absolutely awesome!!! We bought the LivingSocial deal for $25 per person that included unlimited bar and drinks. Get that deal while it lasts if you are planning on riding the high Roller. You get in without waiting in line! You get to drink unlimited good drinks (not the cheap stuff) and you get to see an amazing views of Las Vegas and the Strip! In my opinion - go at dusk! You still see the beautiful mountains and the Strip is starting to lighten up. Unbelievable views! Our bartender (I think her name was Amanda) was absolutely great! She gave us great drinks! She told us some history and we had a really good time there! I would recommend this tour to anyone visiting Las Vegas! Enjoy!!!

This is definitely must-do while in Vegas....at least one time in your life. We did the 6 pm happy hour ride and were able to get a killer deal through groupon - ended up about $48 total for the two of us which included an additional groupon email discount offer.

We probably had 15 people plus the bar setup in our pod. It was crowded but manageable for the 30 minute ride.

We had a few issues:
1) there were a few people who clearly just cared about the free drinks. They rushed in front of the bar upon entering the pod and didn't leave the bartender's side. It was a little obnoxious. Realistically you can and should get about two drinks with this many people.
2) the bartender was crabby as hell and acted like he didn't want to be there.
3) very limited selection of drinks. No wine at all. How hard is it to throw a box of wine in there?

The view is amazing - mountains to the east and the strip to the west. It was still daylight (6 pm) so maybe we would do it one more time after sunset. Although, the pod was probably at capacity with the bar, it was still comfortable and there was plenty of airflow. I was afraid it would get hot once we got up higher. Overall, a very enjoyable experience at 550 feet above the strip.

This was a great experience. I am not a big fan of ferris wheels but this one is pretty cool, especially if you do it at night. The whole ride takes about 30 mins and the recorded commentary inside is only slightly annoying. I would def recommend you bring your camera to get some good shots of the city lights.
I had a lot of fun!  We got the group rate and only paid $23 ish each which was nice. I've never been on suuuuucchhhh a big,  colorful ferris wheel before!  :)

Solid 3.5 stars only if you got the good Groupon deal, 2 tickets for $65 plus 2 free drinks if you were as savvy as us to get the free passes from the Quad security as we were asking directions to this 'ferris wheel' lol.  but being dehyrdated for most of the day, we asked for bottled water instead of beer or magaritas, probably a waste, but a bonus that it was Fiji water, hey it's Vegas...and I digress...

Initially not a big thing for me to do since it's such a touristy thing, and seen all the lights at night as they don't really change, but it's a thing to do, and for a 30-minute excursion, it's not going to take a big chunk of my day.

Impressed by how the staff worker just let 6 ppl per booth, to give lots of space and some privacy, even at 11pm at night.  Still quite steady amount of tourists still lining up.

542 feet is the peak, just fyi.

Went here a few weeks back during a time it wasn't busy that me and two other friends got one all to ourselves! So I can't speak for when it's busy and lack of view cause of the crowd you have to barge through, but I loved having the whole thing to ourselves so I recommend going at a time it's less busy unless you don't mind the crowd. The bar before you go on is nice and convenient. Ride last about 35 minutes and you see every angle of Vegas, also tv displays. Not much seating, one sofa on either side. Good set up. Took great photos. It's good for what it is. It's for SITE SEEING, not necessarily a party. So know what your paying for before complaining.

Tourist trap YES!  But so worth going.  

Basically it's a huge Ferris wheel on the strip in Vegas.  There's usually a line out the door to get in but it moves quick; we got thru in 10 minutes.  Then up to the bar and bathroom area.  It's a 1/2 hour ride so hitting the head before is a good idea.   They scan your tickets and send you to the next stop.  Yup the photo booth -- every attraction has one.  This one had a fancy green screen.  No more details as I opted out.  

Moving along, you are corralled into groups to await your pod.   Think Jodie Foster in Contact.   You enter a big glass (ok plexi) sphere. There is seating for 8 with lots of room to move around to take photos. The ride moves very very very slowly.  Mellow music plays flying themed tunes.   Monitors detail the climb in elevation.  There is an on-screen host that gives you the rules (don't freak out if the ride stops, no smoking, camera setting for the best shot, etc) and lots of Vegas trivia.   When you hit the highest point of the ride you get the best views -- The Eiffel tower, the fountains at the Bellagio, etc.  Take a night ride, Vegas glows at night!  

Once off the ride, 1st stop is the photo pick up area.  No tourist trap would be complete without the last stop being the gift shop!!!'

It's spendy so check GroupOn for deals.  Total Rewards members also get a discount so if you're a member don't forget to mention it.   There is an open bar option but you will pay more.

I would highly recommend doing this while in Vegas! 

I purchased a Groupon for two for $69 that included all you can drink for 30 minutes during the ride and it also included a multitude of discounts within the shopping area. 

The drinks included top shelf liquor which my friend and I took total advantage of and the drinks alone surpassed the money we spent. 

The topper was the amazing views of Vegas which we had done at night and it looked totally amazing!

The server happened to be from Rhode Island and she had a wonderful personality which also added to the experience.

Highly recommend!!!
Breath taking & a nice 30 minute smooth ride! Definitely recommend this to all & it's cool cuz u can bring a drink on the ride!

The Linq is pretty neat, I had never seen it before.  Note -- to get here, don't exit the monorail at the flaminco like you might imagine.  Instead go up to the next stop actually labeled "Linq"

It was a great trip, perhaps a bit short for the money, but the view was great.  Highly suggested for a touristy thing to do.  It does seem that there are plenty of options to view the vegas sky line, this just being the most interesting I suppose.  If this interests you, also check out the view from voodoo at the rio - they have an outdoor patio on the top of the tower.

This is one of the most enjoyable experiences I've had in Vegas. I was originally discouraged by some of the negative reviews I read on here but after trying it out myself, here are some counterpoints to the haters:

Price - Yes. It is a bit pricey at roughly $36 for one adult for an evening ride. But, every other attraction in Vegas is pricey and if you're here, you were probably planning on gambling or eating expensive food or buying expensive drinks or visiting a club or watching a show at one point. Being in Vegas = money and overpaying for things. Why not save up a little for an unforgettable and unique experience?

The unimpressive views near the bottom - Okay, the views aren't great until you get closer to the top of the wheel. But nothing in life is perfect. The views toward the top are amazing, almost breathtaking. The feeling of being in a glass pod "floating" high above the beautiful lights of Vegas with expansive views in nearly every direction is surreal.  I enjoyed the views and didn't think it needed to be closer to the middle of the strip to be enjoyable. 

"Alternatives" - It's really not the same as going into a high building and looking out the windows. The ascent is kind of thrilling, and again, you're almost getting 360 degree views. The Eiffel Tower experience only lets you see Vegas in a small observation area through a type of fence which makes it really hard to take pictures and is exposed to the weather, and the Stratosphere Tower, though nice, is so high up that everything looks relatively small. The pods of the High Roller are closed, air-conditioned, and offer just the right kind of view near the top.

The staff - I had no problems with the staff.

Helpful hints - 
-Best not to wear high heels or difficult shoes - the wheel doesn't stop and you have to get on and get off as it slowly moves (there's a net underneath to catch people who misstep, but still). 
-Use the restroom before you get on the wheel as it's a 30 minute ride - for what it's worth, I don't think being buzzed or drunk is a requisite to enjoying this experience.
-Go on a weeknight - there was no line on a Monday night and I was able to get on a pod within 20 minutes of buying my ticket, a lot of that time was just spent going through security and making my way through the building up to the wheel pods.

False advertising....drink car is only 5.00 extra but the bartender chose to ignore that option and sell 20.00 drinks.  When pointed out to management we were smugly told they weren't giving any money back and it was our decision to buy the kiosk tickets that had no such option.  Avoid at all costs....waste of money and time!

If Las Vegas is lacking anything, it is amusements. Too much of the entertainment involves drink, gambling and sex. Not that I have anything against any of those. While you can get a gondola with a bar, there are plenty without. No need to walk through a casino to get there. Very family friendly. 

We went at sundown and there was no line. Wonderful views with stupid commentary. Just what you would expect. Parking is free and easy. 

We will likely not go again, but it is a must see for everyone.
Cool views. Moves slowly.  Over priced for what you experience. Open bar would definitely be the way to go.

After years of talking about it, I finally went. Not one for lines or crowds I went in the daytime and glad I did.
I breezed right through. Didn't need to take a pic beforehand that you pay for afterward and wasn't interested in the open bar. 
I was on the pod with only 3 other people which was perfect. The views were nice and the guy in the video you watch was ok. 
Would I come back at night? If the price were less because I know it will be crowded with a lot of people drinking.

I like to call this a party in the sky!!!  I was dancing throughout the whole ride!!  What an exceptional addition to the Strip!!! And ofc, in traditional Vegas custom, this baby is in the record breaking book for tallest ferris wheel in THE WORLD.  It's about a 30 minute ride of fun so you get your money's worth.  I would definitely ride the sky on the High Roller again!!

I think this is a must do while in Vegas and pay the extra to go at night and see all the lights of the city. Best views of the city, right here. Sure, it's on the pricey side, but I compare it to going to the top of the Empire State Building or Rockefeller Center. I recommend purchasing tickets from the High Roller box office themselves. I bought tickets from the LInQ box office and soon found out they charge $3 more per ticket. We did get $5 off per ticket as we showed our ticket stub from a show we saw at the casino a couple days before. But I think we could have done that at the High Roller office too. We had a 12 year old and a 2 year old, which were both free and they thought it was cool. We had 12 people in our pod and we could move around it freely and see views from every angle. I can't imagine more than 20 people in these pods would be comfortable even though it says they hold 40 people.

All you get is to spend a lot of money on an observation pod that rotates for a half hour and gives you a splendid view of the city.  You can get military and senior discounts, and there's typically also a Groupon to help lessen the cost (by a fraction).

There's a cheesy announcer on screen that tells bad jokes and lets you know how far you've gone and how high up you are.  You get spectacular views of the city and a half hour's worth of time to relax and see the sights.  If you get the booze package, you get in a booze pod, and if you don't, you don't.  

For what it is - a one foot per second rotation around a wheel that goes up to 550 feet above the Strip - it's worth it.  If you go in expecting more than that, well then I don't know what to tell you.  You go high in the air and look around.  That's it.

Cool 30 Minute ride!

So we visited this Ferris Wheel type thing soon after it opened on March 31, 2014.  It was still nice and clean, and surprisingly not too long of a line. There is of course an overpriced gift shop for you to visit once you get off the ride. Im pretty sure it is unavoidable, when you get off the ride you have to exit through here. (I could be wrong though)

The ride itself is pretty awesome.  I didnt expect that you could walk around during the ride or at least have the room too.  We had approximately 12-15 people on with us and there were seats and ample space to walk around and see ALL the sights. 

If you arent frightened of heights, go check this out!

I have been excited about the High Roller since the preliminary discussions took place years ago. When ground finally broke, it was exciting driving past the wheel, watching it slowly come together. 

Last night, I finally got to experience it for myself. Walking up to the giant wheel is a beautiful sight! You really get a feel of how huge it is. 

After getting our tickets, we hopped on the elevator and made our way to the deck. I was surprised at how quickly you have to get into the cabin because (as mentioned) the wheel doesn't stop rotating. 

Once you're inside though, you can't really feel the movement, it's very smooth. It didn't feel like a half an hour and it didn't feel like you were that high up. The cabins are very spacious and comfortable. 

The ride was over before we knew it. We made the full rotation, got the pretty views, and rode the largest observation wheel in the world. 

It is what it is, something to do, something to see, and something to check off your bucket-list.

Went on opening day and it was practically empty during the evening.  The cost for an evening pass was around 35$ a person and last about 30 mins. So it's around a $1 a minute.  If you want the best seat  in the place it's on the right just as you walk in.  This will give you the strip view with a view of the nicer part of the strip.  BUT don't camp on that spot and let others in to take pictures.  Just happened to be in Vegas opening day so we gave it a try and if think that'll be the only try they'll get.  Parking was a pain in the ass as well, we parked in the Quad and it's not a hotel I'd ever like visit again.

Easily one of the highlights of my Vegas trip. Beautiful views! They offer cheaper day time rides, but I would say it's worth it to shell out the extra bucks for a sunset/ evening ride - I mean it IS the city of lights, not the city of sunlight (even though there's plenty of that, too!)

My advice would be to skip the "happy hour" ride, and just board your pod with a pre purchased drink from the bar prior to boarding. It's only a thirty minute ride, I just can't imagine you'd get your money's worth for the open bar.

Went on a midweek evening, and didn't have a wait at all. It was myself and five other people in my pod- no shortage of seating or space to wander. The views are out of this world, and it's just cool to say you rode the world's tallest Ferris wheel! I'm not the biggest fan of heights, but this didn't bother me a bit. Would definitely check it out!

This was such a great experience!! Did the open Bar and had a Fantastic Bartender!! Derrick was so awesome!! One of the girls was having a really hard time with the height and he literally talked he through it!! If you're reading this THANK YOU DERRICK!!! Can't wait to do it again!!!

Absolutely, great experience!!!!! We did not take advantage of the $7 off by buying the tickets ahead of time, but it's okay. It was $33/person for half an hour of open bar on Saturday. You purchase the tickets and walk your way to a bar and then up the stairs to the pods. The pods do not stop, so you'll have to get in as it's making its way around. You will be sharing the pod with other groups, which I thought was fun. The bartender is definitely quick and knows how to get the crowd going. She made everyone pink gummy bear shots! We went during the day, but the view is beautiful! I would've given 5 stars as I really enjoyed it! However, the bar was a bit limited. There were only about 5 different liquors. No cognac, and only 1 whiskey: Jack. It still did the job, and we were all tipsy within 30 minutes. Loll .I'd definitely come back here again the next time I'm in Vegas! Very worth the experience!!!
The view is really cool the problem was that we couldn't get on our own "ball" which was awkward with the other people

For those who don't like ferris wheels like me, it's not the same experience at all.  I felt a little nervous at first but that went away quickly and I could focus on the experience.  I went during the week, late morning so had no problem getting on and wasn't crowed.  It was a beautiful day so we had a perfect view.  The only disappointment was the ridiculous cost of the photos you can purchase after.  It was $30 for two and if you only wanted one-same price.  It's too bad they are more interested in gouging tourists.  They could sell more if they would be reasonable.  Or give locals a discount, we bring in business, too.  I realize it is probably outsourced but it's still attached to the High Roller so please take note.

I have to give The Linq's High Roller a 5 Star!  For Mother's Day, mothers go on for FREE, WITH FREE FLOWER,FREE  GLASS OF CHAMPAIGN, AND FREE PHOTO! How many frees?!! 
Lines looked long but moved pretty quickly. Staff were awesome considering some ungrateful FREE costumers. 
Thank you!

This was a cool Las Vegas experience.  First, don't buy tickets at the high roller.  You can save money through either Groupon or on the strip at the Tix4Tonight booth.  We bought tickets at the Tix4Tonight booth and saved a few bucks a ticket.

We went around 3pm on a Saturday and there was no line to buy tickets or redeem vouchers.  There was also no line leading up to the attraction, but the set up reminded me of waiting to ride a rollercoaster.

One thing I liked, they do not overcrowd each pod.  They allow about 10 people in each pod which left a lot of room to move around and the ability to see Vegas and the area from all angles.

The glass was super clean which made taking pictures great and the in-pod video host was entertaining.  The entire ride is 30 min.  We did notice around 4pm there was a line to get into the High Roller, so it's probably busy during sunset.

One of the best experiences of our Vegas trip. And probably one of the best picture taking spots in all of Vegas. My girlfriend got the tickets on Groupon for a night ride that included open bar, which was a little more expensive but definitely worth it. Yes there was an open bar in the carriage for the half our it takes to go around in this enormous Ferris wheel. Our bartender was a great guide, super fun to hang out with throughout the ride, and acted as our personal photographer to capture us with some great views of the city in the background.

The experience was phenomenal.  The views at the high roller are only second to those of the helicopter rides. The price was a bit steep, and  fairly short considering.  If you're planning to do a wedding proposal, this would be a great place to do it you can rent one unit out, or just purchase individual tickets. The ride is about 30 minutes long.
Such a waste of money. You see the not so pretty sight of the strip. Go to the stratosphere instead

High in the sky at 550 feet In the air! Taking a ride on the giant temperature controlled observation wheel with floor to ceiling windows is pricey, but the views of the city are breathtaking.

I bought a Groupon deal for $69 for VIP ride package for 2, plus 2-for-1 souvenir drinks and 15% off 1 regularly priced item or photo in the sky retail shop. The Groupon was a great deal for the ride for 2 and BOGO souvenir drink. We passed on purchasing the souvenir photo since it looked super cheesy and photoshopped.

We tried to get there in time for a sunset ride, but there was a line and also a brief boarding wait, so we missed it. I quickly forgot my disappointment when we saw the glimmering lights of the strip and the city from above. The evening views though! The city lights twinkling at night are gorgeous and give you butterflies in your stomach.

It takes 30 minutes to complete a full revolution during which you get an eagle-eyed view of The Strip and beyond. The strip view was our favorite, but we did also enjoy panoramic views of the rest of the city. If you are a Vegas local, this experience is a perfect way to appreciate the jazzy city and beautiful desert topography you live in. 

Forty people can fit into a single observation pod, but they do a pretty good job of not stuffing the pods so that you have room to comfortably move about the space. On our trip there were less than 15 people in the spacious pod. 

Just remember that ticket prices increase after 7pm (because the views and lights of the city are better at night)

Of course make sure to take lots of pictures, but remember to take the time to be in the moment with your loved ones and enjoy the experience! It's a memorable journey to the top! 

Side note: our TV host (television spokesperson of the ride) was totally corny. Let's just say #90sgameshowhostwannabe. The music selection was mainly top 40's and also very cliche but I suppose it makes the trip a little more lighthearted and eases nerves for people who have the fear of heights.

Daaaang!
This was awesome.

I went during the day, so the tickets were $25 instead of $37 at night.
That was not the reason I went during the day, just how it worked out.  I didn't even think about the fact the cost might be different.

We looked all over for where to buy tickets at first.  There are some kiosk built into the walls nearly underneath the wheel so we waited in line for a minute or two, but the people in front of us took so long, and two of the three kiosk were broken.  So we started walking around and realized the wall the kiosks were built into was that of the building you go into to buy tickets!  Duh.  We actually bought our tickets from inside the gift shop before you go up the escalators to the main entrance.  So there are quite a few spots to get tickets.  Just walk into the building, skip the broken kiosks.

We were able to walk right into line.  There are quite a few turnstiles but they were empty.  Yay for 3pm Saturday random timing.

We were able to get onto a tram with only two other people and avoid the 13 people in a group with fussy kids and strollers.  Thank goodness.

So we hop onto the pod/tram/car whatever it's called and begin our approximately 30 minute round-trip (get it? 'round'...because it's...a circle.  Oh never mind.)

The pod rotates while the wheel goes around so you're always parallel to the ground, and it moves so slowly that the ascension is nearly imperceptible.  very very smooth.  Great A/C, super roomy with tons of windows.  

The views are obviously great, and it was totally worth the cost of admission to take this trip.  I would 100% come back and pay extra to see it at night, that would be a fun sight.

The only bad thing, and it's sort of a big one, is the video monitors they have in the pod has a host who talks to you, describes what you're seeing, how high you are, says stupid trivia, etc.  He is so annoying that it's almost maddening when he won't shut-up.  It's on a programmed loop so you can't interact with or (more importantly) stop it.  We all were complaining about how annoying he was.  I would have preferred subtitles and no audio.  So be prepared for that to be lame, but don't let it stop you from coming here and enjoying this really fun and fascinating ride.

I feel like it is way overpriced. The last time that I took some visitors from out of town, we were surrounded by people who were intoxicated inside the pod that takes you around in the Ferris wheel. Fortunately we were trapped inside there with them for 35 minutes. The music played in the pod is cheesy but the view from the top is really neat. If you do go, make sure to only go during the night.

The 30 minutes definitely goes by faster than you would think! I would definitely recommend doing the unlimited bar option. It's pretty boring without that. I also recommend going with a larger group of friends so that you're not stuck with a bunch of strangers. Find cheaper admission tickets from street vendors versus purchasing at the High Roller Station. It's worth riding during the day, then again at night.

This attraction didn't really live up to the hype for me. I thought it moved a little too slow and the views weren't anything spectacular. Granted, I'm a local and have seen the strip plenty of times. 

Definitely go at night. It's $10 more but it looks a lot prettier!

There are a few places on the strip that are a must do, and I think this should be added to the list.

A bunch of people are complaining about the price, but I think that $35 for a half hour ride around is not that bad of a deal.  I've gone twice now, and with the coupons and locals discounts I've never paid full price.  I've never had to wait either, which is very nice.  I guess it's not great for business that I've never had to wait, but at least I was there!

I would suggest going around sunset so that you get a great view on the way up!

My wife and I purchased tickets for the High Roller at the same time we booked our hotel room at Planet Hollywood. I would avoid this process at all costs. It was very cumbersome to redeem the ticket. People at high roller couldn't find our reservation and PH said that they don't store that info. 

Better to just show up and pay at the box office.

After all that, we had a ball. The entrance to the HR is very elaborate. We went around 11pm on a Thursday night. There was no crowds. We got frozen drinks at the bar and were able to take them in the cabin.

The cabin was ok. The pictures definitely make it seem a lot nicer. We had 16 ppl in our cabin and it felt like it shouldn't have much more than that, since most people were standing with no place to sit. 

Views were incredible. Definitely loved the nighttime views of Vegas. 

I think the HR would be a lot more fun if you could reserve an entire cabin for your party.

This was my first trip in Vegas and the High Roller was a beautiful way to see the views at night. The night tickets are more expensive but so worth it. It's a quick 30 min ride but the views are truly beautiful. We did expect it to be a little but more luxurious inside the Ferris Wheel but it's a pretty quick ride so it's not bad. It doesn't stop completely for passengers to get on/off so you do have to be a little quick getting on/off but it's fairly slow so there is enough time. Don't get any of the fruit slush drinks from the lounge though. We had a group of 7 and no one could drink any of them because it tasted awful.

Beautiful views! This is a must see attraction for all ages when visiting Vegas. The highest point provides a 550 foot photo op from the ground, even higher than the London Eye. I've been on the High Roller twice, but only during the day. A couple during my first ride was lucky enough to score their own personal pod since there weren't any people in line behind them. No problem, there was always enough seating when I went on. The whole ride lasts 30 min and moves slowly even as you get on/off. Despite having some sort of disability, you should be able to enjoy this ride. Talk to an employee for details. 

Each pod holds a max of 40 people but they would never squish that many in there. Temperature controlled meaning it's air conditioned in the summer, and room temp in the winter. They have a "happy half hour" option with an actual bar & bartender inside! Prices vary. There are Groupons sometimes, and online discounts. I bought tickets at the box in front the weekend of Memorial Day and tickets were only $20! 

They'll take your group photo in front of a green screen, check out the backgrounds after the ride.

*There's a bar you can buy drinks at before boarding, feel free to bring it with you. Restrooms are located in this area. 

-Daytime $25 
-Nighttime $35
-Happy Half Hour noon to 1am, starts at $37 with unlimited beer & cocktails, 21+ 

My favorite sight to see is the Bellagio fountains while up in the air. Highly recommended!

The exit leads to the gift shop and photo viewing area.

The high roller is located at the end of the Linq area. You can purchase your tickets at a machine along the way to the High Roller or at the High Roller. It costs $25 per person for a daytime pass and $35 per person for a nighttime pass. I'm not too positive when the nighttime pass is in effect. There is also an option for unlimited alcohol but I don't know the price for that.  There is a bar located before you load the pod if you want to drink alcohol but don't want to do the unlimited alcohol. 

The best viewing place on the pod would be to the right as soon as you get in.  When you're at the top you can see basically the whole strip. If you're on the left side, you see the north side of the strip - Harrahs, Venetian/ Encore. You can walk around the pod, however the first time I rode the High Roller, these people who sat at the "good spot" would not leave and basically would not let people take pictures there. The second time I rode it, only my group (4 people) were in the pod so it was nice.  I don't know if it's not as busy anymore but there was no waiting at all. 

It's a 30 minute ride. There is a video playing in the background with random facts to somewhat keep you entertained. 

They offer to take a picture before you load the pod and you can view and purchase it  in the gift shop when you exit. 

Before or after the High Roller you can grab a bite to eat at the Linq or just walk around. There's a lot going on there. Because there is a lot going on there, the traffic going into the Linq area gets backed up. We had the taxi driver drop us off at Battista's Hole in the Wall restaurant and we walked to the High Roller. 

I wouldn't ride the High Roller everytime I go to Vegas. I rode it the second time because our friend gave us free tickets. It would be nice to go on once so you can get a gorgeous view of the strip.

Did this ride twice. The first time was with family and when they first opened. It was exciting. The pods are huge! We had 8 people in our pod and my son was able to run around and be worn out. The views are spectacular,  but only for about 5 minute when you are at the very top. It was comfortable and entertaining. The total ride was just under an hour. I gave it a 4 star and not a 5 because it's way over priced for what it offered if you didn't go with a local. Even the local price was a bit steep. Great concept,  but if the price was much more reasonable, more people would repeat.

Did the bar car with Amanda. She was amazing. Definitely do the bar car with friends. Use a groupon to save some $$$. Nice views of Vegas. If your lucky the Bellagio fountains look amazing. Thanks Amanda for a great trip!!!

Ok so I have been wanting to ride the High Roller since it was erected.   Actually since I saw the London Eye I was fascinated by it.  So finally on while visiting the bestie dreams  American true!!  I was lucky enough to get a ticket on line for a discounted price.  My friend since she's local also got a discount.  Also I received a pic of the scanable ticket which is way easier for me because I tend to be crazy about losing tickets to anything lol.  I just had to make sure I could find it in my email.  
One of the fun things about getting to the High Roller is that you walk through the shops.  So if you have time you can stop and see what's available.  The awesome thing about going during October was the fun decorations that were there. Krampus and scary clowns oh my!!!   So fun!!!  Also got to see Gordon Ramsay's Fish and Chips!!!  Unfortunately I didn't go. Next time!! You can only do so much in Vegas at once lol.
Upon entry it's easy to maneuver and yes they will check your bags.  No big deal it's a security measure.  I luckily had my ticket sent to my email so the ticket lady just had to scan.  The really fun part was when they take pics of you before you get on with the option to buy later.
The fun part about the ride is you get on with different people so you meet new friends and enjoy an amazing view of the strip.  In the pod we got we met some wonderful older women in Vegas to celebrate a birthday.  We had a blast as they play music in the pods.  Yes we all danced and had an amazing time as we watched the sun set over the Las Vegas Skyline.
We picked the perfect time to go because the ride lasts about 30 minutes so we watched the sun set and the lights of the strip come on.
I highly recommend riding the High Roller at sunset.  The views are spectacular!

Definitely the worst experience ever. The idea of vegas night view is awesome, but being trapped with a bunch of drunk people in a cart is not the best. Beyond that the facility that runs it is poorly organized, basically we feel like we've been chasing around like animals. Will be the last time to be on that thing.

tallest observation wheel in the world!
go at night for the best views and go to Sprinkles afterwards (not before, because you can't take your ice cream on the ride).
30 min full rotation and it's absolutely worth it.  Beats the Strat views by a longshot. 
Full bar available in the pods and can seat up to 40 but 20 is probably all I would suggest in each one. They have an event center as well so they can host large programs (up to 150 or so) and you can rent out the pods for groups. 

Check it out!

When my friends told me about this ferris wheel with an open bar that costs nearly $50 a person for a 30 minute trip, I was skeptical. Boy, was I wrong. We visited on a Saturday night- there was a line, but we probably waited only 8 minutes until we were able to buy our tickets. There is an option to go on the ferris wheel without the open bar experience, but we chose to have the open bar. The ferris wheel moves so slowly that you can't even feel it move and it's completely closed, so my fear of ferris wheels was non-existent on this thing. There were probably 10 people total in our ride. The bartender was really great- he was super quick and had been working there since it opened a couple years ago. If you need a pick me up and some motivation to drink more quickly, this will do it to you. I had about 5 drinks in 30 minutes, the 5th one I asked for just as it was finishing up and then I was able to walk around the strip with it. As long as you are finished with your first drink, they will make you another one. Also- I heard that you can order shots 1x once you get to the top of the ferris wheel- wish we would have known that before our ride. Overall, we had a great time. Not only because of the open bar, but the gorgeous view of Las Vegas was definitely worth it in itself. I highly recommend checking it out- it's totally worth the $$.

The HighRoller is a nice slow moving observatory.  While up high at 550ft, you get to witness all of Las Vegas city lights.  There is a slightly comical virtual tour guide keeping you entertained.  

Oh and I forgot to mention, you can purchase a cocktail and take it with you on the HighRoller. Cheers !

Definitely worth experiencing. Fortunately it was only 2 of us and our bartender! We had about 3-4 drinks and the rotation was about 30 minutes.

Our bartender CJ was awesome. She was attentive, polite, and even took pictures for us. Thanks CJ!

The high roller might look like a Ferris wheel but actually....well it kinda is a Ferris wheel. Just on s huge scale & enclosed. 

I mean once at the top, the high roller provides all the Las Vegas sights you need and/or want for those photo/selfie needs.  

It's a smooth , comfortable ascend/descend.  It goes slow so you can absorb all of the sights.  I can see where other reviews gave it less stars and complained - but we were all alone.  Nobody bothered us, I ran around the ball/car (whatever you wanna call it) like a fool. 

Alcohol is served downstairs or you can upgrade for open bar.  Once exiting, you walk down a ramp into none other than a gift shop (why wouldn't you). 

It's definitely worth doing once.  Just try to go with a bunch of people!

High roller was a very very beautiful experience! You can def see all of Las Vegas. It's the perfect length of time to go around and the capsules are very modern and unique. I live in vegas and I would say it's a vegas must while you are on vacation here. The thing we didn't like was that when we walked up (my boyfriend and I) we over heard the girl say on the Walkie talkie "well they aren't all over each other"... Then they made us wait for another couple to ride with us. I thought it was strange and asked why. They said because people have sex up there when they are alone. And because if one person passes out or gets nervous then you need two people to attend to them (Which was the more politically correct answer) as we were getting in another two people walked in right away to their own capsule. They were two men. So that threw out the politically correct answer. Over all I thought it was very rude and sexist against me and my boyfriend that they were assuming we were going to have sex up top.... Staff should figure out something about that. Anyways it's a great one time thing but it's very expensive :) thanks

I'll never do this again. First, we tried to buy tickets at the kiosk, because when you walk up it looks like there's no other way to buy them. The kiosk freaks out and basically charges my card four times, for $600 worth of purchases. 

We go inside, and they're like oh yeah don't use the kiosks, they never work. And we're like then can't you turn them off?! And they basically just shrug. Not only that, but they absolutely insist we must buy tickets inside, because those charges on our card "aren't real" and will fall off. They tell us if the charges do go through (and one of them had already, for the wrong tickets), we can call our bank. So rude.

After much arguing (they really should've comped us tickets. I have never received such bad service in Vegas. We had paid $600 at this point and just had to trust that it wouldn't go past pending), we buy new tickets. 

We got the open bar at night, $52 per person. We waited in line for about 15 minutes after waiting in line to buy tickets. All told it took more than 30 minutes - the length of the ride - to get on this thing. 

The bartender was great and super efficient. We drank two patron margaritas while in the pod, and got beers to go. 

The view was meh. There's a better view from the VooDoo lounge at the rio. Next time I'll just go there.

We went for the happy half hour and had a great time.  We were able to get 2-4 drinks each and the pours were generous.  We had a group of 8 people and were able to stick together on a Friday night. There are different pods for open bar versus not, so be careful when you buy your tickets. The view is great from the top, the only downside is that the ride is really short.

もう最高です！！
8年前に行った時は、まだこんなのなかったのですが、ラスベガスも行くたびにかわりよるですな。
このハイローラーも、その１つで偶然見つけた時に、行ってみようぜ、となり乗りました。
まぁ、日本でいう観覧車と変わりはないですが、ただここから見る景色はほんと壮大でございます！
今回は昼にのったのですが、たぶん絶対夜も綺麗なので絶対おすすめですね。
ハイローラーの１つずつが日本の観覧車のものよりも広くて、あっちこっちと歩ける広さなので
360度ラスベガスの街並みが一望できます。
頂上につくと、お祝いしてくれるアナウンスもありますｗ
ラスベガス行った際はぜひのってください。

I got a Living Social deal for $20 for entry to the ride and a drink from the bar before 6 PM. The views from the wheel are breathtaking, and I can only imagine it would be even better at night. The wheel move slowly a bit over a half hour to go around. We stopped once for about one minute, no doubt to let a handicapped person on. I'm sure that happens more later in the day, which makes the ride longer. The screens above the windows show fun facts and trivia about the city.

It was a fun experience and gave me some of the cooler pictures from my trip.

The boys and I were in town for a bachelor weekend and saw a Groupon for ride+ open bar. We decided to take a chance as it seemed like a fun idea to get hammered on a huge Ferris wheel. Didn't use the groupon, but paid at the gate and got aboard. I was initially a bit pissed because it seemed like they were stuffing too many of us inside, but it actually was a good number of people. The ride was smooth and interesting, and the open bar made it awesome. The bartender was nice and personable. I would totally do it again. Where else in Vegas can you get 4 mixed drinks for 37 bucks, and this comes with a ride on an attraction.

Oh, the High Roller!  I finally took a ride and had a great time.

Now, to me, it's a tad bit overrated, however, I'm a local and can be quite biased.   Plus, I seen views of Vegas from the sky, so it takes a lot to wow me.  Before taking a ride, I happen to come across a blogger that completely hated the High Roller and had all negative things to say.  I found it humorous at first, but now that I've experienced it for myself, that blogger must have had just one single bad experience... or maybe he just sucks at life and can't have a good time.  I don't know.

The cabins/pods are super roomy, not overcrowded and have the A/C on blast.  Thank goodness.  They move rather slowly and feel incredibly safe.  No bumping around or anything along those lines.  The full trip takes about 40 minutes.  You're allowed to visit the bar for one beverage before hopping on.  Locals get a sweet discount..  15/ea, so that was a fun bonus.   The cabins don't stop, so be prepared to slowly but carefully step into the cabin..  it will keep moving.  There's a few attendants there to assist you with stepping on and don't let me frighten you, it's moving REALLY slowly.  Slower than the speed of a ski lift.

My only complaint would be the lack of seating.  There were a couple of women that took up the seats and that was about it.   I didn't mind standing for the full 40 mins taking pictures, etc as the view was fabulous!   Something tells me that some of these cabins have the works...  maybe a bar, better seating, etc..   I guess it just depends on the price and if you're planning a party.  

Great experience!  I highly recommend for all visitors to take a trip.  Feel free to bring the kids!  The price is definitely worth it!

I'm so glad we had the High Roller experience while in Vegas. We opted for the happy half hour experience which includes the ride and an open bar inside the pod. The cost for the nighttime ticket and bar is $52 per person. It's advertised that the pods can hold up to 40 people, but the fifteen or so people in our pod was plenty in my opinion. The wheel takes approximately 30 minutes to make its full revolution, and it never stops moving. You walk on and off the wheel while it's in motion. It moves slow enough that you barely notice it. But don't worry. If you miscalculate your steps and miss the wheel, there's a huge net below to catch you. There are eight monitors inside each pod which show video and track the progress of the wheel by marking the time elapsed and elevation. The views of Vegas from the wheel are spectacular, and the view of the Bellagio fountains are great also. The windows are floor to ceiling so you're able to get great photos. The bartender was also awesome and kept the drinks constantly flowing. Seriously, my hands were never empty. The drinks packed a punch also. I requested a fruity concoction, and the bartender came up with something amazing. I had a total of five drinks in that thirty minutes. Yes, five. I had a major buzz afterwards. But, WooHoo! It was a great experience.

Being the newest cool thing in Las Vegas, you expect a lot from an attraction. The 
High Roller did not disappoint! We had scored some discount "bar-car" tickets on living social, so that was a bonus. Unlimited drinks during the ride with ample room for you and about twenty of your friends, a bartender that's eager to please, and views from 500 feet, what's not to like? Each voyage lasts about 30 mins, so don't be in a rush, check out the views of the ever growing and changing town and enjoy!
There's a commentator on video monitors throughout your pod giving little tidbits of info that's sure to please those that don't drink, and once you get close to the top, there's a count down to the top-- for us we all toasted a shot that the bartender made special. Definitely worth the trip when you visit the Quad

My husband and I decided to pay extra to ride at night and to have an open bar. It was well worth the money. Our bartender was awesome and took a beautiful photo of us when we reached the top. Everyone in our pod had an amazing time. We were celebrating our 5 year anniversary and we had a blast!

There was no line when we got there on a friday night at 8:30 pm, so we went straight in and got out drinks prior to boarding, I got mango margarita no alcohol and my boyfriend got the strawberry margarita w/ alcohol, I ended up sipping his margarita because the mango was alright. As they were doing head count on how many people are going inside the pod, we were put in a group of girls having a bachelorette party . When we got inside, one of them told us that we shouldn't be in their pod "You're not VIP" so I started to feel really uncomfortable. We were the only stranger riding with a big group, they were drunk and very loud so we talked to the manager when we got off and told them we didn't enjoy our ride. The manager was nice to let us ride again. Overall the staff was really nice from the start & the place was clean. Our experience in the observation ferris wheel was satisfactory.

Why oh Why did I have the bright idea to pay more for the Happy Hour ride... We decided to check out the High Roller on a recent trip to Vegas. You can choose between a regular ride around the massive Ferris Wheel style ride or add-on a personal bartender with all you can drink, so of course we chose that. The ride IS not private so you and/or your group will be partnered with others. We had about 15 extra people and the bartender (and bar), even with this the globe is huge so there was still plenty of walk around space. Our bartender was great and made some awesome cocktails.The ride itself takes 30 minutes, but its moving so slow that you feel like you're on a lot longer, we each were able to get 4 drinks in a piece, and if you finish whatever you are drinking right before the wheel lets you off, you are allowed to get a fresh drink made to take with you. For me, this more than justified the $47 pp we paid.
Awesome! Specially is Reese is your bartender!! Best views and so much fun. Must do if your in Vegas!

Yes, I am a fan. I rode it during the day (when literally we were the only ones in the pod) and in the night time when there were people around to share the experience. For those with fear of heights, or better said, fear of falling -- this is a non-event. The scale of thing (as in it is so big and seemingly well built) on top of the slow movement means you really have no sensation that you are going anywhere.

It makes for a tranquil ride but on the downside perhaps a little too uneventful. Without the countdown on the screens when you reach the top you could literally miss being at the peak and if you were in deep conversation with someone you could actually miss the entire ride.

Like I started with -- I am a fan and I consider this a must do experience for those visiting Las Vegas but with that said I think they are going to be hard pushed to get a lot of repeat business for once you done it -- well, you have been there and done that without much draw to go back and experience it again.

Been in it twice since it opened
Watched them build it
Nice staff 
Gift shop
Valet parking location is good tons of shopping and stuff. 
Valet parking
And kids ride free

A bit too touristy for this local 
But it's like the London eye 
Only new. 
The cars have cool music

Good way to kill time 
I prefer the helicopter tour

The views are like none other and I at first didn't want to go on it because I am terrified of heights but one thing that  was surprising was that when you got to the top it didn't sway at all or move at all. I mean come on its 550 ft in the air so there is surly some air up there. Once in a lifetime thing to do!!!

Nice experience. Something different. Wanted to get the happy hour $5 drink special but lots of confusion and no help from anyone on getting it. Kiosks to buy tickets didn't even give the option. Had drink bar with full priced drinks before you got to platform. One of the bartenders just so happened to be getting off a ball so we asked him. He said it was a $10 upgrade not a $5 so highly confusing. Not sure if would do it again....

Had a great time & the views were awesome. Go before 6:00 & save yourself some money & if you drink do the happy hour for an additional $5.00. Went on a Monday around 5:30 & had a short wait & did not need to buy drinks at the bar since we had happy hour tickets. We had 24 of us in the pod & our group of 4 was each able to get 4 drinks apiece in the 30 minute ride. 4 drinks for an additional $5 or a drink from the bar where prices started at $7.00 your choice.

This has been on my bucketlist for a while now.  I finally got a chance to experience the high roller and cross it off my list. It was such a fun 30 minutes. We shared the ride with another couple so there was definitely lots of room to move around in and take lots of pictures. Overall, it was a pleasant experience.

Went April 24. Did it threw living social.  We got the unlimited alcohol on the wheel. Our bartender was CJ aka the good Cheryl. She was great.  The ride felt short even being 30min. Time does fly when you're having fun.  We downed 7 drinks each and she gave a shot at the top point of the ride.  The view was beautiful, the ride was soo smooth. Getting on and off. The ride never stops. Keep that in mind while drinking. People help you on and off the wheel.  They have seats but we stood and walked around. They do bag check which was fine with me.  We were supposed to be before 4pm due to our tickets.  When we got there she asked what time we wanted. Ok cool it didn't' have to be now because we had to go the bathroom before we were stuck 30min no bathroom.  She gave us 4:20pm. We were late 10mins. They didn't care.  She said the ride picks up every 10 min. Everyone from start to the souvenir area were so nice.  It's a walk from then you park, get your tickets and walk up to the ride but wasn't too bad.  Just like any other ride.  I would go again. We went in the day time next time we will do the night with the bar.:) the price for 2 and the bar was Sooooo worth it. Oh in the ride was 6 of us. I walked all over freely. With a great view in every angle. They don't have electricity in the cars so no ice blended, and had basic alcohol but all like rum, vodka, tequila, gin, and juice like cranberry,  orange, pineapple, sodas. So I just stuck with long island ice tea and sex on the beach. I think 2 times experience is this ride. Day then night and that's it.

This is a must for vegas. A bachelorette group of us bought tickets for a bar rotation around 5pm on a Friday night. There were only 4 other people in our car, celebrating a birthday. The views were fantastic, it was so neat walking around the car and taking pictures. The windows are rounded along the bottom, so I got a little woozy walking near the edges lol. The open bar is no joke. Usually open bars equal watered down drinks and slow refills, not here. They had good brands, plenty of hard liquor, beer, and even a cider. Our bartender poured us celebration shots and kept our hands full of drinks the entire 30 minutes. All in all I probably had around 6 drinks, including one for the road. The price of those drinks alone pay for the admission. Would absolutely recommend.

During my weekend in Vegas I  ended up on this super cool attraction.  It's a Ferris/observation wheel that  has pods which hold up to 40 people.  You are taken on a 30 minute ride that offers you views of the strip and Las Vegas from different angles.  We bought tickets for the happy hour pod which has an open bar. My endless glass of Ketel one and tonic enhanced my viewing pleasure of Las Vegas.  "Smiles".  At the pinnacle our server poured the entire pod a shot of ??? we all toasted as we reached the peak.  On the ride back down the patron came out.  Needless to say we had an awesome time with fun strangers partaking with 30 minutes of endless drink and fantastic views.  Cheers y'all.

Awesome views of the city and worth the ticket. I went with a group of 22 and we all fit comfortably in the pod with plenty of room to move around. You can get a ticket that includes alcohol but the ride was only 30 minutes so we opted out. Plenty of bars and restaurants nearby to have drinks before and after for cheaper.

I remember when this was first being built, everyone, including myself, was so excited about it. The High Roller is the largest Ferris wheel, or "observation wheel". It is located at the Linq Promenade and looks really pretty during the day and night. At night, it lights up and they even do a light show, where the lights on the wheel change according to the music. The prices vary depending on the time and Day you go for a 30 minute ride. They do have deals on Groupon or local deals if you know anyone who lives here. I have been once, and it is definitely something to check out. I probably won't go again just because there's really nothing else to do in the pod. I think it would be fun for a date night or when you have visitors. It's an attraction for all ages. They do have a bar before going on the ride, so you can drink in the pod. Sometimes they have events, and I definitely want to try the Yoga one.

if your looking for that perfect view above Las Vegas, the High Roller is defiantly on of the better ones. Located centrally on the strip, the high roller takes you on half hour ride 550 ft above the LV Strip. It is a bit pricy in my opinion but I had some coupons so I took advantage of the opportunity. If money is no object I would get a group of friends and rent you own cabin. I was unfortunate enough to share the ride with a bunch of screaming and crying kids! Once was enough for me on this ride but it was worth the one time trip.

Was here last night and brought some of my family so a party of 6 adults and 2 kidos. The view was great however this ride even with the local $5 off was way over priced. We were all bored and the kids were done 15 mins in. They have a video playing on 10, 12 screens the whole time (completely unnecessary). The kids thought the music and the trivia game was fun; actually more entertaining then the rest. This would be perfect if it was half the cost and half the time. We did a family photo but it's one shot move along so the picture wasn't great. Just a little disappointed since they weren't busy and there was no one after us for a while that they couldn't do a retake.
Did the Happy Hour Late Night High Roller ride and the view was gorgeous. Definitely a must-do at least once in Vegas.
A little over priced but well with the effort. Would ride again. Rode at night.  Out pod only had 8 other people in it at 9pm.

We did the happy half hour during the day. Even if you plan to buy 1 drink getting the bar pod is worth it. At night the bartender says it can get crazy and packed so go if you like a jam packed party go at night. We liked the relaxing ride in the daylight while sipping a couple cocktails. Fun ride, worth the $.

Slow Motion aerial pods for a moderately exceptional view of Las Vegas. These pods all need a glass floor, fresh air and a free drink to be considered cash paying cool.

FUN FACT: Tallest Farris Wheel in the world by THREE INCHES... It better be a High Roller to get lady luck off on just three inches!

Judith was our bartender in our pod at the high roller and we will be back just in hopes to see her again! Thank you Judith for being so amazing.
I wish we could do more than leave her this review. Best bartender I've met hands down.

The High Roller at the Linq has amazing views! We chose not to do the open bar because we knew we wanted to take lots of pictures!  You can still buy a drink beforehand and take with you! I would recommend going at night to see the beautiful lights on the strip!! Would definitely say a must see and do while in Vegas!

I guess you need to do it once...but at least get a groupon so you can get a good drink along with the ride.  Yes the view is cool... but you can see it from other places.  The ride is slow and smooth.  I am afraid of heights and it didn't bother me for whatever reason on this thing...even when the announcer said not to panic with the technical difficulties that has us stuck up top for a bit...

We did Groupon package with open bar. It was totally worth the money. The bartender on board was supper friendly and kept the drinks coming. If your thinking about doing it, DO IT. It gives you a great view of the city.

**Yelp 100 Challenge 2017 98/100**

This was actually WAY COOLER than I thought it would be. We went on a Monday afternoon, and it was only $25. We didn't bother with the open bar car because we didn't want to feel rush; turns out, they have a bar with very reasonably priced drinks ($11 for a tito's/soda) that you can take with you. Being a Monday afternoon, we had almost the whole car to ourselves, which was awesome.

The only annoying part was the guy that they had "narrating" the ride - it was too much, let the music play and people enjoy their views without his yapping! Good mix of music on the way up as well.

Overall, really cool views of the strip! Fun to look around from up high. Great if you're looking for an afternoon activity that doesn't require drinking.
Great time for kids and adults. The happy hour ride is a fun time and you can definitely get a lot to drink in that amount of time. The views are also amazing and breath taking.

This is my first time here visiting The LINQ's High Roller.. And it was pretty cool. The place is very clean. The ride was free for me since I'm a Diamond for Total Rewards. Normally it's $25 for a single ride. You can even pay an additional price to have a 'Happy Hour' ride where you can get a pod that has a bar to enjoy some drinks while you're on the 30 minute ride.

The only thing that bothered me was the boarding and coming off of the pods. The wheel doesn't stop and you have to board it while moving. I was with my grandma who was using a cane, and I didn't think it's really safe for her. She's a senior citizen whose mobility isn't fast, so what would have happened if she slipped and fell? The ride was smooth and the windows were clean so the views from above was good. I went during the day, but people say you should go at night time since all the city lights are on. Regardless, I enjoyed my relaxing half an hour in an air conditioned pod.. Temp when I went was about 109 degrees. It started raining during my ride but no issues with that. Is come back a second time to see what the views at night, and this time pay the extra fee and have a drink as well.

I got to admit I did not want to go on this attraction. My wife made me go. 

Although I would never go again I'm glad I've been. Hopefully that makes sense, it does to me.

Ladies like this stuff and it's a whole lot better than sitting through "The Notebook" movie AGAIN.

The ride takes about 40 minutes. Get the car with the bartender and liquor bar.  You're in Vegas, the best way to see it is with a good buzz!  Lots of bars and restaurants in the Linq area including a newly built O'Sheas.  Fun times!

Free ride!

Well, the ride isn't free but we scored some free tickets! Got to ride the High Roller at the LINQ courtesy of Jeff Civillico during one of his "Comedy In Action" shows at the LINQ Hotel & Casino but he will move to a permanent location at Bugsys Cabaret inside the Flamingo Hotel & Casino in 3 days, Sept 20, 2015.  Separate review of the show... http://www.yelp.com/biz/jeff-civillico-comedy-in-action-las-vegas-3?hrid=Vxrgy9xYS79w-hMhzc6lwg&utm_source=ishare

Anyway, we had front seats during the show and hubby was called to be one of the participants in the unicycle act. He was given two free voucher tickets to the High Roller. Awesome!

The tickets were somewhere in the $35 range each for a night ride but cheaper rate in the daytime. We went that same evening after the show. This giant Ferris wheel doesn't stop during operating hours, it just moves very, very slowly and you just hop in one. The pods were pretty roomy inside with seats and handle bars. There were TV screens that give interesting stats about the High Roller and as you ascend you get a panoramic view of the Las Vegas Strip. There is even a countdown when you reach the very top elevation of the High Roller. You get a 360-view of the strip of the city lights. Each pod holds about 40 people. One revolution takes about 30 minutes and, um, no restrooms on board.

Although very cool experience this is a one-time ride for me and I'm good with that. I can say that I rode the High Roller observation wheel at the LINQ and Jeff Civillico paid for it :)

Review #0361

What a great view of Las Vegas and everything around. I went during the day and there wasn't a wait at all. 

You get a 550 foot view of everything around once at the top and you can move around the car so you can see everything. 

Everything runs smoothly from getting on to getting off the car. 

They also offer a military discount which is awesome.

This is a nice experience but the one star is for the bad service we received during admission. We came in by 9:30pm and we were excited because it was advertise that when we purchase buffet of the buffets we will just upgrade or add a certain amount to ride the high roller. But the customer service associate whom we presented our receipt of buffet of the buffets was uninformed of the advertised promo and had to call the manager to attend to us. But what is more annoying is, while waiting for the manager, the attendant try to answer back rudely and insinuate that what we are trying to say is untrue even of we showed her the photo of pamphlet showing the promo. Though the matter was settled,I think it is best that if there is an advertised promo the workers must be informed. And for that rude attendant,I hope she should learn how to respect customers.

Came here during night time with family and the ride was smooth. I expected it to be scary because it was 550 ft high, but instead it was like looking out an airplane window. The view from above wasn't what I expected but it was a nice view of the lit up hotels and streets. The other side of the pod faces a parking lot most of the time, so that was boring. I also took a time lapse video of the ride so I thought that was cool. 

Overall, nice view of the strip at night for great pictures, highly recommend.

Got up here around 9pm-ish on a Tuesday night and had the entire spot to myself to wander to take in the great views of the Vegas strip at night, woohoo!!!

Is this an absolute tourist trap? You betcha! One round on the giant wheel for the price they charge will annoy anyone but c'mon, it's a once and done type of thing to do in Vegas. I bought my tickets off a third party vendor for the nighttime tickets, which knocked it down $6 from buying tickets on the spot.

Pretty cool we have done this ride in the past. One during sunset which I recommend doing since it is right before price change. Also they offer military discount. Kids 3 and younger are free. Nice big wheel and made amazing. Must do while in Vegas.

This was a fun experience but it was expensive. We opted for the happy hour car. Drinks were good. Depending on how quickly you drink realistically you only have time for about 2 drinks before the ride is over. Go at night when the strip is lit up.

This was alright, there's not much to it, the whole ride itself was bout 30 minutes long. It's actually really spacious inside those circular shit, my friend stayed at their hotel and they gave him two free tickets for this ride and so he just gave it to me soooo hip hip hooray! Everything's always just a tad bit nicer or better when it's free  : )

But sadly my friend and I were stuck in that ball with some bitchy lady who wouldn't allow us to compliment, pet, breathe near or even look at her dog, she literally wasted her time there because she sat through the whole ride, sucks to suck sometimes lady, poor dog.

Must do! A friend suggested this "high roller" Ferris wheel... While at first I thought it was corny, I soon found myself enjoying it very much. 

We bought tickets at $35 a piece ahead of time and went at night (best at night). The Ferris wheel is HUGE. Literally these pods hold about 30+ people. You sort of go through this simulated (Epcot esq) ride escapade before getting to the actual ride. We went on a Wednesday so we skipped any line whatsoever. 

When you enter the pod (you sort of run into it) because it doesn't stop moving. You need to catch up with the ride (same as getting off). If you have any leg and/or coordination issues be careful as you can lose your balance. 

Anywhere in the pod is a great seat! You won't miss a thing. My recommendation is to put down your phone and just enjoy the view. It is 30 minutes total. DO IT! **If you're afraid of heights, this is Definitely not for you.

Awesome experience and a great view of the Strip.  the Telepromo was quite funny as "you have reached 420 feet in the air and we are pretty High" funny stuff.  We did the night round and will do this again on our next trip.
