One of those things in Vegas Definitely worth doing at least once! Amazing view! We paid a little extra for the car with the full bar inside-all you can drink for the 30 min ride. Great views of all the sights of Las Vegas.

This was an awesome experience! I can't begin to explain the enjoyment we had at the high roller...but I will try! 

I had a group of 5 and we purchased the happy half hour. I was a little skeptical because it was almost twice as much as general admission but it was well worth it! Our server, Cheryl, was AMAZING! She was funny, had whit and most of all, she kept the drinks coming! I'm a little bit of a party boy but she appeased my wild spirit and kept me laughing the entire 30 min trip. We saw all of Las Vegas and she even took pics of us, poured shots and made very good drinks. The alcohol was of a nice caliber and we enjoyed our time from the time we got on until we got off. Ultimately, Cheryl was one of the best people we met in Vegas and I would do this again and again if she was my bartender. She had a cute Northeastern accent and was so sweet. Blessed is the (wo)man  that gets the opportunity to ride on her tram. 

High roller half happy hour was nothing less than amazing!

The Ride
----------
Take a 360° High Roller ride around the Ferris Wheel that gives the rider a scene view of the Las Vegas skyline. Best to catch the night ride to see the lights of the Strip.  Options include rides only and 21+ open bar.  The trip around the wheel takes about 30 minutes. 


The Spot
----------
Located at Harrah's The Linq, High Roller is located at the end of a hidden promenade of shops, restaurants and bars. Definitely a place to kill a little time when you want to take a break from the rest of the Strip.


The Staff
----------
Friendly staff guide you through the onboarding process.  If you choose the open bar option, they'll keep the drinks flowing.



Bang-For-The-Buck
--------------------
It's a great view of the Las Vegas strip, especially if done at night. Definitely worth the ride especially if you partake in adult beverages and book your ride with the open bar option.  Be sure to check for Groupon specials which could include discounts for other businesses at the Linq promenade area.  


Conclusion
------------
If you part take in Adult beverages (and you know who you are) or not () definitely worth checking out. Take the night ride for the best experience and check out the nearby promenade. It's tourist-trendy, but isn't that why you're in Vegas... well kinda...

We got married on the high roller at the end of April. We live in Las Vegas and have been on the high roller before for their happy hour rotations and had fun doing that, so we figured it would be a memorable way to get married. It was. From before the wedding getting all the details taken care of, checking in on the day of the event, meeting the photographer that was booked through them, Mio, meeting Pastor Steve about 15 minutes prior to the wedding, pairing Bluetooth for music, champagne and strawberries for the 1st rotation, pictures in front of the green screen, all of it, went great. 
The photographer Mio made us feel so comfortable. It was as if he was a part of the wedding party, he got along with everyone there, groom, bride, and family. He remained professional the entire time yet made us feel like he was part of the group and we had no worries about feeling uncomfortable or awkward. The photos turned out amazing and he captured each moment that I had asked him to and more. We couldn't have been more pleased. He was on time and ready to work and went above and beyond to make sure the groom and I were pleased.
Pastor Steve was professional, timely, and experienced. He suggested certain movements or moments to make sure the ceremony went smoothly and would also give us photos that would be unforgettable. 
The staff at the high roller were on point. They made sure all the little details were taken care of and didn't hesitate to ask if we needed anything else. Timing was perfect. We selected to start at 7 pm so the sun would be setting when we were exchanging our vows. Pastor Steve and staff monitored to make sure we would be starting at the right time so that would be a reality. 
My husband and I had a wonderful time. We would without a doubt recommend to others getting married on the high roller if they are looking for a fun, unique, and stress-free way to get married. I couldn't have imagined a more perfect wedding.

If this is your first time in Vegas, or you've never had the opportunity to see the view from high up in Vegas, then this might be worth experiencing. Otherwise, it was just...fine. The Linq is a pretty cool place, all in all, and the High Roller is a nice enough experience. It takes you in a "pod"- basically a large, glass enclosed room (pretty chilly, as the AC was blasting), and slowly circles so you can see some nice views of the city. We must have hit it at just the right time- 8p on a Friday- because there was absolutely no line. You have the opportunity to purchase overpriced beverages at a bar before entering into your pod, and you're off. The pod plays music (it is at a low volume, it isn't a party), and facts about Vegas. While the views are nice, it is a little on the boring side. I could see it maybe being more exciting if it were more crowded with wild people, though!   I can't see doing this over and over, but I'm glad I can check it off the list.

This is a real nice experience !
The prices are higher at night !

Awesome awesome !!!!!
This was a blast! My wife and I went at night. The line moved quickly to get into the pod. We rode with 6 other people. Very cool. We'd definitely do it again!!!

Fun night on the newest Vegas attraction! I expected the lines to be long considering 1) it was a Friday night and 2) we had a Groupon that we were using, but we only had to wait around 10 minutes. We purchased the Groupon that included the unlimited happy half-hour. 

Boarding the car is a little difficult - you board while the wheel is still moving. There were only about 15 people in our group so we got on easily, but I can only imagine how difficult it would be with more people or if you had already had a few drinks. 

The wheel had great views of the strip at night including the Bellagio fountains and the Mirage volcano. Our bartender was friendly and super fast and we all had plenty of drinks in 30 minutes. 

It's definitely a must-do at least once in Vegas, although i would try to find a Groupon or Living Social to avoid the steep ticket price.

This is a wee bit pricey and we enjoyed the views, no doubt!  Not sure yet if I'd like to check it out during the day but it was awesome to check out Las Vegas valley at night!

For something that moves hella slow when you're actually in it, they don't give you much time to load into the pod though HAHA No, I hadn't been drinking and NO we didn't get the pod that had a bar.  

At its full height potential, I did start to get a little nervous and sat to ride it out til we came down a bit.  

All in all, check it out at least once; tourists or residents...it's a good break from the gambling and drunken shenanigans, I promise!

We went during the daytime and it was $25 per person. Not the cheapest experience for sure but it was well worth it. We were in a cabin with only one other family (of 3) so the 5 of us had plenty of space to spread out and to take as many photos as we wanted.

The guide video was sarcastic and funny; it might not be everyone's cup of tea. The view from the top was incredible! I've been to plenty of observation towers and ferris wheels and this experience did not disappoint.

They also have a Happy Half Hour option with open bar if you're interested in drinking.

Awesome Experience!  Had a group of 20 people and did the bartender car for additional $10.   The bartender is MANDATORY, otherwise it's just an average, 3-star experience - basically a 40 person Ferris wheel that goes over 500'. You can duplicate the view part by just going for a drink at VooDoo Lounge (Rio). I had about 4-5 drinks in the 30+ minute ride and they were "top shelf" (Jack, Patron and Stoli). We did it around 4p, but this would be a great way to start a night out at the clubs. Will do it again...

I liked it! Selfie heaven! haha

The ride is about 30min and you should stick to your front ride side seatings (bc it has the best view.)

Its $35 pp but if you pay $10pp more, you can get the pod with a full bar inside and its UNLIMITED drinks for the duration of the ride. If you get shots, im sure you can get few drinks in 30min.

The best view of the city and surrounding area. We timed it for sunset and it was spectacular. We did the half hour happy  hour and it was well worth it. Top shelf alcohol and the drinks came as fast as you could drink them. I had Kettle One vodka and soda, 5 of them!!!! The last one was to go.

Adan was our bartender and he had about 20 cups lined up with ice ready to pour as soon as the doors closed. He had a great personality and attitude and easy to talk to. He was busy from start to finish and did a great job. Tip them well because they do work hard.

Tuesday is supposed to be half off for locals. It lists it's hours on Tuesday as Noon-2am. Well after midnight they don't count it as Tuesday for the discount anymore, even though it's still within the Tuesday operating hours. The male clerk was rude and treated me like I was stupid for wanting the discount Tuesday night at 1230am. Horrible service.

Currently the tallest Ferris wheel in the world (or observation wheel). 

And it's in Vegas. 

You'll find it at The LINQ's outdoor shopping promenade/district. I'm so glad my GalPalA mentioned this attraction -_0

'Twas part of our to-do list at night so the fee was $34.95 per person. The fee is higher if alcohol is involved. 

You may purchase tickets online, by vending machines, from individuals w/handheld machines (no cash so card only), or at the attraction itself. 

As we were walking towards the High Roller we bumped into employees w/the handheld machines and they printed a receipt that would be our tickets. They were very helpful too.

The High Roller is a slow 30-minute ride where each cabin holds up to 40 individuals. 

There are benches w/plenty of floor space but for the best views just stand against the windows. We were lucky since our cabin only had 8 people. Easy to move around and take pics :)

Now the wheel doesn't stop so pay attention to the employees. When they holler at you, move quickly to hop in as directed. If you wear heels there are nets at the bottom. Joke lol. Just be careful. Don't be that chick :p

So just imagine. When the 30 minutes have passed and you hear and see that it's time to get out, you'd better follow directions and move stat since the new riders are hopping in at the opposite end. I'd suggest wearing flat shoes/boots, sneakers, or wedges.

Enjoy the LV view ^_^

The low star rating is solely for the staff's complete lack of attention to safety on the escalators. Went last night, bought the Groupon for the open bar car - that part was fantastic - great bartender and perfect views.

But while we were entering the building a huge your group came in and were processed through the ticket area on the first floor and sent up the first set of escalators. No one from the High Roller or the tour operator was paying attention and there were about a half dozen kids from the tour group playing on and blocking the escalator that was not running. The escalator that was running was not manned and no one knew that the tour group had COMPLETELY blocked the top of the escalator and were not moving into the HUGE open area near the bar. People were crashing into the people at the back of the line, some almost fell backward down the escalator. We told the people to move and no one did, so we went around against the wall to avoid being in the way of the next people coming up. It was a frightening and EXTREMELY dangerous situation that was repeated on the next escalator.

At the top of the second escalator was one staff member who was questioning riders ABOUT PICTURES - right as they got to the top - well - the tour group members did not understand him and kept stopping, again creating a roadblock at the top as people were crashing into those ahead of them. One of the people in my party had to grab two kids who had run in front of their parents and turned to look down the escalator, then tripped when they hit the people at the top and were falling into the top of the escalator.

The absence of ANY staff on the escalators to address safety and the fact the the only staffer at the escalator was completely oblivious to people crashing into people right in front of him, is inexcusable! They were lucky no one (that we saw at least) was hurt. 

We alerted three different staff members to the situation and neither acknowledged the concern or moved from their posts (one was scanning tickets, one was the idiot at the top of the second escalator who just blinked at us and went back to his questions, last was the girl who was also trying to sell photos. These were the ONLY staff members (other than one bartender) that we saw between security and the area where you get photos taken and load for the ride.

If you go - look up to make sure it's safe to go up. I've never had to think about that before, but after the dangerous situation created by the High Roller's lack of line management or concern for safety - I'll make sure to look before stepping on the staircase.

Brought my GF at the time here because she had never been to Vegas before.  They serve you drinks before you walk up at a bar which is nice.  The ride takes about 30 minutes to complete and the views are spectacular.  You can see everything around the strip which is awesome.  But honestly,  after a little bit it got kind of boring and we were ready to get off and get back down to the ground.  Def a good thing to go on once to see the sights but I doubt I will be repeating.

Just do it....
Happy hour is totally worth it! Your have 30 mins all you can drink, top shelf liquors..  the view is one word- WOW.....

We bought tickets thru Yelp & saved a few bucks. It will also save you some time standing in line if you go during prime hours. I would definitely recommend this attraction during the night hours so you can see the lights & take quality pictures.

Sorry, I don't think it's worth it.  The glass of the ball thing you are in is so dirty and gross. We spent the $50 on the "open bar" one, and they crammed so many people in there, we only got two drinks each. And we had to down them in a half hour.  I though the view was going to be way better than it was. You probably need to get in one right at sunset to get a cool pic. I guess I'm glad I did it so I could say I did, but I don't think it's worth it to do it again.

I don't know why others have left reviews about the High Roller being boring...BECAUSE IT IS SO NOT! 

They must have been on the boring one without the open bar! Score! The best and least expensive time is to get on the last "day" ride with the open bar. Our bartender was awesome and served top shelf liquor. At the end of the ride, we scored 3 drinks and a shot.

I love the bar!!! For all the guests who don't know you can go into the entrance, pass the bag checks and upstairs without a ticket and go to the bar. They check your tickets after the bar. There are restrooms around the corner from the bar so it's better. Whenever my family is in town, we always walk the linq, and stop in upstairs at the bar, and drink a little, and then leave to walk the strip more, maybe see a show and then return to the High Roller later that night to ride. The bar tenders are super friendly and they love talking to guests, and don't get me started on happy hour. ASK ABOUT HAPPY HOUR!! The high roller is a great place and the bar is pretty sick. Check it out sometime and bring your kids too. They have amazing margarita, mango, and strawberry slushies which are non alcoholic unless you request for them and my aunt literally has about six souvenir cups. A little pricy but worth the experience!!

Always bet on Caesars Entertainment to provide a great experience... except when you lose on the tables. The High Roller is their most recent gamble to entice people to walk through their newly refurbished properties. It's worth the price to get a one of a kind view of the strip in a rotating pod.  Give it a try when you have nothing else to do but wait in an air conditioned area with strangers.

I have never experienced worse customer service. I was separated in line by a large, drunk, wedding party and by the time I got to area where cars were loading, my party was already on a car and staff would not let them off. When I shared my frustration and was told that it was my fault and the fault of my friends, I was escorted by manager Sandy and two security guards back to the concession store. I was then told that my ticket was unable to be found in the system and thus couldn't get a refund. Humiliated, mistreated. We'll see what my attorney has to say. Horrible people running that show.

Come here for their Happy Hour Special! I believe it starts from 4-7pm. Everything with alcohol looks so much better! The wait time on a Monday -- was pretty fast. We waited about 5 minutes to board the Ferris wheel. The high roller is the world's largest observation and it's located in Las Vegas! It's located in the rear parking lot of the LINQ Hotel. You won't miss it. Super Huge Spinning Object. 

The happy hour is open bar -- You're stuck with 20 random strangers. At the end of the ride their all your friends! You're packed for sure like sardines, waiting to get drunk! lol It took the Ferris Wheel about 25 minutes to finish a complete circle. The sight seeing is okay.. Nothing major -- I think if they put less people in it.. There is a better chance of walking around and seeing different angles of the strip.

This place is legit! Get the 1/2 hour open bar ticket for $33 (June 2016 price) is it 100% worth it! Our bartender (Amanda??) was AHHHmazing! 

We walked in saying "these people don't know what they did selling open bar to us" and walked out getting our asses handed to us. It's amazing the amount of booze they throw at you in that 1/2 hour! 

You share your pod with other groups, we had about 15 in our pod. Right off the bat, the view from the pod is awesome overlooking the north side of the strip and towards the mountains on the east side of the strip. You are greeted by your bartender pouring drinks for everyone faster than lighting. She seemed like she wanted us to get our money's worth too! I only paid attention to the vodka, but I know they had other hard alcohol and beer. I was surprised to see they had Ketel One. Ketel One is bae. About a quarter of the way in... she poured the 1st of 3 rounds of shots for everyone. The view continues to be awesome and you get those little butterflies when you are rounding the top of the wheel-- you can see the south side of the strip at this point. And if you time it right... you'd be able to perfectly see the Bellagio water show from high up! 

All in all, I personally had 3 cocktails, 3 shots, a cocktail to-go AND an incredible time!! This is legit the best place to drink in Vegas for a $33 ticket price and a view!!! IN LOVE!

I rode this at night, assuming the lights of the Vegas Strip would be what really made it a worthwhile experience. But because of its lame back-alley location, the view is disappointing.

I don't understand why they built this where they did. The tourist frippery of the Strip is hidden from view until you get near the top, maybe 25% of the ride. The other 75% of the ride is spent staring at the ass-end of various dumpy hotel-casinos. I don't know about you, but a view of the Harrahs parking garage ain't worth $40 to me. 

If I were to ride again, I would go around sunset -- then you could at least see the mountains and stuff and the sunset during the boring 75% of the ride. As it was, I just stared into darkness peppered with thousands of suburban streetlights on one side....and the aforementioned parking garages on the other.

The one thing I did enjoy was the mechanics -- looking at the nuts and bolts and stuff holding everything together. From an engineering standpoint, it's fascinating....but in all other respects, this is an utterly boring ride. The HORRENDOUSLY lame video playing throughout the ride just adds insult to injury -- the actor in said video should be lashed to the exterior of one of the cabins and forced to spin around in slow hell for all of eternity, being pelted by the piss and vomit of a thousand Vegas hookers. UGH!

A better deal would be to spend your $40 on two cocktails at MIX, on top of the Delano...it has a much better view, and much shorter lines. (Although when I went, on a Sunday night, there was no line at all...so if you MUST waste your money on this ride, at least go on an off night).

While visiting Las Vegas I decided to take a ride on the High Roller (Ferris Wheel).  We went in the early afternoon.  There were no lines and we ended up in a car with just the 3 from my party.

Bring your camera!  I took alot of photos of the strip and the mountains.

Buy drinks in the lobby before you board.  You can take the drinks with you.

It moves slow!  It takes around 30 minutes to take you all the way around. It never stops and even is moving while you board.  It is great for all ages.

I recommend it if you are visiting Vegas.

I'm always up for trying new adventures especially ones that challenge my fear of heights.  I've been on a lot of these types of rides but I must say that this was the smoothest and I felt the most safe.  I went at dusk and it was cool to see how the strip changed from when I took off to when I got back down.  Plus, where else can you bring a drink on a ride like this.

Gotta check it out and cross it off your bucket list.
A must do!!! Lupe was our tour guide/ bartender and she was knowledgeable about the city and with Snapchat :)

The High Roller is pretty much just a very large ferris wheel but you do get the beautiful views and bright lights of Vegas.

It is a bit pricey, twenty-something to high thirties depending on what time of day you go. We were fortunate to get discounted tickets for it while attending Jersey Boys. Make sure to look at Tix4Tonight or some discount tickets location. We were able to get our tickets for $20, regular price I think $28.

The lines were quick enough and fortunately the cars weren't too packed. We were all able to get standing window spots (I think there were about 20-25 in our car). 

Also, we went at about 4:30pm. It worked out perfectly because we were able to still see daylight when we got on and were able to see the mountains and terrain but by the time we got to the top it was dark and we were able to see the lights of Vegas at its brightest.

Worth doing once . Just make sure to try and find discounted tickets!

Review for Happy Half Hour Night experience: our group decided to take part in the happy half hour at the Groupon rate of $40/person rather than the standard ticket price $52.

The bartender was very lively and explained the rules for everyone to get their drinks. She also did a shot for everyone in the pod at the very top including a countdown. Overall the view was amazing and the drinks not bad at all. In the half hour round trip we managed 3 drinks and 3 shots at a comfortable pace. 

Note: the wheel doesn't stop spinning, so you have to walk on and off the pod while it's moving. Even though it's moving very slowly, this maneuver definitely took more effort exiting after the drinks. Watch out!

My girlfriend and I rode the Highroller during our last trip to Vegas. We were the only ones in the pod, which was kind of cool.

The view once you get to the top is pretty remarkable. You get to see quite a lot of the strip and the surrounding area. However, you're in the back of the Linq so you see the backs of a lot of the hotels. 

The voiceover was equal parts interesting and annoying. Many times that you wanted to just enjoy the view in silence there was a dumb joke thrown in.

We did the Eiffel Tower/Highroller combo which saved us a bit of money. I'll likely ride again, because Vegas.

I bought a Groupon deal for two people for $75 for the late night ride which is from 7pm -1am and it was open bar. 

I wouldn't pay full price for this, and even at $75 for two is was just okay. I left satisfied but not with my socks blown off, even with the open bar. As a matter of fact I would not recommend the open bar because how many freakin drinks can one really consume in 30 min? And you're not allowed to take shots. I had one, my boyfriend had another and we noticed we were already coming down when we decided to get one more and share it. (Its more like 25 min) 
This view isn't anything spectacular. It's nothing that you haven't seen from above the 25th floor on any hotel on the strip. I think the view from The Stratosphere is probably better. 

All in all, its one of those touristy new things in Vegas that you want to/have to check out. So I am glad I did, but I wouldn't do it again. I would recommend that everyone go out and try it though. The ferris wheel concept is pretty cool. Get up there, snap some pictures that you'll keep forever and let me know how you like it.

Go just before the price changes to the night time rate. You'll catch the view of day strip, sunset strip, and night strip. Also for $5 more you can enjoy the all you can drink pod. I really enjoyed the experience and the views. Another must do in vegas.

The ride was nice, we opted out of the happy hour cabin and only had a few people in our cabin which made photo tanking much better.

The only comments are- it's super cold in there!!! And I wish the ride was built in a way you can see something from all around the cabin, now the strip is on one side and the other is just a parking lot... Seems wasteful.. 

PS- if you get voucher for tickets- these are NOT your real tickets, you still have to stand in line with everyone else to get your actual tickets... :(

I am a local and have been on the High Roller three times to escort various visiting family members. I enjoy the ride because you hardly feel like you are moving. It is an ok view of the Vegas valley on one side and an amazing view of the strip on the other. 

The best time to ride is at sunset. This way you get a day view half-way up and a night view on the way down. This of course requires some timing on your part.

Because it is an extremely expensive 30 minute ride, you'll want to time your visit with lower than normal crowds. Then you'll have the best opportunity to board a pod that is not being packed with too many tourist to enjoy the views.

They offer military and local discounts.

Great attraction to visit and get the best view of the strip. I was a little nervous before riding because of my slight fear of heights, but it really wasn't bad at all! It was also moving more quicker than I thought. Outside of the ride it looks like it isn't even moving but once you're actually riding it, it's at a perfect speed to overlook the Vegas strip :)

Loved it, kids loved it, scared of heights wifey loved it too. The first time we had the whole thing to ourselves Which was very cool.  There is a deal on living social where you get the open bar for the same price, maybe next time without the kids.

Check in 1st for $10 off.  A good value.  

If you see kiosk girl outside you can buy ticket & #bypass line.  Same price. Worth it & they aren't out for long.

I think, having done the (k)night ride(r)..I would want the day... To see the Mars landscape.  I seriously felt I was on Mars.



Drinks are cheaper before you get in.

My husband and I rode the High Roller because we got a $20 each package deal with military discount at the Eiffel Tower gift shop. The package deal included the High Roller and Eiffel Tower and allowed us to ride either ride at any time. We went on a Friday night and surprisingly, it wasn't busy at all. The pod has a capacity of 40 but there were only maybe 10 people in our pod. The ride is extremely slow and lasts 30 minutes which allows you plenty of time to take in the amazing view. There are screens in the pod that has a "host" talking throughout the ride that I found to be cheesy but funny. Overall, fun experience if you've never been but a one time ride is plenty for me.

First of all, before you buy that Groupon or Living Social, CALL the High Roller and check the price. I've been 5 times. The first time I was chuffed because I had a Groupon, but when we got there, I was stunned to discover the "locals price" was less than what I paid!. And just between you and me (do not tell anyone else!) Tuesday is half-price for locals. Yep, Two for the price of one. AND you can take your outta-town friends on your locals price -- one local ID can buy 4 tickets. Check it out !! 

That being said -- it is a fun thing to do and NOT scary. Do not be afraid to do this. I am terrified of heights -- chickened out of the zip line at the Rio, but this is not a "ferris wheel." It is a spacious enclosed cabin that moves so slowly that you don't feel it at all. 

One time we did the half-hour-happy hour and the Groupon was good for that because even though we are not big drinkers, we managed to slug back 3 drinks each, so that was a good deal. The bartender was delightful and told us all kinds of inside info on the wheel -- like for instance, what happens if someone has a heart attack or gets seriously ill? How fast can they whip this puppy around in an emergency?

One time, just by chance, we got there at dusk -- paid the daytime price, but got to see the sun set over the mountains. Beautiful. I've been there at night and also in the day time. It's lovely every time. 

This really is a Las Vegas treasure. Treat yourself. 

OH -- and wait -- after you get off, walk back toward the parking area and there is a big machine where you can take your own picture and post it right to Facebook. Check it out!

We booked a pod for my daughter's wedding thru the group sales group. They were hard to work with. They ended up double billing us for the pod. In addition we had requested the option of turning off the videos so we could record the ceremony without the background noise. The request did not get processed and the video remained on.
We requested a reduction in the fee for their mistake. It took 3 weeks for the reduction and we had to file complaint to credit card company to fix the double fee. 
To be fair it was a great ride just noisy for a wedding ceremony. It would a great ride either as an individual fee. The group sales folks are the problem.

The high roller isn't for everyone. It's fun to experience it once. I have gone a number of time and being a local in Las Vegas I've gone so much cause it has been free. Today work took us for fun and it was fun I love that they play music now. It better during night because of the lights but to each there own. If your scared of heights don't go if your claustrophobic  don't go.

We went to the High Roller for a special event, my Birthday.  Some friends of ours and we rented a limousine, went to a high end restaurant for dinner and then on to the High Roller to end the evening.  My wife had purchased Groupon coupons for the adults to enjoy the happy half hour while on the High Roller.  When we got to the Linq we found out that the Groupon needed to be exchanged at the Concierge desk and not at the High Roller ticket counter.  While at the High Roller ticket counter I explained to the person behind the desk that we had one 18 year old and two children under 12.   He told me the 18 year old needed a ticket and the two under 12 did not.  I asked about the Groupon for the Happy Half Hour and that is when we were told about the need to redeem the Groupon at the Concierge.  He also told me the next Happy Half Hour car was going to be available at 8:10 PM.  I then proceeded to the Concierge where I exchanged the Groupon and once again explained the situation, four adults and three children.  No comment was made other than have a good time.  

When we got to the area where you board the High Roller we gave them our tickets and were told that the children would have to board a separate car because no one under 21 was allowed on the Happy Half Hour car!   First we had been told of this rule - in Las Vegas??? Give me a break....  So we asked to speak to a manager.  He showed up and was totally indifferent to our situation.   We asked why no one at the ticket counter had told us about the rule?  He didn't know....   We asked about getting a comped drink from the High Roller bar, he said no.  We asked about refunds, he said there was nothing they could do about Groupon because they don't "get any money from them".  Again, give me a break.....   This situation could have easily been resolved with a few comped drinks.  The Manager was very rude in his approach to us, offering that we should have "a nice night" in a very insincere tone.  The High Roller customer service is terrible and they clearly don't care about their customers.  

The overall experience wasn't all that great anyway, no better than going to the bar at the top of the Stratoshpere.

Buyers beware!

I took a ride around the High Roller Ferris Wheel at the LinQ in Las Vegas this past week.  I thought it was pretty cool and observed excellent views of The Strip and surrounding hotels.  The price was $24.95 plus a $2.00 handling fee (yes strange I know).  Why don't they just raise the price to $26.95 and make people feel better and not think they are being taken advantage of!  This was the admission price for adults before 6:00 p.m. as after that time the charge increases by $10.00 for those wanting to ride a night.  We had a buy one get one free coupon from the hotel which saved us one admission.

The Ferris wheel claims to be the largest one ever built at over 500 feet and with 28 capsules which according to the staff can hold up to 40 passengers each.  I was with 4 other people on my ride.  We were not cramped at all, but I cannot see 40 passengers being shoved into one of these capsules.  Crazy!  I can't imagine more than 10-15 per capsule.

The ride was smooth and some capsules have their own bar inside.  The views were great and we were on and off in about 35 minutes.  There are large mazes built into the rooms that you pass through getting to the loading area.  Someone had ideas of massive crowds when the built this thing.  There were very little people there at 5:30 pm when we were there.  Overall, it's worth doing once.

This place needs to burn to the bloody ground. I had to go to four windows to try to get my living social tickets redeemed, then the elevators are not handicapped accessible unless you have an employee with you. The whole place is a maze with no directions. The loud music that they blare to cater to unwashed miscreants with shitty music taste is completely unnecessary. The London eye puts this place to shame. Never again.

Fun & neat way to see a different view of the city. Way over priced especially since there is no child's price. I am still glad we did it once but if you are on a budget you may want to reconsider. The ticket purchase booth is oddly far from the entrance & confusing with the 10 minute increments. I purchased my tickets & a friend behind me could not get the same time because that time had past. We asked before he purchased & they said it was ok & we didn't have a problem. Not sure what the purpose of the times on the ticket are. We heard the fit about 40+ people in each pod but only had about 12 in ours. That was pretty much the perfect amount & hopefully they won't ever go over 20 unless specifically requested. More than about 15 would start to restrict your ability to move around freely with out bumping into others.

This was an awesome experience. You are in a climate control sphere at the center of the strip. We bought our tickets for this at Paris. I highly recommend doing this. For $30, you can go to the top of the Eiffel Tower (anytime) and a ride (any time) on the high roller.  This is highly recommended because if you were to ride the High roller alone at night it would cost more than that. You can bring whatever you want to drink, so don't waste money on the bar option, and buy everything beforehand. We went to a gift shop on the strip and bought beers for $4 and drank the entire time.
A little pricy (about $70 for two after 6pm). Awesome view. We had no line on a Wednesday night. If you use the flash when taking a pic it will glair off the glass... Just a heads up
Omg so much fun! I did the open bar and it was worth every penny! A must try while in Vegas !!!

One to the best ways to see Vegas other than a helicopter ride and a lot cheaper. 

I knew I had to give this a shot. I've been on the London Eye and was amazed being able to take in the whole city nice and slow so I knew I'd enjoy the Vegas skyline. Plus, as we do everything in 'Murica, our ferris wheel is bigger so....there's that.

I wouldn't recommend buying your tickets at the attraction as they tend to be a little more expensive. The pricing structure is a little confusing depending on where you purchase them from. We had a $5.00 off coupon and tried to use it purchasing our tickets at the box office of the hotel. The lady allowed us to buy a flex pass which let us ride anytime we wanted and only cost us $30 for two, which was cheaper than using the coupon. Odd.

Anyway, we got to the Roller and the prices at the door varied. The most expensive one included car with an open bar for $15.00 extra. Now, I can pound some beer but the ride is only 30 minutes so I didn't want to spend the time shotgunning beer like my younger days. If you do want alcohol, you can purchase a drink in the bar located there before you get on.

The price for a regular car is a little cheaper but still more expensive than the ones I purchased at the hotel box office so I do recommend doing it my way. (To quote Sinatra)

Now, you do have to remember, no matter how much fun activities are with alcohol, there's always people on here who have never been to Vegas and think they are the most entertaining individual to set foot in this city since Wayne Newton. Do them like you do other drunks; don't laugh at them or encourage them and they'll hush. (Unless they fall down or vomit, then you laugh, and laugh, and laugh......)

Anyhow, tips to remember:

Don't buy tickets at the attraction.

Nighttime ride is the best time.

Don't encourage the drunks.

Highlights: 

1) 30 Minutes ride in a glass-lined capsule! Who said rides are just for kids.

2) The 360-degree view down the strip and beyond was tremendous. 

3) The capsule: 
 -- Spacious and cool.
 -- Onboard video showing the altitudes and some major landmarks during the ride.)
 -- Limited seating area. 
 -- Las vegas themed playlist in the background. 

4) I flew solo on the midnight ride ( $31.95 from vegas.com.) I had a blast and it was so much fun. I bet it would be more romantic if... oh well!

5) It nice to be over the strip, not on the strip, for a change!



Next time I'm in Vegas I'll take another sky-bound adventure, probably during daytime.

Four and half Yelps
Our bartender was awesome and personable! We also had great company in the pod we were in. For all you can drink, it is worth cost!

Last night my family and I enjoyed a fun time on the high roller! We bought our tickets on groupon which gave us 2 for 1 drinks, 2 for 1 photos, 15% off at the store && 2 tickets for 65$ .... What a deal.

We printed out the groupons went up to the bar got our drink, walked over to go up to the pods && we were told we had to go back down and redeem them for tickets ... The line was so long!!! However Lonisha, the sweetest lady ever, walked us to a small VIP area to get it done quick. She chit chatted with us while we got out tickets and walked us back up. They also gave us 3 additional 2 for 1 drinks which was very nice!!

The pods have plenty of room even on a busy night, the tvs around the pod show you all kinda of fun stuff to know like: how high you are, where you are on the wheel, a building time lapse && many more. Beautiful views, especially when bellagio has the water show going.

Had a wonderful time on the high roller and we will be back! Thankyou for the great costumer service.

Love love love the Highroller! The Highroller is located in the Linq which is a nice little hip and cool nook on the strip. Everyone who visits Vegas should check out the Highroller. 

My boyfriend took me on the Highroller on one of our dates. The views are amazing! I must admit, I'm deathly afraid of heights, but the pods are so big and you move so slowly that it didn't bother me at all. I highly recommend checking it out.

Happy Hour on the High Roller is definitely the way to do it! I got mine on Groupon! The half hour ride takes you around once so make sure you have your cameras ready after about 13-14 minutes. We went late at night around 11pm and there was no wait and only about 2 or 3 other couples in our sphere. You can get your drinks and start enjoying the view, take photos as you get higher, have a seat and enjoy another beverage on your way down. I'd love to ride it again! Maybe this time during the day. :)
A must see while in Vegas! Best views, clean and enough time in the pod. Sort of tucked behind the main drag, but worth the walk.

I had a great time here on Christmas Day with my family! 
So I decided to treat my family to the high roller experience for Christmas night. My family has never been on it so it was a new and fun experience. I decided to purchase the tickets online first instead of in person. (It's cheaper online) I purchased the open bar ride which was around $47 per person for Christmas Day. Here's my thoughts on high roller:

1. Open bar (hell yes!!!). You can drink as much as you want. But there is a sign that says you can only order 1 drink at a time. 

2. 30 min for the ride was pretty fast to tell u the truth. I'm not sure if it was really 30 mins but it sure was fast. 

3. View was awesome! It was so beautiful and pretty up on top of high roller. You can see all of Las Vegas and the experience was worth it. 

Ultimately, high roller was great and if it's your first time it's worth trying out. I wouldn't always go every time I'm in Vegas but this time for Christmas Day, it was special with my family. (Mom, dad, and brother loved it) great for first timer!

Pretty cool! I'd say it's a must do. It's massive and you can pretty much see it from all over the strip, so that alone will probably pique your interest.  We purchased our tickets on Groupon because it was slightly cheaper.  It ended up being an excellent idea because the pick up line for the vendor sales was much, much shorter than the general line for tickets.  We went on a Saturday night so we were expecting the crowds that many other yelp reviews speak of.  We saw no such thing.  Yes, it was quite a bit of hoops and hurdles to actually get up to the wheel, but barely any line.  We stopped at the bar and got our drinks and were on our way about 5 minutes later.  The whole place was very well-organized and fully staffed.  I was a little freaked out getting on the wheel when I saw that it doesn't actually stop... you need to kind of run on along with a huge group of people, which made me nervous. Nobody touch me! lol.

It takes about 30-35 minutes to make it's way all the way around.  Each pod holds about 40 people. We only had about 20 in ours, so it wasn't bad.  The first 10 minutes are a little boring because you can't see much yet.  But man once you start getting up to the top... beautiful views of the strip and beyond! You go up so high, it makes most of the gigantic hotels seem so small. Amazing photo ops. There were some annoying people who stayed in the prime viewing spot the entire ride, so we had to evict them to the other side of the pod for a bit, lol.

Overall, I enjoyed our visit. I think it's kind of a do once type of thing, especially with the higher pricing.. so I don't know that I'd go again. But everyone should go at least once!

Amazing! The views were spectacular! If you are a local make sure to ask for the discount it was such a fun ride! And they take your picture before to make you feel like a movie star it was such a great experience I would definitely do it again. The ride does take 30 minutes and there is very limited seating. We were lucky to get one that wasn't very full but that is not always the case so you must be okay with standing

My friends and I came to Las Vegas for a bachelorette party. We had heard great things about the high roller and decided to give it a try. It was $32 a person (pretty sure we got the group discount, though). 

This was probably one of the best things we did because the view was amazinggggg. We went about 7:30pm and the view of the city was incredible. Coming from someone who can sometimes be afraid of heights, I thought I might have a panic attack at some point because you are soooo high up. Each "pod" (because I don't know what they are really called) holds up to 30 people. Driving by it you would never believe each pod holds 30 people, but it does. There was 9 of us in one pod with plenty of room to walk around. The only thing I didn't like was inside each one were several tv's hanging up which told you how high you were off the ground. This made me a little nervous knowing how high up I was but I just tried to ignore it as much as possible. Honestly, I was surprised at how slow the wheel turns. It takes exactly 30 minutes to complete from the time you get in the pod until the time you get out (to make the full circle). Very slow moving. Definitely enjoyed the view!! If you are scared of heights though, this probably isn't your thing.

First of all, if you walk in the front door, they will ask for $53 for two people. If you buy the tickets online at their very own website, it's $39.90.  Typical Vegas "screw you every way we can", so I am not particularly surprised.
We went around noon. There were no lines, but a lot of walking through qeue aisles where lines would usually be. I'd never wait that long for this attraction.
When we got to the wheel, there was just one other couple waiting. I asked the attendant if we could just wait for the next pod so we could ride alone.  The attendant said "No you must all get on this one". I looked behind me at the vast empty space of qeues with no one waiting. "Really? There is no one behind us. No one coming"
She just restated her position more forcefully.
I gave up. As we got in our pod, I looked back and noted that a full 4 pods went empty before someone else got on.  I really didn't think the request was out of line.  The smugness that the employee exhibited made it even worse. Bad form!
The ride - meh.  Take a picture out of your airplane when you leave and save $40-53.  Actually, this thing is so far off the strip, we got a better view from our hotel room.  Better yet, go up to the top of the Stratosphere(higher) and not only enjoy the view, but enjoy some rides.  This ride was so boring that they have screens all in the pods with trivia and movies to keep you entertained.

With my family,  I hate highs.  This futuristic looking Eggloo is too huge for my camera to take a shot of the whole wheel,  it's  13 dollars to ride at the daytime and 12 and under are always free to ride,  in the evenings it's 32 dollars.  I like it the cheap  way so I  can see everything,  but I  will try the evening ride some other time .  I still don't like high places but this one feels ok for some odd reason.

I can only give this a 4-star rating...perhaps closer to 3-1/2 stars...why you ask?

This is really just a slow motorized observation deck...and the couple you share the pod with...20 out of town vacationers who have been in the 100+ heat all day, and a couple gamblers who have been drinking since before breakfast...makes the next 30-minutes a little uncomfortable.

I did enjoy the High Roller, but for the cost I expected something a little bit different.

A little history of the making of the High Roller...I was in Shanghai China at a company called ZPMC...these are the same people who fabricate those..."Huge Container Cranes" that we see in our Ports (Los Angeles, Long Beach, Seattle, etc ) unloading those huge ships. Their steel structures division was building the High Roller. How awesome was it to see this underway...and the USA Engineering Firm inspecting everything...Smith Emery Company from Los Angeles and San Francisco. Both firms are outstanding. This is a top notch engineered marvel...you need to ride this at least once. So why not 5-stars...

...for $35 you can wait in a huge line, have a drink (extra $), and spend 30-minutes with 25 sweaty folks sharing the space in the pod...well, for me there isn't enough ventilation, I felt starved for oxygen. Maybe at other times of the day it is better, or perhaps in the later evening. 

When it was all said and done, for me anyway, I was satisfied in having rode the ride, but for the money I just expected something a little bit different.

It was fun and I'd do it again, however, there was no wine on the happy hour.  No big deal because there was beer and mixed drinks, but I'd have preferred wine.  The view was great at sunset, the bartender was fun and funny, fast and knowledgeable.  It was a good time.

When I first came down to the Strip, I saw the biggest Ferris Wheel I have ever seen. I later learned that it is The High Roller. Everyone bought a groupon for each couple in order to save money. Then, we simply checked ourselves in and hopped right onto it. The section is cool. There is a tv with promotions and advertisements, and the music is old school. The bar section has variety of selections, and the bartender's spirit is super energetic. Then again, you need to be upbeat when you serve alcohol to party people. 

The reason why I take a star off from 5-star rating is because I originally thought the high roller would stop one by one for each party to enter into the selected section. However, it doesn't stop, and the guests have to carefully step their feet onto it due to the super slow speed. Keep in mind that the ride will last for about half an hour. 

I personally think it is a bit dangerous to let drunken party people stepping on and off like that because what if they fall down ??? But anyway.... That is what I think. I understand why they have to let the guests stepping on and off while the wheel is still moving because 1) the speed is slow & 2) if they let the guests enter group by group then they have to stop the entire high roller.

The High Roller is the world's largest observatory - a full 550 ft high.  That's about 100 ft higher than London Eye.  It has two prices depending on whether you go day (cheaper) or night.  Regardless you get a nice 360-degree of Vegas.  Keeping you company is a virtual tour guide who's actually funny and not too annoying.

We came here in the afternoon and got our own cabin.  It's a fun experience and worth trying once.  It moves real slow and is not intimidating, even if you don't like heights.

Also cool is the entrance with various Halloween-themed puppets and a real cool launch pad room that simulates a night-club environment.

I am probably in the minority of people here but I had major issues on the High Roller which I have actually never experienced in my life so I would like to share for people doing their research like I did before going on this. 

I do NOT have a fear of heights. I do get motion sickness but you can NOT feel this moving at all because it has stabilizers. I also put motion sickness patches on just in case. I have never found myself to be claustrophobic but for some reason, being in this pod made me feel just that. As soon as the doors closed, I felt terrified because I felt trapped inside and I knew there was no getting off for at least thirty minutes. I guess it was my lack of control and not having any sort of air. I started to feel queasy so I looked around and there were no trash cans so then I was even more nervous that I was going to get sick and there wouldn't be anywhere for that to happen. There absolutely should be a trash can in each pod! Especially if people can drink alcohol on these things. I can't imagine being stuck on it with puke. Bleh!

I tried to enjoy the views but because the glass is doubled, it's a distorted view instead of a clear glass view which made things much worse for me. It did stop a couple of times and knowing we weren't moving also gave me angst. My Mom gets motion sickness and she was absolutely fine. She didn't have any problems at all. 

There are bathrooms just before you get on so you don't need to worry about finding them outside somewhere. There is a souvenir shop you get dumped into at the end.

We went during the day and shared one pod with a family of 8. There was plenty of room for us to move around and take pictures. You can sit or stand. It does not stop for you to get on or off...it continues to move slowly so you need to pay attention! 

I didn't find the views that exciting. Maybe it's because we already had a gorgeous view of the mountainside from our hotel room? I don't know. I enjoyed the Eiffel Tower experience much better than this. It's something that I guess is nice to do at least once...or once during the day and once at night? I personally would never do it again. 

The video running throughout the ride is pretty corny. I guess he's trying to be funny but I think he could just give facts without all of the irritating sarcasm and the corny jokes. 

There is an emergency button you can push if necessary. There is also a spot on the floor that pulls up where you can find "emergency supplies."

At the end my Mom joked around that we got a free ride and it was going around again. I told her I would claw myself out of the door before I went around again. I couldn't wait to get off! I stayed sick for several hours after. I felt extremely nauseous. Wish we didn't do it so we could have enjoyed the rest of the day!

Okay guys. . .  this one is for you. I got the bright idea to propose to my beautiful gf at the tippy top of the High Roller. One problem. . .  you don't realize how big this damn thing is until you get right up on it. I did not want to punk out so I just used my hand as a visor so I could not see how high it was. We finally got to our open bar car and off we went. Our bartender (some 65 year old guy) would not shut the hell up!!!!!! Meanwhile I was planted on one of the bench seats trying to go to my happy place (golf green, Hooters, Monday Night Football, etc. . .). We were with another couple from back east and our bar guy who was bragging about how he was in some stupid bartending flair competition. . .  blah blah blah. I just focused on the bar in front of me and tried to block out all the high improbable disasters that could happen. When we got to the top I managed enough courage to finally move from the bench and get on one knee to do the deed. She said yes!!! My girl crying the rest of the way down was a nice distraction to the horror I was experiencing. Yes, I am a little afraid of heights but all the other reviews said you don't even notice it moving. Lies!!!! You just keep going higher and higher and it just sucked. Anyway we finally made it to the ground and the rest is history.

If you are afraid of heights this is probably not for you. Hey guys, propose at the fountains or at the foot of the Eiffel Tower.

This is seriously a must-do in Vegas. Tallest observation wheel in the world! I'm a sucker for all things ferris wheel, so I was really jazzed about this. Check around for discounts prior to walking in, as a daytime ride will set you back about $25, with prices increasing after 5PM. I believe discounted tix are available for locals online (half off!!) and a few dollars off when purchasing a ticket online for non-locals. The ride is super smooth - it takes the full half hour to make a complete trip, so you barely notice any movement. We rode during day before lunch on a weekday, and had a whole car to ourselves. I enjoyed being able to see the mountains off in the distance, but I suspect a night time view would have its own merits. There are two little seats on the inner edges of the wheel, so if you feel a bit woozy you can have a sit.  

Only downside? The 'announcer' on the televisions within the car was turned up REALLY loud, and ended up being kind of annoying. I did like that they tell you when you've reached the top, and give you some historical facts about the area, but there was no way to adjust the audio. Make sure to use the restroom before entering the pod. 

Great views of the city!!

It is gorgeous day or night but I preferred night time due to the lights. I'm afraid of heights yet didn't feel scared at all. It moves so slowly that you don't feel the movement at all. The view is breathtaking. Strongly suggest riding. If you like alcohol there are certain pods that have a bar in the middle that you can drink on during the cycle of the ride. The souvenir pics are expensive but worth it. Lovely.

You feel like you are on top of the world flying and you get to see ALL of Vegas. 
Tip - purchase a ticket on the bar pod and get unlimited drinks for 30 minutes for only $15 more.

The High Roller remains incredible.  It also remains pricy...but mostly incredible. :-)  This time, I rode it in the evening and had beautiful sunset views.  Despite the price, this Ferris wheel remains on my must-do list for each visit to Vegas.

Goodness, what's with the price?

The views are phenomenal, dialogue is helpful, but the price is terrible. Especially considering the length of time you spend on this thing. We paid $35/person for a 30 minute ride. The line moves very fast and we purchased our tickets a few minutes before riding, not too shabby. However, the price. I understand it's pricier at night due to popularity and nice views of the the strip and all of the pretty lights. 

Would I pay that much again? No way! Try to scout some cheaper tickets. They put these on Groupon every now and then or buy them online for a promotion. 


Views are great, price is unreasonable!

It's a big wheel. 

Are you a Ferris wheel freak? Then this might be your thang, 

Stratosphere rides offer a much more extensive view.
Not worth the hype, there are no strip views . You will feel like you got caged in a slow moving Jail. Go to Hakkassan with same money

Personally this is not for me but I am giving it three stars because I realize I was able to ride this for Free due to the Veterans day special they were offering to give Active Duty / Veterans free Ticket for them plus a guest which is such a awesome deal.  If I had paid full price for my ticket I imagine I would of left with a worse taste in my mouth because this thing is honestly very slow and not nearly as intimate as I had imagined. The pods are roomy because they don't JAM it packed with people but it includes very little space to sit and our pod had a little toddler that ended up dumping my purse everywhere when my friend was taking our photo. The view is truly amazing and I think if you're going to pony up the $ it is worth doing the ride that is at night. If I had to ever ride this again though I would definitely go with the VIP ride that includes open bar because at least I would feel like I was doing something. I am more of a fast paced personality and I don't really "relax" and take in the view all that well especially with their TV monitors blaring that annoying guys voice with fun trivia facts. Overall everyone that worked that evening was super friendly and I did end up buying the photo at the end because it was a pretty good special they were running for three photos it was $35 plus the frame . Since my ticket was free I figured why not? especially since I don't plan on rushing back to the wheel anytime soon.

Wow! What a view!

Not really sure what to say here except that this is a must do when going to Vegas.

It is the highest observation wheel in the world, 107 feet higher than the one in London. We went at night and the view was absolutely amazing. One of my friends had to get talked into going as he wasn't sure if it would be worth it. Afterwards he thanked us repeatedly for talking him into it and talked about it the rest of the trip.

It is more expensive at night, and probably at little overpriced at $35 (plus tax) but I don't regret it at all. I understand that you can get discounts if you stay at the Quad or another hotel (but not all Harrah's hotels) and they regularly have Groupon deals, so keep your eyes open.

It is cheaper during the day, but go at night, trust me!

Some important things to know:

1 - it takes 30 minutes to get all the way around, not including the wait in line if it is busy.
2 - there are no bathrooms in the pods, so tinkle before you go.
3 - there are 2 benches in the pods, but you won't want to sit down.
4 - if you time it correctly you can see the fountains at the Bellagio and it is awesome!
5 - the pods can accommodate up to 40 people so your whole group can get in the same pod. If you go during the off hours (we went after 11pm) they put fewer people in each pod which is nice.

If you are reading these reviews you are thinking about going. Stop thinking and just do it!

It was a FANTASTIC view of the surrounding parking lots!!  I will saw however the price is right for locals!  Just $12.50 a person. The view from the top was quite underwhelming. I'd love to see it at night, just to see the contrast.

Sorry High Roller, you overlook way too many parking lots. This doesn't come even close to the London eye. It over looks Vegas mostly when you reach the top. Overall the ride is comfortable and enjoyable but certainly not the best I have been on so far. The staff is friendly and informative.

I've been to vegas multiple times since this ferris wheel went up and never did I think I would find myself on it. We were in vegas for my friends 30th birthday and before we went, were researching things to do. A friend of mine heard from her coworker that the High Roller had a happy (half) hour option where you get an open bar for the 30 minutes you're on the ferris wheel. That was the nudge we needed to get us to go! 

I booked tickets on their website ahead of time. There was an online deal for 5 dollars off each ticket. I highly recommend booking online ahead of time - we were able to bypass the long line for purchasing tickets or redeeming vouchers and make our way straight up! A few tourist grap photos (that we, like good tourists, ended up purchasing ;) ) later, we were in line for the next happy hour car. There was another group of about 6-7 and a group of 3-4 with us. Even with all these people and a bar in the middle of the car, we weren't cramped for space or deprived of any views.

Our bartender was Tara and she was wonderful! She had cups filled with ice ready as we got on. Once we were on, she quickly explained what she had and worked so fast to give us all our first round. She clearly understood that the ride was only 30 minutes and wanted to help us get the most out of the open bar if we wanted. She was great!

The views are amazing. We went during the day and loved it and I can just imagine how beautiful the views are if you're on the night one (or better yet, if you're up there right around sunset).

I'm sure it's great to go on this ferris wheel in general, but if you're going ( and are 21+ and like to drink .. I'm sure most people do in vegas), I HIGHLY recommend the happy hour option. And, as I said before, I recommend buying your tickets ahead of time online.

The high roller was so much more than I expected! We used the Groupon for the night time happy hour (open bar for 30 minutes). The ride is so smooth you can barely tell you're moving! The views are pretty hard to beat. Our bartender was awesome. He had our drinks waiting on us as soon as we finished. He had a great personality. The cabin had lots of space and benches to sit down. We had about 12 people in our cabin and it was comfortable. This is a must do in Vegas and I will be back!

I purchased the 'Happy Half Hour' package for a night round on this gargantuan ferris wheel. 30 minute turn of the wheel in an enclosed dome and open bar. 
The other people were a lot of fun to talk to, from all walks of life. The bartender was friendly and very quick with the pours. He was slightly surprised as how quickly I was drinking. I'll make sure to make my money worth it, sir. Being Canadian is the natural ability to handle that amount of alcohol.
The view was incredible. You start to lose yourself in the splendor of the sights at that height. The lights of nighttime Vegas are a thing to see, and this was a great way to see them. Terrific views & tasty booze.
Nice thing to do in Vegas! Nice view, nice ride, nice employees. Probably won't do it again.

Worst of TSA attitude meets Tallest Observation Wheel in the World (until someone else builds one a few feet taller).  I went on the High Roller with a friend and once was enough.  At the pinnacle, I wondered if maybe I was being too harsh when someone stated, "I have a better view from my room".   Once is enough.

I was pretty psyched to find out this would be open when I paid a visit to Las Vegas last week.  This was definitely on my TO DO list while visiting, plus I'm always down for something new as I visit every year.

We got there pretty late on a Tuesday night - I don't recall what time this thing runs till but it was after a late dinner.

I knew before going that it was going to cost me $35.  We have something kind of similar in Chicago at Navy Pier, I can't recall how much that costs but it is NOTHING compared to the High Roller...it's more like a carnival ferris wheel.  Yes, it's worth $35 because not only do I only visit once, but the view is AMAZING!!! Best view in Vegas as I've been to Voodoo Lounge, the clubs at the top of the Palms, no view compares to this view!  

As other reviews have mentioned...you pay at a kiosk outside, it's $35 at night.  You cannot bring drinks with you, but you will pass a bar before going up.  I HAD to get a drink on my way in...and I want to say a blue moon cost me about $7.  As with every tourist attraction everywhere they take your picture before you go on, and you exit through a store where you can see your picture if you'd like to purchase it.  I don't even recall looking at ours when we left as I've been through that routine too many times.

We had NO wait whatsoever during this entire experience - probably being late on a Tuesday night and all really helped.  

I read another review that suggested standing to the right in the pod when you enter so I did...I'd have to say that IS the best spot.  Our pod had about 10 people are so and it was easy to move about in there.  The timing was just right as well as we were able to catch the Bellagio Fountain show once we hit the top.

If you have never been to Vegas or haven't been there in a long time, or visiting soon...I highly recommend this tourist attraction, it's really amazing!

A neat ONE TIME experience but not worth $36
550 feet up at the very top and funny commentary inside the cabin
Daytime is cheaper than night time, of course.
Kids 12 and under are free.
They offer $5 Military and they also have a local discount that is almost 1/2 off

This was my forth time going in the High Roller. I've done both day and night rides with one Happy Half Hour ride taking place during the night and now one during the day. If you're not 21 or over than you're missing out because the Happy Half Hour is the best way to go on the High Roller. 

What's not to enjoy about having unlimited drinks for half an hour. It takes thirty minutes for your cabin to go around full circle so knocking back drinks is a great way to spend the time in addition to checking out a great view of Vegas. If you're afraid of heights then chances are a friend or family member convinced you to ride. No worries! having drinks to your disposal will surely take your mind off of it or at least calm you a bit. The High Roller is also a good way to meet people. You'll be in the cabin with a random group of people just looking to have a good time just as you. Some more chatty than others and some simply hilarious. 

Keep in mind if you purchase tickets for the Happy Half Hour during the day, the cost is less and you can show up unannounced at anytime to ride as long as it's before 6pm. Night rides require you to choose a time slot to ride. 

You can always bring your own drinks on the High Roller but for $35, The Happy Half Hour is worth it. I spend that much alone on just a few drinks if not two anywhere else in Vegas within the same amount of time. I'll take "unlimited drinks" for 500 Alex!

High Roller 3/18/2017

My fiancee and I took a ride on the High Roller and it was incredible!! I honestly cannot recommend this experience enough.

We took our ride around 5pm on a weekday. It was not busy and we were the only 2 people in our pod. I was scared at first, but the observation wheel moved very smoothly and at a steady pace so it was difficult to tell we were actually moving. I do not recommend looking straight down - that made me motion sick.

It was amazing to see Vegas and the surrounding desert and mountains in the daylight. We took some incredible photos and it was a very relaxing experience - a nice change of pace from the hustle and bustle of the strip.

The High Roller runs until 1-2am so riders can view the lights of the strip as well. The is also an all-you-can-drink offer in the evening; certain pods have small bars in the them.

There are always deals for the High Roller on websites like Get My Perks and Living Social so be sure to check online prior to purchasing tickets.

An amazing experience for first time visitors and returning vacationers. I definitely want to ride the High Roller at night on my next visit to Vegas.

The ride itself takes about a half hour to make a complete circle, if you are of age, I would HIGHLY recommend getting the bar gondola thing! The drinks are included in the price so it makes it well worth it (I probably downed around 7 mixed drinks lol) Just be warned however, go to the bathroom BEFORE you get on! Otherwise you will be doing the pee pee dance lol
This IMO is one of the MUST do's in Las Vegas!

Wenn man in LV ist ist der Highroller ein Muß! Sagenhafter Blick , eine Umdrehung dauert ca. eine halbe Stunde, man kann sich nicht satt sehen. Wir waren tagsüber drinn und hatten einen wahnsinns Ausblick!

Amazing feat of engineering. Magnificent views. Only drawback was drunken screaming woman in our pod. Bring earplugs and patience if you value anything less than a low roar. 
All in all, the tremendous structure and the 360* views of the entire valley and beyond trumped the loud mouthed inconsiderate twit we were locked in with.

This is a must do for a first time Vegas visitor.  We bought tickets ahead of time but that doesn't save you time in line.  They usher everyone into the same long line where you have to wait for paper tickets.  So don't try to save time by buying ahead of time unless you are getting a good discount.  The workers all seem to dislike their jobs and the video on the tram is very obn
If you're going with a significant other I recommend going at 1 AM. There's not that many people. And you can bring your drinks inside. The view is breathtaking.

The high roller gives you a unique experience of getting to see an aerial view of all of Vegas. So in that regard it was pretty cool.  But I think once is enough for me.  My husband and I got lucky on our timing and managed to get happy hour prices to the adult cabin, but so did about ten other people... and they just kind of pack you in.  Honestly, unless you only want a couple of drinks, it's not worth it. The bartender was pleasant, and tried to keep up, but it's Vegas, and with that many people it was hard.

CHERISH YOUR TIME... SAVE YOUR $$ !!   
This can be summed up in 1 word...  "BORING"  or is a better word, "UNEVENTFUL"?? .. 

Here are the facts...   It's located 1 block OFF the Strip and BEHIND all the Hotels!  You don't get any views until you are past the 10 minute mark .. The you get 10 minutes of "Decent" views, but NOT "Spectacular" SRTIP VIEWS! ... Then 10 minutes of BORING, "Can't wait to get off" views!

They are Giving away lots of discount and FREE tickets, so if you pay full price for this thing... "Tsk-Tsk".  Instead... Go to the Stratosphere or maybe the Eifel Tower .. 

I'm a long time fan of the Caesar's Properties but they are going downhill FAST!  (I say, "Bring the Mob back to Vegas!.. They wore tuxedos, knew how to entertain, gamble, and comp!).  God Bless Frank Sinatra!
Spectacular View of the city!! More fun if you came with a big party.  Just a hint, the best seat is right on the left faving the city.

It's a 30 minute ride so use the bathroom before you get on. The view in the evening is pretty spectacular.  You get to see all of Las Vegas at 550 ft up! Kinda pricey but definitely a thing to do with the fam at least once.

Awesome experience. Highly recommended. Amazing view of Vegas. We bought open bar tickets - some of the cars (not sure how many) have small bars inside. It was great but I had wished I hadn't already started drinking beforehand.

Souvenir green screen photos available.

I finally got to ride the High Roller without being sore the next morning! =P The Linq is now open and it's a neat little alley that connects the strip to the High Roller. My friends and I bought our tickets from two employees of the High Roller next to a kiosk machine near the entrance to the Linq. One of our friends credit cards wasn't working so he couldn't buy a ticket at the Kiosk. The High Roller employees said we'd have to pay at the High Roller store (I'm not sure that's what you'd call it, but it's next to the Ferris wheel). We walked to the store to discover there's a $2.00 processing or handling fee. However, the ticket is cooler from the store. So, if you want a souvenir ticket, buy from the store right next to the High Roller. If you want to save a couple bucks, buy it from the kiosk near the strip. Also, it should be noted day rides are $10 cheaper than night rides. 
Boarding the ride is pretty cool. You're ushered through a corridor of line mazes (there was no line when we went but I'm sure that's going to change). You CAN take drinks on it and make the ride more of a party. There's a bar when you're walking through the corridor so you can get your not-too-over-priced beverage before you board. 
The ride itself isn't hard to board. It's always moving but very slowly. There's a safety net below, just in case one of your friends is too drunk and falls. The ride takes 30 minutes to complete. In 15 minutes you're at the top at 550 feet looking down on Vegas. It's a truly unique view of the strip. I think some of the casinos are going to have to vamp up their roofs! The Quad returns to Imperial Palace status from the top of The High Roller! I didn't have a problem taking dozens of pictures of Vegas from inside our pod. You have to get your camera close to the glass if you don't want any glare. 
The ride sounds pretty safe from what one of the employees told me. In case of a power outage, the High Roller has 2 back-up generators. If the secondary fails, then there's a third. If someone were to have a heart attack or other issue, they can double the speed and reverse the ride, depending on where you are in the circular rotation. The employee said the fire department ran a few drills on the The High Roller a few days before they opened in case something happened and the Ferris wheel stopped by an unforeseeable event. They were able to get to each pod.
Stop reading my review and just ride it already ;)

The ride was about 30-40 minutes long but I can't say I was impressed. You pay for a view that you already get from your hotel rooms (luckily we won the ride and didn't have to pay)!!! Security was extremely rude and honestly can't say well ever go back

Fun!  We had great views of the strip and a comical, knowledgeable and engaging bar tender.  My only suggestion would be to skip the 3 strong shots they give you during the 30 minute ride.  If you take all three you might not have the same fun experience that I did, lol.

Definitely a good place to go for some nice views of the city and to get out of the heat. The pods are big and air-conditioned. The ride is approximately 30 minutes long and goes at a slow leisurely pace.

Buy your tickets online at their website to save a few bucks and to avoid waiting in long lines to purchase.

The happy hour tickets are worth it. The drinks are unlimited, the bartenders are fast and nice, and the atmosphere is a ton of fun!!!
Received free tickets from a vender. Box office would not accept them because of problems with counterfeit vouchers. Waste of a trip to the strip and definitely not worth paying full price for.

We had a great time. We did not actually go on high roller but we walked around the promenade and very much enjoyed out time there. We also went over to Caesars Palace and also the Flamingo and of course the Linq Hotel.  The magic of Matt Franco (last years winner of Americas got talent and he is FANTASTIC !!! ) is at the Linq hotel and you can get a package deal for 75.00 + fees for the show and a anytime ride of the high roller !!! Tuesdays are half price for locals on the high roller . Prices are 26.95 day and 36.95 night. Each sphere holds up to 40 people. You can also rent it for a party !!! Remember there is valet parking which is so convenient. Just a hint also, stand on the right side of cabin for the best views ! (My friends told me) So visit the linq and have a selfie taken on their 2 big screens also. You will have fun, and there is lots of security walking around as well. Enjoy !!!! Keep a eye on groupon for deals.
A must do.....it felt great seen the view of las vegas that high....recommended. ..only things is only 30 minutes short...

Like the "in-flight" video guy suggested, this is definitely in my top 5 observation wheels. Then again, I doubt that I've been on more than 3 or 4...

The High Roller hasn't been open for much more than a year and a half, but it's now a mainstay of the Las Vegas Strip skyline, as it were. I like to point out to friends and family that it's the tallest observation wheel in the world, and I finally got a chance to ride the world's tallest observation wheel when an old high school friend invited me.

I actually found "flex" tickets, valid at all times during operating hours, on the official High Roller web site at a $7 discount (regularly $36.95 all day for adults), so I ended up snagging those tickets while my friend took care of dinner. At first glance, a dollar per minute is not a terrible deal for a tourist attraction. However, consider that a few minutes on both ascent and descent are spent in a relatively poor position for viewing. That leaves the effective amount of prime viewing time at closer to 15-20 minutes than the full half hour.

Those online printouts counted as tickets, so we were waved through multiple areas by friendly employees, with only one stop for ticket scanning. They didn't double-check with our ID's, so I guess I could've gone in with a ticket for "Seymour Butts."
