There are two labyrinthine line areas, but the chains are adjusted in times of low traffic so that you can cut almost straight through the potentially snaking path. When you finally reach the outdoor waiting area, note that the nearer gate is for the "half happy hour" (aka drinking) tickets, and the farther gate is for us normal folks.

Maybe I wasn't in the right mood entirely, or I could've spent a little less time taking photos. On the other hand, I definitely spent at least a few minutes focusing on enjoying the view, but I wasn't thrilled during those minutes. I've either been desensitized to the sights by familiarity or from watching too many establishing shots during CSI episodes.

I think I could have given it an even lower rating had I not lucked into a relatively uncrowded capsule. I guess dinnertime on a cold, autumnal Saturday evening isn't peak riding time because there were only six of us in there. If it had been been more crowded, it could have been a mess with half of the group being stuck on the non-Strip-view side. Kinda the same dilemma as all of those hotels, isn't it?

I don't know if or when I'll be back on the wheel. Perhaps I'll venture for a daytime ride for comparison's sake, or else I'll strap on a GoPro, pregame, then further enjoy the alcoholic version of the ride. That sounds fun. Otherwise, I'll continue to marvel at the massive, beautiful structure as I drive by or even walk under it. That's the most impressive part of the High Roller to me, not the views from the actual ride.

Disclaimer: my husband's company paid for my ticket, so I'm trying to write this from a "would I pay for it" kind of perspective. If someone else is buying yours, there's definitely nothing wrong with this place-- great views and fun staff :)

We had a good time, but I'm not sure I'd pay this much for it myself. We got $40 group "happy half hour" tickets at night, which meant there was an open bar on the pod for our ride. This _sounds_ great, but the pod fit 20ish people and there was one bartender. Do the math-- it just doesn't sound like a great deal unless you are willing/excited to binge-drink for 30 minutes. 

The other bummer was we waited a long time to get onto a bar-car pod, since only 1/4 or so are equipped for an open-bar experience. We probably stood in line about 45-60 minutes between waiting outside to get the tickets and then again to get on a car. Granted, we were in a large group (we needed 3 pods), so I'm not sure if this was an accurate representation of how long the line typically is.

The bartender was super on top of his game though. We piled on and I cynically figured the business model was to work as slowly as possible so that everyone only has time for 1 drink during the half hour ride. Instead, he caught our attention, told us how this was gonna work, and looked at everyone's ID in record time. He moved from left to right, asked what we wanted, and anyone else who wanted the same thing raised their hands so he could make multiple at once. He even had time to take a photo of the group at the top! You're also allowed to take one "roadie" off the car with you at the end, but don't abuse it-- they are pretty swift to enforce this policy. 

4 stars if someone else is buying, 3 if you're buying. If I was to go again, I'd skip the bar-car version since it seems like you'd get through the line a lot faster and not have to worry about drinking your money's worth in 30 minutes.

We did Happy Half Hour off Groupon, totally worth it.  I wasn't too sure what to expect but I am glad I was able to check that off my list of to-do's in Vegas.  It was better than I had expected.  The view up there is amazing and the bartender inside the pod was super friendly and easy going.  Its only a 30 minute ride (give or take) but was able to have 3 cocktails while inside.  We started our night there and then bar hopped the rest of the night.  The music inside was good and people were friendly over all.  Give it try!

This was such a great ride! The views from the top are stunning and the information provided inside the cabin as the wheel moves is very interesting. It really wouldn't be a trip to Vegas without a ride on the high roller in my opinion.

Beautiful view. Amazing experience. 
The wheel does sometimes tremble, which was kind of scary. It wasn't throughout the whole ride or a lot but you do feel it sometimes. 
I am a person who is afraid of heights but I did feel that if you just look straight ahead and not look down it would just feel like you're looking out of a window from a tall building.
Totally breathtaking!  At the apex you're 550 feet above the strip. You can see everything. Must do!  The only thing I would do different is doing it at night.

I stand corrected!  I thought this Ferris wheel was just another Vegas gimmick, but after my visit today I will admit I was wrong. I was blown away by The Linq and even more impressed with the High Roller ride. The ride was so smooth that we couldn't tell it was moving (even with the high winds). The view was amazing, the pods were spacious, and the area was lively. On this day the line moved pretty fast, so waiting wasn't an issue. The kids loved it, my mother in law loved it and my wife had a great time. I recommend it for any occasion. Already planning to do it again.

Holy cow! What a ride! This attraction was something so different I cannot even begin to start! A groupon deal worth every penny!

In a half hour you go around a gigantic ferris wheel drinking as much as possible! Quite a great time we all had for sure! Yes a big thumbs up!
I mean, how can you go wrong with this view?  I've only been up after dark - my favorite time to look at the Vegas lights.  I bet it's gorgeous during sunset too though.

While looking up vegas attractions I saw a Groupon for the High Roller experience. The high roller includes open bar during your thirty minute ride and is the highest observation point in vegas. The Groupon got me and my friend both on the ride for about $20 less than full price admission. They also offer tickets in pods without a bar for just the view. 

The wheel is open till 2am but they don't take any new riders on after 1am. The line to get your tickets even with groupon was extremely long we waited probably 45 minutes and we were close to not getting on the wheel in to time. 

There were several people in the pod with us and it was a bit cramped to move around and get good pictures. The bartender was very efficient and did a great job getting everyones drinks. They had champagne, several different types of spirits, and beers available. I drank stoli raspberry and club soda. 

The wheel itself moves very slow the total revolution is 30 minutes so do not expect a thrill ride but any means. this is an experience to give you a great view of Las Vegas. I would definitely suggest going at night to see everything all lit up. 

While I enjoyed my experience, the views, and drinks it was definitely something to only do once to get some great photos or if you have vegas newbies in town.

I went here  on my birthday, and  was  locals     only $20 bucks. Went at nite, got really windy but it bareley  moves in the wind. No worries, view is awesome, well worth it  Gonna go  on it in day sometime too. Wonderful view up there. My only beef is it takes forever walking to get on the  ride, and then  TV monitor saying dumb stuff,  but ya know. Well worth the view , and will go on it again. You gotta get on this if your a local.

For some reason I was expecting this to be a cross-breed of a ferris wheel and a roller coaster and its pretty much neither. It's simply an observation pod that goes in ONE circle. 

Cons- 
-You don't really get to choose the people you ride with. You are loaded on with about 15 ppl per pod. 
-Not enough seating, its two little sitting areas on each side of the pod and it fits about 4 people on each side.  I am sure you don't want to sit the entire time but if you do its best to gets a seat facing the loading zone. Everything behind the High Roller is vacant all the lights are in the direction facing where you are loaded on. 
-Photographs will suck! Unless you're taking pics of the scenery with no flash, the reflective glass won't allow you to capture cute photos. I tried a couple of selfies but it's really dark in there and turning on the flash will just light up the whole pod and you still get the window glares in your picture. 

Pros- 
-You can drink while you are on the pod. Drinks can be purchased on your way up towards the loading area. 
-The pods are air conditioned. I am sure during the day it could get unbearably hot so luckily enough it's pretty chilly in the pods. 

One cool feature is if you pay an extra $10 ($44.95 for night time) then you can get the Happy Hour ride where you and your friends get open bar the entire 30 mins of the trip. This seems like the only option one should choose seeing as most of the time you are just idly waiting for the pod to hit the highest point. I think that could be fun with a bunch of friends but it is a bit pricey for just 10 mins of drinks. 

I did like the photo option but it comes out the blue right before the loading area so be on the lookout.

We were little hesitant to ride the high roller Ferris wheel at the link in Las Vegas because of the price but it is an amazing experience! My fiancé and I went on there and it is a perfect date... It was beautiful to see Las Vegas from 550 ft in the air. We seen it all lit up at night and if you have never done it we recommend you at least try it once... We would absolutely do it again! It was a wonderful experience! gorgeous!
This place has a phenomenal view when on top. Must do the open bar high roller. Our bartender was great introduced us to new drinks. We had a full orb to ourselves. Will be back next time in vegas.

It's cool. I'll give the High Roller props for lighting up the strip and allowing you to see everything in the city (better at night). The TV personality explaining the observation wheel and what altitude you've currently reached is a bonus. Only downside is the length and price. They offer local and employee discounts so I can complain about the price but seeing a family of 4 have to shell out $120 is hard to stomach.

Amazing. We did have to wait for a bar car a little longer than expected for 12am on a Thurs but ultimately it as a great experience and the bartender in our car was friendly and definitely accommodating. A must try in vegas! Do the Happy Halfy Hour and get unlimited alcohol during the 30-min ride!

Birthday ride on the High Roller. Being afraid of heights is my issue but with a can do attitude and a nice alcoholic beverage in me (It is Vegas, right?!) I rode it.  Best decision, the pod we were on was not crowded, this was on the 22nd of September.  Evening ride, all the lights in Vegas and the valley beyond, stunning!! We bought our tickets in the Flamingo Hotel, you can buy them at the entrance to the ride but both had lines. There's a bar just inside the entrance, but we bought our drinks at a bar on the promenade to the ride.  A guide escorts you to the ride, with a slight detour to have your picture taken.  Then onto the pods! Fun time at the High Roller!!

The High Roller is a pretty cool way to see the city during the day or the lights of Las Vegas from 550ft up in the air, which is the highest point of the continuously moving ride which takes 30 minutes to complete a full revolution. 

To me it is definitely for the tourists to see Vegas from a different view and all the way around you. As a local I have been to Stratosphere to the top and the Rio at the top so this is a little different to view the city. Which by the way I think doing this once is enough,
 
We went during the day, should have waited to go at night because the lights are so pretty.
Of course being a local I wanted to go when it was not too busy so I figured day time was better.

Over all it was a nice day to go and it was not scary at all, felt safe being in the pod. There was only 4 others in while we were on, so it was almost like having it to ourselves.

If your here Visiting it is something to do for sure if you want to see Vegas from a different View.
I would go on again if someone was here from out of town but to go on for the fun of it probably not.

Its great for the people who love taking photos!

Planned to go on the High Roller and then lucky us, we got free tickets from our hotel.    The line was fast and we only had to wait a few minutes before getting on.  Since we had free tickets we didn't get on the happy hour open bar car (do they call it a car??) but that is ok because they let you bring drinks on with you.  You can actually by drinks right before you get one.  I almost feel like you would want to be on the happy hour car because it looked like the bar cart took up lots of room inside.  Either way, just know that once you are on there is not a bathroom inside so you better be able to hold it for half an hour.  The ride was enjoyable and even though we had a total of about 15 or so people inside it didn't feel too crowded.  The views are nice and there is a little TV thing that tells you how high up you are.  The movement is slow so you hardly feel it.  I am not afraid of heights but I think that if you are this probably wouldn't be very scary to you.  Instead of looking down you are looking out at the hotels so it doesn't feel very high up.  This is a great addition to Vegas.

GO AHEAD DO IT ONCE!!

This is a fun 30 minute outing.  Price is a little steep but it's Vegas, everything is expensive.  $30-$40 per person depending on night or day.  You can purchase tickets, grab a drink from the bar (about $10), and hop on.  It's a fantastic view of Vegas!  It was great to do once, but not sure I would do it again.  There is simply too much to do here to do this more than once.

This is possibly the most incredible deal in Las Vegas and Clark County, Nevada, IF you book your tickets in the bar car. (Check Groupon)

As you ascend from the second story departure area, it's quiet. A few folks are nervous.

30 minutes later, the car is a raucous party, with shots lined up and a number of them consumed, and you probably have made a few friends in the process. 

Just go. This is a must-do in Vegas after the sun sets.

Awesome experience! I went during the day time because my group had the Go Card destination passes. We upgraded for an extra ten bucks for the happy half hour open bar (totally worth it).

Definitely a great thing to do. It was really nice to see the city. And the bartender was awesome.

We had to wait a little longer for a pod with the bar inside to come around but it wasn't too bad of a wait.

Would recommend it to others.

Well some say boring... maybe! Some say too expensive... possibly... some say, a waste of time and money... an opinion!
However for me it was well worth it. Spectacular views, and awesome narrative on he screens that tell a great story. So for me, well worth my time and money. I might even do it again at a different time of the day.
The one suggestion I would have. They have a great narrative of what's going on around you. But there are 8 screens on the car. Show some history! I personally LOVE history and he history of Las Vegas is rich!!! They could have built a timeline and shown some before and after shots of what's been happening in the strip! I think this would have been the only the only think different I would like to have seen.

This is a lot of money for a half hour view of the city. It was supposed to be romantic but we got stuck on there with two very intoxicated people who were very loud and kept talking to us. Ugh. I think they need to lower the prices for sure, and as for the drunk people, I don't have a solution. Guess that's just Vegas

I had a great experience doing the high roller. Something I definitely recommend trying out when you're in Vegas for the first time. Seeing above 540 ft of the night life of Las Vegas gives a great perspective of all of the city lights. It's super affordable, and my friend and I split the cost between the printed photos they take with the green screen. It's about 30 mins long from start to finish so if you get antsy on heights, this ride is not for you!! They also have a happy hour and different selections of things you can purchase. It's a big round clear orb looking thing with standing room and sitting benches. You're free to walk in their as the ride continues to ride to see the different angles. The wait in line was not that long at all either. Overall great experience. Worth doing at night.

This was the best experience yet!  The link has a happy hour where within the link there is a full service bar and bartender to cater to your every need.  A-Mazing, this was a great trip and view of the city and the city buildings all while having cocktails ...can you think of anything better.  The view was absolutely breath taking if you're not afraid of heights and if you like looking down.  They also offer a picture option with the group you're traveling with so after you come down from this amazing trip around the world so to speak on what is like a large scale Ferris wheel; you get to see the pictures you took prior, so fun!!  My friends talked me into doing this I thought it would be rather boring but I think having happy hour inside the link made it that much more exciting and fun, this is definitely a MUST TRY!

Arguably the best thing to do in Vegas. Skip everything else that's on the way and just go to the High Roller entrance. There was no line at 11 at night and we waited with just one other group in front of us for a pod.

Offering breathtaking views with the city lit up, this is an engineering wonder. Lasts about 25 minutes.

If I could've done anything different, I personally would've brought dinner to eat while we watched.

The great part of visiting High Roller during the daytime is the lack of crowd / no lines. The interior of the ferris wheel ride could fit 10+, but we and most patrons got the ride all to themselves. Even in hot weather, , you'll be comfortable with the a/c inside. Ride last a nice 30 minutes.  Our tickets cost $19 pp,  which can be bought discounted all over the place.  There's no need to pay full price.

This is a great experience. We bought our tickets online through our mobile phone because there is a $5 discount and you get to skip the long ticket line. I went with my fiancé and we did the daytime happy half hour package which is all you an drink. We had to wait for the pod that had a bar which only took about 5 minutes. It was only us in our pod but we had a great time. The bartender engaged us in great conversation and the drinks were actually strong. I was able to down 3 drinks before we had to get off and my fiancé had 4. 

The view at top was beautiful. On one side you see the strip and the other you could look at the mountains. I'm sure the strip looks even better at night. 

Overall I had a great time and I would definitely recommend this to others.

Should be 5 stars ...

First, I am afraid of heights and do these type of things for a reason.  Scary ?  yeah only to me, others had no problems and 500+ feet is a beautiful view of Las Vegas.  Seems to take forever and I made the most of it.  Bring your camera.  Construction of this attraction fascinated me and the time lapse "video" on board answered a lot of my questions. 

The only down grade is my credit card was compromised at either the ticket booth, where they ran my card info twice or at the souvenir photo booth.  That part sucked.

Learn from our mistakes.

#1 - Locals get a 50% discount.

#2 - Living social has deals all the time. Don't pay full price for a ticket. 

#3 - The happy hour thing is crap. It's a 30-minute ride. If you pay full price for one of these tickets, you're an idiot. Like I said, learn from our mistake. 

#4 - Make sure all of your friends have the same type of ticket so you can't get suckered into spending an extra $15 for the happy hour ride when you already bought drinks.

#5 - For $35, you can go to Foundation Room at Mandalay, have two amazing cocktails, and a better view.

#6 - Watch for backsplash when someone else in your pod gets motion sickness and vomits everywhere.

I had an amazing time! You can have it all from 420 feet in the air... Fun.. Romance...drinks.. Smiles... Even kisses! (My favorite) 

The view was amazing! We went at midnight so the wait wasn't long at all.  We decided to get the open bar option.   We had a ball! It was a great crowd and guess what....Someone got proposed to and SHE SAID YES! 

The price was pretty good and I will definitely be back soon!

So as 4 of us were waiting in line to buy tickets at 9:15pm on a Sunday, a random, friendly girl gave us three tickets and in a flash she was gone.  We were in total disbelief.  I was still skeptical up to the part where they scanned the ticket.  Saved us $111!!  I owe her some Sprinkles at the very least if we ever cross paths again.  

Currently the largest observatory wheel in the world (wonder how much of a pain it will be when it becomes the 2nd), there's not much to say about the ride itself.  You go around for 30 minutes, see the strip, snap pics and it's over.  The waiting area before getting to the actual wheel is very Disney Worldesque.  

The "guide" is a guy on a video screen dishing out facts and bad jokes (420 ft! You're really high!!).   I wonder why they didn't have different performers from Caesars shows doing video segments instead?  Imagine what the Gazillionaire and Penny would say?!  They could do the "quiet tour" with Teller.

The biggest variable with how enjoyable your ride will be are the others in your pod.  Each pod is supposed to fit 40 people.  I saw a family with 5 small and loud kids on their rollerskate sneakers in front of us and I would have done almost anything to avoid being in the same pod including lighting myself on fire.  We rode with about 20 others that were fine and excited to be on the ride.  

Other things:

- Try to go for the seats on the immediate right upon getting into the pod.
- Nighttime has to be better than daytime.  
- Please go to the restroom before getting on.
Definitely worth the $$$ talk about a fun day activity. Will not disappoint. Tremendous amount of fun, with great panoramic views and new friends.

I've been waiting for this to open up since I first saw them building it! My sister and I were able to make it when they first opened and we were really excited. We bought tickets ahead of time for the evening. There wasn't many people, but there was a line.

I like that you can see the strip and it even pauses once you reach the top so you can enjoy the view. The pod is huge! It can hold so many people, but lucky for us it was just my sis and I and one older couple. We technically had the pod all to ourselves. I definitely recommend buying tickets and taking a ride on the high roller because you can see such a nice view and take some great pics of Vegas too.

Wife and I did this. The view is amazing , can't ask for a better view. The real down side and reason I gave only 4 stars , was the ride is too short. The website says 30 minuets and the ride only took 9 , that was my only real disappointment.

A must do while in Las Vegas!  We rode in June 2014 for the first time and really enjoyed it. Yes it's expensive...especially at night $35. But we had no regrets! A pleasant staff ushers you in and our wait was fairly minimal. There is music and videos throughout the experience.  The pods are spacious and can hold 40 people but usually there is 10-20. On ours there was maybe 20 and I was glad for that. The views are great at all points and photo ops are plentiful.  I recommend the night ride as the city looks it's best. The sense of movement was almost undetectable even on a windy night. I have to say that I am painfully scared of heights...but 2 cocktails and I was willing. There were still moments of fear but you can sit down and compose yourself. Very glad I did it!

Great experience, I suggest going both in the day time and night time and planning it around the Bellagio water fountain schedule. At the top of the high roller, you can see it perfect. I enjoyed this with my husband and I will bring my 9 month old next time to ride it with us. I was reading the negative reviews below and I don't think it is entirely the high rollers fault... Yes they should have more security, but it is meant to be shared with other guests. They cannot reserve the space just for you and your kids. Having a child of my own though I can understand your trauma and I am so sorry! That guy needed to be detained and not be allowed back on the ride. What we did was just wait until there wasn't a line and we got our own pod by ourselves. Maybe you should try it to, because you will actually love the ride.

Purchased tickets for their happy hour pod. The pod was a lot smaller and less luxurious than anticipated based on their online video.  

Our bartender was awesome and efficient but otherwise the alcohol was terrible quality and difficult to get down especially in 30 minutes. 

The pod moves more quickly once you're inside and the views are beautiful at night. They also have a countdown of when you reach the center top.

In the future I would recommend saving your $$ and purchasing regular pod tickets (not the happy hour one) and grabbing a drink at the bar inside the place before hopping into the pod.

1st time rider here. Went with a small group. Had purchased tix thru groupon. I suggest this to save $$. We went on Sunday night. Lines were not long because we had pre purchased our tickets. There was bar before the line started and one right before we boarded for those who want to indulge. Be sure to use the bathroom otherwise you will be holding it for a really long time. We rode it at dark to see all the lights. It was really cool to see all the views over the strip at night. I probably wouldn't do it again. I am local but definitely think it's worth a visit. The Linq area is loaded with bars and restaurants too.

Definitely a must do while in Vegas but expect to feel underwhelmed when leaving.

The views during the day is flat, dry, and pretty boring.  However, it's pretty safe to assume spectacular views at night because I am always in awe when I walk the strip at night.

It was pretty slow during the day.  No lines or congested pods, just the people in my party.  My mother was deathly afraid because she was under the impression that this was a thrill ride,  it's not.  It's best described as a mobile observation deck.  The mobile observation deck lasts approximately 30 minutes so make sure you tinkle prior to entering.  And from reading other reviews, looks like you are allowed to bring drinks onboard.

I believe the cost is $25 during the day and $35 at night.

I personally would not return but you definitely have to do it once.
Kids loved the high roller and seeing Las Vegas at night for the first time. The views were amazing. They enjoyed being in their own pod and seeing the lights. Great venue for families to see Vegas.

I had family come to town that wanted to do this and I'm afraid of heights so I was worried but we had a blast. Theres a bar before you get on so we were able to enjoy a drink during the ride and the pod was big enough that the height didn't bother me. 

We went at night and the view was amazing! It moves slow enough that my cousin was able to grab some beautiful pictures on her phone. The price is a little on the high side but I'd go again if the party I was with was wanting to.

Definitely a must do in VEGAS!  Must go at night when the sun sets for the ultra experience of being 550 feet up and seeing and being on top of the Vegas lights and city.  What a freaking amazing view!  The ride is only 30 minutes and cost $32 , but totally worth it.  The caveat is if your only with a few of your family and friend , you will share the pod with strangers.  We shared with a couple who took non stop selfies for 39 minutes which was annoying but at least they were respectful.  Overall fun times.

Like a lot of other reviewers have mentioned, it's best to buy the groupon. No need to pay full price here. Our group of 4 bought the groupon for the open bar pod and it was money well spent. No line mid afternoon, but one began to form behind us quickly. Turns out there are only 2 bar pods on the whole wheel which means if you just missed one, prepare to wait. We had about 20 people in our pod and it was comfortable. Would've liked fewer people so we could've spread out more but people were nice enough to move around so we could get pictures from all sides of the pod. The bartender was awesome, I forget her name. But she was fast and efficient for sure. Shots and drink flew from her hands and no one was without a drink for long. The view at the top is incredible (sunset is awesome!) and the wheel moves slow enough to be able to really take it all in. Overall a great choice!

Being my first trip to Vegas, I wanted to see as much as I could in three days.  I didn't know Vegas had an attraction like this until we flew over it.

I took the monorail up to the Harrah's stop and then walked over to the area.  To get to the High Roller, it certainly a trendy area with the shops.  It was fun to browse.  Before you arrive at the High Roller, you certainly have the opportunity to purchase the tickets before arriving there.

Once you arrive to the location, just follow the lines and then you are there...after having your picture taken, of course....  the pods very large and clean.  There were only three of us in the pod so there were plenty of space.  This is very slow incline and relaxing.  You will see incredible views of the city and the surrounding area.

Downside, not a lot of sitting area in these pods and I thought cost was a little high ($26.95 for 30 minutes) but it's Vegas.  

I would recommend the High Roller, however, I would not return.  Been there Done that.
The High Roller was awesome, definitely go at night, we bought our tickets for 11:50 pm, no line, we were on right away.

The High Roller observation wheel is an absolute must while visiting Las Vegas. The price of admission can be a little steep but it's totally worth it for the 30 minute ride. At the time of my visit, I was able to find a groupon for $19; which was much better than paying the full daytime admission price of $27. Again, it was totally worth it! The views from the wheel are pretty awesome and the pods themselves were too! Each pod can hold up to about 40 people although the average is usually 15. Inside of the pod, there are TVs and music playing which adds to that Vegas party mood. Last but not least, yes, you can have drinks inside on the wheel and if you pay for the VIP ride, there will actual be a bar and a bartender inside of the pod to serve you!

For the briefest of moments...you will find yourself on the top of the strip, with a great view in all directions, in a bubble that looks way larger when you are in it than it does from the street.

If you go at night (as we did), you'll have a fantastic view of the strip, but the other 270 degrees will be pretty dark.  Why don't the mountains have lights on them?  

During the day, you will have a full 360-degree view of the area, strip and all.  As far as photos go...it'll be easier during the day; pictures at night will definitely catch some reflected background.  

Day - see all the things, photo all the things.  
Night - see most of the things, REALLY see the strip, get creative to take good pictures.

Figure out what you want to see more (or do both), but, day or night, definitely don't skimp on the open bar car.  It was a modestly priced Groupon, and the top shelf vodka cranberries kept finding their way to my hand from all available directions.  Pro tip: get a nice big refill just as you are about to get off, and then walk around with it.  Travel drink!

The experience itself was a lot of fun; having never been to Vegas (and coincidentally being very thirsty for Cape Codders) I was able to get a great view of the area while playing a drinking game with myself, called "free drinks for 30 minutes so have another and another."

I definitely won.

Our bartender was great; he had no problem making strong drinks, and took a lot of pictures for us.  Just in case you want to know what you are looking at/how high you are/want to be told a funny/punny joke, the pre recorded video guides you every step of the way.

Regardless of how exactly you choose to do this, know that 30 minutes goes by really quickly, but it will be worth it.

Apparently this review is long past due.  I rode the High Roller a couple of years ago and must have forgotten to write about it.

I should preface this by saying I HATE FERRIS WHEELS!  They scare the crap out of me.  And it isn't the height.  I don't mind that.  There is just something about Ferris wheels that bother me.  But I came here with my family (Grandma and her sisters, Dad and Step-mom) and they wanted to ride.  Who am I to tell my grandma "no?"  

I think we boarded right around sunset and the lighs of the valley were starting to shine brighter than the stars in the sky.  I noticed first how smooth the motion is on this giant observation wheel.  I didn't like that very much.  I could not feel the movement but I could see it.  It was messin' with my head, man.  The views were pretty amazing though.  And it was cool to watch the video screen on the way up as they told how high you were.  That kept my mind from realizing how off balance I was becoming. I was afraid that the 30 minutes it takes to go around was going to seem like forever.  It actually went pretty quickly.  Not too quickly though.  I was happy to step out of the pod and onto solid ground again.  It was an interesting experience but not one that I would care to do again.  Especially with the prices they charge.  One and done.

High Roller was having a sale on their tickets for $20/person during the holidays. Apparently, if you are a Vegas local, you get a better discount on the ticket. It took approximately 30 minutes to make one revolution. I believe the top is approximately 550 ft above the ground. We actually purchased some drinks from Yard House before going onto this ride. Also, I recommend that you use the restroom before you get onto the High Roller. There are restrooms on the 2nd floor. Also, the High Roller paparazzi take your photo so that they can hawk some photos on you. Unfortunately, their amateur paparazzi do not take good photos. You can take better photos with your own camera.   

Once you are in the pod, there are screens on the High Roller that narrate the journey through the full 360. It lets you know when you reach the top because it is somewhat hard to discern considering that the ride is quite smooth. It was really nice to see a view of the Strip in the evening. Hopefully they can keep their prices low as anything above $20 is a rip off. I always see Groupon deals for the High Roller so I would search for coupons and deals online first before going on the High Roller.

This is a must do in Vegas! My friends and I did the Happy Half Hour around midnight with a groupon for $29 (not really sure). The ride itself was great, it was smooth and gives a great view of the strip and the promenade between Linq and Flamingo. Because we came in so late, there were no lines and no wait. As for the happy hour, our bartender was fast and the drinks were made well with a good amount of alcohol. 

Recommendation: 1) Tip the bartender well. you'll get served good drinks. 2) NO HEELS LADIES! This is a tuck-and-roll kind of deal. You must get on and off the pod while it's moving. I wouldn't recommend heels during the jump off after 30 minutes of drinking :)

Worth visiting once but it is just a big Ferris wheel.  Spokesperson was a bit cheesy.  We went during the day as we walked by. It was mainly views of parking lot on lower level but higher up was good.  

I am sure it's better at night but won't be back.  Nothing special other than height.  You can easily get a good view just going to ghost bar.
This was one of my favorite parts of my whole trip! The views were great and the open bar was definitely worth the extra cost. The bartender made a good variety of drinks and kept them coming quick!

you better try at least one time for new observation spot of las vegas strip . i was impressed with the new way to look of the strip view at night time . plus they also have a ton of restuarant and bar are around . try it and you will be enjoy

The High Roller is such a great way to fully see the majority of the Las Vegas Strip. I came here during the day with a friend of mine, and there's a series of different stages you have to pass to fully ensure that you have tickets to be able to enter the ride. I thought this was a great way to fulfill maximum security for the ride, so I appreciate that.

The only thing I didn't appreciate on my way to the High Roller was the blinding photo taking that the employees make you take before you enter the ride. You stand in front of a green screen and wait as they snap your picture twice with a high quality (BLINDING) camera technology system. Personally, I believe this should be optional for those who want to purchase them at the end of the ride for $35. For those who don't, tons of film is wasted, and it's very inconvenient for the environment in my opinion.

When we got into one of the pods, we were only with a few other people, which was awesome because I thought that we would be in a capsule with 10+ other riders. But we had enough room to physically run around the capsule, which was convenient, especially if one of us saw a photo-worthy moment to capture.

The ride lasts approximately 30 minutes. The top of the High Roller, of course, is the best because you can fully see all of Las Vegas in a 360° panorama. Next time, I would definitely go at night so I can capture what Vegas looks like with all of the illuminating city lights.

We were in Vegas for a week of meetings, and only had a few free hours on our last night. My wife had never been to Vegas, and we thought this would give us some bang for the buck. And it did not disappoint. Great views, everyone in our car was awesome, and Kelli the bartender was great. Go at night, and buy the $10 add on for free drinks. Cheaper than buying one for $9 in the lobby. We had the added advantage of a nearly full moon. We hung out on the Linc after, and its a great people watching spot.

A few tips- I think this is worth it if you can get a decent deal, so check Groupon or Living Social. We found a deal on Groupon that included tickets for 2 for 1 drinks at the Sky Bar, 15% off one full price item in the gift shop, and 20% off food and drinks at the Brooklyn Bowl. 

We chose the night ride with open bar. Make sure you bring your ID- the bartender will not serve you if you don't have it, and you look young. Get as many drinks as you can! We had about 10 people inside, so it wasn't easy, but I think I managed 3 total. Also, bring some cash so you can tip the bartender. There's not many places to sit inside the pod, so wear comfy shoes. You will probably be standing for most of the ride.

Prior to getting on the ride, they take pictures of you in front of a green screen. I normally don't bother with these types of pictures, but to my surprise, it came out great. 1 framed picture costs $30. So, dress nicely if you think you'll fall for this like I did.

Enjoyed our family ride on the High Roller Ferris Wheel!!! I was a little leery at first but it was such a smooth ride with beautiful views and great photo ops! My beverage helped calm my nerves! We will go again soon! Pricing was ok. We purchased discount tickets thru our credit union. Processing for the ride was quick and uneventful no long lines! We enjoyed it thoroughly!

Oh hell yeah, you're doing this...  and here's my advice on how to do it the BEST way and even save a little money.

First, you're going to get yourself a Living Social deal (or Groupon - whoever is offering the best deal that week), because paying full price is for suckers.  Get the cheaper alternative when it comes to time - the 12 to 6 PM ticket.  BUT splurge and get the Happy Hour option with that ticket.  You've just saved yourself $5 to $10 based on the specials running on the site at the time.  * I think our tickets were listed on Living Social for $31.99 each, but I waited until they offered an extra 20% off so we ended up paying around $25 for each ticket - a very good deal!  

AND by purchasing the daytime tickets with the HH option, you'll also save yourself a lot of aggravation.  Here's why:

Most tourists want to do the High Roller at night.  So every "cage", including the few Happy Hour ones will be full.  Of People.  And probably children.  Ick.  But if you show up at around 5 when it's just starting to get a little bit dusky, there isn't a line - especially for the Happy Hour "cage" and your party might end up riding alone - that's like having a personal freaking bartender!

We LOVED this attraction.  It was awesome to see all of Las Vegas splayed out before us with the sun slowly going down.  And that awesomeness was helped by a very healthy pour of champagne by a super friendly bartender.  You simply HAVE to go here.  It's not to be missed.  Even those with heights issues should be calm because they can stay to the center of the cage and the ride is so smooth you don't even really realize when you're at the very top of the wheel.
 
Bartender we had was very friendly and quite forthcoming with the refills (dropping a $10 or a $20 in the tip jar upon entry will help speed that along).  So we had a lovely boozy time. Couldn't ask for a better Happy Hour.  BONUS - right off the High Roller, there are lots of options to keep the Happy Hour going just nearby and across the street.  

I highly recommend the High Roller as the way to KICK OFF your designated "fun/get wild/sleep late tomorrow" night in Vegas.

This round 2 for us We've done a day and night trip.. both are special in their own ways.  Don't waste your money on the open bar, bottom shelf drinks.  If you avoid the weekend rush and go on a weekday daytime hours  you might get lucky and get your own cabin like we did!! Defiantly checkout groupon/living social for great deals.

Wow. This was really cool. We rode the High Roller at night on the 4th of July. Spectacular views of not only the strip but also fireworks for as far as the eye could see. There were only 12 people in our car so we had plenty of room to walk around and see every angle possible. The staff was very accommodating and very friendly. I am confined to a wheelchair but everything is accessible and the staff stops the cars so wheelchairs can enter safely. Some things to consider before riding. Obviously if you are afraid of heights this attraction may not be for you. While there is ample room in the cars, confined spaces combined with extreme heights can be a little scary. With that said our car reached the peak height and upon decent they stopped the entire wheel. A recording played stating that a passenger was in need of assistance in another car and after the situation was resolved the wheel would resume momentarily. After 10 minutes we started to move in reverse. Then the car stopped again for another 10 minutes and proceeded forward. Stopped again and went backwards... we went over the highest point three times! The ride is supposed to take about 30 minutes but our trip lasted about an hour and the majority of the time was spent at the top. I will admit it was a bit of a scare and can see how this may spark extreme panic for someone. Otherwise I loved the experience. We did not opt for the open bar but I wish we would have since we were up there so long.

Riding the high roller makes me down. I remember when I found out santa wasn't real. I cried for what seemed like ages. Riding on the so called "scary" high roller brought back those disappointing memories of santa no more from its false advertising as scary. The only thing terrifying is the price, 30 dollars for a night ride online or 37 in person. Save your money for your mortgage, its way scarier than this dream crusher. 

I say disappointing because the high roller is advertised as being scary. The ads mention how scary it is, how people with a fear of heights should be cautious about riding this record high observation wheel. I'm one of those people. I screamed when I sky dived and I cussed when I cliff jumped. But I still did them. Because they terrified me when I looked down. On the high roller, I questioned my own existence. I thought, "why did they trick me? This isn't scary at all. Should I feel guilty for worrying about first world problems? Am I not drunk enough? I don't feel drunk. This is unpleasant. Are they testing my optimism? Why am I alive? I wish I were at work"

Let me sum what this awful experience is like. You walk through endless corridors and feel your excitement build up. "OMG THIS IS THE WORLDS LARGEST WHEEL IM GONNA SO SCARED HAHA NOT IM SO AWESOME YEAHHHH VEGAS WHOOO". You get on the futuristic white orb with your friends and other strangers and you feel reckless with arrogance.

550 feet? HAH. You're Braveheart, you're Batman, you're courage personified. Nothing can stop you. 

And nothing will. There's absolutely no view in the orb that will scary you. No moving air like an open cage in a ferris wheel. The steel bar blocks the glass view so it's not like you're riding in a glass orb, it's more like you're riding win a giant hamster wheel. I felt more safe than driving in California when it's raining. I could sleep in the orb and wouldn't notice anything. 

As the 30 minute ride to hell started. this annoying guy popped on the TV screen to remind us how great Caesar's palace is and how awesome Linq is. I pay 30+ dollars and they advertise to me? Seriously? Not only is the beer outrageously priced here ($10 for a little bottle) but they actually try to sell you stuff while you pay to ride on this giant hamster wheel thing. 

The view is good. Oh wait. not really. I see a suburb. Oh look...MGM. That's cool. Wait, can't I just go to the top of the MGM and pay nothing. Oh yeah I could. But I didn't. I paid to ride this hamster wheel thing. 

And it sucked.You know why? It's not because this is a first world problem. Which it is. 

Its because they advertised this thing as scary. Mortgages in California are scary. Japanese horror movies are scary. Layoffs are scary. This thing is not scary. 

Oh and to add insult to injury, the narrator guy insults you while you ride. He tells you not to be scared even though there is no fear. He starts to mock you and laughs while making awful puns. I never hated tv narrators until I rode in this orb of death. 

Save yourself the money. Buy some beer. Spin some slots. Donate to the homless. But please, do not support this atrocity. This thing will make you wish you weren't on vacation. For 30 minutes, you will ask yourself, "huh, I didn't get reception at 550 feet. Yeah I do. I wonder what my friends are doing on facebook. I should take a selfie but the lighting is awful so i can't"
Seriously, please don't ride on this thing. It's a giant boring wheel of ads for 30 minutes. Support the real fun: casinos and everything not related to this boring wheel. 

Anyone who gives this thing 5 stars should not be trusted. They are lying. I assure you, you will suffer. I am considering a lawsuit for false advertising. They should pay me and even then, it would have to be more than 30 minutes of what I make at my job. 

Don't go. Please. For Santa. For your dreams. For hope. For humanity.

It was pretty fun and worth it if you are already desensitized from all the Vegas prices. It's $38 bucks per person at night and $53 for one with open bar. The whole trip around is about 30 min. It's a fun thing to do with friends. 

Be aware that each pod holds about 20 to 30 individuals and that could include babies and small children. If you are planning to do something crazy in high roller just know that... 

Also, when you call in and ask questions they will act like you can get your own pod if you just ask but that is not true. Just like everything nicer in Vegas, you have to pay hundreds of $$$ to claim the whole thing. Unfortunately, we didn't fiind this out until we already bought out tickets and were being ushered into a pod. Just don't trust what they tell you, because we had 2 seperate staff tell us we can get our own pod for regular admission before we bought our tickets.

VERY IMPORTANT NOTE: Make sure no one in your party is even remotely pukey drunk and/or extremely afraid of heights...

Went on the High Roller with a group of 5 adults, on the Open Bar tickets (you can't mingle ticket types; if you want to ride together all ticket types must be the same,  drinking or non drinking.  We did the Open Bar and the bartender we had was pleasant and made some killer margaritas, and a drink with Chambord called Purple Rain  (Prince had recently died ).  The tickets were about $36 per person, but the novelty of going into this big glass orb on this giant ferris wheel was totally worth it!   The view could be more picturesque,  but since the Roller is so huge, it is set off the strip, and one side views only parking lots.  There is free valet parking,  which is great.  The glass pods are very stable, and you can hardly feel any swaying.  Fun!

We got the daytime admission, which is a pretty good deal.  You can definitely save money by buying it online.  Our admission was $19.95 a person.  The view is awesome and the pods go slow enough so you don't feel antsy or dizzy.  What a fun and touristy experience, that everyone must try. :D  The walk toward the High Roller is nice too, because of the shops along the way there and because of the nice view of the wheel.

I haven't even been on the ride yet but I'm not happy. Our ride was scheduled for 1pm and are still currently waiting in line as they are not letting anyone on because of maintenance. If that is the case the ride should have been completely shutdown until it was up and fully functional. People have been standing just waiting with no updates on when they will allow loading. This could have been handled much better. Two star rating in hopes that once on it was worth the wait.

This attraction is amazing and worth the money and time! We bought tickets from the concierge at our hotel so we paid the day rate of $25 vs. $37. The bad part of that was about a 20 minute wait to get actual tickets printed. There was also an option for a pod with a bar which was a little more in price.

Each pod hold up to 30 people we were grouped with about 18 others, they were all together and a very loud lively group. The pods are attached so there is no movement, no rocking you feel very safe and stable.

The wheel constantly moves it never stops, you walk on from a platform with ease and takes 30 minutes to make it around one time, it moves so slowly you don't even realize you're moving. You are 550 feet in the air at the top the views are amazing it's worth the money and time. We were even able to see the bellagio fountains go off.

It's too bad they didn't have a better location or even maybe on top of a building for this attraction it is behind the linq hotel so the views at first are either of the Las Vegas neighborhoods or the parking lots. But as it gets higher the views are tremendous!

No stars!!! The manager Carolyn and James Donohue was HIGHLY rude!!! After we came up after our ride of the high roller she was smirking and joking about or complaint when her employer was very rude and talked back to us when all we did was kindly ask to get a booth with no young kids and the employee wanted to talk back and tell us that wasn't her job. She quote on quote knew what happened before we complaint and smirked the entire time telling us she already knew what happens from her employee and would NOT apologize to us! We even had another couple aside from our group complain and she was highly rude to her!! I will never come again!!!!

My friends and I went her 2 days for the happy hour. Our first experience was amazing as to why we decided to come back a 2nd time. Our second experience wasn't great at all. 

We first went with Lupe during the Happy hour. She's by far amazing. She made everyone in the pod hyped up and excited for the 30 minutes to begin. She was super friendly and was very quick with making our drinks. She was never rude or mad that we were wanting drinks practically like every minute. She was the best bartender that we've experience and that made us want to go the next day with our other friend that would be joining our group. 

The 2nd time came along and we got Amanda as our bartender. She didn't say hi when we walked into the pod and not welcoming to any of the other guests that joined with us. You can automatically tell that she didn't want to work and was pretty much arguing with other people in the pod. This wasn't the great service that we received before and very disappointed. We probably only was able to get like 2 drinks throughout the 30 minutes since she was arguing with other people and that she was just not into it. I was personally embarrassed that we hyped up this Ferris wheel to our friend.

TBH the only reason why this got a 3 was because of Lupe. If it was Amanda, I would've gave it a 1 star no problem.

This was our first experience on the High Roller.  We did it Saturday night around 11:45 pm.  Wanted the evening experience of viewing the strip.  We purchased a groupon which got us the Happy Half Hour experience.  Which includes an open bar.  The ride with (Happy Half Hour) cost around $79 for 2 people, (Group Cost).  Regular cost was $52 per person.  The lines were relatively short, maybe a 15-20 minute wait, max.  Once you get on the car, the bartender started off extremely loud, but took total control of the car.  There was roughly 15, loud and drunk personnel on board, so the loud start, helped get things under way, so I appreciated it!  Then the drinks started.  Let's just say, I got my $ worth within 30-40 minutes.  The bartender poured a great drink and was very quick about it.  

Bottom line:  Excellent experience.  This is something I would recommend!

One of the most enjoyable 1/2 hours EVER!  I recommend that you splurge for the half-hour happy hour and do it in the evening it is a hoot!  Do it do it do it do it do it - and consider looking on Groupon for some great deals you might be able to get a discount like we did.  I'll add my pics next.
Not sure what more you could want in a half hour, all you can drink well drinks and fantastic views of the strip

This was so cool! Got the happy hour ticket. Got there early but they still let me on. There are bathrooms located on the second floor. Otherwise no place to sit and wait around for your appointed time, since they let me go anyway that was cool. There was also a bar area where you can stand around and wait. It was really modern looking, dark and that cool vibe going. No line anywhere, and I was the only person in my cabin!  I did have to wait for a few cabins to go by since I was waiting for one that had a bar in it. I really enjoyed this experience more since I was the only person inside, crowds annoy me. I could walk all around, stand wherever and not have to worry about my bags as I just set it down and left it there. Bartender Robert was awesome, and in formative. He talked about before the strip was so big, pointed out places to see. And got me buzzed on 3 little margaritas. LoL I so wish I had more cash on hand to drop in his bucket. They work off tips and I thought there would be an ATM around, but there wasn't. You can also leave a comment in the gift shop area about your bartender, which I also did.

You must go, get the happy hour and bring cash! Every trip to Vegas will include a ticket here from now on.

There's a little bench to sit on, but why are you sitting? Walk around, take pictures! Enjoy the 30min ride!

Bought tickets to take my nephew on the High Roller while he was visiting.  It was a really nice experience and we got discounted tickets.  I recommend going at night for the best experience!  The only downside is the super-annoying video playing throughout the ride.

AMAZING VIEWS!!!! Great for couples, families, friends, anyone who wants to see Vegas from a different perspective. 

TICKETS - available online or on location, however it was slow season when we went so no need to buy in advance.

HAPPY HOUR - these are not available when you purchase at the koisk/machine or online but you have to bring your ticket to the main entrance where they will UPGRADE you for the price difference. Regular night time ride is $35, Happy Hour is $45. 

The "cabins" are very large and can probably hold 20 people - but it was slow season so we only had about 12. There is a seat for everyone, but most people stand. The wheel moves VERY slowly, very calm and doesn't even feel like you're moving!! 

The entire ride lasts about 30 mins and the views are phenomenal. However, if you've stayed at the Cosmo, they have wrap around suites 60th floor and up, that have the same views. LOL. 

Great experience overall, definitely would recommend doing it once.

Ride is pricey.  It has some spectacular views but not the best.  I think the views from the Eiffel Tower and Stratosphere are better.  There are some nice views looking east of the strip and some views between the hotels looking onto the strip.  From the strip, walk through the new outdoor mall to the ticket office.  There are some bars and restaurants.  I like the old school neon signs.  The ride is about 30 minutes and during the ride, a video plays giving out some stats about the ride and historical trivia questions about Las Vegas.

Overall, it was worth it the one time.  I probably would not do it again unless some friends wanted to do it.

The High Roller allows you (and friends/family/strangers depending on who you get in a pod with) 30-minutes of scenic views of the Las Vegas Strip and the Las Vegas Valley.

Enjoy pointing out beautifully-lit casinos, marvel at the pods below and above you. Have a dance party to some of the music, or just chill on one of the benches provided. Each pod supposedly holds 40 people. I counted how many were in mine and there was 28. I would not have liked 12 more people in that thing with me.

Don't miss out on taking a look at the valley instead of the Strip, and definitely take a look at the helicopters and planes flying around pretty much where you happen to be, up in the air!

Locals get a discount, and if you buy online you can reserve a time. Skip the line to buy tickets, get a drink at the bar - and head through the many queues they have set up. We were there on a Saturday and we waited probably only about 6 minutes to get on.

Overall - a decent experience, one to do just to say you've done it.

Watching the water show from the Bellagio from the High Roller is a great way to see the show from another angle, avoid all those crowds, and see all the glory of the Vegas nightlights. A great way to spend a fun, relaxing evening on the Strip. Be sure to leave extra time for parking.

So I heard about the High Roller and finally decided to check it out. I was so excited to go on this High Roller because I heard they had a bar in the pods.  So the on one I got on didn't have a bar in the pod but there was a bar before you go into the pod. The drinks are a little high but at the time I wasn't worried about it so I got a Henny. I didn't get some cheap deal on the tickets because I didn't care but I know I could've gotten a cheaper ticket.

The view wasn't all that great because you're not on the strip you actually behind the strip. It does take a good 30 minutes for the ride to end so you get your monies worth. There wasn't any music playing or anything really to get the party started. Yes, I understand this is also a family ride but I'm just saying.

Would I ride the High Roller again? Probably not it's just a tourist trap in my opinion.
Francis (the bartender) was super rude after I paid $37 to even go on the high roller...

Haven't been to Vegas in years, so when I heard they were building a giant ferris wheel along the strip, I was excited to try it out. I got my chance over the weekend and it did not disappoint. My brother got me and my dad tickets on Groupon, which included the entrance fee, a drink, and a souvenir photograph. From the street, this feat of engineering looks amazing. I understand that it's the tallest one in the world, and I don't doubt that. I also did notice that it moves really slow, and was later told that its more of an observation tower type of ride rather than a regular ferris wheel. So my pops and I decided to hop on later than evening, got our drinks and walked right on thru. I guess we went at the perfect time because there was no wait or lines at all. We got up to the loading dock and got into our observation pod immediately. It looks like a mini lounge in there with neon lights and tvs and a 360 degree view of the entire city of Las Vegas. Each pod fits about 40 people, but I think you'll appreciate the experience more if you have the pod relatively empty so you can roam around and take pics at every corner. Yes this ride is sloooooooooooooooow...but you'll appreciate the view along with the video commentary being played on the tvs talking about the history of Las Vegas and other random information about the city. I was able to take some really nice pics up there with my new camera. The whole ride took about 30 minutes to complete and like that its over. I would recommend this to anyone visiting Vegas but it is kinda pricey...the Groupon deal does help, so get that if you do decide to experience this.

I was surprised that I enjoyed this - I'm very afraid of heights - but it is really worth going to. 

The wife got a Living Social deal that included Happy Hour during the ride, so that helped calm my nerves.  But it's also a very very smooth ride and if you're afraid of heights as I am, you can stay towards the middle of the pod instead of looking over the edge.

Something I'm glad I did once.  I probably wouldn't do it again, but yeah - you should check it out for sure when in Vegas.

Great experience, get the groupon or buy tickets online to save cash. Our group did a 30 minute happy hour experience in one of these pods where they surprisingly served top-shelf liquor. You aren't allowed to order 4 drinks and quadruple fist but you can order as much as you want so long as it is one drink at a time. The view is fantastic near the top. Pair the good view with some nice cocktails and good vibes with friends and you are in business. Well worth the price. Will be back.

Stunning views of Las Vegas and the desert. Probably the best. Goes up to 500+ feet. Me and my boyfriend got a whole pod to ourselves. There are animated tv screens that keep you entertained with Vegas facts, trivia, how high up you are, etc. and also plays music in the pod. 30 minute ride round trip (one time around) 

Perfect place for a date night or group hang. The pods can fit a lot of people. 

One less star bc the prices are pretty steep 
$34.95 for after 5 pm for a single ride ticket. Bar was okay.

Amazing views of Las Vegas from the world's highest ferris wheel observatory tower. My friends and I grabbed a drink downstairs and hopped right in to enjoy an amazing 30-minute ride. They have cheaper rates if you go before "night," and so my friends and I purchased the last pro-rated ticket and got to enjoy the night views of Las Vegas at the cheaper rate. So worth it!

A Las Vegas must do!!!! 
My wife and I did this back in February and loved it. We did the one with the open bar. Well worth it and there's much to do in this area.

Fun up high with booze to keep ya afloat

High roller is the shizzzznit

It is high and it is a big wheel with pods that you go into and they give you dranks

Parking: Koval and Wellick I think its wellick (mr Robot...he he he)

Free parking is cool

Grand Marnier on the rocks will make you dizzy when cup is fulllllll
Malibu rum and pineapple 2x
Chambord and some mix our bartender Reece mixed was dope as hell

Then after the ride is done with you get to walk into a small strip of vegas where there is so much going on

Thanks spellcheck

Good times you Yelpers gotta try this place out after the high rolller ride 
Peace!

Overall experience was good. We are locals with 4 year old boy. No line, no crowd. It was only our family in a "ball". Nice view, but the second half of the journey became boring...I would be nice to have "Las Vegas" or "Strip" stories on inside TV or even a guiding speech.

Let me start with the negatives and why I only gave three stars:

Grossly overpriced. Yes it is Vegas and the strip, but it's not like I have a private pod or free alcohol flowing as I boringly look out at the landscape. Oh, wait. I have a 'high view' with A/C blowing on me. There's the savings!!.......not. Also there shouldn't be day to evening costs. Not to mention it's about 30 min. ride roundtrip. It's just not the best experience in town. 

We did it for that 'once in a lifetime' feel and I'm happy to say I have been on it but that's about where it ends. 

Save your $$ and visit the top of Stratosphere; eat dinner in the Paris eiffel tower; or just take a ride on the strip monorail. You'll have a more enjoyable time.

I am a Vegas local and had a great time on the High Roller with some visiting guests. 

It is located near the Linq Promenade area- a happening little piece of Vegas right across from Caesars Palace on the Las Vegas Strip. 

The HR is an amazing sight to see. Astonishing views of the Vegas valley. We went at night so it was even more beautiful in my opinion. The highest observation wheel in the world. (I've been to the London Eye and this is cooler!) The pods are modern with an interactive TV program playing. They have an option for a 'Happy Half Hour' where you drink with an open bar in your pod for the entire 30 minute revolution. 

It's pretty amazing that these pods can hold 30 or so people. You'd never guess when looking from afar. When we got to the top we got to see the Bellagio Fountains dancing to top it all off. 

When you're in Vegas, make sure to do this! If you're a local, they have great locals discounts.

This is such a definite must!! My husband and I were in Vegas for our honeymoon and my first visit to Vegas and this was so beautiful!! Ferris wheels are kinda our thing (first place he told me he loved me was a ferris wheel and proposed on one as well) so we were very happy to find such an amazing thing! I was blown away by the views, and it was so pretty!

We purchased groupons for the happy half hour package at $65 per couple.  We were also the only ones on this half hr ride with open bar. 

The bartender was very friendly and kept the drinks coming! He knew a variety of cocktails and had many options of liquor to choose from. We ended up having 10 drinks each before leaving and I don't remember what happened after that.. I assume it was a good time!

I've done the happy hour tour twice now and it is a good time every time! This is a really fun outing for a group in Vegas. We went around 5 pm for drinks before dinner (tickets are cheaper before 6 pm and when purchased online). The bartenders are generous with drinks and make sure you have a good time!

The High Roller is really cool, mainly because you can drink on it. We went on during the day since it's cheaper but I wish we had gone on at night. It takes 30 minutes to go all the way around and it's a HUGE pod that you're in. I went with 2 friends and we shared the pod with two older ladies, it was so boring. If we knew how big the pods were, we would have brought more people. They have this automated video on the screen the whole, with a "host" talking about the view and talking about Vegas, I get their point but it was a little annoying. They should just play music instead. They have a bar right before you go in to get on the ride, so if you don't have a drink already (yes, you can BYOB) get one! The view is fantastic from that high up but during the day, it's kind dull, I only recommend going at night!

Terrible customer service from the initial cashier alopez. Very rude to my group of mixed locals and visitors. Charged a local at a normal rate in a very rude manner. Very frustrating experience because of her. Rest of staff seemingly very friendly and the ride itself is spectacular.  Due to very rude cashier, I have to rate low.

While I was in the LINQ Promenade, I was debating to go in the giant wheel. I bit the bullet and went to the base of the thing to buy a ticket. A ticket is forty dollars. That's just the 'ride around the circle' price. There's a few options for 'ride around the circle' base ticket. For more monies, you can buy a 'drink at an open bar and ride around in a circle' and I also saw a sign advertising 'do yoga and ride around in a circle'. I wasn't really drinking, so I just got the basic ticket. 
     There was no wait and I was lead up a flight of stairs to a waiting room where I could opt to buy drinks or snacks for my 'ride around the circle' No thanks. I'm good. I walked up to the ride bit and was put in front of a camera, so I could opt to buy a picture of myself. Reminding me of the time I rode around the circle. No thanks. It's just me. I'm good. Eventually, I got to the ride around the circle part.
     I was reminded of amusement parks and fairs where people would wait until the wheel stopped, open the doors, and rush you into the lil basket because the thing didn't actually stop. Same principle here, except the 'lil basket' was now a fully enclosed 30 foot bubble with 360 degree windows, surround sound and digital tourguide. (and/or open bar) (and/or with yoga mats?)
    The ride started up slowly, and at about a quarter rotation, a girl in my bubble began to freak out. Turns out she was claustrophobic and she was having an attack. So...don't go here if you're claustrophobic. She mashed the emergency call button, and the slow ride up slowed, stopped and reversed direction. Sorry about claustrophobic girl, but Yay! Extra ride for me!
    The ride around was incredible, topping out at five hundred fifty feet in the air at the apex of the circle. Las Vegas, all lit up in it's bright grandeur spread out beneath me, and I took many photos.  Picture tip: I found the best way to take pictures was to put the phone right up to the glass. Back a lil bit and you get the reflection of the glass in your picture. 
     After about an hour, I found myself having gone fully around the circle. I hopped out on the other side of the ride, and walked back down towards the promenade. You're immediately dumped into the gift shop, where you can buy the t-shirt or refrigerator magnet to remind you of the time you paid forty dollars to ride around the circle. They're pretty good at trying to take money here.  But I'm glad I rode the circle.

What a fun ride! It didn't feel like 30 minutes at all, you can barely feel the wheel moving. We went during the day so it was less crowded we had no wait and there were 4 other people in the pod with us, so it was perfect. The views were great! I rode the high roller with a travelzoo deal, it was totally worth it!

We bought the happy half hour-It was the most amazing experience, great views, great service, great drinks. AND THEN...a guy peed in the trash can. Drink service stopped. Felt bad for all on board but no apologies from the company. A buzz kill.

This is a must when visiting Las Vegas. The entire cycle takes 30 minutes, providing ample time to take a lot of photos. This is probably my favorite attraction in Vegas right now. The High Roller is the largest observation wheel in the World. There are two different prices for day and night. Its a bit on the high side for an attraction that takes less than an hour of your day to complete, but its worth the experience. 

Great for kids! The wheel moves very slowly, and there is many other people in the "pod" providing a safe environment for families. The High Roller is very close to a Las Vegas Monorail stop.

The high roller is a must do in Vegas! I went by myself while my friends were doing other touristy stuff and gambling. My ticket ended up being about $20 since I went in the middle of the day but I know there's groupons for tickets with an open bar. The ride is about 45 minutes. Since I went during the afternoon and not in a pod with a bar, it was pretty empty. There were about 6 other people including myself. Would love to go back again at night!

My honey brought me here for my birthday and it was beautiful! I loved it! The view is great! Just make sure you buy the open bar ticket! You can get as many drinks as you want throughout the 30 min ride!!

Ok, when you think Las Vegas the LAST thing to come to mind would be a... ferris wheel? My priorities of places to go in Vegas consist of bomb restaurants and crazy clubs so I will admit the High Roller was near the bottom... but this last trip the stars aligned. We got happy hour tickets right before we hit up Marquee and it was AMAZING! 

The happy hour tickets mean you get unlimited (!!!) top shelf (!!!) drinks for the thirty minutes you are going around the wheel. There was about 15 people in our "pod" and we had plenty of room to walk around, chat, take pictures, maybe bust out a few minutes of twerking (it's Vegas). The bartender was awesome and gave strong pours. The views were INSANE! It was really breathtaking seeing the strip from that high up at night, with everything lit up.

Needless to say, I really recommend sneaking in a trip on the high roller if you get the chance. Pay the $50 to do the happy hour deal. It's definitely worth it! SO FUN!

EDIT: When I posted this I noticed if you check in on yelp you get $10 off admission!!!
We bought the groupon for two people and half hour open bar and had an awesome time! The drinks were strong and the bartender was very funny and entertaining

The high roller was an amazing experience.  I would suggest going at night because it is alot prettier with all the lights and stuff.  we were in a pod with about 10 other people which was the perfect amount because it wasnt too crowded and you can still get up and look out their window or sit down. another thing I found to be pretty cool is that they have a few bartenders there where you can buy drinks if you are nervous about going 550 ft in the air.

My wife and I went on Memorial Day 2014 and to our surprise they gave Military Service members ONLY a FREE PASS and that's the reason why I gave it a 3 star instead of 1 star.

PROS:
Plenty of parking in the back of The High Roller. Short walking distance and ADA accessible.

A nice Mini Street Mall (Check out Sprinkle's red velvet!!! I like it even if I hate cupcakes lol the wife forced fed me)

Recognizes Military Service Members. 

Staff are friendly.

Classy, clean environment.

No waiting time (May 26 @ 1900 hrs).


CONS:
They put too many people per cabin and it wasn't even that busy.

The wheel turns TOO FAST!!! If you are in the cab facing West (Facing The Strip) as if the wheel is a clock, going 6-5-4-3-2-1 o' Clock (turning counter-clockwise) you won't be able to see anything but a big wall of the hotel (Mirage?) so it's really nothing to see there. From 12-11-10 o'Clock is where you can see some DECENT VIEW of the strip. You'll have ONLY 8 mins to do so, so make it count!!! At 9-8-7-6 o'Clock are a bunch of NOTHING. So you'll sit and put up with the drunk, overly friendly crowd with you and some may have Vegas Syndrome (Jeeezzz I sound like a grouchy old fart lol)

It's not high enough to see anything on the strip. You'll see SOME nice views of the SMALL PART of the strip (Bellagio) on the window facing SSW. So sit at the SSW-W side of the cabin to make it SOMEWHAT worth it or it would be a complete waste of your time and money. SSE window is being blocked by a metal running in the middle, so you have to stick your face against the glass to see anything worth watching.

Can't get a decent  photo as you have to wrestle people to move out of the way or you'll never get a chance. Taking pictures with flash is a NO GO as the flash reflects on the glass ruining the background. So set up your camera for night shot w/ no flash before hopping in or while going up.

$25 bucks PP DAY and $35 bucks PP NIGHT (Starts at 6 PM if I can remember it right) Any other than a Memorial Day Pass, I would have rated it a 1 Star... I hope I've given you guys a heads-up...

Do this once because it is worth the view. It is not something I would do a second time. Plenty of other roof top locations at the major hotels to spend this money on a couple of drinks and enjoy the view.

I agree with many of the other reviews -- the guy in the video is annoying. I would rather learn more about Vegas than hear a joke about "getting high" at "420" feet.

Scary and exciting and so much fun!  This ride is definitely worth the price of admission.  The views all the way around are breathtaking.  The video that plays is mildly annoying but also has a lot of fun facts.  We went early in the day so there wasn't a line and only 2 other people in the pod with us.
I did see some remnants of what may have been puke on the floor and that was a little disturbing.  I'm sure it happens often and I'm grateful it didn't smell...

Since my sister-in-law was in town from the Islands, and she wanted to check out the High Roller, so we decided to tag along.  It's great that locals get BOGO, but if you're not, I'd have to say it's not worth it then.  But if it's on your bucket list, you should do it just once... like bungee cord jumping or sky diving... should only do it once.  

The view was great during the evening hours... Not sure I would recommend going during the day time though.

Here's a Crystal Clear HD video of the High Roller at Night that I recorded. In the video, you will see how the boarding process works, what it looks like from inside, and of course the beautiful Vegas Strip at Night in glorious HD

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GPQEoGLCun8

I rode it at night and it costs me $35 bucks with $2 service fee. So I ended paying $37. I don't understand why they tack on the service fee. Why not, just make it $37. 

You are paying $37 for just one rotation. The ride duration lasted 30 minutes. 

I heard that the pod can hold up to 40 passangers, but in reality, they wouldn't want to put more than 20 guests in one pod or else people wouldn't have enough space to look out the windows.

The view of the Vegas strip was spectacular since it's in the dead center of the Vegas Strip. 

There's even a 5 seconds countdown to the highest point on the wheel. You can see the countdown at the 6 min 30 seconds mark in the video.

It's best to go on it at night instead of during the day. That's why it costs so much. At night, it's spectacular. 

Will I do it again? Yes. Only if they reduce there price down to Stratosphere tower admission price of $18. It's a little pricey for just one rotation. I do believe that they will offer discount in the near future probably by end of summer.

So, here's crystal cleared HD video of the HIgh Roller from my YouTube channel: 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GPQEoGLCun8

SoCal Attractions 360
