Mom & dad really enjoyed the Vegas lights from 550 feet & the ride.  Service gets a zero.  Box office a five star, along w/ honest Jeremy at the bar who was helping a new bartender & saving us money on souvenirs cups versus a regular cup of $9 wine.  They serve Kendall Jackson Chardonnay which helped to relax me from the tension below the escalators w/ Christina & Suzy.  

Happy Veterans Day, we made it off safely!  Hope you all enjoyed the day like mom, dad, Jeff C. & I did overall.

The view was magnificent (period). Everything else, including the staff, horrible! I'm a local playing tour guide; it was my first experience. I invited guests to this venue after they came from a show. Therefore it was late, precisely in time for the "High Roller Late Night Happy Hour," which began after 10 p.m. on this Wednesday. My guests won cocktail glasses at a show earlier this evening. After paying and going through the layers of holding areas, just prior to entering HRoller, security said no glass allowed. Okay, no problem, I understand the safety concern and I do not dispute that.  Glass in this enclosed pod is not a good idea.  BUT, guess where you have to leave your contraband?  At the concierge at the front of Linq, at the Quad!!! Certainly not anywhere convenient! Did they think of installing maybe paid lockers for added revenue and better customer convenience?!? Someplace more accessible perhaps and not at another zip code!!! At the very least, forewarn the customer of what is not allowed BEFORE they pay the non-refundable fare!

Then they advertise that there is a bar in every pod for happy hour. As we got rushed into our pod, you guessed it;  NO f'ing bar!!! Their reply, "Oh you got the Las Vegas residents discount, so the bar is not included.  That costs extra." So what they're saying is LV residents don't drink alcohol?!!? Why even offer a discount if it really isn't a discount?! You're taking something away in order to give the guest a purported discount. That's asinine!  

This tourist venue does NOT have the customer's interest at heart, just rape the tourist of their money.  So when this local is asked for a recommendation, this is one attraction that does not get my vote. Steer clear. Liars and rip offs!

We wanted to start our day off right and go on the Farris wheel one of the workers told us we could go purchase alcohol so we went and purchased a small bottle and drinks we go to get on they were hassling us and all of a sudden said we couldn't get on because of our alcohol purchase then the manager Carolina was. Such a bitch excuses my language but I've never delt with such a rude closed minded woman int life we were being nice and explaining our situation and your attitude was ridicules just wasted 140 for nothing and ruined our day they need to train there employees to the correct Information before they have people waste there money before they haute people what a waste of my time deffinatily not manager quality

You no longer have to be a high roller to get the best view in town. The High Roller Ferris Wheel will take you on a 30-minute orbit, offering sweeping views of The Strip, for less money then you'll lose in 5 minutes at a blackjack table. 

Located at the end of The LINQ, a trendy new shopping promenade, this new attraction reaches record heights at 550 feet, outdoing even the London Eye by over 100 feet. Having been on the London Eye, I found the High Roller to be a comparably breathtaking experience, minus paying twice as much and travelling half way around the world. 

Like the London Eye, passengers are loaded into enclosed pods, which should help the slightly acrophobic individuals like myself feel safer.

A daytime ride (before 6pm) is about $25, while a nighttime ride (after 6pm) is more expensive at around $35, but worth the price hike to see Sin City lit up like a Lite-Brite toy. 

With shopping, shows, and sinful delights, I like to think of Vegas as a collection of spectacular experiences for people of all backgrounds and pocketbook sizes, and being at the top of this wheel is an affordable high that you may be a bit reluctant to come down from.
A must do while in Vegas. 550 feet in the air gives you a great view of the strip and the surrounding areas. We went at 1 am there was no lines and only had to share our pod with one other couple.

This was a really cool experience and the views are wonderful at night. The line goes by quite fast and the pods are not packed full. The total experience takes about 30mins and they play music while you're on it.
We saw there is a happy hour line where for $5 more per person you get to ride on a pod with a bar (although I'm sure you pay for those drinks). Those pods seemed a lot more crowded.
They also have the ability to stop the pods while loading so the elderly or handicap can get on. Wheelchairs and strollers welcome.

It was a cool view of vegas but I would recommend going at night. Also, check your receipt when you order drinks. I was charged for a drink I didn't even order and when I went back for a refund the bartender persisted that my friend didn't pay for a drink. Which made no sense. Why would you make someone a drink and let them walk away without paying?

I think High Roller is a must do if you visit Vegas. We were lucky enough to get $20 special per adult during Christmas season.
I have a fear of height but High Roller was so steady and gradual that I didn't feel a thing. The view you see from High Roller is priceless. 

Each Roller fits roughly about 15 people and still very roomy. You're free to walk around while the Roller is moving. There's also two small sitting area if you rather park yourself.

Virtual tour guide from TV screen will inform you every 10 minutes of your ride. 
High Roller is located outside of Linq Hotel.

Super cool new experience in Vegas for newcomers and frequent fliers alike.  Yes, a little costly, but for those who don't get to stay on the 50th floor of some of the fancier hotel resorts, this is a great way to check out that sexy skyline that is Las Vegas at night.  Ticket prices are cheaper during the day (and for locals, military, and children), but the experience is truly amazing at night.  In addition to getting an incredible view, if you approaching the High Roller from the Strip, you'll get to walk through this whole new promenade associated with the Linq showcasing foods from all over the country like Ghiradhelli, Sprinkles, and Yardhouse.  The ride is very slow, taking 30 minutes in total to go all the way around.  For those who can't stand for that long, there are small benches on both sides of the pod.  There is a cool and kind of creepy set of screens with one guy providing feedback about your height, the construction of the High Roller and other fun Vegas facts.  Also, very easy to pick up a cab from a taxi stand at the Linq if you're not able to walk back to wherever you are staying.

If I am ever in Las Vegas again, and I probably will be, I will most definitely stop by The High Roller again. I had such a good time, despite being terribly afraid of heights. If you are afraid of heights I'd suggest you drink a little before you get there. I wish I would have.

I found a coupon on Living Social (it's like Groupon) so I only paid $25 and that included the open bar, but you had to get on the wheel before 7pm. It's best if you go around 6pm since the sun has already set and view is much nicer at night time. 

If you don't get the tickets through living social, the day time "happy half hour" is $29.95, it's only a $5 difference, but if you go with 4 people you just saved yourself $20, you're welcome. The night time "happy half hour" is $44.95 that includes the open bar.

Like I said, if you are afraid of heights, you are going to need that open bar if you don't get the open bar, you're going to have a bad time! And you're already in Vegas, what better place to get drunk? 

I spent most of my time near the bar because I needed lots of drinks to cope with the idea that I was at least 300ft in the air, in a glass pod, with about 20 other, possibly heavy, people. The cool thing was, that I really could have as many drinks as I wanted, and I did. 

I had a few of their signature drinks like the Vegas Sunset and High Roller something. I don't quite remember. All I remember is that they were good. I also took some patron shots which I rarely do, but it was my birthday so screw it. 

Eventually I was 550ft up in the air. The view was amazing. I could see all of Las Vegas from my pod. All the buildings that seemed like never ending sky scrapers from the ground now looked like a bunch of twinkly lights in a distance.

For the price it's simply not worth it! They have the AC cranked up so high and in top of that I bought a frost drink, even tho it was the middle of summer I was freezing!!! That and it's boring really. Not enough room for everyone to sit, crowded and uncomfortable. I will not go again.

Great views! We went on a Wednesday night and it was not crowded, only us and one other couple in the pod. Save some money by buying your ticket at the Paris Eiffel Tower, they combine tickets to both for $30/per person, which is less then the $37 charged at the High Roller alone.

We did the "happy hour" ride! If you're over 21 this is the ONLY way to ride! Our bartender, Steve, was an absolute delight! We were celebrating my birthday and he made sure to make my celebration a memorable experience! The view was gorgeous, the car was super comfy, and the service from the ticket desk to our bartender was top notch! If you do the happy hour rides be sure to tip your bartender! They deserve it!

We had a good time. We paid for the less expensive day-time ride and got the really good discount for being a Rapid Rewards member. Ended up costing $19/person as opposed to $27 each. 
The ride itself was fun. 1/2 hour for one time around. They pack on about 20 people per pod which is plenty of room. I think they could pack more if they really wanted to but less is better in this case. I don't see the value in paying extra for the pod w the open bar. There's only one bartender serving 20 or so people for only half hour and there's no where to pee in that 30 minutes. 
I will probably ride this again at some point.

While mildly gimmicky, it is a cool way to see the sights and lights of Vegas. Definitely go at night, there's just more to see then.

The staff was friendly and they have lots of options for tickets (check their site, Groupon, and LivingSocial before dropping any cash on this so you get the best deal), plus some pods have bars on them (of course they do). Of course they try and sucker you in with the pictures, but you can politely decline before entering the High Roller if you'd like.

My only issue is that there isn't much to see on the side opposite The Strip. Perhaps one day it will be more built up, but for now it's pretty much just parking lots.
A thirty minute experience that is truly worth the investment. Cough up the extra $10 to get a pod that includes the open bar. Stunning views and a fabulous experience.

I didn't know it was the largest observation wheel in the world! It was fun! Some people backed out when in line? Lol! It was not scary at all since the wheel is steady and you can walk around in it, we had the VIP tickets happy half hour, for 30 mins we were there and an open bar. I actually got drunk taking advantage of unlimited drinks haha. It was a great experience for sure! Will definitely do it again. There's music inside with flat screen tv playing music videos, pretty cool. It's like a mini bubble club. Love it!

I took my family on the High Roller in July 2016, and we thought the ride offered great views, but was nothing special.

The price for an adult is $35, children under 12 are free.  There are many Groupons and living socials deals to save you a couple of dollars.

You enter a bubble, and as the giant wheel makes one complete revolution you get incredible views of the Las Vegas Strip.  The revolution takes about 30-40 minutes.  The wheel moves very slow and is very stable, if not for the changing view, you would not even know you were moving.

The only down side is that you are crammed in the pod with a lot of people you don't know.  If one of them is a drunk bung-hole, it will be a long 30 minutes.

After you get off the ride, you'll be offered to buy your green screen picture that you took prior to entering the High Roller for the special price of $50!!!  Are they serious?!?  I guess if you are in a group of people on you all share the price it's no big deal.  But if you are just a couple or a family, that is a lot for a posed picture.

If you have never been on the High Roller I would recommend doing it at least once, but only once in the evening, to get the best views.  Make sure you get a deal and don't pay full price.

After filling up from dinner, we decided to check out The High Roller. As far as I understand, The High Roller is the tallest Ferris Wheel/Observation Deck in the world. It towers over the Vegas Strip at 550 feet at this tallest. This particular Ferris Wheel is very slow moving and takes a full 30 minutes to make a full rotation. This isn't a thrill ride, it is all about the view. 

We purchased our tickets inside the Paris Hotel/Casino and got them as a package deal that included a pass to the Observation Deck on the top of the Eiffel Tower. The combo pass cost a total of $30 per ticket. It is a good idea to purchase tickets before you show up to The High Roller. There was a long, slow-moving line to purchase tickets that we were able to skip. There also is an option to upgrade your ticket to an open bar. 

We did wait for about 15 minutes to be able to get on the ride. The compartments hold somewhere between 15-20 people; however, there is only seating available for about 6-8 people. Luckily, our compartment only had two other couples in it so there was plenty of space. The compartment before us seemed like it was jam packed. 

Reaching the peak gives an amazing view of Las Vegas and the Strip. The High Roller is even taller than many of the Hotels/Casinos so you can see the mountains surrounding the valley. Very cool!

Highly recommend purchasing tickets for the happy half hour at night!

For those of you who don't know, the High Roller is the world's largest Ferris wheel. At an imposing 550 feet tall, this Ferris wheel takes about 30mins to make one complete rotation, allowing you ample time to appreciate the views. Tickets are $27 for the daytime and nighttime tickets (from 7pm on) are $37. Of course what is vegas without some alcohol?! Five of the pods are equipped with a bar which incurs a higher price ($37, $52) but the ride is still worth it. I highly recommend purchasing tickets at night as the view is gorgeous. 

The bar itself is lacking in variety but they have the basics covered. I forgot the name of my bartender (sorry, bro) but he was rather quick when making drinks! 

As for the tickets, you can purchase on their site but to try to check groupon for some sort of deal. 

Also, the ferris wheel doesn't really stop so you must be careful when entering and exiting the pod. 

All in all, this was a fun experience and I recommend you guys check this place out as well. Cheers!

As soon as this started going up a few years ago I knew I wanted to try it out.  I still want to try out the Eye in London but the High Roller will suffice for now :)  Prior to our Canyon adventure trip this was THE one thing I knew I would check out no matter what.  The morning of our first day in Vegas after hiking around Utah and Arizona I went over to the Linq and bought my ticket for the first 'round trip' of the day.  My boyfriend never showed much interest in this from the very beginning but I wasn't going to let that stop me from my fun!  

During the day it's quite pretty to see the area and the mountains.  Of course it's not at night when all the lights and the strip are flashing bright but sometimes it's preferable to have a peaceful relaxing experience.  Each capsule that you jump into is pretty spacious with benches to sit and enjoy your party's company it comes equipped with a talking man in a TV screen which I found quite amusing, they seriously must have timed it to match  each part of the wheel you get to.  Granted, it takes about a half hour to get through one revolution but still it was amusing to listen to that talking man, I am curious what he says during the night time revolutions.  

Anyways, it was a fun experience and it was great to see the strip and the mountains from high up on the wheel.   I will tell you that if you're extremely afraid of heights it may not be the best thing for you, but it's certainly not too bad.  I get a bit nervous of heights and Angel's Landing was one thing that made me hecka nervous, but the high roller should be on your list of things to do when in Vegas, if the high ticket price scares you check it out during the day, preferably before the Linq gets too crowded :)

The High Roller is just one of those things that you have to do at least once. And if you want to do it right, then do it once the moon is out and the sun has gracefully bowed down. The ticket prices do increase after 6pm, but for me the view was worth it. We paid slightly under $150 (after taxesd and fees) for 4 adults and my son was free. 

There was a line for the tickets the night we went, but quickly found out that their are windows where tickets can be purchased. A lady was helping us and almost double charged us but quickly caught and fixed her error. 

Once we purchased our tickets, entering was fairly easy. They did a quick security check of the ladies purses, no check on the men. We then followed some escalators and made our way up. 

Once you enter the loading area, they herd you into different waiting sections. Boarding our pod did not take a long wait but boarding it with a child and my mother was almost a challenge. They had to run more than we did a fast walk.

There were roughly 20 people in our pod and only half of them were intoxicated, so it wasn't a bad ride. There is ample seating for everyone and music to help you enjoy your ride. The pod moves so slow, it doesn't actually feel like you are moving at all. Which is great for taking pictures.

They have monitors in the pods but the music was so loud, I couldn't really hear what was being said on the monitor. It does let you know when you reach the highest point of 550 feet and that is nice.

It was a wonderful experience and we got some amazing pictures. I highly recommend it for anyone to do at least once.
I wish they could space you out more on a slow night. We were in a pod with loud and rude kids, kind of running the experience. Overall worth doing once, but not really that worth a second visit

We were a group of 20 locals who could not wait long enough for that Happy Hour!  We had a pod to ourselves, it had a nice bar, and the bartender was great.  She served strong drinks which kept us buzzed and happy.  Views were fantastic, mostly of Strip casinos.  The big draw was the party atmosphere.  Drink as much as you can for 30 minutes at a higher altitude.  The altitude must have helped since it did not take long for people to start mingling, talking, and laughing.  If your spirit is not high when you take off, it will be when you land.  Highly recommended for locals and visitors alike!

If you are debating the High Roller Happy Hour. Don't! Just pay the extra little bit, it is SO worth it! We went right at 5:30 p.m. on a Sunday. The sun was just starting to set when we got in line and by the time we got to our pod, it was completely dark. PERFECT! Me and my 2 friends were on with 6 others, so there were 9 of us on the pod, plus the bartender. I would say this was a perfect size for the Open Bar, as the Bar itself takes up quite a bit of room. Our bartender was GREAT!!! If you think 30 minutes isn't enough time or that the bartenders will be stingy, WRONG. I ended up with 7 drinks. Yes, they come in small plastic cups but our bartender was not stingy with the alcohol. Also, by the 2nd round, he knew what everyone was drinking and was already making the next round before we even walked back over to the bar. By the end of the ride, I had had 7 drinks + 1 shot. It was one of my friend's birthday and the bartender made the entire pod gummy bear shots, so we could all do a celebratory shot together. The bartender also made us all one last drink, so we could all take one to go, as we were coming back to the landing. We had a pod of people from all over the world and they were all great and laid back. No mean drunk jerks or the like. It was SO fun! 

Oh yeah, and the views are pretty great too. If you are debating between doing the regular ticket vs. the happy hour... GET THE HAPPY HOUR. Hands Down. I would totally do it again.

Oh My Gosh.
I must preface this by saying we got a slammin deal on Travel Zoo. We got the night time, open bar pod for only $29/each! WOW! That being said, I would pay full price to be able to do it again.

You enter, and pay or show your promo code. The line moves surprisingly fast. Then you got up to a bar (if you have the free drinks - I wouldn't waste your money here). You then go up another level, and take a photo on a green wall. --they show you your pictures after you get off (like a roller coaster) but they are green screen-ed onto this TERRIBLE computer generated graphic of the Vegas skyline (puke!) PLUS they wanted $50 for the photo! I would totally skip this if I were you! 

Anyways - you go outside and separate into your lines depending on your ticket. You hop on the pod (while it is still moving! lol) and start your journey. The bar tender in our pod was awesome. She had all sorts of hard alcohol/mixers also coors light, miller light, and one other beer. She was serving them up like wild - you could get as many as you want. I think I had 4 cocktails in the 30 minute time period.

Dude. I will be doing the High Roller every. time. I come to Vegas. If you are thinking about it....DO IT!
Rode the High Roller last week for the first time.  We got a Groupon for the "Happy Half Hour".  Amazing view!  Staff was all very fun and energetic.  Highly recommended!!

You need to know that I am an acrophobic.  I mean it is so bad that I can't go up a ladder in my own home.  I kept fighting my husband about going on this, because if I had a panic attack, there is no off, I would be stuck there for 30 minutes.  I have lost my mind on ferris wheels before.  So the fear was real.

I was feeling particularly strong this day and when Hubby said, come on.  I finally said ok.  It was during the day on a weekday.  There were minimal waits for the tickets and no waiting to get on.

The HARDEST part for me was to get on the moving pod on a high platform with no guard rails.  In my mind, I kept seeing myself miss and then I fall to my death.  Well there is no chance of that happening, but with phobia all reasoning goes out the door.  Hubby helped me get into the pod.  I was absolutely thrilled to find out we ride alone.  They do not fill each pod, its only your group.  So whether there are 2 of you or 10, only your group goes in.  That was excellent, because it helped with my trepidation.  

I immediately sat down on the bench once we were inside and took a few slow deep breaths.  I sat quietly and realized you can barely tell you are moving.  I felt like I was in a hotel room or a restaurant on a higher level in a high rise.  Since I didn't have obvious movement or sudden jolts, I relaxed.  

I was able to get up and take a few photos, but i never ventured from the center of the pod.  Hubby was up against the glass the whole time or dancing, he loves heights.  There is a silly CGI character that comes up on the tv screens and gives you trivia about the High Roller or Vegas throughout the entire ride, and he also tells you when you reach the highest point of 550 feet in the sky.

The ride was smooth, did not stress me out like I expected and the views are endless.  I honestly didn't think I would enjoy this, but I did and I would do it again.  Remember, I am the one that can't climb a ladder without a panic attack.

I absolutely loved this Ferris wheel...I just wish the ride was longer. It supposedly takes half an hour to go around, but I think it's more like 20 minutes. For the price they charge, you should get to go around twice atleast.  We decided to go Tuesday night at 11:40pm so that we'd still be on it at midnight when it turned August 26th (my birthday). There were only two other people and a small child in our pod, which was super nice, I was afraid of it being over crowded and not being able to move around but we pretty much had it to ourselves. The view from the top is stunningly beautiful...360 degree views of the entire city. I'm not so sure I'd be interested in a day time ride, but it is cheaper, I'd definitely do the night time ride again and I'd probably drop the extra money and get the open bar pod!

I love that it opens until 2am. The Vegas Strip is a beaut and having a 360 degrees panoramic view while 550 feet up in the air is thrilling and a genius idea. There's a bar where you can purchase your drinks prior to the ride. They do take a picture of you and your party prior to the ride and of course sell it to you for a hefty price afterwards. It's a little pricier to go at night but I think to see the Vegas strip at night is a beautiful sight to see. We went after midnight so we only shared a pod with another couple. It's a  great once-in-a-lifetime activity to put on your to-do list in Vegas!

DO NOT GO EARLY AS THE FIRST BAR GROUP OF THE DAY! They do not allow you to SIT anywhere in their building. No one was there but us, a gentleman came and asked us to stand (we were sitting on the floor). We were told there are no chairs because we HAVE TO STAND. so, no elderly, no little kids, or anyone needing a moment to sit.

After months of anticipation I was finally able to do the ferris wheel experience and it was the time of my life to say the very least.

Somehow my wife convinced the height freaks of my family to go on here, but go figure once up there they weren't even phased at all..We all wanted to do the happy hour which at $52 for non-locals isn't that bad..I know it was discounted for locals, but not exactly sure of the price on that one as my step mom surprised us with tickets instead..Grr! Ha-ha

The pod itself is massive in size from an outside look and even on the inside it was more roomy even with the bar in it than I had anticipated. Our pod alone had maybe like 20 people in it and there was still plenty of walking space so I'm glad it wasn't wall to wall personal space invasions or my review would be much different!

The view is amazing and at night it is a thing of beauty..I did get quite a tip for anyone wondering what the best time would be..We went at 7:40pm and I guess some guy had calculated this enough to time it with the Bellagio fountains..So come 8:00pm when we reached the top of the wheel we had the view and a picture to catch the fountain show as well in the background..That was certainly well worth the price in full! 

I do have to recognize our bartender, Reece, as he was outstanding. I think between our group we tipped him about $30, but it was well deserved..He kept such a positive vibe the entire outing and honestly if you're genuinely nice to the guy he certainly keeps you well taken care of drink wise (if you know what I mean)..I think between the 3 drinks I had I could've burned a hair leg with the amount of alcohol I consumed in that short of a time..Ha-ha! The coolest thing he did was when I attempted to get a final drink..I initially wanted to try the famous gummy bear shot, but was running out of time to get it for various reasons..He ended up making me a gummy bear drink for the road instead..How cool is that? I really hope he is there for us next year!

Cool experience with my friends. The HAPPY HOUR RIDE is the best and I highly recommend it. You get to drink as much as you can and the bartender even has the group do a round of shots. The high roller moves slower than you would expect. However, this was great since you only go around once. The ride itself is 30 minutes long and you get to see a beautiful view of Las Vegas. It has air conditioning to keep you cool. Our bartender was great, fun and full of energy! He was busy serving up the drinks. Overall I had a ball and I think this is worth doing at least ONCE in your life!

Breath taking views totally worth it. Don't worry there are two bathroom and a full bar available before you go 550 feet in the air. The observations pods feel really safe and sturdy. The entire ride takes about 30 minutes and allows you to see the entire city and beyond. We went in the evening but I hear that a  day time ride will bring different views as well.

Great attraction when visiting Las Vegas. I recommend doing this attraction at night. You'll get a great view of the city and lights. Ride will last approximately 30 mins from start to finish. We paid $37 for tickets. To me, this was a little over priced.

The High Roller was one of the things that I was looking forward to doing the most in Vegas and it didn't disappoint. It may not be the most heart-pounding, adrenaline-pumping activity, but it makes for a really nice thing to do during downtime. We went there the night we got in after an agonizing 24 hours of travel and it was the perfect way to unwind and relax while still being able to enjoy the fact that we had actually made it to Vegas. 

Because it wasn't a terribly busy night and we were a group of eight, we ended up getting an entire pod to ourselves. It was incredibly spacious, totally clean and had crystal-clear 360 views of the beautifully lit city. The ride was extremely smooth and even though you're hundreds of miles in the air, you couldn't feel more secure. There is a screen with a commentator telling you fun facts about the city which is nice for the info buffs out there but it isn't too overpowering if you're with friends and just want to enjoy their company and the view, as was the case with us. The roughly 30 minutes that it lasts is a great amount of time because if you're weary when it starts, its over pretty quick but its more than enough time to see all the sights and take lots of pics. 

I don't know what it would be like in the day (other than less expensive), but I totally recommend doing it at night. I would imagine it's also really nice for families with children or older adults, as like I said before, it's not a gut-wrenching ride nor is it like a cramped up Ferris wheel that feels like you'll either expire from claustrophobia or the tinny, rinky-dink coop falling off. Its location at The Linq is nice as well as it's at the end of The Promenade and is surrounded by quite a few nice shops and family-friendly eateries. All in all, I'd say is definitely worth a do!

As soon as I heard about the opening of the High Roller I couldn't wait to go on it. I have a soft spot for pretty views and rides. A week before my trip I saw High Roller being advertised on Groupon so I got the deal! 

I went on a Sunday night around 8:30pm with a group of 5. Because we all had either a groupon or Living social voucher, we were able to skip the lines and go straight to the ride. 

It was a beautiful view of the strip. I personally think its best to go at night to see all the glamorous lights that shine throughout Vegas. If I were rating the view itself- it would get 5 stars. 

CON- you are in the ferris wheels with groups of "strangers." the group we got stuck with was weird and ruined our experience. I understand to make it a faster line- you have to group groups together but I wish we had our own cart. The ride also  looks a lot more entertaining while in motion in advertisements. 

Overall it was a nice experience to see the strip up high at night. I would not ride again. It is overpriced. I can just go to the rooftop somewhere and get a similar view, for free!

My 94 year old MIL wanted to do this for her birthday, so we went over there around noon on a Monday. There were no crowds, needless to say! But it was fun, and since it was a beautiful clear day we could see all around, the mountains, the airport, the Wynn golf course--just very nice. She absolutely loved it! They are able to completely stop it for people who need extra time to get on or off, so that was good, as I was concerned about her trying to get on something that was moving. The locals day price was only $11.50 so it was certainly worth that.

Our bartender was very friendly and the views were amazing. We went at sunset and the skyline was quiet beautiful. There were about 25 in our car and the line did get long to get a drink but the experience was great.

You want smooth? This ride is smooooth. And the views, of course, are incredible.

Full disclosure: I'm deathly afraid of heights and this thing goes crazy high. But apart from a few jitters at the start, I was thrilled and amazed at how comfortable I felt.  I was seriously bummed when the ride ended.

There are deals to be had online and apparently with Groupon so do a little homework before you go.

Time it right and try to go at twilight so you can see Sin City both in the light and then all lit up.

Normally I would say this is a one and done activity but I could and would do this again. We had an absolute blast.

Went yesterday with a group of seven and got the happy half hour deal. We had a 40 year resident of Las Vegas at the bar serving drinks and telling us details of the construction and taking pictures of us. She was excellent.

We had no trouble downing drinks in the thirty or so minutes we were up there and for 10 bucks on Christmas Eve, you can't find a better time to be had. Let me be clear, admission was twenty bucks plus an extra ten for the bar car

I'd do this again at twice the cost it was that much fun.

New "must do" attraction in Vegas. Great for groups! Booked group tickets on-line by e-mail and picked them up when we were there. Chose 4:30 to see the sunset and some of the Vegas lights since prices went up at 5. Went with 12 people. Everyone got anywhere from 3-5 drinks during the ride (you can bring one to go). Bring cash for tips! Bring your camera. Pictures came out so great, they look green-screened. Will go again next time we're in Vegas.

We showed up early on a Sunday and got an entire capsule to ourselves. I brought my family including my wife, 1 year old son and my mother. It was a nice way to enjoy the views of the city and given that we didn't have to wait in line it was even better. Service was good. Everyone was nice. What more can you ask for?

Nothing is more magical than an evening on the High Roller Happy Half Hour. 
1) Cheryl is a speedy bar tender who promises to make your all you can drink worth it!
2) the three adjectives to describe this are : charming, cheerful, and chock full of fun.
3) get the group rate for 10 or more!

Overall if I could give it 10 stars I would. No need to pregame. 

#noonelosesthebrodericks

Loved the high roller! My husband and I got free tickets for signing up for a Visa card that I'll never use.. So it essentially saved us $80 (current groupon available). Our cart only has 8 people in it and we went at night as well. The cart in front of us was very full, we are assuming at maximum capacity. The views of the city are beautiful and the ride is very smooth you can't even tell you are moving. The video inside is pretty annoying but didn't notice it too much until the end. You can bring drinks with you or you can buy right before you go in. It was one of my favorite things to do in Vegas!

I was expecting something a lot more exciting so yeah, it was ok.  I didn't feel like this was a "wow" for me, although my spouse thought it was cool so there ya go.  I had a Living Social deal for 2 ppl, nighttime entry and 2 drinks( worth 10.00 each) for 54.00.  If you're contemplating a visit, please check groupon or Living Social.  There is always a deal to be had.

Great ride and great views of the strip. If possible try to time getting in your pod 15 minutes before the hour so you catch the Bellagio fountain show. Only downside is the dude on the tv screens taking during the ride.  Constant cheesy jokes including "lol we are 420 feet up blaze it dudes."

The High Roller is the world's tallest observation wheel with 360 degree views of the Strip and suburbs.  You share a pod with a few others for a 30 minute or so ride. The pod has some seating so if your pod isn't too full you can sit and there are TV monitors broadcasting a recorded Host who gives information and updates throughout the ride.

You choose your time slot when you purchase your tickets so think about how you want to see the city, during the day you can see farther and with more detail, at night you get the city lights.

I wouldn't say this is a must do when in Vegas, only go if you like observation decks/wheels. Compared to other city's observation decks/wheels, the High Roller is very well done.

It was a nice ride. Glad it was slow because you get a good chance to see Vegas and the surrounding areas. 

I rode it during the day and all my friends said they went at night and loved it. Of course that means I'll be taking a night ride not time I'm there.

My family and I experienced the ride last weekend while in town. It's kinda neat at night to ride if your not looking for high speed and thrills. Very scenic at the top, kinda one of those things you can check off your list that you did it. The only complaint it's a little pricy.

Been on the high roller three times and always have a blast! Me and my boyfriend always do the happy half hour and our bartenders usually make the experience a great one (Derrick was our favorite)!
It's always a fun time and they even make it a point sometimes to do a drinking game! The price is very reasonable for unlimited drinks in 30 minutes, with a fantastic view.

Our only problem (and why this is a four star rating) was this last week. Me and my boyfriend made it on time to do the before 5pm special. We had been the day before so we got the $10 off to come again. They didn't give it to us because it didn't include HHH, which is fine. Though we have gotten a military discount before, the cashier at the front who happened to be very rude, blatantly said that we couldn't get it and that if we wanted to wait, we could, but by then it would be after the 5 o'clock happy hour price.
$37 for open bars amazing with the view. It's so worth it! All you can drink !!!! Tips: buy the ticket that include alcohol !
Awesome view with unlimited alcohol what more can you ask for. Had a great time met people from san fran and got super wasted

Well, it's not what I expected...you could barley tell it's moving, unless you look at the the pod from below. 

Bc looking at the strip at a very slow pace is difficult to tell, but yes, you are moving. 

And even with led light and changing colors from time to time, we're inside the pod, it's not as enjoyable view from inside the pod as it is outside. 

I used my iPhone 6 and had it on "Lapse-time" and played it back and it was awesome!! If you have a rubber case, you can place it on the window facing the strip...don't move it or you'll ruin it. 

The pod I was in had about no more than 15 people. 
I paid $35 per ticket for night time. Before you get on the pod, in the middle section has a bar where you can purchase drinks. 

For those who paid "Full Admission" has a bar in the middle of their pod for larger groups. Pay a little more extra...good for a huge group and fits up to 40 people. 

The ride for me was 20-24 mins...haha yes, we timed it. Most say it's 30mins. Also, Please use the restroom before you hop on this pod...for those who has a bladder issue.

I really wanted to like the High Roller. The whole idea sounded really cool. However, once you add in the high $$ just to get in here, it just wasn't.

It takes a good 30+ to get all the way around the wheel, assuming it doesn't stop for no reason (ours did several times). The view would be cool - if it wasn't one you couldn't get from a high room at any of the strip facing hotel rooms. 

I'm glad we got a discount on our tix, cause even tho I still feel like we overpaid, we didn't pay as much as it could've been.

Yes, this was definitely an experience...half hour, we didn't opt for the open bar but it was still so worth it.  There were only 6 of us in the pod and we took quite a lot of selfies....it's the best way to see the city lights so night time ride is definitely recommended.  The price is a little high but I still think it's worth it.  It's pretty cool, even for those who are afraid of heights...it isn't scary at all, just beautiful!

Really cool ride and goes up 550 feet so be aware if you're afraid of heights! Went on around 6:30 and the view was great and there were only 6 of us in the bubble. Only thing that scared me is that they're able to fit 40 people in the bubble and I personally would feel claustrophobic if that happened! Pretty awesome thing to do when in Vegas!
Great experience ever. Got the open bar totally worth it. Tory was the best bar tender ever and Deja was most helpful at the sky shop. Thank you for a wonderful time.

The one-of-a-kind High Roller is the world's tallest observation ferris wheel ~ an incredible 30-minute experience.

Aerial view of the Las Vegas Strip as never seen before March 2014 except briefly by plane or helicopter.  

28 transparent pods hold 40 passengers each, though I've never ridden with more than 8 on weekdays.  

Fascinating in day & also when thousands of lights glow in the sky.  

I went @ Sunset & captured both in postcard-quality photos & videos.
Amazing views, kids were free, locals over 12 get half off. The pod was very clean and we enjoyed seeing our city sparkling at night. Check it out!
Not worth the money and most importantly time! If ur off on a weekend dont waste ur time n money taking the ride. The ball is overly crowded leaving u not enough space to see the view.

SO recommend this! For only $70 we got the groupon and did the happy hour at 9:15pm on a friday night. There was only about 10 people in our happy hour pod and we felt like we had more than enough room to take plenty of photos and enjoy the views. Everyone says to look towards the strip, but don't forget to turn around! the moon was beautiful! We didn't wait in line at all, we went to the concierge and purchased our tickets earlier in the day so we just walked right up the high roller and walked right on. Very easy and the bartender was hilarious and made the trip really fun. 

We each had about 4-5 strong drinks and 2 shots each. His was a double and a single so I guess he had three shots. WELL worth the money!

TIP: If you play black jack at Flamingo's you can receive a free High Roller voucher ticket! 

The High Roller definitely stands out in Vegas. It's huge! You really can't miss it. Seeing this for the first time, I was set on checking it out. I mean it looks pretty damn cool :D 

Ended up checking it out on a Tuesday around midnight.  After experiencing the High Roller, I thought it was alright. I mean, it's kind of cool because you go so high, and you can see a lot of things from up there. However it is pretty boring. 

There is no alcohol served in the pods, so you have to make sure to grab a drink at the bar before you go up. There also is no bathroom in the pods, so if you gatta go - you better hold it! 

The pods are really nice though. Sleek and clean. Only a few seats and they have a TV monitor inside with a guy narrating everything for you.  He's super enthusiastic and does trivia along with a countdown for when you get to the top. 

Overall, I'm happy I got to experience the High Roller for free. If I had to pay to experience this again, I wouldn't do it.

Awesome experience. We did the open bar option... Unlimited drinks while you ride! Seeing the views of the strip are really cool. Our bartender was awesome and kept the drinks coming. It's 30 minutes that you ride, but it goes pretty quick (time wise). I couldn't believe it was over when it was. Maybe I was having too much fun ;) it's still was a great time. If you have a group of friends while visiting, make sure you do this.

Awesome. Totally awesome! It's been awhile since I've quoted Jeff Spicolli.

The High Roller Happy Half-Hour was one of the highlights of our Vegas trip. We bought the Groupon for $69, which was definitely the way to go. It included 2 Happy Hour tickets (more on that later), and we were able to pick the time (evening is definitely best). 

The view is incredible. I am sure it would be beautiful in the daytime as well, but seeing Vegas lit up at night from the top of the wheel was breathtaking. 

I've never really been afraid of heights, but when we were towards the very top and we could literally look down and see the tops of every casino, it was a little unnerving. The alcohol definitely helped. 

The Happy Half Hour passes include an open bar/all you can drink option. I was dubious of this - how many drinks can you really imbibe in one half hour, especially when there are 25 other people in the car with you and only one bartender? As it turns out - no worries there! Our bartender Tim (or Tom?) was AWESOME! He had a whole system down pat to get drinks ready faster than you can throw them back! And he wasn't using generic well brands - they were stocked with Skyy Vodka, Jack, Bacardi, etc. 

I will definitely make a trip back to the High Roller every time I come back to Vegas!

What a wonderful way to experience the views of Las Vegas.  Insted of walking around in circles under the heat do yourself a favor and pay the 36 bucks to see the strip in an air conditioned room . We went on father's day and all father's were free and even received a 10 dollar credit for the bar which the hubby really appreciate since the coronas were 9 bucks a piece. All the staff was genuinely friendly and looked happy to assist us as we wondered lost inside the very confusing building.  They had 2 different box offices and 4 kiosks(which were not working) so we were a bit confused as to where we had to go to purchase our tickets. I'd say to avoid the lines and buy your tickets at home since once you have your tickets you go straight to the ride. The only reason I gave it 4 stars is do to the fact that the wheel does not stop when your are boarding or when you are exiting.  It was pretty scary since we had a stroller with us and my husband had to quickly exit and pull our stroller while I jumped out with our child. Overall it was a great experience and for those of you who are complaining about the price keep in mind this is an attraction and like any other attractions they are going to be expensive. Nothing in Vegas is free!
I would recommend going when the sun starts to set, the strip lights are turned on, and the moon is out. The pods are a different experience.  Great way to view Las Vegas.

$35 at night to see the views of vegas. If this is something you like to do or have done in other countries like the UK, you'll like it. Personally, I think it's a waste of money. But if you have money to spend or you really want to see a different view of the strip this is for you.

During our last trip to vegas we wanted to try the high roller but we never got the chance.  This trip we decided to stay at the Linq which allowed us to give it a whirl, bad pun intended....We opted for the night time happy half hour and since we purchased Absinthe tickets as well, we got the high roller tickets for $30 each instead of the full price.  That night, after we went to Absinthe we headed over to the high roller around 1030 pm or so.  There were only a few people in line in front of us, so the wait for the "bar car" was less than 10 minutes.  The bartender gave us his spiel, carded us and away we went...There ended up being about 7 of us on in the pod which was about perfect.  The view was speculator and the bartender did a great job making sure everyone had a drink in hand, and their glass was never empty. I would highly recommend anyone who hasn't done this to do so on their next trip...I would also recommend going in the evening when you can see Las Vegas at night, it was truly spectacular.

I hate to say this, but this ride was a huge disappointment.  I mean, we had just as good of a view from our room and we didn't have to spend $50 extra dollars to sit in a pod with strangers to see it!  

Here is the thing, the London Eye (which I have been on) is special because there aren't many (if any) places along that part of the Thames to get the amazing views of the city.  In Vegas?  They are a dime a dozen! Eiffel tower, Stratosphere, or any high floor room in ANY hotel facing the strip!  

Seriously, it was majorly overpriced (and I got a discount!), super slow (painfully) and so so boring.  Then everyone on the pod ends up crowding on one side of the thing because no one cares about the valley side!  Plus we got stuck ONE CAR away from being off the thing.  Just sat there FOREVER looking at nothing but the platform and not being able to get off. It was a real fail in my opinion.  I guess I am glad we did it so now we know, but I will never bother again.  

BORING, SLOW & OVERPRICED!  Use that $50+ to upgrade your room with views of the strip- then you get the great view anytime of day or night!

It is a bit pricey but you can find deals in Living Social or Groupon! They're very friendly and it's an amazing experience. A way to continue to face my fears! And get beautiful photos of the city of Las Vegas from up high! Looks extra beautiful in the night time! I suggest buying a drink or two before going up!

I am terrified of heights. My dear asked about going this when we were there July '15 and I was adamant: NO!

After a bit of persuading this time, though, I agreed. We got $5 off per ticket for staying at a Caesars property and we chose to go during the day to get great mountain scenery since we had such an awesome nighttime view at our hotel.

They have all the lines managed very efficiently and you have an option to switch to Half Happy Hour before you ride - which is open bar for thirty minutes! We opted not to because we thought we were leaving that day. 

The High Roller never stops so you have to half-heartedly "hop" on - think escalator. 

AMAZING. I am so glad we decided to go during the day because the mountain scenery was breathtaking. Our pod was not too crowded which I was grateful for. The in-ride "entertainment" is amusing enough and provides a countdown for when you are at the apex of your journey.

 10/10 would ride again, especially at night to get that experience. (and next time, happy hour!) Very pleased with how this attraction was managed.

This is a must if you're in Vegas!! My husband and I got lucky, we asked an employee where to purchase the tickets  and she gave us 2 for $20 each. That saved us $20 each!! Get yourself a Fat Tuesday tho the drinks they have before going inside the High Roller are not good.

Not a bad experience. Lines move quickly and the views are pretty awesome. Not a bad way to spend 30 mins. I wouldn't pay full price though. Get disconnected tix from one of the vendors or Groupon. Daytime rides offer views of the desert. Evening rides you see the lights.

What made this experience awesome is we pretty much got the pod to ourselves.  It was only my husband, another couple and the bartender.  It was pretty roomy for us to walk around.  I can't imagine being in a crowded pod.  It wouldn't be much fun.  We went on a Thursday night at 7:20pm.  We had the all you can drink ticket.  It might be worth paying for it to be in a less crowded pod.  At least there will not be any kids.  The sad part, the bartender didn't know how to make a midori sour or any specialty drink.  She couldn't make me a margarita either. I was pretty disappointed.

If you're in Vegas the High Roller is definitely an awesome attraction especially at night! Seeing the lights of the entire strip is beautiful. You share a ride with 6 other people or so and alternate taking photos from the northeast direction (facing the strip). I do wish it was a little less pricier but we were able to get $5 off with my friend's military discount. It's $12 cheaper during the day but the view is not as exciting.

I have to admit, I was a tad bit nervous, approaching this massive attraction. I don't do so well with heights. Still, I booked the Happy Hour pod. It was a Wednesday night. 
Cheryl was our bartender and we all immediately fell in love with her. I'm a light drinker, but on this off-peak night, I got my money's worth-5 drinks, in 1/2 an hour! 
There were only 5 of us inside and the ride was smooth, non-frightening and worth the view, information, experience, and drinks.

The high roller was fabulous!! I used a groupon for our trip. We went on 1/31/15. My husband and i enjoyed the view!! So pretty at night time!! The open bar option was fabulous. Our bar tender was fun!! The high roller is the best photo op in Vegas!! Im scared of heights but i wasnt scared or afraid on the high roller at all.  I would go again on another trip!!

The space is much bigger than I thought - can hold up to 40 ppl in each ball! It moves slowly and gives a good bird view of the strip and city. Night view is the best. 

They provide a Bose portable speaker with Bluetooth for you to play music in each ball - but some ppl seem to have a hard time connecting to it, always try different phones.

So worth it! Only $35 per person (Apparently rides as low as $15 during the day now), just double fist the drinks when you get on. There wasnt a long line and we went prime time evening hours. They only put about 15-20 people on the pod at once, but Ive talked to people who said they were on them with less than 10. Its 30 minutes per rotation, it goes by quicker than you think.  Views are great both day and night.

Really neat! We got to see everything from up there. We went during the day time and got the whole pod to ourselves. If you stay at the Paris Las Vegas, you and your guests who are staying with you get free tickets to the High Roller. Lovely surprise!
Great timing on a Sunday night at 11:00 pm. A whole pod to ourselves!!! Smooth ride, my beer didn't spill. Amazing to be sooo high off the ground! A lot of fun, I might ride it again.

Cool and very neat experience riding the High Roller wheel. Great views of the strip & city from it. We rode at night. The cost was $70+ for 2 ppl. But I say it's worth it. Also used the outside kiosk & was able to get in fast & bypass the long line. Also bought frozen drinks to enjoy the ride. It's a 30 minute ride.

We went on a beautiful Wednesday night which wasn't overly crowded..
This new ride was fun,beautiful views,clean but come on over $75.00 for 2 is pricey.
It is definitely not a thrill or much excitement rather than just a fun time.
Never would I pay for it again.....

Awesome adventure! Went over about 4:15pm because we wanted a sunset ride. Lots of people in line, but the line moved so fast. 
Ladies at the check in desk were so nice and friendly, actually everyone we encountered that worked there was super cool! Made the experience more fun.
We got in a cube with about 30 other people and happy we all had a sweet ride together . Everyone was really nice, made the 30min ride go smoothly.
I will say at the very top of the ride, I started to get a bit dizzy, and on the way down, felt kinda weird.
But all in all, it was so awesome and I would go on it again. 
Check in on Yelp and get a $10 off your ticket or use for the next time!

If you want a relaxing break from the crowds, wait and go late, right before they close. You'll end up with stellar night views of the strip, and a small group of people, if any others at all. Loved it!

I never thought I would go on this and if I ever did I thought I would go at night. 

Well I went with a large group and I went in the day. I'm glad I did. It was actually a lot of fun. We paid for the bar car, all you can drink for the 30 minute ride. Our waitress was fun and made drinks quickly. There was a girl that turned 21 there and we all took shots with her. Fun. 

The scenery in the day was GREAT! You can see everything! I really recommend it!

I bought a Living Social voucher for $25 for 30 minutes and open bar. I enjoyed myself, but definitely would NOT pay full price for this. They pack about 25 people in each pod with only one bartender. It would have been nicer if there were two bartenders. The regular pods (without alcohol) have less people in them. The pods are WAY bigger than they appear. There is not much seating inside either, so prepare to stand. Try to go at dusk or night to enjoy all the lights. We even saw the Bellagio fountains dancing from the High Roller.

I was lucky that we got to experience this free, because it was not super exciting and the price  is not what I would ever pay to do this, but we both found it enjoyable. 
The video that plays was funny, but it was also a distraction from being in the moment and taking in the view. 

At the time I felt like I was dragging my husband through this and since it was hot, I felt really bad about it. Luckily afterward I heard him telling others about it and he thought it was kinda a cool thing, but agreed it wouldn't be something that you would need to do more than once and that the price was too high. 
It would have been worth it if the admission and bar drinks were included, at about $20 for me. So maybe after all the hype has died down, they will make it more reasonably priced? 
If you are dragging around someone that is hurting, probably best to Valet the car. lol

I am a repeat high roller. My first time here was with family last summer. It is air conditioned even during summer desert heat but not blasting cold. Keep cold water or adult drink in hand.
beautiful views both day and night!!!

This was something my mom was dead set on doing in Vegas, so we walked to the hotel and experienced this gigantic Ferris wheel. It isn't really much of an adventure, so I think the price is kind of a joke. The view is great, it really is, expect there are much taller buildings in the way at certain intervals. 

The people who work here clearly don't care and that is upsetting when you are on vacation, and even more upsetting since this is a new attraction and these people are already not amused. The employees at any attraction are just as important as the attraction, look at Disney's philosophy, so maybe this company should put more emphasis on how they treat and train their employees.

Yes! Come! We got a groupon for the open bar and loved it. Five o'clock is the perfect time to come, just as the sun is setting. We started with the sun and ended in dark. The drinks were strong and flowing. I would come back.

A fun and breathtaking view, but not so indispensable that it's a must see. 

Try to go right before sunset, so sunset will occur as you hit the top. We time this perfectly, and it was great seeing the transition to dusk. 

While they do offer alcohol included packages, the bar cars are much more crowded, and we seemed to enjoy a much more spacious, relaxing, and romantic trip in a standard car. The narration on the accompanying video is a bit douchey and distracting. 

They are also very good with safety/disability issues.  I had a broken ankle, and was pleased to have the staff pause the ride so I could board safely. They also kept track of my car, so it paused without having me having to ask again when I was disembarking. Overall, a fun experience.
Lots of hype; tickets were free so won't complain.  Beautiful view of strip at night but hard to take pictures of it due to reflection from glass.

Such a fun and different thing to do while in Vegas. High up with amazing views of the strip and you have an open bar. So much fun! We were fortunate enough to have a great group of people who happened to be in our pod with us. When we got to the top, we got to see the Bellagio fountains going off! 
The bartender was great! She got involved in conversations with us and had such a fun and upbeat personality. 
Be sure to go at sunset or at night for the best experience. It seemed a lot longer than 30 minutes. Don't let the price and length of the ride deter you.

Best view of the Las Vegas strip! When we went it was not crowded and we only shared our pod with another couple ! It's about a 30-45 min experience and it is definitely better to go at night so you can see all the lights from the Strip. Again best view of the strip !

overpriced observation deck. workers are not very helpful. entrance had 2 lines. the door on the left was supposed to be for people who already had tickets and the door on the right was supposed to be for people who needed to purchase or upgrade their tickets. because there was no one directing the crowd, a line started going out of the left door to purchase tickets. if you entered the right side, you'd cut in front of all the people waiting in the left line. most people saw that they would be cutting and went into the left line. *some* people decided they didn't care and just cut in front of everyone. would have been nice if workers were there to stop that or at least have people line up out of the correct door. 

there was a sarcastic video playing while you waited in the ticket line. it was entertaining at first, but then it follows you through the whole ride...got tiring.

view was "ok". you can see the top of a few buildings and part of the strip. windows were super dirty too, so pictures didn't come out too nice. not quite worth $40. 

it's one of those things you'd do once and never again.

It's barely worth the $25, and I doubt I'd do it again. Even for $10.
It was OK. They could lose the hoaky video.
 It would be better if it were much taller and located where you could really suck in the sights with the ole's eyeballs.
I like having cocktails at the top of the Stratosphere (twice as tall) much better.

Maybe take in the Quads bars and restaurants and unique shops along the way in to plus the adventure and make the visit a bit more worthwhile.

If it had a pod equipped with a cocktail bar and music it would be a more fun party than bringing your drink along with a gaggle of tourists.

We'll see the day when girls will be handing out free ride coupons in the casinos.

Definitely Worth coming here in Vegas! Purchased our tickets from a 3rd party , so we had to unfortunately wait in the line to check in, but saved $5 per ticket . We did the ride during the day , and it exceeded my expectations! I could only imagine how it looks at during the night !  Once walking up the escalators there is a bar where you can grab drinks and take on the ride! It was just our party and another couple , there was more than enough room for us ! Highly recommended !

I was undecided if I should give 4 or 5 stars, but I decided to give 5 because one annoying employee doesn't make a huge difference in my opinion. It was my boos birthday on June 30th, neither of us had been here so I decided to surprise him. Finding the parking garage was difficult as was finding the actual High Roller through the hotel, but I don't really mind walking around especially if you are with someone you love. When we finally made it to the ticket counter the employee who was helping us was a bit rude. I told her I was a local to get the local price of course, but then she pointed to my boyfriend and asked " is he one too?". Thankfully he is, but you're telling me if I ,a local, wanted to purchase two local tickets I couldn't? Aren't I , the local, the one purchasing them? It shouldn't matter whom the other ticket is for. I am not sure if that is an actual rule or she was just being rude. ANYWAY , on to the actual ride. It was wonderfully amazing. We got there around 1am and had a whole cabin to ourselves, twas quite magical. The view is amazing and the right was not to long not to short. All in all, if you get some kind of discount it is totally worth it!

Great experience with the family! They loved every minute of it! Plus, kids 12 and under were free so as parents we were happy too. Nice views of the strip and the city of  Las Vegas. It would've been nice for them to experience it at night with all the lights but we liked that we avoided the crowds.

Great 30min ride with music and a 360 view of the strip.You are in the ride with other people unless with a group so keep that in mind for pictures as we had to move around to take our own pictures and let others take pictures with the view.No complaints just enjoyed the view,and they have an open bar which we opted to not do.

This would have been a 5-star rating if not for the poor customer service of the person at the ticket window. I purchased a ticket at full price and as I was walking to the entrance I noticed a sign that said if I donated $5 and had a mustache (which I do) then I get to ride for free. So I go back to the window and ask why he did not inform me of this option. He then told me that I could get the deal, but that he was not authorized to issue a refund. Unfortunately, I was with a group of people and did not have the time to address this with a supervisor/manger. The ride and view were spectacular!

I then emailed the main office a day later and explained the situation looking to get some feedback on how management would handle this and how they would prevent something like this in the future. It's been a week and still no response. I've been there and done that so I WILL NOT BE GOING THERE AGAIN.

We bought a groupon for 2 people. Price was about 65.00. We did one circle that took 30 minutes. Im glad we got to experience it but i wouldnt do it more than once. The views were so-so. The stratosphere has better views and more to do so i think thats the way to go.

This was on my bucket list and I didn't even know it!  Definitely spring for the pod with the bar.  $104. for my daughter and I.  We went at sunset and had no line at all.  We were bewildered how 30 minutes went by so fast!  Amazing view of the strip, even saw the fountains at the Bellagio.  Simply a must do!

MUST DO IN VEGAS!!! 

The BF and I took a weekend vacay to Vegas and bought the groupon for the happy half hour at night. If it's still available, you must purchase it. The happy half hour ride is definitely the way to go as opposed to the regular pods. 

Luckily, the BF and I were in a pod with only two other people. So, it was just four of us, plus the OPEN BAR. During the thirty minute ride, we were able to get in about four or five drinks. Our bartender was also awesome! She prepped a round of shots for us without us even asking and made sure to top us off before the ride ended. If you're gonna do the high roller, you must do the open bar option.

In terms of the view, it was beautiful! Vegas was beautifully lit up and it looked incredible. I'm not sure what the view is like during the day but it was beautiful at night. You could even see the Bellagio fountain show. 

Overall, one of the best things I've done in Vegas thus far. I would definitely do it again! Over and over again if I could!

Eh, this could be so much better. They over pack the pods and your drinks are extremely limited. In addition, they make it seem like it's a dressy event and it is so not. We were the only people dressed up.

Move over Singapore Flyer! You are no longer the tallest observation wheel in the world!   The High Roller at The Linq in Las Vegas is!

Nestled behind The Imperial Palace, er I mean, The Linq is a giant wheel of metal and glass bubbles that does one rotation inside of 30 minutes!

My gf and I were lucky that our timing was impeccable because we arrived when one of the pods was almost out of entrance range, that there was only one other couple inside it.  Unlike the other pods where there were more than 6-8 people inside!  It is almost as if we had the pod to ourselves, almost!

While the overall environment controlled cabin was pleasent, the seating could have been improved by using padded seats instead of the hard, sterile plastic that awaited our butts! Not that it mattered too, too much as you would find yourself standing most of the time in this ride marveling at the bright Vegas strip lights below! 

What is definitely sorely needed is a way to disable the annoying infomercial playing on the screen inside the cabin.  The host of the informative show was tolerable the first 5 minutes, but a whole 30 minutes of badly scripted jokes and anecdotes,  one has had enough crass!   Perhaps there should be a way to switch to a radio station, or to satellite radio playing music instead?

The High Roller is best experienced during night time, or at dusk. Although, I wouldn't mind going during the day if the oppportunity came up.  

The selections at the pre-boarding bar could be a little bit better, as it was quite pricy.  Like most tourist attractions, you can't bring your own food or drinks, even if it is Vegas where one could get intoxicated on the strip itself!

Happy high rolling!

We had fun! The ride takes about 30-40 minutes and the night view of Vegas is awesome. 
Upon arriving we saw a huge line but then realized it was to purchase your ticket. We bought our tickets online and printed them at home and we walked right on. There is a bar to buy drinks before you get on. During the ride t.v. screens are telling you how high you are while on the ride. 
It was fun but a little too expensive for my taste.

Had I not gotten a locals discount, this would totally be a 4 star review. If you follow me, you know I am HUGE on local love and appreciation! So thank you, High Roller for jumping along board! Only 40 bucks for myself, my bf, and the daughter since luckily she's still 12! 
I did not expect much. I was raised in this city, what can this wheel show me that I have not yet seen? 
Well, a view I did not know existed for one. A shot of the Bellagio fountain show that puts a whole new aspect on it. And to be able to fully see the entire city from east to west, north to south, was simply breathtaking. 
TIPS:
1. Go with a larger crowd, so you have the chance of getting the pod to yourself, or you and another group ONLY. It fits 30, but I would say only 18-20 comfortably. 
2. When you step into the pod, go for the seats on the right. They have a better view IMO. 
3. Take advantage of the restroom and bar before going up. It is a 30 minute ride. 
4. Be respectful. If you have bratty kids who throw fits, stay at home. If you might be too drunk, don't do it. And BY ALL MEANS, if you are afraid of heights, SHUT UP and deal with it, or stay on the ground. We don't all want to try to convince you to walk to the window and look down, really. 

Other than that, enjoy! There are not many places you can go in this city, and enjoy the scenery. Especially from the strip!

It seems like the views look way better at night. The view was cool at 4:30pm, but nothing super impressive. Also, I wouldn't suggest going on this if you're afraid of heights. 

We got a deal where it was unlimited drinks while the wheel goes around for about half an hour. Luckily, it wasn't too crowded and the bartender makes the drinks pretty quickly. As skeptical as I was, it really was unlimited drinks. My friend definitely took advantage. Let's just say it didn't end up well after we got off.

Overall, it's pretty chill, unlimited drinks, check out the vegas view and just hang out. It was cool for this one time, but I probably wouldn't do this again. Well, maybe a night for a cool view.

My first time on Las Vegas, flight landed in the afternoon and as we came from the sky, you could see this large Ferris Wheel. Asked our Uber driver about it and he started.. 1st, don't call it a Ferris Wheel (but it is) it's The High Roller. It's about a 30 mins, you can choose to bring a drink or opt for the open bar cart and make sure you go to the bathroom before getting on. Best time to get on would be right when the sun is about to set. You able to see the city with and without lights. 

Trying to take the Uber's advice to go at sunset was a fail for us. We weren't able to get on at sunset due to other plans and this was my last night so we just went with it. As you are getting ready to enter, you go through the High Roller lounge where you can seat down, purchase snacks and drinks, use the restroom until you're ready to go. Honestly if you're going to purchase a drink, you might as well do the open bar. I believe 1 drink in the lounge was $12 and it's about an extra $15 for the open bar. I could be wrong on the pricing but it's worth to do the open bar. On our way to the cart, we took there pictures by the employees and was given a ticket to view and/or purchase them after our ride. We purchased 4 pictures for $40. 

The carts seem to move extremely slow when your looking at it but when you're about to get on, you realize it's not moving as slow as you imagined. Of course we opted for the open bar. Why not?!? Our Bartender was awesome! I feel bad for her because we did have some itty-bitty young bopper 21 yr olds being rude to her. But she kept herself together. She made anything you wanted, my drink was rum, pineapple and a splash of cranberry juice. I believe I had about 5 in the 30 mins we were in the cart. 

The view is awesome even during the day. Looking past the building, you can see the beautiful mountains. This is should be a requirement for to ride at least once. The view was just breathtaking! 


At the end of the day... Yes, I would definitely do it again when in Vegas!

Went on a Saturday night, right after sunset, and we were able to get a whole pod to ourselves. Make sure to go at night!! It is such an amazing experience and well worth the money! It's really smooth and won't cause motion sickness since it's slow moving

Relax and enjoy, don't be scared it's very safe. Don't bring any drinks it might spill because the pod sways a bit. It can be quite long. I don't recommend it to very young kids who might panic inside.

Enjoyable half hour-ish trip over the Vegas Strip in a pod on a giant Ferris wheel. You get some great views of the strip and beyond. The pod is totally enclosed and when I went on a weekday afternoon there were only six of us in the pod so it wasn't too crowded either. I don't like heights but had zero problems on this since it felt more like being in a building than an open Ferris wheel car. The host in the automated tour video is annoying (tries to be funny and is an epic fail) and we'd have muted him had we been given the choice. 

Try to get a living social deal to get a lot of money off and a free alcoholic drink up to $10 at the bar before you enter the pod. Be warned there is no bathroom on the pod but there is one before you board. Also, the pod doesn't totally stop when you enter and exit so be careful.

This is a unique view of Vegas and something that I'd recommend whether you're new to Vegas or a regular visitor. Not sure I'd do it again during the day but maybe I'd check it out at night.

Fantastic experience! Used Groupon for discounted Happy Half Hour tickets. Had a wonderful tie! Mark the bartender was a fantastic source of local information, was super friendly and a great bartender! We loved the spectacular views, the interesting conversation, and the top shelf open bar. Was a great value for the money! We recommend this experience and we will be back!
Fun!!!! Worth the ride and certainly the view! 30 minutes round trip with open bar inside - went at midnight, would defin like to go again during the daytime, next time! Highly recommend

A-OK. We got a living social deal for a ride on the High Roller and a drink up to the value of $9 for $18 each, It was a few more dollars for the night time ride, We turned up showed our ticket and went to get a drink from the bar, the whole building was pretty cool! A bit like a theme park queue at Disneyland, then it was time to board our pod, i think we got lucky as there was a huge party before us who all got in one pod together then we were next and we were in a pod with only a few others so i think its all pot luck on what time you go, The whole ride takes around 30 minutes with a pretty annoying video commentary of some annoying guy, The pods are quite large with plastic hard seating in places around the pod, but you do get a 360 degree view of Las Vegas through the big windows around the pod, Unfortunatly though the view isn't all that great, all you get to see is the back of the Hotels,the mountains in the distance  and the Airport,  and we got a better view from our hotel at the Cosmopolitan. Though it was cool to go on the tallest observation wheel in the world at a staggering 550ft!!!

Glad we went at night.  
The trivia was fun.
The comedian video host was.... trying.
The views were AMAZING.
30 minute ride - it moves much slower than you expect it to.

**Talk about uneventful, anti-climactic, overpriced, and overall boring**

PROTIP: Go at night when you can see lights. It's very boring during the day.

Thank god this was free for me; otherwise, I would've given it a lower rating.

Lets begin with a few things wrong with this attraction:
1. The High Roller is so awkwardly placed behind the strip so you don't actually get to see anything on the strip; you see the high buildings and hotels and that's about it.
2. The place to buy tickets is actually not in the lobby with the prices of the ride (where it would logically be); instead you get tickets on the side of the building with NO SIGNS.
3. There are more employees working at the High Roller than there are guests (who thought this would make money?).
4. When you're inside the sphere that goes around, the music is so ridiculously loud that you NEED to be drunk to enjoy it. There are monitors that line the top that tell you how high you've gotten, 100ft... 200ft...300ft... etc; however, if the sphere ever stops for maintenance reasons, the count is totally off. We were at the apex when the monitor told us we were 3/4 of the way through with our ride. FAIL.

Pros: Cool if it's free
Cons: Expensive if it's not:

Now I am NOT a fan of heights or Ferris wheels for the matter. But I must say that I was quit content on this HUGE observation wheel since it moved so slow and I could focus on taking pictures and admiring the view as well. 
I went during the daytime but the view must be more impressive at nighttime.

Give me an open bar, a pod hoisted 500+ feet in the air and a few buddies (and a boo) by my side on Valentine's Day and I.AM.THERE.  Whereas some people are afraid of heights, I'm afraid of the ground. Heights are where my soul soars.  Yep, I said it. 

But seriously - I dig a good ferris wheel and the High Roller did not disappoint.  At $45/per Happy Hour ride, it isn't the cheapest thing off the Strip; and yes, the view could be better given it's a block back from the main action - but it's still fun!  We didn't really take full advantage of the bar so give that a thorough think-through before you buy (why buy when casino drinks are free, eh?).  I'd also recommend a nighttime trip because nighttime in Vegas is cool. Though there's a lot to be said for the stunning desert views during the day. Basically, you can't go wrong.  Other than that, enjoy your 30 minute ride to the "top" of the Strip and use a Groupon if you can!

Tips for Groupon buyers:
If you buy a Groupon remember that the day you redeem it is the day you must use it.
