Groupon reservations also require the Groupon to be presented at the Linq concierge in person to reserve a specific time. 
The "Polaroid" is a useless addition to the Groupon, so don't get too excited.
Highlight of our trip!  Views of Vegas are amazing.  We got on one of the four pods that has a bar on it - there were 25 of us on the pod with a full open bar.  Amazing time!

I enjoyed this ride but did have an issue with the happy hour day charge versus night charge.  We purchased the tickets through a third-party vendor and had to pay $10 to upgrade to the evening.  Gratefully, the staff accommodated our request to change to the evening - I just want everybody to be aware of the small print!  Great views and Reese was a wonderful bartender!

My friend and I purchased the Happy Half Hour Open Bar groupon deal for $79 for two people, $40 bucks each. Totally worth it! The deal comes with open bar while you are in the pod, a 2-for-1 coupon for drinks at the Sky Bar if you want to continue drinking after the ride and 20% food coupon at Brooklyn Bowl. 

We lucked out cause there were only 4 people in our pod, which can fit up to 25 people.  I was able to drink 4 kettle one vodka and cranberry during the 30 min ride, which saved me money! The view is beautiful!

The Groupon is a must! If I had gotten the regular ticket which is about $35 and bought a drink at the Sky Bar to bring in, it would have costed me more than the open bar deal.  Without groupon the happy half hour open bar ride would be over $50.
Lots of fun, beautiful sights from the top. Felt very safe and secure, even with a fear of heights!

For a panoramic view experience, they're better places in Las Vegas. First of all, to get to the high roller entrance, you will have to walk a lot. We took the monorail, seeing that it stops a few yards from the wheel, but in reality, you have to return to the strip to get to the street that leads to the high roller entrance. So I wouldn't recommend the monorail to go there. 
Once you get to the entrance, there's a quick bag security check and off you go in the next line to be selected by groups of 10 to 15. 
Because the experience lasts 30 minutes, I really needed to make sure I could sit. The employee was really nice and accommodating and made sure I was up front to enter and choose my seat. 
The concept is really cool and he view is nice. We were lucky and got to see the Bellagio fountain show while on top of the wheel, which made the experience quite unique and fun. The first and last few minutes are not impressive as you only see the ugly close by building, but once you pass the half way point it makes it nice. 
Make sure you do your research as they're many offers to do this very cheap. Enjoy the view.

Well, I've been on the London Eye, so when in Vegas for a night (work meeting), and faced with the the opportunity to ride on the World's current tallest Ferris Wheel it seemed a great idea.

The view as you are going up is definitely obstructed but once you get about 2/3 of the way to the top the view is amazing. I only had my iPhone to take pictures but got some great shots.

A few critical notes:

1) I wish the'd dim the lights for night trips.  Would allow you to take better photos without the glare of the overhead lights in your pod. 
2) I also think they should have looked into glare-free glass for the pods ... for the same reasons!  (Can you tell I'm a photographer?)

This is a very cool experience to get a view  Las Vegas, you get a half an hour slow ride inside this capsule. There are a few TV monitors inside showing some helpful info about the High Roller. The funniest thing I heard was the highest point of ride is 420 feet, that's pretty "high" as the guy said in the video. Ha haa 

They also have a bar you can get your drink on before you get on the ride. And also a photo opp for you to purchase later on. I can't believe this place opens till 2AM!!! Gotta go back when I m drunk!!! Ha haa

I am rating the high roller one star because I am extremely disappointed with my visit there this passed weekend. This was my second time on the High Roller and though our first time was nice, this second time around was so bad it will for sure be our last. CJ was our bartender. Older lady with reddish hair and a pixie haircut. HER ATTITUDE WAS HORRIBLE! Why would you work at a place on the Las Vegas Strip, in this type of ambience if you have such a nasty attitude and sour personality? It was a group of 8 of us and there was maybe about 8 other people on the ride with us. We paid for the Happy Hour tickets which means you pay more for 30 minutes of open bar. I ONLY HAD ONE DRINK TO AVOID HAVING TO INTERACT WITH HER IN ANY WAY! IT WAS THAT BAD. One of our friends went to go ask for another beer and she said no because she had "just gave him one"...she was confusing him with another of the guys. Even if she had "just gave him one" why would it matter if we paid for open bar. I also heard her scolding someone else on the ride because he threw his cup in the trash can too hard?!!!! She was more a bitter mom than a bartender. Super super super disappointed with having her as our bartender!!!!!!! We already wrote a review at the high roller survey tablets provided but I had to write another one on here. I hope she reads this.

Damn how did I NOT review this from the last time I was here. All I can say is WOW. This place never fails me. I went last year during the day but I was by myself, and it was fun regardless. I took my boyfriend here for his birthday at night for the happy hour, and it was worth every penny and step there. Our bartender Orlando was AMAZING. We decided to fill out a comment card for him, and I hope his great warm customer service and efforts gets recognized. I wish I could go back.
This is honestly a rip off. The price is not worth it. Just head over to the Stratosphere tower for a way better view for half the price. Never again wasting money on the high roller!

Definitely a must visit for Las Vegas.  The high roller was a very fun and cool experience especially since my friends and I got a whole observation pod to ourselves.  
Make sure you and your party is ready to hop on cause the wheel is moving continuously and you don't want to leave someone behind.  The pod is quiet spacious with 2 benches on each side and surrounded by windows for you to see the views.  The upper section of the pod has monitors that tell you how high up you are and when you get to the top.  Plenty of great views no matter where you are on the wheel.  We went during the day and it was still a great experience, but next time, I want to go at night.  
As I mentioned, we did get the whole pod to ourselves but we went around 5PM then walked around the Linq for a bit and saw the line for it did get really long around 7.  Overall, highly recommended.  They even have a happy hour ticket where you can open bar on the pod.

Bad customer service when we purchased our tickets! The girls didn't even acknowledge us! 
The ride was great,definitely worth it

Must-see in Vegas.

I thought I would be disappointed, but they did a great job here. Better than the London Eye, and one of the best observation decks (not just ferris wheels) in the world.

Pros:

1) Vegas has been lacking a great observation area to see the whole city from high up. I suppose you could do this from the top of Paris or the Stratosphere, but neither was appealing to me. Go at 530pm when it is the cheaper day rate but you get the better night view.

2) This one is pleasant the entire 30 minutes (versus a traditional boring line for 25 minutes followed by only 5 minutes with a view). I like how it is constant and very smooth motion (versus stopping for each capsule to load/unload).

3) Better than the ride/view, I like what the High Roller does for the skyline. The LED lighting could have been really annoying but instead it is very smart. There's a wide variety of lighting combos/patterns, and it does not rotate predictably. The lighting transition is smooth and not jerky, and it substantially improves the back side of the Strip.

Cons:

1) If you have a Living Social or Groupon voucher, you must first go to the Concierge desk in the middle of the Linq Promenade (across from the restrooms). We didn't know and waited in line in the freezing wind for 20 minutes at the High Roller guest services window, only to be told to go wait in a different line. 

2) It's hard to take a sharp picture, esp. at night. The glass is curved and you get glare at any angle. Also, the thing moves constantly, and there's a lot of people in the way (and their reflections).

3) The capsules serving alcohol sound like a good idea, but it means you are trapped in a small bubble with 40 drunks.
Had to try it on our first trip to Vegas. Great ride and beautiful view! Got a great deal on Groupon: 2 happy hour tix for $48.50. Definitely worth it-
This is good to try once.  It takes about 30 minutes to go around the whole wheel.  We were lucky we went during the noon hour where it wasn't too busy.  My friend and I had a car all to ourselves.

Went here with a group during a conference in Vegas and loved it!

There seem to be a lot of steps (processes, not stairs) in getting to the actual platform to alight onto the wheel.  And of course, each of them comes with an opportunity to spend money.  However, it's worth it for a delightful 30 minute ride that is over way too quickly.

The pods are roomy and air conditioned with great visibility on all sides.  

The views are spectacular.  When you see yourself looking down at the top of giant hotels such as Venetian, you'll realize how high up you are.  

I also liked looking at the mechanics of the wheel as it went around.  It's a pretty awesome achievement.  I'd definitely go again.

This is nice attraction in the middle of the Strip.  Well, kind of.  You have to walk through the Linq promenade, all the way to the end.  It's kind of crowded on a Saturday night.  There is kind of a "boardwalk" atmosphere to the whole place.  You then buy your tickets and stand in line to get on.

It's very well-coordinated.  Passengers get off, you get on from the other side.  There is a mad dash for the attendants to collect half-empty drink bottles and glasses that people leave behind, but all in all, they are really efficient and get everything going.  Once in a while, they do have to stop the wheel for either handicap access or major cleaning.

So, then they close your pod and up you go.  The whole ride is VERY slow.  You barely feel the movement.  It's nice if you can have a private pod with your own party, so then you don't have to be on the ride with strangers for over 35 mins.  You go up and around.  They have monitors in there to tell you your exact altitude.  The views of Vegas are pretty spectacular.  We could see the Fountains of Bellagio as we came down.

I would say the that High Roller is something to check off your bucket list.  But you probably don't have to do it a second time.

Warning:  Do not waste your money!   This was the most boring ride!  I would not do again even if it was free!   Of course it was expensive.  We went after 6pm when it is $35/adult.  Luckily the night we were it was "ladies night" so my ticket was just $19.  Thankfully, kids under 12 are free so the damage could have been much worse.

There was about a ten minute wait to buy tickets and then a 10-15 minute wait to get into our "pod".  The pod is large and could probably fit 40 people.  Our pod was nice and roomy with only about 20 people inside.  There was plenty of room to move about and take pictures.  But take pictures of what?  Until the pod gets up to the top there is not much of a view.  Even when you do get to the top, you get to see lights and hotels.  I just really did not find those sights to be very interesting or exciting.  This activity was weak for the kids as well. They though it would be like a gigantic ferris wheel but they were greatly disappointed.  

I noticed some other reviewers complained about the "lame video". I actually found the video to be moderately entertaining because there was nothing else to do!  I could not even Yelp as my phone battery was dying!

I know this is Vegas and I don't mind paying the high Vegas prices for an activity that is enjoyable.  This is not one of those activities. The only thing High Roller would be good for is as a substitute for a sleeping pill!

While touted as "The Best View of the City" I preferred the view from the Eiffel Tower at Paris, even when I was in the correct area of the pod.  So I was a little disappointed by that.

That being said, I did enjoy the experience. I  strongly recommend buying the "happy hour" upgrade. All you can drink for $15 plus the assurance there will be no screaming kids in your pod?? Best deal on the strip.

We spent the extra money to book tickets on the happy hour car meaning for the entire 30 minute ride there is an open bar. What is not advertised is that the bar tender will shout at you and otherwise ridicule you loudly if you do not immediately respond with a drink order when asked or will loudly tell you that you should be ashamed of yourself for ordering a drink like the one you just ordered and to choose something else. That literally did happen to me this evening after asking for a mojito. What a colossal waste of money and a thoroughly unenjoyable experience. 

Aside from that, the ride itself was ok but I can't say I'd repeat or recommend it to anyone who is looking for something enjoyable. It definitely was NOT.

Pretty amazing view. Goes slow so if you are nervous it makes it less scary. 

Make sure to find the discounted tickets. We paid nightly price with two kids free but we found out later we still could have paid about half that price!
So much fun! I went during the day which was cool but I imagine it would be even prettier at night. Definitely a cool spot for tourists.

550 ft tall Ferris wheel in a private pod, at night with a view of Las Vegas and beyond along with 30 of my friends/ industry partners and a full bar?!  Yes please!  The experience was so amazing and fun!  

I didn't know what to expect. I came here with a group of about 30 people as a small part of an industry conference opening night party. 

Full disclosure ; my entry was company sponsored as a part of the event. So bang for the buck stuff I don't know. But locals told me they often have coupons, groupons and other deals.  It looks like they have happy hours and other deals too 

A Ferris wheel in my mind  = rocky two seater with your feet hanging out, getting stuck at the top and danger. On top of that someone always screams, cries or pukes.  Not this. For one thing it's way way taller than anything you've ever experienced. But it's not scary.  It's beautiful.  They had a full bar and great bartender. You can fit a large group of people and your shoes and phone won't fall out. No hanging on to your hats and sunglasses on this ride. 
AND the pod is even air conditioned.

The view was absolutely amazing. It was like having a floating balcony that moved for 30 minutes. 

It's a really cool thing to do if you've got time, the means and are in Las Vegas. Daytime or nighttime I'm told are both great, but completely different experiences. We went at night and it was beautiful.

We happened to get some free tickets to ride the High Roller on a recent trip to Vegas. We had a busy day and night with shows, gambling, and sightseeing, so we didn't make it to the High Roller until around 1 am. This was actually a great time to go as there were very few people in line. Our group had six people and a baby, and we wound up getting a pod with us and one other person. This was great because we were able to wander around the pod at our leisure without worrying about getting in someone else's way or photo. 

The ride lasts about 30 minutes. There's some seating on the inside, but not a lot. It was fine for our small group, though we didn't sit too much anyways. It revolves at a slow pace, so you can't really feel the movement. The views are nice, though I think you get a better view from Mix Lounge at Mandalay Bay. It's a cool one-time experience. However, if I got free tickets again, I would probably give it another go.

This was our first time in Vegas and the High Roller was definitely worth the $35 per person. Our group consisted of 3 females between the ages of 24 and 26 and we did a late afternoon happy half hour ride. We lucked out and it ended up only being us 3 and the bartender in the orb (they can fit up to 25 people in each one) so it was basically a private party. The views were great and drinks were flowing, not to mention they were decent liquors that were served (Ketel One, Jack Daniels, etc.) and not well. Our bartender Steve was the best and made our experience that much more!!!!! Kudos to him and his professionalism as well as hospitality and knowledge of the area. He offered to take photos, made multiple drink suggestions, and surprised us with a few delicious shots.

When we first boarded the ride we thought the 1/2 hour was going to go by so fast, which it did but was SO much more than we expected. After drinking countless drinks and shots our ride was over and we exited the orb and thanked Steve for his generous service and tipped him accordingly. Before exiting the gift shop we filled out a honest survey about our incredible experience, specifically highlighting Steve.

2 weeks after our trip I received a hand-written letter from Steve thanking us for our positive comments and for choosing to experience the High Roller on our most recent trip. He followed up with well wishes on a safe travel home and an invite back to Vegas. Lastly, he included a handful of great postcards that had excellent pictures of the High Roller and the Vegas Strip...SPEECHLESS! Talk about incredible customer service!!!

I highly recommend the High Roller to everyone visiting Vegas, especially the Happy Half Hour if you are 21! If you are lucky enough to get Steve as a bartender then I know you will have an un-forgettable time!

Steve - If you see this please know that you provided some of the best customer service the three of us have ever experienced and we appreciated it more than you know! Keep up the great work :)

My husband and I both agree that the High Roller was one of the highlights of our entire trip to Vegas. I started out not knowing what to expect...but I was absolutely thrilled!

We did a daytime ride because it was a bit less expensive - and we chose not to do the Happy Hour experience. Because of this, we had a pod entirely to ourselves!

The views are absolutely unbelievable, and the entire experience takes about a half hour - which means that you get plenty of time to actually take pictures and enjoy the view. You can also send a picture of yourself and get a free copy of it at a store nearby. 

This is worth the money!

Great attraction go at night! Amazing views of city!

The biggest ferris wheel in the world 550 feet up!!

We came with a group of 18 and had the pod to ourselves, was a great experience to take in everything.  Goes pretty slowly, there is a tv in the pod where it will update you on the current height.

Great experience, if you are in vegas check it out...

The price is reasonable for locals, especially the day price before 6 PM ($13/$18, day/night). $25/$35 might be considered petty theft for tourists but there's always a deal going on either the website or on Groupon that might take a little bit of the sting away. Las Vegas' skyline is unique and I appreciate it. So it doesn't get old for me and the locals' pricing is something I can stomach a couple times a year when I go up with visitors. For tourists, this might be a one and done deal just to say you were on the highest observation wheel in the world.

Our last visit was my third time, and the first for many of our party of 10 which included 5 children all under the age of thirteen. The kids under 12 were free. Parking is pretty convenient in the large LINQ lot and if you don't feel like walking, valet is a couple of feet away from the entrance. Pre-purchasing your tickets can save you some time because there is a separate line at the entrance for those that have done so. After you grab a beverage at the bar, boarding is easy and once inside, claim the windows on the west side of the pod to get the best views of the Strip.

There were no chest bumps or screams of excitement in the pod from our group, but everyone enjoyed the experience. My 6 year old niece recognized the Ghirardelli sign and made it a point that it would be our first stop after we disembarked. I'm sure we'll be back on the High Roller again when we have more family visiting from out of town next month.

I was a guest of the Linq and the high roller was calling our name! We we're able snag a a pair of tickets with a little discount by showing our room key or invoice that you are staying there. They have two options a happy hour ride where you have a bartender on there serving you drinks or just a regular ride but you can still bring your drink on with you. We did the regular ride which was perfect and almost have the cost. The ride is about 30 minutes long and it lets you see almost all Vegas has to offer! You can see the strip and beyond to the specs of sand of the Desert. You get the best view of the city at the High roller if you can spend it, it's definitely worth it. It's great for just one or two people to a larger group. It's something everyone can enjoy and appreciate.

I went to this High Roller Ferris Wheel this 4th of July Weekend, I tried to purchase tickets using the machine outside, the machine gave me an error message never received the tickets for the Ferris wheel never showed it was processing gave me error message only, I received an email from my bank regarding this transaction turns out it was showing as processing in my bank account, I went to the box office they claim that it would automatically get reversed, just the inconvenience of waiting three working days I do not recommend using these machines, to my understanding after calling them it happens often, seems nothing is being done to fix the problem. I recommend going into the box office to purchase these tickets.

I rode the High Roller once during the day and was unimpressed.  Yes, the size is there, and the ride is smooth, but there are definite problems.  For instance, you are, during the entire 30 minutes, subjected to loud, trashy music, insipid comments by a video host, and advertisements for Caesar's.  Tasteless and annoying.  There are VERY few seats in the gondola.  The box office adds $2 per ticket service fee without telling you.  There is no senior discount.  MAYBE if you buy from a machine you can avoid the service fee.  There is the usual gift shop.  Although the experience is probably better at night, the high price and the terrible music and the silly $2 service fee gouge will persuade me not to bother with an evening ride.  Overpriced and hohum unless you are drunk.  Typically Vegas?  You decide.  I say don't bother.  (But I love the London Eye.)

Finally got to ride the High Roller last week and I must say it's a little overrated. I wouldn't have paid full price for it. Beautiful night view but after 15 mins I got bored and just sat down the rest of the ride. The tv and the lame music they play got annoying. As everybody else said this would be a one time try.

My husband and I bought tickets off a discount site and went to the High Roller this weekend. The parking was a nightmare. No signs telling you where to go or where to walk to the High roller, that is the LINQS issue though. Once we got into the building for the High Roller. Everyone was extremely friendly. The line went quickly and before we knew it we were in our Happy 1/2 hour drinking pod with about 18 other people. Our bartender Joseph was very entertaining. He not only served us quick drinks that tasted amazing he also was very entertaining. Everyone was smiling and laughing. We had a great time. Since we are locals we can get a deal we will definitely be back when guests visit. It may seem like an expensive trip but it was very worth it and it's a must do at least once. If you're a drinker I would splurge for the bar pod.

If you get in with a good group & a fabulous bartender then its great!!! We went at 430PM and caught the sunset. The bartender had great drink combos and offered up shots. If you only drink beer this might not be as fun for you. I loved how our bartender gave us to go drinks! I only wish we got to go around twice. Bring cash to tip your bartender!

The new High Roller located at The Linq is the world's tallest observation wheel that provides a 360 degree view of Las Vegas and the Strip. Being a local, I decided that I would go ahead and try it out (mostly just to say that I have done it).

Just a little about the attraction... there are a total of 28 cabins that hold about 40 passengers each. It's about a 30 minute ride that takes you 550 feet above the Strip. The cost for adults is $19.95 (open till 6PM) and $34.95 (6PM till close). We decided to go later in the evening when the views would be at their best. Luckily when we arrived (11PM or so), there wasn't a wait and were able to purchase our tickets and board the cabin within 5 minutes. There is a bar that you are able to stop at before boarding if you wish to take a drink with you. If you looking to waste a bunch of money, you can also rent a private cabin for your group (approx. $1300) or even purchase a bottle service (approx. $1800). Keep in mind, this is only good for once around so it's a pretty penny for only a 30 minute ride. 

All in all, it was a fun experience. We got some great pictures and the view is amazing, but I don't know if I would pay $34.95 to do it again. It's one of those, you do it once and then never again. I know since I've gone, they've started to offer packages, local discounts and discounts through Groupon, etc. I would be sure to check those out before heading straight to the box office to get tickets. 

A couple tips...
TIP #1: Go at night... they open at 12PM, but the views are far better if you go during the sunset or later at night.
TIP #2: I mentioned it before, but check various sites for discounts!
TIP #3: If you aren't walking there, there's a valet located off of Koval (of course it's complimentary!).

This coaster is not even a coaster. It was awesome. It's a sight seeing adventure! It's great if you have a bug group. It's lasts 30 minutes long and at night especially it's such an awesome view. When you fly into McCarran Intl Airport you can see it because it lights up all different colors. I would totally recemend this place

Groupon!!  

Be sure to get the pod with the open bar after 10pm - it's the only way to do it!

Extremely LAME. The high roller has no lasting attraction other than tallest in the US for now. Views are see first sentence. If you give me tickets I will not go again. The glass inside the pods are covered in smudges and smears from hundred of nasty human fingers. Hazmat. Poor views. If your standards and expectations are low (especially after a drink) this is for you. Waste of time and money. Ohh the staff & management are obnoxious crass insulting and unprofessional. So yeah there's the undisciplined, treat everyone like a dumb tourist ass for you if you don't like lame & underwhelming views with strangers and oily finger prints all over the glass for which I'm positive would contain fecal matter. Ever notice  when washing your hands not many actually wash their hands after using the bathrooms. Those same hands and fingers all on the glass. Go at nite and you get the build up from all the day time people too.

Save your money, don't do it! Lol

Pros: Nice strip view up top. 21 and up slots that offer drink all you can while on the ride. Tip: buy the groupon.

Cons: Nice strip view up top. (You can just go to any strip hotel, go to the top floor and see the same thing. 

21 and up slots that offer drink all you can while on the ride: go play slots, and order drink all you can. Lol

How much can you really drink in 30 mins to justify your $40 ticket? If it's $5 for the ride, I'd be more all up for it. It really isn't just worth it. t least I can say, I've done it.

the High Roller had it's Grand Opening just days before my friends and I arrived. what luck!

the Linq shopping plaza which houses the ferris wheel, was conveniently connected to the Flamingo hotel where we were staying. We weren't informed until later but if you show your hotel room key at the ticket booth, you can save $5 off the ticket price.

Shortly after we paid, it was time to make our way to the loading bay. I was especially fond of the air-conditionined walk through since it reminded me of Disney attraction walk throughs complete with winding turn styles, TV screens, and futuristic background music.  The escalator took us to the Sky Bar where drinks and light snacks could be purchased and taken on the ride. We chatted with the lovely bartender, Phaedra, who made us some really good margaritas then we made our way to the platform and stepped onto a very slow moving pod to take us on our ride in the sky.  People need not fear stumbling and falling when entering the pod. Although the ferris wheel is constantly moving, it goes slow enough for people to carefully board and enjoy the views for the thirty minute ride.

My friends and I were lucky enough to get our own pod but each can hold up to forty people. The surrounding windows give you a panoramic view of the strip and the TVs always give notification of how many feet you've reached...550 being the highest. Also on the TVs, was a host providing satire and comic relief every few minutes. I especially loved the on-purpose "we're so high right now!" joke he made once we reached 420 feet. Ha. 420. good one, guy. The ride is well worth it. When you look beyond the hotels and casinos, you can appreciate the beautiful mountains and desert best seen from 550 feet.
The view isn't really that good. If you want a good view, go to the Stratosphere. This is way overpriced and disappointing.

Um. I am kinda scared of heights. I think I am not, and I do shit like this, but I am. (Eiffel tower, space needle, this)
So, I dont really "enjoy" it. I dont cry or shit my pants, but I'm not relaxed and in the moment. I'm very anxious and unsettled. So, if you are like me, dont bother with this ride. 

However, if this doesnt phase you, or it's worth the discomfort, check this out. They have a pod with a bar in it. Unfortunately, I did not go in that one. Maybe I should have, ha! Anyway, the pod I was in seated 10 comfortably, but the pod holds more. The views are pretty cool. And, since it takes about a half hour to complete the revolution, you have time to take pictures. I have some of the Bellagio fountains, pretty cool!

It was $30 per person with a coupon, and $25 for under 18. We went on a Saturday night and there was zero line and zero wait. It took longer to park and walk there.

Our group of 7 had a great time on the High Roller. We went at dusk and it was a great time to go. We could see the Las Vegas skyline well, yet the lights were also very visible, so it was the best of both worlds. The open bar option is a must if you like to drink. We each squeezed in 3 drinks and a couple of us 4 drinks as we got one just as we were leaving our "pod" to take with us. Definitely a good time if you're looking for something special that doesn't take too long.

It would be a four for the view but the organization is terrible.  For the price of $35, they should try to ensure that people are not crowded in, so that there isn't a crowd that stands in front of the best view for the entire ride.

By the time we got to the top, we only waited about 7 minutes.  I wouldn't have minded waiting a bit longer if they tried not cramming in a bunch of people.

There's one main reason people ride this thing - the VIEW!  They should work to deliver on this.

It has the makings of a worthwhile ride but it isn't.

So much fun! Went during the day and there as NO wait and our pod wasn't full at all... offered such an awesome view of Vegas! Can hardly wait to go back and check it out at night. Loved that I could purchase and bring a cocktail on with me...helped ease my nerves!

This is something that you have to experience at least once in your life.  

Shout out to the property, as we got to ride for free, due to some work connections of the hubby's.

I would like to return with the kids, but maybe in the day time.  They have some decent local specials, and buy in advance online.

It was husband and my wedding anniversary and we were hitting the strip like we were ballers.  The night was an amazing experience.  I got a drink for the ride, as did the big guy.  

At first, I was having difficulty looking down.  Perhaps, I have a little bit of a fear of heights.  Perhaps, the plastic orb I was riding in attached to a metal circle was freaking me out a bit.  It took me about 5 minutes to really get over my fears and get up to walk around.  

The views of the valley are really breathtaking.  At one point, we had a good view into the Flamingo's property and were able to see the chapel where we got married 13 years before.  

The people in the pod were pretty cool.  We asked a couple to take our pictures and reciprocated.  There was NO WAY we were at capacity, but I don't think that they really forced that many people in there.  We were there on a Saturday night, so I am not even sure what a "busy" night would look like.  We wait about 20 minutes, but I didn't think it was too long.  

Generally, I enjoyed the experience and think that people should add this to their Vegas bucket list!

Yes, it's expensive, but it's totally worth it.  I'd much rather spend a few bucks to get the most amazing views of the city as opposed to gambling.

Tip:  Get your tickets at the automated kiosks!  It's so much faster than the customer service line!

We went in the evening, and it was spectacular.  I have some issues with ferris wheels and hate roller coasters, but the height here was totally ok because of how slowly the pods move.

Yes, it's a tourist trap.  But it's a must-do.

You should definitely plan for this on your trip. We went at around 9pm and we got a whole pod to ourselves. Just 4 of us, with our bartender. It was awesome, the bartender was so efficient, and the drunks were strong and really good. The late night view was just amazing. You won't even feel your pod moving as its really pretty slow, but the 30 minutes will fly by. The views are indescribable. And your friends will get jealous at your pictures. We did get lucky though, because the group before us and after us had at least 10 people. It's Vegas, the odds are never in your favor ;)

I thoroughly enjoyed the high roller!  The pods are really large and can fit about 20 ppl inside! It was a little scary getting on and off since it's always moving!  The views were absolutely breathtaking and it's so slow that even if you're afraid of heights you'll be fine.  There's a video that plays during the ride that provides a few facts and some music. There's a bar before you get on the ride also. I went during the daytime and felt like you get to see so much more than at night but I think either time works.

The high roller was really good drinks were perfect and view amazing was moving really slow but me and my wife still enjoyed ourselves this should be start off point in Vegas before you do anything else

I love you High Roller. Thank you for one of the best pre-game's I've ever done.

My boyfriend kept insisting we go on this. They have a Happy Hour that's pretty much AYCE mixed drinks (Vodka, Jack, Rum, just basic stuff) for the whole duration of the ride, which is about 30 minutes.

We bought our tickets ONLINE (Saves you $5!) and got there a little early. We only had to share our little pod with one other group, who turned out to be really cool and fun too. Our bartender was awesome, she was super fast with the drinks. Apparently, they're not supposed to pour you shots? But she did it anyways. 

I drank about 2 shots, 4 mixed drinks in 30 minutes and by the time we got off, we were alllll schwastedddd. 

-1 Star for safety hazard -- the ferris wheel does NOT stop for you to get on. It literally keeps going and you basically have to walk/jump on super quickly. THIS IS THE SAME FOR WHEN YOU GET OFF. AYCD + moving ferris wheel = DISASTER. Haha.

Pretty freakin awesome! My group went on the happy hour pod for $35 on Saturday night which was all you can drink. Surprisingly enough it wasn't packed at all. We got right to the front and went on immediately. It took about 35 minutes to go around once which is plenty of time to view the strip and catch a buzz. Inside was a small bar with a bartender making drinks quickly. All you can drink means my group was drinking fast! The drinks were kind of weak but we kept sucking them down trying to get our money's worth of drinks. Good music inside, benches to sit, awesome views, what more do you need?!

I have rode my fair share of observation (Ferris) wheels around the world. So by comparison, I can say the High Roller misses the mark for the top of my list.

Take the Singapore Flyer for example. Singapore's observation wheel is situated in a location where a 360° view is visible almost through the entire ride. In addition, the flyer adds a higher element of education to it's attraction. These two ingredients are missing from the High Roller.

The London Eye, which is constantly crowded, doesn't provide many amenities, but it is by far the best way to view London and learn some recent and historical artifacts about the city. The location right on the Thames is also premium. Vegas ain't got the history London does and the location of High Roller does it no justice.

Lastly, the Navy Pier wheel in Chicago. Situated right on Lake Michigan and offset right behind one of the best skylines in America, AND before it closed for renovation, it had a price point of less than $10. That sounds like a win-win-win situation to me.

I see a lot of Yelpers griping about the price. This doesn't make it OK, but the price is commensurate with other high end observation wheels around the world. London Eye is £28, Singapore Flyer is roughly $33SGD. Both of the prices are similar given the economy of each respective city.

In general, I'm not excited about the location and views. The Eiffel Tower at Paris Hotel, the roof top at Palms, and Stratosphere all provide better viewing opportunities. One element Vegas is missing compared to other wheels is a body of water. That seems to be a common theme. The price I don't mind cause I know I only need to do it once. The marketers understand this and charge us appropriately. The all you can drink ride is clutch. For an extra $15 you have 30 minutes to get hammered if you accept the challenge. No other wheel around the world offers that. Others may have champagne and wine tastings, but not unlimited alcohol.

I recommend doing it once. I think the daytime is better if you desire to see a panoramic real time view of the mountains, the Mojave desert and the landscape of the city. Nighttime is only ideal for seeing the Vegas lights. All the lights distort the view of the horizon in each direction such that you are limited to sights around the strip and surrounding Vegas city radius.

Heaven forbid you go there when there's no lines the bored staff will be rude, careless ,not explain where to stand in line or which direction to go ,then throw you in front of a bright light tell you to smile with your thumbs up,but not tell you what that's for. I didn't care for the staff or the treatment. If they are this way when bored , how are they when they are busy. Not impressed in the slightest .

The High Roller was a very fun experience. I went with my family for my mom's birthday. We got our tickets around 12am. Purchasing our tickets went smoothly. They also provided great customer service. 

Once we got to the line, we had to rush a bit for our ride. Luckily, it wasn't busy. We were able to use a whole cabin to ourselves. But if you are unable to move quickly, I would speak to them and ask for information about their procedures before buying a ticket. They don't stop the wheel for you to get on.  

The whole ride was one spin but took 30 minutes long. There was even a small count down till we reached to the highest peak of the ride. Had a fun time.

This observation wheel was high on my list of things to do this trip to Vegas. I romanticized the view of the city in my head but the actual experience fell short. I couldn't find the hours online but we arrived on a Tuesday night about 11:30pm. They informed us that the last riders would have to be on the wheel by 12. After paying nearly $80 for our two tickets, a quick trip to a really dirty bathroom (isn't this place brand new?!?) and getting a free drink (I found a text code in the taxi cab interactive TV on the way over) we walked up to the landing where you get in the pods. There were four in our party and another three people paired with us. I'm not sure why though since there was several open pods that we could have each been in by ourselves (there were about 10 people in the other pod so I guess I shouldn't complain). Entering the pod is interesting as it never stops and once inside, they lock you in adn there are two benches on either side that allow you to sit down. The pod was clean and luckily the windows were too. As other's have mentioned, there is a guide up on the screen and I can't say he added to the experience. As we climbed and reach the top, the view was anticlimactic. Last year we had dinner at the Stratosphere and that view is better! And for another $70, you can have a great dinner! Overall I can't say I regret going but I definitely wouldn't go again.

Absolutely loved it!  Riding the High Roller was the perfect end to an amazing evening - what incredible views of the Strip and the ride is completely seamless and a super smooth ride.  Even during the evening, we were able to board quickly and our group of 10 ended up with our own pod - bonus!  We were fortunate to see the Bellagio fountains go off when we reached the apex of the High Roller...how cool!
The view is absolutely amazing, as is the staff! We went to see the High Roller about a week ago and we were not disappointed! Go at night. It's worth the extra money and the lights are spectacular.

I was extremely hesitant because I hate Ferris wheels and am not too fond of heights, but was convinced to go by my little sis-in-law and ended up having a blast!!  

Definitely go for the open bar option!  (Check for Groupons as well) Our bartender was awesome and they served all u can drink top shelf liquor alongside beer & wine for the full 30 minute trip, you can get one to go too (as long as you finish what you have first).

It's very intimidating to look at, but moves VERY slowly, you can hardly tell your moving, never even got that butterfly feeling in my stomach.

If your in Vegas, I say give it a shot.

Tickets start at 7 dollars (through the internet, partner... Never at the gate).
Happy Half Hour admission includes one 30-minute ride and an open bar inside the cabin! Happy Half Hour cabins roll daily from 4pm to 1am, Monday- Thursday and from NOON-1am Friday-Sunday.

Vegas, the only place where a brainstorming session ends with a concept, so ridiculously insane, that NASA actually needs to update their Zero G astronaut training just to keep their billion dollar government funded vomitorium in the now.

Measuring 520 feet in diameter, the High Roller eclipses both the London Eye and Singapore Flyer. This is the sort of Merry Go round or Tilt a World, that would give Godzilla pause. It is huge, humongous, dazzling and lit up like a Christmas tree on meth when the sun dips below the desert horizon.
WOW! Have to try it at least once!  Yes, a bit scary but absolutely beautiful and kids will love it!  I'm a fan!

I was so scared to do this. Since I am afraid of heights. I felt so safe in the pods. The high roller went slow that I was comfortable. I did sit a lot but was comfortable when I got up at the top. Definitely recommend this. No wait time and it took about 30 minutes to get around.

I went with my family last night at 8:30 PM, and it was a fun experience! Our tickets were only $25 due to the locals discount on Tuesdays (bought online), and they were made better by the multiple free drink tickets we received after my stepfather simply asked! The drinks have basically no alcohol in them, but you can't go wrong with a strawberry margarita on a warm summer night! You can take your drinks on the ride, which is nice as there were some in our group who are afraid of heights, so the alcohol took off the edge! We had about 25 people in our pod, and once we got to the top, the view of the Strip was pretty. I would definitely go on the High Roller at night or at sunset to see all the lights on the Strip and around the Las Vegas Valley. Definitely a fun attraction for families, locals or tourists!

The view is amazing but our visit was tainted by the horrible customer service we received at the beginning of our visit. The "manager" sat by as an employee continually condescended my family and then snapped at me when I let him know that he was rude and patronizing. Mike from the Bay Area, you have abhorrent social skills. Customer service needs to be vastly improved. Just buy your tickets in advance and don't bother with "guest services" so you do not have to deal with the attitude.

We came here on a Tuesday, a bit before 6pm 
- $24.95 before 6pm 
- $4 other fees (I don't know exactly what the other fees are but it seems like $2/person)
$53.90

- We parked in the Flamingo parking structure. 
- We got a tickets real fast. If you use a credit card, you can get it off from the salesman that uses the iPhone. Ticket is printed off the phone too. 
- Max pod can hold up to 40, but when we went there were only about 10 people in it. 
- Constantly moving. You got to hop your way in and out. Good thing they have a net beneath so the slow pokes. haha. The entrance and exit is curved, so no jumping necessary.  
- 30 min ride.
- Tried to do a panoramic pic but is hard bc people get in the way. fail. 
- Highest point is 550 ft. There's an exciting countdown.
- Pods remind me of DBZ capsule corp. haha 
- This is the world's tallest observation wheel. 2nd is the Singapore flyer at 541 ft. 
- Great view of the Vegas sunset.
- Great addition to the Vegas strip! Definite must ride even for locals. Good way to re-appreciate the city again.
The VIP Bar cabin was worth the extra $$, it was a wonderful ride and would do it again and again.

Beautiful 360 degree views of the strip!

Everyone should do the High Roller at least once while visiting Vegas.  I recommend going on the sunset ride.  You will get gorgeous unblocked views of the strip and get to see all the bright lights from the casinos.  The ride is about 45 minutes or so and you can't even tell you are moving.  We were lucky and got put into a pretty empty pod (6 of us total) so there was plenty of room even though they can hold a good amount of people (I think about 20-30 would be the most I would want in order to see everything).

There is a small screen inside the pod that tells you how many feet up you are and when you have reached the top of the ride.  The screen also shows interesting facts about Las Vegas' history.

Our experience at the High Roller was not as advertised. Perhaps going during the day when the view is less spectacular helped contribute to that, but either way we felt we paid a good deal of money for a largely mediocre time. 

We bought our tickets online because it shaves a few bucks off that way. We also decided to go during the day as opposed to a night ride because the difference in price was a steep $20 per person. After doing research, we chose to spend the extra money for a happy hour pod which provides access to an open bar throughout the duration of the 30 minute ride and the ticket price includes your drinks.

There are no set times on the tickets since the ride constantly rotates (even when you board, but don't worry it moves slowly). We didn't realize there is only one happy hour pod on the entire wheel, so we had to wait in line and let the others roll by until it was at ground level for us to get on. 

Being the first HH ride of the day, we also had to wait for them to wheel the bar in. The line kept growing along with my anxiety from seeing the size of the pods. While spacious, we watched general admission ticket buyers (who paid less) going ahead of us (some getting a pod all to themselves) while we got to be packed in like sardines. Have I mentioned I'm both claustrophobic and terrified of heights? Talk about self-inflicted wounds. 

I'm not sure why I assumed there would be a limit of 15 people or so as to not overcrowd the pods, but I was wrong. They put 25 of us in there which doesn't sound bad, until the doors close and you are having to squeeze through people to walk around and see the different views. 

We also didn't realize that "happy hour" actually meant sales pitch hour. We now know how much it costs to rent the pods out for corporate events, holidays, and weddings. Because of an unfortunate incident of a man drinking 25 beers in one ride and then peeing in the bartenders sink, you are also not allowed to hold more than one drink at a time. As in you can't order one for your spouse on the other side of the pod and pass it to them, everyone has to come to the bar themselves and only touch their own drinks.

While I understand the reasoning behind it, it made serving everyone take longer and we were only able to get two small drinks each the entire time. Worth the price? We didn't think so. 

If you still want to go however, then this is what I suggest:

1) Go at night. 
2) Don't pay extra for a HH pod. The ride is short, go to the bar afterwards. 
3) Snag a standing spot on the side you enter from as that's where the best view is. 
4) Buy your tickets online for a better price.

Used a groupon and went over Super Bowl weekend, we literally walked right on at about 8pm on a Friday night. We did the happy hour ride and our bar tender was very funny and made the experience even better. I would give 5 stars but it's too expensive, I would never have paid full price and it goes pretty fast. Good to try once for the experience.

We didn't ride this ride for a couple of reasons.
It was too expensive, just about $20.  If you look for those hotel coupon books, they will give you a discount of $3-$4 per person.  We rode the London Eye in London and this looked just like it so we decided to skip it altho' we did get under it to see what it looked like. 
They have electronic kiosks for you to purchase your tickets.  Not sure if the Las Vegas area is as nice to look at compared to London but $20/per person was too much in my opinion for a short ride.

2 years ago when I was in Vegas, I watched the construction of the high roller.  So when we came to Vegas this time, I had this on my trip bucket list.

I wish they helped with where to park your car when you come ride this, but we managed to find a parking garage in Linq and then just followed the HUGE high roller wheel and found a ticket booth.

We went after 6pm, so the ticket was more expensive. 
I definitely recommend finding some type of Groupon or deal if you can get one. 

The employees were very organized and moved everyone through the line quickly.

When we reached the top of the circle, I did have a panic moment, and was looking for an emergency exit - just to figure out the worst case scenario.
This ride was smooth, and slow, and a great way to see the Vegas strip.

Hopefully the Bellagio has a show while you are up there :)

SCAM ALERT!! People!!! Never buy the VIP groupon for $65 for the high roller at LINQ ever!! It supposed to include free open bar and a free picture for the value of $65! I bought this groupon to use on Valentine's Day! Went there around 9 PM and they say you have to wait until 10:30 to get the VIP free open bar carriage! But when we went in there were so many carriages with the bar included that were available and I realized that is how they save money when you have bought a groupon!! After 30 minutes ride, I waited 20 minutes in line to get my free picture which was also included in the Groupon and they said come back in 30 minutes to get it while others get their pictures right away!! What a scam!! I am a local and I could have taken the same shitty ride for 30$ for two people instead of paying $65!! This is such a BOGUS  deal and never ever fall in to that!!!

I have mixed feelings about The High Roller. Yes it was a cool experience but for me it's definitely a 'One & Done'. Don't get me wrong, there's something exhilarating about being so high up in the sky overlooking the city in the comfort of your own air conditioned pod. It's like zip lining without the whiplash, and much slower. And you're not sitting in restraints. Ok scratch that, it's nothing like zip lining. But the views are gorgeous and there is this tiny adrenaline rush you get once you step in. It's probably because of the feeling you get thinking your pod could plummet to ground at any moment if one of those wires were to snap. Tell me I'm not alone in these twisted thoughts? 

I gave it 4 stars but it's more like 3.5. And even though I would consider this a tourist trap, it's still fun to play tourist once in a while. Biggest gripe is that it's very expensive, even for locals. I think it's geared more towards out-of-towners and the younger crowd who want to snap photos and share the experience via social media. #MyTripIsBetterThanYours. I suggest you get a drink (or I should say drinkS) at the bar before ascending up. The alcohol makes it a far better experience IMO.

This is a pretty good amusement for the money. I would suggest going at night because the views of the city lights are better than the parking structures you see during the day. But even that isn't all that bad because it is interesting and the views of the valley are amazing.

I am a local Las Vegan.  This is the dumbest "ride" on the strip. Not to be totally rude but it was stupid, waste of $26.00. The view to the west is of the roof of all the hotels (ugly) and the view to the east is of a huge parking lot.  I went for a ride on a Thursday at 12noon (it opens at noon FYI). Although there was no waiting in line for me at that time, there are 2 theme park type "zig zag" waiting/staging lines at two locations, one is hidden up the escalator so don't be fooled, there will be hours of waiting, especially at night for the lamest 30 minute ride of your life. Yawn.... Get me off!  Entering and exiting the pod is much like a ski lift, it does not stop so you have to gracefully leap off! Just another FYI. And, the price at night is $36. No locals or military discounts. There are photographers inside (just like at Disney) that take your picture against a green wall to sell you a photo at the end. Photography is allowed, but the glare and reflection is an issue.

If you are on the strip, particularly in the evening, and have some extra time hit up the High Roller at The Linq! The views are AMAZING as you take about a 30 min pod ride 500 ft up ferris wheel style with scenic views of the strip and beyond. The pods you ride in are modern, air conditioned, and cozy. If you dont go during peak hours you will avoid lines and packed pods. Make sure you use the restroom before you get on or you'll be doing the dance for another 30-40 mins as your ride slowly moves along. Some people complain about the pricing but if you do some leg work on the net you can find discounts i'm sure. Great for families also. Memorable Vegas experience!

Cool place to take the kids. We went during the day around 3pm and had the whole pod to ourselves. Very nice views. It's kind of a one and done type of thing. Once you go up and do this you check it off the box and move on. I don't think I'd ever go back up because it's just a standard Ferris wheel. It definitely was a good break for the kids after walking all day. The A/C inside makes it comfortable. Price could be lower to try and attract me again, but I don't see myself purchasing tickets for this again.

Not a wonderful experience, but not a terrible one either. Personally, a bit mediocre, nothing breathtaking or particularly memorable -- we saw a bunch of the hotels and they were all lit up. Yet it was not as bright and flashy as I had envisioned in my head. That could be my fault, hyping it up from what others have said. It was a lot brighter and more energetic on the ground than in the air. 

Overall, it was quiet in our little pod cause it was around Christmas/a weeknight around 11PM. It was only my husband and I, plus a dad and his three daughters. The music playing was lively and energetic, maybe a way to inject more fun in the experience. The young girls were dancing around and it was cute. Actually found that a bit more entertaining than the view. 

I think a lot of the 5 star reviews involve the packages that come with unlimited booze. Because, anything is super fun while drunk. However, my husband and I aren't drinkers so opted for just the regular ticket. 

Pricey for what the experience really is: 30 minutes long, some songs blasting. Regular night time ticket --no booze -- $37. I got discounted vouchers and paid $29 per ticket instead and I still kind of think it was a rip- off. Also the ascent was super slow, and I thought it would be a bit faster. The slow ascent was good though, because it seemed very gradual and any faster might make some people nervous or nauseous. 

The staff is also very friendly from every interaction I had -- before entering the box for the ticket line, the guy manning the entrance was helpful in directing me where to go. I had never been here and had a voucher and was unsure where to go. The girl assisting us with tickets was nice. Bag check girl was sweet, commenting on how she liked my bag, saying you're welcome as we thanked them. 

Once you go upstairs, there's a bar and bathrooms. I'm guessing you could buy some alcoholic beverages and take it with you? Then we pass through another area where they make us take pictures in front of a green screen, no doubt to try to sell us when we leave. It was actually very cute in terms of the background shot, but we didn't like how we looked and opted not to get it. Finally, we get to the last line area, but quickly run into the open pod as it's moving, and then we made our way up! No lines anywhere, but this was obviously not peak season in Las Vegas. At other times of the year, especially Spring/Summer, I can foresee the lines being long. 

I'm not sure how many people they permit inside one pod, but hopefully they do not over pack everyone inside and have a strict limit. It would be hard to get a good view, and it might feel a bit claustrophobic. I also wonder if the pods differ in size. The non-open bar ones are small, and have less people inside. The open bar pods must accommodate a bar/staff, and a lot more people. 

While mostly everyone stands, there are some seats that you can sit down if you need a little rest. 

Also, the gift shop was super cute and fun to look through. I normally never buy stuff in gift shops because the mark-ups are insane, but I saw an adorable "Sad Panda" shirt (panda looking bummed that their mug of (presumably) beer had tipped and spilled on the ground) and could not resist the purchase. Again, those cashiers were friendly and joking around with customers behind me. For working in a quiet store at midnight, that's some good energy and customer service.

Now full disclosure I didn't have to pay for my ride on the high roller so that might change my review for it.

Anyways the high roller in the linq is a perfect place to bring your love one, family, friends, out of town friends to see how beautiful this city can really be. I recommend going during sunset to get the best view at the best time of vegas. It's a full 30 mins around the whole Ferris wheel   which isn't bad if the guy on the monitor wasn't talking the whole time and making lame jokes to everyone. Honestly if I didn't hear that guy on the monitor talk almost the whole time this high roller would have gotten 5 stars, but that guy was ridiculous. The music they played on there like The Temper Traps "Sweet Disposition" was absolutely perfect for the trip going up. 

Also another defining factor was that I work at Caesars and if you have a photo ID of you working on there you get on for FREE. So I didn't spend any money to get on and there was barely any line at all and I got to see vegas from the tallest Ferris Wheel in the world. So it wasn't a bad deal at all.
Must do in Vegas if you're scared of heights I wouldn't do it unless you've had a couple of cocktails ! Views are incredible smooth ride I really enjoyed it

We went here this past Thursday night. We got a sweet deal from Groupon where you get 2 for 1 and an open bar!! We had so much fun! The bartender was great and kept us entertained. We had a good group of people in our.. Ball? Sphere!?! It was so beautiful seeing Vegas lit up from the top of the wheel! What I loved most is that you can barely feel it move! I would love to go again..

It's good to try once in your life, but I can't see myself doing this again. It's a good thing we had a BOGO coupon.

Pods are larger than they appear, so don't worry about overcrowding.

You can easily get these high views by going to the stratosphere or any hotel that is higher than 40 stories high.

Night views are better than day time views.

No lines and no waiting! We went around 5:45 pm-ish on a Sunday. That's something you don't hear very often when talking about Vegas attractions. We rode this in the daytime. It was one of the pods with an open bar. Our bartender was awesome..I didn't catch his name. Boo. But he made sure everyone had plenty to drink! The thing doesn't stop unless it has to so you are getting on while it's still moving...which I thought made things interesting. ha! It creeps along and takes about 30 minutes to do a full spin. You are about 500 feet in the air at the very top so be ready for some awesome views. My friend is TERRIFIED of heights and was pleasantly surprised by the ride. The pods are huge and have seats to make it a relaxing experience for those who are less than impressed by heights. It can be pricey but it's definitely something you should try at least once!

One of the newest attractions in Las Vegas, High Roller was one of the recommended sites to see. We were wandering around The Strip after Midnight and ended up walking to it to see it. We bought tickets at the ticket booth before getting on the ride. It was around 36 dollars to just rider it per person but we opted for the Happy Hour option which includes 30 minutes of open bar. 

There was no line to get on to the ride, but we did have to wait a couple cars to pass by since the Open Bar ones only come every once in while. The Observation Car is fairly roomy with a makeshift bar in the middle. The bar provided for the usual basic cocktails, champagne and beer. 

The ride itself is pretty smooth. It goes slow so it doesn't feel like you are moving too much until you look out side. The view is breathtaking, especially at night see the whole strip. It was a little difficult to get any great pictures because of the glares from the window.

For $35 this was just ok. I tried to find some good deals on Living Social and Groupon  but I couldn't. The ride is only 30 minutes long but anything more than 30 minutes would've been too long. 

I mainly came up here to take pictures. However, that was difficult because the windows are glass with no way to open them and that the glass was dirty. I turned off my camera flash but that only helped a little bit.
Lame. I know the weather isn't their fault but don't act rude and irritated because you had to refund out tickets.

Open bar was amazing. The thirty minute ride felt longer. I was able to finish three drinks but next time I plan to get four to get my money's worth. Look for deAls, go in the evening, check out living social, go during the weekday but at the end it's so worth it. It's one of a kind. The tourist crowd is a lot of fun. It's expensive enough to get a good of crowd of people. I plan to do this again and again and again. Open bar is the only way to go for sure.
We enjoyed this attraction and the beautiful views of Vegas. We were surprised to learn that they can fit up to 25 guests on each gondola and some even have an open bar.

Do whatever you can to get a discount. Military, local, or whatever. Just make sure to ask them about discounts. Now on a serious note. Should or should you not get the open bar car or not. If you want to knock a few back, pre-game, get drunk, etc... Then you need to get the drinking car. The bartenders are really fast and trust me you can do some serious damage during the ride. The cart without the drinks is cool too. Tip... Make sure you have a good place to stand near the strip before you get to the top. Everyone will try to take pics on that side and if you wait too long, you will miss out. The view is only good for 30% of the ride. 

Pros - open bar for a good price, something different, location. Parking

Cons - Price without discount, amount of folks in a car.

Was actually very impressed with my experience on the Linq High Roller! 
Need to cry off that big loss? Take a calming ride around the wheel and plan out how to break the news to your wife.
It's a great post-EDM pool party head rester before heading back out on the town, or a way to let your gourmet buffet settle afterwards. Would definitely recommend at night vs. in the daytime - the lights are amazing from up there. And you're guaranteed to at least to catch a glimpse of (if not the whole) Bellagio fountain show. We timed it just right to have a full view of the fountains in action, and it's a beautiful new perspective of the show. 
DEFINITELY upgrade to the bar car. Worth the money. With the price of drinks anywhere if you're not gambling, you'll easily fit in enough to get your upgrade worth. Our car specifically wasn't too crowded at all to have a good time, and waited just a couple minutes longer than we would have for a normal ride. We went with a group of about 12 and could all find a seat with a great view for pictures and no crowd at the bar.
A few people in our group do have a fear of heights, but the cars themselves are ENORMOUS and stable. Those ladies didn't feel at all fearful of the view. If you're unsure because of height purposes, I would recommend walking all the way up to the base of the wheel where people load into the cars, to guage the true size and strength of the wheel. There is no way of ever being in danger in that thing!
I was skeptical whether the ride would be worth it, but after having seen all the usual Vegas sites, it's a nice add to the strip for something new!
No lines and friendly staff. The view is amazing. Nice and clean. Exactly as advertised.

We went during sunset and thank goodness, no crowd in sight at all.  We had a pod that was shared with just a few individuals, so that allowed us to see a beautiful sunset along with the moon rising.  How awesome is that?

There was a holiday special, around $20 for any time, and locals also have a discount too.  Too bad we didn't check out the prices and ended up overpaying on some website.  Boo!  The kiosk that is inside the building is where we redeemed our vouchers.  I did notice a massive line outside, another way to purchase tickets.  
As you ascend on the escalators, there's a bar on the top floor to purchase drinks before or after the High Roller experience. 

Either way, it's an awesome 30 minute experience.  I didn't expect it, but I did get weak in the knees when I realized how high we were.  You're so engaged with your party, the guy on the TV screen, giving facts about the High Roller is nearly non-existent.  

Yeah, there are the pods that have their own personal bartender.  If you're not a drinker trying to get your money's worth for 30 minutes, I would say, do whatever makes your heart content.  

It's definitely an experience, a bird's eye view of the hotels and realizing how massive they are and the other end of just mountains and of course the awesome view of the sunset and the moon =)

This was such a fun experience. Purchased a groupon for the 2 for $89 night time open bar and it was worth it. We went just after midnight because we wanted to be on it for my friends 30th Birthday. Choosing this time worked out in our favor as there were only 4 other people in the pod with us. (The pods with bars can accommodate up to 26 people according to the bar tender.) they had a decent variety of alcohol- vodkas, gin, whiskey, tequila, beers. Lots to choose from. The ride is 30 minutes long and you can drink as much as you can- you can only have one drink at a time and are allowed to take a drink off with you. The bartender in the Pod, Mark, was very fun and attentive.  The views are nice and it's fun to see how close things are in relation to each other. The groupon also gave us bogo drinks in the bar in the waiting area. We opted for champagne to toast and the bartender Brett was so nice. I definitely recommend doing this at least once, assuming you're not afraid of heights.
Great views and decent drinks! We had a fun time snapping some pictures, viewing Vegas from a different view and sipping on some decent drinks. The value was pretty good for the new experience.

Right off the bat I will definitely do this again the next time I visit Vegas.

 We went in the middle of the afternoon so it was really slow and it was only three other people in the cabin with us and we liked that.

I showed my total rewards card at the front desk in order to get a discount on ticket price then we grabbed a drink at the bar on the second floor and then headed towards the ride.

View is crazy good and just gets completely amazing as you get towards the top, they also have a video showing some Vegas history.

Ride was so smooth i was able to set my beer down on the seat while I took pictures

This was an amazing experience on this wheel for my first time. From the ground it really doesn't look that big but when you are in the air at the top (550 Ft in the air) you feel like you are on top of the strip. The views are amazing and those little pods can hold 45 people...wow. 

The price is a little steep (35 a person) but for the same views you can get in a helicopter, totally worth it.

Great. Worth the $ for the views. During the day or night, we don't think you can go wrong. 
Nice thing about going during off times, is you may have the ride to your self.

On Wednesday, July 8th at 10:50pm, I boarded the High Roller.

Luckily our group found a Groupon for One happy half hour late night package with open bar for two: valid 7pm to 1am ($75). Plus, we had 20% off on top of the Groupon price, so it ended up being $30 per person. Make sure to check in and select a time before you plan on actually going on the High Roller. We dropped by, went and had dinner and then came back.

I heard someone say they offer top shelf liquor for the open bar, but that's not true. It's the standard liquor you would expect with Jack Daniels being the whiskey. I'm a dark drinker, so I stuck to Jack and Coke. I heard someone try to order a red bull vodka, but unfortunately, they don't have any energy drinks.

Since I couldn't drink much during this open bar, I was excited that they offered Fiji water. With the one cocktail I consumed, I'm pretty sure I drank enough Fiji water to make up for the rest of the cocktails I didn't consume.

Now onto the reason for this, the Ferris Wheel! I love ferris wheels since I love views. But I realize I love them when it's quiet and serene. I've been on a number of them, but it's always been with 1-3 other people. Being in a pod with loud drinkers took a little away from that. At night, the lights of Vegas are great, but it didn't feel like we were at the top for very long. And you can't see anything on the desert side since it's just darkness.

I'm glad I finally tried the ferris wheel with friends that wanted to go as this might have been something I'd drag the roommate on. Great to try once, but I wouldn't do it again.

The High Roller was awesome in the day and especially the night time. They even have an open bar with a bartender in select pods that looks fun even though I don't really drink anymore. 
The people stumbling out look to be having a blast. 
$25 in the day, $35 at night. Discounts for locals. 
I would recommend it. !!

This is a must-do if when you're in Las Vegas, so you can tell everyone you've been on the highest observation wheel in the world. The high roller is offering some amazing deals right now on their website, so don't forget to check before booking. The one that suited us best, was the $5 off for locals, and kids ride free with paid ticket. What would typically cost us $140+ for our family of 4, came out to only $60. That made it completely worth it. I printed my tickets at home, but since it was low on toner, some of the barcodes didn't fully make it. No worries, because they were able to find my reservation through my confirmation # anyway. 

We chose the 8PM ride because we were there with another family and our kiddies are not night owls. We walked right through all the lines and immediately were able to get on because there was no one ahead of us. They were generous (smart) enough to give our party of 9 our own pod which was nice because we were able to let the kids run free inside instead of having to worry about them bothering people. The kids LOVED it! You go in and there's a guy who tells you about the high roller and makes "funny" jokes. The kids' favorite part was the screen which told you how high your elevation was and being up in the air in general. The views are spectacular, and 8pm was perfect to see the sun set into night. I feel like we almost got a double ride. On the way down, the music was going and the kids just turned it into their own little dance party. It was definitely the most expensive dance party I've ever been to, but worth every penny.

If you'd like to watch the sun set on the high roller, be sure to check out weather.com or something similar that will tell you the exact time the sun sets, so you can catch day & night like us. It's beautiful.

Date & Time:  Thursday July 19, 2014 @ 5pm
Location:  LINQ
Companions:  Sis-in-law, Bro-in-law, Niece & Nephews + Husband
Scene:  Groups in T-Shirts & Shorts
Music:  Pop
Decor:  White Ferris Wheel Pods
Total:  $210

Amazing experience! I did the happy hour open bar concept and my bartender was Phaedra. She told us about various facts abt Vegas and the drinks were excellent! I would recommend everyone taking this version of the ride.

Went on the high roller on May 3rd, 2015. 
Spent $50 for an all you can drink ride. 

30 Minutes + All you can drink = a drinking game within itself. 

I think I had 4 Bud Lites (Took 2 more with me as we left the pod) then had some shots in there also. 

Needless to say I was sauced upon leaving. A+.

Definitely worth doing!
A little expensive though, so I would suggest doing it at night time to really enjoy the experience and view.

The view is amazing, however taking good photographs can be difficult because of the glass..

Such incredible views, it's hard to give the high roller a bad review! My boyfriend and I went at 3:30 in the afternoon on a Monday, which was great because it wasn't busy, and we opted for the open bar option. If you go before 5 it's $40. We had the bar to ourselves and got to enjoy looooots of drinks and good conversation with our bartender Judith who was amazing! The $40 deal is sooo worth it for all the alcohol, breathtaking views of Vegas, and Judith's company! She even offered to take pictures of the us which turned out great. I can't wait to come back to Vegas and try The High Roller at night time!

Put it on your Bucket List.
Great experience and super at night to see Vegas Strip all lit up. We could see it from our hotel pool spinning during the day and I couldn't wait to get on it at night. It was a lot bigger inside than I would have thought and we were able to move around and walk and see Vegas from every angle. You don't even feel like you're moving. Do it once. You won't need to ever do it again, but it's well worth the memory. At least you'll leave Vegas with that, even if you don't win at the casinos!
I definitely give it a thumbs up it's worth the $25, but they can lower the prices on the pictures

Great view of the strip at night. You could pay extra for an all you can drink bar furbished compartment. It took 30 minutes to complete the ride. You will be placed on the ride with others. The walk leading up to the high roller was a nice break from the strip.

Amazing experience! Went around 1am for the night scenery. It's way less crowded and mostly couples.so I would say if you want to bring your love one, bring them after 1 am. You could ask for a bar too! Otherwise, you have to bring a group for a fun experience! The Price, however, took away one star.

In November, I took a trip around 4pm to take advantage of the sunset and day prices. It was mid-week and pretty empty. We got tickets from my brother as a gift, so we went straight inside. After a quick bag check, we proceeded through the maze to get on. That didn't take much time at all and once outside, we were directed to one of the chained off boarding areas. Since it was so slow, it was just four of us in one pod (hold us to 40 people). That definitely helped the experience. There was so much room that it was mostly private. It also allowed us to venture all areas of the pod easily. The pod is equipped with seating around the edges and encased in floor-to-ceiling windows. It also has air conditioning. There are a few TV screens with a video guiding you through the ride, like reaching the highest point of 550 feet and fun facts about Vegas and specifically the High Roller. 

I went again in December during the evening when my best friend was visiting. A bit more people this time around (it was 7:30pm on a Tuesday, but it was also the day before NYE), but we still managed to beat the crowd! We actually waited longer in line to get our tickets than to get to the High Roller. Everything was pleasant, except there were two young children in our pod and they were unfortunately unruly - they were running around, climbing between the door and its hinges (where it says DO NOT STAND), and CRYINGGG. Oh, the best part? Their parents were more concerned about taking photos of themselves than watching their children. Anyway, one big difference between going during the day and the evening: it's tougher to take photos at night. Trying not to get the reflections of everyone in your photos is difficult, especially if your pod is fuller. 

Tickets
Day Standard: $24.95
Night Standard: $34.95
One Day Flex: $44.95
Three Day Flex: $54.95
Happy Half Hour Day: $29.95 (open bar 12pm-6pm)
Happy Half Hour Night: $44.95 (open bar 6pm-1am)
Family Pack Day: $74.95 (two adults, two youth)
Family Pack Night: $99.95

*Flex: choose the day or day(s), then ride any time.
