Nevada residents: Use promo code "LOCALS" online for $5 off standard tickets and receive a free ticket for your children 12 years or younger. You can also present your Nevada ID at the High Roller Guest Services Desk. For Tuesday Night Bloq Parties, present Nevada ID for 50% off tickets.

Other Facts: Full rotation is 30 minutes. Tickets can be purchased online or in-person at the walk-up window, touchscreen kiosks, or the High Roller Guest Services Desk. Prices change over at 7pm. Children under 3 ride for free.

We came here on a Monday around the time of hotel check out. No line, and we were able to pretty much walk onto a pod.

Make sure you have a Total Rewards card (from gambling at any of the Bally's/Caesar's hotels). You'll get a solid discount by using that here, regardless if you gamble or not.

It's a 30 minute ride. You can pay extra for a "Happy Hour" pod, which includes access to a full bar/bartender for your 30-minute trip. Difference in price for Happy Hour is $10 during the day and $15 at night. Can you drink enough in 30-minutes to make it worth $10? :)

During the ride, they have a recorded actor telling cheesy jokes, and Vegas trivia. 

This is a pretty unique Vegas attraction that gives you a full aerial view of the trip. I'd recommend it!

The High Roller was a great way to see the city at night!  We bought the Groupon, which gave us two tickets to an open bar pod for $80 ($60 if you did a ride before 5:00). I would guess every 5th pod or so is an open bar pod and the rest are just regular pods without the bar option.  

The ride itself:  It was really pretty seeing the city at night while riding the High Roller.  I would defintely suggest anyone in Vegas do it once.  It's not likely something I would do again, but it was a neat view for a one time thing.

The open bar:  I was a bit worried that the pod would have cheap liquor and that there would be too many people to have time to get more than one drink.  Luckily, the liquor was of good quality (skyy vodka, jack daniels, malibu, etc) and had a variety of beer and mixer options.  Our bartender whipped up a few mixed drinks that were really good!  The open bar option was worth the extra bucks!

Fifty bucks for my family of 4 to enjoy a cool ride offering air-conditioning, great views, and a memorable experience.  No locals discount with the family package, but we'd do it again at this price.  Exceeded my expectations.

The view was awesome. The ride is really slow so it does allow you to view the city at different levels. My issue was the drink prices and the way it was explained or attempted to be explained to me. I paid $18 for a frozen daqauri with an extra shot of tequila. I felt nothing. Way too high for a drink. But the ride was pretty nice. You go in a small group so don't expect to go alone unless there is no one else around.
Not as terrifying as I imagined. Provided lovely 360 views of the city. I do recommend a night time ride to take in the lights of the strip

Yes this is quite the experience. One of their über Ferris wheels in the world. At $20 during the day it's quite a fun ride, but the real magic happens when you ride it at night and Vegas shows off her lights. It's about a 20-30 minute loop and pretty family friendly. That being said... This is Vegas, there are bar in the cue lines and most people will have some kind of adult beverage at night.

It's one of those tourist things you have to experience at least once. Plus its the world's biggest ferris wheel. It's a pricey ride at $35. Obviously, go at night to appreciate all the pretty lights of the Strip. It's slow and doesn't feel you are moving. I believe it travels one mile per hour. 30 minutes for one rotation.

We were invited to go on the high roller by our friends that had tickets to go at night for a party pod. We had such a good time! Ther is a bar in a he middle of the pod and our bartender was really nice! The pod goes around very slowly. The whole trip lasts for about 30 minutes. I don't usually like heights but this didn't bother me at all. Beautiful views of lLas Vegas. Being locals, we don't take  in all that Las Vegas has to offer. Tonight was a reminder of how great it is to live in this city. We are very glad we went on the high roller and  will definitely recommend this to visitors as well as other locals.

Being a local I don't usually partake in the tourist traps but I was invited along with my son to give it a try. I'm not the biggest fan of heights but it was a good time! 

Be prepared to spend about 45 minutes on the ride it goes up very slowly which is fine with me like I said I'm not a fan of heights! Haha. The views are pretty amazing and each capsule is huge and climate controlled. 

Would I pay to do it again? Probably not but if you want a great view of Vegas this is it!

I'm afraid of heights, so almost didn't go on this. Thankfully the massive scale of the buildings on the strip made things feel not quite as high as you actually are. The ride was super smooth. There were times when it took me a while to realize we were moving again. 

I went early in the day so there were only 5 of us in our observation pod, giving us plenty of room to move around and clear views. I think it would be cool to go at night to see the lights, but my guess is it would also be more crowded. 

There's a bar and bathrooms before you board. My advice is skip the bar. A bottle of water is $7 there, so prices are steep. The whole ride is only about 30 minutes so no real need for a cocktail, but you can book a ticket for their "happy half hour" with open bar if you feel the need. 

Subtracted a star because the video commentary is super cheesy. Other than that, this was super fun.

As a local, I chose to go here on a weekday, not a holiday so when we went here, it was not crowded. Nice views. I didn't sit down because you don't need to. It's very stable so you don't even feel it moving. Plus you get to see the view more when you're standing up. The staff are nice. The only "sort of" scary part is getting off because it doesn't really stop; but since it's super slow, you can get off easily. Don't worry. If you're drunk and you got off the ledge, there's a net on the bottom to catch you. (This is my sarcastic tone.)

Tip: 
If you have a Nevada ID, show it at the ticket counter so you can get $5 off per ticket. 
If you're not a Nevada resident, get a Total Rewards card because you can get $2 off per ticket when you show it at the ticket counter. (It's free to sign up for Total Rewards in Caesar's Palace website.)
Note: 
There's a $2 service charge per ticket.

My husband and I spent a few days in Las Vegas and enjoyed the overview offered by this  attraction. It was a pleasant slow ride that provided nice views of the hotel district as well as the mountains in the background. It was on the pricey side but that seems to be the norm for Las Vegas.

I didn't care for the video narration.  

We were the only people in our pod/compartment.  There wasn't any line.

The High Roller is the worlds largest FERRIS WHEEL.  At 550 feet it is HUGE - 100 feet taller than the "London Eye."  Each "pod" can hold up to 30 people.  You can find discount COUPONS on-line that will lower your cost.

For a few dollars more, you can ride in an ALL YOU CAN DRINK OPEN BAR pod.  The bartender kept them flowing during our entire 30+ minute ride.  There are only 2 "BAR PODS" so you have to wait a little longer for one to "come around."  Totally worth it.  Most people in our party were able to suck down 3-4 drinks during the ride.  With the cost of drinks in Las Vegas, they definitely each drank their $45 worth!

The views at night are gorgeous - especially if you can time your ride with the Bellagio Fountains Show!

The pods do not stop rotating for you to embark or disembark.  They open the doors and you hop on the slow moving pod.  No bathrooms are on the pods, so GO BEFORE YOU RIDE of bring a fresh set of Depends.

We went late in the evening when the lines were short.  The ropes and ques indicate that they must get insanely huge lines at times.  

Of course the exit routes you through the gift shop - like all amusement park rides on the planet.
We had an amazing time and I say it's because of our bartender Phaedra!!! She is amazing and she made our group feel welcome and great!!!! If you go and get open bar, ask for Phaedra!!!

So much fun! We bought the Living Social deal which was close to $30 for the night time open bar ticket. The ride is about 30 minutes and you get unlimited drinks during this. My entire group was able to get 3 drinks and the bartender poured very generously. You are also able to get a shot or champagne if you prefer. So much fun and such pretty views! It goes slow enough where you can't feel the motion. Would love to try during the sunset next time as we got there a little late and went about an hour after sunset, which was still pretty.

This was so much better than expected. I got a groupon for $75 for 2 between 10pm-1am in the happy hour open bar bubble. The regular price for the happy hour is $52 pp. So I lucked up. The bubbles dont stop moving. You have to hop on quickly. We lucked up and a guy on a scooter was getting on so it had to stop. Our drunk bubble was hype. The bartender was awesome, got everyones 1st drink done in 2 minutes and kept dishing them out quickly along with keeping everyone entertained. And if you have a drink when the 30 minutes is over you can take it with you. You dont even know you are moving unless it stops and the view is awesome. I soooooo want to do it again tonight....but you cant use the groupon the same day you purchase it.

If you gonna travel to Las Vegas you should visit High Roller. I was in Las Vegas 3 times before but never knew about this high roller. But last time my friend said that we must see night Las Vegas from a bird's eyes view. It was amazing and I got unforgettable emotions. Alot of lights, nice buildings and magic of Las Vegas you will see like never before. 
Definitely, 5 stars and my recommendation!

Make sure to follow them on social media! Thanks to a post we saw on Instagram we scored free tickets! I've been on the ride before and it was worth it to go again! Last time I went during the day, the views of the dessert and the strip are just breath taking! It is about a 30min ride and there are fun facts and music playing the whole time. When you get in try to score the seats in the front right for the best views for photos! Every view is great but I think that to be the best of the strip and hotels. If you time it right you can enjoy the Bellggio fountains from the sky! This time we went at night and the glow of the lights is beautiful! Take your flash off your camera to avoid glare in the photos but have a light shine on your face from another phone if possible!

Loved it.  We are locals and this was our first ride.  I would recommend for tourist or locals.  We went of a Thursday afternoon, no lines.  great views.  We had a part of 6 and got a car all to ourselves,   Added bonus was great shops and dining choices at the Linq.

This is one of the best attractions on the Strip! Getting a voucher from a third party is a better deal than getting tickets from their box office. (In my opinion.) I used Rush49.com and got two (2) Happy Half Hour tickets for $54.00. 

We got there right at sunset, and I can honestly say that's the best time to go. The view is amazing and the photo ops will be proof. 

The bartender in our pod was great. He was friendly and very timely when getting people their drinks. I was sad they didn't have the liquor for my favorite drink, but since our bartender was awesome, his recommendations were satisfying. 

Vegas locals and tourist MUST go on the High Roller at least once!

I found a groupon for the happy half hour for me and my hubby. We joined my friend and her hubby and had a really good time. We had plenty of time to get as many drinks as we wanted... In fact my friends each had 4 drinks! The views were great and the other people within the pod happily took pics for us. The atmosphere was fun and we had a mini dance party as well! I would definitely do the High Roller while at night to see the bright lights of Vegas!

Decided to use a groupon and go here on Valentines with my husband. First off the groupone was decent. We were able to do the Happy Half Hour car for the same price as a regular ticket. I'm glad we chose the car with drinks. We would have bought a drink before hand to take with us anyway but this way we had 3 during the ride.

Now Valentines was super busy. We waited until almost 11pm to go so the lines died down. The Concierge is where you go before hand if you have a groupon. They thought our wait was going to be 90 minutes but we decided to go for it anyway. It ended up only being about 15 minutes so we were pleasantly surprised.

The ride itself was really nice. Terrific views the whole way, the bartender was friendly and the car wasn't stuffed with people. Plenty of room to walk around and see views from all sides.

The only reason I don't give this 5 stars is it's a little expensive but still worth checking out at least once. I could see taking friends from out of town on it.

I don't do heights or closed in spaces.  That out of the way, this ride was fantastic. I didn't have any panic at all.  I did stay back of the glass where it radiused out. I went early in the day.  There was no waiting and they were not even packing the cars in.  Got some beautiful pics of the area.
This is such a cool new addition to the strip in Vegas. Party in the sky. 30 min round trip.

Located in The Linq on the Las Vegas Strip. This is the worlds largest observation wheel. It's in Las Vegas so they offer a happy hour as well! The views are spectacular, the whole thing takes about 45 min, it's well worth the price, it's the latest must do in Las Vegas. Live it up you are in Las Vegas for cryin' out loud!

If you are able to ride this during sunset, you're in for a treat! We watched the sun set and was able to still see the lights on the Strip.
It was well worth it. We rode in the happy hour pod and the bartender was able to serve 2-3 drinks per person.
I will ride the High Roller on my next visit to Vegas

I've been on the High Roller twice. The first time, I went with my now ex boyfriend the day before my 20th birthday and the second time, I went with my brother and his family, who were visiting us, two days before Christmas. It was his stepdaughter and stepson's first time in Las Vegas and they were absolutely wowed at the view of the entire Strip. The High Roller was definitely worth a half hour of my time the two times I've been on there. I will be coming back!
Blonde moustaches do not count for "free moustache ride movember".  Sorry my moustache is the wrong color.

We went before midnight on a Saturday night. Line went quickly. We got a groupon deal $79 for half hour happy hour with open bar for 2 people. Normal price is $104 for 2, so we saved $75 for 6 people *sunglasses emoji* Luckily I read Yelp reviews before I went on and ordered shots, the mixed drinks were shady, hardly any alcohol. But the shots were legit and we spent all the time drinking, enjoying the views and taking pics. It felt like 20 mins, but it was worth it. I definitely recommend, it is the highest at 550 feet. The new Linq area is nice (new to me), there were some cool bars with great music.

I felt like it was a nice ride. They have it set up exactly like an amusement park/fair ride, but they have a bar you can get drinks from while you wait to get on or to take with you on the ride. It's just mainly an observation ride,it goes something like 500 feet up to get a good luck at Vegas from up high, really nice view. The ride is about 30 minutes long (slow moving for observing)once you actually board so plan around that if you have something else to do. The ticket prices are $26.95 if you ride during the day, $36.95 at night and there's up to $7.00 off if you buy them online; on Tuesday's there's a 50% discount for locals with Nevada ID.

There are 28 cabins and each one holds up to 40 people. You can also rent a whole cabin out and have your own bartender on board. They will wheel on this mobile bartender cart for your party. Also they have other party packages that you'll just have to call for.

Before you get on they take pictures of you, and you can purchase them in the gift shop when the ride is done. When you're on board you can either stand or sit down (they have 2 half circle benches on each side of the cabin). During the whole ride they have tv's playing; and it plays music(nothing you know or would sing to, something closer to elevator music), shows trivia, facts about the High Roller observation wheel, and let's you know how far up in the air you are as you go up doing a countdown to the highest point.

It was a nice view, something you should at least do once while in Vegas. I would suggest that if you try it, to make it a much better experience you should definitely go with a group of 3 or more people,  and with alcohol of course  :-).

Really nice ! Only downside is if you do the open bar option and they allow 25 people on at a time you probably are only going to get 2 drinks ..... Not sure if that's worth the price but the view is nice take about 30 mins .....

Wow, really great!  Totally worth the money for the fancy ferris wheel. It takes about 30 minutes to go all the way around, and they do NOT stop for you to get on, though it moves very slowly.  Periodically a "tour guide" on the televisions inside the pods tells you a little bit about what you're seeing, how the ferris wheel works, and celebrates with you when you arrive at the pinnacle.

We went during the day, but I would recommend the night ride with alcohol, because... VEGAS!

One of the latest add-ons to Las vegas skyline, a giant ferry wheel right in the middle of the strip.

Its said to be worlds largest, and nobody would probably know or even question it once in it. The 30-minute ride will give you a nice and different 360-experience of vegas and possibility to snap some great pictures from the top.

This is an ongoing attraction with no stops, so you will get in and out while it moves. During day, you will get a nice overview of vegas surroundings as mountains and dessert emerge in front of you. During night you will get the whole vegas neon show right in front of your nose.

They have an open bar option for a couple of bucks more, which is a great way of enjoying some drinks during the ride. This is definitely worth the money, and the bartender will enhance your experience even more. The bartender will take pictures of you, throw some jokes and provide drinks to everyone in an efficient way.

The only bad thing i can come up with is that before you know it, your 30-minutes ride will be over!

I have been on the High Roller twice now and I have to say it is much more enjoyable with drinks ;-) but if you're not a drinker it's worth the views. 

Let me start by saying that this is a VERY SAFE ride and if you're afraid of heights or get vertigo this might actually be a good viewing point where you will not feel overwhelmed. I brought a friend who is afraid of heights and she said she enjoyed it. The ride moves very slow so you don't really feel like you're on a "ride" per se. It's similar to an elevator going up (you can barely feel it).

The views are great and it takes about 30 minutes roundtrip. I recommend going up at night as night views are always nicer (in my opinion). The pods are fairly large and fit quite a few people. I have never been in a pod that was crowded so I found that seating was plenty. 

It's a great ride if you want a unique view of the strip and the entire las vegas valley. I will say it's not the best spot to go if you want to get a great overhead view of the Bellagio fountains (go to the Paris Eiffel Tower Experience for that (see my review)). 

I honestly couldn't say much about pricing because I always get to go up for free (That's right, I'm connected like that ;-) ) but I would say it's consistent with other attractions on the strip offering up similar views. Plus, there's alcohol! 

**As long as it's not heavy rainstorm outside, it's still possible to do this ride, however, the view might not be so great. I live in Las Vegas and I've seen the High Roller operate in the rain.

This is an awesome experience especially with the open bar package. It is a 30 minute ride and all you can drink. We have been on it twice. The first time it was only thee couples on it and was a great experience. The second time, it would have been a small group but the group before us had a girl puking all over so we had to wait for the next one. By that time, the group grew to over 20 people on the ride. It was crowded and you could not see much since all the spaces on the ride was packed. I was real annoyed with that.

Went on the High Roller for the first time in April. I am afraid of heights and thought this was a bad idea. I was way wrong. I got on normal pod with a friend and got to enjoy a beautiful 30 minute view of Vegas. Told myself next time I will do the happy hour ride. I did with my husband in early November. It was great! Wasn't too crowded and the bartender did a great job. I'm not much of a drinker and asker her to make whatever she wanted for me. I loved them and was able to get one for the road. I will be taking my friends to Vegas in April 2017 and we are going to do the happy hour too.

It's alright. Night time is probably better than the day time. But the day time tickets are cheaper and it's significantly uncrowded during the day time.

Process-wise, you purchase your tickets and have until XX time to use it (i.e. 5pm for a day time ticket or whatever time they tell you). You then get in line and follow the signs. When we went, there was no line whatsoever. We were in a pod with 4 other people. They take your picture before you board and provide you prints and digital versions of it afterwards for a high cost. There's a bar just before you board if you want to purchase drinks. Note: You can also bring drinks with you on board from any establishment so long as it's not glass. We opted to bring a large alcoholic slushie from Purple Zebra (also located on The LINQ). The pods don't stop when you board. They don't move quickly, so it's easy to board while they're moving, but it can throw you off balance a bit.

Once in the pods, there are video monitors that display different things, including the height you are at and a welcome message with basic safety instruction and overview info.

The rotation takes about 30 minutes and moves quite slowly. It was nice to do once. And we'll probably do it again when tourists are visiting. But I think the Stratosphere view is better. All in all, it was a bit underwhelming. Neat, but nothing spectacular or particularly cool.

Delivers exactly what is advertised - a gaudy, backlighting-happy and ABSOLUTELY MASSIVE Ferris Wheel that gives you the absolute best view of Las Vegas, where you can also, of course, imbibe fruity alcoholic drinks. Very easy to book and do - the line goes fast even if there's a ton of people on it. They've Disney-fied the wait a bit, so even the line is kind of entertaining, and everyone there is ready to have a good time. Getting drunk partiers or goodball goobers in your "pod" is just part of the experience. Take a selfie with your loved one or bestie and have an avatar you'll keep up for at least a couple weeks.

Also, they're always having some kind of deal or Groupon or whatever - the deals aren't mind-blowing but you can save a couple bucks if you look.

Oh, and obviously, it's highly recommended to go at night. Duh.

the crews act like shit! they forced us to enter the damn cart! One of my friend refused to enter because she didnt want to be together with a bunch of drunk animals while one of the staff told her 'you have to go now' and we were pushed into the damn stupid cart! There is not enough seats inside and it was damn crowded! will never go there again! sucks!

Fun Fun Fun!!! Great view from the World's highest Ferris Wheel. Best view of Las Vegas. 

Make sure you come after 6:00 so you can do the Happy Hour Ride. Full all inclusive bar with all you can drink!  

The ride lasts about 30 minutes. It doesn't even feel like you're moving. 

Wait lines move quickly. Also good rates on Groupon. Highly recommend!!! I regretted not doing it the last time I was her. Like I said...Fun! Fun! Fun!

It's the highest observation tower in the world, I think, so you must indulge!
If you think you've seen the Valley enough times, the High Roller offers panoramic views that may surprise you. Two of us had comp tickets and the third got a $5 off locals discount ($31.95) Not much seating in the pod for anymore than a few people. 
The hype has receded and there were no lines on the Saturday evening we went. Only 2 other people joined our party of 3- woo hoo party in the pod!
We didn't get the bar/happy hour deal.
I loved the evening at sunset ride which afforded daytime and sunset views!
A decent gift shop too with kitcshy goods galore. 
Locals get a discount, which is ever changing, no surprise there.

This is totally worth the price!  The views of the strip are amazing, and the pods are so spacious that you can walk around during the trip and see a true 360 degree view.  There are also sets of TV's in the pods that tell you which point in your journey you have reached.  It's a neat way to see your progress around the wheel and figure out just how far up you are!

Definitely get a cocktail before getting on board, and be sure to hit up the ladies or mens room - the trip lasts anywhere from 30 - 50 minutes based on how many times the wheel has to stop.  Cheers!

Nice view and interesting ride, but not the management. If you purchase happy hour ride, all the people need to buy the same package regardless the person drinks or not, which is $52  for night time and $37 for day time. If you will not drink more than one drink within half hour, it is cheaper to purchase a drink ($9-12) at the bar in the waiting area. 

We had two people in our party and one did not drink, but in order to stay together we purchased the $52 ticket. We were first in line. Then there were 24-people party came up. They asked us if we mind to take next ride, because their policy is to load the bigger party first and a cabin can only take up to 24 people. We were "okay" at first, but after wait for 5 minutes and first happy hour cabin still not show up and wondering how long it would be and asked it will be another 12 minutes. Then I asked the clarification about the logic to load the 24 people before us, since regardless they had to have their own cabin, why we cannot be loaded first?

After we asked for the clarification, the floor workers had  to get the manager's approval what to do. When they decided to load us after 5 minutes, after the manager's approval. We were not in the mood for happy hour. So I asked could we take the regular cabin and got refund the differences. They said okay, as long as we purchased the tickets from them.

So when I finished the ride, they gave me the refund. The did not refund the correct amounts with total-reward discount. I told them that they did wrong. I had to talk to three people before I could talk to the manger, Carolyn Gargiulo. The manger basically said it's my choice to take the none-happy-hour cabin, even though they were the one took long time getting "APPROVAL" to load the smaller party first. It's my fault not showing the reward card, when I asked refund, when I did not have chance and showed my reward card for purchasing the happy-hour ticket. She said "the ticket is not refundable. We already nice enough to refund the $15 dollar." So we became the customer did everything wrong.

Think the ride is good, but not worthy the money with the bad management. Yo can go to Ghost Bar to see the same view. I gave 2 stars for the roller. Otherwise, it's 1.

We were in Vegas for July 4 weekend.

Purchased 2 special tickets for the high roller at a super special price of $100.  We were to board the high roller at 9PM for a 30 min ride to see the fireworks at the strip.

1. They charged our credit card twice and it's been a huge pain trying to reach someone who can help us. We had to go through our AMEX to get one of the charges taken off since no representative at high roller seems to know what to do.

2. Pure chaos when we were trying to board the high roller.  We were in long lines and people kept cutting in and pushing.  We felt like cattle herded into one entrance at one point.  No one knew what was going on and no one was there to regulate the guests.

3. We did not board the high roller until PAST 930PM which means we missed the entire fire work show Caesar's palace had at 9PM.  This was due to lack of organization.  

Thankfully, the High roller had their own fire works show, so we did get to see fireworks for July 4th.  However, we didn't have to purchase super expensive tickets to see that.  We could have bought regular priced tickets (still expensive at $70/2 tickets).

Was not amazed by the high roller.  Sure great views of vegas, but you can get those views free of charge at Stratosphere or a high rise restaurant with a view.

Will not be spending money here again.

Had a customer event on this. Outstanding. We did the drinks and ride for about 30 people. Well worth the money. you get drinks and awesome views. The best part is we had our customers attentions for the whole time. Good stuff.

What a great view! We took a spin on the High Roller during the day, I bet it's even more beautiful at night when the strip is all lit up. I am pretty sensitive to motion, I always get carsick, airsick, seasick etc so I was a little worried the high roller would make me feel queasy but it moves so slowly you barely notice. You go around once and it takes about 30 minutes. We opted to do the bar car, only $5 more so well worth it. The drinks aren't huge but everyone was easily able to do 2-3 drinks on the 30 minute ride. Plus you can get a drink made right as the ride is ending and take it with you!

Awesome views!   We did this late at night around 1am great time only 2 other couples on board with us so plenty of room to walk around and take pictures. You see all the beautiful lights of Las Vegas, the video announcer is kinda cheesy, but not too bad overall. Would absolutely do this again at night. You can take you own drinks on board they also take a your photo right before you get on and you can purchase afterwards. The only annoying thing is that you have to show your ticket multiple times before boarding.

My boyfriend bought a groupon for the bar one with unlimited drinks.  We did this on friday night when we landed. The line went quickly, I am glad we got people that were not too drunk in our roller.  The bar tender was fast and the drinks were not bad.  We saved alot of money doing this.

Half hour ride over Vegas with a presumably improved experience with the happy hour bar special.  Those with a fear of heights won't even notice as the capsule  is pretty spacious (30 people) and even has some seating.  It moves very slowly and the movement felt is minimal overall.  
Getting on and off feels like the haunted mansion ride at Disney as a plus!  It is definitely a little on the pricey end as I believe the London eye is on only a little more than half the price.  Overall, nice experience to try once and indulge, but you can still get killer views in the great hotel rooms.

I had to go on the High Roller for business a few weeks ago. Luckily I live in Las Vegas so it only cost me $20. I think like every other Las Vegas corporate gouging this attraction to is up there. Not sure of the non-resident fee but it ain't cheap.  I understand that they're not doing well, which comes as no great surprise.. People just can't afford to shell out that kind of money to see basically the same view they could see from the top of their hotel.

What a wonderful experience! We got the open bar mon to thurs special from living social for 25 bucks. What a steal! 30 min open bar yes please! It took a while to redeem. Thought we could redeem at high roller linq, but had to the go to the concierge first. The open selection was moderate but who cares it's open bar don't except expensive exquisite alcohol. It's a 30 mins ride so please don't come on the ride with with a heavy bladder. Overall the view was amazing and the fact the don't overcrowd you in one ride was good. We went on a weekday so there was no line, but if you went on a weekend not sure how it be. It probably be super long! The reason why I'm giving it a 4 star was at the end of the ride you can view your picture for the ride, well there was a girl who worked at the counter that was a total bitch. We saw our picture didn't like it so we decline not to get it and she gave the biggest attitude. Rolled her eyes at us and then took the picture and ripped it right in front of us. It's like ok bitch you could of at least waited for us to walk away. Hopefully all of them are not like that, but seriously I'm sorry you hate your job but don't take it out on us.

GO TO HAPPY HALF HOUR!!!! YOU WILL NOT REGRET IT!   I wanted to try this when I was here in the summer,but always found it a little pricey for the night time ride .. searched on groupon ,which then turn out to be more expensive! Looked around an if you book it online from ceasar it's 42$ per person instead of 52$...when we got there i kept trying to ask what was in the bar,was it beer..wine..well drinks only! ?? Wtf only thing the employees would say was it a full bar ( so I'm instantly thinking  a scam) THANK GOD I WAS WRONG! ..Not only did we get the cabin to ourselves for a 9pm ride but the bar is fully stocked with all liquor! .didn't even ask if they had beer cause at this point it was irrelevant.  The bar as 3 types of absolute ,sky vodak, caption morgan,Jack daniels, beefeater, an a few other bottle an they can pretty much make ALL SPECIALTY COCKTAILS & since there was only 2 of us we got to drink the whole 28 min ride.. I had  vodka pineapple, cosmo,a drink the bartender called white gummy bear, vodak cranberry,an a cosmo to go. .my husband had long Islands and mia tias ..so we'll worth the alcohol  and ride. .. DON'T FOR TO TIP YOUR BARTENDER!!!!!!!!! :)  such a great time can't remember ours name ,but I'm from vallejo ca so him being from fairfield, ca made it feel like I was parting with nothing but good fam!

I went here on the 16th and it was pretty cool. You go inside this giant ball and it has a couple benches. It fits quite a few people. The tickets we got were "all you can drink" and there's a bartender and he makes you what you want...it's not a full bar so don't expect too much. I suggest asking him if he has any special drinks he makes. The bartender that we had made us some "bartender special" drinks and they were really good. Bring cash to tip. The ride lasts about a half hour and when you enter the ride, try to stay by the side that you entered...then you can see the strip! The other side doesn't have too much on it. It's cool to do once but I probably wouldn't do it again. Personally, I think it needed to be in a better location. Also, the bartender cut my husband off and he wasn't even drunk lol. They're small cups and a lot of ice. "All-you-can-drink" my ass. And no, he wasn't drunk at any point when we got off the ride either so I don't know why he was cut off. My uncle had more drinks than my husband and didn't get cut off.

This was a great way to see the mountains and enjoy some down-time outside the casinos. We totally opted for the happy hour/open bar ticket and it was awesome. The bartender was pouring loose and fast for everyone. It takes about a half hour to go around, but if you show up with an agenda, you can easily pack in 4-5 rounds before you have to depart. Just be ready to stumble somewhere to get food to soak up the alcohol so you can continue the party!
Awesome!  You have to do this at night. The lights are spectacular and the view is amazing.  We were at the very top when the Bellagio water show started -amazing!

Very poor customer service right from the beginning. First off we called and bought 4 tickets from the box office, 2 open bar and 2 non open bar as gifts for my parents that are elderly and do not drink. When we arrived at the High roller with our printed out tickets the girl working the front desk didn't greet us and was very rude saying that we couldn't ride together unless we purchased the open bar tickets for everyone in our party at a price of $47 dollars each and asked us " Why would you think people not drinking would be allowed on the drinking car?" Well because at no time during the whole buying process was this explained to us and why should non drinking patrons be forced to pay the open bar price just to be able to ride with there Family!
To make a long story short everyone that was working there was either Rude or just ignores you while playing on there cell phone. So don't waste your money, you are better off going up to the top of the Stratosphere, it has a better view and lasts as long as you want.

This was a lot of fun! We found a groupon for their "happy half hour" open bar and went with some friends. The cabin had a mini bar with a pretty good selection and one bartender. We were worried that the bartender wouldn't be able to keep up with all the people but it really wasn't a problem. We all had at least 4 drinks each and that's pretty good for a 30 minute ride. Really great way to get the evening started!

Always take guests here when they are in town. its a good way for them to get an overview of the strip which enjoying the nice 30 minute ride. Plus we love walking down the linq to get to it. Just make sure you dont go during a busy period as the lines can get rather long.

Fun thing to do.

In Veags, there is a lot to do / nothing to do. This was a fun easy and 'clean' way to kill some time with my colleagues. You got to see all the lights and all the sights and get a good sense of the size / layout of vegas. Also, very reasonably priced!

Something I'd check out for a Vegas first timer. One of the best views of Vegas!

Was fortunate to have my reward still applicable a year after I got it. $10 upgrade got me to the open bar ride! 2 drinks in 30 mins, while drinking fairly slow as I was already feeling the alcohol.

Great view of Vegas but definitely not a MUST GO TO type of option. I think there are plenty of better things to do with your $30+ per head ride rather than this, however if you're curious to ride the biggest wheel in the world, then go for it! Night time it gets more expensive. 

30 minutes and you're out. Just stand and enjoy the view.

Tuesday is Block Party night at the LINQ which showcases Las Vegas local artists crafty types and musicians in a somewhat corporately manipulated "First Friday" type event.  Many of the Bars, Restaurants, and other businesses also have specials they offer on this day.  

It was my BIRTHDAY and I wanted to do something fun and touristy on the "Las Vgas Strip".  The "High Roller" had a family group special which gave us passes for 4 adults and two young children and four beverages of our choice for only $64.  I thought this was a great deal so we gave the "High Roller" a whirl.  Everyone had a blast.  The view starts out a little slow with a birds eye view of parking lots and crappy rooftops.  there is a screen that tells you what elevation you are at which increases your anxiousness to reach the pinnacle of the experience.  Once you get to the top the views become amazing and the ride gets better from there as you start to tumble over the edge of the wheel.  

We had so much fun as a family on the "High Roller" we all wanted to go again when we went down to the bottom.  Unfortunately they do not have and wrist band to ride all day on this Ferris Wheel,  However we will be back very soon to ride at night where I am sure the glow of the Las Vegas Skyline will be truly a breathe taking experience.

650th REVIEW!!!!

Was in Vegas celebrating a friends Whorey 40 Bday Bash, and since there was a group of us we wanted to do something fun together, and most of us were from Arizona and California, so we said let's do the High Roller.

Let's get some facts out of the way, The High Roller is within the LINQ quarter (which by the way is pretty cool) best way to save time on parking is use the valet, its adjacent to the High Roller Ticket area. Speaking of tickets, its 24.95 during the day, and 34.95 during the night, same ride just different perspective. Also for a few more bucks you can get a rolling Open Bar in with you and your group for the length of the ride. 

If you not into having a rolling bar, as you work your way up to the High Roller, you will run into a bar waiting for you. Here you can partake in ordering some booze or liquid courage for your ride. I went with Sparkling Raspberry, it was Skyy Raspberry Vodka, lemon juice, simple syrup, raspberries and Champagne, this lovely drink was 11 bucks! It was the perfect drink.

So this is when it starts to look a bit like Disneyland, you and your group get corralled in area, you wait for someone to open the gate, you move along fast and hop into your pod, keep it moving, don't slow down, reminded me of boarding the ride at the Haunted Mansion, just keep it moving hop on and enjoy your ride.  But just to be clear, if you are in wheelchair, or have special needs and are unable to hop in, they do stop the ride so you can safely enter and exit the pod.  This group did the hopping.

Ok I thought I would freak out, I am scared of heights, but this was easy, and when we reached the top, which is 550ft above the ground it was amazing! You can see for miles!  It takes 30 minutes to go up and around, the pod could fit 40 people, we were just a party of 10, there are places to sit too, or you can stand, which I did and just watch the view rise and fall. I would do it again in a heartbeat! 

Give The High Roller a try!

Go for the Happy Half Hour on the High Roller! the price of a ticket is already $24.95 (during the daytime) so why not add another $5 for unlimited drinks - its a no brainer haha. our cabin was pretty much at full capacity for our ride in the afternoon with about 25 people there for happy hour. i was worried at first that i wouldnt get my money's worth with only 1 bartender, 30 minutes and all these people...but our bartender, Phaedra was a pro! she handled our group with such ease and quickness. since she's a vegas local too she was part tour guide during our 30-minute ride and i learned some fun facts about the city. the high roller ride itself is so smooth and the cabins move slowly where you can barely even feel it moving. so 1 shot, 5 drinks and 1 drink to-go later haha...this is a really fun way to spend some time while you're in vegas!
This is a must!!! The view is amazing! You seriously can't tell it's moving, until you look down. Lol! Definitely will do this again!!!

My husband and I paid for the open bar pod and went on about 4 pm on a Saturday. It was pretty empty at that time, but this was such a cool experience that would be very fun with a larger group!! The bartender was awesome, she made very strong drinks, and offered us more drinks before we got off. The views overlooking the strip and beyond were incredible. Highly recommend!

We bought tickets for that - even though I DO NOT like Ferris wheels, enclosed or not. I'm not afraid of heights or experience vertigo, but it's something about falling or the machine breaking. 

You can buy all you can drink bar tickets for a 30 minute ride - which seems like a good deal until you realize that you spend most of your time taking pictures and me keeping away from the edges. We got a local discount because of Mr. Harris' ID, and bought more beers from the bar inside for the ride. 

Very cool experience at night. I recommend it.

Okay, I loved riding this. Especially since we got the open bar plus admission. It was really cool catching the Bellagio Fountain show while being up so high. The view at night is really nice. We totally got lucky because only a few people got on with us. I recommend anyone who has not ridden this to get the open bar option trust me you will love it.

went last saturday afternoon, wasn't too busy at 2pm.  the Linq was busy though!  lot of people walking around.  anyway, tickets are easy to purchase...and total time up to platform for entry is only about 5 minutes.  the pods are in constant motion, so you board while it's still moving.  but don't worry, there is a net if you fall!  ride is a total of 30 minutes, with only a few times it did stop completely during the total rotation.  ride is very smooth and effortless.  worth the $25 per person admission.  view is amazing.  our pod only had about 10 people in it, and it didn't seem crowded at all.  they are very large.  we'd be back, but at night!  everything is new and clean around the Linq.  worth a visit.

Awesome!

To be 550 ft over Las Vegas was great. They play some fun music and everyone was really social inside the orb. IA

It was worth the $25. Its a 30 minute ride so go to the bathroom before you get in.

I purchased a Groupon for this before I went to Vegas, and decided to do the Happy Half Hour - unlimited drinks while you are riding the wheel. The entire trip takes about 40 minutes. What does this mean? Chug those drinks! When the pod arrived - we got on, along with about 30 other people. Inside there was a bar set up and a bartender that was ready for the onslaught. The rules are simple - one drink at a time and no "double fisting" That said, there were some people who didn't - whatever... it was fine. 
The drinks that were poured were STRONG...some of the strongest I have ever had, so you may want to ask them to pour them smaller if you need to. People were drinking them fast - myself included, and within about 15 minutes the energy in the Pod was great... Strangers all laughing sharing stories, and enjoying the great views of Vegas. At the top of the wheel, the bartender encouraged everyone to have a shot - which we all did. By the time we made our way to the bottom of he revolution, everyone had had many drinks - and walked out into the night feeling amazing. My advice - get a Groupon, ( I even got a further discount with a Groupon promotion) and drink to get your money's worth. It is a great experience - the views, the slickness of the capsule revolving ( you don't even notice it) and the fun bar. A must see and something we will do again when we return.

Visited January 2017
Wow what a great experience! The best deal is through groupon! Open bar for the half hour ride! Great view at night! It is a must do on your list in Las Vegas!

The high roller is so fun! 

I bought a deal for 2 including the bar pod on travelzoo, and it was well worth it! 

We went mid day on a Friday in July and ended up getting our own pod! Our bartender was so friendly, and made great drinks! She kept them coming even faster than we were ready to drink them, and gave me plenty of water as well (I was drained after walking miles down the strip in 112 degree weather). I enjoyed patron tequila drinks, and the dude was happy with Jack and cokes. 

Great views of the whole strip! 30 min of fun, and the AC was amazing on such a hot day.

Overall a really great experience. We went during the day at around 3pm (not good for pictures) and at night at 6-7pm. If you want go and take pictures during the day for the lower prices, go as close to 5pm as possible so that the sun is close to setting and you'll get really warm pictures: At night, try to go as early as possible because it's the busiest at around 9-10pm and since 7pm and 9pm city landscapes are the same. Since the prices are a big high, play the TR game online where you can spin a wheel to get anything from $8 off to 50% off to 2 free tickets-- to save some money! The best spot to view the strip is the immediate right when you enter the pod which is right side that is nearest the door when you enter.

A couple weeks before our trip to Vegas, out of the blue we were wondering where the highest Ferris wheel in the world is (I am a huge Ferris wheel fan). Imagine my delight when I found out it had newly opened on the Strip! I had to do a little convincing because my partner doesn't love heights, but the fact that the viewing capsule is all enclosed made a big difference. We got tickets for nighttime because we wanted to see the lights, and it was awesome. We even saw the Bellagio fountain from the top of the wheel! Unfortunately, we had to share our capsule with some really drunk obnoxious dudes. That's really the only drawback. Overall a beautiful experience and a great way to see the lights of Vegas. It's definitely a little pricey, but the experience is worth it.

If you go to Las Vegas this is a must do attraction. I recommend doing this at night. Look on Groupon or search other discount sites for discounted tickets. The groupon I got was for two people at a rate less than two tickets separately. The Groupon included a buu one get one half off on beverages as well as 15% off of the souvenir shop purchase. You can take as many pictures as you want with your own camera, so I dont think it is worth buying their computer generated picture. Buy your ticket early and see the attraction right when it starts getting dark, the lines can tend to get long. Weekdays are better than weekends.
Not the hype that was advertised, the view was okay but just another Vegas attraction to suck money. would be cool for a romantic setting if offered a dining experience or something similar.

My boyfriend and I went on the High Roller this past Thursday evening around 10pm. We used a groupon and were able to redeem it easily at guest services. There wasn't a wait at all when we went and we actually had an observation pod to ourselves. The pod next to us was the happy hour pod and it was PACKED with people - they looked like they could barely move. The groupon price is $69 which is basically the price of two night tickets - it's only a deal if you get the happy hour all-you-can-drink option ($109 for two), but beware that you might be packed in like sardines. 

There are two benches inside to sit down and you get a 360 degree view through the observation pod windows. It was pretty cool to see the strip all lit up from 550 feet up (if you get lucky you can see the bellagio water fountain show) and there's music playing but the ride is incredibly slow. The entire experience is 30-45 minutes and once you get to the top, coming down is pretty uneventful. There are some screens with a really corny narrator who gives you information about the ride - I wish there was an option to turn him off. We ended up going again on Saturday with my cousins who had free passes. I honestly wouldn't go again unless I was going for free but it's definitely something to experience.

So finally did it, been in Vegas for 2 yrs.  you have to get the open bar it's great.  Our bartender Brett was awesome.  He interacted with us and recommended drinks.  Shots! Shots! Shots!  It's a great view of the strip.  

Our pod didn't have a lot of ppl which was great!  Wasn't overcrowded.  The longest wait we had was waiting for a pod with a bartender.  The line to pay was super fast and no wait to get In.  Wednesday night I guests slow everywhere.  Patron shots woohoo!! He made some gummy bear something shouts which everyone was happy with.  I'd definitely recommend the high roller next time in Vegas.  The ride seemed to go pretty fast but if drinking and talking or taking selfies I guess 30mins is nothing.

Great place to hang out with friends and family. It has a spectacular view over looking the strip. It's a little pricey.... BUT if u have access to Neil's Air Force base go to the it ticket office and purchase it there because it's only 17$ before 6pm and I think it's just a little more for a night time show.

I love ferris wheels.

Initially, I was skeptical about High Roller despite my undying affection for these marvels of engineering.

Firstly, I didn't think the enclosed nature would be that cool, and I felt like the price would be exorbitant for what you get.

Don't get me wrong--High Roller isn't cheap. It's $20-$23 for adults ($15-$17 for kids) during the day and $32-$27 for adults ($25-$27 for kids) during the night. The price differences are the online pricing and the in-person pricing, so for this reason, I recommend buying online.

That said, you are paying for a really cool experience. I was amazed by the views when I first went up in the night: you get to see the famous Vegas lights illuminating the casinos all around you. It's really something, and the ride takes 20+ minutes so you get to have plenty of time to take pictures and soak it in.

I also went during the daytime, and I have to say it is an entirely different experience. It felt less epic--maybe moreso because it was my second time, though--but it was still really cool to see all the details I missed during the nighttime. Seeing the multitude of pool parties, walking people, and crazy car skid marks on the roof parking lots across casinos--awesome!!

Usually, it seems like they put you and your group (if you have one) in separate pods so that you don't have to be bothered by other people. This is really great.

Also, the in-bubble video experience tries really hard to be funny, and to be fair, sometimes it is. Definitely recommend listening in, since you're basically forced to.

BTW, check out the High Roller when there's an open bar! Looks fun for the passengers, but I've never tried it!

Overall, it's great to try once. Once! That's all I ask. You won't regret it, even if you have a fear of heights (you're safe!). 

Love for ferris wheels: further validated.

I had a great time on this. I would love to have done it at sunset, but I was equally awesome at night. It's not necessarily something that I'd have to do again, but definitely worth the experience. The staff there were very nice and had a good time joking with all of us. Just beware, they can see everything that goes on in the pods! ;)

I like this place there is not much wait time since each room can have up to 40 people. Great view, very romantic.

If you are in Las Vegas you should try this at least one time.

I recommend this place to all friends and family.

I am a local and have been here many times but the most recent was the first time I rode in the open bar cart.  All staff from the beginning of my experience to the end were incredibly nice.  I did however encounter one cashier whom I was not dealing with as the person I was with was paying that rubbed me the wrong way.  I would have expected him to address me when a asking if I was a local opposed asking the person I was with "is she local?"  I was looking at my phone but directly in front of him and he could have asked me himself.  I may be over sensitive to these type of occurances from working in the hospitality industry but this is the only reason I did not give 5 stars.  Our bartender was a very sweet and personable young woman who made the experience very enjoyable!  I would definitely recommend this for its value.

We went to ride the High Roller on Tuesday, June 17th at around 11 pm. We were stuck in the pod for about 20 minutes because the entire attraction stopped working. We were 2 pods away from the very top. Instead of doing a full rotation we had to go down the same way we went up. Apparently this was the first time the high roller had stopped working. The views were amazing, but the experience was not the best. When we went to the customer service desk they asked if we wanted a ticket for another day or a refund. Of course we chose the refund of $72+ for two people.

We went during the day. This was a decent experience and I'm glad to have done it at vegas.  You get a really good view of the strip and you'll get some good pictures out of it. The ride is about 30 min.

The High Roller. A person you'd like to know or a cool ride. Ours started out a little bumpy with some false advertising... but Mariah was kind enough to fix us up after I protested the bad wording on their advertising. Seriously, hire some new people to write those things because that was bullshittery at its finest. 

Anyhoodle, after she was kind enough to fix our problem, we grabbed drinks in the skylounge and went up in the giant ferris wheel type thingie. You step into a little air conditioned pod. Actually, not that little. You could get a good sized group in there. I'd check for a groupon though or similar because the ride itself is kind of boring. They put some weird serial killer looking guy on the screen and he tries to be funny but it falls weirdly short. Also, it's hard to hear. 

I'd do this again for $20 if it included a drink. I would not do this for their asking price. Make sure you get the senior or the military discount as well. The folks at the re-seller stands won't offer that.

So fun. First of all go at night. Second of all buy discount tickets on Groupon or LivingSocial. Third it's air-conditioned which is an incredible bonus fourth it's not scary at all except for stepping on and stepping off which gets a little dicey the rest of it though phenomenal view of the city

$34.95 a person (night price) for a 30 minute tour above the Vegas Strip (or the back of the strip).  Great views at night.

We went on 12/27/2014 around 9pm and there wasn't much of a wait.  There are a lot of switchbacks when it is crowded, so the company prepared well.  After you buy your ticket, you go up an escalator, then through a hallway where you can have your picture taken (on a green screen), so the company can place the ferris wheel behind you, then you have a chance to buy a drink and use the restrooms (and I suggest you do one or both), then through switchbacks, then outside and you can see the giant pods.  You wait to be corralled into another waiting area, then you wait for your turn to go inside.

Since there weren't too many people when we went, they filled the cabin with about 12 people.  It was comfortable to move around in the pod and the tinted windows allowed you to take pictures without too much color variation.

The ferris wheel moves slowly, so you can take in the views.  There is a virtual host who tells you facts about the ride, some about the city, and towards the end shows you a time-lapse video of the making of the High Roller.  

Once you make a 360 in the pod, you exit the other side and walk down the path to the gift shop (of course).  The first part of the gift shop is where you can see the picture that you took right after going up the escalator.  They give you a number to easily retrieve your photo.  We didn't buy one.

That's it.  You exit to the alley with shops and restaurants.

Please see my pictures.

Xie Xie!!

Anxious to see Vegas from many views and perspectives, our party of four jumped at the libation included 550' observation ferris wheel at a price of $60 person -with unlimited opportunities. The ride is 30 minutes in duration and the quantity of guests per cab can go anywhere between; half empty, full and a bit of a challenge to move around. A mood was set when the doors closed and the tender stated; "the way this works is you help me and I help you". He started with a too sweet concoction for all and then took limited requests of one's favorite drinks. My analysis... should be closer to $45 ($47 if you purchase on-line), and seen as a one trick pony.

My family, 2 adults, kids 13, 11 & 9, all enjoyed this little adventure. We went on a Sunday afternoon around 12: 30. No lines. The bartender was great. Very personable. My sister and I were very happy with her service. I wish I had gotten her name!

We got on the ride right away and there was my family and another couple. That's it. Seven people. It was really nice. We all were able to walk around to each corner and enjoy the views. For us the 30 minutes went by fast. We watched the Bellagio water show while we were near the top and enjoyed the desert views.  I would do this again. I found it relaxing. I'd try doing it at night as well. 

Pricey, yes. But free kids admission was an excellent plus.

We went at night and the strip looks awesome! Take lots of pics. It was about 30min. I used a local discount and saved about $6. Not good for kids with fear of heights, as the kids in our cabin were wining the entire time.

It is a fun thing to do if you want to see Las Vegas from above the grown. You could do the same and go to the top of the Eiffel Tower. It was a fun experience and a fun thing to do. What I had an issue with was we went on a Monday. Slow day. Not many people there. We didn't want to go on a crowded bubble. Which we didn't but we had four other people on it. We would have liked to have gotten a bubble to ourselves but the guy would not let us. He said we had to go with the crowd. We could have waited but he was unwilling. Again, it was a very slow day. Many of the bubbles were empty. Why not allow that? What it did to me was sour the experience. And when I got off I walked thru the shop and not sure I will recommend it to anybody. I was on a vacation. And like I said, it was a slow day. Would I do it again. No. And certainly not for the price they are asking for. Find a discount somewhere.

During a quick trip to Las Vegas in late 2013, we noticed construction of a gigantic Ferris wheel. In fact, we could clearly see the construction site and the recently erected wheel from our Vdara suite. My husband, who has architectural and engineering background, urged me to take a walk with him to "investigate". The area was closed off but we saw signs advertising the High Roller. Ooh, we vowed to return for its completion because we remembered our thrilling experience of  "riding" in the then, tallest observatory wheel, The London Eye (443' tall) in 2006. But, The High Roller had promises of being taller and would stand 550'!

Fast forward to mid-May 2014, we returned to Las Vegas. We found a newly created pedestrian mall, The Linq, located in between The Flamingo and The Quad (formerly Imperial Palace). The mall was bustling with people who were out and about into shops and restaurants. We could see the High Roller revolving at a "comfortable" speed at 30-35 minutes per revolution. Each pod could entertain up to 40 people and had "full bars"...geez, what else more would you expect from this city? Drinking and thrills!!! The ticket prices weren't as expensive as in London. 

So...Excuse Time: we were in LV for only 3 days and passed by the High Roller daily while exercise walking the Strip. We had plenty of time to get tickets and take that ride but, alas, we were at an impasse as to when to ride. I thought it would be better to ride during the daytime so at least you can SEE the sights and not have some rider who might be so intoxicated he/she might make it an uncomfortable half hour. My husband, on the other hand, said he'd rather ride at night. He likened the potential pod view to the gorgeous city view we had from the Palms Resort's Ghostbar on the 55th floor, except that we'd be moving. But, it really came down to the fact that we "chickened out"! 

We plan to return to Las Vegas and will definitely take this thrill around dusk, just to "keep the Peace" between us.

LOVED IT!!

We opted to make an 8:30pm reservation and it was perfect! Saturday night, not crowded, beautiful evening lights of the Strip....the wheel itself gives no sensation of motion, the view is up and out, not down, down, down like tower-type observation attractions, so I think even folks uncomfortable with heights would not be put off. Each pod is air conditioned and roomy, although the only downside is that there isn't a lot of seating....BUT, if you're a photo nut like me, you won't sit any how! A must-do....

We got tickets for two at 5:30 when the sun is setting. It's a perfect time for all you can drink happy hour! The ride is about 30 minutes with about 20 people in each pod. 
It's a wonderful place to take out of towners for an amazing view of the strip.

I actually took my husband here for his birthday when they opened . The line was pretty empty.  I don't know why I was expecting for more of a roller coaster feeling but I honestly barely felt anything . It was okay, the room that we rode in had about 2 different parties . I wouldn't really ride it again but at least I can say I rode on it lol

Way overrated. Yes, you do get nice views of the strip, but is it really worth the $25-$35+ for only half an hour? I do give it to the guy in the computer for being funny and corny, but it totally was not worth paying for 5 people to go. Maybe if it was like 45-min to an hour long, with a vending machine inside for drinks/alcohol it would be more worth it

This was a fun one time venture. Open bar but weak drinks and a less than accommodating bartender. The service at the Line - concierge however was so great! They helped me with my groupon and app...they gave me water and we're sweet to charge my phone!! We reserved the sunset time and the view is great..A must do for vegas newbies
Super fun place to have a drink and take a tour of Las Vegas strip. The place is affordable, it's $40 per person includes happy hour, open bar, and 30min ride.

Last year we remembered the high roller was our favorite part of our trip. Once again it has been! The happy half hour is awesome, top shelf drinks all inclusive. Give your bartender a nice tip and have some fun! We went at 830, so we saw the fountains of Bellagio right when we reached the top. Such a magical experience. Bartender was fast and friendly. If you only do one attraction make it the High Roller. It's great for everyone!

Went to Vegas in Feb/15 and had to ride the high roller.  Did the 30 min happy hour pod and met an awesome bartender named Jeremy from Wisconsin. This guy wasn't just a good bartender he was a really nice guy.  He my girl and I hit it off in that short 30min. We promised him we would be back to see him. So for my b day 5/20 we went to Vegas and back to the High Roller.  Jeremy was there and we waited for his pod, and guess what people? We had an awesome time and I know it made Jeremy' night!  Cause bartenders don't get repeat customers unless they are working in a bar.  That said when you go to the High Roller ask for JEREMY'S POD you will be glad you did!....AND MAKE SURE YOU TIP THE MAN GRACIOUSLY!!!
For $50 dollars, you get a nice view and unlimited mixed drinks for 30 min.  Worth it.
Super awesome and worth the $$. We paid $30 for one adult/one child. It took a total of about 30 minutes to go around. We got the whole bubble to ourselves!

For someone who has sky dived and still fear heights (they say it's best to conquer your fears by facing it... well, it didn't work for me) this was an exciting and yet scary experience for me. The ride is smooth but as it gets higher and higher so did my blood pressure and sweaty palms. Seemed like everyone else in our cabin was just fine - my family plus another family. Kids and adults were standing on the edge some even leaning against the rail which really made me nervous! The structure and engineer work looks impressive until I noticed there were two bolts missing attaching our cabin to the wheel (I'm sure it was by design but couldn't they have filled those holes?). Plus side -- views were great all around and my kids under 13 rode for free and we got $5 discounts off adult tickets. My recommendation for those who fear heights but still want to go on it, have a drink before going up. Oh and the on boarding off boarding part was interesting -- you walk up to the moving cabin with no safety railings in place (not really) just workers there to guide you -- think if you misstepped and fell over the edge oh man! Luckily there's a safety net in place, however you don't see it until you're in the cabin so you have to kind of take a leap of faith.

I am deathly afraid of heights. Seriously...I cant hardly stand on a chair without my knees shaking. With that being said, I wanted to do something fun this time around while in town that didn't involve the casino so instead of attempting the insane roller coaster at the New York New York which is still on my Las Vegas Bucket List, by the way, I chose to attempt the High Roller with my colleague.

We hit the new Linq strip that is set up much like an outdoor mall that just seemed to go on and on. It was a great night and the streets were filled with Las Vegas visitors and residents. 

Once we got to the main floor where the restrooms are located along with a full bar, I ran to the bathroom before our 30 minute ride on the High Roller. The bathroom is quite small for such a monumental attraction. I was very surprised...but let me pass on a little tip to you heading over here...stop at starbucks on your way back to the High Roller. It'll be on your right handside on your way to the attraction. Their restrooms are clean and you won't have to wait in a long line like you will at the High Roller. I believe there was 3 or 4 stalls. Now I did learn that they can actually fit up to 1,120 people on the wheel at any given time so to have only 3 toilets available is a little ridiculous but hey that's just me. 

It's around $25 for a daytime ride and $37 for a nighttime ride. I just learned that the nighttime ride went up to $39.95...supply and demand, folks. Honestly, it may be a lot of money especially if you have a family to pay for but it was worth EVERY penny. Whether my legs went numb at the top or not, I still give it a solid 4 stars. The view is amazing. You actually are above most of the hotels on the strip at the higher points and to see the twinkling lights out in the distance of Nevada's beautiful land, is out of this world. 

Do it, don't hesitate, and be sure to hit Sprinkles for some of their Capt'n Crunch ice cream or cupcakes after your ride!

Gah I so wanted this to be amazing. They allow WAY too many people inside each pod. They should only allow as many people as there is window space. Also it was FREEZING cold in there. I know it's hot in Vegas, but dang... At night it cools down. Fix the temp. I wouldn't recommend this attraction based on the price and how many people were in the pod. Not worth it. Go to Paris and see the Eiffel Tower instead

It was a great experience going on the high roller! I never been up so high before in Las Vegas. Being able to see the strip as well as most of the city was breathtaking.

 The entire ride is about 30 minutes and the HR reaches higher than most of the hotels. The inside of the cabin is pretty spacious. A small party (12-13?) of people can fit inside.

Before you get on, there's a small bar where you're able to buy drinks. They don't allow food on the high roller, so they allow you to finish it in the bar area.
awesome time on the high roller with my hunny and our bartender jeremy!!! he's awesome, do the happy hour ride you'll enjoy it!!!!

Awesome in every sense of the word. This is a magnificent modern engineering masterpiece. The whole experience is top notch.

Tell all your friends and family this is a must to experience while Las Vegas.

The ride itself was amazing! The views from the top breathtaking. We went on Mother's Day (Mom's ride free, and kids under 11 also ride free). My daughter loved watching the people, cars, and buildings transition into tiny objects. 

The ONLY thing I can say is that the "acoustics" were horrible!! Not only was the music much too loud, but there were several kids jumping around (having a good time) and getting restless about mid- ride. So the loud music, TV video, coupled with the kids left me feeling  "sensory overloaded." 

Overall- worth it!

$35 for 30 min ride, I was expecting a bit more. After viewing their website, suggesting that you can actually have a " party" in these carts, I was expecting to have the cart to our own party. & also a much bigger cart. However, we were crowded with two other parties. Which I thought was unnecessary because 1) our party was a large group of people 2) it was late at night, there was not much people, the cart behind us was EMPTY

it ended up that it wasn't too much of a party atmosphere because the cart was not that huge, there was limited sitting area. Whatever playing on the tv also seems like for kids instead of adults. Also the other group was a group of guys and I guess got really high cuz they saw our huge group of girls. The WHOLE time was trying to talk to us. ehhh.... 

Also the High Roller actually never stops, so running in and out of the cart freaked me out, since I was with my friends bachelorette, and we were all wearing high heels. 

Although the view is great, but I wouldn't pay $35 for this.

Staff was friendly and nice. We did not have the bar option.

The views were absolutely stunning, but a little pricey. You cannot take your drinks into the venue, but you can buy them there and take them onto the actual ride. 

Beware. Bottled water is $7.00 dollars and the frozen drinks were $9.00 - it was a no-brainer.

So much fun! I went with a friend we did the open bar. Such and amazing time. Here are some highlights: 

- our bartender was so awesome. He started us out with a round of shots. Kept the atmosphere pumped. Took pictures for everyone with the amazing view of the strip in the background. 

- the price!! Seriously worth it. It may seem high for an open bar, but trust me you'll leave feeling great 

- the views. Absolutely breathtaking.

So it was St. Patty's day and there was this giant green Ferris wheel that has great views. Naturally I decided to go at night because that's when it looks best. It is a great sight, but not sure it is worth the $35 it is. Somehow or another I got $5 off and because of the day they gave out free t-shirts that say I shamrocked the high roller St. pat's 15.  Overall it was pretty cool and got a lot of cool views, but probably won't ride it again.
A bit expensive. Very unique. A great view. Roomy pods. Not scary. A great experience. That's all I've got.

Well we're alive, so that's a good start! If you're terrified of heights, don't go. I was really scared but luckily not enough to pass out. It's about 30 minutes long and it goes up to about 550 feet. You share it with a couple other people so it made me less nervous. If I'm going down, we all are! It was a really smooth ride though. There is also a button if you need to contact help asap (like if someone fainted), only issue is it won't really do much. You still have to wait the whole 30 minutes. You can't really feel yourself going up but you go up a foot every second. When you're on the top, you see the entire city. It was cool because I was able to watch the water show at the Bellagio from there! It goes higher than every hotel here. You can see Henderson all the way to Centennial. It really is an amazing view at night. This city really is beautiful! Sometimes. Also when you enter/exit, watch your step because it does NOT pause! It's cheaper during the day but mind you, you'll probably see nothing but mountains and dirt. It's worth the extra money and going at night. If you're over 21, you can actually bring alcohol on it as well! Might help those who are a bit nervous. You can easily get discounts on the tickets. There's even one when you check in for the first time! They take your pictures before you get on but for 3 pictures in an album is $50 for a picture of you photoshopped on it. No thanks. It's something you have to do at least once here! I recommend going on it. 

Funny fact: When you reach 420 feet in the air, the man on the TV's shows up and says, "We're now 420 feet in the air.. You know what that means.. We're high. I laughed.

This review is pretty easy:

Cost $35 for the view you are paying for the view and nothing else. More or less pictures of the view. Oh and hopefully you get in the same pod with some cool people if not that can make or break your round a bout. So it is up to you how much is the view of Vegas worth to you. Night is always better to me because the day time all you see is desert.

This was my second time on the high roller. I originally went the first week it was open. This time I toook 4 people. We had the open bar.  The staff was very accommodating. We were able to skip the line. Pretty cool. 

I'm not afraid of heights per say. I get nervous when I'm high up in open air. The high roller has pods that fit about 30 people inside. There 100% inclosed. If this wheel was open I would not be able to go on due to my nervous mess. 

The alcohol. We had the open bar. For the most part. The liquor was standard. They had Malibu rum captain Morgan rum. Absolute and stoli vodka. For beer they had Budweiser and Heineken. For wine they had Kendall Jackson. They had angry orchard cider too. We each had about 4 drinks a peice. Not bad. 

The views. When I'm in Vegas my hotel room always has a view of the bellagio fountians. So for me. I am used to good views in Vegas day or night. But. If you want a good view of the Vegas strip. The high roller is your best bet. Instead of spending $500-$1000 a night. 

Overall. Everyone I was with was impressed with the high roller. I would say the open bar is the way to go! I'll prob be back here with people who want the expreience.

I'm struggling to give this 3 or 4 stars. I went for 4 because the ride was so much fun, but the ticketing process could be done much better. I bought tickets on Living Social for four Happy Half-hour rides. i bought four because we have 4 people who are of age, but one who is too young. I planned on buying the underage ticket on site. I had envisioned that we could all ride together knowing the youngest one could not drink. However, no one under 21 is allowed the bar cars, so we had to separate our party. Looking back, it is nice to not have crying, whining children in the car, but I didn't realize we were going to have to separate, so that was disappointing. When I went to purchase the youngest ticket there was a line to the ticket booth. I saw two ATMs which offer the option to purchase tickets. I tried one, but it wouldn't process my card. It seemed to have gotten stuck in the process. I went to the other one without any issues. It was easy. We then had to figure out how to get on the ride. There was another apparent entry so I went into the gift shop to ask someone where to enter. She showed me and said, "I'm not sure why those people are in line. That is where you buy tickets and get on." So we entered the area, through security and then headed upstairs to get in line. The attendant said he couldn't take my ticket through Living Social, so I had to go downstairs to exchange it. We went downstairs to the "group sales" area which was actually the backside of the long line of about 55 people in which there was only one person selling the tickets. Another person came to help, but was distracted by 3 others, obviously not enough staff to sell tickets and help guests. This was a Friday night during the holiday break. Finally we were told to go to the LINQ concierge. We then headed there were we found out we had to split our tickets. My husband volunteered to ride with our daughter, so I rode with our other children. We then had to enter the line again, through security and then got on the pod. We arrived at bartender changing time so we had to wait for the bartender to set the bar as she liked.
