She, Cheryl, was great and willing to serve and really didn't stop pouring for the rest of the trip around. We were able to see the lights. I'm sure we got our money's worth, but now I know what to expect from ticketing I'll be more prepared in the future. Since we are locals and anticipate company, we'll probably be going again.

Gah, I have been on this wheel way more times than I'd like to admit. I am a local, so when ever visitors come we make sure to hit up this wheel. We take a silly photo before we go on the wheel with a green screen that they will later show you the back drop of the wheel.

The wait isn't too long, but granted I have pretty keen patience for waiting in lines. I can see how customers who didn't pre-purchase tickets might get annoyed of the lines.

Anyways. The wheel itself takes about 1 half hour. Usually there is 15 or less people in each pod with a pretty good amount of standing space. The half hour is perfect amount of time, because you will never be waiting too long to use the rest room.

My main annoyance with the pod is that they have very cheesy advertisements on the video screens. The diversity in what gets displayed on the screens hasn't varied too much since I first went on it last year.

I think they should just make some pods customized to not have the videos played, but instead just good dance music..However, you will always get a great view of the city. So this isn't a sight to miss.

Found a great deal on Living Social. Went late at night and enjoyed the open bar ball. Luckily there were just five of us in our pod so there was plenty of room and plenty of drinks to go around. The bartender was great and made the ride so much fun! The drinks were strong and she introduced us to new kinds of drinks! It's fun when you near the apex, to countdown and take a shot! We had such fun and enjoyed the incredible views - especially the Bellagio fountain show. An absolute must!

You get a great view of the stip on here. The ride is about 30 minutes but it almost seems like it goes by really fast. If you haven't tried it, I would definately recommend it. It is kind of pricey at $37 a person....if I ever decide to go on again, I will opt for the pd with the bar!

The High Roller is a MUST while in Vegas! My family and I had a great time and it's a great way to see Vegas from a different view. We went at night and the unlimited booze for 30min is a BIG PLUS. I wish they had different music (it was like elevator music) but we made due for the little time we listened. Will definitely make the High Roller a Vegas tradition! We were able to find a deal on Groupon $79 for two at night!

Worth doing once for $32 ($5 off coupon) at night and $10 less daytime. Worth it the second time for free. This thing is an engineering marvel. Such a compact footprint. Disney would be proud. Skip the pictures and gift shop.

This place was pretty nice. Since i'm from Chicago i'm no stranger to the ferris wheel, which essentially, is what the high roller is. The view from the top was nice gave a whole view of the strip[ and looking at it from night time with all the lights on was even better. Even for someone like me whole a fear of highs and roller coasters because i felt a bit safe being in a enclosed area. The top was a bit frightening, but nothing a little liquor wont help. Me and my friends got the but pricey one with the open bar and since the trip is 30 min long you have the option to drink as much as you like while you're on the ride. 

The hospitality of the bartender was really nice to she knew how to make most of the drinks we requested as well as told us what she can make. But do remember that this bar is in a enclosed sphere going in a circle throughout the say so they might not have all the material to making anything upon request.
It was fun~we got the bar 1... be warned.. they dont have red wine.. which was a huge disappointment.. but great views at night!!

This was an awesome thing to do. Honestly we went in the  afternoon (5 pm) and it was great. Got to see everything the mountains, hotels, and the bellagio  fountain. Plus it's cheaper in the afternoon and the open bar is a huge plus. That is probably the best vodka cranberry I've ever had. Which is weird, yes I know. But seriously they don't mess around with drinks. If you have time to kill it's only a half an hour and it's great!

A friend and I managed to get a 2 for 1 voucher after joining the Total Rewards program. Really recommend finding promos, online deals, etc. when visiting to save as much as you can and they offer some good deals if you look for them! Since day admission is only $25, we saved a bunch by splitting the cost. Apparently the High Roller is larger than the London Eye, but having ridden both I really couldn't tell the difference. It may be bigger, but there's a lot more to see when you're on top of the London Eye as opposed to just looking over the Strip. The ride took about 30 minutes total and my group and I mostly had the whole pod to ourselves which was nice. They do offer an open bar pod for an additional $10, but since I'm not really a big drinker I doubt I would've taken advantage of that in 30 minutes. From what I witnessed they try to squeeze in as many people that can fit in the bar pods. I was perfectly happy in my quiet pod, lot of space to walk around and take in the views and snap some pictures.

The High Roller

First the staff at the ticket booth were very rude and matter-of-fact when spoke too.  

Second this is a very expensive $37 per ticket ride for 30 minutes.  

What was seen was basically hotels from the air.
Loud blaring music in the POD.

Waste of money

We took friends from out of town and went during the bust Memorial Day weekend. No line, no hassles, great views, great time! Only 8 people on our pod, our group of four, two Asian guys who were very quiet, and two older ladies visiting from Australia. 

Here are my tips when you go: 
1. Try to get there a few minutes before your scheduled time. 10-15 minutes is good.
2. Go to the bathroom before you get on...there's no potty on the ride. Ride lasts about 30 minutes.
3. Take a drink on the ride with you. Get a 24oz Beer ($12) at the bar right before you go. Beer always makes things better!
4. Take a camera, many great photo opportunities! 
5. Be friendly! We offered to take photos for everyone on our ride and they took photos of us. Again, things are always better when everyone gets along! 

Great ride, we'll take all of our Vegas visitors there. I wouldn't recommend it for little kids. There's nothing to do but see the view, they'll get bored and nobody likes to be stuck on a ride with a whiny kid or crying baby. 

Enjoy!

We went on a Sunday afternoon in which there was a little to no wait. The view was beautiful and my girls were at first scared but soon relaxed and enjoyed themselves. We never felt like we were actually moving so if you have motion sickness there's no need to worry. I want to go back to get a night view.

I created a Yelp account just so I could leave this review. We LOVED the High Roller! We did the happy half hour deal. Yes, it's 37 dollars a person. BUT, you get unlimited alcohol for the entire 30 minute ride. Before the ride, we bought 2 drinks and it cost us $21. So, the price of the ride is well worth it! Cheryl was our bartender and she was AWESOME!! I was all about a malibu and OJ. Cheryl quickly removed that idea from my head. She made me a rainbow plethora of amazing drinks. They were all amazing. The ride and Cheryl were the best things we've experienced in Vegas and so worth the money! A wonderful way to spend 30 minutes and 37 dollars!

The Vegas Strip Lights at Night have always been Amazing, but to see it from the High Roller is something else entirely. It is a huge treat and a must to do at least once. I went just before Christmas (12/20/14), cool and beautiful weather was ideal.

I was fortunate to go with a private party group with our own pod, no waiting in line. Staff was professional and upbeat with excitement to get the group ready for the awesome experience to come. We had a wheel chair in our party, and without missing a beat, someone ran out put down a ramp and momentarily stopped the ride to quickly accommodate the use of the ramp. The upbeat music, the flashing TV screens pumping with excitement, showing facts about the ride add to the fun of the experience. Counting down and celebrating when your pod is at the top of the wheel, like a mini NYE celebration in every pod!

The ride is spacious and long enough that you can get to see it all and take plenty of great pictures to prove it.

I have been fortunate enough to ride 2 similar rides, The London Eye and Singapore Flyer. I did both of them in the day, as a typical tourist and enjoyed, but Vegas does it Vegas Style! Night time, bright lights made all the difference in the world.

Best tip I can recommend is to have a cocktail or two before at one of the many spots nearby and go at NIGHT.

We came to Vegas to celebrate our daughter's 21st birthday.  We had a party of 12 and I was thinking about reserving a private pod ahead of time but when I found out the price I decided to forego that option.  However when we got to the front of the line, I politely asked the employee if we could have our own pod and she said yes! I think it also helped that it wasn't too busy during the day.

We went on a beautiful clear day.  The daytime views were gorgeous!  This definitely is not a ride for those people who have fear of heights!  However you can sit down and not venture close to the windows if you are afraid! The ride lasts about 30 minutes and the time goes by quickly!

The High Roller is a little pricey but you can find discount deals on the internet if you purchase in advance. Great activity if you want to stay away from the casinos!

The tallest in the world! The whole thing screams Vegas - it's huge and stands out in The Linq.

We've enjoyed this ride a few times (being locals) and the ride at night gives amazing views of the strip, including the Bellagio fountains. The ride lasts 30 minutes and allows you to take your drink/food onboard.

If you're a photographer, you'll have a great time taking pictures from the inside the bubble. The only problem I had was the cleanliness of the glass (on the outside) which would show up in pictures. Therefore, I had to find clean spots to stick my camera lens into to get un-blurred photos.

When your ride is over, there are plenty of shops, restaurants, and live music to check out at The Linq. Stay for some ice cream or enjoy some of the food/drinks and bounce your head to the live music.

I recommend taking a ride and enjoying the view!

Check out some of my pictures here: https://goo.gl/c0gXuS

Nice experience and a great way to see Vegas.  As far as views go,  the right side is the RIGHT side.  The price was right along the lines of everything else in Vegas. This is a great way to wind down and get away from the beef, booze and broads for a while.

The view is great. The pictures I took were amazing. My selfie stick captured even larger scenic views. The ride last 30 minutes and it gives you a 5 second count down before you hit the peak of height. Not all pods have bars. If you decided to add this option its $10 more and unlimited. I did not purchase the bar options because you are allowed to bring your own drinks as long as not in glass containers. And honestly I was so busy taking pictures, talking, and making memories, I didn't even finish the drink I brought in with me.

*Prices*
Before7 pm $26.95
After 7 pm $36.96 
$10 added to each for open bar 7 pm and earlier. $15 added after 7 pm. 
Once up the escalator, you meet with photographers ready to take your picture which will be available for purchase after. Then walk into a small area with a few pictures on the wall with dates of construction of the wheel and its progress. Check it out, most people by pass it. It's ways good to know some history. 

The lines seem longer at night. Sure there is lots of lights, but you don't get to see the city's architecture and layout in such detail. I purchased the before 7pm ticket and rode around 6 pm. This was a great time to see the sights. When purchasing tickets at the kiosk you can not use coupons. Head inside to purchase tickets. I found a $5 off each ticket in my hotel room booklet! Whoo-hoo! Women dressed in lime green will be on the Linq Promenade handing out $2 off coupons. They can not be combined but it's still a savings of you can't get your hands on the $5 off ones. Once off the wheel you are ushered into a gift shop with pictures available for purchase. Omg there some pricy pictures. Lol this gift shop sells full size family size bags of chips! Unnecessary information but funny.

This observation wheel is the largest in the world. It's definitely a must do once. Also make sure you get a coupon. No reason to pay full price. You can earn total reward points by making this purchase but they will not be awarded to you on site. Ask for your receipt and head to your total rewards booth where points will be given then.

So COOL!!! Glad we came down to check this out! Been watching them build it and now I get to ride it. The line is indoors with a couple different staging areas. There's even a bar half way up. 
Pay attention when you are boarding. When I road it did NOT stop. But hey there's a safety net underneath, just incase lol.
There's enough time once you get on if you change your mind and want to get off. 
There's plenty of room to walk around and a couple of benches to sit. 
The whole rotation takes about 30 minutes. 
I have to ride it again at night. I'll bet the view is amazing!
Be sure to view your photo on your way out. They do green screen souvenir photo on the way up.

Waste of money. Ferris wheel is unbearably slow and the view on one side is a parking lot. Only go in the bar car if you are already drunk. You will feel right at home with all the loud and wasted people. Only positive is the drinks and liquor used are good quality. They had Patron tequila instead of the cheapo brand.

Do it once, then Never do it again.

This is a nice addition to Vegas and the views are nice, but it is located in an award place. The wheel goes up 550 ft and gives you views of backsides or hotels, swimming pools, parking lots, and residential / ghetto areas of Vegas far off the Strip. This wheel would have been much better built right against the strip. The ride is also very slow, it takes 30 minutes to make one full rotation. So the excitement is from the views you see and not so much the actual ride itself. You'll get much better views from the Stratosphere Tower which is also cheaper to visit. We timed getting in line correctly and got our own private cabin. There's a cute funny blonde actor guy too who narrates the ride on video screens instead the cabins.

When we rode the prices were $27 per Adult before 6pm and $37 per Adult after 6pm. It is not cheap and is $10 more expensive at night, so try to find discounts.

This is an attraction which you really only need to do once in your life and then never again. So I say go for it, but only once.

Going to Las Vegas with 4 children under the age of 5 is absurd, but it was my husband's 50th birthday and I had the nanny!!! I also wanted my 5 year old to experience being 550 feet up on the ferris wheel " the tallest observation wheel on the planet." I read the previous reviews to get an inside scoop for an awesome experience. I got my 3 adult tickets at kiosk for $34.95 to bypass the line, but had a service fee of $6. We rode at 11:30pm. 

We were escorted by James to the elevators since we had little kiddos riding the wagon and a stroller.  We stopped by the bar so daddy and mommy can get a drink and restroom for the kids since it's a 30 min ride. 

The views were spectacular, the staff were amazing, and most of all there were only 4 set of families in the air condition capsule. We were able to enjoy and take pictures at every angle of the 360 degree rotating cabin.
HHH is a must!!! It's only 30 minutes for $40. a person but is worth every penny. Drinks are flowing, music is bumping and we had a great time. Our bartender Sheryl was a blast, thank you!!!

This place was freaking awesome.  Came down to celebrate my best friends wedding.  After the reception dinner we decided to head hear to continue the celebration.  We got on the pod with the bar. You pay $52 and you get free drinks the wheel ride. The ride took about 30 minutes and it was so smooth you never realized you were moving. We got to party with other guests and it was a great place to mingle and take pics.  A definite recommendation
This thing is huge. The carts are big. I think we paid around $22. No lie I was kinda drunk don't remember how long the ride lasted.

What an awesome Vegas experience.  I'm in love with this thing!

The ride at night-time is spectacular.  Pricey, but doesn't break the bank.  They have ticket kiosks right at the beginning of the Linq promenade, and the High Roller is at the very end.  Very handy.

My group and I went at about 11:30 pm on a Tuesday night and there was hardly a line at both the kiosks and the actual High Roller itself.  They ushered us into the building and through ropes of lines but didn't have to wait longer than 30 seconds to actually get into the ride.  I'm sure on weekends or at different hours this is another story, but I was pleasantly surprised by how quickly we were on the ride.

The actual observation room is very spacious and can fit a large amount of people. The ride itself lasts about 30 minutes and has a video commentary,  but not excessively loud, so you can still talk among you and your group.  

The drinks at the High Roller are about the same price as any bar on the Strip, but the bartenders were nice and friendly and made the drinks very quickly.  I think the cups are novelty and you can take them after you're done, but I threw mine away in the midst of all the fun I was having :(

This is a super awesome addition to the Strip and I'm so glad it's here.  It's a beautiful 30 minutes of gorgeous Las Vegas scenery and a relaxing ride.

We went mid afternoon and got a pod to ourselves - it's a great experience and is higher than any other observation wheel, so you do get a good view.

The commentary is very cheesy but the little ones will love it.

Having done the London Eye several times, I didn't really feel wowed but if you have never done a wheel before it's defiantly worth the trip. Younger kids are free too, so it's good value at $54 for two adults. (Compare that to the London Eye and it's a bargain!!)

$5 open bar is a must try, as well.

Just went with my girlfriend and got a deal on groupon for the happy hour package. The view from the top is pretty spectacular. You see the entire city, every hotel, etc. It's like seeing the city whn you fly into Vegas, just at a much slower pace so you can enjoy it. We luckily had a fairly empty car with maybe 12 people so never had to wait for drinks and since the view is better on the right side of the car, people had no problems taking turns and sharing. As far as the price, even with the groupon, 80$ for 2 people for 30 minutes of drinking (which went extremely fast) even with the view wasn't exactly worth it. My advice...try to get a deal on the non-happy hour car and bring in your own booze! As long as you bring plastic or cans, you can bring whatever you want. A group can grab a couple of 12 packs and get loaded and view for much less...with a date, maybe somewine in a box! lol

This is pretty awesome!  You definitely want to go at night....the view is beautiful!  You can hardly feel it moving.  I stood right up next to the glass and felt safe!  Very romantic!  Better than blowing your money on the slots!

Best view on the strip! We had a groupon for the Happy Half Hour. Totally worth it. You get a private bartender for your "pod." We had about 10 people in our pod with us. Drink as much as you want for a half hr and enjoy GORGEOUS views of the strip! I don't think there is any place in Vegas which offers better views than one of these pods.

Worth springing for the Nighttime one. Not sure it would have been as nice a view during the day.

The ride is so boring.  You can technically book a hotel room facing the strip and request for the room at the top of their building and have the same view for probably cheaper.  Whatever you do, don't purchase the VIP package, especially by using Travelzoo's coupon code.  Terrible deal ( http://www.travelzoo.com/entertainment/las-vegas/-63-High-Roller-VIP-Ride-Package-for-Two-1871376/?conf=1&cm=signedin&source=_tzlock&placement=Overlay-TravelDeal-DealPage-SignUpFP5), especially if you are going to ride this ride before 7pm (day time cut off) since the day pass is only 24.99$/per person (that's 50$ for 2 instead of 63$ for two) If you're thinking that it comes with free drinks and photos with this package, it doesn't.  They made me pay for those things and when I told them that my ticket and this thing says it's complimentary, they told me to contact Travelzoo or Linq's itself.  I will post pictures later to show you the receipt I paid for for the extra items listed here. You're basically paying for more to ride this boring ride and for the coupons.  Oh, and also, that deal from Travelzoo can only be purchased on a computer and not a mobile device--I didn't know that so wasted so much time calling them (they kept bouncing me around from one to another, from Linq's itself and Travelzoo agents, instead of just telling me that) and trying to enter it with different Internet browser as they advised it. And when I did it on a computer, Linq's website was down, so I didn't know that it would only work with a computer till I had my friend test it out for me a few days later while I was on the rode driving to Vegas.  Seriously, save your money and go ziplining or ride on their roller coasters or do a tour or something there instead.

Joe the manager was a terrible help when it came for a refund. And all we wanted was a second ride!(aka give them more business) My co-worker and I tried to buy tickets for a SECOND ride because we enjoyed it so much- we apparently got sold the wrong tickets and then got escorted by security to the exit! Who treats paying customers that way?! Then Joe accused us of being wrong and never buying ANY tickets! We had pictures (that we had BOUGHT from them 5 minutes prior) to prove we were just on their ride. Never trust this company! It's a scam and a waste of energy! Joe should be fired and so should "his" security team who tried to treat us with the worst respect! Joe is so rude and terrible! Never give them business! Worst business ever! Joe needs training!!!

this is a fun, family friendly attraction in vegas that really only warrants one ride in your lifetime... so here are my tips to make it the best ride the first time around.

1. go to the bathroom BEFORE you get on the ferris wheel, otherwise you will be holding your number 1 or 2 for at least 30 minutes bro.

2. ride it at night time. yes, it's cheaper during the day, but if the twinkling lights of vegas are what you want to see, then you will have a 100% better view at night.

3. if you are claustrophobic or have a fear or heights, you probably should not ride this. you are trapped in a clear bubble that is towering quite high over the strip.

4. if your heart is set on experiencing the high roller, buy your tickets online. you'll save a couple of bucks.

5. there is limited seating inside the pods. if you can't stand for an extended period of time, this may be an uncomfortable ride for you.

6. it's totally fine to bring a drink on board but there are no trash cans from what i can remember inside the pod. so you may be holding onto that cup or bottle for quite a while.

Must do this at night. You can see all of Vegas from the top. All you can drink ( get a coupon from Groupon or living social) during the ride. There is a regular one and one with the open bar. I must admit I was scared. Super high. As soon as you get on order your drink so you can get at least 2 drinks down before you get off. The line can get long. The pod holds up to 40 people. Something to do once. Don't really need to do it again. Overall it was a nice experience. I give it 4 stars just because of the drink line.
This was an awesome experience. They have a groupon that is a deal! Our bartender poured very strong drinks and the views were breathtaking!

Must Read before you go on - make sure you use the restroom before you get on especially if you are drinking.. its about a 30 min ride and you are not getting off. If you are afraid of heights, think twice before you go. You are enclosed so its not like a regular fair ferris wheel that is out in the open with air to help ease your stomach. 

Two types of tickets - Full Admission and General 

Full Admission (pricey $38 at night) - you get a bar in the center of the pods... fits about 40 people standing. Fun for groups. Even can be a great spot to propose if everyone in there is your friends and family.

General Admission ($10) - no bar open with a little space to sit but still no restroom.

I would have not gone on if I had to pay for the ticket, but since I won the tickets gambling my group decided to try it out. I will not go back on it as I didn't care for it as much. The city lights were beautiful at night but to be enclosed for that long especially when you are drinking was not that great. Also we had a few people that were afraid of heights and ended up feeling sick when they got off... If you must go up bring something salty to eat just in case someone gets queezy..its about 300 ft up the ground.

Came here using a livingsocial deal with the bf.  Neither of us are big drinkers but they only had the happy hour tickets available so we went with that.  Totally lucked out and we were the only ones (besides the very nice bartender) in the car!!!  

Having a bar in the car was pretty cool.  It was amazing to watch them run on with more ice and run off with trash etc as the thing was rolling and before we were let on.  Given the huge group that was in there just before us, i was impressed by the cleanliness of the car.

Drinks were decent.  And it really was all you can drink.  Juat the regular bar drinks and beer.  No champagne which was what i wanted but no big deal.

To get on the drink car, you also get escorted to a separate area. Ade me feel like a VIP.

The views are amazing.  Went at night and saw the strip and lights that went far far out.  

Summary: get the happy hour.  Worth the view.  Do it once, probably not worth the price for twice though.

High Roller it is!! Finally we got on. Night-view is amazing!! Pretty lights and so high up there.  550ft.. The pod wasn't so bad.  We had around 15 people in the pod.  FYI.  Please don't pass gas inside!  Somebody decided to pass gas and that sure killed the moment for a bit.  Inside the pod the A/C was luckily working at the time.  Bring out your phones, and cameras to taking some wonderful night shots.  OH yeah, do selfies also.  lolz.!! Overall gotta try it out.  Been to other ferris wheel in other countries this one sure tops my list.  Worth the ride in Vegas!!

If you want an aerial view of the city of Vegas without doling out money on helicopters then this is your thing. Beautifully built, the wheel gives a 360 degree view of the city and is nicely lit. Although I found the ride a bit expensive especially at night time.

Really fun experience. We finally made it over to the High Roller on a touristy Sunday afternoon and ended up getting a whole pod to ourselves. Tickets are $25 during the day and $35 at night. Definitely worth it for that amazing view!

We had SO much fun! I'm so glad we came across a groupon for this and decided to try it out. It's a 30 minute ride with all you can drink open bar for about $25 a person. With drink prices in Vegas, that's a steal. I was pleasantly surprised that they had some good brands of liquor because part of me was expecting well cocktails. Our bartender was super fun, the views were amazing and we met some fun people. Highly recommend the high roller.
Our hotel package included two free tickets. Awesome views of Vegas. We really enjoyed it, but could have done without video of guy with weak jokes.

So we were at the Linq and while we were there we decided to check the High Roller.  It's not that bad.  It's pretty big inside, so its not too crowded and you can see from all angles in the ball.  The man speaking on the tv is kind of low.  He does let you know when you're at the very top.  There's a/c in the ball so you're not hot or suffocating. It goes at a steady speed and never stops even when you're getting off and on.  So if you feel uneasy you could always ask one of the employees to help you on.  There's a bar inside before getting on and another bar outside right before you get on if you change your mind and need a refresher. Be prepared to spend over $60-$65 for two people.

Cool place to go for good views of the strip in LAs Vegas. This is right behind the Linq hotel in the middle of the strip and it's right by a monorail station. This is also right by the large parking lot for Harrah's. It costs $23 for the daytime ride and $37 for the night ride. They also offer a ride with an open bar but it is more expensive and it looks like it gets crowded.

We went on a Friday afternoon and we had the car almost all to ourselves. The ride is very stable and not an issue if you're afraid of heights like I am. It takes a half hour to go around and it gets high enough that you can see a lot even though you are behind a few casinos.

Definitely a very cool experience and good for kids too.

So much better than I thought it would be! Went during the day and could see the whole desert, in addition to the city. We got the deal on livingsocial and it was a great way to go. We went when it was quiet (no kids) and really enjoyed it.

If you're going to ride the High Roller check Groupon for a deal first. Paying full price (depending on what time you're going and which pod) is just silly. It's 30mins and it goes by pretty fast. I would say it's one of those things you'll ride once and never again. I was in the bar pod, which is all you can drink but you can only have one drink at a time. We made sure to get our moneys worth while in there so we were drinking fast. It was cool to experience it and see the valley like that but again a one time deal for me.

I always have such a blast whenever I go on the High Roller!  There's usually pretty good deals on Groupon or Travelzoo if you're interested in the all-you-could drink deal.  It's about a 30 minute ride.  During that time you pretty much just enjoy the view and try to take down as many drinks as possible.  The bartender usually has a hidden Patron bottle with him/her.  Our bartender didn't take it out until someone ordered a Tequila Sunrise.  They aren't allowed to pour shots, but if you ask them to make it a strong one, they will pour more alcohol into your drink.  Don't forget to tip them! The view is pretty amazing once you reach the top so make sure you have your camera handy.

This is a very nice attraction that is definitely worth going on at least once in your life....but you don't ever need to go on it again after that.

First off, it's pricey.  Even for locals.  That right there deters me from wanting to go on it again.  It's not the most comfortable when you're in the pod.  I only had about 20 other people in the pod with me, which is about half of what it CAN hold, yet it was still difficult to move around, and I just wanted to yell, "MOVE!  You've been hogging the best spot for the whole ride!  Let someone else get a chance!" to some people.

Also, there is a super annoying guy in the video that plays the entire time you're on the ride.  And it's true: 30 minutes is a long time when you're going a foot a second.  Once you get to the top and see the amazing view, then you're bored out of your mind for the second half as it comes down.

Again, it is worth going on at least once to experience it and see the cool sights, but that's about it.

P.S. They need to invest in some good photo editing equipment.  In the picture my brother and I took, we both had glaring red eyes and looked like Terminators!

With all the hustle and bustle of the Vegas Strip, the High Roller is actually a great way to unwind a bit and enjoy great views, it's a pretty relaxing ride, and at about 30mins, it might be the longest you can stretch $35 in this town!  It is one of those experiences that feels way too touristy, but you just have to try it once to say you did it. I did enjoy it, but I also feel that once was enough.  

A word to the wise, you should try to get a spot on the entrance side quickly upon entering the pod because that's the side with all the best views, and I found many of the riders were very unwilling to let others come to their spot to take pictures at the height of the ride (one couple actually settled on the floor at the left window and they never freakin' moved!); the views on the other side are rather unimpressive.
The happy hour option is amazing! Top shelf liquor with a bartender that had a great personality. The views of the strip were amazing! Definitely a must-do if you're in Las Vegas!

TIP: Don't wear high heels here. The High Roller never stops so you're gonna have to jump in and out. If you're not ok with possibly spraining your ankle then wear flats.

The Yelpers before me have already mentioned all the pros - nice view, clean and air-conditioned cabins, and little to no line. BUT we ran into trouble while trying to redeem the Living Social deal we had purchased for a $35 nighttime ticket + free drink. We waited in line at the Guest Services window and the girl told us we had to redeem it at the Linq concierge, a couple doors down. To make a long story short, we found out later that we could've redeemed it at the window we originally were at OR in the main ticket office. I really have no idea why that girl had us go down to the Linq concierge. A regular price ticket is $35 so I don't think all the hassle was worth it for a 30 minute ride.

We went in the afternoon,  to escape the heat and get good pictures.  Took the bar cart.  It was absolutely beautiful! ! It went so slow you couldn't tell it was moving.  There's a 10 second countdown when you reach the top 550 feet in the air.  
Amanda, our bartender, was very nice,  made good drinks,  and was knowledgeable and helpful. 
Highly recommend this ride!

My friend treat me here and I treat her back with drinks. It was nice, just to experience it even just once. I guess it's a nice place to catch up with friends who are new to the place so they can see around too.

Amazing!!! The view, the smooth ride, the time spent on the high roller, the TV guide telling you facts about the high roller. All amazing! Best yet when we were on the high roller the water fountain was going on at the Bellagio and was a plus. I will definitely do it again.

The last part of my playing tourist yesterday was to ride the High Roller.  It has been great fun to watch this being built and to anticipate riding it.  I have a fear of heights and I abhor glass elevators.  This seemed to me like the making of a perfect fetal position ride.  But, I screwed up my courage, bought my ticket, and scampered into the car.  

Let's back up a bit.  You can buy tickets online, at one of the many self-serve kiosks in the Linq and other places around the Quad/Linq area.  You can also buy in person.  If you do, and you have a Total Rewards card, the $2 fee you pay online is discounted.  No special price for Nevada residents.

After getting your ticket and going through several theme park like queuing areas, one on the first floor and then another one on the second floor at the top of the escalators.  

After walking down a ramp, you're urged to move along quickly because the wheel generally doesn't stop and you enter after the people have exited on the other side.  Once everyone is in, the car door shuts and is locked.  The ride is very smooth and it was very easy for me to do.  I was so interested in moving from side to side taking photos and enjoying the view.  It really didn't bother me.

After what seemed like 10 minutes, the ride was over and it was time to exit.  I strode down the ramp with a swagger as if to say, "Yes, I did it! Yo!" 

Now, to go back and do the ride at night to see the lights.

Meh, boring.  It's one of those attractions where you go in it and then think, this is it?  You just check it off the list.  Been there, done that and don't need to do it again.  At $35 for a half hour trip around the wheel, I would say it was overpriced.  Yes there is a great view of Las Vegas and it's better to go at night with all the lights.  It's SOOOOO slow.  If you are worried about getting sick or it being like a thrill ride, it isn't like that.  It's an observation wheel.  It had just opened  about a month before we were on it and there were hardly any people going on it.  I think the price is to blame.

Pretty cool for a ferris wheel. We rode it early on a Friday night and had a whole car to ourselves. Nice relaxing approximately half hour ride with some very cool views. Worth the 32.00$ but I probably wouldn't do it again.

Bought a Groupon for the half hour happy hour, not really sure what to expect. The higher roller was the highlight of my trip! We went on Friday night and did not wait in line longer than 5 minutes. 
The view was amazing! You can see everything, including the Bellagio fountains. The compartment we were in was not too crowded and there was even a proposal! 
Plus, it is an open bar so I took it as a personal challenge as to how much champagne I can drink in 30 minutes. Which is a lot.

Another highly recommended thing to do with your group of friends when visiting Las Vegas! 

It's a bit pricey, so check if there's a groupon or discount for it. My friends and I did the Happy Half Hour (HHH) and basically had a whole pod to ourselves (with the exception or four random people that were in it with us). While on the pod you can only order one drink at a time, so drink fast so you can get more. Make the most of your time and money. Drink. 

While on the pod, you'll have amazing views of Vegas and of the strip so it does create for awesome photo opportunities. Take advantage of them... get a new profile picture if you want, take some snap chat videos to make your friends jealous, or post to your IG and get those likes. You'll enjoy your time on the pod drinking during HHH. Will definitely be back next time i'm in Las Vegas.

I'll tell you what I remembered before I blacked out from drinking too much. 1st of all get the one that have a bar, unlimited drinking for 30 minutes "WORTH IT" 2nd go at night more beautiful at night, 3rd at 550ft... Wow. & 4th... That's all I remember. It was lights out for me. All I remember was walking into the MGM. My feet was hurting the next day.

Love the ride itself the view was breathtaking tickets were easy to get and also cheaper online. Love the idea of the open bar however our bartender was not having a good day he was very rude and pushy with his tip jar. Even calling out everyone who didn't tip at all which is disrespectful. Although the bartender was horrible I would definitely ride again.

Offers a nice view of the city but this isn't cheap : $35/pp when we came here around 8 PM on Sunday and we bought our ticket at the base of the ride. Practically no line at this time when we went; our entire group inside the pod was small so it wasn't crowded ~ 8 people. It offers a beautiful view of the city in 30 minutes.

We came here a few weeks ago and enjoyed our 1st ride on High Roller Ferris Wheel. The views and experience were marvelous.

Unlike traditional ferris wheel that go at steady quick pace, high roller moved fairly slow allowing you more time to just chill out and enjoy the spectacular views of the entire Vegas strip. Pods are large and can hold about 40 people. Thank goodness they don't cram a lot of people inside. We had 12 in our party which was perfect and ride was comfortable.

It's located at the far end of LINQ's outdoor promenade. We parked in back lot across the street from ferris wheel and were able to find ample space. Price of admission was $27 day and $37 night. We went at night and sight of neon lights were amazing. There's an option for an open bar which is $20 more. It had just rained a few hours earlier and everything was perfectly clear by the time we reached highest peak of the ride. The best picture taking moments were definitely in order. We can see the entire city of Las Vegas from above and most of hotels along the strips. Because the pods were fully enclosed in glass we had to turn off our flash to prevent light glares from bouncing off the window and affecting our pictures.

The entire trip took about 30 minutes and experience was worth it. Not sure if I would do it again, but the all you can drink open bar sounds enticing. LOL!

A "Must do" for anyone visiting Las Vegas!  As senior citizens we got half-off tickets, a great way to celebrate our 45th wedding anniversary.  We got there at opening time, so got a "pod" to ourselves.
Fun to do. Ride is over in 30 minutes. Great views of entire Las Vegas Valley. If you are local go on Tuesday. 50% off with Nevada ID.
Pricey but nice view at night. Must do it once I'd say but nothing spectacular. It's nice that they serve drinks. The line goes pretty quick.

Unique views of Vegas and the surrounding community. Bought our tickets for a night run inside Harrahs. Yes, it's pricey, but discounts are out there if price is a concern, spend the time, save some money. We pretty much walked right through LINQ and right up to the pod. Friendly crew all the way, friendly riders too. Loading looks a bit hairy, but it's smooth enough if you follow the lead of the people ahead of you and heed the guidance of the crew member (the pod move along the loading dock so you're working with a moving target like an escalator, but the movement is lateral). The lower quadrants are pretty uneventful as you get oriented. A video host makes annoying appearances throughout the ride, sometimes bringing interesting facts, other times pumping up the excitement like only a generic videotaped pep rally can. The timelapse constuction video is cool. They could slow it down, or repeat it and offer it on the lower parts of the ride where the parking lot is currently the backdrop. Various data comes and goes. A continuous graphic showing your position and altitude would be nice. Also, they could use the screens to help locate and identify noteworthy spots and attractions. The views are great. If you're not blessed with a upper floor view at your hotel or your room faces the suburbs, this is a cheap way to see what you're missing. You can take some pretty good pictures in the pod, but be aware of the distortion in some areas where the "glass" is curved. The ride is smooth, very few motion issues, the air is mostly fresh with comfy a/c and our pod was not overstuffed so we could all move around. 

I'd walk slowly and observantly to the pod and consider your neighbors as you approach the loading zone. If you don't want to be locked up with drunk fratboys, mobs of kids, or loud ethnic ladies screaming a foreign language endlessly into their phones........adjust your arrival time. Our pod had about a dozen riders. One girl was having an emotional breakdown quietly with her friend consoling her (didn't appear to be ride related). Another girl left her drink on a rail, which fell to the floor with no way to clean it up (no cup holders, finish your stuff down stairs). But the rest of our travel mates were pleasant and courteous and seemed to have a very positive experience. Glad we partook. It's by no means a thrill ride and visually its very calm and pleasant and they can easily accomdate handicapped and disabled folks. Fun time.
Was so much fun. Definitely worth the $30ish. Our bartender was Cheryl and she was soo fun!

As a long standing Las Vegas local, we have seen it all.  We went to the High Roller, excited to see the newest attraction. I have a fear of heights, but I felt I would be safe on the High Roller.

The pods are in continual motion, but very slow.  You do not feel the height.  I would be more concerned with someone who doesn't like closed spaces vs heights in the pod.  

The sound echos off the walls pretty easy so the person across the pod can be speaking to the person next to them and it feels they are sitting right next to you.  

We went during the day and plan to go back at night, so we have both experiences.

I would recommend someone contacting the Linq or other hotels to clean up their roofs as this is part of the view.  Some pretty bad looking views out there.

The High Roller, the world's tallest ferris wheel, located in Linq Hotel is a must try at least once in day or night when you are in Vegas.  We haven't tried riding during night time but will definitely do once we go back to Las Vegas.  The day time ride is amazing because you get to see what else Las Vegas has to offer beyond The Strip.  I think one of the perks of riding the High Roller during the day is you get to move around freely inside the pod because no one else is there if your group is lucky especially if you go for the pod with the open bar.  I prefer the pod with the open bar for the unlimited drinks mainly because of the free drinks!  You just pay a little bit more for the tickets but it's unlimited drinks for 30 minutes!  Always remember to tip.  This was a good experience and highly recommended for people who would like to see a great view of The Strip in Las Vegas.

Great view of the strip and surrounding Las Vegas! Buy tickets and enter right before 5pm. After 5pm the prices go up. We ended up going right before sunset, which was  beautiful. The ride is only 30 minutes and goes around once. Time does fly when you are having fun. The booths are open so no privacy. Be sure to grab a drink from the bar to take up with you!

Timing is everything.  We planned our adventure on the High Roller to begin just at sun down so when we reached the top all of Vegas was lit up.  We had no waiting issues and actually were able to get one earlier than our reservation time was set up for.
Bar at the top while you wait is smart and handy, although please be sure you have used the restroom as you will not be seeing one for another 30 minutes plus. Don't be "That Person" that ruins it for everyone.
That being said the ride itself was smooth sailing.  You do not feel like you are even moving.  Pods are quite roomy and have some seating available.  We stood as we wanted to take in as much as we could.  Have your cameras and smart phones ready - you will want to capture a few shots for sure!
I would highly recommend this and would definitely do this again!

This is such an awesome experience! The happy hour adults only is the way to go. Nice selection of alcohol. Stellar service from Reese. He is a friendly bartender. Took great photos. Kept the party "rolling". Served ladies first. Quick skills. I plan to do this every time we visit Vegas. Very memorable for my 40th bday!

enjoyed the ride and the view from the top.  i think it is worth it - you can get some really cool pictures of vegas from varying angles.  i'm sure right at dusk or late evening would have beautiful views (we went mid-afternoon on a clear day so we could see pretty far out).

the only thing i would say is that it is so new, the price or deals will start popping up... if each person was ~$15-20, it would definitely be right on target - as it stands its probably $10-15 over-priced.  wait a bit and i'm sure there will be deals to be had!

My Vegas routine is usually eat, sleep, party, repeat. Especially during the summertime, there's dayclubs and nightclubs to hit up and not much time to do anything else. But during the winter months, the High Roller is a perfect way to spend 30 minutes. Get the Happy Hour option with open bar. Get your buzz on while enjoying fabulous Las Vegas views.

I've been on it for both the day and evening option. The day option is cheaper, and in my opinion is better only because you can take photos of both you and the strip in the background. It was difficult to take a good photo at night. 

I believe they also increased the prices recently, but just check out their website or Groupon for discounts. Seems like they always have some type of promotion going on. I paid $35 last year for evening, but $30 for daytime this past weekend.

The ferris wheel moves continuously, but most of the pods are not equipped with a bar. We waited about 10 minutes for a pod with the bar and each pod fits about 24 people. They should definitely stock more pods with bars, since the line for drinkers was twice as long as the non-drinkers. 

Once inside, my friends were able to get 4 drinks in the span of 30 minutes. You can even ask for a drink right before the end of the ride and take it out with you. They had a pretty good selection of liquor, including my favorite, Chambord! 30 minutes pass by really quickly, so I guess my only complaint is that the ride was too short.

Perfect way to end a Vegas Trip! Take a group of friends, look for a livingsocial or groupon deal on the All you can drink package and enjoy the great view of Las Vegas. The trip is about 30 minutes long, so if you drink fast, you can have about 3 drinks comfortably. Our bartender was able to make us some margaritas, Mai tais and Jack & Pepsi (instead of Jack & Coke). One of my friends is not too fond of heights BUT even she was able to fully enjoy the experience because while you're in the pod the movement isn't severe that it scares you. Highly recommend doing this!

Great experience! Beautiful views of Vegas! The only downfall is that we did the happy hour ride and got Francis as a bartender who was extremely rude and constantly asked for tips. We tipped him over $20 and he made himself more drinks than he made us. Great experience, horrible bartender!
Paid extra for the happy half hour. It would not have been so bad but they packed it do you we're practically elbow to elbow.

LOL. WHAT A JOKE. It's currently 12:04 on a Saturday in VEGAS. HAHA. THEY DIDNT LET a group of 20 people get in due to dress code. they said we were too lewd. If "too lewd means a short dress in Vegas on a Saturday-in a 21 and over event.... Then I guess...  Smh. Which I could give this place a fair warning. So upsetting. After I bought a groupon... They couldn't even give me a receipt.  So my coupon was redeemed. I lost my money, did NOT GET A REFUND AND WASNT ALLOWED IN. if I was ballsy enough I'd post a pic of my "lewd" outfit. Just a heads up: wear your Sunday BEST when you step foot in this place.

The high roller is one of those things you should try and experience once, and never have to do again. Prices vary all the time, depending on the season and deals they have going on, but we got ours from Groupon for $69. This includes a ride package for two, buy one get one drink free coupon, and 15% off a souvenir photo. To be honest, if we didn't have the Groupon deal, I don't think the ride is worth the regular pricing. 

The pod holds about 40 people and has two benches inside. There was around 10 people when we rode and there was ample walking space inside, so we didn't feel cramped at all. The tv host narrates the whole 30 minute ride, and could be somewhat annoying, depending on your tolerance. 

The strip view at night from 550ft up is one of a kind and definitely cool to see. But like I've said before, I wouldn't do it again unless it was for free.

Teenage daughter loved it.  No line at all on a Thurs night around 9:45pm.  The ride is about 30-40 minutes.  We got a discount online, on Cesear Hotel's website.  Ticket was  $32.  Pricing is a little crazy but it is one of the tallest ferry wheel rides.

Didn't know you can bring drinks on it!  I'm scared of heights but that will definitely take the edge off. Next time!

YELP 365 CHALLENGE 2014-(92/365) "Free Ride"

So we just happened to be "playing Tourists" at The LINQ and we passed the High Roller and inquired about their projected opening. The gentlemen at the door mentioned that Caesar's Gaming Employees had access to ride, then asked us if we were locals.
We said "Yes we are!" so he handed us a couple of tickets and said "Enjoy your ride!".

As you step inside, you pass through a couple staging areas where employees are constantly telling you "right this way" and "enjoy your ride!" then you take a quick souvenir photo(to pick up after wards at the sky shop). one area shows you a quick video and gives you a last chance to back out like a wuss if you choose to do the walk of shame. Lastly, there's restrooms to do your business so you're not holding it for the duration of the ride(Half an hour long) For those who wanna snack and booze it up during your ride, there's a concession stand to get drinks and snacks before you board your pod.

You are lead outside to a waiting area beside the High Roller, and when its your time to enter, do so calmly, but quickly! The wheel is constantly moving very slow, and hardly ever stops! Its like getting on and off an escalator. Inside, there's enough seating for about 10-12 people, and the rest of the space is standing room only, or if you wish, sit on the pod floor. Up to 40 people fit in one pod, but during our ride, we had about 15-20 people which was better IMHO....sufficient space to sit/stand and move around freely inside the pod during the ride which also allowed for lots of pictures which I'm sure will be more limited as it opens to the public and more people are allowed in the pods. I also feel bad for those who don't do well in claustrophobic settings. as this ride may make one feel that way.

As the ride ends, exit the pod the same way you entered it, but on the opposite side you entered from, You are then led under the High Roller to the Sky Shop were you can pick up gifts and even your souvenir photo if you wish. It is an awesome ride that everyone should experience at least once. I heard that it is beautiful at night when the wheel and the strip is all lit up. ALOHA!!!

Shaka Meter:  \uuu/  \uuu/  \uuu/  \uuu/  \uuu/  5

* I heard the admission may be $30 and the hours may be from 10 am to 2 am

We went at night and just before the crowd hit. The view was amazing and interesting to see Las Vegas from yet another view! We were also surprised at how reasonable the prices were on the beverages. We found a Groupon Coupon which made it even a better deal!

Fun experience. We went at 650pm its cheaper if you get on before 7pm. The wheel never stops moving so you jump on to your designated POD. The friendly, helpful staff will guide you. There is netting underneath the wheel , I asked if anyone ever fell they said no. Good to know. I invited 20 of my friends to go with me, 8 showed up. The capsule would have fit that many people. The capsule is large and spacious. I invited my friends because I didn't want to be in a capsule for 30 minutes with strangers. The revolution takes 30 minutes. When you get to the very top "you spin me around" plays and the wheel stops for a few minutes. I liked the view, you can see Henderson and the Wynn and Encore properties. You wont get a main strip view but I didn't mind that. I had a great time, you will too. I went on a Tuesday, if you are a local resident that makes a big difference in the price you will pay

Really cool, fun thing to do. You can see the whole valley as well as all the spots on the strip. Went during the day and it was empty, got right on. Highly recommend this. It's about a thirty minute ride and only cost 21.95 a person. Relaxing.

I'd recommend everyone give this attraction a ride at least once. 

It's pricey for what it is... if your a local you get a 50% discount. Yea for locals!

Go at night... it's stunning.

This is awesome! We went during the day-cheaper price. Slow thirty minute ride. Beautiful view of Vegas all around. Music plays in cabin. You can sit or stand. 
Some cabins offer drinks. Air conditioned. Wonderful!
Don't miss it!

Pretty cool experience. As someone who's been on the London Eye it's very hard to believe that it's larger than it. The pods are definitely smaller than the ones on the London Eye. Other than that the military discount is cool and the views are great! Option of an open bar is pretty cool as well.

Breathtaking view of Vegas from the top. I think it's worth paying few extra bucks for the ride in the evening as that's when Vegas is at its best. All the glitter and glamor of Vegas can be seen in one glance down your trolley. You can sip a cocktail from the high roller bar while soaking in all that Vegas has to offer. Definitely recommended.

Tip: the view of strip is much better than that of the other side, so stay closer to the door when you enter for a better view, specially if the trolley appears to be crowded.

Had a blast! And we got a groupon deal! Sweet! Do yourself a favor and get open bar. Had about 3 or 4 drinks each and they allowed us to carry on our Fat Tuesday drinks. In retrospect that is a lot of alcohol in a very short period of time. Lord don't listen to me  maybe you shouldn't get open bar lol. Bartender was fun and made decent mixes for being on a Ferris wheel. Just tell him what u like. To bad I don't remember his name. (Or much of anything for that matter) It wasn't top shelf but it def wasn't bottom shelf alcohol. (Ex. Absolute) 30 minute ride. Goes pretty quick but time flys when ur having fun lol. Don't worry about height fears or anything like that. You literally don't even know you are moving. No rocking or anything like that. There was about 12 or so people in the cart comfortably.Go at night ,daytime seems boring. They gave us bogo coupons to the bar on the way out which we used. Drink was really good and the bartender was cool shared some local advice with us. 

I guess it's pricey without a groupon. We paid 70 bucks with open bar for two with our deal. Not sure the regular price but it's worth it. Great experience!
Fun view of the city, we had the whole thing to ourselves & the kids loved it- pretty much a private party 420 ft above the strip. Good locals pricing.

Review for Happy Half Hour Day experience: our group decided to take part in the happy half hour at the Groupon rate which was reasonable and gave us no trouble when we got there.

There was no big line to get into the attraction except when you get outside to actually get on the High Roller, even then the line moved quickly. It's actually only when you are about to get on you notice that the wheel doesn't stop rotation and you literally have to hop on, which is pretty cool and questionable since we were hopping on to drink!

Now to the nitty gritty, I gave a three because the person I saw the most, Phadrah (however you spell it) the Bartender heavily negatively impacted my experience. I understand she has a job to do but from the beginning I could see she wasn't about being a Bartender just wasting my time. Note this cab can hold up to 40 people so it should be imperative to provide SPEEDY AND FRIENDLY service. If I could call her out her name I would because I felt she put Bartenders to shame and at the same time tried to prevent me from getting the most out of the deal. I've worked in customer service and been a patron to many a bar and not once still I feel she even cared if I was having a good time much less if I felt thirsty. I was basically on the verge of making my own drinks, but stuck to mainly beer so that I wouldn't have to heavily rely on her service. And when we got towards the end she didn't even have the courtesy to do a last call, she simply started talking about how much it was to privately rent it out (really, do we look interested!) and to focus on a video of how the High Roller was built, that she never even put on.... Then to top if off she was giving side eyes before we left with the biggest attitude when a few of us tried to get our last drink before we left (Keep your feelings at home! Don't bring them to work!) 

Keep in mind, the views were great and probably would've been better at night but given that I actually drink during Happy Hours I would be a little concerned for my safety during the night ride since you have to jump off at the end. But Overall, a good experience and meeting new intoxicated people is hilarious as well !!!!

Now I can say I've been on the largest ferris wheel in the world! (:

Bought the LivingSocial deal for $25/person which includes a 30 min ride & "happy hour" which means all you can drink open bar!  Whats not to love about that?!

The only thing the LivingSocial deal doesn't tell you is that the tickets are FIRST COME FIRST SERVE!  Wish I had known that because my boyfriend and I sped walked from Cosmo to Linq within 15 mins only to find that they were SOLD OUT!! 
*WORD OF ADVICE* purchase your ticket early and come back later when it's time.

Each pod holds about 10-15 people and there are some with and without the bar. The ride is 30 mins but it goes by QUICK, especially if you're drinking inside.  The view was a bit disappointing but I should've expected it since the ferris wheel is placed behind the strip overlooking a ton of garages & parking lots.  Nevertheless, still a good photo op!

If you purchase the deal with the "all you can drink", you will find yourself your own personal bartender inside the pod with you.  Best part is, the drinks were STRONG!  Just name your drink & he'll make it for you--but don't forget to tip!

Within 30 mins, my boyfriend and I managed to get 3 Jack & cokes, 2 Pineapple Vodkas, 3 shots of whatever he poured us at the end and a can of beer.  Not bad ;)

This really is just a one-time thing but it would be fun for a pregaming event if you have a big group with you!

I waited for the Groupon before I went on this, 'cause it's pricy. $69 for admission for 2 with either flex pass (go day/night whenever you like) or Happy Half Hour (open bar for the duration of your trip, weekdays only). It also comes with a 20% off food at Brooklyn Bowl, a free polaroid at the Polaroid store, and 15% off any item in the gift shop.

First thing I noticed: everyone here hates their job. The bag checkers could not have cared less about us. I showed my Groupon voucher and the girls says, "Sorry, I need to see the ticket." I was like...okay, isn't this a ticket? And she sighs and huffs and puffs and says, "NO, a REAL ticket. Go to the concierge." Cryptic and rude! But we went to concierge next to the Brooklyn Bowl and got real tickets printed out and were finally allowed in.

It's a long, long windy path up to the actual High Roller. There's a set of green screens against a wall and some "photographers" who basically push you up against the screen, click two pictures, and hand you a ticket without even looking at you. I was really shocked! I gladly would have payed for my picture if it hadn't been so hurried and awful. This is a MONDAY NIGHT, mind you, with NO LINE. They aren't busy, and they just don't care. Terrible customer service.

Finally get there to the loading deck. From my understanding, there are bars in each compartment with bartenders and all. Turns out there's just a small rolling beverage cart they throw in there with a bartender and squeeze a rather large amount of people in one car. Not a lot of seating, which was uncomfortable. Bartender was very friendly.

There's video screens up top of the car that are supposed to give an "interactive experience". They don't. They just let you know what elevation you're at and give a small HOORAY! when you reach the pinnacle. The view is pretty, but not worth what we spent. I was ultimately disappointed with the whole experience. Better customer service, please!

Pretty cool view of the strip at night. They do tell you when you are at the apex of the ride so you can take pictures. 
For me it's a check off the bucket list cuz there's no point in going again

I've been on this ride twice, once at night and once during the day.  Both views were great.  The evening trip was in the bar car with music playing, everyone was in a good mood it was so much fun.  Loved it! 
The views are awesome! You go slow enough that you don't even know you are moving.  Great for taking photos of the strip and the entire city. Can't wait to go back!

Admittedly there are great views up near the top.  We were in a pod with about 12 total so there was lots of room to move around but there were usually people standing against the windows where we wanted to take pictures so we had to wait till they were done to get a photo ourselves.  Tip: stand on the side facing the strip when you get in, which is right when you get in the doors.  And as others said it is not a scary ride at all.  The biggest issue was the price. We went up at night and it was $36.95? per adult. pricey for a half hour ferris wheel ride.  Don't think I'd do this again.

This ferris wheel is good one time experience if you're out in Las Vegas especially at night where the view is nicely lit up. We got the happy hour 30 minute open bar tickets and my goodness the price is just ridiculous for the actual ride. The open bar cost $15 dollars more and if you casually drink your beverage you get around 3 rounds that's $5 dollars a drink and the bartender expect you to tip either after the ride is over or while you're getting your drink as our bartender told us after reading off the specialty drinks ending it in "i just ask for is you guys to take care of me by giving me a little something in my tip jar." 

All in all it's a good experience for a one time thing as the wow factor to come again isn't worth it for the price.

Find tickets ahead of time and else where!!!
 I had found some tickets online for 30$
 but we weren't going to go afterall.

 On the last night in Vegas we decided to go 

We ended up finding a girl standing outside in a green shirt saying she had tickets 40% off they weren't. 
They were only 2$ cheaper. We each paid 50$ for a night ride on open bar it was nice.... 

 I did some math and 3 drinks at a bar I went to the day before was 40$ so I guess drinking 5 drinks on the ride paid off my ticket??? This is me trying to convince myself it was a deal....



It's Hella expensive... sure it's cool but honestly I think the day ride with the open bar is cheaper.... only if u want...

I got this free from a friend.  It's basically a very very slow Ferris wheel that oversees the strip.  It's good for first time tourists to go on I guess to take pictures.  For picky people like me I would not go on this boring thing again... it's just too slow and you can oversee the strip for free on top of stratosphere.

Nothing but great experience on the high holler, took my family and my girl friend last year on the high roller were I did surprise proposal for my girl, and asked her if she would marry me!

I got a private room, with a full bar just for me and my family. (Pricey to get a private room) got to pay for all the people missing the spots. 

Got pre-drinks in the lobby with the Fam, took photos, then up we go. I had the bartender make us drinks, he was aware of what was going on since I told him. So he made lots of good drinks while we are slowly rollin to the top, Once we got all the way to the top I pop the question with the ring and asked her to marry me! It was a great experience, great view, and full of joy.
It was on her birthday, she had no clue and idea what was about to happen lol. 

Lets say I don't remember the other half of rolling down part lol.

Thanks high roller

Its worth seeing, but its pretty expensive! IF you do the open bar package, make sure you're there with friends OR your there on a day where its less packed or else you'll be sharing a ride with a lot of other people which doesn't allow you to get much bang for your buck.

Super fun experience! We've gone twice, during the daytime and once at night. 

The pods are spacious and air conditioned (thank goodness!) and there is a video that plays while you're going around that tells you how high you are up and some other fun Vegas facts.

There are seats in the pod in case you prefer to sit. It's not a herky-jerky ride, you barely realize you're moving. I'm not a fan of heights, but I never felt uncomfortable at all. 

I'm glad we got to experience the ride twice because it's fun at night to see all the lights, but nice during the day to see the mountains and surrounding Vegas area that you might not normally get to see. 

If you're staying at Harrah's and are in their rewards program, they give out free drink passes and discounted tickets. Family members of ours were staying at one of those properties and hooked us up for the daytime ride!

I had a great time on the High Roller Sunday afternoon. I was in town for a long wedding weekend from San Diego and had purchased tickets for the High Roller on Groupon for $65 for 2 for daytime happy hour.. Had also bought them on a day where groupon had a 20% code and I had $5 in groupon bucks so I only paid $47.. Totally worth it! It was so awesome seeing Vegas from that high up. 

Our bartender was really good and entertaining too. I don't remember her name but she was a cute African American girl and was very sweet. She gave us some history about the High Roller and how long it took to get built and how much it would cost to rent a pod out for the night etc.. It would be so much fun to rent out for a Birthday party or NYE! I guess people have actually gotten married on it which would be cool but I believe only 18-20 people can be on it at once. We heard some very funny stories of stuff that has happened on one of these pods.. Craziness! 

The last time I was in Vegas about 2 years ago the High Roller wasn't quite done being built so I'm really glad I was able to experience it this time. I would definitely recommend going on the pod with a bar.. I could see it being somewhat boring without it.. Only 2 of the pods have a bar I believe. Was able to take some really cool pictures and video during our 30 minute ride.. And was able to get in 3 beverages making the price I paid completely worth it.

The High Roller holds the Guiness World record for being the tallest Observation Wheel. It is 550 feet with 28 pods that holds upto 40people. My friends and I went there on a Tuesday. They had half off tickets for the local. One of my friends told us to go right at sunset for the best view and low and behold he was right. The 30 mins ride went by so quick as we observed the panoramic view, conversed, took bunch of pictures. Every minute the color of the sky changes with the Bellagio fountain turned on. It was a breathtaking view. The movement is slow and the height was not scary at all to me. As it was descending, I heard one of my friend say " is that Mindy from Mindy Project?" Sure enough it was her, she was about to get on the Pod. She was being photographed and the bar was rolled inside the Pod. Later found out it was her indeed and it was her birthday and she was there with another female celebrity. We had a fabulous time!

I had the pleasure of being able to experience the Highroller view during the day AND night! Both are amazing, MUST see views when in Vegas. I did the happy half hour option both times which I believe is totally worth it and so much fun! Unlimited cocktails of your choice while riding the 30 minute ride. I had a great experience both times and would recommend for anyone visiting Vegas.

I've been to Las Vegas many times over the years, but had never heard of the High Roller before my visit late last year. 

The most important thing to know is that this ride is soo much more delicious with a deal. Why pay full price for a 30 minute experience when you can buy a half priced deal on Groupon/Living Social? I had a lot of fun on the High Roller, but mostly because of the great deal we got. And also because I am the champion of any open bar, and was able to get about 8 drinks in before we landed. 

The view from the High Roller is amazing. I loved the idea of having a 360 degree view, so that it didn't matter where you stood, you could see everything! The ride goes super slow, so there is plenty of time to soak everything in. 

I enjoyed myself. Would I do it again? Possibly. It's a nice change of pace from lots of other activities you can partake in on the Strip. But then again.. there are a lot of other fun activities to partake in! It is definitely worth trying out once, though.

Get the happy hour deal. You get a cabin that has a bar and bathroom! The bar has unlimited drinks. Our bartender Phaedra was a blast. She showed us all the highlights as we traveled around the ferris wheel. Happy hour deal was around $30 a ticket.

Nice way to see the city, especially at night. I was a little disappointed that when you get to the very top of the wheel most of the Strip is STILL obscured by the closer hotel buildings in the foreground, but what you can see is still worth the trip up. Try to go on a weekday so you don't have to fight other riders crowding up to the windows for the best views. Great for kids!
As a local one of the reasons I enjoy going to The Strip is for the high roller!  They also provide a discount for locals.

I went in the afternoon with the full bar.  Spectacular views.  You could see the fountains going off at the Bellagio ( goes every 15 min)....since the ride on the link is 30 min you are guaranteed to see the fountain show.
Our bartender was really friendly and the bar was open.

I had made reservations on Expedia for the night before, but didn't get over there.  I went the next day and the staff honored my ticket which they didn't have to do and I really appreciated it.  All the staff is very friendly.

The ride never stops so you walk on and off while it moves, but since it goes so slowly there is almost imperceptible movement as the ride goes up to the top.

I want Togo back at night.

I consider this a must do item on a trip to Las Vegas.
Had a great time!

Best way to pre game and try something new/see a view? Go on a Happy Hour ride!
Make sure you check groupon/other sites for deals! $35 for all you can drink for 30 minutes and 1 to go!

Came here during the night with 2 friends using a groupon and a living social deal, we each paid $35. This was going to be our pregame before a night of clubbing so we drank, A LOT.

We had 2 patron shots (not silver though), 1 cosmo, 1 margarita, and 1 margarita to go. However, I was done after all of this and had to go back to the hotel :( No clubbing for me that night. And yes, they can give shots!

The view: Meh, it's fun to do if you've never done it before, but I probably won't do it again. There wasn't any music in the ball, it was mostly advertisement for the high roller and info about it.

Pro-tip: If you're gonna come in here and get 1 beer, skip the happy hour and take a regular one please? More room for us people who are trying to get our money's worth in drinks :p

This was definitely a fun experience. The entire thing was very well-run and coordinated by the High Roller staff. The bar they have is kinda cool too, but I usually don't mix alcohol and heights. The view you get of Las Vegas from the very top is unbeatable, and I definitely recommend going at night. The cars have cool little screens around the top showing you your progress and your height off the ground as well (although the corny narrator guy takes away from this slightly). You can bring cameras with you, just remember to turn your flash off! Overall an awesome time - highly recommended.

Rode the high roller yesterday afternoon. Took advantage of the happy half hour deal and enjoyed cocktails on the ride. There were only 4 people on our trip but it can hold 25. Great views of the strip! Even got to see the bellagio fountains. Night ride would probably be a sight with the lights!

Las Vegas High Roller im Vergnügungskomplex The LINQ

Wow, was für eine Aussicht ...
... aus dem derzeit mit 167 m, höchsten Riesenrad der Welt. 

Wir hatten eine einzigartige Sicht direkt auf den Las Vegas Strip mit seinem Lichtermeer, wie aus einem Helikopter, einfach einmalig. Sollte man unbedingt wahrnehmen, wenn man schon hier in Las Vegas ist. 

Unsere Empfehlung, auch wenn es abends mit ca. 37$ etwas teuer ist, als tagsüber mit ca. 27$, sollte man den unvergesslichen Ausblick in der Abenddämmerung oder bei Nacht, genießen.

Das Rad hat 28 Gondeln für je 40 Passagiere (in unserer Gondel waren wir mit 8 Personen) und braucht für eine Umdrehung etwa eine halbe Stunde. 

Durch die Größe der Gondeln und die kaum merkbare Fahrt, sind Schwindelgefühle oder Übelkeit durch die Höhe, aus unserer Sicht nicht befürchten. Auch das Einsteigen in die Gondel (sie ist ständig in Bewegung), ist durch die Größe kein Problem, wenn man nicht gehbehindert ist.

Wir haben es auf jeden Fall nicht bereut und können diese Attraktion hiermit weiterempfehlen. 

Ps. Das größte Riesenrad Europas steht in London und hat 135 m.

The best thing about this ride is that the kids are free. Smart choice. We went at night, so the views were great. Except that the other group kept hogging the corner with the better view of the strip. I would go again.

Free kids admission under 12 years old.  $53 for the family in the daytime.  (Daytime was actually really cool, to see mountains/panorama, etc.)

Video is pretty lame.  (We did enjoy the 420 reference, good on them for putting in a stoner reference.)  

We are definitely going to come back for the $30 happy hour experience.  Tip the bartender $20 to pour quickly and make them sorry they offer such a deal, as we will annihilate that shit.
Loved this! Awesome views of Las Vegas! There's even a bar where you can get your cocktails before boarding.  This is a must-do as part of your Vegas experience.

Try it!  The ride is gentle, taking ~30 minutes per revolution.
The views are spectacular and 360 at that!
If you can, go for the "happy hour".  For $10 more you get free drinks of your choosing.  Love the adjacent Promenade.

If you're all about views... this is the place. But for the price - Only one time is good.

$40 general admission gets you the following:
- About 10  people in one pod all together
- Seats are available but people tend to stand around
- Windows with finger prints all over

But, once you're on top... you feel your legs shaking a little.

We took a ride on the High Roller to end our evening and it didn't disappoint.  The skyline was beautiful and it's a great way to see the entire strip from the best view possible.  This excursion was a gift from my mother & I know she mentioned purchasing them through Groupon because they gave a better deal then going directly through Linq.  The open-bar option, which we did, was super neat.  The bartender was also from the Midwest, so he knew a lot about where we were from.  He poured three or four rounds of shots for everyone, not including our mixed drinks.  They had a wide selection, more than I thought they would, on an individual pod and he kept the momentum up.  Everyone was talking by the end of the 30 minute ride and we met some really neat people.  I don't think I would do it again, because once you've seen it you've seen it, but I would highly recommend!
