I'm in a giant pod in the sky! I actually had a dream I was riding this one night before it opened... We got to ride before they officially opened! Hunnie Bunnie was thrilled she got to finally ride it AND ride it before her cousin! 
DEFINITELY wait to go at night time so you can see all of the pretty lights over the Valley! Not even worth it during the day.
Before you get on they take your photo which has different backgrounds for you to choose from after your ride. 
In the waiting area you can purchase cocktails. 
There are benches inside the pod, but otherwise there is plenty of standing room and room to walk around.
There is music and there are TV monitors but nothing was playing when we were riding. 
I think my one ride will be enough for my life.

Great view & a must do at least once! It is pretty pricey but we got a black friday deal so it was reasonable. We did the happy half hour at night. For the half hour ride you have unlimited drinks- there is a bar inside certain pods.

The pods move slowly & you get on/off while it's moving. They view at night was great & we happened to be up there when the bellagio fountains were dancing!

Breath taking views of the Strip. We went right at sunset so we got to see the strip lit-up at night. There was about 12 people in our bubble, any more would be getting crowded. It is pretty high. I'm afraid of heights and it's kinda scary. I'm glad I did it, face your fears...

i went tonight and it was not crowded at all except they put my family and I with 3 drunk guys who where loud and annoying. the pod has 8 screens (4 on each side) playing the same video which is a bit too much. also, the music and videos were way too loud for such a small place. the view was only good when you got to the top, the rest of it is parking lots and roofs of buildings, which really disappointed us :( also, every single employee that we ran into had an attitude! overall, the pods are clean and air conditioned which was the only good part. this was a one time thing and i wouldn't do it again, plus it's waaaay too overpriced :(

Got complimentary tickets to come to the high roller ferris wheel. Surprisedly the lines or the wait wasn't that long. Usually the price is 39.99 for one ticket but they were having a black Friday special. 39.99 buy one get one free. Kids under 12 are free and they don't have a height limit. While walking up to the highest point to reach the ferris wheel there are people who take a few photos and there is a bar. You can order drink and bring it in the ferris wheel. The ferris wheel was very spacious. It's has 8 tv inside. The ride was 30 minutes long. Overall it was a beautiful inside and out. The views were amazing at night time.

Das aktuell größte Riesenrad der Welt steht nun in Las Vegas. Besonders am Abend ist die Aussicht grandios. Wir hatten das Glück,  an einem Mittwoch Abend mit nur 4 Personen in einer Gondel zu fahren. Die Fahrt dauert 30 Minuten und wir konnten den Luxus der leeren Gondel nutzen und in alle Richtungen sehen und uns frei Bewegen. Ich empfand das als echtes Plus! 
Der Rundumblick auf die Straßen, die prächtigen Casinobauten und die Wasserspiele vor dem Bellagio ist es definitiv Wert. Daher Merke, wenn man die nicht ganz preiswerte Fahrt machen möchte, sucht man sich besser einen Wochentag, an dem in LV üblicherweise nicht so viel los ist. Die Preisgestaltung kann man etwas beeinflussen, diverse Internetseiten bieten nutzbare Coupons an. Das Riesenrad hält nicht an, es bewegt sich, zwar langsam aber spürbar, sodass man beim Ein- und Aussteigen schon beweglich sein sollte. Es werden spezielle Bar-Gondeln angeboten, wer es möchte soll es probieren. Mein Fahr- und Aussichtserlebnis auf die Lichter der Stadt war ausgezeichnet. Was mich stört war am Ende der unvermeidliche Souvenirladen, durch den man geschleust wird. Nunja, so ist Vegas halt.

My tip for the High Roller is to get the tickets at the discounted price as they bundle them with other shows. They are significantly cheaper then and you can also get them as flex tickets meaning you can go during the day or night. It was a wonderful experience and getting to see Vegas from that high up was truly amazing. We went around 10pm on a Sunday and there was really no one else in the pod with us so we got to freely explore every angle. Only thing that stops this from being a 5 star review is that I have no desire to ride on the High Roller again. If there was something to keep bringing me back then my rating would be higher. While nice during the day, it is more impressive to view the city lit up at night.

Great deal for "All you can Drink" pod. Awesome views, countdown when you get to 550'. Now you only have 30 minutes to slam, all you can slam. Need I say more. Double shots of Patron were awesome!! Try it, it's worth it and fun!! They take your photo at the beginning which blinds you for a minute but all worth it. You can purchase the photos at the end, which we did. You need to move quick to get on and off so wear flat shoes, not heels. No worries though, there is a net underneath, just in case!

It's great for kids in the regular pod, but remember, you will be in there for 30 minutes and there is only so much room!!
We went on a Saturday night and let me tell you this is the Best ride.  30 min's long and it was awesome.. you have to go...

I've gone on the High Roller a couple times. Always had a fun time. Went with a couple dates and another time took my dad after a night of drinking in Vegas. Great views and plenty of time to get pictures. Definitely recommend going at night so you can see Vegas lit up the way it is intended to look. 2 out of the 3 times I went i did the VIP option with a drink cart included. Can't go wrong with unlimited drinks. Both times the bartender on board was a great host. I will for sure be going back

Drop dead gorgeous view surrounding your 30min ride. It's about 36 bucks pp if you want to experience this at night. I purposely chose the very last ride at 1:30am so we could hit up several lounge before ended up in this 'bubble'. Staff were friendly, only three other people in this ride at the same time, perfect!  Don't expect to be going semi fast cuz it's not...VERY slow. It's romantic. Have to be back to check out the Linq...looks really cool, updated spot on the strip.

I participated in the happy half hour on the high roller during the evening and it was a blast! The bartender comes into the cabin with a roll away bar and serves you whatever you'd like for the half hour. The views of the city were breathtaking and even if u don't like height you can enjoy this ride because they have seating on the inner part of the cabin so you aren't too close to the glass!

I purchased a ticket for The High Roller Wheel on March 2, 2015. We were given the option to ride it for $25 or to purchase the open bar for $30 (the ride with your personal bartender). My two siblings and I decided to purchase the open bar ticket. We were refused service after one drink while the other guest were able to order three and four. We never once displayed a belligerent or intoxicated demeanor. This is nothing more than a classic case of age and race discrimination. When we asked why we couldn't we order another drink the barmaid Sheryl tells us because we ordered straight shots we were unable to order more.Yet, there were older Caucasian guests who ordered shots who were able to get 3 or 4 drinks with no questions asked. At no time was this explained when we purchased the ticket or explained in writing on the receipt. Open bar simply means drink as much as you want or at least two drinks. Once the ride ended we asked to speak with a manager to get a refund, the Director of Operations, James Donahue, refused to hear us out and would not let us get a full refund. This situation completely ruined our first experience of the High Roller and put a damper on the rest of our Las Vegas experience. What happened to customer service? Isn't the customer always right?

An hour before sunset, we starting walking to The Linq to ride The High Roller. It was a 15-20 minute relaxed walk from Elara to The Linq. A promenade of outdoor shopping, dining, and entertainment leads you to the focal point, The High Roller. There is a bar in the queue where you can order up your favorite drink to take with you on the ride. It is 550 feet tall and each cabin can hold up to 40 people. The 30-minute ride will show you views of the Las Vegas Strip and vicinity - Red Rock to the west and Henderson to the east. Due to the heavy cloud coverage, sunset was not seen, but it could be great on a nice clear day. The colors on The High Roller were red, white, and blue for Memorial Day Weekend.
Great views of the city! Also, the pods are not crowded at all. Even though it is pretty tall, you hardly noticed the ascent and descent. It is very smooth and subtle. Great experience!

This gives you are great view of the strip. I have only rode this at night and loved the views. There has never been a long line unless you are waiting for the Bar Pods because there arent that many of those. There is really no need to pay extra for the bar pod because you will pass a full bar when walking to the part where you get on so you can just buy your drink there. The ride is smooth, great music, and a celebration when you get to the top.

This was a fun experience! We went at night and the view was amazing!! Cabins were clean, drinks were good, and seriously, the view!! I did feel like the cabins could be upgraded a little. You're in the sphere for about thirty minutes and the seats are fairly cheap and uncomfortable. 

I bought the groupon, so all in a I paid $60 for two tickets and two drinks. Many reviewers feel this is expensive but I thought it was a fairly good value. Like most have said, I probably wouldn't do it again but it's definitely a must-try. Go at night. Can't beat that view.

Must try at least once. Keep an eye out for the fountains, on the strip, from the top. When you get done, there is a strip mall to walk through and get ice cream. A nice walk because all the stores air conditioning is keeping you cool as you window shop.

Got free tickets for happy hour for diamond aspiration from Harrah's.  We came around 10pm on Sunday. There was no line, prior to entering the high roller they take your picture with a green screen. 

I would have preferred if they had a fake high roller capsule where we get to stand in, and take a picture. Instead they just put any background with the green screen, didn't seem special to me, so we didn't purchase it. 

The ride lasts about 30 minutes.  When the doors opened, everybody that was lined up for happy hour and as lead into the cabin as quickly as possible.  Inside there is a bartender, and bar in the middle. 
He quickly checks all our ids after the door closes. 

I'm not a drinker, so he happily made something non alcoholic, those that drink alcohol had like 4 or 5 drinks within half an hour.  Heard that they have good quality booze too, not just the cheap ones. 

The views up here are quite outstanding, except I feel like you can get these views if you stay at a nice hotel on a high floor facing the strip.  

The downside is we had about 20 people in our cabin.  One side of the cabin has gorgeous views of the strip, while the other side has the city view, and a couple of hotels. So all 20 people are trying to squeeze onto one side to take a glimpse of the strip view.  When trying to get a selfie, it's hard because you have someone next to your shoulder. 
Other people would ask you to step aside so you are not part of their selfie. 

Since there was no line, I think they could have put like 10 in per cabin and waited for the next one. But hey its Vegas, time = money.  
Can't complain since I got it for free, those that paid, I hope they drank their share of $52.00 within 30 minutes.

The views from the High Roller are really nice. It is now the highest point in Vegas. Went on a Saturday in the daytime and there wasn't a line. We were able to just to right on in. We bought a deal online that gave us unlimited drinks on the ride. It take 30 minutes to make the revolution so you have 30 minutes to drink as much as you can. The bartender was purposely talking at certain points it seems to hold people back from ordering drinks. Sure it was a management thing and not her. All and all it was an enjoyable experience.

We purchased tickets online and walked right in 4 minutes before our scheduled time. We considered doing the Happy Hour tickets for a few dollars more, but I'm very glad we didn't. You walk through a bar area on the way in, and at the time we went, you got a free drink if you texted the number to vote for High Roller Best of Las Vegas in its category! Score-- Happy Hour for free!

Also, the Happy Hour car was super packed with nowhere to sit and our car was just us and 2 other couples, with ample seating. It gave us lots of room to take pictures without blocking anyone's view. 30 minutes is a little long and boring, no lie, but for my motion sickness' sake, I was glad it didn't go any faster. I felt fine even having a little drink, and the video of the guy speaking was hilarious, but probably just to Millenials like myself. 

This is fun, but honestly you can get the same views for cheaper if that's all you're after. They take a professional photo they put on different backgrounds on the way up and hope to charge you a lot of money for it at the end, but for us, it wasn't worth it.

Fantastic experience.  The views at all times and in all directions were fascinating.  The carriage was huge, and we were lucky during the day to not have to share with another group.  Friendly staff.  High prices :(.  But this is a MUST do when in Vegas.
nice size pods, kind of a long process from tickets to go on to ride, 10 mins at the top is the best part.

The best part of this ride was the Magnificent view of Las Vegas at night. Plenty of photo ops. The weird part was there wasn't a bar in the pods as advertised. There is a bar in the lobby but not in the pods. Its a 30min ride so it can get old quick. It is exactly what you would think it will be like.

The high roller was super fun and unique to do, however I felt it was over crowded and over priced. We couldn't get a military discount on night tickets which is lame, and overall it was just over priced. I gave this rating 4 stars because I did enjoy the attraction but I won't spend the money to go again.

Bought two tickets to the happy hour car and it was the best idea ever! We visit Vegas annually for Cinemacon. We walked right on with no wait on Sunday evening. Our bartender was extremely friendly and fun and even made sure we all had drinks to-go after. It winds up being a great deal when you add the happy hour to it! 
Our bartender knew how to take the best photos of us (as a professional photographer I was totally impressed by this!)
Would go again!

Highroller is a must do when you're in Vegas. The wheel moves slowly and takes 30 minutes for complete rotation. The most terrifying part was getting on and off the moving wheel. I am afraid of heights so it was hard to look out on the beginning but u do get use to it after a while.It was a great experience. My husband and I did both day and night
 The night view is absolutely beautiful but they are normally busy at night so u have to share a wheel, we shared with 2 wonderful and friendly couples. The day ride was nice too, (the city looks totally different during the day) so we had a wheel for ourselves which was nice. We bought drinks at the bar and enjoyed the ride. Both rides were nice experiences. Would definitely recommend this.

All I can say is that everybody has to experience this attraction at least once in their life! As a local yes we really don't go down to the strip and do these type of things unless some family or friends or in town, well hang on let me speak for myself lol I generally don't. I can't believe it's been up as long as it has and I'm just now getting to grab a ride! This was a nice spot to celebrate a portion of my significant other's birthday for sure! I went on the The Linq website and bought the tickets for the ride with the locals discount and open bar! I feel like if you are going to do it, you have to do it big! When you choose the open bar option you share the spaceship ball with whomever else bought tickets and chose to ride at that time as well. The bartender we had was amazing! Wish I remembered his name, but I think he made those drinks a little TOO good! For $90 for 2 people and all you can drink I actually feel it was a pretty good deal! Would I return? Possibly!

The high roller is at the end of a trendy row of casino and clubs. It's geared toward a younger crowd and has an outdoor club feel. The night time ride is $37 a person. It was not an amazing view since you see the parking lot in the rear of the area for most of the ride. There is a person who CEOs on the screen and explains what height your at and does a apex countdown. I would go once to say you've done it but it's not as fun as the bars on the ground.

Although it is a 30 minute ride, it is worth the experience. Share this with good company. I honestly suggest riding it during the night time; the view is prettier in my opinion :) they have a cabin with a small bar, however the drinks are limited :/ & if you're lucky, you'll drink about 4 by the time the ride is over, so Not worth the extra money. Just pre game :)

This is a must experience, my boyfriend and I went at night around 7 pm, we paid the upcharge to do the happy hour cart and it was so worth it. We really lucked up because we got our own cart, just happened that everyone else was going in the non happy hour cart (a lot of people seemed to be unaware that it was an option at any time of day/night) so it was just him, me, and our friendly/knowledgable bartender. We had unlimited drinks for the full 30 min trip and he even poured us a last one to go which was nice, we tipped him at the very end instead of per drink. Was really a great time, probably our favorite part of the trip, would definitely recommend.

The High Roller is a fairly new attraction to Vegas and is a GIANT ferris wheel with these really large pods that fit between 35-40 people each. My boyfriend and I got a Groupon for 2 all you can drink happy hour rides for $69. Not a terrible deal.

It was really easy to redeem the tickets and get our ride scheduled. I think we were the last happy hour pod of the night, so there were a decent amount of people, but I would say no more than 25-30. Kinda busy, but still plenty of room to move around. The bartender that was in the pod was pouring shots and making the drinks pretty strong. I had 3 and took another one to go when we were done, and I was feeling pretty good. 

This is a great option to get a nice view of the city, although you only get a good view for about 5-10 minutes of the entire ride. I'm sure if you don't have a Groupon and are going with like, a family, then this can probably get pretty expensive. So going to the Stratosphere may be a better option if you're wanting a good view of the city and don't want to pay an arm and a leg. But, definitely something that everyone should try once.

ラスベガスを一望出来る大きな観覧車です。(ロンドンアイのようなもの)
この日は、午後から突然の強風が吹き、それでも中止にならず運行していたので乗りました。(夜には砂嵐注意報がでました)家族単位で皆んな貸し切り状態で乗っている位ガラガラのお客さんの入り。

広い内部ですが、風で砂が舞い、曇ってみえるラスベガス、残念

しかも、風でドアがガチャガチャと動き、ある意味恐怖

普段は、綺麗はみえるようですので一度は乗ると楽しめると思います！

Attention: Review for only the HH package. 

Purchased the Groupon HH late night deal for $79 which sounds like a steal at first till you actually experience the ride. The ride and views themselves were amazing but issue you'll find is that there's only one bartender serving alcohol in 6oz cups for about 25 riders. This means by the time you're ready for that next cocktail, you'll be waiting roughly 10 minutes. Unless you're creative, realistically you're only going to receive 2-3 small drinks in the 25 minute ride (I timed it). So ask yourself, is it worth the extra cost for the HH deal? I would recommend you purchase non-HH ticket, bring your own drinks and direct your undivided attention to the breathtaking views versus trying to fight for the attention of the bartender.

My suggestion for High Roller personnel: I strongly recommend bringing up two bartenders. Our bartender was doing his best to cram all the orders in a timely manner but it was apparent that it was simply too many for one person to handle. This particular bartender was noticeably getting annoyed at the fact he was not getting many tips but what do you expect when it's taking roughly 10 min for the next drink? You tip for service and with one bartender the level of service was not there.

A group of friends and I went to the high roller last week and thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. The pod was very comfortable and our bartender, Cheryl, had excellent customer service skills! She was great with the whole crew. The views of Las Vegas from the pod are excellent and I highly recommend going just before 5 PM, which gives you a discounted deal and some awesome lighting for photos as the sun goes down. The mountains and cityscape are beautiful from up there! We had a great time!

We opted for the bar upgrade and it was awesome! We got a great look of the city while sipping on some cocktails. Definitely worth the money. I thought the bartender was not personable. He definitely didn't want to be there and told us we had to tip. We of course would have anyways but I didn't like that he said that to us. I give four stars only because the bartending service was a joke. At least we got a few drinks out of it :)

********************* 1120 *********************

         Shining bright on the Las Vegas Strip, the 550-foot-tall High Roller is the world's largest observation wheel. We were here for July 4th weekend, and the firework show on the strip was AMAZING. 

       This stunning Las Vegas attraction provides tourists and locals alike the ride of a lifetime.  The High Roller has 28 pods, Italian-handcrafted glass-enclosed cabins. 

        30-minute ride, the time it takes for the entire wheel to rotate,  with two benches for seating. Each stylish, modern-styled cabin holds up to 40 people. 

       There's also an adjacent wheelhouse that guests can reserve for private parties and banquets.
        
       The ever-changing colors are such a beauty and display a nightly glorious light show. The lights turn on starting at dusk and stay on until early morning. Lights range from bright pink, turquoise, purple, green and white, as well as color combinations, think of rainbow, so beautiful at night. 

      Ticket is $19.95 for day time and $34.95 at night time, totally worth it!

I went here during the summer and they seemed to care more about locals then. I enjoyed my experience the first time that I brought my family back when they came to visit for Christmas. Now the local discount saved me only $2 and they only allowed me to buy one ticket and not for my family. Will never recommend or bring back any family members again. The lady who checked me out gave me the explanation saying it's because the tickets are cheaper now. Hmmmmm ok! Cheaper for general people so let's make the prices higher for locals. Great strategy High Roller!!

The view at night is beautiful but the guy on the video is freaking annoying. Every 3 minutes, there some annoying thing he says. What if people want to view the city in the beauty of silence?! Not worth $36.
Went at night. Great view but overpriced. If you go before 6 it's about $15 cheaper but you miss out on the Vegas night lights. Try to get a seat on the immediate right for the best views.

This was a fantastic ride!  We did the Happy Hour, and got free drinks for our 30 minute ride.  We got to see all of Vegas at night and it was amazing.  We even got up in the air just in time to watch the Bellagio Fountains going off.  Gorgeous, gorgeous view, and the pods are pretty large enough.

No.  Here's why:

Even in the day they charge $50 for two people + $4 for the privileged of buying tickets (how corporations have conditioned us to accept this is beyond me (maybe they should start charging "wheel rotation fees" or or "safety fees.").  And what do you get for that $54?  30 minutes in a bubble with 40 other dopes getting a view you could get from tens of thousands of rooms in Vegas, not to mention just by having a drink in the Stratosphere Bar (which is 200' higher), or taking off from the airport.  And, of that 30 minutes, only a few of them are from the wheel's apex.

Rooms in Vegas are so cheap that that extra $54 (they charge $74 at night) would surely upgrade you to a room with a great view for 24 hours and without 40 other people.  On top of that, there's this comedian video screen thing playing in the bubble most of the time.  Some of it's amusing, but then it gets to the not-so-subtle advertising as when he tells us about how he loves the "amazing cupcakes at the Sprinkles shop" on The Linq or when the trivia game asks about the history of the Yard House restaurant (also, you guessed it, on the Linq).  Who cares?! The Linq, by the way, is just overpriced, slickly-marketed eats, bars, etc.

Then, of course, you get dropped off in the gift shop where they offer to sell you a $35 photo of yourself so you can always be haunted by the memory of what a schmuck you were.  

They're trying to sell this as some great experience.  It isn't.  Not in Vegas. It may have cost them a lot to build, and the engineering is impressive, no doubt.  And if it was located in an area where there was no other way to get the view, well, maybe it would be worth it, but in Vegas it's worth maybe $10.  Really.

Spend your $74 for a better hotel room or drinks at the Stratosphere  Wish I had...

I've been eyeing to go on this Ferris Wheel every since it was built.  I'm very happy that I got a Groupon for this because the prices are pretty outrageous for a 30 mins ride.  It's a pretty nice view of the Strip but on the other side it was just blah.  

I'm not the kind of person who gets motion sickness but the High Roller definitely made me nauseous because of how slow it was going.  Thank god I didn't puke because it would have totally stank up our pod.  Plus there was only the bartender, my bf and me in the pod so I don't have to worry about embarassment.  

Our Groupon was for the pods with an open bar and Reese was our bartender.  He was so much fun to talk to and very attentive drink-wise.  He made sure we took advantage of the open bar because the drinks kept coming.  

Would I do it again? Hell no.  I don't feel like getting sick again.  Was it a fun experience? Yes it was and I'm glad I did it.

It's a fabulous idea until somebody throws up in the pod. It's cool for a one-time thin but not life changing. We had an okay experience mostly because someone had thrown up earlier that day and the smell was still lingering. Also, it's only a 35 minute ride so the "all-you-can-drink" is not really that valuable.

Great time here! Wonderful during sunset time because you get to see when the Vegas lights are off and on. Fits 40 people and takes 30 minutes to go around. Very structurally safe. I'm not nervous for heights or anything but I did feel light headed up there. Worth going on. $24.99 during the day and $34.99 during the evening.

Arguably the best view of downtown Las Vegas. The tickets seem pricey but they are worth it. You won't get better day or night photos anywhere. This modern Ferris wheel provides a comfortable and extremely spacious seating area. Plus the video of the "host" talking during the ride is hilarious. Be sure to listen!

It was a fun experience. Leading up to the ride was a bar and then a spot to take photos  which can be purchased later. The entrance was lit with led lighting and music. Very lively atmosphere.

 The ride itself was 30 minutes and a really good view of the Las Vegas Strip. It's something you should do at least once. We will probably bring friends and family visiting from out of town. My kids really enjoyed it we had a private pod and they danced around to this music being played. 

The location at the end of the Promenade was great with plenty of choices of restaurants and quick deserts. We walked over to Caesars shopped and had dinner after our ride.There was some live entertainment, props for photos and a handful of impersonators. 

Tip. If you're a local USE your NV I.d. the discount was great. In addition children under 12 are free.

When to Vegas for my first time in March this year and I have to say I LOVED IT! We got on the high roller and we were able to watch the bellagio show from up above.. Gorgeous view at night..Paid about $70 for 2 people, seems pretty reasonable..

Fun experiemce! Beware that afterwards if you want to buy the photos they take before you get on the High Roller, they cost $35 for one photo pr $55 for three. 
Just go down to Photo To Go and take a picture in their 'Welcome to Las Vegas' cutout, get the first one free and the additional small sizes for $1 each. Theu have other sizes and types for other pricing.
Enjoy!

The only other "pod" Ferris Wheel I had been on before was the Millennium Wheel (I think they call it the London Eye now) back in 2004 and, despite the long line and hefty price, I was quite impressed with that ride. Amazing views of Big Ben and the rest of London overlooking the River Thames. 

So...when I found out the largest pod wheel in the world had recently been erected in Vegas...well, I had to go! My husband and I and another couple went at around 1 something a.m. after partying on The Strip all night. Good decision. There was absolutely no line. Walked right into the pod that was probably 3x the size of the one in London, with only 2 other people on board. Off we went. The High Roller moves soooooo slow you can't even tell you're moving. Very smooth. Yes, great views but actually had better views from our room at the Cosmopolitan that overlooked The Strip and the Bellagio Fountains. If only they could have put the wheel in a different location. Still a cool experience; however, once is enough. 


At $34.95 p/p plus tax and $9 draft beers each, it's a one time must do experience in Vegas...and/or fork out another 100 bucks per person and take a helicopter tour! Much better views and greater overall experience. [Review for Maverick Helicopters]

Before I started drafting my review, I was trying to think what I could write about, what was my major impression from my High Roller ride. I came up with a few ideas and when I read reviews posted by others on Yelp I saw a lot of the same comments I was going to make. So, I guess if many people (including me) are saying the same thing, then it must be true to some extent.

Overall, I like the experience. There were no lines. I think it took about 5-10 minutes to pick up our tickets, take pictures in front of the green screen, and get in the cabin. We wasted more time when we were trying to use ticket machine outside. Out of 4 machines (3 were out of order). We waited in line to use the only working machine but it actually went offline when people who were right in front of us tried to use it to purchase tickets.

As I said, there were almost no lines which is a huge plans. If you ever visited attractions anywhere in the world, you probably know that you can spend at least an hour waiting in line.

Our experience inside the cabine was alright. There were only a dozen of people inside so it wasn't crowded at all. I took a bunch of photos with my camera. Unfortunately, there is no 360 degree view at night. You can totally see the strip and certain developed areas of Vegas, but in general the side of the wheel opposite to the Strip is pretty dark and there is nothing really to look at night.

There was a video demonstration during the presentation that I thought was a little underwhelming. Although there was a certain educational element, but I expected to hear much more about Vegas, it's history, landscapes, attractions, etc.

Somebody said that the ride is "painfully boring". I disagree with this comment, but the last quarter of the ride feels a little slow when there is nothing else to see and everyone can't wait to get back on the ground. I think it can be fixed with a better video programming or perhaps even different sound track.

High Roller is not the tallest structure in Vegas. There are several hotels that are taller including Stratosphere tower, Trump, Encore, Wynn, etc. Thus if you want to get up high to see the Strip and other areas of Vegas, you don't have to go on a high roller ride.

The price is okay. It's Vegas, so you probably going to spend way to much money on things that you don't need. Therefore spending money on something that you will have long lasting memories about is not a bad thing.

Overall, I don't regret going there and spending money on the ride. Will I do it again? Probably not. May be I can do a day-time ride next time because I expect it to be slightly different experience. But I don't think I will go back for the night time ride. One time seems to be enough.

Last night I went to the high roller right before they were closing to purchase the last ride at the pay station (which wasn't working), we then found a high roller store that sold the tickets who wouldn't service us because we were a couple mins late. 
My family and I then came back the next afternoon, and purchased the tickets, only to find out they had technical errors. 
At that point I wanted to talk to the manager about the level of service we had experienced during that time (no one cared and didn't give a $h!t).  Caroline, the manager came out and had ZERO customer service. I explained to that we wanted to take our daughter here because we were leaving her for the summer and she's been wanting to go on this ride, we purchased drinks, took photos, but couldn't get on. 
The lady looked so dumbfounded, all she could say is "you and everyone else, what do you expect?!".  I let her know she had poor customer service skills. 
It's unfortunate how us customers spend money on expensive drinks, and the manager Caroline has no empathy. She ends up leaving, storms off and says "too bad you feel that way". Sandy was the only rep there that understood (someone else should recruit her that values people). 
My husband and I were thinking about renewing our vows there, even spoke to someone about it....NOT ANYMORE!!  Get rid of Caroline, she's terrible for the business.

High Roller was really cool, though the video "tour guide" was a bit obnoxious and annoying. 

You pay $35 for a 30 minute ride on a massive ferris wheel. If you pay a bit more (and ask for it), you can do the happy hour car, which had I known about before we paid, I would have opted for that! It looked like if you wait for the happy hour car, you end up waiting a little bit longer. 

The view is really cool! I went at night, so all the lights were on, and it was quite impressive. I got a bunch of cool pictures, though the glass on the car is not flat, so there was some distortion, plus it was dirty so the photos look that way. 

Overall, I had a good time. Definitely a one time thing, though.

The staff that was working on the night of August 31, 2014 was extremely rude to us.  I am a very cautious and aware individual and as we approached the bag checking area I noticed that there was a couple getting rowdy and being obnoxious with the High Roller Crew.  While we were trying to take pictures, this same group of people was spilling their drinks all over the green screen and causing havoc at the bar area. So, based on the fact that I PAID for this experience, I did not want to ruin our unique occasion by being on the same observation cabin as that group. While we approached the staff as politely as possible about waiting for the next cabin or even going to the next waiting area the staff was extremely rude saying you can wait downstairs. Not realizing that she was just being sarcastic about the situation, implying that we could just leave.  Then "RACHEL THE SUPERVISOR" approached us in the most inappropriate and aggressive manner, immediately saying you need to keep it moving or I will call security.  If the experience to the High Roller was FREE, I could understand being treated with such disrespect.  Now i'm not sure about you, but if I am a paying customer of a business, I expect to be provided a service and If I see an oppurtunity to avoid a bad situation, I am gonna take it.  Throughout our entire vacation, we were infatuated with the oppurtunity to experience such an amazing landmark.  Unfortunately, RACHEL THE SUPERVISOR and her outstanding colleagues treated us with such disrespect and their failure to handle the situation has ruined our families entire experience at The High Roller. Thank you for the experience.

A must do while in Vegas, especially the bar car. The staff are slightly rude, at least they were on May 13. I was embarrassed for the bar tender who asked for a tip before having an opportunity to tip...Also, if you happen to be looking for a water fountain at the attraction, you won't find one, you have to buy a $7-8 dollar bottle (depending on who you ask) annoying stuff aside, great views of the strip, good music and fun time with friends

We went up on a clear afternoon - this 30 min ride was amazing. It's a great way to see the entire Strip. My husband hates heights but because each car is so stable you don't feel like you're up that high. Glad we spent the money to do this.

I bought my ticket thru Groupon and chose the happy hour option. Our bartender was great, had 5 drinks throughout my ride. The view at night was gorgeous, it was great seeing Vegas and the strip from a different angle.

We had a great time at the high roller. We came in during the weekday. We got in our cabinet fast. To top it off, we got our very own cabinet without sharing it with anyone else! 

They have a bar there, so you order a drink or two before heading to the high roller. The view was beautiful; it's about half hour long. We also brought our stroller with no problem and kid had a good time at looking outside.

Open bar is a must on this.... the view is amazing once you get to the top of the wheel. If u go a little later u might be able to get ur own little pod in stead if being with like fifteen other people
The best way to end the night! Spectacular views of Vegas. They need to work on their service at the bar. Literally one person working and she was moving so slow we almost gave up.

Come here late at night. Less crowds so you'll have a good amount of room to move about the cabin. Sure, you might not get to see the vast wastelands of the desert surrounding Las Vegas, but in my opinion, it's totally worth the trade off. 

Here's my real complaint though: the price. You're looking at between $40-$50ish dollars depending on where you buy tickets for 2 people. That's insane. The only reason why my wife and I went was because we got comped tickets. If it wasn't for that, there's no way we'd do anything but laugh at those prices.

Also, what's with the 'comedy routine' the video host does the whole time? How about you just let us enjoy our ride & save that stuff for open mic night. Sorry, I just thought it was a horrible attempt at being funny.
Overpriced. You do get a nice view of the strip, but again, overpriced. You'll do this once, and probably will never do it again.

Nice way to observe how big las vegas is ...
Buy your drinks before or get in plastic cups...
So ñ e of the employees highly motivated other search az ND tire of the same shit...
I been there few times.. I can understand lol

This is a Terrible ride I have even have. My friend and I we were in a group of 11. And the worker there have set us in a group with other group together. But at the end my friend daughter went in first then the worker stop my friend they say is to the limit already tell him to take the next one my friend daughter is only 5 year old. They fxxking left a 5 year old kid alone with bunch of stranger and won't stop and let the ride still go. This is the most terrible experience I even have. And it hear from other passenger told me there have been a lot of malfunction to the ride. The door close itself without wait for all passenger in etc ... Did any one have the information where it can file a compliant to the head Office please advise.

We got our tickets on Groupon, which I highly suggest because regular priced tickets for the LINQ are just ridiculously high. We came around 10 pm on a Sunday on Fourth of July weekend and it was pretty empty. They allow drinks in the observation wheel which are available for purchase in their lounge which is on the way to the observation wheel.

They have like 8-10 seats available in each cabin so if the wheel is packed, be prepared to stand for 30 minutes.

The view is beautiful, even though you can only see half of the Strip. You cannot see anything past the Venetian. 

It barely feels like it is even moving so for those of you scared of heights and whatever else, don't be. 

The windows in each cabin are beyond dirty so taking pictures is kind of a waste, but possible.

Tip:
The wheel stays in operation even when it rains.

Overall I'm glad I got to go on the highest observation wheel in the world, but I won't be back. This is kind of a once in a lifetime experience so I highly suggest everyone does it once.

This was so fun! Get a deal off of groupon or travelzoo. We went around dinner time so it was just my friends and I on our pod. We did the happy hour half hour and it was well worth the money. So fun! you pay pretty much just for the drinks and get a gorgeous view of the strip!!! I'd do this again for sure

Great views and lots of fun but, the "open bar" was anything but. Not worth the extra money for open bar and here is why. We had 20 people in our cab and 1 bar tender. It took nearly the whole ride to serve one drink. And bud and coors light for beer selection.

Okay so I found that the key to this thing is riding it at just the right time. This past Sunday we took family in town around noon. We walked right on and we had our own pod. I am not sure why it is so popular at night? The days are much better and you can see farther and much more sites. It was a beautiful day and a much better experience. We took our 2 and 4 year old with us and they had a ball. If we had gone at night I don't think we would have brought the kids.

I only paid $20 for two people!    So...my 12 year old son and I were walking past the Flamingo on Christmas night, there was a  High Roller gal outside selling "ladies night" tickets, 2 people for $20 and included a drink ticket.  That was a deal!  Not only did I avoid the line in front of the ride, I only had to pay $20 AND we got a free drink (more like a mango slushie).  It was really cool, the views were fantastic and it wasn't so crowded in our pod that we couldn't see from the various sides.  I'd like to try it during the day time too.  I have height issues but I didn't feel them in here.  It is a very smooth ride.

Great experience! One of the nicest view and you get to see everything in Vegas but from a much better perspective. Definitely worth going at least once just to experience it. I would recommend going later before closing to avoid the crowd. I mean, it is about 30 minutes of ride with limited seating... The best seat in the house is the right seat you see after entering.

This was the "high"light of our Vegas trip!  Buy your tickets online for the best value- we saved $7 per ticket this way.  It also lets you skip the line outside and you can literally buy it online just before you walk in.  Once you get to the ferris wheel itself, you'll get into a cabin with perhaps 20-30 other people if you go at a peak time.  We chose to go on a Monday night, so it wasn't crowded and we got lucky- only 4 other people in the entire cabin with my wife and I!  The ride lasts 30 minutes and gives you amazing views of the Strip and surrounding areas.  There are a few tv's in the cabin and a "guide" that pipes up occasionally to tell you some interesting facts and try to keep you calm in case you're afraid of heights.  An amazing experience and well worth the money.

5 Stars all the way!  High Roller is 30 minutes of spectacular 360 degree views of Las Vegas and the valley floor, mountains.  The BEST time to ride is anytime after Dark.  Why? You get to see all the colorful lights of all the casinos, the strip, entire City; and, the water show at the Bellagio when seen from 500+ feet above is beautiful. 

The pods are ultra comfy, nicely air conditioned.  There's nice music piped in.  There are 2 pods that have full bar service aboard.  For $70 you can ride this pod and have drinks unlimited for the entire ride.  I must say, my husband and I will ride this pod next time.  :))).  

It's said that 40 people fit in the pod; however, it's less than 40 that enter.  You are definitely not sardined in. It's a very comfortable and roomy ride. 

You can't come to Vegas and not High Roll on the High Roller.  It's definitely the bees knees of Vegas to me :)))

Cheers to High Roller!!!

We hopped on the happy hour or should I say half hour.
But its ok any longer and i wouldn't have been able to walk out on my own. Well worth the price. Our bartender was great and poured as much as you can handle. Night time happy hour I'm sure has a prettier view with the lights of the strip but still was nice.

Such a fun way to ring in a birthday. I highly recommend the drink cars. You'll be happy you took my recommendation, the drinks are great. Our bartender we had that night was from New York, great guy. He makes great drinks, especially his signature fruity drink. I could drink those all day in Vegas. The only reason for a 4/5, not enough options in liquor/drinks. They need to supply the bartenders with Ginger beer, I love myself Moscow Mules and I know a lot of other people do as well. Lastly be nice to the bartenders they put up with a lot of crazy drunk people, and they give you service with a smile, make sure to bring $5 or $10 w you to tip the bartender, cause they work hard.
So much fun and a great way to see the city lights! I highly recommend going at night. Las Vegas is beautiful. Although, I may be a little biased since I was born and raised there.

The High Roller is the signature attraction of the LINQ, first and foremost a shopping/dining/entertainment area with a hotel and casino shortly forthcoming. Measuring at 550 feet it is the world's tallest observation wheel, 107 feet taller than the London Eye. 28 cabins make up the wheel; up to 40 people can fit into one cabin.

PRICING: General admission pricing is as follows
1x Day (11:30am to 7pm) $24.95 / $29.95 in the Happy Hour (open bar) Cabin
1x Night (7pm to 2:30am) $34.95 / $44.95 in the Happy Hour (open bar) Cabin
1 Day ($44.95) and 3 Day ($54.95) passes to board with no time restriction BUT you are limited to one ride daily.
Supposedly there's a way to get cheaper tickets if you are a) a local, b) stay at the Quad or Flamingo or c) play at any Caesar's blackjack table and get a suited blackjack to get comped tickets.

LINE
The No1DP and I went around 11:00pm on a Sunday, which meant there was literally only 5-10 people in front of us and we only saw them as we were about to board. There is plenty of space to accommodate the line inside the building. With lots of line space there were several checkpoints - after No1DP bought our tickets we had to show our tickets to staff at least 3 times.

There's an opportunity to buy the adult smoothies while in line but I don't think you can bring those in the pods. There's also a photo opportunity where you can purchase photos after the ride but I declined to purchase ours as I looked too ugly in them.

PODS
-HAS AIR CONDITIONING. Trust me, this was much appreciated.
-Two small benches on each side
-Eight monitor screens on top with a cheesy yet entertaining announcer that informs you of the safety rules and various facts about the High Roller or Vegas itself.
-Keep in mind that pods are continuously in motion as you are being loaded and unloaded.

VIEW
The view was surprisingly much better than what we saw at a helicopter ride early last year. However if you are riding at night this doesn't translate to good photos. If you're using flash the glass will reflect it so there goes your chance to take a good view pic or selfie.

I'd recommend this attraction to Vegas visitors. No1DP and I thought it was worth the money but we would wait until later to avoid the lines!

vale la pena! en la noche es mas caro que en el dia pero son vistas muy diferentes. recomiedo la vista nocturna.  en cuanto a pagar por el open bar no creo que valga la pena almenos que anden super ambientados todos y tendrias que tomarte minimo 2-3 tragos para que salga el costo almenos que sean shots porque cuantos tragos te puedes tomar en 30 minutos que dura la vuelta completa??? de igual manera si se te antoja un tragon antes de subir hay barra-bar. asi como baños,... sube y acomodate entrando de el lado derecho donde se encuentra la mejor vista de las vegas! enjoy!

You can buy tickets online or when you get there. Around $50 each. But they do have deals living social Groupon , through casinos.... 

It was amazing. Very calm ride. Exciting. You see everything. I went at night and all the lights was just magical. 

Kids are free! 

Picture at the end kinda pricey , not the best quality. I had a thick stand of hair going across my face and he didn't say anything. Just took one shot. I guess it's good if you don't plan on buying the picture ... my dad still did but I don't like it.

Ooh, yeah...it's so James Bond.  I had the privilege of riding the High Roller about an hour after sundown for the very first time.  I enjoyed the digital host and trivia inside of "the bubble" that I rode in. Seating was comfy and the bubble is cozy and intimate without producing a sense of claustrophobia.  What a cool experience. High Roller is similar to the one in London. Staff is professional and friendly and of several Vegas attractions, the High Roller is actually the one worth paying for.  Invest in yourself by having the High Roller experience! Take your glass of champagne aboard the bubble and relax while enjoying breathtaking views and a very enriching perspective of the city.

Well this review is from someone extremely afraid of heights. I was goaded into going on by my husband and kids. Somehow I lucked out, one of the passengers in our pod used a scooter. They stopped the wheel so she could board, so I didn't have to walk in while it was moving. After the first 10 minutes it was very enjoyable, it never felt unsafe. I highly recommend doing this, the view was amazing. I'm glad I didn't chicken out. Thanks family  and a huge special thank you to the very nice lady with the scooter. Another great thing, if you are a Nevada resident admission is half price.

This was a fun outing.  We walked into pod 12, grabbed a seat, then enjoyed the view of the Strip, bathed in the dying light of day.  Unlike a ferris wheel, the High Roller's climate-controlled pods allow one to walk around and check out the views from whatever angle one wants.  It is difficult to discern movement at all, since the High Roller rotates so slowly.  The entire 30 minute revolution is accompanied by a virtual guide, projected onto the TV screens inside the pod.  (Lots of corny jokes!)  Apex of the ride is 550 feet.  Drinks and snacks available prior to boarding and are stupid expensive, but if that's your thing, then have at it.  Prices are $25/person during the day and $35/person at night (I believe "night" prices start at 7pm?).  If you can afford to go at night, that's when I'd go, as it's pretty cool to see the sunset and night lights of the Strip.

As a Vegas local, I'm always taking my out of town family and visitors onto the high roller, so I have been about 10 times in the past two years, and thought I had a great experience each time, but nothing compares to what prompted me to write this review... which is CHERYL. 
Cheryl was our bartender last night and she was amazing. She made us drinks we didn't even know we wanted! She was fun and witty and cute and I hope we get her pod next time when we go! We will be going again in about 7 days with new visitors!
Thanks Cheryl! 
-your Boston crew

Went on a Thursday night and only had our group of 5 and another couple in our pod, so had plenty of room to walk around.  One person in our group had a cane and they offered to slow the pod down even further for him to get on.  Great customer service right there.  They had a ladies night special for $19.99 which included a night ride and two cocktails.  Pretty good value.  Even though I live in Vegas I enjoyed the ride.  It was nice seeing the Bellagio fountain go off.

LOVE it!!! You can see everything from the atop the high roller. Well worth the price and so glad we did it. We went daytime and didn't regret it at all. I imagine at night the lights are brilliant but you wouldn't be able to see as far. Choose for yourself, but we loved it.

The highest ferris wheel in Las Vegas ,  it was so much fun.  The lines were fast ,  people were nice and polite,  the ride took 30 minutes .  The view of Las Vegas from way up so high was spectacular.

Very nice view, especially at night.

The engineering that went into this ride is amazing.

You can also brag that you have been up the largest ferris wheel in the world.

I don't know if it's a "must do" in Vegas given everything else you can do but it's definitely something to consider.

OK- Here is my "from a local" perspective on the High Roller

-It is a really cool thing to do, and should be done.

-Find a deal! LivingSocial, GoldStar, Vegas.com they are out there!

-Choose the ticket that includes the open bar "Happy Hour" I do not even drink, and a cabin full of people having fun is just more fun! Trust me on this one.

-Go at Sunset or after dark. Las Vegas is magical at night, and seeing it from this perspective is amazing!

Hope that helps, have fun!

The High Roller is the world's tallest observation wheel (however there are multiple wheels currently being constructed that will be taller when completed). When at its apex it is 550' tall and it offers a unique view of Las Vegas that can not be seen anywhere else.

Admission varies depending on the time of day you decide to ride, if you want to drink while riding and how you obtain your tickets. All you can drink 'Happy Hour' deals are available. Locals can get half priced tickets and non-locals can find deals on Groupon quite often. Discounts are also offered for military, guests of nearby hotels and for purchasing your tickets online. 

Before you board the wheel, there is an opportunity to purchase drinks and employees will also take your photo so you can purchase them as souvenirs. It takes 30 minutes for the wheel to make a full rotation so be sure to use the restroom before you board. 

I have experience the High Roller both during the day and in the evening. During the day, even though it was the weekend, there were far fewer people riding and we only had to share our cabin with one person. Evenings are far busier, and your chances of getting stuck in a cabin with an upset toddler or inconsiderate adults is far higher. 

For me, the High Roller look cool from the outside but actually riding it isn't all that. The view of the Bellagio Fountains during the descent is fantastic, but for the vast majority of the ride the main attractions of the Las Vegas Strip are blocked by parking garages and boring looking hotels. 

I think the High Roller is something people should experience at least once, but be sure to get discounted tickets!

While I was in Vegas for a conference I had the chance to take "spin" on the high roller.  I am not one for thrill rides and do not like edges, but am not overly bothered by heights.  The worlds largest observation wheel, fancy term for ferris wheel is pretty cool.  Like a gondola it never stops, but moves very slow so when getting on/off you have to sort of hop into the car.  The cars are very large so I wouldn't worry if you are claustrophobic.  The windows are floor to ceiling and there are railings around the edge. There are seats (not enough for all ppl) in the middle.  The floor is metal so you don't see down to the ground.  It moves very slow and takes 30 minutes to complete the round.  I went at night and the lights were very cool, however during the day you could probably see the mountains and see for miles which would be cool too.  At first when we were getting 350+ ft I thought I might just close my eyes and open them when near the end, but then I decided it was all going to be alright and opened them - WOW we were above everything in town.  I was lucky to ride for free, not sure I would pay $25, but I guess it is a cool memory and you'd spend that on slots any way.  Enjoy!

Super cool attraction!
Amazing views - we went at night, and I would think that is the better time to go.  However, they know that, and charge a $10 premium for going at night.  
I think its worth it, as they views are spectacular.

My fiance has a small fear of heights, but he felt safe and wasnt scared inside the pod.  It is very large (fits 40 people) with seating for about 10 people. 


Check living social for some discounts.
I think it basically lets you go at night for the daytime rate.

TIP:
Go to the bathroom before hand, the ride is 30 minutes long.

Awesome sauce!!!!! My experience was six star/baller style/living it up in Vegas type thing. Okay so let me explain why I'm uber excited about my ride on the Highroller. We came about 11:30 pm no lines at all and since we purchased from Groupon we picked up tickets at concierge, who were very helpful. The staff from entrance to the end we're all great actually. My groupon expired for the promotional value because we did not use last time we were here, but the difference was only 4 bucks, not bad. So when it comes time to board, we jump on, grab a seat on the bench, 2 international women jump on behind us do the same thing, and wham door closes it is just us four to a whole pod. Me and hubby are on one side smiling and snapping pics, gorgeous young girls on other side smiling and dancing. Party on VIP pod number 22 no bar needed, and no entourage included. We are free to slide all over benches, walk all around the pod, enjoying a 360 view at night in Vegas. Now we're almost at 550 feet, the Bellagio fountains are looking spectacular, were taking pictures for the girls and they are doing the same for us, we're all smiling from ear to ear, me and hubby talking, their going crazy in their own native language, and life is good. It is amazing how huge this thing is and how high up you are over the city. My hubby enjoyed the functionality of the wheel itself the most, whatever. I had a great time and I recommend to anyone visiting, however I would avoid the one with the bar since they seem to be the most crowded with the longer lines, but to each his own. Also groupon does run this promotion a lot.

This was a new addition since our last trip to Vegas.

We got the all you can drink happy hour ;) with a Groupon.

The experience starts off with getting your tickets redeemed ... The girl wasn't that welcoming. It was around 1030 pm. You go up a series of stairs and take a couple of keepsake pictures for purchase after.

We waited a bit for the happy hour pod to arrive once we got to the platform and then you walk/jump onto the moving pod which is a bit risky. Once on the pod the party started and our bartender was great. The views are fantastic and the whole rotation is about half an hr. You exit into a themed store and then are back on the Linq Promenade. 

All in all, it was worth it to go on this once. I wouldn't go again unless someone else paid for me or if it was part of a bachelor party.

This was a great experience, but in all honesty I wouldn't do it again. 

The High Roller is super overpriced even using a Groupon coupon. I got a Groupon deal for $65 for 2 people and it was not worth it.

I'd say that this ride is probably worth maybe at the max $20 a person. There were also a few discrepancies with the buy 1 get 1 free drink offer. 

You need to stand in line for them to print out a voucher, which was never mentioned to us until we got all the way to the top and in all honesty it felt like a rip off.

So in a nutshell you'll end up paying anywhere from $60 to $90 to ride the High Roller and you're not guaranteed to receive the 2 for 1 deal on drinks.

Overall it's okay and glad I can say I tried it, but wouldn't really recommend it to any friends.

First of all: I have a very serious fear of heights. Despite this, I really wanted to try this attraction, as I'd heard so many good things. Plus, I was promised that it's not really like a big ferris wheel, it's more like looking out the window of an airplane (which, oddly, I have no problems with). 

So, with more than a little trepidation and a very good friend (literally) holding my hand, we began our ascent in the dark of night. I knew better than to try to look anywhere other than straight out the sides during the first part of the ride; this affords a great view of the Vegas skyline and surrounding areas. While I was never able to muster enough courage to look out the front or back (which affords a view of the wheel and other cars), I did cast a glance downward a few times, and managed to keep my wits about me. 

The cars themselves are nice on the inside, and there's really very little feeling of motion. The  ride takes 28 minutes to do a full revolution and is constantly in motion, so there's no start/stop. As has been mentioned by others, there are drinks on board, but seriously, take stock of what you think you can drink in 28 minutes before you go for the "AYCD" package. 

Bottom line, if you want to get a spectacular view of Vegas, definitely check out the High Roller. Look for discounts, they're readily available, although some may come with time of day restrictions or the like.

OMG - FUN - Fun - fUn!!

What you should know - is some of their "pods" have a fully staffed/stocked bar and if you buy your ticket for the "bar car" before 6:00pm you get a better price.  Even Groupon couldn't match the before 6 pricing and since the ride takes about 35 minutes to go around completely - you can easily drink 3 cocktails - if you're like us Honey Badgers!!  

TIP: Make sure you hit a restroom before you board!

http://www.vegas.com/attractions/on-the-strip/high-roller-las-vegas/

It's located at the east end of the LINQ Promenade - easily accessed if you're walking.  

What a spectacular view! I recommend going at night - although at some point on a return visit - I want to do it during the day so I can see those beautiful mountains to the west!

We had a BLAST!! You couldn't even tell it was moving. Music played and we took pictures and really enjoyed ourselves!!

In classic attraction style - the exit filters you through a gift shop.  Prior to entering the POD you get your picture taken by a pro. You view them at the end before the gift shop and there wasn't any pressure to buy them. We did - because they were awesome and we were making memories!!

I will do it again!!

it's A-OK coz it is very expensive.. I feel like I need to get better than that with the ticket price.. but the customer service is nice.. looks safe.. all the things and built are new and secure.. Views on top aren't that amazing..(this is just for me). overall it's really an A-OK.. you literally express it like that after the trip.
So much fun and a beautiful way to see Vegas in the air conditioning.  Go early and look for discounts.   A great place to take your significant other.   Romantic and exciting too.

I was skeptical at first, thinking that's a lot of money just to ride a ferris wheel. Well, it's not just a ferris wheel! The experience is like nothing I've ever had before. The ride was smooth with breathtaking views, and the bubble makes you feel safe while allowing you to see everywhere around you: left, right, in front, behind, up, and down! I do think this is a ride I'm only interested in experiencing twice though (once in the day, and once at night), and I can see why the night tickets cost more. With a large group, it might be fun to do the bar option as well. I mean, it is Vegas, so you should be drinking everywhere you go, right?

The highest Ferris wheel in Vegas that is enclosed and colorful in the dark night sky! 

Definitely go at least once at night if you are in Vegas! You can see the whole city from the top. You can also drink while enclosed in the Ferris wheel ball. 

The only thing I didn't like was the glare that you can see from the glass.  Really hard to take nice pictures with a glare. 

There is a TV with a person speaking to you inside the closed ball. Kind of monotoned and weird but hey, it's just a TV.

very cool experience, the linq is huge and getting off and on was a tad scary but overall  a great time. my boyfriend and i got on late that night, which was around july of last year. we got sprinkles cupcakes and ate them when we got to the top, definitely something to do atleast once.

How can anybody  dislike the high roller? This amusement park revitalized the area and is a welcome addition to the "neighborhood" and skyline.

It may not look it from close up but from a distance it is a landmark on the strip towering above everything around it.

Views of the High Roller are clear from lots of pool facing Flamingo rooms and other nearby hotel resorts.

Have a drink and jump on this with your buddies. Just make sure you go to the john if you have a bladder problem as it takes quite an amount of time to make a full loop.

Luv it, it was included in our package that we got from The Ellen Show.  There were spectacular views of Vegas, plenty of room to roam in the pod. Very impressed!  Didn't want the pics that we took before boarding the ride, I took enough selfies of my own and also didn't want to pay $35 for it...lol.   We will definitely come back in August for our 14th year anniversary.
The line moved quick. The staff was friendly. We did the regular ride and skipped the happy hour. Nighttime views amazing!!! Add this to your must do list if you haven't already!!!

I've been on the High Roller 6 or 7 times now, so I suppose it's finally time to write a review... 
It's $21 a ticket for the day ride with a local ID. It's a bit more for night time, and a bit more for non locals. But kids under 12 are always free!

They try to make it really fun while you're walking through to get to the boarding area by having cool lights and music to get you pumped up. They take a profession photo in front of a green screen and add the city backdrop or the Vegas mountains. They're $20 for 1 photo or $35 for 2 with a digital copy and paper frame. 

Because it is Vegas after all, of course there's a bar right before boarding so you can get your favorite adult beverage or "liquid courage", if you're afraid of heights. 

There are small TV screens inside the pod that provide a "tour guide" to tell you a little about what you're seeing. It informs you of the exact miles up in the air you are at all times. They play music, have a 5 second countdown to the highest point, and even show a video montage of the making of the Farris wheel. 

Overall, it's something you should do once. I have a 3 year old who insists on going every time someone comes in town, so that's the only reason I have been so many times... ENJOY!!!

My friend got me a ticket to High Roller which he got for $17. I can count with 1 hand how many times I've been on a ferris wheel. It's a 550ft tall observation deck. You can go to Stratosphere if you want to be up higher...and jump off 858ft!

Going in the pod could be a little bit tricky if the people in front of you are scared, too slow or aren't alert...making the pod seem to be moving faster. Once you're in, the wheel moves ever so slowly and it stops. It takes 20-30 minutes to complete a whole rotation. You can either sit or stand and enjoy the view. I can see tourists enjoying this a lot.

I wish there was a way to have a pod with screaming kids and their guardians grouped together and those who don't have their own pod. Otherwise, it just turns out to be a torturous and the longest 30 minutes of your life. I'll bring Advil and earplugs next time.

i'm not one for touristy crap but i really enjoyed this and highly recommend!
i went during the day, where it is cheaper, less crowded, and you get to see the beautiful desert landscape.
Open bar is a must- it's only $5 extra during the day and you can easily get 2-3 drinks in.  our bartender was the nicest guy ever, funny, and hooked up our drinks nicely.  our pod had a small group - only 6 people.
JUST MAKE SURE YOU PEE BEFORE YOU GET ON!
also, even though i liked it a lot, i 'wouldn't wait in a long line for it.  there was no line at all when we went.

This is terrific and much better than it looks. Not that it doesn't look fine. But it is bigger and goes MUCH higher than you would ever anticipate looking at it. I've done it  twice now, with different groups, both times at night. Each time everyone was amazed by the views, by the actual machine, by everything. If you are wavering... just do it, it is worth it!

Way more awesome than I thought it would be. 

Basically you get to be in a small room that functions as a car on the ferris wheel (similar to the London Eye). You hardly even noticed you are moving until you look back outside and notice the view has changed. The half hour long is plenty but not so short that you feel gipped. We had only one couple in our car other than our group of three in our car and it was no big deal.

We did the open bar which was great. They had all types of liquor. However, their beer selection was severely lacking and cheap. Fortunately our bartender knew how to make some awesome drinks and you get one to go and since its Vegas can walk around with it. I am a little ashamed to admit I learned that I could drink quite a bit in half an hour. I will say though that our bartender was really cranky and we were tipping well so I don't know what the deal was.

Anyways, the views are awesome. I've been to Vegas plenty of times and this was definitely a way of seeing Vegas I have never experienced. Seeing the whole strip is awesome and seeing real Vegas and Nevada out into the distance is awesome. We went at sunset and so had awesome views of the sunset, the mountains, and then all of the hotels as they began to take over and light up the sky. 

My only problem with this place is the price. While its probably worth it once if you like Vegas, have the money to spend, or are really looking for something to do, but it is pretty expensive. 

In short, my friends wanted to do this and I thought it would be super lame and we would walk away saying "wow that sucked. what a waste." We all walked away saying how awesome and fun this was! Yay!

This is an amazing attraction, but if you are afraid of heights then keep in mind that the ride takes 30 minutes to make one loop. The price is really steep but if you get the family pack (2 Adult, 2 Child tickets) then you can save a lot of money. It is definitely an unforgettable experience right in the middle section of the strip.

Fun way to view Vegas! Enjoyed the happy hour pod, with bar, drinks included in ticket. The ride moves slowly, and lasts 30 minutes. Anyone who suffers from motion sickness can tolerate this. You cannot feel any movement.

This was a pretty cool attraction.  But they are advertising it HARD all around town which actually made me worry it was going to suck; why would they have to pimp it so hard if it actually was awesome?  But it really was pretty nice and we enjoyed it.

I got the Groupon for 2 "all you can drink" tickets.  We did the Groupon (which I think has gone up in price) and I believe we were saving about $5 per person, I'm not sure if you're saving much at all if you go during the day when it's cheaper. And I think you can get $5 off anyway if you download the app (I saw that advertised at the airport), so be sure to do the math. It did kind of suck that to ride with out friend who wasn't drinking, she had to pay for the "all you can drink" ticket so keep that in mind. 

There was some kind of computer issue where you buy the tickets so it took forever for me to pull up my Groupon on my phone (I was also have connectivity issues) but we got everything going eventually.  I always get confused about how far apart everything is on the Strip- we parked at the Venetian but the walk to the Linq felt very far, but mostly because it was chilly and rainy. 

You may ask "how much can I drink in 30 minutes?" and if you are in the pod with only 4 other people and the bartender is as cool as ours was, the answer is "more than you should!"  You do not feel it at all, no swinging like a traditional ferris wheel, it's very self contained. Supposedly the drinkin' pod can fit up to 20 people which I do think would get very crowded and cut into your drinkin' time so keep that in mind. It was raining and quite chilly when we went so I think that's probably why it wasn't as crowded. But it looked super cool up there and was overall a neat scene. I finished my drink as the ride was coming to an end and the bartender literally handed me a beer as I was walking off; I DEF got my money's worth! BUT I was too drunk to remember to use my discount in the gift shop (that came with the Groupon) so that's where they get ya!
The high roller is must try in Vegas ! Ride on the Ferris wheel for 30 mins and have a open bar while you view the city of Vegas 550 above the city !
Pretty cool view from the top.  If going again, we'd pay the extra for the open bar.  Video presentation got a little cheesy at times, but a good time killer!

So I got dragged here because some friends were in town and really wanted to do it. I have to say it was rather underwhelming and definitely not one of the better $35 I've spent.

First off, the video they play during the ride could be one of the most obnoxious videos ever known to mankind. It's loud, full of stupid jokes, and has no redeeming qualities. Why not just play music or even just have silence? People who get on this thing are there for the view (or maybe the drinks.....?), not some stupid video.

Second, it's a lot different from other observation wheels (like the London Eye) because there are so many close-by buildings that block the view from the High Roller. It's only during the top quarter or so of the ride that you get the full nice unobstructed view of the Strip, so a lot of it just feels like wasted time. And since it's at the Linq, we're not talking about the latest and greatest casino hotels that are blocking the view - just the older, shabbier casinos that are in this area. We went at night, and so because of this I would even say I might rather go in the daytime, as during the day it might be possible to see more of what's off-Strip and also the mountains.

So yeah, very underwhelming. I guess it might be fun as a one-time thing for a first-time visitor to Vegas, but if what you want is a view of the Strip and a couple drinks, there are other places for that. You almost certainly won't be subjected to obnoxious videos at those places either.

Yep all you can drink happy hour. Got a deal on living social and it was legit. You can drink all you want, views are great. Bar tender will be in there with you and others depending on how big your group is. Good time over all and fun way to start a night! Only complaint is that I wish it was longer and the cups you drink out of were better.

Let me start with I HATE heights but this was not scary at all. We had the car where you got unlimited drinks. Impressive to say the least, top shelf with a fantastic bartender. Recommend the night ride for sure. The only weird part is entering the car bc the wheel is in constant motion...slow but moving none the less. I would do this again for sure. My group was so fun & the view was of the chain.
I loved the high Roller happy half hour night ride :) the only reason i didn't give it 5 stars is because i think it's quite expensive. Even so, i will be riding it again when i return next month :)

Pretty awesome tourist attraction. Takes you way up high. Kinda romantic of you think. You can't bring your outside drinks in..... However, there is a bar near the entrance and they give you your drinks in this plastic souvenir cup that you can keep. Those drinks you can bring into the high roller. What a way to make money right? Haha 

The views are awesome and you don't have to worry about your pod being too crowded either. Oh ya, you have to walk on while it's still moving.... Don't worry there's a safety net. It only moves 1mph so it's really slow. I can't even tell it moving!

This is definitely something to do while in Vegas!

Worth to check out if you have Groupon or Livingsocial for half of the admission fee.  We went at midnight on a Friday night.  There was no line and only 7 people in the gondola.  The entire ride takes 30 minutes and you do get amazing views of Vegas.  I highly recommend going at night instead of day time.

This was a pretty cool ride, very slow so u can view Vegas in ease. Around 20-30 mins for us. It's very pricey, but worth the one time  trip. It's not something I would do every time we go to Vegas. If your afraid of heights.. Understand u will be 550 ft above the platform at one point! 
The Linq is a great addition to what used to be an alleyway, reminds me of downtown Disney-without the Disney and more for adult entertainment. Plenty of places to get a drink, a quick bite, a cozy dinner with ur special someone or a delicious dessert. 
It's def a must stop for something new and fun on ur Vegas trip!

The High Roller was really fun! I wouldn't pay full price, but I got a two-for-one flex pass deal on Groupon with buy one get one free drinks, prints, and a discount in the store.

The total ride is about 30 minutes long. It's incredibly smooth and you really don't feel the cabin moving. They kind of pack you in there when it's busy, so I tried to go on a less busy time, but of course at night. Even if you're afraid of heights, I think you'd be ok in this because you really feel as if you are on an observation deck and not in an observation wheel.

It's one of those things that when you visit Vegas, you should do at least once. Beautiful view, the staff were very friendly, and I would suggest to anyone. But, again, at a discount. $45/ticket is way too much for a 30 minute ride. If you want a free, pretty view, you can always go to the Mandarin Oriental Mandarin Bar and look out the panoramic windows on the 23rd floor.

The view was definitely amazing. It was fun seeing the whole strip like that. However, when it says that the ride is open until 2 and you have bought a happy half hour ticket, know that it is only good until 1am. It does not specify this and we were disappointed when we showed up. However, they did provide a refund of the happy hour price and we were still able to ride.
We had a wonderful experience on the High Roller, my sister timed it so we would be up high as the sun started to set, it was so beautiful!

This is one of my all-time favorite experiences in Vegas. A 30 minute ride with a beautiful view of the Las Vegas strip... With an all-you-can-drink bar!
