We went early (after lunch) so there was no line. You have to pay extra for the bartender pod but it's worth it! Our bartender was so friendly and personable, giving us drink after drink and carrying an interesting conversation with us. He even gave us each one drink for the road when the ride was finished. I would definitely go back again when in Vegas.

Did this last night via Groupon (Nighttime Happy Hour for 2). There's a bag check you have to go through before you get to a small bar, then someone by a doorway leading up to the ferris wheel scans your ticket, go through a little maze line, get your pictures taken in front of a green screen (2 pictures) and finally depending on what kind of ticket you purchased (either with or without the open bar option), you wait in one of two lines and wait to board a pod while it's still moving so watch your step! 

Had way too many people in the pod we were in (about 16). ID had to be shown to the bartender to receive a small plastic cup you had to reuse. Liquor and mixers on board was limited but enough to make what most people drink anyway. Beers are domestic only (Coors Light, Bud Light, Budweiser, etc.). I managed to get in 2 mixed drinks and a shot. Great views of the Vegas strip and the not-so-much there side.

After the 30 minute ride was over you exit the still moving pod (watch your step!), walk down a few ramps and into the photo sales area. You can purchase one picture with a black book frame for $30 or get 2 frames with 3 pictures for $50 (extremely overpriced but like a tourist with a "for memories sake" mentality, I took the bait and $50 lighter). You then proceed through a gift shop and exit the building. Overall the experience was just OK and more than likely won't do it again for the price I paid for.

Pretty expensive but there are a lot of deals if you know where to look.  If you're over 21 I definitely recommend doing happy half hour open bar.  It's an awesome game of how much can you drink in 30 minutes and that makes the ride so much more fun.  The pods are stable and you shouldn't really feel anything.  The views are amazing especially at night.  Make sure you do your business before riding as there's no restroom on board.  The night I went it was St Patrick's Day and they were giving away free commemorative shirts!  I would say it's worth doing at least once.

A must-do experience while in Vegas! Be warned though, if you're looking for a mind-blowing, extreme experience, this is not it. The wheel moves very slow and I think the most thrilling part of the experience for me as someone who's scared of heights was just entering and exiting the slow-moving bubble as it kept moving. Trust me, very scary.

The views are incredible! Our group of 7 were paired with another couple for our bubble and we chose the open bar option -- totally worth the extra $$. Our bartender was awesome! She joked and catered to us and even demanded we get our money's worth by drinking more, more, more! When we hit the highest point, she surprised us with celebratory shots! She joined in on helping us take group pictures. It was great having this level of service for our experience!

Love the views -- and to say you've been on the world's tallest observation wheel? Totally worth it! 

Tips: Take a restroom break before you go (it's a 30 minute journey and especially if you opt for open bar) and capture a thousand pictures -- you won't regret it!

Love it!!! I have gone both in the daytime and at night! The staff is so friendly, and helpful. The views are amazing, and the pods are never crowded. If you ate afraid of heights, don't worry! It is a VERY smooth ride, and you don't even realize your moving. This is a must try for everyone in LV

This was fun. I felt like there was too many people in the pod because it was the open bar one. There was probably 20 people so it was crowded and not much seating. The drinks were good but limited. The bartender we had took a while to take out order because he kept going to the people right in front of him when I was to the side. The views were so pretty wish the ride lasted longer!

They currently have locals specials every day -- $5 discounts on both day and evening tickets, with kids 6 and under riding free. The cost for me and my son to ride was less than $22. Not bad at all for a half hour ride. On Tuesdays locals can get 50% off. The entrance/exit to the High Roller is right by the base of it, on the east end of the Linq. On the weeknight we went there wasn't much of a line. We quickly purchased tickets and made our way to the pods all within a few minutes.

Each pod can hold up to 40 people, but I like that they only loaded 6 other people into ours. There was plenty of space to walk around and check out the views from every angle. The pods sway very little, so even those that are afraid of heights may not feel the effects of being 550 feet up in the air.

Going right around sunset provides amazing views of the valley with plenty of photo ops. It's great to do once, but I'm sure I'll have to bring friends/family here whenever they're in town. 

Parking is available for free in the lot east of the High Roller, but the most convenient way to park is to use the valet located at the base of the observation wheel.

I rode High Roller while visiting Las Vegas. I went on the High Roller before 5pm. The ticket purchase line before going up to HR was long but moved steady. It wasn't a very long wait to get on after getting tickets. We got the drink package, which included open bar for 30 min. Our pod had about 8 people in it. Pods has air condition. The views​ of Vegas on High Roller is awesome. I was able to take cool pictures at the top. High Roller was a very smooth ride. The drinks were prepared fast/well by our bartender. The bartender was professional and down to earth. I thought High Roller drink package was a good deal IMO (our bartender was awesome). Having a good bartender is important. I had a lot of fun riding High Roller. If you're looking for something fun to do in Vegas,High Roller is a good choice.

We did this on our last night and it was great! It was a Tuesday night at about 8:15 and we were in the pod with only two other people....who were not drunk so it was great! I am terrified of heights and I did just fine! It was a really incredible view and a great experience! Next time we will try it during the day....we even purchased the photos they took of us before getting on! Great experience!

Cool experience seeing the Las Vegas valley from the peak of the observatory. Definitely worth to take some cool pictures, but the price to get on can add up if your going in a group. I'd say they should charge less and make the ride shorter because you'll feel over it by the time your on your way back down. The playing on the informational video inside the pod can be pretty annoying too. No matter, still a cool experience

I am mortified of heights but my husband and our good friend convinced me to get on this thing. It was well worth it. It is the largest observation tower in the world. At its apex it reaches 550 feet. The whole trip takes about 30 minutes.  This isn't meant for someone who is in a hurry. The view was beautiful from up top and you could barely feel it moving.

It's definitely not worth the $35 for a night time ride.

Drinks at the bar were made really weak and u pay $12 for them!

The great part of this attraction is obviously the view! Im scared of heights but it was an adventure! 
30mins of amazing views of the city.  You are placed in a bubble on a humungous ferris wheel.  

My bf and I went around 11pm, we got our own pod, it was intimate and romantic! 

Total tourist attraction!

Staff was super friendly.

My husband and i have done almost everything in Vegas, so we thought this would be fun.  The prices are higher at night somewhere around $35 each and that's without drinks.  The all you can drink tickets are $52, but the ride is only 30 minutes.  I got a $13 dollar drink before we boarded, so I suppose the all you can drink prices are worth it in terms of THEIR prices.  Other than that its a rip off.  

As far as the view is concerned its really disappointing.  If you look at the placement of it on the strip its not surprising, but I thought it would be okay with the height.  

All in all I wouldn't suggest riding this thing, unless its one of the last things you haven't done in Vegas.  Or if you have minors that can't really do anything else.  The Eiffel Tower at the Paris has spectacular views of the Bellagio water show and the strip and the Stratosphere has awesome views as well.

The High Roller is located close to the Linq hotel, a short ride away from the strip on the Monirail. The whole place is pretty awesome from dive bars to restaurants leading to the High Roller. 

If you buy the tickets online at www.vegas.com, the cost is about $32 per person. If you buy it at the High Roller box office it's about $37 with some additional fees. Also, online you have the choice between an open bar ride for $52 which basically means you get to choose between beer and cocktails or the simple ride for $32.

All I have to say is the High Roller was worth the ride! It gives you an amazing view not only of the Las Vegas strip but also an incredible view of the city of Las Vegas.

My friend and I decided to take the night ride of the High Roller and the view was simply breathtaking. It is highest observation point in the world and it gave us an incredible view of the lights over the strip, the rest of the beautiful city of Las Vegas and most importantly we got to see the water show from the Bellagio!

If you are in Las Vegas this is an attraction you don't want to miss. My advice however would be to take the night tour like we did. You will not regret it. Also make sure you buy the ticket online to save a few bucks.

Awesome ride and the views at night are spectacular. We rode in the open bar....because we could!  It was great a little over 30 mins ride time and we'll there's a bar!  Nice ride with someone special. We had a blast. 

Oh and the shopping restaurant area between Harrah and the Flamingo is outstanding.
Great view of The Strip from the top.

Price=Expensive. $35 to go after dark. Which is pricey. Its cool n all.. gives a good view of the city. Cool for the experience but because of the price we most likely won't go again. 
We purchased a groupon for $69 two people.. with the option of happy hour(normally a $10 add on) so there is where it would save.
Take a camera - gives for some nice photos of the vegas lights.

A VIEW to a Thrill.

It's high rolling high in the sky on one of the newest additions to the Las Vegas skyline.  The high roller, a larger than life ferris wheel, now affords people stunning views of the Las Vegas strip and surrounding areas.  

NOTE:  Operates 1130am to 200am daily.  Tickets can be bought at various booths/stands up and down the Las Vegas strip, automated kiosks along the Linq promenade, or at ground level ticket office at the entrance to the High Roller.

LOCATION:  The high roller is the centerpiece and main attraction at the Linq (formerly Imperial Palace).  It rises above the Vegas strip behind the Linq hotel at the end of the shopping promenade.

TICKET TO RIDE:  We bought night tickets for their "happy half hour" so we could admire the bright lights of Vegas.  An open bar is placed in the center of the cabin to allow free-flowing drinks while taking in the views of the city.  Ticket price:  $44.95

BY THE NUMBERS:

*Passenger cabins:  28

*Capacity per cabin:  40 

*Height:  550 feet

*One Revolution:  30 minutes

*Flat screen tv's per cabin: 8

BOARDING:  Passenger will first pass thru a security check point on the ground floor.  The second floor has a bar as well as restrooms.  I'd recommend using the restroom first if needed since there are none in the cabins.  I would advise to pay attention to the attendants just before boarding as they will instruct you in which line to stand in, where to stand, and when to board.  The wheel moves slowly enough (one foot per second) and thus does not stop entirely to allow passengers to board or exit the cabins.

RIDE:  It was definitely a happy half hour as the drinks were readily prepared and given, while the bartender was quite friendly and outgoing.  As there were just four passengers in our cabin, there was much conversation, laughter, and a few group "cheers" as well.  The views were just simply amazing, and it was such a delight to have the opportunity to gaze at the bright lights below.  The ride was over before we knew it as you barely feel any movement as the wheel rotates.  Soon enough our cabin was at the peak, and at the very next moment it was time to make our exit.

EXIT:  Passengers disembark the cabins much the same way they entered, just on the opposite side.  Trinkets or souvenir photos can be purchased at the gift shop on the first floor.

BOTTOM LINE:  The happiest half hour I've ever experienced.  Time well spent surely.

A little taste of Disneyland right here in good old Las Vegas!
 I think that everyone should go for a ride on the HR at least once. I took the advice of a fellow Yelper and I went at dusk (8pm in mid June). It made for the start of the ride being at dusk and the last part of the ride at dark.
 Being able to get such an amazing view of the valley that we live in was a real treat. Sure, many of us have arrived in town via airplane at dusk/dark, but it's not quite the same thing. :)
I would recommend buying your tickets online and print them out before you arrive to avoid the long lines.
 I timed our ride and it was 35 mins- the ride did stop a few times to assist in the arrival/departure of riders with special needs.
 It did get a little scary/uneasy at the very top, but upbeat music played so that helped distract me a bit. 
I doubt I will take a second ride because once was enough. But make sure to cross it off YOUR bucket list.

I Just got back from Vegas and have some advice if you would like to ride. First, it is awesome. Second, do it during the day if possible (shorter lines, and it is cheaper). Third, DO THE BAR CAR! It is all-you-can-drink! It is a 30 minute ride, and you can drink as much as you want. The only exception is they will not give you as many  shots as you want. You get one shot to "cheers" with at the very top.

The only negative I have is that they did not offer mimosas, but they had vodka cranberry.

Bought the tickets off of living social that included a free drink at the bar.

Went at around 6pm. Basically no lines at all. Ride lasted about 30mins total.

This is one of those things you wanna try at least one.

If you plan to ride go at around 8pm when the sun is about to set.  Also, save your free drink ticket till you get outside. There is another bar outside right before you board.

The bartender inside made us lousy mixed drinks. Better to redeem your ticket outside.

What a total rip off.  Waited on line to buy tickets that may have 60 to 35 dollars depending on the person we spoke to.  Plus an additional 2 dollar service charge per ticket.   No one knew what was going on and there was confusion among the  staff.   Do your self a favor. Save your money and go see the city from the roof of any parking garage

I had to plan my best friends bachelorette in Vegas & when I saw the happy half hour deal on the High Roller, I was sold!
We had 5 of us girls in a pod with another group of 5 & it truly was an experience. Our bartender did not disappoint (I wish I remembered her name!) great views & an abundance of booze ;)

Loooved this!! Ferris wheel moves very slowly giving you plenty of time to down some shots and see the city. Our bar tender was friendly and had a lot of energy. So glad we did this at night, it wouldn't have been the same without the lights.

Rode the High Roller with some friends this past weekend at night and purchased the happy hour deal ($47pp with open bar). Note: there are NOT bathrooms on board so I highly recommend visiting the potty before boarding! The wheel spins very slow and does not stop when loading and unloading. So basically, you need to step aboard a moving bubble to get on. The inside fits 40 people, but I think that would be overcrowded. Our bubble had about 20 people and there were still plenty of "excuse me" and "oops I'm sorry" while moving about. 
Open bar means simple mixed drinks and wine. I didn't see any beer around. The bartender was very kind and drinks are served as soon as you board. 

The views were really amazing and you can move freely around in the bubble to see all sides of Vegas. The wheel is located in the LINQ Promenade in the middle of the Strip (easy to find obviously due to its massive size). It has been deemed the world's highest observation tower at 550 feet. There was a woman on board with us that was afraid of heights but she said she was not terrible scared. Her tip was to look straight out at the horizon rather than down at any point for those of you who have a bit of fear. The entire duration was 30 minutes long. It is a good tourist stop, but I don't think I would do it again for the price. Hotel room views are also quite spectacular if you don't want to spend the money.

Use your local ID before 6 PM and ride this beast for $12.50. You have to do it at least once. I happened to do it during the 60 MPH winds and Las Vegas #duststorm2017 lol so it did move a time or two and have an eerie windy sound that got a tad scary LOL but it was fine, this is a fun, smooth ride up to 550' ;) Up to 40 people can fit in each "pod" but if you time it right (use the restroom) you can sometimes get a pod of your own. I have ridden this three times and actually it's fun being on it with strangers you can get to know them it's funny. But getting your own car, now that is hot LOL do know that a couple did get in big trouble in the news a few months back for shenanigans on this ride but yeah :) it's a must do when in town and/or visiting the strip with your family/friends. Oh PS if you aren't a local, check GROUPON.

550 feet high on the tallest observation wheel in the world...the High Roller Ferris Wheel in Las Vegas!!

Tickets are purchased online or at the ticket counter up front and then you go up an escalator to get to where you will board. As others said it's best to find a deal online. (Note: they won't accept online codes at the ticket counter.) Unfortunately me for I bought my tickets last minute and had to pay the full night price of $36.95. I am definitely going to buy tickets beforehand in the future but no regrets on the full price because I did enjoy myself that night.

Before boarding, there is a lounge area where you can purchase drinks which start at about $10. (Note: for those who do want to purchase drinks, one may want to consider purchasing a ticket with the open bar in the pod because it's only $20 more and a better deal than getting a drink at the lounge area).

I rode the High Roller around close to 11pm at night so got the most amazing view of The Strip. The ride in total is about 30 minutes. You share the pod with others but the pod is huge! I have heard it can fit up to 40 people but if you are fortunate you may just get a pod to yourselves. This is harder to do at night though because night rides are pretty popular. I actually ended up in a pod with a wedding party but it wasn't crowded at all! There is plenty of room in the pod though regardless if you share with others and lots of space to move around and take pictures! Going there is a video going on that tells you how high you are in increments and once you get close to the peak, the countdown begins.

Reaching the peak is the best part. You really get a full view of all of the Vegas strip and it is absolutely gorgeous and breathtaking. From seeing the Eiffel Tower at Paris to the Cosmopolitan to Bellagio. I found myself snapping away endlessly at all the views!

It is truly an amazing experience to ride the High Roller! Picturesque view of Vegas like no other and truly a lot of fun! The High Roller is awesome.

This was a fun new way to see all of the Vegas lights! We came in at night around 8pm. The ticket line was long so I suggest getting tickets on-line or elsewhere. If going during the day the cost is 25.00 and at night 35.00 plus tax. 

You'll be directed up some stairs and there is a photo option and a bar as you are making your way to the wheel (we brought our own cocktails). Once in line for the roller it moved quickly.  Each cabin will hold about 40 ppl. It moved quickly when getting in the wheel doesn't stop to let you in or out so you'd better get in where you can fit in! 

Once the doors close there are tv screens with a narrator giving you information on the elevation and keep the ride entertaining. The high point is about 550 ft. and views are amazing!! 

The ride takes about 30 minutes and once off you are directed down where you can view the photo taken at the beginning/ buy them and  a walk through the souvenir shop. 

Overall this was a great experience! Check off the Vegas bucket list!

This was a must on our visit!!!!! We did the 21+ and it was the best experience. We had Virginia as our bartender and she was phenomenal! It's all you can drink in that 30 minute ride and she was the most personable and friendly bartender! I loved her! If you have time to kill or are looking to see all of Vegas!

This is a well designed and executed experience.  

There are plenty of options available for getting a deal whether it's their bundle pricing or hotel coupons.    We used the Power Pass which included the High Roller once a day so we rode once in the day and once at night.   

Our wait was minimal due to being off-season and weekday but if you have  wait a bit it's worth it.   

The wheel takes 30 minutes and is very smooth.  Video screens provide some programming with a hipster host but he doesn't talk the whole time and they fill with some music and details about the construction of the massive undertaking.  At 550 feet it's putting you eye to eye with everything in the skyline with an unobstructed view.

The cabins fit 40 and we're really glad that it wasn't full.  Having only a handful of guests, we were able to walk about the cabin and enjoy the tranquil time away from the chaos of the city.

When you're in Vegas, put this on your list.

This was fun, but not the highlight of Vegas.  The only reason I say 4 is because I personally found it rather slow and we missed happy hour so I'm sure it would've been much more exciting if we had been drinking lol

We got really lucky! No line on a Friday night and our own "pod". I love the tv screens and the "host", it was funny and informative. The music was great, I seriously thought it was my birthday gift and the playlist was just for me. Super cute and romantic date idea, or great for a party as well. Love this!

If you like to drink and get in some pretty cool views of Las Vegas. This is for you! We got tickets off Groupon ahead of time so it made prices better. I'm
Not a huge drinker but because my friends are, and we want to be together. I had to purchase open bar option. So that's something to know.  We did the ride at night and was able to get some nice pics. The drinks were not that strong, but bartender is cool. Make sure you charge your phone before going on this! I'm so sad my phone died right before I got here and couldn't get my pics :(

Over the weekend my boyfriend and I took an amazing trip to Las Vegas one of the coolest moments of our trip was when we boarded The High Roller, which is a large observation wheel that goes up to 550 feet high over the Las Vegas strip. The wheel is located in a shopping and dining center located at The LINQ Promenade. The observation wheel has 28 glass cabins and it takes around 30 minutes to go around. My experience on The High Roller was awesome. We boarded the wheel at around 9pm, and there was almost no wait time. We were a total of 5 people in our cabin which was great because we got to enjoy 360 degree views with no disruptions. If you are ever planning on visiting Vegas anytime soon The Linq High Roller is definitely the new spot you do not not want to miss!

Wow! Nice 30 minute ride in pod type thingy. Goes way up over the buildings so you can see all over the valley. Very safe and great place for pictures. Must do at least once! Nice shops along the walkway leading to the ride.

This feat of modern engineering invites you to travel inside an air conditioned and slowly rotating sphere on the outside of a 450-foot bicycle-style wheel. The views of the city and surrounding desertscape are spectacular and ride is incredibly slow and smooth.

We went on a weekday afternoon and had an entire cabin to ourselves!

The only negative about this amazing experience (it's currently the tallest wheel in the world!) is the poorly written and produced media forced on you on the cabin's multiple video screens.

The video is hosted by a dorky actor with pedantic humor. The motion graphics don't seem to consistently show where you are on the wheel or your elevation. A dashboard-style display with audio-only announcements would have been much more effective.

The music is also kind odd - it would be great to select your music preference (and control the volume). Two great additions would be digital binoculars that allow you to zoom in to see distant things much closer, and an augmented reality screen that names every building you see. (There's currently no reference for anything below).

The time lapse building video was the best thing they showed.

Regardless, riding the High Roller is a new must-do experience in Vegas. The only question is to do it by day or by night?

YEAH!!! A big fan, even though I am scared of heights. If you buy your tickets from Vegas.com it might be a couple dollars cheaper. We did the happy hour which was all you can drink for 30 min inside the pod. There were about 6 other people in our pod and it was not even crowded at all. I'll be honest I was so scared when we were at the highest point and I pretty much sat still. The drinks kind of helped! Our bartender was on a mission to get us all super drunk, the shots kept coming and coming, even when I had not taken the last shot. In 30 minutes I drank 2 vodka cranberry, 1 shot of Patron, 2 shots of the bartender's special and 2 beers. I stepped out of that pod piss arse drunk and had a great night. I would definitely do it again but at night!
Great ride with my family and friend on Christmas and we loved it! Loved seeing the city at night and it was such a smooth ride!

We went on a Tuesday night expecting that it wouldn't be so busy. However, since it's Summer, don't expect it to be any less busy for any day of the week. It was still packed! There were a lot of people lined up in what looked like a big crowded mess, so I feel like the staff could've done a better job creating an area for a single file line. The guy on watch was just standing there as new people who wanted to go on the ride were wondering where the hell they were supposed to go to. However, the wait time into the ride itself wasn't so bad as there were customers coming in and out of the viewing pod at all times, due to the way it's structured. 

That brings me to my biggest blunder. The ride is boring, absolutely boring. Especially for the price too! My boyfriend and I paid 30 bucks each for a total of 60 dollars. It takes forever just to get to the scenic views of the strip, and while I must say that the views are actually nice, it definitely is not 60 dollars worth of "nice." The Ferris wheel lasts for 30 minutes long, going in one full rotation before it is over. Within that rotation, a good lets-say 15 minutes of it is just waiting for the view to arrive. The view is just as good going to the top level of a parking garage and taking pictures there. By the time we did get to the top and had taken our pictures, we sat back down legitimately wondering when we'd get back to the bottom and leave to go back to our sight seeing. 

On the bright side, I'll admit that my boyfriend is an absolute pussy. He hates heights of all kind, and this viewing pod definitely made him feel safe, perhaps due to the spaciousness and the slow pace it was going at. However the pace could be a good or bad thing depending on the person. 

I give this attraction three stars because this is definitely something worth experiencing, but not for what it's priced at.

This was the worst experience possible. We went for my bachelorette party and prepaid to get an open bar, needless to say we paid for it and didn't get it.  When asked about it staff and managers had every excuse but no answers and wouldn't mKe the situation right. Would highly not recommend. Not worth the price and they are just trying to take more money than is paid for.

Back again and this is still a great ride.  They also have a valet that is very close by if you want to get in and get out quickly.  It costs $8.00 but is worth it.  

Love the view from this ride despite the cost.

We bought Groupons for the Happy hour deal before we left, and we are so happy we took that decision!!

We were lucky enough not to get into the packed cabin, and were only 6 in the next one. It was a 30 minutes ride with open bar. The waitress was AMAZING!! So nice and friendly, we let her prepare the cocktails that she wanted, and it was pretty good! We didn't have time to finish a glass that we had another one waiting on us, and we had one ready at the end to leave the cabin. So basically we were drinking non-stop for 30minutes. 

The view was amazing! We did it by night, and I think it's the way to go.
Next time we go to Vegas we will go back for sure!!

Vegas local ... Waited months for this to open Very boring not worth 40$ go to the stratosphere instead  ... My tvs didn't work windows were dirty .... Then was told "we don't give refunds"  ... F the highroller

And noooooo discount for locals ... Least we know what caesars thinks of it's neighbors

Great views of the city.

Full disclosure: I got to ride for free, and didn't have to wait in line, so for that, it was awesome. However, if I was paying and waiting, I might just go someplace where I can enjoy a cocktail with my outstanding views. 

If you're a tourist with a little money to burn, the High Roller is cool. If you're not afraid to take a cab (or you're local), go to the Mandarin Bar or the martini bar at the Stratosphere.
My husband and I went here with a couple of good friends. It was amazing. The view was great, drinks were good, and our bartender was funny. Highly recommended!

Ok if I'm paying almost $40 for an all u can drink booth, don't stuff us in like sardines.  Our bartender served me sauza for patron, yuck!  Also he was kind of an asshole.  With a bar and jam packed full of people we couldn't see different views.  Pods are smaller then i anticipated. If you are staying on the 20th floor or higher in a hotel, you will have a better view.  Not worth it.
For the price i expected more but maybe next time i will do the happy hour i just felt like it was very pricey for the ride

I went with a large group on Saturday around 8pm. We purchased our tickets from the outdoor kiosk and passed the other ticket line. The wait time was not bad at all (10 mins) but I believe it was because most of the people in line were not doing the open bar option so we were put ahead.

$45 at the door/$39 on living social.

Our bartender Francis is a cool guy! Beautiful view with pretty lights. A lot of long island iced teas! The ride did seem to go by faster than expected. Without the Happy Hour option, it would have not been as ecstatic. Overall, good experience and friendly staff.

great vibe, quite a number of features to choose from at The LINQ..The High Roller is breathtaking as you look up from the spacious walkway, once on board enjoy the smooth orbit and fantastic view with that special someone, good friends or random riders. I prefer the experience at night. as the various lights pierce the evening sky.

I give it a 4 due to price only. The rest of it is awesome. Take it at night. You can see forever. It's 30 min ride. It's slow sometimes you don't even feel your moving. You can stand and walk around. It's cool to see the strip lights at night. They take your pic before getting on. You see it afterward and can purchase it.  We did.

i got a deal from living social or groupon, i forgot which one it was.  anyways, don't pay full price for the high roller.  you can always find deals or coupons online.  

i went around midnight, and keep in mind they close at 2am.
the line was not long at midnight, on a Saturday, but then again, i suppose everyone else is in the club getting turnt and going home with strangers.  lol 

the ride lasts around 30 mins, and the top of the peak sits at 550 ft?  it provides a nice view, but not the complete vegas strip. 

they also have an upgrade, if you want to get your drink on... i know some of the cabins have an open bar and its aycd for roughly 30 mins.  i was scared to go on, because one has to wonder, if someone pukes inside, then you're stuck with the smell and might puke yourself.  haha.  honestly though, it might not be a bad idea to get access to the open bar and then after you finish, take a taxi to a nearby club and get the buzz going inside the club and not have to pay 20 bucks for a drink.  

i'd recommend going on this, but once is enought.

FANTASTIC!!
Spending 30 minutes on a slow moving ferris-wheel doesn't sound like much... But go with a couple of friends and pay for the bar-car "Happy 1/2-Hour" upgrade and it quickly becomes a fantastic time!!
Our bartender, Reese (sp?), was AWESOME!  He kept our drinks topped off the whole time while simultaneously taking great photos of all of us, and just being a top-notch host!
This was the perfect late night, trip-making, time!!
Totally worth it!

It was fun and quite the view.  

It was going to be $36/ea, saw a Linq strip guide in our room and on one of the pages for a "save" site  you could log-in on line to get for $25/ea, but link never asked for code so scam who knows.  Went down to the Linq guest services and they were going to give us tix at $25, but when we mentioned we had VIP tix for Matt Franci's show, got us $20/ea tix plus free Auto Show tix.  Nice!

Save on the open bar one, you waste more time looking at the bartender for drinks then looking at the view.
Some of the best views of Vegas and surrounding areas can be had from atop here.  Just wished they served lunch or dinner for Guests to experience.
Expensive but worth the experience!! We went on a Saturday night and got a pod with just the people we were with. Amazing views and just a really unique experience.

My wife and I were in Vegas this past weekend and wanted to try out the new High Roller to see what it's about. The whole area is new-ish. I'm not sure when it opened up but this was our first time here. The Linq has a lot of restaurants, bars and food shops in the area. We went with my parents as well. On the way to the High Roller, we saw they had kiosks to buy tickets closer to the strip. So we just decided to buy our tickets there to make it faster. We didn't know it at the time, but this saved us a lot of time!

When you buy your tickets through the kiosk, you get to pick a time slot of when you want to ride the High Roller. I would suggest giving yourself 20 minutes because it is still a pretty far walk just to get to the High Roller entrance and giving yourself some bathroom time.

The walkway to the High Roller entrance is where all the shops and restaurants are. There's a lot of music being played in the area. It seems like a really busy place and is a nice place just to stop by and chill.

When we got to the High Roller entrance, we saw a long line. Luckily we bought our tickets through the machine and we got to walk right through! So just a tip, purchase your tickets through the kiosk to save yourself some time. When you walk in the workers check purses/bags. Then you walk through the place. It reminds me of disneyland because of the way the lines are setup. We went on a Saturday at 9:10PM. We got really lucky cause we got to walk right through all the way to the top without waiting in any lines. They have an area to use the bathroom and buy drinks. I would suggest to use the bathroom since the ride is 30 minutes long and there's no place to go when you're in the pod. The drinks aren't that expensive. My wife and I tried the frozen drinks with some shots of alch.

You get grouped with around 20 people. The pods move continuously so you have to enter and exit pretty carefully. The pods have TVs inside that tells you how high you are and when you reach the apex of the ride. It also shows trivia and how the High Roller was made in a time lapse video. The views pretty nice, especially at night! You get to see the strip lit up. It was a super full moon that night as well. We got to see the Bellagio water show for a bit too. The pod has two seating areas. I would say the best place to go to in the pod would be the right side next to the entrance doors when you walk in. It has the best view of the strip when you reach the top. So try to make it out to that area if you can. But pretty much you can walk around the whole pod and enjoy all the views.

I would definitely recommend taking a ride on the High Roller if you're in Vegas. You can ride it during the day but try to go at night as you get to see all the lights Vegas has to offer. It was $35/person at night and cheaper during the day. Not that bad for a really good and fun experience.
This was a cool experience, very nice views. But it's like a do it one time and don't need to do it again.

Their was no line when we went on a Friday night...and the price for two plus two drinks was like robbery. We weren't offered a photo-op as we walked past the photo area. The two photo guys were too busy talking to each other that we were ignored. When we were at the boarding area, the attendant frantically waive you to hurry up and jump on board the moving pod.  The ride is slow moving and the monitors that are inside are blaring loud and obnoxious. Maybe they need to change the voice to be more pleasant than "infomercial yelling". The views were nice at night and made for great pictures of the strip. But beware that if your cabin is full, it'll be hard to grab window space in your pod for photos...there was only 10 ppl in ours and it was a struggle.  Overall, it's an expensive ride.

For a stunning view of Las Vegas, just get on the High Roller. You get to see all of the hotels around the strip, and some of the pool areas of the hotels where you don't normally see when you're on the ground. 

The pods are relatively large so there may be other people with you if it is particularly busy. What's cool about it is there's a video inside the pod telling you exactly where you are on the ferris wheel. There's also an announcement for when you reach the very top of the circle and that's the time when everybody goes towards the edge and snap some photos. However, I can't say the photos are the best since it is behind the glass so I would just sit back and enjoy the view :) 

I just thought of this because I heard of stories where people propose at/in the ferris wheel. If you're thinking of proposing, there may be other people in the pod as it is not guaranteed you have the pod to yourself. Just saying ;)

This is a perfect sunset Booz shot fest before getting on with your night on the strip. Definitely worth doing just for the great and different view of the city. Got tickets on living social. If you buy the alcohol included tickets you will be on a pod that does not allow under 21. It has a small bar in the middle and also holds less ppl so jic you're claustrophobic. But depending on what time you go you may also be onboard with the intoxicated. Pick your poison more ppl and children or partiers :) we got neither and there were only about 6 ppl so it was a blast. It's not scary at all you can't even really feel it move. It's neat!

Hers the deal, it's expensive and it only lasts 30 minutes, but it is Vegas and nothings cheap. The views are spectacular. We got the pod without the full bar and for is it was perfect. Go at night as the city is beautiful from that high up. When we went there was no wait or long lines.

First, come at night and take the bar option. Totally worth it. For $15 more you get unlimited drinks for the full 30 min ride. The bartender is awesome and the view is AMAZING! Totally a must do when you come to Vegas.

Me and my Fiancé did the High Roller Happy 1/2 Hour, needless to say we were very happy! For those not familiar you can pay a little extra to be able to drink unlimited drinks for a half hour! The bar tender was ridiculously fast and generous with the alcohol. We never felt like we were waiting for a drink and you can basically get any drink you want, we drank long islands, rum and cokes and Malibu bay breezes. We left satisfied with the amazing view, with new memories and great pictures, and of course a little tipsy! One of my favorite experiences from our trip!

THE high roller was better than expected ! Phedra was the 
Most amazing bartender/ tour guide (I apologize if the spelling if her name is wrong) I love herrrr so much!

We rode the high roller on my 22nd birthday and we just so happened to step into bubble #22! We went on at 7:50pm and there was no line. The lighting was perfect and by the time we were done, it was night-time and then we saw a huge line. Glad we got on right before subset. Im terrified of heights but it was very slow moving and very enjoyable.

Going on the high roller was a good time! We have been on the wheel in London, the London Eye and this was larger. We went on a Sunday, about 8PM, no wait. There was a large indoor area that was disneyland style with their line setup so I can imagine that this ride does get busy. 

We paid $5 extra for the booze car. OK. Think about this, you pay $5 extra (per person) and get unlimited drinks while on board! The bartender was ready and set up when we walked on to get our drink on. Then, at the top she served everyone a shot. She was very personable and knew how to make drinks fast. This was key, as you had limited time to drink. You CAN get drinks on the normal cars just before getting on, there is a full bar. But $5!!!! How can you go wrong? 

The sights were good, it was amazing that some of the hotels were still taller than the wheel. There is an outdoor shopping plaza that leads from the strip to the wheel, all new. Lots of food and shopping. There is valet parking at the base of the wheel and taxis to take home if you are a bit tipsy.

My family and I had a great time riding the High Roller! We arrived at 2 pm on a weekday and bought our tickets with a locals discount at the box office and were able to walk right onto a pod all to ourselves without waiting in line. The views were incredible and I would highly recommend taking a ride!

The ride doesn't worth the money. It costs $25 at day time and $35 at night time. A $2 fee per ticket was charged at the ticket booth. 

It was crowded. There were about 30 people in the pod. During the ride, the people were standing on the strip side and blocking the view. They don't want to walk around and look at the other side. I saw the people with different hair styles. :(

I think it is better to spend the money to upgrade the hotel room, go up to the Eiffel Tower or take the helicopter ride.

With sweeping views of the mountains, the desert, and the strip, this is a great idea for a first time Vegas visitor.
One of my my travel companions was a first time Vegas visitor, so we did this excursion for her benefit. To save a little cash, we purchased the day pass and were surprisingly pleased with the view. In fact, as a Vegas veteran, I'd say the daytime view is preferable over the night time as you can see so much more of the topography around the city. 
The pod itself looks very Jetson-y. It very slowly creepy pasts the entrance line and you walk on. A pod can fit 40 but I thought my pod with about 20 people, a beer cart with a bartender was comfortable if not cozy. Just be sure you like the people in your pod because the ride is about 30 minutes- no gettin' off! And no bathrooms on the pods either- don't drink too much!

This was an awesome experience! My wife and I got a Groupon for the Happy 1/2 Hour. We went early right when they opened on a Friday noon. We were the only two in the pod and we had the bar and the really cool bartender to ourselves. The drinks were sooo good! The bartender (Can't remember her name) was very knowledgeable about the ride and the area so it was fun talking with her. The time in the ride goes real quick but it is worth ever minute the views were breathtaking! It is so fun to see Vegas from that high up. I can't wait to do that at night! I have already recommended this to quite a few people!! This is a must do in Vegas!

It was an enjoyable ride. I bought a discount ticket for the daytime in the pod with an open bar. That was the right decision because it meant no rowdy kids, and it gave us a bartender who enetertained us with her stories of tthings that have happened on the ride. I don't think it would have been worth it to take the normal ride. It's not just the fact there is alcohol. It was the general atmosphere of the ride.

This was an awesome experience and a great way to view the city! Like others, we had a Groupon deal that was well worth the money. I don't think we would have been as happy if we paid full-price. We chose the "Happy Hour" special and had an 8pm reservation. While it was fun, we did have quite a few people in our "pod" (20).  Regardless, you were able to get about 2 drinks a person.

It should be noted that, if you purchase a Groupon, you will need to make a reservation in person the day you want to redeem the coupon. I wish we would have known this...

The High Roller is an over 500 feet tall gigantic ferris wheel on the Vegas strip. It is owned by and operated by Caesars Entertainment Corporation. My husband and I had a blast riding the ferris wheel at night and viewing the strip from far above. It is a super-fun ride, a little scary the first time, gulped down a large mixed drink before getting on he world's largest observation wheel. The wheel takes about 1/2 hour to complete a full revolution, has enclosed glass windows and bench seating and plenty of room to stand, walk around and take photographs. There are also special packages available, such as a daytime yoga experience 550 in the air woo-hoo, a chocolate and wine package, and happy half hour cabins with a full bar, private parties, special events, you name it!. You can even get married in one of the cabins! I would suggest magic hour/sunset for the best views and photo opportunities.

Great view. I think experiences my vary here. Depending on the size of the group in your bubble and depending on the attitudes of the other in your bubble as well. 
We had 6 people and it was was a about right. No one getting in anyones way and everyone was friendly. This is a fairly nice tourtisy trap for Vegas. The downfall on this place is the price per ticket if you are not a local. I would not have paid full price for this ride which is 35 bucks a pop at night. 

If you have the money to spend and 30 minutes to set back an relax i would recomend this. If saving money for something better and more value is your thing than I would pass.

My husband and I went during happy hour on a Tuesday. Going up on a Tuesday lol lol was fun, the view was beautiful and the drinks were graciously flowing. I will definitely be getting more deals on groupon so I can return for happy hour.

What a great addition to the Strip! As with almost everything in Vegas, the rack rate is high, but you can find deals, especially on Groupon / Living Social.  Note: ) If you have a prepaid voucher, you have to go to the Concierge desk first, then you just walk right in. Or at least we did. The night we went it was cold, so there weren't any crowds. 

The line keeps moving because the wheel keeps moving. It doesn't stop for loading/unloading. That makes the ride smooth as well. You almost don't feel like you're moving, until you realize your position has changed.  We opted not to be in a booze car, because the idea of being trapped in a pod with drunk people wasn't appealing, but those pods were empty when we saw them go by.  Since the crowds were small, they weren't overloading the pods, either, which was great. We got great shots from every angle. Unlike a lot of observation rides, this one has views from almost every point on the wheel. 

Interesting bit of trivia: Since the High Roller went in and has become so popular, the backside hotel rooms have been upgraded to "High Roller view rooms". That's Vegas for you...adding value through marketing. :)

Great place to take out of towners, or to add to a family Strip excursion.

Surprisingly good and better than expected. I'm rounding up from a 3.5 stars because of the price and parking. We bought groupon or living social deals or something and had a pretty good discount. 

The location isn't so great (Linq) but there was also some kind of an outdoor mall very nearby so it was convenient to access other bars and restaurants as well as shops. Parking was slightly confusing and we ended up parking at Linq hotel and walked quite a bit over, but I believe instead of the structure you could park in the outdoor lot which is a lot closer. since we had purchased a voucher we had to go to the ticket booth to redeem tickets which wasn't super clear but it's also not rocket science. I believe you're also not limited to only purchasing drinks inside so my hubs and I bought drinks for cheaper at the bar across from the entrance and walked in. We didn't get the all you can drink option since it was half an hour and I hate rushed drinking (can't win). 

The view was pretty amazing and I don't think there's anything quite like it in vegas. The most similar experience I've had to this is the Great Wheel in Seattle. This was slightly more impressive because of all the twinkling lights and just the lit-up-ness that is vegas. Our car wasn't really very crowded so hubs and I enjoyed our drinks occasionally sat and walked around took pictures, etc. There were some people who dominated one corner, just constantly took pictures the ENTIRE 30 minutes and that was annoying but whatever. The organization also was not bad at all and I also noticed they were equipped to accommodate the handicapped which is fantastic. It's one of those things that's worth it if you do it once, I don't have a burning desire to go back to this anytime soon but it was definitely a cool experience.

Probably the most overpriced tourist thing you can do in Vegas at $36 pp (after dark) but everyone should do it once. 
It's an amazing view and it's great that they don't pack people in the pods. We only had maybe 15 people so there was no issue getting to a window. 
Cheesey green screen pictures before you ride not withstanding.

This was our second time on the High Roller, last time was during the day. We did the happy hour ride this time and it was awesome!! Our bartender Cheryl was originally from Rhode Island and had fun and lively attitude :) You should definitely experience both the day and night hours.
Beautiful view at night and well done.  Remember to take fun people and drinks with you.  You are in closed space for 20 mins... good times though!

The High Roller is located in the LINQ Promenade, a block off the main strip. It's the world's tallest Ferris wheel standing at 550-foot tall. It takes half an hour to get to the highest point. You get into these circular observation cabins that can fit about 40 people. Some of the cabins have bars in them and some don't. There are a few seats inside the cabin. If you don't manage to get a seat, it's standing room only. I lucked out. It was only my husband and I, with another couple in our cabin. We were free to roam around on all sides, and get seated when we felt like it. They have TV screens inside the cabin to tell you about the High Roller. It also tells you how high you are and how many more minutes until you reach the top.

The view of the Vegas strip at night from the High Roller is beautiful. Both sides of the strip is fully lighted with moving lights. I'm afraid of heights and thought that I would freak out, but I didn't. The cabins don't move that fast and I was too busy taking in the scenery.

They have packages or you can host open bar parties. I'm not a drinker, so I got in the cabin without a bar. The cabin that was in front of us that had the open bar was packed full of people. 

If you go during the day the price is cheaper than going at night. I don't remember how much they wanted for the day but at night it's $36.95 per person, without the open bar. I managed to snag a deal. I was at the Paris Hotel gift shop purchasing tickets to get on the Eiffel Tower. The clerk told me about this deal that they were having, $33 for both the Eiffel Tower and the High Roller. I jumped on it as I was planning on doing both anyway. If you're in Vegas, you have to try the High Roller at least once.

High roller is SUCH a nice interlude from the hustle and craziness of the strip. It's like a much needed nap that we never realized we need as babies. It kills crankiness. Plus, if you absolutely can't live without a cocktail in hand, there are several beverage pods that cater to you lushes.

Prices are very reasonable (except for the typical overpriced photos), but if you have ANY points on your total rewards cards, use them.

I've been on this thing both during the day and night, and I honestly think you should try it both times. Views are incredibly spectacular, but soooo different. Amazing perspectives.

Wheelchair? No problem. They are completely equipped to handle handicapped access, which makes it that much more amaze balls.

I kind of have a love/hate relationship with High Roller.  It was an amazing view but a little pricey.  It was slow and kind of boring but the view was amazing.  

I can't make up my mind if I like it or hate it.  It was worth doing if you have the time and extra dollars.  I am not much of drinker to be on it drunk.  

I guess you can take some kids on it and they'd enjoy it more. 

This should be a 3.5 rating rather than a full 4...

An awesome experience. The view was very beautiful. Single ride takes approximately 25-30 mins. It's super fun especially at night. It runs till 2 am. So last ride is around 1:30 am. Yelp has a coupon if you check-in there but I was told that you can only use it when you are going for the second time and for eligibility you have to carry the old ticket and show review on Yelp at the counter. We went around 1:00 am so the lines were empty at that point. Watching Bellagio fountain show might be a good idea. The cabins were big & some of the cabins had bar counters too. The staff was nice & friendly.

I went during the day mid-morning and there was only a group of 4 elderly people with us, so our ride was pleasant. I don't recommend coming during the day. The view would be comparable to any high-rise hotel on the strip or probably the observation deck at Eiffel Tower. The strip is really pretty at night with all the lights and the Bellagio Fountains so I imagine it would be nicer to see. Warning, it's 30 minutes being in a pod with no cell service!

Our ride on the High Roller was amazing with Lupe as bartender, we had such a great time we decided to ride again the following night. What a mistake that turned out to be with Tyler as the bar tender who was rude and doesn't care about the experience... actually more about making his work easier instead of entertainingNext time you visit Las Vegas and consider this experience...ask for Lupe as your bartender.

I went on the High Roller a couple of weeks ago while I was in Vegas. Man what a treat! The views are spectacular and the ride is so smooth. I rode it at midnight. The pod that you ride in is nice with a couple of seats and flat screen TV s. I even paid a little extra to get the full bar. Well worth it! The ride cost $36 but with the full bar it was $52. It lasts about 30 minutes. Considering that I won the money it really didn't cost me anything! If you're in Vegas I highly recommend the High Roller!

We purchased tickets through Living Social to ride the High Roller. We went to the ride and were told to go to the concierge and exchanged them for tickets, everything was good until we were told that it was down for scheduled maintenance, we then came back at the we were told and it was still down, but now with no ETA as to what time it would be up. We were then told we had to get a refund from Living Social that there was nothing they could do for us. We in turn asked to speak with a Mgr. Her name was Carolyn, instead of trying to find what she could for us or find our length of stay and offering tickets for another day or time, she said that there was nothing she could do, To go get a refund from the third party. When we asked how we needed to do this she became overwhelmed and called her security guard, Lee over to make us leave. My husband did not make any gestures of hostility or raise his voice to her to instigate this reaction. As we were leaving Lee went to put his hand on me to ensure I was leaving and I stated "Don't you dare put your hands on me, you are not allowed to touch anyone as a security guard." Lee then said "I can't help it if its an accident." I then said "You have no right to touch me." And left. We went to the concierge explained what happened, they made our vouchers were unreserved and proceeded to the main office to find out who is Carolyn's Mgr. was. His name is Jim Donahue. After explaining again the Security Mgr. Chris (who was very helpful and understood how not to escalate an already escalated and stressful situation) tried to call for Jim to come and speak with us but he was to busy. So, we ended up with Carolyn again. Not only did she come with an attitude stating (her exact words) "How can I help you again?" Then instead of listening to my husband speak, she proceeded to talk over him saying that it wasn't her fault that things were unorganized, but resorted to putting the blame on her marketing department. Realizing he was going nowhere with this he left. On another note, I wouldn't want to be in Jim Donahue's shoes, having to deal with customers Carolyn has previously delt with.

High Roller was cool, but glad I got a Groupon; otherwise, overpriced. Good views, not horrible drinks, and it's something to say you've done.

Just make sure you don't get stuck in a cabin with a shrill screaming child that takes your $10 drink while irresponsible mom isn't paying attention, which was our experience. 3 stars for lack of age screening.

I wasn't sold on this place at first glance. We were there for Memorial Day weekend and no deals were being accepted so we had the single option of buying full price tickets. At $52 a ticket for the night happy half hour ride it was a tough sell, but when you're in Vegas that money doesn't go that far anyway so we sprang for it. We ended up thinking it was worth the money. It felt different than anything else we had done in Vegas so far. Definitely go at night when the views are best and make sure to get the happy half hour ticket. During the day would be pretty underwhelming... The bartender was great at giving us drinks quick and even made a round of shots at the top. They want you to at least try and get your money's worth. I'd recommend this to everyone, especially when you can get deals on non-holiday weekends.

Honestly I really didn't want to go on this ride because it was super touristy and I wanted to avoid that because they tend to be super pricey but our family begged us to go and I'm glad I did. I have family that live in vegas and the were some card holder so for the 5 of us it costs us about $50 which was a lot cheaper than it would've been considering it would've been almost $150. Its cheaper to go during the day because after 5PM the prices get more expensive. When we went on the ride the sun was just starting to set. The line for the tickets moved pretty fast. They check your bag before you go in. We bought the one with no open bar and when we went on the ride we shared it with a family of 4 so it was 9 of us in this big bubble. Good size because it was a lot of space. The ride is 30 min log and goes by kinda fast. Going around sunset was the best because you'd catch the sun setting down at the top while the strip lights up. Personally thought the cost of this ride was overpriced but its touristy so its expected. There is seating on the ride and handles for you to hold on you. You can get a 360 view of vegas and it's great.

Great view and great bartender!

We went at 9:00 PM last night and really enjoyed it.

Look for deals on Travelzoo,  Groupon, etc before purchasing tickets. We got the Happy Hour Night for about $39. The price at the window is $54.

My main complaint is that they could have put fewer people in the POD. We were a little cramped and people looked frustrated because they wanted to look out a section while others were standing and talking.  

Regardless,  still had fun and the bartender kept the drinks combing.  

 Scared of heights? Seriously,  don't even worry about it. This doesn't give you that "high" feeling. 

Pictures? Turn off the flash if you want cool city pictures. 

Don't forget to tip the bartender!

Props on the designer (Arup Engineering) and their finished product. It's hard to believe that this is the latest.. tallest "ferris wheel" in the world since their 2008 Singapore Flyer standing at 541 ft. 

The high roller is 9 ft taller than the flyer and bragging rights becomes ours!!!

A great tourist attraction hands down and worth every cent if you decide to hop on!

The 360° glass view is breathtaking. Located as the main attraction in the newest addition to the Las Vegas strip "The Linq".. but more than that.. it exposes the true beauty of this small city in the dessert at a view you can only find in comparison to it's freestanding cousin "Stratosphere" 

Be part of 2014 history and do it once!

-SCA
This is a great tourist attraction to check out at least once during your Las Vegas visit. I have only tried it during the day, but I bet it would be even more amazing at night with all the lights.

The name itself will make you want to start singing...I feel a song coming on..."Big wheel keep on turnin' Proud Mary keep on burn in' Rollin', rollin', rollin' on the river..."

The kids had been begging to go to the "giant ferris wheel" so we finally made it. Honestly, at first I couldn't wait to visit this new tourist destination, but as the summer "rolled" along, I thought, "Ugh, 30 minutes in a ball in the heat?"  I was wrong!  And I'm so glad I'm the mommy robot and do what my kids want because this was a winner!

We took advantage of the daytime rates, kids under 12 free rates, and a locals discount rate!  No military rate. 

We walked up to the window and bought our tickets-no line and friendly friendly service by all the staff members...family of four only $33! Woo-hoo!

We zoomed up the escalators and found a beverage bar and restrooms to use prior to boarding.  You can take drinks with you too.

We were very lucky, on this day most folks were watching the World Cup Soccer match when USA was playing-so it was a ghost town.  Staff was very friendly and directed us into our own air-conditioned pod! Woo-hoo! 

The "ferris wheel" is the largest observation wheel in the world.  It moves very slow, with non-stop playing music (it's actually the same music heard in the Linq shopping area).  

A non-stop video guides you and your informed how high you are and other safety features.  Since we had the entire pod to ourselves we decided to dance, take pictures and just have fun.  It went by very quickly and the views were incredible of the entire city.

The kids loved it, however, one of my kids did have some anxiety and felt that the "ball was going to fall off." I suddenly realized he had a fear of heights!  This was a new revelation.  I was happy that we had the pod to ourselves because we could slowly work towards the window and take our time (30 minutes) to let him enjoy the sights and calm down his anxiety and fear.  Upon the ride ending he was ready to go on again and said he would be brave next time!  AAAAhhhh.  So I guess we will be going back!

Don't miss and take advantage of these great summer rates!

It's pretty neat. We went on Black Friday and they had a two-for-one deal so the price wasn't too bad. But if we had to pay full price it would not have been worth it. But, on the whole, it was pretty cool. The views are really good of the strip and the surrounding Las Vegas area. Pictures don't turn out so good because the glass on the inside tends to be smudged. Also, lots of drunk douche bags, but that's pretty much par for the course in Las Vegas.

The biggest drawback is definitely the price. It's very expensive.

We had a living social deal for the day time happy hours. We were the only person in car with the bartender. 

Great views, ok selection on drinks. In your in the area def check it out. It's the biggest observation wheel!

Yes, it's a little on the pricey side, but opt to go during the day and the tickets are less expensive and there are fewer people. The engineering was beautiful on this 550 ft behemoth. You can see much of the strip and beyond (hence, go during the day) during this 30-minute ride.

They have a bar before the loading platform and you can bring drinks inside the ride. We had two other couples with our family of four so there was plenty of room and we ended up taking pictures for each other!

The cabins are air conditioned and there's two seating areas (holds about 8 people) so you can relax, enjoy the cool reprieve, and just appreciate this great new addition to the strip!

Husband and I went while on mini trip to Vegas- we got the open bar pod and it was worth the $10 extra. Short wait time during the day (less than 10 mins) - well worth the price- beautiful views- plan on going back at night! Also- this attraction is located on a little strip that is a nice place to walk and has cafe or bars available to sit outside and have drinks or lunch.

A fun one-time ride, for sure! 

On our first trip up we were lucky enough to go on the "alcohol pod" where Ketel One was serving up 3 sample cocktails using their flavored vodka. We received unlimited "tastes" despite them saying we would receive 1 taste each. This was a definite plus and made the ride way more exciting! 

Our line seemed pretty long but moved quickly. And since we opted to wait for the Ketel One pod, we probably wound up waiting a few trips more than we would have had to if we rode on the "regular" one. 

The pod was bigger than I expected and, although I think each pod fits 40, ours wasn't nearly full. I thought I'd feel more "claustrophobic" in there but it was pretty roomy. There are some great views but I can't say they were anything I haven't seen before from some of the other vantage points on the strip. Got to watch the Bellagio fountains from up high, see plenty of the strip and beyond. 

We went during a half-off for locals time and I probably wouldn't have paid full price. A total ripoff but if you're doing the tourist thing I recommend going up at least once.

Absolutely loved the High Roller!  I'd recommend the happy hour package as it is fun to power drink over the 30 minute ride. Our group and bartender were both great. It is fun from the start as you get on and off of the moving carriage. The view alone is well worth the price.

Pretty fun experience. Tickets came with the promotion I used to book our room at the Linq. They were only good until 5 when the rates must go up, but we went right at 5 and got to see the sun set while we were on it. We didn't get a bubble with a bar in it, but there's a bar where you can purchase overpriced drinks before you get on. There was no line at all and they only put 8 people in our bubble, so we had plenty of room. I'm not sure, but on a busy day, it wouldn't surprise me if they packed it a little tight. The ride was very smooth, you could hardly feel it moving.

A good deal for $20 or whatever it was.  I will look into the open bar one next time, even though I just want unlimited soda, ha

It wasn't good for my vertigo or claustrophobia but I would do it again.

Doing the daytime happy 1/2 hour was really worth it because I bought our tickets through a Travelzoo deal so it was only $39 for the two of us, though I knew the two of us wouldn't be able to drink much in 30 minutes. Sure enough, we were quite inebriated afterwards but the views were so nice. We luckily made it there just before 5 so we got the night time views but for day time pricing. It was really nice to be able to see all the lights on. Our pod also luckily had just a small group of about 7 so we had enough space to walk around. The bartender was a funny guy who was nice enough to make us all a round to take to go. While there you can only have one drink at a time. Make sure to bring some change to tip. :)

I had a little anxiety as I reached the top but so cool to be up that high. Take the monorail from MGM and it drops you off right at the LINQ! I bought the 3 for $58.50 on Groupon, worth the money! They have a bar right before you get on where you can buy drinks, beware the bar tender is old & bitter :/

Fun times on the high roller! 
This attraction is very cool! You get a fabulous view of Las Vegas! There is even a pod that has a bartender and serves alcohol/drinks! It worth the extra few bucks, you can easily down 3 drinks if you want too... I brought my own on, they also will let you do that if its in a plastic cup! I liked the  video tour guide,  he was quite funny but I wouldn't recommend buying the High Roller souvenir drinking-pod-cup with straw, though it looks really cool, the cap doesn't seal and it leaks like crazy!

In the newly revamped Linq section of Vegas (bye bye sticky Imperial Palace), lies this towering wheel of fun. If you aren't afraid of heights and want to take in aerial views of the whole area or see the Vegas lights from up high at night, then this is definitely worth checking out at least once. 

Be forewarned, it's not cheap. We got a deal for 2 for 1 with Total Rewards but it'll set you back about $25 - $30 per person depending on when you go. With that in mind, you might as well pay the extra $5 to do the bar car! Yes folks, they have a bar car on the ferris wheel complete with all the booze you can drink in the 30 minute ride. 

We went right about sunset time the week of Christmas and it wasn't very busy at all but I imagine the lines can get pretty long during their busier season. Another warning, the cars don't stop moving for you to get on like a typical ferris wheel. It moves really slowly but it tripped me up a bit getting on. I'm normally white knuckling on an old fashioned ferris wheel but the big, enclosed cars on this make it a lot less scary. It's nice you get a full 30 minutes to take in all the views too. 

I wouldn't say this is something you need to do every time you visit Vegas but it's definitely worth doing at least once, and again, bar car!

I went into the ticket counter to get information about the different offerings for the High Roller. There I was greeted by the most uninterested customer service representative I've ever encountered!!! Her name is Amonde.  Don't wear a name tag if you don't want to work!!!!!! She never made eye contact and her answers were vague!!! If all the employees are like her you'll never have customers!!!  Don't go to Amonde!!

"Vegas Must Do"

Definitely a must do. I paid an extra $15 for the drink pod and had unlimited drinks for the roughly 35min ride. The views were spectacular. Went at 10:30pm on a Friday night so absolutely no lines and only had one other couple in the pod with us. It was intimate and beautiful with full view of Vegas. Just be careful in heels, the pods don't necessarily stop so can be a bit hard to hop on and off while still moving in heels. :)

Visited October 2015
We loved it. There were no lines! We were greeted by friendly employees. The cars were cool and not crowded. The views were fabulous. My son had a blast. Free for kids under 12. Great entertainment.

Over rated...most of what you see is in between massive amounts of buildings you really do not get a view of the strip until you're almost to the top which is more than halfway there.... I don't know maybe it's because I'm from Seattle and we have an incredible Ferris wheel on the pier where every inch of your view is spectacular

Pensávamos que não estava funcionando! De longe ela parece estar imóvel!!! Ao chegar perto você percebe que é justamente o contrário, ela não para nunca!!!!

Uma das melhores experiências de Las Vegas é essa que é a maior roda gigante desse nosso planeta azulzinho - alguns pés acima da London Eye, seja lá o que isso significa no raio desse país que não usa o sistema métrico!

A partir do crepúsculo o preço dá uma subida e há a opção - também mais cara - de ir numa cabine com bar! Vacilamos de não comprar essa opção, intencionando de dividir um drink nas alturas! Não havia a opção de compra lá, apenas na fila, que dependendo do dia parece ser gigante. Tivemos sorte de ser muito rápido!

"Como a vista é linda da roda gigante é tão grande" - uma pena não ter música brasileira para animar a viagem de cerca de 40 minutos! Só pensava no Raimundos!

Lá de cima você tem uma privilegiada vista para o deserto, de um lado, e do outro uma boa vista para alguns dos principais cassinos e hotéis da famosa street!

Ao chegar no cume há um momento bem espacial no sistema de vídeo e som! E se você tiver sorte como minha namorada e eu, ainda vai conseguir o belo espetáculo das fontes do Bellagio lá de cima!!

This was so exciting! You can see great views of Las Vegas at 550ft. in the air. You shouldn't miss this opportunity whether your a visitor or local. It's beautiful at night and I plan on going again during the day time! There's a chocolate tasting option and so much more available.

Found a groupon deal for happy hour for two, $79 bucks or something like that. I would definitely recommend the high roller to anyone who visits the Las Vegas Strip! 

When we got there around 9:30 pm, the line was starting to get pretty long, but it was moving quickly which is always a good thing. Once we got our tickets, we had received a ticket for a buy one get one free alcoholic beverage at the bar before walking to the actual high roller. That was really cool. We also got another coupon for I believe 15% off at the gift shop, which is also nice. 

The happy hour roller had its own separate line (v.i.p) didn't have a big line at all, my boyfriend and I were the first ones in line. Then maybe around seven other people showed up. Ten minutes later, we all got on the high roller, which doesn't not stop moving!! You actually have to get on it while rotating! Pretty epic. There is a net underneath, just in case! Our bartender was friendly from the start!! I can't remember his name... But, he was extremely fun and made sure everyone had a drink in their hand! Since I am 21, I asked him what went good with skyy vodka, and he started mixing away! I should have asked him what it was called, it was delicious! 

Amazing view. The lights at night were amazing and everything looked beautiful! Felt like a mini party in there!! I would definitely do the high roller again!! Our bartender even offered me a drink on the way out! Of course, I took the offer! Overall, it was an amazing experience and I highly recommend the happy hour wheel. Thirty minutes of an amazing view with an open bar! Or, you can just go without the happy hour deal and I'm sure it's just as fun!! That view is amazing and I would recommend going at night!

The High Roller was pretty cool, if you like big ferris wheels. The cars can fit quite a few people, but my husband and I opted for the dry car (the ones without an open bar), and since all the other people in line were waiting for boozy cars, we got a whole car to ourselves! The view is really cool, especially at night (which is when we went). There are tv screens at the top with some dude that talks a lot - facts about the wheel, facts about Vegas, blah blah blah. I really didn't listen much to him. I was too busy taking pictures. With the bright lights of the wheel, it is tough to get really phenomenal photos as there are some pretty bright reflections, but if you have photo skills, you can make it work. A fun thing to do!

Used the groupon for the happy hour here and we were not disappointed. We had a blast, for HH they roll in a booze set up complete with bartender and you party and drink for 30 min, we even got a beak wetter for the road. Super, super fun

It's a good idea to buy the tix online, in advance, for cheaper. But they give you a time slot and you have to move your Vegas schedule around for that, so screw it! Did it twice so far and both times we bought tix here, when we got here! Because we do Vegas right! You can buy drinks at the bar before you get in line. Also, go the bathroom, you'll be stuck in there for at least half an hour with a drink in your hand! And if you get the open bar pod (costs a little bit more) you can have quite a few drinks with no bathroom in sight! Great views, especially at night, fun selfies, doesn't feel like moving at all, but if you are afraid of heights you might feel a little uncomfortable. Same if you are claustrophobic, but enough about me, enjoy the ride!

Had an amazing experience on this ride. Each pod can fit 40 people but they only put 15-- that way there's more room to move around. This is the tallest observation wheel in the world! 550 feet high! Don't forget to bring your Camera/Polaroid :) & I'd recommend going during sunset or night time when all the lights are on.

Not a good experience for me, I am scared of height, and I am claustrophobic, if it weren't for hubby, I would never have agreed to go on this ride, it wasn't fun for me, I couldn't move and couldn't look out, I just stayed at one spot for 30 minutes..... The ride was very slow, but I could still feel the shaking now and then, probably because of the high wind that night. What I didn't like the most was the ride didn't stop when we stepped on it, it was very scary! 

Hubby bought fast lane pass, it was $60 per person, general admission is $25, check in at the computers outside the High Roller ride building, very convenient. Turned out we didn't need fast pass at all, we went there so late, there was no lines, only very few people were going to the ride, darn! 

Minus the scary parts, the views were amazing, at 550 foot tall, 360 degree sights, tourists could see the entire night views of Las Vegas, maybe even further, it was actually pretty cool. They serve drinks at a small lounge area before getting on the ride, we bought 2 frozen drinks, 2 fireball shots and a bottle water for $48. They take photos for tourists on the way to the ride.

It could be a fun and different experience in Vegas, a good place for a date too, of course assuming both are not scared of heights!

Ps. Valet parking offers bottle waters, remember to ask a few.
