Best deal in town. The half hour happy hour. Can say no more. You have to do it its an unlimited bar included if you upgrade. 

Its a Vagus must do its line husband day care.

Loved the views! We went at night and were able to see the fountains at the Bellagio. Our bar tender (Fran or Frank, can't remember his name) was super friendly and kept the drinks flowing. He definitely made the whole experience top notch. Glad we did it! I'd love to do it again.

This afternoon I went on the High Roller, which is the world's tallest observation wheel.

The High Roller is a 550-foot tall giant ferris wheel. The wheel began construction in 2011 and opened in March 2014. The High Roller features 28 spherical passenger cabins which can accommodate up to 40 passengers each and is illuminated with dynamic multicolored LED lights nightly.

It cost $25 for the 30 minute ride.  You can spend an extra $5 and go in the happy hour cabin where you can drink all you want (I passed).

There were just three of us in our cabin.  The views were great!

The cabins don't stop ... you get on as it's moving.  There is a net underneath in case you misstep.

It was fun and a great way to see the city.

AWESOME VIEW! We were also staying at the stratosphere so we had already seen it all but the whole ride was awesome. why the 4 stars & not 5? A Sprite & Coke was $14. $14 frickin dollars. Anyways, overall good. but do not buy drinks

To much fun, especially if your family members are afraid of heights  made my 1st visit (5/30) since the GRAND OPENING whenever it opened. I live in VEGAS and I don't follow the crowd, but I'm happy that I got to have this experience with my cousin's from CALI and my girlfriend.

You will laugh at the, "We are now at 420ft marker, WE ARE REALLY HIGH GUYS!"

FAMILY HOUR PACKAGE (Saturdays 10:00am-11:30am, before the ride opens to the general public). $50 includes 2 adults, 3 kids, 3 toys (valued at $12 ea in the gift shop), 3 juice boxes. Because we got to go in before it was open to the public, we had NO LINES, NO WAITING, and our PRIVATE POD with nobody else inside. If you have kids, you know how very important these things are. 

The High Roller is the world's largest observation wheel standing at 550 feet tall at the very tip. 
The ride takes 30 minutes to make a roundtrip. 
The ride does not stop. (Translation: you need to pay attention when you get into your pod or you'll fall into the net below.)
The pod fits up to 40 people. 
There are 28 pods.   

PRICE in Mar 2015: pay attention to times of day, day of week, and whether you want bottomless alcoholic drinks/bar in your pod because the prices fluctuate. These were the prices at the time of our visit last week. The website looks like they may have raised the prices already. 

Non alcoholic pods:
Day: $24.95/adult.
Night $34.95/adult
Kids 12yrs and under are FREE. 

There are group rates (10+), family rates, and family hour rates, so check out all your options online before buying your ticket because it can get pricey.  

Luckily for me I always follow in the footsteps of some great yelpers who have paved the way. I had no idea that this High Roller even existed in Las Vegas until Rod U. checked into their "Happy Hour" and Michael C. reviewed this attraction last month. Thank you to both Michael and Rod for making me a High Roller rider! This was one of the highlights of our trip to Vegas with the kids.

First time taking the high roller. And it's the best thing to do on the last night at Vegas. 

The high roller was recommended to us by the concierge and it's a good thing we did it. 

It's a 30min ride but memorable. Each pod doesn't have much sitting room But don't worry you won't spend much time sitting anyways. 

I definitely would recommend checking this out. You'll feel like your on top of the world once you reach the apex of the ride.
High Roller was more like Sloooooooow Roller.   So slow that we all thought it wasn't even moving.  Make sure to go at night!  We went at night and all the lights were amazing.

Have been to the High Roller twice. From the parking valet to the experience, it was excellent! I highly recommend this attraction to anyone coming to Las Vegas. It is NOT a ride, it is truly an observation experience. There is no feeling of movement or bouncing or anything. It is super smooth and you do not even know you are high up on this observation pod. I loved it and our guests have totally enjoyed this part of their trip. Remember you can see the Bellagio fountains too and it is a really cool way to experience that as well. I have only gone at night and really do look forward to viewing during the day as well. It is fun and a great way to see the Las Vegas lights.

The view from the top is amazing, but the narration is beyond obnoxious, and being forced to suffer through Avicii's music in an enclosed capsule does not give me a good feeling. Not even sometimes.

Do it once to say you did it and to see what the big deal is about.

But don't do it full price. Caesars is desperate to put bodies on that thing so if you throw a rock in the air you'll find a discount, deal or promotion of some kind.

I love ferris wheels and have been wanting to go on the High Roller observation wheel since it opened. My guy finally surprised me with tickets on an impromptu date night and off we went. Note that there are tons of discounts to be had (military, local, senior, Yelp check in, online offer, etc)- find one that works for you because $35/pp (adult) is ridiculous.

Pre-purchase your tickets online to save time in line. The boarding process is long and somewhat disorganized process involving an escalator, a stop by a bar, "mandatory" photo ops (just keep walking), and a maze. Just keep walking, and eventually you'll get to the boarding area. Hit the bathroom when you get a chance, because the line and 30 minute ride can mean an hour til you get to use it again.

TIP: get in the front right corner of your pod as soon as you board so you are in the best spot for photos. Pods aren't overly filled- expect about 20-30 people, and there is seating available. Some pods have bars and HH, we did not do this option. As everyone else says, the view is actually not that impressive and only rave worthy for the 3-5 minutes spent at the top. There's a guide/trivia video playing during the trip, complete with dad jokes. After disembarking, you exit through the gift shop.

This thing is apparently bigger than the London eye so we had to ride it! It's a pretty nice view up there and would be good to have the gondola just to yourselves which isn't always the case cuz they said it can fit up to 40 peeps.. we got lucky and it was just me and the hubby when we got on it.. :)

The views were great. We went at night which is 10 dollars more (35 vs 25) but it was well worth it to see the skyline at night. Some of the cabins have bars so you can drink for the entire 30 minutes. Definitely a must try in Vegas but not sure if I would do it multiple times. Only negative is like most attractions they have the annoying green screen picture you can buy

PS: We had a coupon for 5 dollars off and in addition they are currently running a promotion that if you text vote for them for best attraction you get a free drink. The free drink is large and can even be a frozen drink

High roller was good but could have done without the happy hour one becuz they water it down and it's more juice than liquor.. best advice is to save yourself 15 bucks and pre drink. Nice to see but not as turned up as you think more like elevator music

A must see "Vegas" tourist attractions. The High Roller behind the Linq Hotel. 550 Ft High Ferris Wheels that  Spins for 30 Minutes. Bright with lights at night. "The World Tallest Observation Wheel". 

It rotates and revolves a full 360 Degrees Wheels for 30 Minutes. See through glass ball cabin with closed indoor bench seats and advertising tv. Fit up to 40 people maximum. You get a Full see through View high and low of Vegas and the Linq Hotel view. Day and Night. Kids young as 7 can you go.

You get the option of taking personal photos with different High Rollers background and frame to keep. Cost $25.

Tickets options of buying VIP, Open bar. Unlimited drinks for 30 Minutes. Or pay an extra $20/person at the door. Open as late as until 2AM. 

Prices are about $25/ person during the day. $35/person at night. After 5PM. Or pay All Day Admission for $59.95 Express Lane. No waiting passes.

There is A High Roller Gift shop when you get out. Down the escalator. Chooses are Toys,t-shirt,toys etc. and more merchandises.

After seeing that it was finally open, I decided to give a try. It's easy to get there. When you see Linq sign on strip, you turn into a alley full with stores and restaurants, at the end of the alley is the Ferris wheel. It was easy to get the tickets, although I think it was a little expensive. It was a very quiet day so I did not wait in line at all. I wanted to ride my own cabin; however, they had a rule that no single rider.  So I shared the cabin with a nice couple. I'm glad there were other people in the cabin because they took many pictures of mine while at the top. Cabins are fully covered. It takes around 40 minutes to make a full round trip. One cabin takes around 10-12 people I think. View was amazing. I'm glad I tried it. They have tv's inside that give you information, warn you when you are at top. If you are afraid of heights, you may want to sit at the middle of the cabin and don't get close to window or look down. Staff was very friendly. I think one time is a must but enough, may not repeat.

For my 23rd birthday, my boyfriend and I got a Groupon for a VIP ride package for two with Happy Half Hour passes for only $69! It was All-You-Can-Drink in the thirty minutes it takes for the Ferris wheel to go around once so you can enjoy the view of all Las Vegas. My boyfriend and I went around 6:30pm and, surprisingly, there were not very many people waiting in line. There were a total of only seven people in our passenger cabin (i.e., the bartender, two other couples, and my boyfriend and I). My boyfriend and I took advantage of the All-You-Can-Drink option because in that half-hour, we each had about four shots and five cocktails. I definitely had a good time because I cannot recall much of what happened the rest of the night ;)

I would recommend The High Roller to everyone!

The "ride" is 30 minutes long and a great view of the strip. There are several rooms between the entrance and where you board the Ferris wheel where you can drink and gamble so the time at the attraction can be as long as you want. Stand close to the door where you board for the best view of the strip.

You have to take 45 mins out of your life and experience this if you're in Las Vegas! 

A small group of us were in town for my brothers bachelor party and came across this awesome land mark on the strip. Are you KIDDING ME??? They actually have a ferris-wheel that has pods that hold 30-40 people with a open bar in each one??!! Wow! Who ever thought of this deserves a damn high fives and the fortune that they are making from it. 

We booked our appointment to board our pod and it came to about $40 per person for about 7 of us. You are given tickets like you would if you were seeing a movies in a theater or something. We decided to venture around the strip since we had time before our appointed time to board the pod. 

Once we arrived back and boarded the pod you are blown away with the size of it you can fit a lot of people in once of these pods and they have about 25 of them on this wheel. Amazing to see for your own eyes!!

The first thing I noticed was the open bar the was handing out drinks like they were going out of style. It was seriously like a mini club in this thing. It' took about 45 mins for the wheel to go completely around. However I was having so much fun I seemed like 5-10 mins haha. 

What a great experience!

The High Roller was the highlight of my trip, day or night you are guaranteed epic views of Las Vegas. The roomy, glass pod with 360 degree views takes you 550 feet into the air for a breath taking 30 min ride. I highly recommend taking the ride twice, once in the daytime and once while the sun is setting.

This was so much fun!!! My family and I went in the middle of the day which has its perks. We could see everything and it kind of satisfied my affinity for thrill rides (just by sitting on the edge of the pod). Supposedly they can fit 40 people in a pod. That seems like it would be pretty crowded to me but whatever!  We got drinks at the bar on the way in and didn't even finish our beers before we made it back around. We were wanting to pay the extra fee to have an open bar in the pod but the option was never offered? In the end we were glad we didn't because like I said, we didn't finish our one beer each for the most part. I'm sure it would be gorgeous at night with all the lights and being able to see the fountains at Bellagio.

BONUS. Our beers came in souvenir cups just like every other attraction in Vegas but still!

Cool experience - we only had 8 people in our pod so we could walk around, chat & snap.  It's about 30 minutes to make the loop and you don't even feel the movement - smooth!   There is a bar in the waiting area to get a beverage of your choice that you can take in the pod. The staff seemed bored, but the ride was pretty darn cool.

This place needs to work on their customer service. If there is no one in line, let people take a pod of their own. I realize that the kids working here are just doing their job, but the manager had totally a nonsensical rationale for their policy.  Whatever. 

The view was amazing and it's a fun alternative attraction in Vegas, but I hope they get their customer service up to par before the heavy tourist season.

This was probably one of my favorite things to do here in Las Vegas this go around. I thought I was going to be nervous because of the height and being so far up, but it wasn't bad at all you barely felt like you were moving. 

I bought a great deal on Groupon for the ride and the happy hour deal we had like 3 or 4 drinks a piece back to back after each other. The experience and the mood and the people that we shared the ride with all made it fun. We were helping the couples take pictures of them with the AMAZING night view of the strip and all of the city. The wait in the line downstairs where you buy tickets and check in took a LONG time like 45 minutes probably  and it was hot outside but WELL worth the experience and view a once in a life time thing.

Love the High Roller, it's conveniently located and fairly affordable for how long the ride is. I wouldn't say it's "the best" view in Vegas but it's definitely a unique view from very high up. The ride took around 30 minutes (if I'm remembering correctly). They have their own bar priced around the same as any bar in the nearby vicinity. You ride with around 6-8 other people but the pods you ride in are huge, the only time I remember wanting a bit more space was at the very top when everybody wanted a photo of the one corner with the best view. I went on a Thursday night during EDC week (late June) and we only had to wait around 10 minutes to ride. Tickets are very easily purchased at the electronic kiosks but CHECK GROUPON or online deal sites before going. 4 stars rather than 5 because while it is affordable they kind of mess with you on the pricing... it's the same price for 4 people vs. 3 but the kiosk doesn't mention that...

This is a very fun time with great views of all of Vegas, as expected. 

I have done this at day time and night and really do think the night views have that extra sparkle of twinkle lights and think its a better option for a first time roller. 

You can find coupons for this at many hotels that are Caesars owned or even ask at the total rewards desk. 

Oh and make sure you use the bathroom before going, sounds simple but the bathrooms at the bar area before you get on are very small and cramped. You could be waiting for some time.

A view from the top. We waited until our last night to go to the high roller.  It was last on the list because we figured if the line was outrageous or the cost was too much, we would just skip it.  Glad we didn't.  First off, they give a pretty good military, student, and senior discount so the price was okay.  Second, the wait from the time we walked in, bought our tickets, went through the line, and got on the ride was less than 15 minutes.  The ride itself takes about 30 minutes.  All in all, it is something I would recommend if this was a first trip to the strip but once you do it once you would not have to go back.

Slowest moving Ferris wheel ever......but it's an awesome slow moving Ferris wheel. 

The High Roller is a very unique Ferris wheel ride designed to soak in the view of Las Vegas once you reach to the very top. 

It takes about 30 minutes to reach to the top. Moving at one foot per second. 

The views are absolutely astonishing from every angle. Nothing but to enjoy the views. 

Do I recommend it...absolutely. 

One of the best views you will get of Las Vegas. You will be sad when you are coming down and getting off, but be prepared to be amazed.

The high roller itself deserves five stars however, the staff made me drop it down to four.  When we purchased our tickets there was no mention about paying the upgrade then to have a bar in our pod.  We got to the ticket counter at 5:30,so we were able to purchase our tickets for $24.95/pp.  they never mentioned anything about the happy hour price to add $5/pp to add unlimited drinking in the pods that had bars.  We go upstairs use the restrooms and get into the line.  We are waiting get up and are about to board to find out that we have to go back to the beginning of the line to add the upgrade.  Once that cluster was figured out we had to get back into line and wait about twenty minutes for a pod with the bar.  

Once we boarded I was impressed with what drinks options were available.  Drinks were poured to all 15-20 of us that were on board before the doors closed and the Ferris wheel began to move.  You can not tell that you are moving.  The views are so amazing!  At one point our bartender offered up shots to people which many took.  Many of us didn't just because there in no bathroom on board.  It was neat being u
Able to look up at the TV's to see how high up in the air you were while moving.  This was probably one of the funniest things we have done while out in vegas.  You have to go at night to see the vegas lights.

I've been on the High Roller twice, one last year December and a recent visit this past November. It really isn't as exciting as it was the first time. It's the best view though of the Vegas strip when you're up high. It's a 30 minute ride to make a full circle. I think it's a must to experience it once while you're out here in Vegas. It's $27 during the day and $37 at night. 

Although, It really is all the better to experience this ride at night though to see the lights glimmer throughout the strip. You can get $7 off if you purchase online. The High Roller is a such a tourist attraction that stands out at the LINQ's shopping promenade where you can walk around to shop or dine. We were fortunate enough to have the cabin to ourselves both times I went and it's so much more fun with a group of friends or family members to enjoy the whole experience. 

The cabin is spacious with benches you can sit on while admiring the view from the window. It's a slow paced ride so you wont feel much of the movement if you're in one place. Overall, even though it's pricey, it's gives a memorable experience of one of the top things to do while in Vegas.

Horrible family memory won't be forgotten soon enough!!
We went on ride with our 5 year old and his best friend's family.
Unfortunately we shared the ride with older couple and their middle aged son.
Brief acknowledgment from the older couple that our two 5 year olds were normal rambunctious excitement would be welcomed. However their middle aged son decided to have an episode halfway through the ride and literally yell at our 5 year old son to calm down. As any father would I got between him and my son and he did not calm down and continued profanities. I went on defense mode protecting my family from this clearly unstable individual who happened to be carrying a knife visible on 
his belt. I pleaded with his elder parents to intervene and reason with their son as clearly this would escalate into a physical altercation. At that point they managed to bring him down but both my son and his best friend both in the clutches of their distraught mothers were clearly beyond having any experience other than us calming them and hoping that they will be ok. They were not ok. The ride ended and upon departure the elder couple and their Middle aged son bee lined for the exit. I got together with the other disturbed father and we went to get security to stop this maniac and get him to apologize. NO SECURITY IN SITE!!! I stopped the maniac and yelled for security to help with the situation. NO SECURITY IN SITE!!! These people walked out the door and I continued to yell for help. NO SECURITY IN SITE!!! Finally a Manager came out and wanted me to calm down "not to interfere with anyone's positive experience". So I managed to calm down and after clearly explaining our horrible experience he offered nothing but a simple sorry. That is the best way to describe their security and customer care....SORRY.

Funny thing is there is a sign on their front door with a picture of a gun with a line through it...what about a maniac and a knife 

Proceed with caution

Family of 5 here.  Enjoyed it very much.  Price was fair for what you got, would've loved to have done the drinks happy 'hour' pod but with kids with us, that was not allowed.  Our pod had 3 other families on it so seating was at a premium.  I was saddened to realize that our family would not be able to sit if we wanted but after it started I soon discovered we didn't need to sit anyway.  However, if we could sit-the people behind us could see easier.  Fun, great view and would very easily do this again.

Its a cool experience but its a 1 time thing. It gets boring pretty quick, and its overpriced!!! i don't think its worth the money $37per person. its a 30 min roundtrip, you share the globe container what ever you want to call it) with other people. i will not be riding this again unless its free.

If you need a wonderful view of Vegas come to the High Roller! Love how each cabin are big, have seats, and have air conditioners! Also I should say my friend is afraid of heights but she loves the High Roller! If your scared of heights you'll be fine. Plus if you get the happy half hour ticket there's a bar inside your cabin with free drinks! The only reason why I didn't give the High Roller 5 stars is the price. Even this should be noted, this is the tallest observation wheel in the world the High Roller is 550 feet tall! 100% will come back!

I love Las Vegas!  Whenever they do things here, they do it with all the flair they can muster.  In Atlanta, where I live, they have this ferris wheel called the Skyview, which is nice but at 200 feet it is dwarfed by the nearby skyscrapers in the downtown area.  In Vegas, it is not enough to have a big ferris wheel.  It must be on the Strip amongst the neon lights and be 550 feet, making it currently the tallest ferris wheel in the world.  In Vegas, they prefer you not to call it a mere ferris wheel but an "observation wheel."  And nothing says Vegas, like the name of this observation wheel:  The High Roller!   That's Las Vegas style and what separates it from other cities that want to be world class but don't really know how.  

The High Roller has only been here for two years but it's already become one of the things you must do in this city that never sleeps.  You've probably even heard by now of the scandalous behavior of man and woman who were arrested a couple of months ago for having sex while riding the High Roller.  Who would have known that is considered a felony in Sin City (of all places)?  Unfortunately for me, I only rode the High Roller; none of the female riders rode me:^)  

I chose to ride the High Roller on a late Saturday night/early Sunday morning because I wanted to see the city all lit up well after dark.  It costs $36.95 to ride at night, which is about ten dollars more than during the day.  

The High Roller is located at the Linq Hotel and most of the observation wheel personnel is young and hip.  I was surprised at the excellent customer service I received.  They weren't nonchalant and acting like they'd rather be somewhere else.  There wasn't a long line either.  I just walked up, purchased my ticket; nothing to it.  They take a picture of you standing in front of a green screen just in case you want to buy the photo in the souvenir shop after your ride.  I believe they superimpose a background of the High Roller in the photo but I elected not to purchase a pic afterwards.  

I was surprised at how big the pods were on the High Roller.  They are big enough where you can either sit down or walk around in them while you're inside.  The observation wheel moves slowly and never really stops, so you board it while it's in motion.  Including myself, there were only five people in my pod.  The pods are round and the spotless windows curve from the ceiling to the floor.  There is a video screen inside with a young hipster on it trying to be informative, smug, and cool all at the same time.  He talks while there is low volume music playing during the whole half hour ride.  

The nighttime views of the Strip were amazing.  And those of you who have a fear of heights don't have much to worry about here.  To me it was like looking out the window of a tall building overlooking the Strip.  You know the wheel is moving but it's at a gradual pace.  Make sure you bring your camera!  

The High Roller is the hot, new way to view Vegas from above but I will say this:  I still believe the Stratosphere Tower observation deck at the Stratosphere Hotel has the best view of the city because it's over three hundred feet taller than the highest vantage point on the High Roller.  But I still had fun and when I got back home I could tell everyone that I've ridden the world's tallest ferris wheel (pardon me, I mean observation wheel).  It's become the thing to do in Las Vegas and you should try it at least once.

My friend was visiting from out of town and we wanted to do something "touristy" so I suggested the High Roller. I found a Groupon for 2 tickets for their Happy Half Hour, for $80. Happy half hour means there is a bartender in your pod and you get to drink alcohol!  We were able to board the ride after 7pm, so we went around 7:30 which was perfect.  The sun was just starting to set, so we got to see all the lights turn on and it was really a beautiful sight to see. Our pod was pretty crowded, at least 20 people. I guess the pods can hold up to 40 people! I suppose this would be cool for weddings or other events, but I wished there were less people so we could fully enjoy the experience. Some of our views were blocked by heads and other body parts and we ended up kinda crunched in the corner. The good thing is that since it was a 21+ crowd, there were no kids! I love kids, but definitely am glad there weren't any on my ride up. As others have mentioned, the full revolution takes 30 minutes, it goes sooo slloooww that you can barely tell you are moving. You have to walk on and walk off fairly quickly since the pods never stop, so be advised of this. Luckily there is a net down below, in case someone were to fall. 

Our bartender on the ride was awesome! She was really upbeat and had a great personality. She had to work quickly to make drinks for all 20 of us, We both ordered Angry Orchard's and I was surprised that they were in large cans, not the standard 12oz. The bartender also made shots for everyone once we got to the top of the ride, which was nice. Now that I've done it once, I don't see myself going back. 

Protip: Do not fart in the pod! Someone farted on the way up, and since it was soooo crowded it was utterly horrible. At least the pod is air conditioned!
AMAZING views, super fun and it's nice to chill on the inside. I recommend going at night, you'll get the best pictures!

Ok so I finally got to check out the high roller with a friend who works for Caesar's Entertainment which means we walked on like a Boss for free. I went on a week night so it was a ghost town we shared our bubble with just three other people. I was hoping we had been alone as I had some Shenanigans in mind, lol. 

It was interesting and I am glad to have been able to check it out however is something you only need to experience once.  I took some cool photos, ours did not have a bar in it which is ok since we were planning on hitting up a bar afterwards for some sweet libations. 

Short story, been there done that and won't need seconds in this case.

This was one of the best experiences we had in Vegas. We did the half hour happy hour and it was so worth it. Our bartender Amanda was awesome. She made sure we didn't go empty. The view was great and the staff was really nice.

i was taking my dad to vegas and i wanted to show him how pretty vegas looks like at night but high up in the air. so i thought this ride was gonna worth every penny. i then went on the internet to search and i found this deal on group on for two and has open bar for only 64 bucks for 2 people. so there is no time or date restrictions since it was on a monday and non holiday. 

we went on the ride around 9ish on a monday night. we went on the ride and it was about half hour long. with a host inside the cart with an open bar with bacardi, long island, margaritas, jack Daniel's, fiji water, and sky vodka, beers, and many more stuff. the woman who served us drinks was very nice and friendly and gave us all we want. 

if you are planning to buy a drink and enjoy in the cart you can also purchase drinks before you enter the cart if you don't want an open bar.  they have a bar outside the entrance. 

the prices of the drinks at the bar are ridiculous about 15 bucks for a well drink and a beer is like 10 bucks and 12 bucks for imported beer. i would just pay for the open bar price and drink all i want. 

the view is breath taking and it shows vegas 360 degree with all the lights and different buildings to view. This ride was very worth the money and we were up in the air at 550 feet up. 

don't forget about group on deal if your considering riding this ride. 
it comes with open bar and a free polaroid picture too 3x5 size. which is worth 10 bucks. and is included in the group on package deal.

Want to see the Las Vegas sights from the air without spending a fortune on one of those helicopter tours?  High Roller at the Linq Hotel/Casino is the thing to do. It's a ferris wheel on steroids!

It's about a 35 minute ride all the way around with amazing views. We opted for the most expensive tickets...$47 for the night time ride and a pod with an open bar. That's right, open bar folks. Pretty well stocked, tended bar and as much as you can drink in 35 minutes. They even let you take one to go when you get back on the ground. 

The ride itself was amazing. Fantastic views all around. They play good music and also have an informative video playing with information on the High Roller ride experience. I would do it again!

They do have less expensive tickets...Day time is less, not having an open bar is less, etc. I have also seen discounts online. 

Be sure to get tickets in advance! There was hardly anyone there the evening we went, but from the looks of it, it can be very busy. They have several staging areas for the crowds to wait in line.

What a great attraction in Las Vegas. High Roller offers awesome views of Las Vegas from the sky. Went on Groupon and bought the deal that includes the 30 min ride, open bar, and some coupons to local places. The price for everything is $79 for TWO people at night. Day time is cheaper but I highly recommend night time. Lines can get long so be prepared to wait. When we walked up to the entrance, there are two separate lines. One side if tickets have already been purchased and the other side for people who have groupons or need to purchase tickets. After the first phase, there is another line for boarding a pod. If you have someone who is handicapped, on the left after they check your bags is an entrance and elevator to take you near the front of the line. Certain pods have the open bar while some don't. Inside the pod, the bartender speaks his opening line and starts to mix drinks. They have very few dark liquors but lots of light ones. Beer section is slim since all they have are American beers. But the drinks are strong and during the 30 min ride, you can finish about 2 of them and take one to go. They have monitors inside telling you how high you are going and when you reach the peak at the top. Take as many photos you like but just be polite to others since they want pictures too and inside is fairly small with about 15 people in there.

Thoroughly enjoyed the 30 minute ride with my husband. We went on Tuesday night so there was no line and we only had 8 people in our Pod.  We got a $5 discount from a coupon book I picked up. The view of Las Vegas was amazing but you really can't take any real good pictures  from inside because of the glare.
I personally would not wait if they had a real long line. 
One thing I don't recommended is buying drinks in their bar unless you like to pay a lot for hardly any alcohol in your drink. For an extra $10 you can get a pod that serves you all the booze you can drink in 30 minutes but I am not exactly sure what that means so be sure to ask for specifics. There is no restroom in the pods so that could turn out to the a really bad idea.
When you get of your ride you get sent right through their gift store on your way out.

My hubby and I came here to pre-celebrate my bday! We saw groupon deal for this new ride so we decided to give it a try! And surprisingly I like this experience very much! Every time when I go to Vegas shopping, casino & buffet are the only three things I will do.. Even though I know the view of Las Vegas will be amazing I still hadn't gotten any chance to see it. But after the high roller I saw the amazing view of Las Vegas without paying a lot and also in a very quiet space.. The space is very big and u can bring wine up there... It's a romantic experience and I love it!!

My brother and I came here to celebrate the holidays. After going back and forth between doing this and trying the Eiffel Tower Experience, we decided to go with this. We loved it! Due to poor planning, I literally just purchased the tickets on my phone right before we went in - $20 for general admission for the two of us. But, I know there are several deals available online when you purchase tickets in advance.

Again, after reading reviews, we decided that the best time to go was right around sunset. That way, we could catch views of the city while it's still light out, but as the sun sets behind the mountains. It was really gorgeous. If you get nothing else from my review, go right before sunset! I looked up the time for sunset so we would get there at the right time.

The wheel brought us a new experience in Vegas. Even though we've been going to Vegas since we were little kids, we had never experienced it quite like this. I recommend going here if you're looking for a family-friendly activity. There's also the happy hour option if you're looking for something a little extra.

They had videos of a guy telling us fun facts. As a pod, my fellow riders and I were kind of making jokes the whole way around. The ride seemed really short because we were having so much fun! But in reality, it went slowly enough for us to nab some breathtaking photos.

Went here during Our NYE stay in Vegas.  Surprisingly it wasn't that crowded.  We went around 4:30pm which is well ahead of the cutoff time before they jack up the price, and by the time we hit midpoint it was already dark and I believe the wait lasted maybe 10 minutes before we got on.  We didn't get the open bar pod.  

Great views of the hotels on the strip.  Too bad the fountains at bellagio weren't dancing on our way down.  They had to speed up the ride to get someone off.  Not sure what happened but the ambulance was there for whomever needed it.  I would do it again, but next time try the open bar pod.
The greatest wheel I ever had seen and rode it! I'm from Seattle it was much bigger  than the Seattle great wheel. And two thumb up for the night ride!
Price is good. Has a beautiful view and its nice. Perfect for a date or if you wanna party its great if you get the one with theopen bar.

The High Roller is something everyone should do once, and only once, on your trip to Vegas.  We did the High Roller Happy Half Hour which is $15 more than the standard ticket.  What this gets you is access into one of the cars that has a pop up bar during the night hours.  (Not every care has one, it was like every other car)  It's a full bar, and all you can drink.  The roller lasts 30 minutes and if you are casually drinking like our group, everyone got 2-3 drinks.  However, some people stood in front of the bar pounding drinks and were able to really get their money's worth.  The cars are air conditioned, fully enclosed, and allows for panoramic views of the Las Vegas Strip and lots of photo opportunities.  They take a photo of your group as you enter the line and you can buy a photo package at the end, it was $40 and you got two photos and an access code to access your photos online for 30 days.   

Buy your tickets ahead of time or else you're stuck waiting a very very long time.  We bought ours ahead of time and still had to wait about a half hour.  That's our only complaint, they have you standing outside waiting on the platform instead of inside in the air conditioning.  The platform has no fans or any type of circulation and we were so hot it was unbearable.  I know it's the desert and it's hot, so all the reason to have some fans or water misters! 

Other than that, the High Roller Happy Half Hour was a great experience, we got really good pictures with our family and friends, and it wasn't as scary as I thought it would be!

The ride itself was cool, but the narrative video was corny.  We could have done without.  I recommend you swap the kid with a bookworm who shares educational history facts about the city, casinos, etc.  

The evening price was a little  on the high side considering it doesn't cost them any more to run the ride during evening hours. But, it's one of those things you gotta do at least once.  

Might consider riding again if changes are made and windows are cleaned.

I highly recommend taking this ride at nighttime! My husband and I booked this ride on our recent trip to Vegas. We ended up going on a later ride (opting out of the open bar) during off-peak hours around midnight. I was so happy we waited until the end of the night to do so because there was no line and we were able to hop right on with only 3 other members in our pod. This gave us the option to sit on the bench or roam about the pod for pictures whenever we wanted. The ride was extremely relaxing, it takes about 30 minutes for the entire trip around the wheel. I am not a fan of ferris wheels normally, but the pod was extremely sturdy and I felt safe the entire time. Throughout the ride you are given some information about the High Roller and its production. If you are lucky you might even be able to catch the Bellagio fountain show when you are at the peak, which is great for photo taking. Overall a wonderful experience.

I bought two happy hour tickets, which I though was reasonably priced with drinks included. The time was 8:15 so the view was great from up top at night. Our bartender was awesome! We really had such a great time! It was so much fun there was music in the background and again drinks were included. I keep recommending this to anyone going to Vegas, I think it's a must there to get the night started.

Too expensive for what it is. 
Each ticket for a ride during the evening is almost $40. It was cool to experience, but it's definitely overpriced. I don't think I'll ever visit the High Roller again.

I received my ticket through Yelp's Nerdy Bowling event for $14.95 in the nighttime, but it was a half off night anyway so there were a lot of people in line that night!! 

On the regular, it's pretty expensive: 
Daytime $20, Nighttime, $35

The other prices they show are not worth it, just pick a time with them and go then! Don't spend extra just because you're late all the time! Also, there's usually always a way to get $5 off when you buy your tix at certain locations! 

The line didn't take too long, even though there was a ton of people that day. The pods seat a lot of people and are pretty comfortable to move around in--you aren't too crowded. There are two benches to sit inside which probably fit 8-9 people at the most.

There are TV monitors inside, which feature and provide: facts, a quiz, your height information, elevator music, and a very very enthusiastic, blonde High Roller Guide dude. He even counts down to when you reach the top!!! It's EPIC. (And yes, I do mean that semi sarcastically.) It was a little corny and odd. I feel like they need the height information, but a new way to pull viewers to watch the TV screen from time to time.

It was pretty fun to see the views of Vegas; more specifically the view of the pod corner that faces the Luxor which is definitely more interesting than the other corners ;P It was a calming, beautiful and aesthetic 30 minutes of my life. 

Definitely something I would only pay for during a sale or when family stops by Vegas on vacation or during a firework holiday! 

P.S. if you didn't grab a seat in the beginning, don't worry, the people sitting down will eventually get restless and stand up :) 

Also, the color changing lights of the High Roller are beautiful, too, and a perfect photo op when walking on the Linq "street"!

Fabulous view!!! just fabulous!!! Don't bother going during the day if you are riding the High Roller which is the main attraction. You want the view at night people.... Ideally if you want to see it go from dusk to night, find out when the sunset is.  In July I went at 8:00  and by the time we got up to the very top, it was night and we saw everything light up beautifully!  We even saw the Bellagio fountain show.  It was amazing!  The ride is about 30 minutes.  Recommend buying tickets in advance.  It was a fun new experience in Vegas.  Also since you are going high up, I wouldn't recommend going if it's windy or during one of their desert storms.  Highly Recommend this attraction!!!

You know this thing was pretty cool. Great views, but $35 a head. I guess thats not that bad for the view, but I should have gotten an extra beer before I went up there, haha.

If it was $35 + a drink ticket or something. Then we would be talking.

The lover's boss treated us with tickets to the high roller. I honestly had never been interested in riding it as afterall, I've been on an airplane time after time departing and arriving into Las Vegas. I think I've seen the strip enough times both day and night to know what it looks like from high above. But when you are treated with such tickets...you better believe we will enjoy that thang! We had the tickets to the pod where it was an open bar. Open bar?!?! Yessss sir!!!! But the ride itself is like 30 minutes...speed drinking?!?! Yessss sir!!! Lol. The bartender was very nice and she definitely didn't water down our alcohol. Drunk in 30 minutes? Yes, yes. It happenend. Im not ashamed i consumed so much alcohol with a cup still in my hand once the ride was done. This was a mommy and daddy night out and i was trying to seize the moment. And hey, don't forget to tip the bartender just because it's open bar...perhaps you'll end up with watered down alcohol if you fail to do so. Also, you order one drink at a time. It's not an alcohol buffet. So order one, drink it, repeat...if you get belligerent...bartender will stop serving you. But don't get speed drinking wasted where you completely miss the whole reason you're on the high roller.

Guys, we have the largest observatory in the world...so observe, damnt! There are screens around the pod that  shows you your elevation. Once you get to the highest peak, it's like New Year's Eve. The screen will let you know you've made it to the top of the top! Then before you know it, you're off the thing. 

I will say that when you look out...there's something serene about overlooking the strip. You look down knowing there's chaos and raunchyness below you...but you aren't in it. You see the lights, Bellagio's water show going off.. and it really is a nice thing to watch if you put yourself in that serene state-of-a-mind. Look, I was able to do it how many cups in...so you can too. Lol. 

Since we had tickets before hand...we didn't have to stand in whatever long crazy line was happening at the very entrance of the building. Once you enter, there are escalators going up that leads you to a dimmed area that serves alcohol. This part is NOT included if you have an open bar ticket. Once you get to this part, there is another escalator going up to where your souvenir photo gets taken. So get your ticket out because it'll get checked before you can even get on those escalators. After that, your ticket gets looked at again then are directed to which line you gotta stand in according to the type of ticket you have. This part is probably the worst part because if you had to stand in line to buy your ticket, then you're going to have to stand in line all over again waiting to get on a pod. They let x amount of people per pod so if it's a crazy night...I don't know how long it'll take until you get on. It gets pretty warm too with all the body heat. Can't imagine on a hot summer's night. Thankfully, our night wasn't a crazy night. We waited long enough and the pod was adequately cooled.

We had a great time, but I think the high roller is more for tourists or if you are just looking for something different to do in this valley on a Friday night, etc...I don't forsee this as something I'll tell my husband, hey...let's go on the high roller this weekend. While our experience was a great one...I think if we didn't have the open bar pod, had to wait in lines forever, then 30mins after getting into the pod we are getting out...I'd probably feel a tad underwhelmed. Probably would've rated 3 stars. It was a fun night, a nice experience...but that's it for us on that one. 

Definitely kid friendly if they aren't afraid of heights. I'm not sure if strollers are even allowed on, so definitely double-check before booking your ticket.

Enjoy!

Pretty cool activity to do while in vegas.  Its fairly new, similar to the Eiffel tower experience and the stratosphere so if you enjoyed those you'll like this one as well.  

Price wise, its more expensive during the night as you get better views than day time.  There's also sometimes a groupon so make sure to check your groupon if your gonna go.  

Also make sure to buy your tickets early as the line waiting to buy tickets is usually longer than getting on the ride.  

As for the ride itself, its pretty nice as you get a great view of the strip.  The ride itself is about 30 mins and they usually put 10 to 15 people on each pod.  

Overall, its a great ride, great for kids, and reasonably priced.

The high roller ride was so worth the money and was a great experience unfortunately I have to give a 3 star because the bartender in our pod was very grumpy. He looked and acted like he did not want to be there and was not very fun. We tried to engage in small talks, but he reaponded with single word answers. However, once we started tipping, I think his body language and facial expression seemed to have improved. Maybe he's just grumpy that people don't normally tip but it's his job and he shouldn't go in with any less expectations.

This ride would have been better at night. Night time in Las Vegas is a sight to see it is beautiful. We went on the half price happy hour deal (another groupon deal). It was open bar for 2 for 59.99 during the day and 79.99 if you take he ride at night. The bartender wasn't all that friendly he didn't even say hello when we walked in. He was an older gentlemen not a lot of personality to be working as a bartender. The ride takes about a half hour to make it all the way around so you have time for about 4 or 5 mixed drinks depending on how many people are in your car. We had 8. The view is awesome from the top. Glad I did it the only complaint was wish we  would have had a better bartender.

This was an awesome experience.  We were attending a wedding in Vegas and the High Roller was a pre-wedding social event.  The views were incredible and the ride was so smooth.  I was having so much fun that I wanted our group to go around twice.  30 minutes was not enough time to enjoy the ride.

I've always wanted to visit this attraction in Vegas and we finally did.  I purchased our tickets online, in advance, and highly highly recommend it.  We paid $35 per person for the daytime happy hour ride - anytime before 5pm, with a bar in your cabin.  I've heard they're frequently on Groupon, so might check there for a discount too.  We wanted to go around sunset, which was 4:35pm the night we rode.  We arrived around 4:15 and were on our way by 4:30pm.

We arrived and saw a HUGE line - if you had tickets already, you skipped that line.  I am guessing it was an hour or two wait, it was so long.  Then, we passed a bar (where you can purchase drinks if you don't have the happy hour ticket) and then passed another line of people waiting.  Went to get our pic snapped really quickly and then we were at the head of the line for a cabin.  First, they loaded a bar and a bartender, then we jumped on.  Turns out we were the only occupants, so that made it even more amazing!

Now, I'm afraid of heights, but this didn't bother me at all.  The ride is slow, smooth and you really don't seem like you're that high up.  Our bartender, Mark, was funny, professional and really hit it off with Ross.  Our drinks were properly made, not weak like expected.  He said the cabins can hold about 25 people and it's still not squishy.  Me, I preferred the personal cabin and individualized service.  I asked how much a Jack and Coke would be (that's what I was drinking) if I'd have purchased it at the bar vs. the happy hour cabin and he said about $11....uh no brainer - get the happy hour option!

The cabins go around, very slowly, and by having our ride at sunset, we got to see the sun setting AND the twinkling lights of The Strip come on.  Best of both worlds, day and night.

I'd like to return with a group of friends, because that's the only way I think the experience could be better.  A+ service, friendliness and professionalism of each of the workers we met.  

Good times and for SURE buy tickets in advance and get the bar option.

We recently went to Las Vegas for a 6 day vacation and did a lot of different things in those 6 days but the High Roller was by far one of the best things we did while in Vegas.  First of all, it's unlike anything you've ever done before, and yes that includes those restaurants that you eat at while way up in the air.  Secondly, it's a hell of a lot of fun.  And third, if you can hold your liquor then it's one of the best values in all of Vegas!  That's right, get the drinking package and get ready to drink.  My wife and I got tickets through Groupon for a discounted rate and we chose to go with the dusk/drinking package.  That is of course the most expensive combination but after our discount it put it solidly in the value zone considering what we got out of the experience.

Let me start by saying what High Roller and others will say if you're worried about heights and/or getting sick from the ride.  This thing moves so slow you really won't be able to tell it's moving just by feeling the movement of it.  You really cannot even tell that it's moving at all unless you focus on a pole or an item near to it that you can see what you are relative to and then you can see while it's moving it's moving so slow you can barely see much movement.  So there is no need to worry about getting motion sickness at all because this isn't a ferris wheel, even if it looks like one.  Secondly I know some folks, including myself, worried a bit about being too crowded into the pod and maybe getting a bit of claustrophobia.  Well no worries because they use their judgement as to the amount of people and they won't pack you in like sardines.  

As for the amount of alcohol you can/will get in a 30 minute ride.  Well how fast can you drink?  The bartender, of which there is only one, moves lightning fast and doles out the drinks.  I was unable to ever once think I was hurting for a drink and I drank 8 double shots.  That's right I got doubles and that was not a problem.  Now I did tip the bartender $1-$2 each time we got a drink, so as to keep him nice and happy, as did most folks.  Speaking of the bartender, he was a heck of a lot of fun.  Not only was he lightning fast but he told some stories, cracked jokes and was just really a lot of fun.

Now the view is amazing at night.  Simply amazing.  You can see for miles and it's really incredible.  I know not everyone is like me and is all about the drink so I felt I definitely should mention the view, heh.  My wife really loved it too, and yes she has some fear of heights but she said she was quite comfortable throughout our ride and she would do it again.  

By the time our ride was over it I had definitely had my fill of alcohol for the night and was really good and buzzed (ok I won't lie, I was pretty drunk actually) and then it was our time to hit up Vegas and just have some fun.  This was not only just a fun time but it was such a unique experience as well.  We do plan to come back to Vegas and I know the wife and I plan to once again look up the High Roller and enjoy a wild 30 minute trip into the Vegas skies and so should you if you're in Vegas!  Highly recommended!  Get your drink on!

First of all, let me tell you that the High Roller in Las Vegas is not an amusement park.  Although, it does look like a giant Ferris wheel.   As others mentioned, it is the world's largest and tallest observation wheel.   There are 28 round glass enclosed cabins.  Each cabin can accommodate up to 40 people.  There are benches for sitting down, but we spent the 30 minute trip standing and drinking while enjoying the views of Las Vegas.  

Had a ton of fun. Started as a 3 star review.  The more I continue to write, I realized that I actually had a 4 star experience.  Our experience was in a cabin that included a bar.  Our bartender was awesome!!   He kept everyone's glass full, if that is what they wanted.  He was entertaining!  He showed the perfect example of what good customer service should be like.  

Even though we went during the afternoon, the views of Las Vegas were terrific!  I imagine it must be nicer in the evening when the lights are on in all their glory.  Of course, the price is higher in the evening.  

Tip:  Make sure to use the restroom before entering the cabin.  There are no restrooms inside the cabin.  I drank so much in 30 minutes that by the end, I was really needing to go!  Also, be careful when exiting after you have drank so much.  Would be embarrassing to trip as you exited the cabin.  There are deals available if you search hard enough.  Have fun and enjoy Las Vegas!!

My new favorite place in Vegas! Came here on a girls trip for our last night, and man it was crazy!

You can buy one with an open bar and without. Prices vary, along with if you want a day or night ticket. We got a 5pm ride with an open bar. 

The whole ticket process is simple, and our bartender was the best! Super friendly, happy to take a bunch of pictures, etc. 

The ride is 30 min. In full rotation, and we loved it! Definitely fun for a whole group of friends.

This was my first time in Vegas and we stayed at the LINQ, so this was a must. Plus the if you show ur LINQ room key they give you $5 off.
The ride was nice and I really enjoyed the view. I would recommend doing it at night to take advantage of the lights, we even saw part of the water show from the strip. The electronic host was funny too and provided some Vegas fun facts.

Watch your step!

I went on the high roller before it officially started charging and I must say it was a wonderful free ride! The entrance is modern with an after thought of feeling Like you're at an adult disneyland because your are in line for a spell, then taking a picture in front of a green screen, which you know they will have for you afterwards. When you get to the platform, youll see that the attraction never stops and you ought to walk quickly into the pod, you'll see why when you get to that point. Its a steady ride up and I went when the sun set behind the other hotels and seeing the casino lights flicker on was quite enjoyable. The pod was clean and comfortable to be standing in for 30 minutes. Which is surprising because of how many people can fit in the pod...about 30 I believe.

Now would I pay for the pleasure of this new attraction? Perhaps only one more time. The next time ill bring my own alcohol. But you be the judge!
Loved it. I am afraid of heights and survived. Very beautiful at sunset for sure but not sure it's worth almost $40. Hopefully once it's around longer the prices reduce.

We decided to try this and it was an enjoyable experience.  It's a departure from the craziness of Las Vegas and it gave my wife and I a chance to have a drink and just watch the city for 35 minutes in a car full of people who have high energy but are not crazy.  We opted for the ride that had an open bar and it was top shelf with a great bartender who was excellent and kept the party going.  If you are looking for something different to start your evening, try it out.
Was fun for $26 and way less of a hassle than the London one. Didn't seem that busy for a Sunday. Really no wait at all! Hope it has great success.

This was such an awesome experience. If you're coming in town to explore or party, this is super fun to do, day or night. I am not particularly fond of heights, so as I approached the wheel, I was freaking out a little bit, but once you actually step into the pod, you don'f feel like you're moving at all. I went during the day for the Happy Hour Open Bar which was a deal in itself. The full ride was only 30 minutes for Happy Hour, but it was enough time to have around 4 drinks or so. The price for that ticket was around $37 which was amazing because you can get as many drinks as you can finish, in my case, it was 4, where, if you bought them on the strip, they'd average to $9 each, making it $36 in addition, you get a cool view of all of Las Vegas and the pools and hotels. Our bartender was Phaedra and she was awesome! A Las Vegas local, she told us some cool stories and background on the LINQ and Vegas itself. She also made the drinks strong, so you can get a nice buzz quickly.  We had a small group so it was easy to talk to her and enjoy the ride. It was beautiful during the day, but next time, im definitely going at night. They said the Happy Hour Open Bar was a limited time promotion, so i would catch the deal while it lasts! and if you don't get it, the have a full bar just before you get in, so you can get your drinks there.

Just got stuck at the very top of this ride with my 5 year old and my 8 year old for over 30 minutes.  We were having a lot of fun until about 15 minutes into the automated announcements telling us and other passengers to "remain calm" ... ?! Guess what people do when you tell them there is a malfunction on a ride like this and don't give them any details other than tell them to "remain calm".... They do not exactly remain calm.  My kids were understandably upset and crying.   I understand there can be issues on rides like this and if the manager, Carolyn Gargiuolo, had had any customer relations skills whatsoever and hadn't been a piece of trash talking crap to me right off the bat I might have been understanding. Babe didn't try to explain anything she just verbally attacked me as soon as I asked her "who do I talk to about getting my move back?" .... Okay Caesars .... Way to go.... I DO NOT recommend this ride.  Basically anything can happen in any pod where they are forced to hold you up for ANY amount of time and they will apparently send you a Carolyn to save their $50.  Not cool and definitely not professional!

Wow, what a cool experience! Even when you're very afraid of heights! My boyfriends mom purchased passes for all of us to go up and experience this after discussing doing it on our last trip. What a wonderful idea she had because this was a highlight of the trip! People working here legitimately look like they hate their lives, but if you purchase tickets before getting there you really do not have a ton of interaction with the employees. The only thing that confuses me is when it was being built and I saw commercials they mad it appear as there was a tiny bar in each of the pods. We passed by the bar right before entering because of this reason. We were surprised and a little disappointed to learn that apparently only some had a bar (I think, I've seen photos with some pods having a bar). We went on a night it was not busy so we had the pod to ourselves. The 30 minutes speeds by and you almost they forget about you so you can go around one more time! Next time I will remember to either have a drink beforehand (that fear of heights really gets to you at the top!).

We went through Living Social and got a discount that brought the price down from the expected $36 for riding at night. We went through security and after walking for a bit and an escalator, we were ready.  The ride doesn't stop so it's good to be ready to board. 

We only had about 12 people in our pod, so it was really easy to take pictures and get around.  The 30 minute ride felt like it went really fast, but it was a good amount of time.  With 360 degree views, there is always something to look at. I even met a really nice couple from Philly so that was nice too. 

Overall, I got some great shots, and minus a screaming child, it was a great trip. I recommend doing this at night and looking for deals on Living Social or Groupon.

For a chance to see the strip from a different view, this is worth a spin!

I am at least partially to blame for my experience at the High Roller.  I allowed myself to go through this with all of my senses.  If I was less than fully aware of what was going on I probably wouldn't have been bothered by the 6 different mini-lines we had to wade through.  The views behind the former Imperial Palace at night are far from spectacular.  I doubt there are any other places in Vegas at such an altitude that have a worse view regardless of price.  I'm not saying the view is bad, but for the price ($70+ for two) there is much better value to be had elsewhere.  Surprisingly parking is free and offers a nice view of the structure. I won't go into the  details but in general processed and cheesy aptly describe the experience.  There may be enough going on in and around the ferris wheel to distract you from the relatively high price for a forgettable experience.  On your life journey I would recommend you pass on High Roller.

Definitely go online to get the discount so it's only $31 a person. Don't forget that you have the option to do the happy hour which you upgrade to get unlimited drinks for 30 minutes. this is a nice tourusty activity that's a slow 30 minute Ferris Wheel ride where you can stand up and drink alcohol. We went Christmas night at 12:30am when it was dead with no line. The service was not the friendliest but it was nice to get a drink at the bar and bring in our drink on the ride.  there are spectacular views.

Great view of the strip. The high roller makes for a fun outing.

This is not any old ferris wheel. The enclosed pods of the high roller can fit well over a dozen people. And with a maximum altitude of 550ft you get a great view of the strip, especially art night, and specially on the way down.

The ride lasts about 30 minutes, and has video of a guide playing for the duration. The video is funny but ranges to annoying at some points, but it's not unbearable.

There's a bar a bit before you get , and some of the pods are equipped with a full bar.

If you are in Vegas and have the time and money it's worth checking out.

Really disappointing. $74 for the two of us, and unfortunately it was just as the sun was setting (not their fault), but it made good photos impossible. 

We thought "anytime" tickets meant we could come anytime. That was technically true, we could come anytime but just once.

The novelty of the experience diminished five minutes into the trip. I suspect it would be incredible at night.

Finally got to try a ride on the High Roller. I definitely think this is a worthwhile tourist attraction on the strip to try at least once. We got our tix on-line, $20 adult and $8 child, under 5 free) which was the best price I saw. Attendants were friendly and helpful. No line during the day, so we practically walked on. Note they don't open until 11:30 AM.  I actually liked going during the day b/c you can really see the whole of Las Vegas. Only 6 people per pod, so it wasn't crowded at all and plenty of room to move around and see everything.  You can't feel the motion of the pod, very smooth ride, but you can definitely see that you are constantly moving.  It was cool when we reached the apex, they let you know when you're there.  Got some beautiful pics on a sunny winter day in LV.  Great attraction for families!

Happiness will not ensue when guests are told that the ride is 30 minutes then only given 25 minutes. It was fun, but I doubt that we will make a return trip.  Didn't quite understand why we paid for the open bar car then received the hairy eyeball from the bartender when we ordered multiple drinks. We tipped well. Reservations in advance are highly recommended.

This was a great experience as a local. You have a view of the entire strip and an amazing view of the city as well. For travelers I would suggest as soon as you enter the doors to grab a seat facing the doors you just entered as The Strip view will be coming up from that side.  Beverages are allowed as long as they're not in a glass and they do check bags before entering.  Our total adventure was 30 minutes in total and we had a breathtaking city/strip view at the very top.

A Must see only at night.

The view from the top of the High Roller is great. The best place to see the lights of Vegas.

Came here on a Friday night. I had the 2 for 1 groupon with the open bar for 30 minutes. 

Checking in was pretty easy, we came at night so it was pretty busy, we got in within 20 minutes or so. 

They had about 20 people in the same room. The bar is kind of in the middle and it was really an open bar which was awesome and they were not watered down either.

The views were cool, overlooking the strip, but me and my bf both got pretty nauseous. 

I'm giving it 3 stars because it was worth it for us with the groupon but if we had to pay full price I don't think 30 mins of open bar would be worth it.

Relaxing, serene, relaxing music.
ALWAYS PAY FOR THE HAPPY HOUR. Definetely worth it. Amazing 360 degree views. Air-conditioned perfectly.
Will definetely do this again.
Very fun.

The view was nice. We purchased a Groupon for the open bar option. It may have saved money? But it was not worth it. Our pod was full, so the half hour ride amounted to getting ONE drink. It was either that or wait in line for the one bartender and miss all the views. It was pretty dead that night. It would have been nice if our group of 8 could have had our own ride to ourselves. Then it would have been worth it!

BEST EXPERIENCE IN VEGAS. so slow, you hardly feel it move. Stunning veiw. I recommend it to everyone. I'm terrified of heights but would do it again in a heartbeat. 550 ft tall, world's tallest ferris wheel.

The seafood cocktails are plentiful, and tasty. The micheladas are ridiculously on point. The garlic shrimp is consistently delish. The staff is very friendly and courteous. The seafood platter was a good deal and a lot of food!

Let's begin with. Place was hot!!! The AC was either not working or owner was trying to save some money.  Portions are small and prices are big. Food quality was ok.  Would I recommend this place? Not likely and most likely I will not be back either.
Never again bad costumer service and not so good food. And so expensive!  I rather make it myself or wait till i go to cali

Came here with mom for some dinner after some errands. Mom had a feel for mariscos so we decided to try this place. We arrived about 30 minutes before closing and sat down. We were then told by the waitress that the kitchen is closed for hot dishes but they do have cold dishes since it was near closing time. Although, she wasn't nice about it at all. Ok, we were understanding of that since we knew they needed to clean the floor and do anything else before closing. So we ordered two cocteles de camarón. Pretty easy and simple. As we were finishing up she came by with the check and placed it on our table. I was near to finishing at about 10 after 9 and not nearly 3 minutes go by until she comes by to tell us we need to hurry and pay in such a rude way. I'm big on customer service and that completely changed my mind about the place. I mean the coctel de camarón was good but the service from the waitress was awful due to her rudeness, which makes me not want to return. I know maybe she was tired and wanted to finish her shift but there was still a family of 4 next to us who arrived much later than us and she could have been said it in a much better form. My mom asked her a question in a polite way as I was paying and when the waitress was going to answer she seemed bothered to answer the question. Really?! Bottom line, food was good but service was bad. I mean I've never been to a place where they hurry up their customers to pay. Who does that?! And if that's the case, maybe they should consider changing their closing hour in order to give them enough time to do what they need to do before their actual closing time. Including having their customers pay their bill.
Came to eat on 12-31-2016 and while eating the owner gave us a FREE bottle of champagne to celebrate the new year!!! But the food was really good too, super good mariscos spot!

Tried the tacos "Gobernadores". These are great. You must try them! This is a nice clean seafood restaurant. Not really expensive and the portions are a good size. Highly recommend this small business!
Very good soup they give you when you get seated.. really great michaladas and guac this place is great

Tostadas de ceviche where delicious, but a little high priced @7. My boyfriend got a tostada of aguachile and for $9 it wasn't spicy at all, he even had to add hot sauce. I would recommend the ceviche but not aguachile. I would also recommend going midday since other reviews complain about loud music and I went around 2:00p.m. And the  music was fine, it was actually pretty empty, so service was good. Not sure if I will be returning to try their shrimp cocktail or just wait to go to CA?

We ordered a small shrimp cocktail and it wasn't what we expected. It lacked flavor, spice.  We had to ask for avocado as It wasn't included. We also ordered the ceviche tostada and it also lacked flavor.  The pico de gallo on the ceviche had a refrigerated taste.  We will not be returning.

Very disappointed. This place is way over priced for the average seafood they try to serve in addition to the poor service. Then when I tried to use a certificate from Restaurant.com they wouldn't honor it and I ended up paying full price. I wouldn't ever have gone there if I hadn't seen it on Restaurant.com. I will never go here again and I will tell everyone I know not to go here either.

Went here for lunch today and I would say that overall I was really impressed. They brought us chips that were delicious.  They were thin and we actually preferred to use them rather than the crackers or tostadas that came with our food. They also brought us a cup of their soup which was good but a bit too warm for this weather (it was still good, maybe as the weather cools I will order some of their caldos). I ordered the campechana while my wife ordered the pescado ceviche and even though we ordered the medium size it was a very healthy portion of food. Many places skimp on the seafood but this place gives more than enough to fill you up.  I actually wanted a bit more veggies because it was packed with shrimp, etc .  Service was great but at first we were one of only two tables but the place was quickly filling up.  My only complaint would be how warm the place was because they had a few fans on the counter to help cool the place down (my reason for four stars). Maybe something was up with the air conditioner but with seafood you really want to be in a cool place.  Looks like they listen to their reviews because the music was low and you can easily hear yourself or your partner. Place was clean and they were attentive. Will return again to try some of their other dishes. Hope they keep the quality and cleanliness and I will be a returning customer. I thought prices were fair but I eat a lot at Scottsdale restaurants so it could be an unfair comparison in prices

Nice, clean, small family owned restaurant with good menu.  We just tried the jalapeño dish stuffed with shrimp and cheese wrapped in bacon.  It was delish!

The restaurant is very small and well decorated. Nice new tables and dishes. 

The room was a little warm, but that was OK.  It wasn't unbearable. And the service was slow but expected as it is a very small space and only one waitress.  

We loved the food. It was great! But I gave it 3 stars for the room temp and slow service.

I had a terrible experience so I'm telling everyone I can. I ate there with my wife. We both ran out of soda refills twice. My cocktail crackers were not replenished,not because they refused to but because the waitress never came back to the table to check on us. I had to get up and walk over to the counter to have my chips filled. I thought that would let them know I wasn't happy but it didn't work. They didn't come by my table or the other two tables that were occupied by patrons. The food presentation was excellent but the flavor was mediocre at best. I get a request from them for me to post my review on their website. When I post my experience I receive a response telling me they know what kind of person I am. I couldn't believe it, I spent good money there.... More than other restaurants that have better service and now they are telling me they have formed an opinion on what I am like because I rated them a 1 star. They have probably removed it from their website if they have any sense but they can't remove this one. Don't waste your time, the food looks amazing but has no flavor. There is no value in the overall experience. Don't let the website pictures fool you, there's not enough clientele in my opinion to keep the food from sitting too long. I believe that's why there's no flavor. You have been informed. Don't say I didn't tell you.
Good ceviche tostadas, soda fountain has good ratio for soda to taste sweet! Got the shrimp cocktail.
Great authentic Mexican seafood! The best cheladas almost as good as the one I make. Great ceviche service and place is clean.
Friendly environment, great service, and food was fantastic, really. You must try one of their micheladas surely will be back!

My family and I decided to try this place. It was a Friday afternoon, we ordered a shrimp cocktail and fish tacos which included rice and beans. As far as drinks it was a soda and 2 beers. The food was okay, the price was over the top. We will not be going back to eat there again!

Walked in and wasn't even greeted ! Sat there for 10 minutes and not even acknowledged. $10 for a Michelada and overpriced menu. Horrible service always makes a place SHIT ! Walked right out!! I'll take my money somewhere else.

The food was okay but not great.  The carne asada tacos had a mild taste of taco seasoning,  which is not my thing. The fish and shrimp tacos are topped with grilled onions and red and green peppers like a fajita instead of cabbage and cilantro.
If you are here because of the entertainment.com coupon, they do NOT honor it. They claim to not have signed up for it.

Wanted ceviche, was craving it all day, ordered a fish ceviche order, right before that a Modelo Especial beer and my lady a sweet drink(designated driver) after 10 minutes girl comes over says they ran out of fish ceviche, only reason I was there for......
I guess I understand since it's lent and all 

I was being charged for drinks since I did ordered them
I immediately went to pay my beer and sweet drink we ordered but owner type person asked if it was all ok
Which obviously it wasn't, he waived charge for my drink (should've drink it) i didn't 

Never the less, although I was treated fair
I didn't get what I was there for 



Owners suggestion 

Don't run out of ceviche on lent 


Not sure if we'll come back, if I do We'll see 


I ended eating monster tacos  from jack in the box
Worst customer service ever!!! The prices are really high and the food is not all that good at all. If you are looking for a good mexican mariscos restaurant beware...DO NOT GO HERE!

By far the worst mariscos ever. I ordered shrimp empanadas, an agua chile and horchata to go paying almost $60. The empanadas were burnt and i the agua chile had maybe 7 shrimp. Way over priced. Disappointed with the empanadas because theyre hard to find.
Good micheladas good food ( except ceviche de pescado) ... good horchata clean place, small place, a bit pricey .. Service was great ... Over all was good.
Terrible food...terrible music....I will never comeback to this place the Stake is cheap and the food too expensive  ....very disappointed no lo recomiendo

The food is delicious... 
My niece and I decided to stop by for lunch it was great. The staff is friendly and the food is very tasty. I am definitely going to go back with my hubby I'm sure he will enjoy the seafood they have a lot of variety.
The food is great but a bit pricey. You do get what you pay for food wise, with good sized portions & ice cold drinks. The only knock is the service is slow, even when the place is empty.
The Michelada was good  and the shrimp were delicious. . The rice was good . It came with flour or corn tortillas. Never had shrimp culichi. But it's a must to try.

A pleasant surprise

I live in the area but have never been to Mariscos Camaron Pela'o that is until today, and all I have to say is, it was was definitely a good stop.

The restaurant is pleasantly decorated, a cross between a Mexican beach bar and a sports bar with large screen TVs.
