I was really hoping for a good barbecue joint in my new 'hood, and I hit the jackpot tonight. This place is great!

OK I felt the pressure to revise my review. I was way to harsh!
It's not the place for BBQ. It's just not.
The atmosphere is nice the sides are mostly creative and pleasing to the pallet.
But being around BBQ my entire life and all types including Memphis and Dallas, I can say that every time someone tries to fancy up BBQ I am disappointed. Good Try but I am not buying.
Wonder what these guys could do with a steak? With all those creative juices flowing Now I bet they could do that well!

Excellent!  We stopped in with the kids on a Wednesday night. Timely attentive service and the food came out super quick. Spicy green beans, jalapeño cheese grits, apple sauce - all delicious. I'm an eastern NC barbecue fan at heart, but this was well made with good smoke flavor and nice bark mixed in. Six sauces to choose from, most of which I liked. Even my 7 year old gobbled up the slider, slaw and all. We'll be back for sure.

Good, casual, easy eats. Ate at the bar. Comfy seats, lots of leg room at the wood bar top and tv's. 

Happy with my tofu sandwich on the rice bun and mac n cheese (not handmade but hit the spot). 

Dan did the pulled pork and said it was good. Side of Brussels. Spicy.

Good beer and cocktails. Good service but we did arrive at 9:30 on a weeknight. No one else was around.

Disappointing! Very inconstant It was great last time but very lacking tonight! The grits were plain, the pulled chicken was soaked in some nasty juice! The guy at the bar was rude. Just not impressed

I spent more here than I normally would for lunch, but the spicy green beans and jalapeno chese grits were tasty. The pulled chicken was good quality, but a bit dry.  I wanted an additional spicy BBQ sauce beyond Spicy Hoisin -- it's good, but I prefer hoisin for Moo Shu, not 'cue...  I like that they're adding something unique to Cotswold, and I hope they make it.

I have been hearing about this place from my co-worker. Today I decided to go. It's really not a big restaurant (which is a plus for me). The have a bar, outside eating area. Also there are TV on the wall watch was playing ESPN and news. Lucky me I want on taco Tuesday($2 per taco) and when I said my tacos where sooooo delicious!!!!

Pretty good barbecue. Located in the Cotswold shopping center. We got the Cotswold platter which includes two meats, two sides, and some cornbread. My favorite side here is the sweet potato waffle fries - hands down the best sweet potato fries that you can find in Charlotte! They also have a nice variety of homemade sauces that you can have with your barbecued meats.

I met a few friends here for dinner after it came recommended from another friend.  Glad to see a locally owned restaurant in Cotswold.  The area was getting too populated with chains.

So the place features barbecue with an asian twist and has plenty of options for vegetarians as well like Smoked tofu for your protein.  Everything Vegetarian is marked with a V on the menu.  Good job in pointing it out for us! 

The seating is a mix of booths, high top tables, bar seating and a nice outdoor patio.

At the recommendation of our server, I went with the side plate with the choices of brussels sprouts, asian slaw, the veggie of the week and the jalapeno cheese grits.  Normally I am not a grits fan but these were really good!  The other 3 sides were good but not great in my opinion.  

Still, I wan to come back here and try the smoked tofu and their other vegetarian options.  I see plenty of promise here!

Another lovely meal!!
My second time here, the added details to the presentation of the food A+ in my book.
The food is great, from the chicken fried rice, spicy green beans and today the chicken wings. 
Excellent!!!!   A lovely place to try if your looking for something different!
The nachos with pulled pork are out of this world. The bbq has been excellent every time we have been. Service is always prompt and polite.

Great BBQ, nice bartenders.  

I keep going back just to get take out orders of Spicy Green beans.  I guess I should really should learn how to make them myself so I don't have to go get take out to pair with my home cooked dinners.  Go try them! 

-Alan D.

Disappointed... I tried twice but not impressed either time. The décor is nice but that is about it. I am not a fan of BBQ to begin with but this seemed like a neat place and I wanted to like it. The first time I tried the Asian shrimp tacos. The sauce was good however the shrimp was lacking. I had 3 on each taco and the corn taco was like rubber. Had I known it was a corn taco I would have passed. The second time I thought I would try the mac and cheese expecting it to be homemade, maybe a nice crust but instead it was runny. On the 2nd trip my friend ordered a margarita and I don't know how to describe it other than bad, very bad.

My new favorite!!!  This was our second time in as many weeks and we'll definitely be back.  This place is unique and affordable to boot.  I can't recommend it enough.  

Meal one - the cutlery: a sample of ribs,pork, brisket and sausage. It was just the right amount without being too filling. 

Meal two - BBQ Salad with Chicken.  I switched dressing to the vinaigrette.  simply awesome.

I have died and gone to pork heaven!!!  The whole place is awesome, staff, environment and food.

Had the pulled pork and doused it with "queen bee".  It was tender, smoky flavored, perfectfully seasoned pork.  The queen bee sweet tomato based sauce gives Kansas City die hards something to compete with.

Had the Mac and cheese (perfect creamy and cheesy goodness) with the spicy green beans.  The green beans are not spicy but seasoned with something kind of Asian. Good but not great.  I will be back with my family.

Everyone is a restaurant critic... I'm glad to have a Q joint close to me! The Mac is good and the greens are too. Cheese grits nice touch. Is this the greatest BBQ on the planet? No. But its certainly good and the sides are too. So hey, be glad it's not another chain sandwich/bakery/hamburger joint. Ugh! Beef brisket around the corner from my house... I'm there!

Super cute modern bbq place that's fit for foodies. Great bar selection. Meats come out dry as in no sauce and then select your sauce from the sauce caddy on the table. Cheese and jalapeños grits are amazing! Sweet potato waffle cut fries are nice and crisp. Kind knowledgeable staff, decent prices and modern decor. I had the pulled chicken, bf had ribs. Great experience.

Today my work associates and I stopped by the Improper Pig for lunch at the Cotswold location. I have heard good things about this place before, but I was not prepared for how absolutely delicious the food would be.


We were greeted, welcomed and sat immediately on their spacious, comfortable outside patio. We were also greeted by our server within moments of sitting at the table, who had a great attitude and gave us prompt service throughout the meal. Our waters were never empty and that is quite refreshing on a warm patio.


The manager Christian came by to greet us and discuss the specials and his favorite menu items, which sounded so fabulous, one of my associates ended up going with his suggestion of the ribs - he was not disappointed.


Our meal started off with an order of the Twice Baked Jalapeños appetizer. The cilantro lime crema and spiciness was absolutely amazing. The manager even gave us a tip to try it with the sweet and sour sauce, which helped balance out the spice. These were so delicious, I could have eaten an entire plate of them for my entrée.


Our table ordered the following: St Louis Style Ribs with a side of Sweet Potato Hash and Green Beans, BBQ Salad with pulled pork, Pulled pork platter with black bean salad side, and my choice, the special burger, the Belly Burger.


Every entrée was met with extreme satisfaction - ribs were cooking to perfection, the BBQ salad in my associates words was "the best BBQ salad I have ever had", and my burger was so good, I ate every single bite on my plate.


The Belly Burger was 70% Beef, 30% pork, blue cheese, special sweet Mary's BBQ, pickled onions, arugula, and tomato. I worked at Bad Daddy's for almost four years and in my entire time working there, haven't had a burger as tasty as this one. So absolutely phenomenal. The homemade chips were delicious as well that came on the side.


I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone that hasn't tried. While reviewing their menu, I noticed a ton of options for all types of eaters - tofu, vegetarian, gluten free, vegan, etc. They also appeared to have a nice bar selection, although this was a work lunch so we did not delve too much into those options! Service was impeccable and the manager Christian was extremely welcoming and informative on the menu. We are now Raving Fans and can't wait to come back!!

Terrific service. The pulled chicken BBQ sandwich was basic and why shouldn't it be; however, I would like to see a choice of bun. The bun is like a Costco super saver kids' birthday party bun. Plain. White. I chose sweet potato fries. Too salty. Like big, chunky, caked on salt. I felt myself dehydrating into George Hamilton.  The sauces are a decent variety.  Have it eastern or western, hot or nothing at all. 

I don't see this making it in the long run as the Cotswold crowd may be just slightly too sophisticated for this pleasant but less than wow-ing food.

The Improper Pig, not sure where to begin. I was so wishing to like it more than I did, but overall just thought it was okay.
My dinner group met here on a weekend and were seated on the outdoor, covered patio on cooler nights.  Although it was nice to sit outside service was very slow, as our waitress seemed to be no where to be found several times throughout the evening.

Having not been I was able to enjoy some appetizers that we ordered for the table. The chorizo stuffed jalapeños were by far the best thing I ate the whole night. They were cooked too perfection with a great, but not so hot, kick. The cornbread on the other hand was dry and I definitely had better. And, I am not a kale chip fan, but they needed more salt or seasoning, definitely just blah.

I went ahead and ordered the combo platter with pulled chicken and brisket, with Brussels Sprouts and Sweet Potato Fries. The pulled chicken was just okay, not as moist as I have had or liked and the brisket was good, definitely melt in your mouth moist, but just a lot of fat.
As for the sides, I definitely recommend the Sweet Potato Fries, so good! 

The Improper Pig offers a variety of sauces tableside, so you can pick and choose. Unfortunately I found most of them a little too sweet and missed a true barbeque sauce.

Overall, I am glad I finally made it to this quaint addition to the Cotswold Shopping Center, but with too many other barbeque joints, that I find better, not sure I would rush back anytime soon.

I would call this "eccentric BBQ."  This place is a nice hole in the wall.  Environment is nice.  It has a small bar.   The menu is pretty good.  Service and prices were fine.  I ordered BBQ pork sandwich, cheese grits and coleslaw.   Everything was ok.  I've had worse,  but I've had better too.  If you are in the neighborhood, and looking for a place to grab a bite with a friend, you should consider it.

We had been here one time last year and enjoyed it. So recently I picked it for a Saturday night date night. We were seated right when we walked in and ordered drinks (Stella for me, margarita for him). We were both pleased with our drinks (he described his as tart but good). 

We started with the pork roll, which was really good but a not so good portion size. It is listed as an appetizer but is more like a side item. It is one egg roll cut in half. It was good but for the price, you should at least get two!

My fella had the improper charcuterie, which he loved. In fact he told me that he doesn't think he would order anything else. I had the salmon chow bao taco with green beans. I liked both. The slaw on the taco lacked flavor so I ended up just taking most of it off, but it was tasty and I loved the sauce on the salmon. The green beans are awesome! I could eat them all day every day!

Overall, it was a date night success. We will be back!

Arrived just before 7pm on a friday night, little surprised to see a nearly empty restaurant.  But had a great meal and dining experience.

I ordered the pork sandwich, with coleslaw and baked beans.  My wife ordered pulled chicken with coleslaw.  Both were very tasty.  Only criticism would be the servings were a little smaller than I had expected.

Would recommend to friends and we will be back.
So far I've been here three times and every time has been absolutely fantastic. Swift service with a smile and excellent menu choices

This is a great local spot, like Southern barbecue with a unique twist. The second time I went was even better than the first, they're still pretty new, but I think the place is flowing now. Portions are good, sauces are homemade and you add your own at the table. There are vegetarian options as well as carnivorous ones, so it's a crowd pleaser. I typically leave both full and with a box for later. Prices are reasonable and I've had great service both times. One of my dining partners has food allergies, and they were more than accommodating for him as well. Check it out!

My wife and I ate here May 3rd.  We had brisket YUM and pork and egg roll appetizers one with pork and one with sweet potatoes (this was the only item I wouldn't get again).  Sides were mac and cheese, brussel sprouts YUM and collards

The flavors were great - the meat was  very moist,  and had a very light smoky flavor.  I expected a smokier meat, but it was so delicate and moist and tasted fresh that I'm definitely a fan.  

It was also neat that there are Asian influences in some of the menu items as sauces, so this is an typical bbq place.  

It is a little pricier than typical BBQ restaurants, but I thought the quality of food and flavors was worth the price- all the sides were a little better than you would normally find.and I cant wait to go back.

Great barbeque, service, drinks, and ambience. Our server, Michelle, was welcoming and had excellent suggestions for drinks and entrée options.  We sat in the outside area, which was perfect for a calm and warm evening. While there was a good crowd, the staff was attentive and the nose level was perfect for a chat with my dining companion. Highly recommend this restaurant for top notch BBQ, drinks, and attractive, clean décor.
Good food. Good service. The jalapeño grits are awesome!!!! The pork and chicken are flavored well and not over cooked. They also have great sauce choices at the table.

Okay - it's taken a while to do a follow up review because I wanted to try as much from the menu as possible and dine in as well. As life would have it, I've only just recently gotten around to getting in there.

And the results are....

Hmmm. Weeeell...  Here's the deal folks. I LOVE BBQ! I grew up with it. I cook it at home, and I'll pick it almost over anything else that's fast and warm. This, however, does not make me a BBQ expert. That being said, I don't love their BBQ. The menu does have on it the usual BBQ items (pulled pork, brisket, ribs, etc.), but at the risk of upsetting the fragile Cotswold pallate, don't order those items. I love these guys and Cotswold is desperately missing a great BBQ joint, but this is not it. I know in my last review, I asked them not to mess around too much with BBQ, but they didn't listen to me, and mess around they have. And I'm glad they did!

Absolutely ALL of their appetizers are amaaaazing. You MUST try the BBQ Kale Chips, or the Improper Nachos. And I believe I've mentioned Twice-Baked Jalepenos previously. I mean, stuffed with cream cheese and chorizo? Can you find any reason to not want that?!? And their Good Luck Soup, albeit a bit messy to eat, is the perfect ping of pot-licker yumminess. Don't listen to their menu. It's nothing like Brunswick Stew. It IS like absolute tastiness! If there weren't so many other interesting things on the menu, I would just make a meal out of their apps. But if I did that, I would miss out on the tender Shrimp Tacos (although, their tortilla choice needs a bit of adjustment), or their Korean BBQ Salmon, or their Cowboy Rubbed Grilled Ribeye (perfectly cooked). And that would be a crying shame.

And their desserts! I've tried two of their cobblers. It's the kind of dessert that makes you feel guilty eating it, no matter how fit you are. And their Chocolate Cream Pie is the definition of decadence. 

So, to sum up, I'm sorry. Truly. But if you want tender, slide off the bone, melt-in-your-mouth BBQ, this may not be the place for you. With my limited knowledge of BBQ preparation, just seems like they need a little more time - both on the grill and as a restaurant - to figure that part out.

But, if you want great service, fun environment, and something new and DELISH, please, please, please drop by the strangely and properly named Improper Pig. You will not regret it.

This place is a jewel. Food is outstanding. Tons of different things on the menu. All kind of different barbecue sauces to try. Great drink specials.  You will not be disappointed. So good. Always look forward to this place. Staff is very friendly.

Overall a fairly good dining experience. The BBQ was tasty and the sides were delicious. Service was a little slow considering the restaurant was only half full, and prices were a little high, especially on the appetizers. One of the best things about the whole meal was the stuffed jalapeños but it was only 4 small little pieces for $6 or $7 and it left me wanting more, however, for that price I had to pass. Bartender was also a little inexperienced (you don't shake a Manhattan) and you don't upcharge a $4 special drink to $10 because you put it over ice and add a splash of vermouth.  I will definitely come back in a couple months and try this place again. Hopefully by then they've worked out the kinks.
The fish tacos is what I always go for   Collard greens are without a doubt some of the best I have tried.  One of my favorite lunch spots

3.5 stars. This big is improper. You must have BBQ when you're in the Carolinas. Stopped here for lunch on a Sunday afternoon and it wasn't too packed. We were seated at a high top table and I started off with a sweet tea. I went with the pulled pork sandwich which is served with your choice of side. Went with the mac and cheese.

The nice thing about The Improper Pig is they have about six BBQ sauces for you to choose from: a ketchup-based BBQ, a vinegar-based one, a Thai one, and several other choices. I'm all about variety and several of the sauces are excellent. On the downside, you have to squirt the sauce on your plate and sauces start intermingling. It would be nice if they had individual containers. The BBQ was a bit dry but still was good when doused in sauce. The mac and cheese was average. I did try my buddies sweet potato fries and that's the way to to go. Waffle sweet potato fries. That is a winning side in my book.

I had a couple tacos that were very good, the onion rings were amazing and the Brussel sprouts OMG to die for.  We also had the stuffed jalapeno peppers, you better like spicy but they are also veryyy tasty.  we are fan and will be back

My go to restaurant (family, friends, coworkers) come here whenever we're indecisive about what we want to eat...reason being..this place has something for everyone. Asian glazed salmon is my favorite. They have really good mac&cheese ( gotta get it early). I've gotten it for dinner and it was a really runny..so I make sure I get it when I come for lunch. They have apple sauce on the kids menu..amazing!!!!  The brussel sprouts are good..but cooked with bacon..(I found out after I ordered them). 
They have a salad that's great, unable to remember the name of it..but it's good..it has roasted sweet potatoes in it.

Decided to try out this spot for lunch as it is close to my work, and I am so glad that I did. Not only is the atmosphere great but the services was too! I felt so welcomed, and was seated immediately. The food was great, my fiance ordered the jalapenos for an appetizer and wow, there were fabulous, wish they were a bit spicier but we both love spicy foods. I ordered the BBQ salmon and he order the platter, and we both were stuffed! The food was cooked perfectly and the sides were so tasty. If we didn't have to go back to work I would have checked out their great drink specials! The prices were right on and again the service was wonderful, we will be back for sure and highly recommend for anyone.

I expected more from Improper Pig.I went here one day for lunch and did not think it was that great at all.I ordered the black eyed peas salad which the waitor told me was good and it was totally disgusting.I changed it for the spicy green beans which weren't all that great,but better than the previous side.My smoked chicken needed more seasoning and the sauce did not make it any better.I don't plan to return.
Food is great, chill atmosphere. Lots of options even for those who are vegan/vegetarian.

This was my first time trying Improper Pig and I was very impressed with the food. 

I liked the look and feel inside the restaurant and they have a patio area.  

In regards to the food.... I ordered a half rack of ribs with a side of Mac and cheese.  And then I ordered one additional side of the collard greens.  A half of rack with one side was $14.  I would think that for a rib plate...it would automatically come with two sides.  My husband ordered a pulled pork plate with the jalapeño grits and Mac and cheese.  After trying my ribs and my husband's pulled pork, I ended up trading with him.  The pulled pork was better than the ribs.  The ribs wasnt as tender as Midwood.  But the pulled pork was really good.  I paired the pulled pork with the Queen Bee sauce since its a sweet BBQ sauce.   But what I really loved was the mac and cheese.  It was very cheesy and I could tell that they used cheddar cheese to make it.  The collard greens were good, although once you get to the bottom....it drowned in vinegar.  The jalapeño cheese grits was good too... Even though it wasn't as thick as I'm use to.  Nevertheless, it was still good.  

Prior to ordering our entrées, we had the southern egg rolls.  There was only one thing missing....these rolls does not include meat.  If they were to put pull pork in their rolls, then it would have been better.  But I won't complain because it was still good and it was a free appetizer.  If you download their stealz app, they give you the appetizer for free.  So that was nice.  Overall, I liked this place for their pulled pork and Mac and cheese. I will definitely be back again.

Carving for something fulfilling? Skip this joint.
Want something fast food? Skip it again. 

Just curious to try it out then by all means come try it for yourself and see how you like it. 

This place is seriously over hyped. The lines were super long and the food wait as long as waiting in line. 

For the sandwiches they're ok. 
Tried
* cheeseburger: tasted like the frozen version 
* chicken sandwich and chicken ring one are the same...I'm just assuming the chicken ring is kid friendly. 
*fries were okay and I usually love crinkle fries.
*onion strips I did kind of enjoyed. 

Since its in Vegas this place is right next to a casino setting. Seating areas are kind of limited so if you come here late night good luck on finding a seat unless it's a week day. I probably won't be back unless I'm super duper hungry and/or drunk.
Small burgers I ate 3 and was still hungry. They don't have a tons of condiments inside the burger itself but adding some ketchup was fine with me. It's a great place if your on a budget.

Went here for lunch and soon as we get in line they close. How are you going to advertise that you are open for 24 hours then say we need to clean the grills and will be closed 3-4 hours.

Maybe I'm just "hangry" but if you looking to check this place out go at an awkward time and call before going. Don't waste your time when you could be doing other things in Vegas.

I decided to check out White Castle on the Strip and I am sorry to say that I was sorely disappointed with what they offered. I ordered the cheeseburger combo and got 4 sliders with slivers of beef and fries which were not that good. The best thing was the coke that came with the combo.  This place is overrated and I have no plans to go back
I'm from back east so having a White Castle around is like heaven. Great burgers just wish they had more seating.

Love it, yes I love it. First time trying a white castle. Happend to be right across from our hotel at the Mirage. Service was good. Line was long when we stopped by the day before so we hit it up for breakfast at like 8 or 9 am yesterday. No line. Super friendly service, price is on par with most food places on the strip. Food came out quickly and was amazing. I love how the bread on the sliders isnt too bready or doughy, I guess in other words its not "heavy", and now i have a hard time figuring out if i like In n Out or white castle more. Everyone should try this place.

I was excited to try but when I did it was NOT good! I expected more. The sliders were small and thats all they have no regular size burgers. I shoutld have tried the chicken rings! Welp next time! But the wait was normal not too bad went on a Sunday afternoon!

Was good... But definitely need to have more than ONE single cashier working when there is a line out the door! The gentleman that was cashiering was extremely slow and took his sweet ass time checking every cash bill very carefully too...everyone in line was furious! Won't be back to this location! What a disaster

White Castle, what are you doing in Vegas? I came here with a goal to try this place. I watched the movie and heard the hype and I pumped up my wife and son about the franchise. The tradition and history was the draw and the curiosity was the nail in the coffin. So our drive to Vegas was filled with goals, must do's, promises, and plans to try White Castle and Nathan's Hot Dogs. We were on a budget because we were staying for a week and we had a football tournament to attend. But White Castle was a must have and we decided on taking a walk from Excalibur to White Castle. It is a 1 hour walk from end to end because the sidewalks are so crowded and a 2 mile hike if you look at a GPS. It was a cold night and we worked up an appetite walking to the location but that did not help the outcome. Finally when we arrived with our faces half frozen we found a place to sit across from all the slot machines. The restaurant is very noisy because it is open on to the game floor. I lined up and saw the huge selection of options and I decided to keep it simple. My order:
Original slider and original slider with cheese: They were a total disappointment bland with no seasoning not even a pinch of salt the cheese was flavor less but did add some texture. The onions got lost in the process and added nothing to the flavor. My 11 year old could not even finish one slider and he walked there with no dinner he thought it was gross and said he was scared for life.(preteen drama) I think when three people who enjoy fast food aren't willing to eat the food something is extremely wrong. (Negative rating if possible)
Loaded fries: Those were okay and edible but nothing to rave about I would definitely order the wedges from Jack's than these. 
Fries: What can I say about prepackaged frozen fries other than they weren't burnt or soggy.  
Onion rings: They were good but not worth remembering or craving.
Wo when the sides are okay and the burgers suck you get one star that is all there is to it and I don't think if I was in the East coast I would ever go looking for a White Castle or waste my money at one. Oh yeah and the customer service was just okay you can tell the staff was tired and not happy to be there even though it wasn't even 10pm. I though the walk would enhance the experience but it just added to the disappointment so I apologize if I upset White Castle fans with my review.
deliciosas...algo diferente que tienes que probar si vas a las vegas

I was so shocked and excited after arriving in Las Vegas to find out that White Castle now exists in the middle of the desert! All I can say is, regardless of whether you are a huge fan, you need to stop by here at least once to order a sack of sliders. They are delicious, fun to eat, and very convenient when you've been staying up all day and night wandering around the casinos. In fact, this particular location is open 24 hours a day!

Now, I'm not saying that I ate baby burgers for breakfast, lunch, and dinner on my last vacation, but if I did I could definitely say it was worth it. Only in Vegas.

Decided to try this for the first time and I thought everything was pretty gross as far as flavor goes. The fries were soggy with no flavor and the burgers were just meh, nothing special. I guess I'm more of an in n out person.

One good thing I will mention is that this was on New Year's Eve so it was very busy and the line was long but the food came out really fast and the people were friendly. I wouldn't eat here again because I personally don't like it but service wasn't bad at all.

I've always wanted to try White Castle after seeing it from the movie bzillion years ago & I'm so glad I finally had the chance to here in Vegas! Years ago, I had the frozen one once & IMO it was horrible. Everyone else claims the frozen was better but perhaps I got a bad batch?!  Reviews are so mixed here but the sliders were better than I had expected. For I am huge fan of sliders. 

-:::- VENUE  -:::-

Located on the strip between Harrah's & Venetian. It's a good size location with it's own front entrance yet connected visibly to Casino Royale. We didn't bother with driving for we figured parking would be a pain. So we walked from the Elara hotel -- which wasn't bad at all. We went on a Saturday afternoon around 4ish & there wasn't a wait when we arrived. We didn't dine there for we took our orders to-go. The place was fairly clean with decent amount of seating (tables & high tops) and a self serve beverage station.  It's your typical fast food joint so really there isn't that much to expect. I like the outdoor venue castle themed decor tho!

-:::- SERVICE -:::-

The older gentleman who was cashiering was very courteous & sweet! Despite there was a line that came in right after us (& there was none prior!) he was patient & tried to get us the best deal for the amount of variety we ordered. The service was definitely quick & accommodating.

-:::- MENU/FOOD  -:::-

Mentioned by another Yelper & my gf (this was her 2nd visit) it's way better to order the Double Slider or Double Cheese Slider. Double the flavor! The buns are very soft & squish-able =P  I actually liked the slider size & the packaging. 

All of us didn't bother with the combo or sides & went straight for the sliders a la carte.  Food came out pretty quick too. We all got our orders in less than 15 minutes. Eating it fresh off the grill/fryer is ideal. But we had some late night after clubbing & some the following morning for bfast which after heating it up in the microwave -- IMO it was still yums! 

Interestingly, my group ruled that they liked the Fish Slider the best. I personally liked both the Double Cheese & Fish slider. Chicken was a bit dry but easily solved by packing on some sauces White Castle provides. 

Double Cheese Slider   [4.5/5]
Chicken Breast Slider    [4.0/5]
Fish Slider                     [4.5/5]

FYI: this is NOT a gourmet burger (don't compare it to one) nor a gourmet slider. It is a fast food joint slider & it did the job! White Castle is one of a kind!


-:::- NOTES  -:::-

1) Sliders comes with pickles & onions. If you don't like either let them know ahead of time.

Next time I'm back in town I'm definitely hitting up White Castle again & to try their b-fast as well. I hope they open a White Castle in the OC in the near future!

With all of the money spent building a WC. in Vegas & the "Vegas tax" prices, you'd think they'd bother to use the proper mustard (Dusseldorf), instead of generic yellow. The sliders here are simply not authentic.

I wish I could leave zero stars, because I just spit the food out of my mouth. Soggy buns and the meat was like a paste. I've been to the original a few times and loved it, and they also do the foodie fest every year with a White Castle food truck, I had them last summer and they were great. 7 bucks for 3 disgusting little sliders. Nasty!!!
It's White Castle! Remember the novelty of this place when I lived on east coast. Better burger options here in Vegas, but had a since of nostalgia for me.

It's ratchet, but what can you expect? It's White Castle. Given that, the food is pretty decent for being so cheap, but if I ate more than 3 burgers, I'd honestly feel sick because it's just too much unhealthy.

Terrible burgers. This is my 4th Dub C experience, twice at this location.  I just don't get it. The buns are soggy. There is no meat. Too many onions... and a pickle? It's a toss up as to whether the store bought frozen ones are better or not. 

The chicken rings were interesting but had an aftertaste of cheap blended cooking oil. 

The fries are okay. Skinny Frispo-style.

Despite recently opening and many of the negative reviews,  service was fast and easy both visits. The restaurant was dirty the first trip a few days ago, but clean during today's visit.

Straight awful and disgusting. I've been wanting to try these ever since like a decade ago when I first saw Harold and Kumar's Adventure to White Castle and these did not deliver. I think it's just something you have to grow up with as a kid to crave for nostalgia's sake when you're super high. As a grown-up who's never had these before, these were basically worse than McDonald's. They tasted like chemicals and I'm not even sure if it was even real meat. It made me and my girlfriend feel extremely gross after, and I had to walk it off for the rest of the day to feel normal again. Would never ever try this again even if someone paid me to eat it.

You know, I wasn't too impressed with this joint. The burgers were okay, had those double burger sliders.  They really tasted plain to me. I had to put ketchup on mines to add a little flavor. To me, they didn't live up to the hype.

This may be the first time I have ever given a spot a 1 based off of just food alone. Say What?

Service Run Through- They have people making these at oompa loompa rates in the back and so the long line moves fairly quickly. Cashier service is stereotypical lunch lady status. 

"The sliders are downright disgusting." - 2 AM drunk person

Yeah I'm quoting myself but when a slider doesn't taste good when it's 2 AM and you're drunk you know something is wrong here. I can usually spit out some sarcastic remark about how bad something is but these are just bad to the point of being indescribable. The fries are flavorless so prepare yourself for some hands on salting.

Let me blame impractical jokers for the 2 step flow of communication that got me to come in here. I understand this is fast food blah blah but even a sloppy big mac would have been the better choice. Don't let the east coast bias suck you in. It's Vegas, there are way more options at 2 AM in a city that never sleeps. If you're just dying to have some white castle sliders just get some of the frozen ones from your grocery store and let them thaw out for a day, they call that doing it Vegas style.

It's only getting a 2 star because my son loves these burgers. He says it reminds him of crabby patties on SpongeBob. 1st red flag that these are not that great!
They need to learn to put seasoning on the burgers because the ones I had tasted so bland and yucky. The loaded fries are so dang small for the price you pay. Also if you want mayo, oh GOD it's like gold to the employees, they will only hand you 3 for every 10 sliders.
Now to price.  HELLO!!!!!! Lower the price. "Vegas" price is such BS and if they want to say because the rent is high us another stupid excuse. These sliders are only worth $.87 a piece and not over 1 dollar like they charge here.
It's really not worth the hype and I find that In & Out is 10 times better. They actually put flavor on their burgers.

So here we have it, the very first Castle of The Sliders to open shop west of the Mississippi River. 

Now if you come here expecting a charbroiled masterpiece akin to Five Guys or In-N-Out, you've come to the wrong place. *side-eyeing most of the other reviewers here* It's not the highest quality food around and none of the nostalgic Midwesterners and East Coasters are saying it is either. What it is, is a place for "cheap," late night grub after a debaucherous night out. An experience amplified by booze or "greens" so to speak. And now, thanks to Harold & Kumar, a meme in of itself. There's a whole novelty associated with it that up until now couldn't be experience by people on the West Coast. THAT'S what the big deal is, so if you fail to comprehend, care to spare us of the elitism?

Since this was a late night trip, I was able to walk right in. It was nice to see how fast they were working at getting food out for people. I was taken aback by the prices, but I guess it's to be expected since it's on The Strip and most people on this side of the country wouldn't know any better either way. 

I must say, the fresh white castle sliders were a step up from the frozen ones. The cheese was nice and melted, with fresh minced onion and topped off with a super sweet pickle. The chicken rings were tasty too. The fries were just plain ol' crinkle cut fries so not anything special. 

Fittingly the place is located in Casino Royale, home to the cheapest bar on the strip. I need to make a point to get a good buzz going there before stumbling into white castle. That way I can get the full, well rounded experience.

The FInal Verdict

Pros:
White Castle.
Better than frozen.
In close proximity to the cheapest bar on the strip.

Cons:
Marked up prices.

Return Factor: 10/10. I still need to try this place while drunk.

Would classify as hangover food and nothing special. Expensive and not delicious. Located in the opening of a big, smoky casino. Nice stop on the strip if you want to waste money on not so delicious food and just looking to eat anything. The sliders are so tiny and nothing was that great in taste about them. Can't understand why people would select this place for a meal. Would never choose to eat here again, which is why I'm choosing to rate the place with 1 star.

The only reason why I'm giving this 3 stars is because it's White Castle, something you can only get in the freezer section of the supermarket if you're on the west coast. But now, it's made it's way to the main strip of Vegas, which is great news for those of us who don't want to journey to the east coast just for these little sliders.

Truth be told, I was totally unimpressed. The burgers were inconsistent, lukewarm, and tasted bland. Some had pickles, some didn't. I was missing cheese on some of my cheese sliders too. I'm sure this is due to how crazy busy the place has been ever since it opened a couple of a weeks ago. Hopefully they get all the kinks worked out soon. Also, this White Castle is pretty pricey. A combo with 4 sliders, fries, and a drink will cost you $7.99. Add cheese to them and it's $8.99. Kind of expensive for pretty mediocre food if you ask me.

Open 24 hours but there seems to always be a line! We went for lunch on a Monday and there was a line out the door. It's probably because of all the hype since it just opened. Definitely worth a try just to see what the fuss is about, but now that I've tried it, I'll probably pass next time unless things improve. Located across from the Mirage.

I don't understand the rave about this place. Out of years of curiosity, I finally decided to try this place out. Why in Las Vegas? I don't know maybe because it is the only location I know of for now and no I would not try it from frozen bought from grocery stores. I'd rather have it freshly made to have a real experience of the slider.

Now, I've heard that the grilled onions are the specialty ingredient that gives the slider buns and patty a flavorful taste. Although true, the slider is very simplistic. Cheese and an extremely thin piece of Wendy's shaped patty, that is it. And guess how much it is, almost $2!! Seriously, this little tiny cube of a slider is more expensive than a burger from the dollar menu in Mc Donald's? Nuh uh... I can't comprehend the favoritism of this place.

Chicken rings were alright as what I would expect, a chicken nugget in the shape of a ring like an onion ring. What is weird is that the onion, on the other hand, doesn't come in rings as we are used to, but in chip form. The onion chips might be the only reason why I would come back to White Castle now. The pieces of onion are thick and wide and yep it does taste like onion and not just the fried batter.

Overall I think I'd appreciate this place more if their menu was less expensive for the amount they serve. This place is 24 hours so it caters to the drunk club goers. Actually now that I've thought of it, maybe the prices are high in order to keep dirty homeless people from coming in or hanging around. If I end up visiting the East Coast maybe I'd give White Castle another try someday but for now I'll stick with other burger places.

Ok it's in casino royale but surprisingly not smoky. I was there in the day time tho. As a local we parked in the mirage walked toward Carnegie deli past rhumbar outside and across the street. Go left and it will be on your right past out back. 
It smells like an armpit.  Ok strong onions. The line  is confusing a bit. Walk past all the ppl waiting for their food to order. You'll see what I mean...

These are not the burgers I was looking for ...

The White Castle of my youth was known for potent grilled onion flavor in a bun laden with grease drippings. The onions and grease are key to the entire experience. Without them, you've just got a tiny, boring, dry cheeseburger ... which is what you get here. 

I mean, you can see them grilling the food right there, but somehow it comes out tasting almost exactly like the crappy frozen microwave version! You don't taste the onions at all and there's minimal grease to liven up that dry bun. 

Dunno if this is typical corporate quality-cutting when something develops a following, or just this particular location not having their stuff together, but this ain't the White Castle people rave about. About as cheap as Strip food gets at 1.30 for regular and 1.60 with cheese, but you might as well just microwave up a six pack if it's gonna be like this ...

Where's the ketchup and why so salty ?! I'm from NY, and had White Castle twice in the past three weeks ago in NY so I feel like I can make a fair comparison. This location is not a fair representation of the white castle experience.

As a west coaster, I was extremely excited to see White Castle on the strip. Of course we had to try it!! Small burgers but the food was pretty good! Also got onion chips or something like that. It's basically onion rings but cut to slices and not rings. They were my favorite thing! Super good! 

Defiantly glad I had the opportunity to try this place. I would eat it again but maybe not go out of my way to get it.

White Castle was a childhood staple for me.  I absolutely LOVED them.  Unfortunately as I've gotten older, I only get heartburn and an upset stomach now.

They say, you can never go home again.  This is a perfect example.

The Veggie Sliders are baaaack!! (They are vegan with the Sweet Thai sauce, or ketchup, of course.) 

I'm from the midwest, where White Castles are part of the urban culture and everyone has a story or two to tell about a WC experience.  When I gave up beef in high school, I would eat the chicken rings and fish sandwiches/nibblers. After giving up all meat, I was left with french fries. However, I moved to AZ a few years ago and I swear, as soon as I moved, they introduced the veggie sliders. Unfortunately, there were no White Castles west of my hometown at the time. Then came the opening of this Vegas location in 2015. I was ecstatic! 

I drove to Vegas, went straight to this White Castle, and glazed in amazement as I saw that they sold the Veggie Sliders. Once I reached the cashier to order the Veggie Sliders I was advised that they stopped selling them.  I cannot express the levels of 1st world sadness that came over me. I sulked into the background as the rest of my family joyously ordered cheese fries and chicken rings with extra honey mustard.   We returned a few months later so family and friends could get their fix and lo and behold, the veggie sliders were back!! Security cameras may or may not show me dancing around in front of the register. 

The veggie sliders are a Dr. Praeger creation, made with veggies (carrots, broccoli, spinach, etc.) instead of soy.  Do not compare them to the original sliders (although, if they teamed up with Beyond Meat or Gardein, they could replicate those); you will only be disappointed.  These sliders are vegan (including the bun), and the Sweet Thai sauce option is also vegan. Some veg*ns do not like them; I love them!  I love being able to eat a full meal at the same place that my non-veg family eats. And I don't care if they are "healthy" or not (they may be). You don't go to White Castle for healthy meals; you go for the junk food!


This Vegas location stays packed, particularly later in the evenings.  I've had success in beating the crowds by going earlier in the day, before noon.  The employees are constantly cleaning the dining area, so it tends to stay clean and well stocked.  The drinks are self-serve here, unlike other WCs, which took away my joy of asking for a "mix" (which only White Castle OGs will understand).  


The prices at this location are jacked up, up to 50% or more on some items (e.g. The Veggie Sliders cost .99 back home; they cost $1.79 here! Milkshakes are nearly $6!!).  Also, this may very well be the only White Castle in existence that doesn't have a drive-thru, so come prepared to go inside. And definitely walk, not drive, as parking is almost non-existent along the strip.

Aside from my complaints, the fact that after nearly a century there is finally a White Castle west of the Mississippi, it's open 24/7, and they have the veggie sliders, AND it's a short road trip for me, is a win-win.
Food doesn't live up to the hype. Wasn't impressed, staff was decent . Over all it was an average experience.
Omg I miss these little things! ! Just like back in Chicago.  Just need to get one in San Diego now.

Disgusting.  I wanted to see what the hype was all about. Should of not wasted my time. 

First of all, parking for us Vegas peeps is not convenient. It's actually IN the Best Western. So you need to go around back and park in the garage. 

I must say that the employees are awesome!!!  They are helpful, nice and not hating their jobs. Which is amazing considering the line NEVER stops. 

They do have beer on tap. I should've got one...might have made things taste better!

The food was fresh but nasty and soggy. Not my thing. Chicken rings are gross. Why do they get to call it chicken???  The onion bites weren't bad. Not making another trip just for those though!

I can say "been there, done that"!
Just wasn't the same as back home I asked for extra pickles I asked for steamed cheeseburgers and I got nothing

If you want to eat dog food sure try this spot. Ordered 30 sliders, 6 orders of fries and nuggets. Everything was complete garbage. The burger patty was a square party which by far had the be the cheapest processed meat i have ever tasted. All the came in the sliders was meat, cheese, onions and pickles. The sliders were soggy and tasteless. Refrain from eating here please! Save your money and go elsewhere. Dont believe the hype.

The food and the service were on point.  Since there are no White Castles in Cali I had to give it a try.  Just know the burgers are small, so order a bunch.  I guess the correct term would be a slider, but this spot is worth trying.  Way better than the frozen versions at my grocery store.

I've never had White Castle except from the frozen aisle so when we were in the area, we decided to stop by for a little bite to eat. It was around midnight so it was not busy at all. The young lady who took our order did not look like she wanted to be there but she did greet us with a hi.

My bf and I ordered the number 1 and four extra sliders and the food was OK, nothing special. A little expensive for small sliders and I thought it had way too much onions .

There was an employee cleaning the tables and I noticed he coughed a few times and he did not cover his mouth. It was so disgusting to see. 

I probably won't be back anytime soon.

Highly, highly, highly,highly over-rated.  I've been wanting to eat at White Castle for ages but obviously, this White Castle is the only location on the west coast.  Since I'm here in Vegas for a month for work, I knew that I had to try White Castle.  Obviously White Castle is a huge novelty and I had huge expectations.  I was sorely disappointed.  I got the meal with 4 sliders (2 cheese and 2 without), fries, and a drink.  The buns were soggy, the meat was extremely flimsy and tasted so artificial, and the fries were unevenly cooked and unseasoned.  The fries tasted as if they were from the freezer section.  The only reason to eat here is for the novelty - there is a ridiculous number of good eateries.  Do not waste your calories here!

1 star for novelty and 1 star for a decently cheap place to eat on the Strip.

So we're in Vegas...kinda drunk and hungry. What do we do? Go to White Castle! 

Yeah...soooooo not good at all. I don't know why my friends on the East Coast rave over these gross mini burgers. Honestly they taste like they've been microwaved. *shudder* 

If you must, try it out so that you get it out of your system and off of a bucket list of some kind.

A friend reminded me not to try this chain the last time I came to Vegas.  I think I know why now.  Since my sister wanted to try it out, we ordered three of the sliders.  The bread was soggy.   Patty was just there.  The customer service was great.

Best hang over food. Burgers and fries. Enough said. 

Only thing I have problem with is they stop serving coffee after 11am or noon. 

Coffee should be all day thing esp in a city like Vegas.


Otherwise burger is pretty much basic and self explanatory. Cheeseburger over regular burger and you need to eat at least 3 of those to compare to eating one burger since it's so small.

Get regular fries and onion rings... they both go well with the burger. They also have beer on tap.

Enjoy!

Came here with my dad who is from chicago so he was super excited. for as busy as it was it was very clean and the staff super up beat.... the food is your standard white castle burger and fries.... nothing more nothing less

First experience here, and I was not impressed. 

The line was long but moved fast, and it's so busy that they yell out your order # over a loud speaker for you to claim your food. The sliders were this onion-y steamed mess, and I can see why they might be appealing if you're drunk. However, If you come here sober looking for a tasty snack you will definitely be disappointed. Also, be prepared to be overcharged like at most places on the strip.

Overall, I don't think that I'd come here again. It was a nice novelty to experience but one time will be enough for me.

Finally got to try this without having to go to the Midwest.  It was a bucket list checked item.  The lady who took our order was so so sweet.  She asked if we wanted onion chips or fries with our order and we wernt sure what onion chips were so she gave us a sample.  How sweet was that?  We went with it.  The burgers are steamed format with onions and yes it tastes much better fresh than frozen.  I must say though that being a Cali girl that it just can't compare to In N Out and The Habit. I really wanted to love WC but it was only so-so.  Shake Shack is next on my list.

This isn't a fancy kobe burger from a 5 star restaurant people.. It's White Castle! It's fast food. It's perfect. Not sure what all the low star reviews are about but geez.. THESE LITTLE BURGERS ARE DELICIOUS. The burgers melt in your mouth & your left thinking "Why didn't I buy 30.." 5 stars to you, White Castle. You will be missed!

First time ever eating at a white castle. Always wanted to go after watching the Harold and Kumar film. The food was pretty good, but not satisfying. If you want to be full, you'd need to get about 10 sliders. I would say the sliders are perfect for a snack. My order was messed up and the manager was kind to offer me some dessert as an apology. The staff were super nice. The place was clean as any vegas joint can be. I would be back again.

Don't get me wrong. These steamy little cheeseburger sliders are good, but they didn't satisfy my curiosity in a way I thought they would. They taste just like the microwaveable sliders you can get at the grocery store, so I'm much happier just getting those. Fries are nothing great. Remind me of Del Taco fries. I'd come back for a quick fix, but I'm proud to say that I'll take west coast In-n-Out over east coast White Castle any day!!

I was super excited to see that they had a white castle in vegas since the only white castle burgers I had were the microwavable ones. However, after waiting in such a long line, I was disappointed to see that these burgers taste EXACTLY like the microwavable burgers. Even the fish filet sandwich tastes exactly like mcdonald's fish filet. I just wished they tasted a little better. Granted, I still love how white castle has sliders because its small and is more fitting for my small appetite. Now I know that I am not missing out on much if I just buy frozen sliders from Stop & Shop.

The frozen white castle sliders are great!  So I would think the ones at the actual restaurant would be better... 

Got four cheese sliders, ate one and threw the rest away...lol

Went to In & Out after...lol

Been wanting to venture out to White Castle for about a decade now. Ever since Harold and Kumar made their voyage, I've been anticipating my own. Had a few days off from work and figured it was time to try these burgers fresh, instead of the ones from the frozen food section that I have once in a while.

Walking down the strip towards White Castle was awesome and exciting but when I finally pulled out my first slider my excitement faded a bit (not much, it's Vegas!). The bread was very soggy and they tasted about the same as the frozen ones to me. Though these had more cheese. Was expecting a fresh White Castle patty to be tastier. Maybe this just isn't a great location. I'm definitely trying White Castle again if I ever encounter another chain.

If you happen to stop by a White Castle I would firstly advise you not to settle for this and turn away. Vegas has so many better options! What? Sorry! If you're on some quest like me or just dgaf than I'd recommend asking for a toasted bun if you choose to eat here. It is a cool experience to have if you are a fan of the Harold and Kumar movies, but beyond that these burgers are kinda average (both frozen ones and these).

While the burger itself wasn't what i was hoping for, I was still glad I made the drive to White Castle. It was an experience I knew I wanted to have and though the burgers weren't satisfying, the overall experience was fun. Oh yeah and the fries were meh too. Though crispy. Throw some Cajun Seasoning on them sumbitches or something! Thank God for Ketchup. 

Pros:
+ Staff was nice

Cons:
- Bun was very soggy
- Fries were bland
- Location could have been cleaner (several dirty tables)

First time to white castle.  The food was all right, but our order wasn't put in, so we waited.  Then we find out that our order wasn't complete.  We waited for a few minutes longer for someone to hand us the rest of our order.  Which was made into a huge ordeal.  Also the employee who call out the orders that are ready for pick up needs to back off on yelling through the intercom.

Umm, why is the best hamburger joint getting such hate?? It's the best chain ever. Supper delicious 
I wish we had em in texas

Because this is on the strip, it's a little more expensive. Aside from that, I enjoyed the food. I got a couple of  hamburger sliders, fries and onion chips. 

Sliders were good. Although I felt that the patties were so thin that you can barely taste it. The pickles were just as thick if not thicker than the patty. I loved the grilled onions on the slider. more flavor. I could probably eat a dozen of these guys. These fries are the best because the wrinkle cut fries has way more crisp because there's a larger surface area for it be fried than a normal straight cut fry. NOW let me tell you about the onion chips. If you like onion rights you will like this because they are just big size fried onion wedges. I would highly recommend this over the fries just because the fries were not as crispy as I would have liked. A great place to grab a snack after all the drinking.

Over hyped. Soggy buns, flavorless patty's with diced onions. Came here drunk at 3am Saturday night, speedy service but the flavors did not deliver, taste exactly the same as the frozen packs at the grocery stores. The sides were good though like the onion rings. So many better choices but if your curiosity is getting the best of you then prepare for disappointment.

GARBAGE!  After a day of drinking and gambling I wanted a quick bite before bed and saw that White Castle was right by my hotel.  Looking forward to trying it out and all the people that rave about, its not all that or even that.  The burgers were flavorless, except the pickle and whatever onions they used that gave me severe heartburn all night and the next day.  three days later and my stomach still hates me for eating them and for almost $10 for sliders and fries, I could got a real burger.  Save your money and spend a few extra dollars somewhere else, this is just a tourist trap.
Not bad and kinda good while walking around on the strip looking for that midnight snack. I got the sliders (with no cheese) and some fries.

Came here twice on my recent trip and I thought the food was really good.  The sliders were like butter.  It's so good.  I don't think I can eat 10 of them though, but I had a few.  Got some double cheeses and the loaded fries.  Good stuff.  I think the fries could of been bigger though, but it's all good.  

Service was fairly quick and the employees were very nice.  Totally recommend this spot if you want a quick bite.  Got some good seating.

Came here to see what the hype was all about. First time trying it my gf and I shared the #1. 4 original sliders, fries and a drink. Of course we got some t shirts (because we're tourists).

Don't know what all the fuss was about, it's mediocre. The bun or roll is good with the grilled onions but the hamburger patty is too small, the meat to bread ratio is off. Guess you had to grow up eating it to be a fan. To each their own.

On the bright side, no crazy lines. Lots of clean tables and the service was fast and friendly.

I wouldn't suggest going there. Main thing that I didn't like was meat. The  meat looked and tasted like cardboard. I got acidity right away and my stomach was upset all night. Service was slow. Huge line. I will never eat there again.

When I saw that White Castle got only 2.5 stars I was like naawww that can't be, but guess what; it's truly what it deserves.

Being from New Jersey, I pretty much grew up eating White Castle. Ever since I moved here in 2005 I always complained that there was no White Castle and that the frozen ones don't taste the same. But holy shit, I would actually prefer the frozen one's over these "fresh" ones. I was just insanely disappointed.

My husband has never had White Castle in his life and he really wanted to go randomly at 3AM. It's inside the Best Western casino/hotel which is just a really random place to have it in the first place. I actually didn't wanna try White Castle in Vegas because I already had a feeling that it wasn't going to live up to it's name here like it does on the East Coast and I was so right.

We ordered 4 cheese sliders to share with fries & a drink. Order came quickly and of course hubby couldn't wait to try it. The sliders were warm and the cheese was barely melted which means it was most likely just sitting out for a while. I let that go cuz I haven't had "fresh" White Castle in forever and I was just hungry as fuck. All was good until hubby bit into his second slider then started making this weird ass noise and faces at me until I looked at his burger and saw a freaking curly ass strand of hair in his slider. FUCK THAT. Instantly, my stomach just churned and I just felt like I had a stomach ache. I'm sure that if I hadn't seen that piece of hair I would've been fine, but that just ruined White Castle for me (at least in Vegas). He brought it to the cashier, hair still intact and shit and they gave him 2 double cheese sliders. Nice of the cashier but it still didn't make up for how shitty we felt after eating there. What's sad too is that I overheard other people saying how much this place sucks :/

So I came to the conclusion that I'm never going to waste a drive to the Strip again and if I want White Castle I will just go to Smith's and get the frozen ones. Seriously, you're probably better off not driving down there and dealing with all the tourist and drunk people.

It's cool that Vegas is trying to expand on all of the popular foods from other states but I seriously think White Castle belongs only on the East Coast. I still love White Castle though but just not this location. Maybe they should consider making a location away from Strip!

I guess my expectations were a bit too high when I came to this place thanks to Harold and Kumar. The slider burgers were edible, but they tasted plain. Simple taste of bread, patty, and whatever else was in there. It is a good place in Vegas if you get too drunk since they're open 24 hours and it is convenient, but this is just an average fast-food joint for the quality of their food.

At least I can say that I've been to White Castle(although not with Harold and Kumar). :)

White Castle was a must-try on this last trip to Vegas with my friends. 

We each ordered the original sliders with cheese combo, which comes with four sliders, fries and a drink. I liked the overall flavor of the sliders, especially the grilled onions, but the patty was like the consistency of a McDonald's patty. I also liked that there were different sauce options but some were kinda bland. Fries were good, no problems there. I did appreciate that the sliders were individually boxed and that it was reasonably priced.

Service was awesome - everyone at this location was so sweet and made sure that our order was correct. 

I really don't have much to compare White Castle to but I have to say that out of In-n-Out, Shake Shack, and White Castle - In-n-Out is still my number one choice when it comes to a burger. If you haven't tried White Castle, it's definitely worth a trip to cross it off your burger bucket list.
Your average burger place.  Its a novelty coz its the only one in Nevada.  Normally White Castle comes frozen in a box. I was surprise they had the vegi burger.

Haha!! Finally got to try this place after years and years of wanting to try their infamous burgers after the Kumar and Harold movie. This was probably the first spot we hit up after we arrived in Las Vegas because that's how badly and excited we were to come here. Here are my thoughts...they taste just like the frozen ones!!! They taste exactly the same except it has a pickle haha. They are kinda expensive too for a dinky burger. I am glad I got to finally try it. If I crave for it I can always get the frozen ones. The milkshake was good. The bigger combo you get the cheaper the burgers are per unit. They are quite expensive for what it is individually. It is probably expensive because of the brand and because it's located on the strip. Everything on the strip is super expensive and overpriced. I think a cheeseburger is like $1.69 each? Overall, this is one of those places you gotta check out when you're in Las Vegas because it's the only one in the east coast. It's opened 24/7 so that's awesome. Hungry? Why wait? Grab a White Castle burger. Just don't spoil your appetite. I ate so much burger while in Vegas that I didn't enjoy my Gordon Ramsey burger at BurGR and didn't enjoy my Shake Shack burger too lmao. I would definitely come here again to show off since it's the only one in the east coast.

This place was so good. Loved the cheeseburgers and fries. The only thing I didn't like was the place they put it in. It was right next to the casino. The casino was small and the only way to get to White Castle, is to go to the small casino. But I still loved White Castle!
This is located further down on the strip, just past Harrahas. We had never eaten here before and have heard much about it. A fun and good experience... glad to have had it once.

I never had White Castle before, but you know... I was one of those millennials who had a curiosity due to that damn Harold and Kumar movie. 

My friends and I were nearby, and we saw there was no lines so we thought we would try it. We got the combo with the 4 burgers, fries, and a drink. We all had Fat Tuesdays so I gave my drink cup away, haha. The fries were standard, and the burger was okay. It's just like a thin hamburger patty, with cheese, in a Hawaiian roll, haha. I guess this is stuff you probably should have grew up with in order to like it, or maybe should have help from Miss Mary Jane like Harold and Kumar.. I don't know, haha.
The best i love the onion chips the food is amazing the lil burgers melt in your mouth luv this place thank you white castles for coming to Las Vegas

I have finally got the chance to try white castle and it's just hyped. It did not meet my expectations, its just a plain slider with low quality tasting meat. I also got loaded fries, which was better than the sliders. Would I come again? No, I don't think it was worth the money and one employee just made my experience worse than it already was. He was inattentive, impatient with customers, and always busy talking to his coworkers. This is my first time and will definitely be my last.

I live in Georgia, where we don't really have White Castle restaurants.  We do have something called Krystal, which sells small sized boxed burgers too but all the northern transplants down here (which are annoyingly plentiful) always say White Castle is so much better and they always wax nostalgic about growing up devouring their burgers.  I'm not a fan of Krystal either, so I believed them.  

The only White Castle burgers I'd ever tasted were the refrigerated, microwavable ones you buy at the grocery store.  They were bland, but I gave the transplants the benefit of the doubt.  After all, the microwavable sandwiches probably didn't taste like the real thing.  

Fast forward to March 23, 2016:  I'm on vacation in Las Vegas and I'm staying at the Casino Royale Hotel.  There happens to be a White Castle restaurant right here in my hotel!  It was late at night, I was starving after a long day of just having fun on the Strip without eating anything.  Just about anything would have been delicious to me at the time.  I walked in, ordered their $9.99 package (which includes 4 small cheeseburgers, fries and a soft drink) and immediately took it back to my room.  

A previous poster here, named Leanne L., summed it up perfectly:  It tasted no different from the microwavable White Castle burgers you get at the supermarket.  And the fries were only slightly better.  After all these years of having northerners tell me how great White Castle is, I was disappointed.  It sucked when the best part of my meal was the Coca Cola I drank.  

I guess the northern transplants will tell me that since the restaurant I went to was located in Vegas, it was just a bastardized version of White Castle and not the one they grew up eating.  We all know Sin City likes to replicate themes from other places, but I doubt this is the case here.  I doubt I'll eat there again unless I'm just desperately hungry and don't feel like walking all over the Strip to go somewhere else.  I do admit that their chocolate cheesecake on a stick looked good on the menu, but I didn't try that.  

I give them good marks for having friendly cashiers and quick service even though the place was crowded.  But I was there for the food and it really wasn't much different from Krystal.  Little, bitty tasteless burgers with cheese, diced onions and no tomatoes.
Lol tastes exactly like the microwaveable. What's the point. Just go to Walgreens next door and get the frozen ones if the line is too long here

Tried White Castle for the first time last night. I'm disappointed to say that I'm not a fan of it. It's overrated and bland. I only ate it because I was out with friends. I can't believe I wasted my money on some gross food.

My boyfriend's a fan and he liked it.  So that's why it gets 3 stars.

It's a weirdly laid-out restaurant in a small, shady hotel.  Service was less than friendly.  The food was White Castle-y.  And my boyfriend liked it.  So there's that.

So when my brother and I were kids, our mom would drag us back east from time to time and our favorite part of the trips were going to White Castle.

So j was excited to go but that excitement went away quickly after the 1st bite. I honestly think the frozen ones I buy at the store have more flavor.

The restaurant is clean. The service was good. I was just expecting more from the little burgers. Oh well.

Good stuff for the price! Hadn't had a White Castle before so I decided to give them a try. Had the #2 combo which is for 4 cheese sliders, regular fries and a regular drink for $8.99.  Actually a lot of food for one so my wife helped with the fries. Give them a try next time you're in Vegas.

Such a long wait for such small burgers, but I would wait again, totally worth it if you are a fan of sliders. I got the 20pack w/fries and an order of onion chips. Tasted great . Wished they had more workers for the long lines they have of hungry people waiting .

After a night of dancing, my friends and I went to White Castle. No regrets.

I have had White Castle burgers in the past. From the freezer section at the supermarket. I have always wonder if they are really that, uh, good, in real life. After Tao, we stopped at White Castle and bought the 20 piece combo with fries and chicken rings. Yes, chicken rings. 

The verdict: White Castle burgers taste just like the burgers you get out of the freezer aisle. They were pretty damn satisfying and tasty. The fries were good and the chicken rings were definitely questionable. I would definitely go back!

Everything at white castle was exactly what i had expected. Minus the less than adequate crinkle cut fries. 

Up til this point in life, I've only had the white castle burgers from the frozen aisle. I must say, the taste unbelievably similar. Even though it wasn't mind blowningly better than the frozen ones, I was not disappoint one bit. The original hamburger had a very rich beefy flavor; while the cheeseburger was nice and cheesy. It's soft, simple, and quite addicting. 

As good as whitecastle may sound, I wouldn't go out of my way to get it. Afterall, it's still fast food. Probably not the best for your health. Please open one in southern California so I can eat it more often!

Very nice employees, fresh, hot food. When we went there was no line and the wait time was less than 5 min. We go every year and depending on the time of day/day of the week it can be busy. But we like the place, better than the microwave one's e get from the store for sure. Worth stopping in for sure!

To all west coast tofu eating tree hugging hippies, please stay out of my beloved White Castle. All you do is slow me from getting my crave case. I can not begin to understand how someone could "evaluate" a White Castle as if it was some kind of high end steakhouse. 

1. White Castle is NOT an east coast thing. The first White Castle was opened in Wichita Kansas.  
2. There are none west of the Mississippi? 31 in Missouri, one in Vegas and 68 in Illinois which sits on the east side of the great river, I say close enough.

Eat them sober, why? A shot of tequila should come with four ingredients, tequila, lime, salt and a Whitie! A twelve pack of beer should be called a twenty pack, twelve beer and eight sliders.

If it was up to me I would add one more option to the menu. Grind up all the west coast Castle bashers, mix them with the beef and call it the west coast Whitie. Go back to your over-rated In and Out burger!

I've heard that this place was really good but the downside was the wait time. Unfortunately, I did not have the same experience. There really was no wait time and the food was pretty bland. I was suckered in by all the Hype around it due to Harold and Kumar. I would give it another chance though.

This place is really good but not as good compared to In n Out. There might be a lot of people in there but don't be intimidated! The food comes out in just a minute! There are many workers there to make your food. However the employees there aren't very friendly.

Since we've never had white castle aside from the frozen burgers from the grocery store this was a must stop.

We had the luck of getting a 10% off coupon while on our way there. 

We opted for the number 7 combo which consisted of 10 sliders, 2 fries, and 2 drinks. We upgraded the sliders to have cheese because who can eat a burger without cheese? Total after discount came to around 21 bucks.

The sliders were good and didn't require ketchup surprisingly. The fries come unseasoned so you need to add your own salt and pepper.

The downside is that you wind up having gas all day after eating them. The plus side is theyre way better than the freezer stuff.

I had to try this place just because of watching Harold and Kumar movie and I don't think I will go back. 

It's jus ok and the burgers are really tiny and the onions on top don't really taste the best. 
There are plenty of better fast food places them this place. 

If you want to try it like I did then just get a single small burger just to say you tried it and don't get the fries. M

I am so glad I don't have to move back to the mid-west for these wonderful little sliders. Truth behold, don't come in here with high expectations because it is fast food, after all. There are very few places in Las Vegas where you can get a meal for under $10, aside from your typical McDonalds, Subway, Panda Express...White Castle is just another fast food option.

I came here the second week of opening and there are still long lines. If you don't like waiting an hour for sliders, come during the graveyard shift and the wait becomes only 10-15 minutes. Management still needs to train its employees better. All their trash bins were full at 10pm, and no staff was emptying out the trash, leaving piles of WC boxes stacked up a mile high. But I believe once the hype dwindles down, WC management will figure out what changes need to be made for this location.

I'll be back White Castle!

Pretty disappointing experience. We usually frequent the smaller, specialty donut shops but opted to use DD this time. We had preordered a couple dozen donuts (needed certain donuts) and a box of donut holes (again a certain kind). Now mind you we called the day before to make sure they had the certain donuts since we were going to use them to make a "donut cake" for someone with thier favorite donuts. 

Went to pick them up and they didn't have the whole order. No real apology just a "uh, oops someone must have given them away, there's another DD on blah blah". And that was that! We were already in a rush but we had to spend an additional 30 min calling and driving to other donut shops to find the rest of the donuts we needed. 

So clearly calling a day before was pointless because they clearly don't care. Service was beyond poor and considering we don't really think their donuts are that amazing I think we will stick to the smaller shops that actually do focus on service and care about their patrons.

All I can say is that the staff here are so nice and accommodating and friendly. The manager was super nice and the staff made my drink and made sure it was to my taste :) I highly recommend this place!!! Oh and the food tastes great!!!!

I'm gonna get slaughtered for giving this place a bad review, but whatever. 

I was told by several people that I absolutely HAD to check out Primanti Bros while I was in Pittsburgh. I was excited about visiting this institution during my stay... but it really didn't deliver for me. 

Yes, this was a huge sandwich with fries and cole slaw in it, but the sheer quantity of food didn't make up for the fact that it was really bland. Maybe I just got the wrong thing (the Pittsburger Cheese Steak - which is somehow their #2 seller...?). My friend liked her sandwich, which was eggs and bacon, I believe. Maybe we just went to the wrong Primanti Bros location. 

I would give this place another shot if I'm ever in town again, but my first impression wasn't a great one.
Food was ok. Not seasoned, fries were soggy and the people behind the counter were not friendly at all

The sandwiches are interesting and the fries in them are interesting.

I don't like fries or potatoey fries, mostly just the crispy ones.

The sandwich was good and quick but because I'm not a huge fan of fries it wouldn't make sense for me to go back.

It also was super crowded.

Here's how you can make your own Primanti Bros Sandwich at home:

Take two slices of Italian Bread, between them, mash together bland cole slaw, fries, some assorted meat, tomatoes. And at your fingertips is Pitt's pride and joy.  I'm not from here, so maybe I don't share the love. We weren't really drunk when we were eating here, and it was in the middle of the day. 

The service was pretty slow, but when our order was taken, the sandwich came out very fast.

It was a good sandwich in terms of having really hot meat, and cold tomatoes and cole slaw, but I didn't think its as tasty as it could have been.

I think the bread should be buttered and toasted/grilled texas toast, and they should use seasoned fries. Use some sweet North Carolina style Cole slaw. 
I came, I saw, and I conquered, but I'm giving it back. I probably won't be back ever again.

Dropped in on Sunday, 12/22/2013, for a beer. We sat at the bar and were served promptly. Food looked amazing. The waitress checked in with us, we were under some time pressure so I took the opportunity to try to pay while things were slow.  Somehow the normal queues seem to have been missed and she simply stated "oh, you can keep the tab open, there's no rush" and walked away leaving the card on the counter.

And boy did she mean no rush.
