I ordered the gaucho taco that was recommended by our waiter that was one of the best tacos I had ever had and trust me I've had tons of tacos and don't even get me started about the shrimp tacos they have

I so wanted to love this place. I was in the area to get a haircut with fave barber but told he was on break. So I decided to venture out in the area for lunch. The beautiful entrance door caught my attention and decided to try it.

Since I broke my foot, I'm crutchin' along with the dang boot on my left foot. I must have arrived minutes before the lunch rush. I sat at a little table in a corner. Waitress took my order.  Because the tables are so close to one another and filled, I couldn't go to the Salsa bar to try a few sauces. 

I ordered the guacamole which was yummy -- love guaca guaca! When I ordered two chicken tacos, I expected two nice size tacos. Instead I felt as though I ordered two tacos off the menu section for kids.

Waitress never returned to refill my glass of tea. I may return and give this place a try when I'm no longer in need of crutches. Nothing grand here...now run along kids...

PS...They do not accept AMEX!

Just go here. You won't be disappointed.

The atmosphere is cozy and hip with rustic tables and chairs and dia de los muertos artwork lining the walls. The staff is FRIENDLY. I can't emphasize that enough. I have been for lunch and they handle the crowds well. At dinner, and during slower traffic times, they are very attentive and ensure that you have everything you need.

The food. Where do I begin. I will start with the amazing salsa bar. They have about a dozen salsas per day. Fresh. My favorite is the seven chile salsa which is simply roasted chiles and red onions. They are all amazing though.

As far as the tacos, I have only ever eaten the pibil and the mole, and that's because they are so good, that I can't branch out yet. Every time I go, those are the ones I am craving. The pibil is so good that it makes me fully appreciate Johnny Depp's character in "Once Upon a Time in Mexico" having such a love of good pibil. 

If you go at lunch, go before 11:30 to beat the crowd. This is one of my favorite places to eat. Hands down. Get some horchata to go as well. They top it with fruit and pecans. Yum!

Best fish taco I've had so far. On that scale I give it a well deserved 5 stars. I also had the pork and chicken street tacos, I would probably only order the fish taco next time. 
Authentic. Great choice of house made salsas.

Considering salsa is my favorite food group, La Condesa is a small piece of heaven. The carne asada and cabo shrimp tacos are delicious. This place gets very busy during lunch and is pretty cramped. Wouldn't recommend for large groups. Mmmmm salsa.

I used to come here when most people wouldn't venture this far down 16th. Now you can expect an hour wait on the weekend. It is well written it, though.  I rec the Gandhi taco on corn tortilla, with addition of fried oaxaca cheese. Obviously not vegan anymore, but yum!!

Authentic Mexican food made with quality ingredients in a comfortable setting. Salsa bar has great variety from the usual to ones with strawberry. Munch on salsa and chips while they make your food which does take a little time as it's cooked to order. I like my food spicy but like to counter it with their horchata which is chock full of fruit and pecans. My favorites are the chicken mole and grilled veggie tacos.

Wow wow wow wow wow
Best Mexican around. Only reason I tried this place was because of all the reviews. Doesn't look like much from the outside but it was amazing. Awesome salsa bar! The guacamole is different but awesome! The street tacos with great too. I'll be coming back to try more stuff!

Food was very good, it wasn't what I expected as they use different ingredients together (like pecans in the sangria or cranberries and mango in the guacamole). Everything was fresh and home made. The only thing lacking slightly was the service. They got a few things wrong, took awhile, and was a little slow. But it definitely wouldn't stop me from going back. Menu is very extensive and you can customize.

Pros: Full bar, salsa bar

Cons: No bartender, watery salsas, poor service.

We visited this shop for a weekend lunch.  We were starving and didn't have a lot of time, so we opted to quickly sit at the bar.  We waited 5 minutes, and a server brought us chips.  We then went and picked out a few salsas from the salsa bar.

Out of the 4 salsas I tried, I liked none of them.  They were very thin and watery, and the plastic containers are smaller than the chips - so you can only dip the corner of a chip (but the salsa won't stick), and you can't pour the salsa onto a chip (because it will run off).  The only chips that sort of work are the 'defective' folded ones. I have no idea why everyone raves about the salsa bar, perhaps for the novelty of it, but chips don't work as a salsa-delivery vehicle for watery salsa.

After 10 minutes, we still did not have water, and 15 minutes into us sitting there, we apologized and left.  Their tacos may well be amazing, but we didn't have time to sit around.  Waiting for 15 minutes (literally) with no water delivery during an AZ summer should be criminal.

There appeared to only be 2 servers for the entire restaurant, and no bartender, and they clearly couldn't handle a lunchtime rush by themselves.  Luckily, there are many other excellent taco shops in the area.

A hole in the wall but amazing quesadilla!!! The tacos were alright, the star of this restaurant would definitely have to be the quesadilla, you can't go here and not order one or two or THREE!! Lol the bread/crust/dough if the quesadilla is amazing! The salsa bar for the nachos they provide while you wait for your food is fun and there are some good selections, esp the cilantro one and I don't even like cilantro.

Other than the fact that I should have brushed up on my Rosetta Stone Spanish Edition before trying to find La Condessa I can honestly say I haven't had better tacos in PHX. 
The place is a little hard to find if it's your first time so after multiple turn arounds and a stop at the Panaderia to ask for directions my colleague and I arrived at taco bliss. 

The meal starts off with an endless bowl of fresh tortilla chips and a salsa bar that would make Bobby Flay  jealous. They had some of the best homemade salsas with a large variety. From your classic Pico De Gallo to a Creamy Cilantro salsa. 

I ordered the two taco platter with a tinga taco and a carne asada Taco. These were both great. The carne asada was a little dry for my taste but with the assist of the homemade salsa's it was a perfect combo. The tinga taco was a perfect combination of slowly cooked shredded chicken and seasoning. My colleague got a carne asada burrito and a tinga taco and was satisfied by both. 

In short if I am looking for a great taco for a good price I am going back to La Condesa.

The best Mexican food around.
Salsa bar has too many options - cilantro salsa got me like crazy.
The classic lime margarita ( superb tasty), gandhi bowl, gandhi taco, vegan burro ( I don't remember the name) second one on their vegan menu- these are the things we ordered and every dish stands top.

Really liked it. FYI the waiting time is crazy. Entered at 8:10 and we seated by 9:00. I have no idea if they actually take reservations but a must try place.

Small restaurant, really good food. The Shark taco and Horchata are the best I've ever had. Don't care too much for the name of the restaurant (theme) or the dark artwork displayed. The food was worth me tolerating these images of the  SPIRIT of Death....he...he...
Everything I've had there has been amazing. The Veggie Burro is my favorite. The salsa bar kicks butt and the horchata is the best in town.

Offers a style of authentic Mexican food that varies from the northern regions of Mexico (Sonoran Mexican food) to the food that is found in deeper Mexico like mole, peanut salsa, etc. they have a very good vegan/vegetarian menu. Very authentic and very unique. Great art pieces to look at as well.

Me and my girlfriend were watching Diners, Drive ins, and Dines when Guy stopped here. We realized they were about 15 minutes away so we thought to check it out. It's a tiny little hole in the wall place that has about 10 tables. It can get kind of cramped but it is definitely worth it when that food hits your tongue. This place has the best mexican food! The only reason I don't give it 5 stars is because of how tiny it is and the fact that you have to pay $2.40 to get extra chips. Aside from this, this place is awesome!

This is taco heaven. 

Starting with the salsa bar that has several different types of salsas. From your classic pico, to pecan, strawberry, and the popular cilantro-cream, plus many more. Emphasis on the pecan because sweet jesus that stuff is so good. 

Refreshing Jamaica? Check. Sweet, milky horchata with nuts & fruit? Check. 

Lots of variety. The Mahi Mahi tacos, the Sonoran carne, the Dogfish, the Cabo shrimp - all of them are incredibly delicious. They do seafood very well here; never over or undercooked, and usually served up with fresh cabbage and drizzled with mayo, mole, or what have you. The rice is also excellent - always tender and perfectly seasoned. The Bullet burro (beans & cheese) is also pretty good, especially when you smother it in their fresh cilantro salsa. 

I've noticed some people saying they wish it was located in downtown-downtown Phoenix (what they really mean is gentrified), but I disagree. I like the location, especially because it's nestled in on the same street with other less "hip" mom & pop shops. It has a great neighborhood vibe - very comfortable. 
 
Put simply, I love this place. If you haven't tried it, you're missing out.

The sauce bar alone is worth the trip. Jenny C and her horrible taste buds can have her Taco Bell and their sauce. I enjoyed trying peanut, strawberry, radish, cilantro, guacamole, Cabo, chipotle, and Mexican salsa. We ordered a carne asada burrito. Good sauce in it, a healthy amount of peppers and avocado and cucumber. Fresh tortilla and ingredients. Cool dia de las muertes decor and a tight, cramped but bustling crowd. It's probably a better foodie place than a first date location. I loved it. I realize tastes differ, but anyone who thinks Taco Bell has more to offer ought to get their head and not just their tongue checked out for damage. That's you Jenny C.

I went to La Santisima for the first time when a friend took me here for lunch. I have been here about a dozen times since then!This place was on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives, so there is a lot of hype around this place, and trust me, it's real!

La Santisima has a superb menu with a big variety of items to pick from. Their tacos are delicious and they have a great Aztec Tinga taco. The quesadillas are huge, I can only eat about half when I get it.

They offer a large salsa bar that has at least 10 different salsas ranging from spicy to mild flavors. 

They offer a house margarita for $5 that is delicious, I get about two when I come hehe.They have a small bar but the drink offering is big, including Mexican beers. 

Service is friendly, fast, and courteous. 6-7 PM seems to be a peak time for this restaurant, so make sure you're here on time to get a table since it's a bit small and can fill up quick!
The salsa bar is worth writing sonnets about. Mayan Cochinita Pibil Taco with cilantro salsa might be the only thing I eat for the rest of my life.

Top 5 taco spots in my books. Double tortilla with ample amount of succulent meat with juice dropping on the plate. Each bite is mouth watering and goes great with my margarita at 11am after a hike. The salsa bar was impressive with over 10 different types. It made me want to salsa dance my way back to my seat and taco about how good the salsa was.

Reasons why I love this place:
1. Horchata with all kinds of goodies inside, like pecans and cantaloups and strawberries, I mean these are "real" and not those freeze-dried stuff. My poblem with it is it only comes in one size--32 ounces, which is like two meals for me.

2. The salsa bar...never knew there could be so many kinds of salsa! That alone is an adventure in taste-testing. My personal fave is the jicama one, which really is more of a relish but who's checking. 

3. Chicken mole and pibil...they do it right. Their mole could be a bit spicier for my taste but that's what the salsas are there for. I had the chicken mole as a taco and the pibil as a burro (separate occasion, alright, don't think I'm a pig now).

It's a great date place, I think. It's small, it's quaint, in a good neighborhood, and the satffers are very friendy. 

I love this place so much that I didn't even care about the tiny creature scurrying across the floor near the front door. That's  not their fault though. That was just an unfortunate situation. Not a reflection of them.

So try it.
We love this place. Delicious food, quaint atmosphere, and delicious food. Recently expanded to double the space, there may still be a wait, but it's worth it.
Salsa bar is HUGE but not maintained.  I sampled 5 tacos. None were that great. I was disappointed by this place. Service was 4/5. They really need to clean the place and the salad bar more often.

I have never loved tacos. This place changed my mind... The quality and size of their tacos surpasses that of America's (Sorry America's Taco Shop lovers) and it adds a strong local cultural vice that other taco shops lack with its Dia de los Muertos themed paintings. The meat is well-marinated (especially the carne asada) and the dozen-plus salsas are each different by tasty and made to perfection. You can spend ten-to-fifteen minutes just sorting through the salsa bar. I am lucky enough to live nearby and I take advantage of the shark tacos on most days :) I am so glad that it's caught on! I know that I will keep coming back!!!

yes another review of awesome accolades to a great taco shop. With all my repeat visits I thought I had written a review on this awesome taco shop. Apparently not. So, this is why I'm a fan of La Condesa... it's simply their beer battered dogfish shark tacos!!! they are soooooooooooooo good, it's like beachside fish tacos without the freaking beach, the taste, smells, and overall experience eating these totally delicious fish tacos can give you a mindf*** yes it's that good! and dipping them these beauties into my favorite salsa of all time.... confetti machine razzle dazzle... the salsa cilantro! it's soooooooo good so creamy, so perfect with their fish taco, and afterwards enjoying their horchata with fruit and cinnamon on top.... HEAVEN! love their quesas, the fish taco, La Condesa you have a fan!

Answer the phone. We try repeatedly on several several occasions to phone in an order. Yes we understand the order will take an hour, we account for that but ANSWER the phone. Good gracious how rude and unprofessional, you don't answer the phone because you don't want the business. I've heard you mumble this when I've been here. Disgrace for my neighborhood taco shop. YOU SHOULD BE ASHAMED. Ridiculous 

Update. 7/7/2107
AGAIN and AGAIN
No one answers the phone. You think a recording will pass for not answering. You give your neighborhood a BAD name because you can't properly staff your restaurant. Oh and today's recording says "Happy 4th of July", 3 days later.

REALLY great salsa bar selection here! I would go here strictly for that reason alone. The food here is great. The drinks are delicious as well. They hand make the cocktails with love and use real fruit. I had the blueberry martini and there were so many fresh blueberries in it I could barely finish it haha! My hubby got the horchada with rum...it tasted like a pina colada! Yum yum. In a rougher part of town, but this is definitely our new go to spot for Mexican food when driving to/from the airport back up to North Scottsdale :)
Amazing! I go here weekly. Love tue cilantro salsa and the steak tacos my fav! The paintings are a great addition to the local culture.
The food is as authentic as it gets. The specialty tacos were amazing. The salsa bar was out of this world. Loved the peanut salsa

The best part of this place is the salsa bar and chips!  There were 15 different salsas to try and you can make a meal out of that!  The beef street tacos were yummy along with the rice.  The horchata was very tasty and unique with the fruit!  Go early because there was a line out the door, but it is worth the wait.

Thank you yelpers! I was searching for mexican late at night and was really craving something authentic. I struck gold with La Condesa.  It is a true diamond in the rough part of phoenix.
I ordered the carne asada burrito which is simply meat and beans. Anywhere else that would be boring and plain, but it was seasoned perfectly and full of flavor. A perfect vessel for the salsa bar from heaven. Every bite was different depending on what spicy concoction I chose.
I also couldn't resist trying the maya conchita pibil taco, which was packed full of juicy shredded pork. So juicy in fact that I had to eat it quick because the corn tortillas were getting a bit soggy. Did I mind? Oh no. I just sopped up any juice left and sighed with pure contentment. They topped the taco with nothing else but pickled red onions that were delicious. Simple done right.  Can't wait to go back and get that horchata!

Chicken Mole tacos are so delicious. Great art, not too busy on Saturday evening, small place... Every good Mexican place has great salsa and beans...and they bring you chips...they are doin it right.

This 4 is more like 4.5 stars and that's only because of the size and the 45 minute wait (which never end up really being 45 minutes.. and as a NYker.. this is not such a big deal.. it's the norm). When we had our food.. we understood why the name.. we reacted with "ay santisima" lol! 

The salsa bar is very creative and gave us mad options like the "peanut chipotle" and more. Now let's talk about these margaritas.. man oh mighty.. best margaritas I've had! and I've had my fair share of em! It's strong enough and they throw in a slice of grapefruit that really gives it a nice zing! The service was great, yes the bar is tiny and they clearly are understaffed but that didn't stop our server from giving us 5 star service! Drinks came quick and so did the food! Now the menu.. it can be a little intimidating and overwhelming with the immense options.. but definitely go for something you haven't had before, you won't regret it! I can't wait to go back!
Expect more than your traditional mom-and-pop Mexican restaurant. fantastic food, i love it! The Salsa Bar is to die for!

Great little place.  Could tell it would be fantastic by the lineup to get in.

Very good tacos and an even better salsa bar. Decor is spot on.

Pricing was very reasonable as well.

Love this place! Great atmosphere, excellent variety of salsas, amazing horchata and the tacos are fabulous! We came from south Gilbert for no other reason than to come here. It's definitely worth the trip!

I was excited to try this restaurant because of the other great reviews that others had written. The restaurant is fairly small, but definitely authentically Mexican. 

When my party and I first sat down, we were given a bowl of fresh tortilla chips, and were encouraged to try a variety of salsas at the salsa bar. The salsas were interesting to taste, and helped make this restaurant unique from others that I have tried.

I ordered the tamarind soda, which was nothing special, and honestly just tasted like normal soda. Although the restaurant is well-known for their tacos, I decided to order the Al Pastor burro (burrito) which contained pork, guacamole, pineapple salsa and lettuce. The burrito tasted flavorful, fresh and delicious. I would definitely come back for another round.
This place had an awesome selection and different from the Mexican food/tacos that I'm used to. I'd say a must try if you're in the area.

If you can get seated next to the salsa bar then SCORE!! Lol.  So many tasty salsa's to choose from! Try them all!! Basically everything is amazing! The veggie tacos are delicious!  I love the peanut salsa and cilantro salsa.  The house margarita is big, fresh squeezed with citrus pieces to nibble on, and its so delicious!  My favorite menu item is the quesa!! The marin and the veggie are loaded with flavor! Oh, and try they guacamole! They put cranberries and jicama in it :)

Delicioso! 

This is a neighborhood hole in the wall that serves some pretty great mole. I am a mole fiend. Love the stuff. Can't get enough. Their's is dark, rich, spicy, and the right amount of sweet. (Also how I like my men, hey-o). 

(Just kidding.) 

Also, who doesn't love a salsa bar? I've never even heard of most of them: pecan salsa? peanut salsa? Um, why are you only giving me 4 lids for the to-go cups? Like I'm not going to try them all ...

Item's tasted include.

Free Chips and Salsa Bar - options including Chipotle, Pico de Gailo, Robano Pibil, Peanut, Jicama, Pecan, Soy, etc.

Baja Sur Shark Taco - Corn Tortilla with Beer Battered Wild Dogfish and lettuce with cilantro mayo

Cabo Shrimp Taco with Beer Battered Wild Tiger Shrimp and cilantro mayo, jicama

Mayan Cochinita Pibil Taco - Roasted Pork Shoulder with Achiote Rojo slow cooked in banana leaves topped with lime marinated onions and salsa habanera mayo

Oaxacan Black Mole Chicken Taco - Spices, Chiles, Nuts, and Chocolate

Realizing that an inordinate portion of our travel west, from the Port Fonda experience at Greendirt Farm outside of Kansas City to The Shed and Salsa Brava, had focused on Mexican food I couldn't help but pass by La Condessa while my mother was in town for tacos and although I know some in Phoenix may claim the space is not "authentic" enough for them (from what I've gathered, according to some locals you need to have questionable evaluations from the Health Department to be legit) I can say without a doubt that although I've not been south of the border, these are the best tacos I've ever tasted.

Beginning first with another free chips-and-salsa-bar stocked with a baker's dozen of house-made salsas and sauces paired with slightly salted, almost greaseless, and pleasantly warm tortilla chips and moving on to the four tacos featuring local produce and fresh proteins on (unfortunately not house made) imported flour tortillas I particularly enjoyed the crunchy texture and delicate flavors of the shrimp taco while the bright acidity of the pork shoulder and smoky spice of the chicken taco both worked nicely as well.  

Perhaps not as regional as some taco stands (or trucks) and instead choosing to focus on the depth and breadth of Mexican cuisine from coast to coast I'm sure the is "better" or "more authentic" cuisine to be found both here and over the border, but thus far I've not experienced it (outside of the vastly more upscale, expensive, and certainly less authentic Distrito.)

Best salsa bar in Phoenix
Amazing tacos
Always a wait in the evenings and you can't even order drinks at the bar while you wait which kind of sucks.

Best authentic Mexican food in Phoenix that I have ever had! They have an amazing salsa bar with flavors I never could have thought to be salsas. I have the mahi burro and it was awesome. Everything made from scratch down to the tortillas. It's in a kind of "rough" location, but don't let that stop you from this place!

Incredible!  Stupendous!  Filling!  And then there's the Margaritas.  

My friend, Kenner Bob, from up Iowa way, was in town for her annual visit to Aridzona and it's my most excellent pleasure to choose the joint for us to brunch and have a smart cocktail, or two ("Let's all have a little drinkey!").

I'd spotted La Santisima via Yelp about three months ago and knew immediately I wanted to try it. I'm so glad I waited for Kenner Bob's visit as it turned out to be the perfect place.

We started our culinary journey with the joint's Guacamole. Admittedly, I'm not one for bastardized guac, but this guac was da bomb. Chunky with diced mango, dried cranberries and the usual salt, pepper and garlic. Every bite equated nuclear yummy noises from both of us. 

Kenner Bob chose two tacos (all street sized) from the Mix-n-Match menu:  Mahi-Mahi,  Chicken Tinga (I think) and one from the Specialty section:  a beef brisket number that was sublime. 

I chose the Tiger Shrimp, Chicken Tinga and a Pork taco that escapes my memory.  I loved the Pork number. 

Sides for both of us were the included rice and beans. The rice was buttery and tasted like cream was involved in its making. Scrumdiddleyumptious, it was. I'm a rice fanatic so I could've eaten 20 or six tubfulls.

Trust me when I say it would take at least 20 visits to this joint to work one's way through the menu. Kenner Bob and I took 20 minutes -- whist eating the chips, salsa and guac -- to decide on what to order.  Everything -- and I mean EVERYthing -- sounded delicious.  We could've read every choice's description but we finally had to "shoot the engineer" and place our order.  The waitrons are incredibly patient and understanding of dyed-in-the-wool foodies trying to decide which goodies to order. 

The added drawing ticket to this joint are the Margaritas. There are about 10 choices.  Kenner Bob ordered the Award Winning Margarita and after one sip she said, "I'd vote for it!"  For Kenner Bob it was the perfect Marg:  sour but not overly so; sweet but not treacly.  

My Marg was incredible. To save my life I can't remember the name of it but it contained an herbal liqueur.  Truly, if this danged ol' cocktail doesn't cure you then you weren't sick. 

If you're seeking true Mexican cuisine in a super casual restaurant -- and killer-diller Margaritas -- corer  rápidiamente to La Santisima.

This place just keeps getting better and better. They have updated their menu which now includes red and green chili. I tried the red chili and it was amazing and truly unique. Also, great margaritas! Still one of my favorite places!

Not what i expected. I got a quesadilla and there was a puddle of grease on the plate. Not just a little grease, it was tons of it. I took a bite and it dripped down the side of my lip. Could only take 2 bites. I showed the waiter and he just shrugged his shoulders and apologized. I know he didnt cook it, but he didnt offer to remake it or worst case scenario take it off the bill. 2 street tacos and 2 bites of a quesadilla, that looked nothing like advertised for $21. Never again, lesson learned.

went here because I was excited at their vegan reviews of how great their tacos were. When I got here I had no idea how popular this place actually was. There was a 30 minute waiting period, but I expected long wait since we came at 6pm. We wanted to try out their guacamole, but they were already sold out? that kinda saddened me lol.. especially since they ran out of the best salsa in the first 20 mins of us sitting down (least spicy and most flavor). I tried many other ones but none compared. They never bothered to fill it back up either which I didnt understand, but maybe since it was later at night they thought that would be pointless. they were also very busy the whole staff is always running around catering to everyone which I actually loved. The people who work there, work their asses off. I could tell. Plus none of them were rude at all, which is always a great thing because most restaurants dont treat everyone the same. The food was great I cant complain too much. Definitely recommend this for meat eaters though. It caters to vegans with a large selection of options unlike most restaurants, but not the healthiest if you are a real vegan. Corn tortillas aren't exactly healthy, and I have had better fried cauliflower. If you came here with family that wasn't vegan Id say you are safe here for everyone!

In Phoenix there is nobody more important than the person who takes care of your A/C.  Mechanical M D deserves more than 5 stars.  He is available when he needs to be, gets things done quickly and will actually repair things rather than just take the easy route and replace them.  He tries to protect your wallet and that is unusual.  I didn't even think to mention "trustworthy".  That is getting harder to come by these days.  Next time you have A/C problems just call Mechanical M D and don't worry.

On an extremely hot June day,  I was in the mood for Horchata and had read about La Condesa's with the Fruit and nut pieces.   I enjoyed my drink sitting at the empty Bar area while I waited for my To Go.   Its worth just going for the Horchata.   I ordered One Baja Sur Dogfish Shark Taco as my Appetizer which was lightly battered and fried perfecty in obviously clean oil.    My Entree was the Oaxacan Black Mole Chicken Quesa.  The 2 Quesas were crispy, pastry like and filled with Mole Chicken.  Oaxaca cheese was sprinkled on top and was a nice compliment .   Although, The Mole was just a tad bit too sweet, for me, I am looking forward to trying the other Quesas on the menu.   I was not familiar with "Quesa's" prior to my visit.

Yes! Finally made it here and it was DELICIOUS! Queso fundido, tacos (carne asada, mole Oaxaca con pollo, y de puerco) chips y salsa bar, & tloloc burro (nopales, black beans, veggie) was all exceptional! The mango margarita .. perfect! For sure, were returning!

These are not your buddy's street tacos.
La Condesa hits the nail on the head when it comes to flavor. Cochinita Pibil that tastes like Cochinita Pibil... though I would be fine with a little more achiote.
The tinga is great, with citrusy notes on top of slow cooked beef full of chorizo and onion flavor--don't worry, the onion sweetens it up.

My personal favorite is the baja shrimp taco. Big juicy pieces of breaded shrimp stuffed into two corn tortillas with cabbage and mayo on top.

My only point of contention; they should warn people that more than two tacos is actually quite a lot of food. It would help get over the sticker shock. Beans and rice are unnecessary.

A suggestion: Provide people with suggestions for salsa/taco pairings and make everyone drink the fruity horchata, it's awesome.

So my sister and I decided to try this place out, due to YELP reviews, and man are we happy we did. It was sooo good. 

Loved the salsa bar (the pecan, surprisingly, was my favorite) and we both got different versions of their quesadillas. She got the pork pastor and I got the chicken mole. Both were outstanding and different than anything else we've had. 

They hand make their own corn tortillas, fill them with cheese and your filling of choice, and then deep fry them. This gave them a crisp outer shell but a light and almost creamy masa interior. So good!  

FYI - the neighborhood seemed a little questionable (lots of bars on the Windows) but we went during the day and felt perfectly safe. The place was bumping with other happy diners and we'll definitely be back.

HOLD THE TACO! This place is legit! The restaurant is small, and cramped, but I get it... the food was carefully made with a genuine love of feeding people and they want to feed as many as they can in their small space. 

The tacos were legit, the fish tacos were amazeballs, and the veggie options were ridiculous. I had a shrimp taco, and a veggie taco, both were outstanding. The fresh salsa bar was ridiculous too, in a good way :)

Go here, eat tacos, thank me later.

Note, lots of pescie and veggie options! #veggie4life #veggielife #pescielife
Unique, great Mexican food. Certainly not your typical, heavy tacos. The smoked marlin taco is amaz.

Well this place is stinkin delicious.  The service is a bit slow, and the restaurant is not that big, so expect a crowd- but the fresh food definitely makes up for anything the former was lacking.  We enjoyed the specialty burrito with steak, and it was mouth wateringly good!  The salsa bar is a nice touch, and everything tastes really fresh and well made.  I'll be sure to stop again when I'm in the area!
Absolutely first rate, best Mexican (Oaxacan) food in town. Best I have ever tasted! Incredible flavor profiles. This is not your typical Mexican fair, it is bistro chef quality. Highly recommended!

Suggest getting street tacos
Chicken mole
Shark and whitefish Baja style
Pork pibil

Chips and chiles sauces incredible!! 

Partners had the gaucho:: awesome

The mole ........ Food of the Aztecs gods... Yummy
This place is great... Thanks yelp for this place in town for a convention. Needed to find a lace with margaritas and tacos. Both exceeded expectations. Best place in phx that I have tried so far.
Best tacos in Phoenix, hands-down.  They have a great salsa bar, and delicious mole.  A great place to bring visitors from out of town.

Aargh - the two reasons I come are the two reasons I can't give this place what could be it's due worth.  I came specifically to try their salsas and their horchata.  Unfortunately I never really got to try either b/c they had run out pretty much out of all of it.  Probably a good sign that they are busy and popular but at the same time, a big disappointment.  I tried their two taco plate.  The cochinita pibil and veggie tacos.  Both were ok.  The beans were ok but not nearly as good as America's homemade beans.  The rice was like everyone said - not your typical mexican rice.  Not bad though.  Apparently they were so busy they could barely keep up with "supply".  The salsa bar was pretty dismal.  They had just a little of the cilantro and peanut one.  Horchata was all out.   I'm disappointed that I missed out but at least it's a good sign that they are the place to go.  Will definitely be back to hopefully try again.

TIP: If you are coming at night, be very careful.  It was really dark and there weren't any real lighted signs.  I could barely see it so it's easy to pass it.

The horchata is amazing! The food is good. The salsa bar is fun. The service is iffy. The prices are starting to drive me nuts. I've been coming here since just after it first opened as "La Condesa," because it's down the street from my house and I could walk. It was good, unpretentious,  and reasonably priced. They have changed their menu at least 4 times since they first opened. I appreciate the added variety, but not the price jumps. One taco used to fill me up and I could get it for under three bucks. Now I have no idea what they charge, so I only go when I'm fine with spending 8 bucks on a cheese quesadilla (which I will say is very delicious but not really worth $8 all by itself). Anyhow, try it, because the food is good, and leave other expectations at the door.

La Condesa not only has two of my favorite tacos The Baja Sur Shark Taco, and The Oaxaca Black Mole Chicken Taco but the hole in the wall feeling you can't get a chain place. 

The seating is community style with large tables and smaller ones. It's a little tight space wise but it works for the style of the restaurant. Prices are reasonable, food quality is great, and they have one of the best if not the best salsa bars I've ever experienced. There's also a full bar for those that drink.

This place is awesome and I love that I can support local business while getting my grub on!

I had an extremely hard time deciding whether to rate this restaurant three or four stars. It is a solid 3.5 stars, but I decided to raise it due to the free salsa bar and authentic food.

The restaurant is a small location with an all-you can eat salsa bar with various flavours such as cilantro salsa, peanut salsa, tomatillo salsa, and strawberry salsa just to name a few from the selection. The meal also came with a free bowl of tortilla chips, but extra bowls cost more. The tortilla chips were a little thin for me, but definitely tasted authentic.

I ordered the taco plate with two different tacos. When ordering it was a bit difficult to understand what the waiter was saying, but contrary to the menu, he said that you can have two different tacos on the menu instead of one type on the taco plate for $8.99. In the end I paid more than the $8.99 for my taco plate in the end.

I got to taste three different tacos and a part of a burrito after sharing with some other people eating with me. My wild white fish taco was extremely crunchy, but disappointing due to the fish ultimately being too big for the corn wraps. The traditional Mexican taco was very spicy, and the meat was fairly flavourful. The best taco was the pork shoulder taco which was moist and tasted great. I also tried all of the tacos with the spicy guacamole provided at the salsa bar for an added kick. The pork burrito used a flour tortilla and was relatively bland aside from the pineapple salsa which was a refreshing sweet flavour.

Overall it was a nice portion, but was a little expensive. The food is definitely authentic and provided a delicious taco.

Great place!
Reasonable price with delicious food and friendly service.
The cafe were cute and sweet, and the shop inside was beautiful and interesting.

I think most people have a "go to" restaurant & for us it's this amazing place for Mexican food.  We've been around the Phoenix area for many years.  It's wonderful to see a new business succeed right from the start.  That's this place !  Wonderful menu!  Excellent service!  Nice atmosphere!  If you're in the east valley or really anywhere in the valley, give it a try!  You won't be disappointed!

Great place, great Flavours - 7 chili, cilantro and strawberry salsa are must try.  In my first visit, I tried chicken tinga and a burro, the meat was well cooked and juicy. 

Place was small, but nice ambience. 

The neighborhood was litle shady but  the quality of food defeats all those negative factors. 

Definitely recommended.

Ps - the place is open late till 11pm, even though yelp hours shows 9pm.

La Condesa, I give up on you. We try and try to excuse the terrible service, but no more. It's not worth it. It's too slow and inattentive and they just don't give a damn, so I'll take my $33 elsewhere.

This time we were disappointed by the food, too. We returned our horchata for being too thin and tasteless, and you brought us new ones after we finished eating. You drizzled a pretty crema all over the top of my torta (sorry, lonche). How do I pick it up and eat it? 

In the past we forgave the dirty tables and loudness because your cochinita pibil was pure bliss. But not even that makes up for the service. :(

Meh. The best part of my order was the rice. I had a taco combo plate with 3 tacos. The taco shells were way too crispy and dripping with grease. I could hardly bite them. Not really impressed with the flavors of the different meats I chose. For what I ordered, over-priced and the flavor was underwhelming.

I really like La Condesa.  What stands out is the variety of fresh salsas on their salsa bar, and the great variety of tacos to choose from. I've had the shrimp, and a couple of different versions of their steak tacos.  I've also had the mole chicken, which was great as well.

Service can be a little sketchy here, mostly because they're often very busy.  But if you're in the area, it's a great place to try.

We drove down from Prescott, for the day, to do a little shopping and found this place via Yelp. 

SO glad we decided to drive the extra 20 minutes to get there (despite being surrounded by restaurants at the mall). 

This place is good for vegans, vegetarians, and meat eaters alike.  I chose the Ghandi and the veggie tacos (cactus), while my friend had meaty street tacos. The food was fresh & delicious and the portion size was perfect.  

Loved the salsa bar!!  Other reviewers mentioned the dried cranberries in the guacamole. It was a delicious sweet addition and the guac was perfect!

We will definitely return for a meal next time we're in Phoenix hungry for Mexican food.
Delicious! The quesadillas are a must have. Loved the salsas, had many to pick from. Highly recommend this yummy place.

Poor service, took over an hour to get burritos, freezing air conditioning blowing right on us, sound system not working just crackling loudly the whole time. They charge 5$ more just to get sour cream and enchilada sauce on burrito.
Unique atmosphere complimented by wide variety of free salsa. Reasonable prices and pleasant service. Food is great!

I went multiple times during my time in Phoenix and luckily did not have to wait too long each time. The streets tacos are hearty and well seasoned. The best part are all the salsa options you get to choose from and the included chips that come with your order. It is really fun trying all the salsas and they go great with the food. The margaritas are also pretty delicious based on the sips I had from others. The horchata is pretty unique with the added fruit and is not as creamy as other preparations but is still refreshing!

A nice spot for lunch or dinner!

I bought a groupon here last year and finally got around to trying the place. My son and I are pretty picky eaters, so we kind of created our own. I ordered a chicken and bean burrito enchilada style, with rice and beans on the side. I don't know what the heck was in that burrito, but pretty sure the meat was not chicken. I had a stomach ache before even walking out....I honestly should have asked for a different item. I don't know what was wrong with the meat. The portion itself was huge. Very large plate. The salsa bar I liked, lots of different options, Inside was cute. Warning though, parking is a hot mess, its literally on 16th st. Good luck getting out of there during traffic. Waiter was nice, but slow. Over all I was disappointed. I will say, the beer battered fish taco sounded good. May go back to try that, but other than that based on what I ate, we wont be returning.

Came in at around 4PM on a Saturday, parking was terrible but we assumed it had to be good since the parking lot was packed. Walked in and the whole front room was packed with patrons so we waited patiently to be seated. The artwork was phenomenal and the full bar was inviting, but after five minutes of not being acknowledged in any way, we were starting to lose patience. Finally we were seated in the back room, which is much larger and at the time nearly empty except for two groups of 5 people.

We both ordered three tacos each, which were way pricier than we were expecting, they range between 3.99 and 5.50 each or you can do a mix and match plate. Many of their options are seafood so that limited us a bit since we aren't fans, though if you like seafood maybe you'll have better luck than we did!

The salsa bar is extensive so we were excited, we loaded up 12 mini condiment cups, filling them with everything from clearly pico to some more mysterious salsas. Tried out a few on the chips as we waited for our food and found that none of them were spicy in any way, the best was the Pico and another similar to it. 

Finally our tacos arrived and we dug in. Well we tried to. Instead we each ate about half of each taco (except for the barbiccoa which both of us got, I ate both of them after he discovered he hated it). Each taco ranged from bad to almost inedible. Each taco was miniscule, barely the size of my hand and barely filled except for the lack luster and down right gross tasting garnish. The meat quality on the other habd was great, tasteless but great quality so there was room for it to be delicious, they just failed that goal. In the end the only tacos I could suggest were the barbiccoa, which I found good enough to even crave again but for the price and how lacking everything else was, I can guarantee we will not be returning.

I would suggest this place to anyone with family or friends who like a great setting and casual drinks with some small bites, especially if they're not generally fans of Mexican food. The place is inviting and interesting with plenty of tasteless options to explore.

If you're a fan of big fancy, red carpet joints, this is not the place for you. The service is not good, it is understaffed, the restaurant itself is small and there are a boat load of people there. If you like eating some kick ass Mexican food though, this place tops the list. I had the pork and bean burrito with a side of their chipotle salsa. The meat was so tender and the flavor was so developed, I wept a little with each bite. This is on my radar for the next time I come out to Phoenix.  Just hope they find a bigger location or open a taco truck.

I've been coming here for years for the food. It's awesome. The service might be the worst of any restaurant I've ever been to though. Saturday night, 8pm. The restaurant is 40% full with 15 people standing by the bar waiting for a table for 20 minutes. Their famous salsa bar is half empty and has been for 30 minutes. Not one person working there is hustling. I ask who the manager is. Oh, they're at the other store. No owner or manager on on your busiest night at dinner rush? Whoever runs the show here is leaving a lot of money on the table and regularly disappointing your patrons.

On my way home from the baseball game I decided to stop in here and see what all the excitement was about.  I drove past it and then turned around and got a parking spot right by the door.

I ordered the dogfish shark taco and the cochinita pibil taco combo with rice and beans.  I received some chips as I left the order counter and stopped at the salsa bar to get some pico de gallo.  When I got to my table I scooped some pico onto my tortilla chip and wow, what great fresh taste!

I also had some tomatillo, jicama and chipotle salsas that I tried on my tacos.  The shark taco was good and the cochinita pibil was even better.  Even the small cups of rice and beans where really good.

I grabbed a menu on my way out and am already trying to plan what I'll have on my next visit.  I especially can't wait to try the horchata.
This place was such a pleasant surprise. The food was absolutely delicious, the salsa bar was great, and the grapefruit margarita was super refreshing. Will certainly be back!

Went here for happy hour after work (5:00pm) on a Friday night and my party (of 2) was able to be seated right away.  I really liked some of the artwork hanging in the restaurant.  We ordered several types of tacos and loved them all.  Even more impressive was the well stocked salsa bar ranging from cheese causes and mild salsas to some that really make your mouth burn.  I had a great time here and will definitely go back.

I've been here a few times. Its small and always crowded when I come. Food takes longer than usual to come out but it's worth the wait. They have an awesome salsa bar but if you get there at the end of the night you might find it empty, which is disappointing. Don't come here if you're expecting street taco prices because they are far from that. Carne asada tacos are good but not worth it for me.

Anyways I go here for their AWESOME fish and shrimp tacos. They are pretty big and are delicious. Their food stays pretty consistent in taste. One of my favorites in town that I have found so far (my quest for good tacos never ends).

The bakery sells traditional Mexican pastries which are excellent. The baked goods in the window are self-serve, to be placed on a tray, while the ones on the counter are not. There are a few tables in the front; I didn't see the back area. They sell a variety of coffee and tea. I suggest the guava pastries and the concha. I'll return to try other sweets.

I've been here about 4 times now. I love this place. The name has changed, they've been serving alcohol for a while now, there's a new location in Glendale (I need to go), and the menu has expanded but isn't quite represented online yet. Even the physical menus can be different. The one I had had a few more items on it than my friends'. The horchata is still the best I've ever had. The margaritas are so freaking good.

I tried the marlin taco that wasn't there last time I visited. I love trying things I've never had before. Marlin is an odd fish. Their preparation makes it look and taste almost like pork. It's just... different. Still good though!

My friend got the veggie burro. She said it was pretty tasty, but a little on the bland side. We agreed that it can be hard to make vegetarian food flavorful at times. She liked the salsa bar because she could add a different flavor between bites.

They get slammed on weekends. I was here at 7pm on a Friday. They need more than 2 people serving and clearing on weekends. When every table is packed there's almost no room to move. Getting to the salsa bar can be pretty awkward.

Fond memories here at La Santisima. Every single time I come here for their La Santisima veggie taco plate, it feels like a great life decision. These tacos are heavenly with fresh sautéed mushrooms, spinach, zucchini and onions with melted cheese. Then there is the salsa bar with around a dozen house made salsas. They best is the Mexican salsa and the pecan salsa crema. Oh and can't forget about their massive horchata drink they serve with chopped nuts and fruit on top. For those who partake, they have a bar with several tequilas, and probably other things. Small place, but cozy and intimate. Good spot for a casual date night where you can be a cool Phoenician that knows of the perfect spot for dinner. Parking is on 16th street, kind of a weird diagonal situation where you hope you don't get side swiped by traffic... But hey. Totally worth it if you do. These tacos. Yum.

Dear Arizona,

Over 1.5 years ago, I visited your state and ate at a Mexican restaurant that I neither remember the name nor want to. It was awful. And I reviewed that restaurant and commented that a place so highly reviewed in Arizona must have meant people in Arizona don't get food. I was wrong. So wrong. And for that, I apologize. After visiting la Santisima (a different restaurant than the above mentioned disaster), I realized you guys have got the Mexican food down to a T.

Your Midwestern friend,
-Deena

Okay now for the review:
We were in town for a wedding and we had a lot of time between the wedding and our arrival so we looked up some good places to eat. Thank GOD for yelp because it helped us find this holy landmark of Mexican food. 

Atmosphere: 3.5/5. Small restaurant. You will definitely wait so get there early. Nice paintings around. Modern American music playing which is fine by me. You don't need to play mariachi music for the place to be authentic. If your food is this good, I don't care if you play Beyoncé or sounds of the Amazon. 

Food: fresh corn tortillas. Fresh chips. Guacamole with chunks of avocado so ripe it melts in your mouth. Salsa with fresh peppers. Mole so good it could only be holy. Fish and shrimp tacos as well as "shark" tacos that melt like butter !! Horchata with fresh fruit and cinnamon and nuts. Oh my gosh. Never ending food ecstasy here. I wish I had an extra stomach so I could have ordered more food to try before I left this place. 

Service: they are a limited number of servers but they bust their humps walking around serving , taking orders , etc. Five stars to them! 

Miscellaneous: limited parking out front. They take all credit cards except American Express. 

PROS: great food and memorable flavors
CONS: can't think of any

I went with a friend over here after work one night on a recommendation. I loved my food it was much bigger than I thought and more gourmet to. I was expecting a little cheese crisp filled with meat, but it was so much more than that. I had a margarita that was really good but I think it was grapefruit all it says on the menu is margarita's but no description of any of them.

The place was very tiny and cramped, but it was colorful in a good way and was not super busy. The service was a little slow and it was our first time so it took a while before they told us you get your sauce's from the little bar.

I will be back in the future, overall it was a good price and taste food.

I ordered a burrito and 2 tacos w/ rice/beans. I was charged $20.85 for what I thought was a rip off. Looking at the chicken it appears like it's been sitting at room temperature all day. It's black, dry and old looking. They must think people are stupid and won't know the difference. It's harsh to say, but I could not finish a meal I purchased due to disgust.
Hole in way gem,not to be missed. Great tacos ..good serving size..salsa bar is great..margaritas with real alcohol. Super value for money

Only reason i cant give them 0 stars b/c its not an option.Never stopping here ever again....stopped on a Sat 1/21/17 asked for table of 8, I get it its a small place and tables are scarce but was told 20min wait....waited 1.5hrs for nothing. Multiple parties of 4 went ahead of us. When I asked why the wait was taking so long and having multiple 4 people parties go ahead when  their tables could have been combined to accommodate us, the waitress gave me attitude and back peddled b/c she couldn't come up with a reason why others were being seated before us. If they weren't going to accommodate us just communicate and we could have gone elsewhere without wasting 1.5hrs of time. Can't rate the food b/c we were never given any service.

La Condessa is muy Bueno in many ways. The tacos are always fresh, from shark to carne asada you really can't go wrong. (Although I heard it is bad karma to eat shark).

They carry Mexican beers that I have never heard of before, last time I had an Estrella and it was delicious. They have a full bar with tons of exotic tequilas and they are generous on the pours.

The servers are attentive and sweet and the set up is old style cool. 

What really keeps me coming back is the salsa bar (oh the salsa bar)! Pecan salsa, 7 pepper, chipotle, sesame... They carry over a dozen and you will have to come many times to experience the perfect salsa/taco combination. It is worth every delectable trip!

my friends convinced me to give this place another chance. 

the salsa bar is SO good. I don't really recall what I ordered to eat but i do remember not loving it. it was decent though. 

the salsa on the other hand is amazing! salsa all day long!

The La Santisima Specialty Taco was delicious. Best ever.

The Salsa Bar is amazing. 

I'm going to bring my friends back here.

The owner called me by name, that felt good. This was my first visit.
Awesome selection of tacos and great salsa's... the restaurant itself it very tiny though! When its busy good luck finding a seat. You can always carry out.

Absolutely phenomenal. I can't say enough about this GOURMET taco restaurant. Granted, this menu has more than tacos but you need to look no further than those filthy goooooood tacos. I have came here a few time with several different groups, not once did the sitting render tasteless. I've ordered almost every taco and each is extraordinary within itself. I am a Carne Asada enthusiast! With that said this dandy delight of a taco magician has various types of steak cooked various ways, all producing the bountiful bliss of juicy satisfaction. The salsa bar is a blessing in itself, so many varieties you don't run across at any other taco restaurant. The reviews speak for them self... Get here!
Everything was really good. We loved the salsa bar with all the interesting choices.  Carne asada tacos were great. Can't wait to come back and try the fish tacos.

Are you tired of, or bored with, the typical Sonoran fare that surrounds us on nearly every corner in the valley?  If so, then you need to put one of the two locations of La Santisima on your list. The only things that you would recognize are the usage of the words: tortilla, taco, quesadilla, and burro. It's that unique. 

I've eaten more times than I can count at 16th St, and several times in Glendale. Here's what you need to know between the two. The original 16th St is small, almost cramped. Parking is literally ON the street edge, and around the corner. It can be dangerous backing out of your spot into the northbound flow of 16th St. You will often find a wait to be seated, and there is no indoor waiting area, just a bench outside, and seating for perhaps six at the (full liquor) bar. You will more than likely be privy to your your neighboring diners' conversations, as well as bumping into them at the salsa bar. It's got wonderful ambience, certainly, but it's not for large-parties, or those having issues with claustrophobia, or anxiety that might be sparked due to tight quarters. Those using wheelchairs or scooters should go directly to Glendale. There is ample parking in the rear, and at neighboring venues. The dining room is at least twice, or thrice, that of 16th st, and there is patio seating along Glendale, outside. I've not ever had to wait there, due to the extra seating available. 

The salsa bar gets much praise from other reviewers, and I'll get that out of the way first. Yes, there are a dozen, or perhaps 14 choices there. However, batches are kept small for freshness, and they may not have a couple of your faves once you've discovered them. However, there will certainly be ample remaining choices to top your light, airy, housemade(?) chips. Your first basket is gratis, but they do charge for extras (sometimes, LOL). It's very, VERY easy to ruin your appetite with these, due to the wonderful tastes and combos that you simply have not likely seen elsewhere. Chopped jicama, lightly salted w/cilantro? A roasted combo of several different peppers, and onions? Watermelon salsa? Peanut mole? You get the idea....

The menu lays out their special recipe combos pretty well. You can certainly get a standard type street taco plate, with or w/o rice and beans, with several of their takes on the standards, such as carne asada, al pastor, etc. The rice is simple, yet not your standard rosa-colored 'Spanish' rice. It even appealed to a former Asian g/f, who ate plain white rice as a staple. Beans are on the creamy side, more 'refried' than charro style....again quite tasty for their type. However, I almost always succumb to one of their bowls. All can be ordered as burro wrapped in a large tortilla, but I always get a bowl. Afterall, I know I will be semi-full from those chips! I've had the House Special bowl more times than I can remember, and it does not disappoint. But, I've explored out of my comfort zone a time or two, without disappointment. 
Quesadillas come in a large fresh corn tortilla, unlike anything I've ever seen at another restaurant. That adds a unique texture and flavor to their already delicious fillings. However, if you think you would be put-off by it somehow, be sure you specify that you wish to have a traditional flour tortilla.

I have to make a special plug for their guacamole. Like other recipes, this one is unique, and  darned yummy. They add cranberry, jicama, and I believe mango to your standard avocado blending. It's creamy green nirvana. Well worth that second basket of chips, for sure. Don't plan on sharing a small serving with any more than one other diner. Otherwise, violence could very well break out at your table. 

Well then, it's time for dessert. This is perhaps the only reason I am hesitant to provide them with 5-stars. Frustration! Their take on a leche flan is quite different than what you're used to (that's the theme here, right?). Picture more of a tres-leches sponge-cake, because that's what it is (in my book), and what it should be called (to my thinking, LOL). Suffice to say, in the many times I've eaten here, it's been sold-OUT all but ONE TIME!!!!  I even ask for it BEFORE I ORDER MY MEAL, just in the hopes of reserving one for myself at the end. No such luck, LOL. 

Alright, it's time to go eat!
The burro was fabulous. Hard to describe how wonderful the food is. The horchata was the best we ever had.
Good food but service is lacking.  Self service, sort of.  No trash cans, no easy refills.  Food is well worth the experience, though.

The mole tacos were disappointing after all the wonderful reviews of them. They were very sweet. Don't get the rice or beans. The teaspoonful they give you spreads out from being watered down. The salsas are good. The waitress seems like she must be the entitled child of the owner. Also, I think I'd also rather eat off of a paper plate than the questionably leaded & chipped Mexican plates. 

Guy Fiery must have been drunk or hungover. Also they surely knew he was arriving so the place must've been cleaned that day. I have seen cleaner food trucks than this.

i reallllly need to come here more often. this is definitely a little gem of a mexican restaurant that fires on all cylinders. 

the restaurant itself is adorable-i love all the awesome dia de los muertos paintings on the walls and the unique decor. while it isn't in the greatest neighborhood, you'd have no idea once you walked inside.  

the salsa bar! oh my god, i don't even know where to start with how amazing this thing is.  i am a huge salsa fan (wouldn't mind eating it with every meal, or as a meal, whatever) and i've never known of a restaurant to have so many options! i could literally come here and only eat chips and salsa for hours and never get bored because of all the choices! 

horchata! they put an interesting spin on the horchata by adding pecans and fresh fruit to it.  i thought this might be weird since i've never had it that way, but it was totally delicious and refreshing.  

food! the menu is packed with delicious items that have some unbelievable flavors.  i recommend the carne asada burrito or the bullet (bean and cheese).  

i'll be coming back soon!
The wide variety of tacos here are the perfect vehicle for the inventive salsas! Would recommend to people who like eating at good restaurants.

The food here is absolutely amazing! Our group had tacos and a quesa, with every single item being delicious. We had to wait a short time for a table, but even a long wait is so worth it. We loved their salsa bar too.

I'll start by saying that the food here is usually great. The pacific white fish taco is perfect. The salsa bar is just alright. My real complaint here is the service. Every time I walk in the servers all just ignore me until I actually say something like "uh hi I'm here to eat food" it's very awkward and makes you feel unwelcome. I'm an industry person and I really can't imagine letting a table sit for that long without at least checking on them. Bad vibes.

as tony would say....'Grrrrreeeeeat' little taco shop 
just a little north of McDowell on 16th st, drive slow or else you'll miss it 
the shark taco were awesome, perfect crisp 
i did tried the carne asada meat, which could of used a little more favors 
the salas bar was pretty cool, lots of chooses 
the best part about the meal was the horchata....Mmmmmm 
my mouth waters just thinking about it 
it's about $4 or $5 for a 32oz horchata....better share it with someone 
they put fruits and peacan.....yummmm 
i would drive there just for the shark tacos and horchata

Awesome taco and salsa choices, but no big crowds.

For a foodie, it's great there are no long lines and waits for seating, but peoples, YOU'RE MISSIN' OUT! In Saturday for lunch, had a seat at the empty bar. Tables mostly full, but not jammed with folks. Good for me though, service was quick, and room to kick back.

Ordered Azteca Tinga and Oaxaca Black Mole Chicken tacos, but oddly, was served Mayan Cochinita Pibil Taco instead of the Azteca. I double-checked with the server 'cuz the Cochinita was absolutely mouth-watering! Over-the-top when paired with the Cilantro salsa (just a touch). A definite repeat item. Black Mole was certainly delivered as described, with dark, somewhat smokey-molasses flavor, but a bit too heavy for me.

Ti[p: Pick just two-to-three salsa to sample, and then decide on how best to enjoy them-some just with chips, others to top off a taco. How to be sure what's best? Duh, come back again!

I could have only eaten chips and all the salsas from the salsa bar and I would have been a happy camper. I wish I could have packed the salsa bar home with me, but unfortunately, it doesn't work like that. (TSA has a limit in liquid ratios). 

I tried almost every salsa from the bar and I have to say, the best one is actually a combination. Mix the guacamole and peanut salsas together, and you instantly have salsa crack. I could have eaten tubs of the mixture and still wouldn't be sick if it. The heat of the guacamole salsa balances quite well with the umami of the peanut salsa.

Street tacos were good too but my mind was on the richness of the salsas. They should just change their name to Salsa Heaven. 

Other than the salsas, please note the service was subpar and the prices on the menus and what they actually bill you is inconsistent, but only by a few cents so no point in arguing.
Looking for a great variety and exceptionally fresh Mexican food, this is the place. Also has an excellent array of vegan and vegetarian options.

This is a great little hole-in-the-wall mexican joint. Overall I'd say while service can be a bit iffy, the food is great and reasonably priced.

Chips and salsa is one of my fave foods, and it's complimentary here. The self-serve salsa bar in the back is extensive, with about 8-12 different salsas at a time. I've been here twice and my favorites are their jicama salsa, pico de gallo, and chipotle. I wish the salsa cups were larger, but that's a minor peeve ... and let's face it, I'm not someone who's ashamed to go up to the salsa bar 5 times. (Given the rate at which I inhale chips, I probably need to fit in some excercise laps to the salsa bar anyway.)

On my most recent visit (around 5:30pm on a Thursday) we ordered standard margaritas. I wasn't super impressed with them (and think they were just made from a mix), but when I got the bill and saw they were only $3 each, I wasn't too upset. They did have a proper drink menu, so next time I'm here I may try one of their other cocktails.

Just as a menu tip for if you're debating between tacos, the "street tacos" near the bottom of the menu are smaller (~4") than the "gourmet" ones listed at the top (~5").  I've gotten both kinds and prefer the smaller street tacos, but maybe I'm just biased toward miniature foods. The first time I visited I also ordered rice and beans, which were better than I've had at most places, though I'm not a huge fan of rice & beans in general.

I love mole and they have mole tacos and other mole dishes which I would LOVE to try, but alas thanks to my nut allergy I can't ... I'll have to live vicariously through my fellow Yelpers' reviews & photos on that one!

Had really fantastic tacos at lunch today. The Cochinita Pibil was note perfect, and the Marlin brought me back to Mazatlan. Salsa bar is tremendous as well, my favorites were the strawberry, the pecan, and the chipotle. Get there early for Lunch!

It's simply delicious, especially if you want a meal. The chips and salsa were delicious and varied from peanut to salsa roja. I recommend Sopa Azteca it has a quick and you can taste the flavors of the broth, the Oaxaca cheese and chip strips topped off with avocado slices. The fish tacos are amazing, as they have a real Baja flavor; topped with mayo, beer battered fish! My fiancé ordered the Sonoran carne azada burrito. The horchata was served with pecans and strawberries (you can opt out of strawberries). The portions were great and therefore we didn't order dessert. Yes the wait is long, however they are waiting on the state to approve a new line of cooks(?) But trust me, it's worth the wait.
Fun little restUrant! I like the food. Nice salsa bar!! Try the quesa!!!! I love the arrecha with pabolano peppers!!!!

Amazing salsa bar! There wasn't one that I disliked, although there was a chipotle one that I loved the most. The pastor tacos were the best of the street tacos we tried. Amazing flavor! The carne asada was okay; not great. Would go back for the salsa, pastor, and to try other things.
This place is great.  I really like the food and the atmosphere.  It's a pretty straightforward place that's got a bit of flair tossed in.  So it's a good spot for the foodie and the not so foodie.

Dear Condesa,
I wish you had a few more vegetarian items, and that you didn't get all persnickety and confusing about the whole torta/lonche thing, because that led me into an ordering error. However, bygones. While I didn't love my veggie lonche, it was obviously very fresh and prepared with care. Also, please refill the salsa bar more frequently so that I won't be tempted to get too much of the really spicy ones and burn the he** out of my mouth. And put more tequila in the (non-happy hour) margaritas. Thank you!
Amalia C.
P.S. Your chairs are too heavy.
P.P.S. In reflection, maybe this was more of a 2-star for me personally but my husband really liked his street al pastor and carne asada taco plato and again, it all seemed fresh. So I bumped you up. You're welcome!

LOVE the dogfish shark taco and the chicken mole taco. The salsa bar is awesome. The horchata is delicious. Perfect tacos at a reasonable price. But the restaurant is small, so avoid peak times or get your food to go.

One of the best Mexican spots in town. The food is great (salsa bar!) and so are the margaritas. That said, it is crammed - try to go on a night when it's less busy to avoid feeling the full brunt of that.
The service was a little bit slow but worth the wait after visiting here from the East Coast it was great to get some real authentic Mexican food I had the shark tacos & recommend to everyone
I love it here. It is the place that I take out of town visitors. I love the salsa bar. It is small and often you have to wait but I think that the food makes up for those things.

I am giving this place 4 stars because it is unique. The night we went it was crowded...but we went because of all the hype on Yelp and my quest for Fish Tacos. The service was good. I tried all the salsa's and only liked a few. And as for the tacos...they were ok. The Shark Taco needed a better sauce and I would have enjoyed it much better. Truthfully, I didn't find the shark tacos as great as everyone else does on these reviews, but then again, I am new to Fish Tacos. I also tried the Mayan Cochinita Pibil Taco, I found this flavor strong (unlike other Mexican places I have tried), so that is good, but I didn't really care for it.

The bad, my son ordered the steak Quesa. He didn't care for it at all, I did like this, but then the waitress took the entire thing away when we weren't done with it and Dave didn't even get a chance to try it. So that was a bit disappointing, given he didn't eat hardly any of it. 

Overall...I am glad we went.

Once again, Yelp did not disappoint.  My brother ~ who lived in San Antonio ~ and is addicted to good Mexican Food came to visit.  With the pressure of finding a great place, I turned to Yelp.  Excellent selection!!! So many yummy salsas and the Tacos were quite good.  Not as amazing as Barrio Queen but definitely yummy.  The Margaritas were beyond divine tho ...as was the fried Quesadilla and I am not s fan of rice and beans, but these were exceptional.

Thanks Yelpers!  We were in town Sunday - trying to find something new and close by.  Yelp provided the answer - over 1,300 reviews with a score of 4 1/2 stars ... gotta do it.  SO GLAD WE DID.

5 of us showed up for some Gourmet Taco's.  A bit of a wait - but not bad.  Not a lot of room to sit/wait inside - and it could be a hot wait on the sidewalk out front on a summer day - but - once we were inside and seated...Happiness ensued.

A pretty comprehensive menu - various taco preparations - from a traditional Barbacoa (Mariachi), Chicken Tinga, a Sonoran Arrachera steak, to my choice - the Sonora Carne Asada Burro.  Wonderful!  Very flavorful, tender and moist meat.  My dining companions had a variety of taco's and quesadillas, and everyone was completely satisfied.  Lots of wow's every time someone tried something new.

The salsa bar was great - only complaint - I like to really dip my chips, and the small cups provided just enough room to put the tip in, and just enough for a taste.  They were all very tasty - some much more hot than others.  Loved the sweet/slightly hot fresh mango salsa.  I could eat just a bowl of that and be happy!

Too full for deserts.  Well be back again for sure!  Enjoy!
OMG! The best horchata and the salsa bar was great. The tacos were to die for and I loved the mole taco.

Came here to check out a New Mexican spot and it is definitely my favorite. Everything is fresh and tastes amazingly good!! I tried their shark taco and my brother had their fried quesadillas  Great service too. Can't wait to come back.

Though the food was decent, not amazing, the service was poor enough to not ever be back. I felt bad for the servers, there was 2 of them and they seemed overwhelmed. There was no sign of a manager or even a busser or greeter, so I think they just had way too much on their plate to give good service or even to smile. Like many of the other reviews the best thing about this place is the salsa bar, however most of the "good" salsas were empty and never refilled during our visit.

Some of the best Mexican food I have had in AZ. Only thing I would love for them to do is give bigger bowls for your salsa in case you really want to dunk a chip but I still managed anyway! Amazing drinks! I will be back again and again!

I can't say enough good about this place.  I found it on Yelp as we were on our way home from the airport.  I am vegetarian, and good Mexican vegetarian food is hard to find.  I must say this place is a treasure.  I had the potato/nopalito taco and a black bean taco with mango salsa.  Both of them were the best I have ever had.  I would definitely go here again.  There is an amazing salsa bar with all kinds of delicious salsas.  Definitely a keeper.

The best in PHX. My favorite place to go to get food and eat a dope ass meal is here. Let me start off by saying that I fudging love salsa and this place has a salsa bar... case closed. You might have to wait like 30-45 mins but it's well worth it in the end. Trust me.
Best Mexican food!!!! Love the salsa bar food is always fresh and amazing !! Have had everything on the menu and absolutely love it !!! Everyone in downtown Phoenix must try this place !!
Love the strawberry salsa here.  My only complaint is that they do not take Amex!  4th star is only because they didn't accept my Amex. The salsa bar and taco selection are incredible .

I've been coming to La Santisima for 8 years. The service has always been slow but the food was always hot and spot on.  Recently they switched management and now the food is going downhill. The tacos are smaller, salsa bar is always half full and quality is poor. My go to taco is the Mexi Mignon. It's a grilled piece of filet mignon with a homemade slaw and fried cheese. This taco is out of this world good. However, my last visit they used chopped steak, no slaw, different sauce and fried cheese. This is a $10 taco. I will not be coming back until they bring the quality of their food back. Shame on the owners for cutting corners on what was the best taco place in  AZ.

I wanted to love this place. The chicken mole tacos are killer and the only reason they're getting two stars instead of one.   A confluence of negatives brought what should have been a five-star review down - fast.

1. Our waiter didn't have his heart in it.  He barely smiled, didn't share any pleasantries and was drier than toast.  No offer to refill water, to show us the dessert menu.  Just overall lacking in basic customer service skills.  

2. When was the last time you went to a Mexican restaurant and didn't bring home a doggy bag?   The portions here are for a bride-to-be trying to lose weight before a wedding.  The shape of the rice was a 1/4 measuring cup.  The refried beans were about 2 tablespoons worth.

3. The wait for menus.  The wait to be acknowledged.  The wait for drinks.  The wait for the meal.  The wait for the check.  i wanted to belt out that tacky song: "Cuando, cuando, cuando?!?"

4. The temperature.  Lukewarm food is not cool.  It sat somewhere for some unknown reason.  I'd usually send it back but damn!  I thought I'd eat next week.

5. The outside at night.  What's up with the no lights?  We drove by the first time because we had no idea it was open.  

6. The margaritas are creative but DAMN!  Inordinately expensive.  We are not on the Upper East SIde of Manhattan.

7.  The plates.  I guess they're reminiscent of Mexican pottery but they looked like they could contain lead.  No bueno.  

The salsa bar is killer - they make their own unusual and tasty concoctions (pecan salsa?).  Quite lovely.  

But they really need to step up their game and stop resting on the laurels of Diners, Drive Ins and Dives.
Al Pastor street tacos are where its at!!  Solid margaritas.  Hole in the wall place with a good vibe.
Great food! Reminded me of my time in Oaxaca! Wish they had silverware because the plastic ware made cutting the Quesa tough lol but so small in the grand scheme of a great restaurant!
Great food, me and my boyfriend eat here quite a few times.  Tacos are like street tacos, defiantly worth the drive.
If you have an interest in the best tacos in the state, then stop playing games and come to this place. not fancy, not cheap, but worth the time and money. these guys are the real deal
Just had half of a shrimp burro and half of a mahi mahi burro and it was absolutely fabulous. The cilantro sauce and mushrooms made it! A+ Also - best horchata on the planet!

Vegan: I got the veganized quesadilla based on a few reviews here. They can't add beans inside like somebody mentioned, only on the side (make sure to ask for beans without cheese on top) If you are a "junk vegan" you may be good to go. I personally hardly eat fried things and wanted to make an exception for this. They fry the whole thing so it sits in a layer of oil on the plate and the spinach and mushrooms etc inside are soaked as well - all I tasted was the oil. I have only been vegan for a year so I can imagine this must be really good with the cheese but in vegan you may be better off with a burrito or taco. 
Omni hubby had the tacos and loved them! Salsas are really nice as well, cilantro, pecan and Mexican were really good.
I would go back to try their other stuff!

I read all the great reviews on here and in the 'Phoenix's 23 of the Valleys best new places to chow down' and was excited - both my sister and I love street tacos.
Maybe I missed something, but I have never been more dissappointed in my culinary adventures. The chips were alright...the array of salsas was impressive and all the ones I sampled were quite good. We ordered 5 different tacos a la carte - Cabo Shrimp Taco, Sonoran Carne Asada Taco, Aztec Tinga Taco, Mayan Cochinita Pibil Taco, La Condesa Shrimp taco. 
The Cabo was tasty, but nothing to write home about, the carne asada was tasteless and overdone, the Aztec Tinga was not bad... but very one note and we were over it after the first bite. The Condesa Shrimp taco had  WAAAY too much garlic and the shrimp had zero flavor - I came across at least 10 full slices and I still have the taste of garlic in my mouth hours later. 
Overall it wasn't horrible - it just wasn't good - definately not 25 dollars worth -  this is not a place I would return to nor would I recommend it to anyone else
If you want good street tacos see my reviews.

Really great salsa bar, tacos, quesadillas and burros.  Service is hit or miss depending on how busy they are but are very friendly.
