Just get the food ala carte, the beans and rice portions with a combo are small and aren't that great.  Not a very good selection of beers and the regular margarita is just so so.

Came here with my cousin for some HH.

We in total had 4 margs ($3 on happy hour, can't beat that). And they were actually really good!

We both also had the Al Pastor burro which was good portioned and delicious.

Our server was friendly, however, the petite lady with dark hair when we entered was NOT. Dunno what her problem was. We "may" be back, but hopefully not when she's there. We got such a snotty vibe- and its not a good look. Maybe cause we're cute girls & she's a hater?

When we walked in, no one presented themselves as a hostess so I ask snotty do we seat ourselves? NO response. Ignored. Lol! Ok, so we just sat ourselves. 

I agree with other reviews, that we just sat there with no water, a basket of chips, and no service for like 10-12 minutes with workers wondering around knowing that we were sitting there. We had never been here before, so we didn't know about getting our own salsas until we were sitting for 10 mins and finally were able to ask. Even a "thank you!" on our part to snotty woman was ignored.. Ok lol. Just cause foods good doesn't mean you should lack in service.... And your SERVICE is what I will be telling people about if they ask about your restaurant.

Awesome food, great service! Love the guacamole. The lighting outside the restaurant is not so good, so we passed the place twice. Once inside, everything we ordered was great! Tacos with mole, El Pastor tacos, steak tacos and - did I mention - guacamole! A must do in Phoenix. Go now!

Everything is good. And hands down best salsa bar imaginable. Best, best, best! Small and always crowed though, which I blame mostly on the awesomeness salsa bar.... Did I mention how great the salsa bar here is?
The street tacos were delicious and we had fun sampling the different types of salsa. This food has f-l-a-v-o-r.... there is definitely a  reason this place is busy!!

Totally worth the crappy parking situation here! My girlfriend and I came in on random weeknight for early dinner and the place was already full. Wow! Could be due to the limited seating or maybe because the food is terrific. Both? Likely. Chips arrived promptly straight from the oil pan - nice and toasty. And we helped ourselves to the salsa bar - which is completely fresh, creative, and whets your palette at the get-go! We loved the cilantro salsa and salsa mexicana the best. Zesty! The servers were quick to take our order despite being busy and minutes later my tacos de arrachera arrived. Sooo good! I mean. Wow! Meat was tender and juicy ....and the combination of spices and flavors was heaven. My friend ordered the Condesa specialty taco. Another winning ticket! Condesa has nailed the right way to make beans too. And..don't get me started on the deliciousness of the horchata. I've had me some horchata many places ..but this really rocked my world. Rocked it! 

Condesa, I have just two requests: Please do something about the sitting area so we can actually fit in this place. Also, please don't be out of flan next time I come in! Thanks!

So Sunday rolls around, and I'm hungover and day dreaming of someone to drop off a wheel chair for me to get around my house in the most lazy way possible. Then I see La Santisima on TV and I freaked out, and realized they're open on Sundays.

I managed to shower and get dressed in record time to make it there by noon. They tell me it's a 40 minute wait, and my stomach plays a symphony of sounds only okay in a hospital to be heard, I say "that's perfectly fine" and then go drunk sweat outside in the sun. 40 minutes went by and I prayed the tacos would be amazing and worth the wait.

We got seated inside and helped ourself to every single salsa at the salsa bar. There were a few that lit my threat on fire, but,  whatever, alls fair in love and salsa with this gringo.

I got the three taco plate with the mariachi loco, Cabo shrimp, and chicken tinga as well as a half order of the guacamole. I LOVED the guacamole, the tinga, and the mariachi... I felt the Cabo shrimp could've used something. But one thing that kind of was lacking was the service, not that I minded. I was content with my horchata to nurse my hangover. But our server forgot about our guacamole and I think the table next to us may have gotten the wrong order (the owner corrected it). I'll let it slide because they are crazy busy at all times.
Authentic food is so lacking in our culture today.  This is a rare find for excellent, native Mexican food.

Amazing house recipe horchata.
Salsa bar to die for. 
Street tacos: the BEST. 
Will go back as often as we can. 
Tamarindo Margarita AMAZING!

I was here!  Guy Fieri came earlier than me as well!

The best modern Mexican and first Mexican place we went to in Phoenix.  This place is a hit!

The service was slow and they forgot our drink orders a few times.  But the tequila they suggested was good.

Here comes the most important part.. their food.  We ordered their shark taco to share.  I had their El Gaucho Burro and my wife had their El Gaucho Quesa.  My wife is not a big quesadilla fan, but she liked it and it was so good when I tried it!  Her quesa had the perfect crisp texture to each bite.  My burro was excellent.  Since we both had El Gaucho, the fillings were the same ingredients.  Here's the climax.  They put cucumbers and bell peppers into their El Gaucho Burro and Quesa; that is a genius idea!  Those 2 ingredients brang out the taste of each individual ingredient from our burro and quesa.

Man, it was good!

Prices are good.

They have their own salsa bar.  I recommend their creamy cilantro salsa.  They also have good spicy ones as well.

A chips refill for your chips and salsa will cost you about $2?

Oh yeah, this place is pretty small.  They try to utilize as much as they can.

Very rare you will find Chinese eating Mexican, but I saw a few here.

Got to come here.

Wow...this place really knocked my socks off.  This is exactly what Phoenix needs, a cool place to eat great Sonoran/Mexican food.  The owners sure had a nice vision and succeded in creating a great spot for the neighborhood.

The tacos and quesadilla I've had here was nothing less than spectacular.  Having lots of flavor and not skimping on the portions. The salsa bar is quite fun as well with many different and uniques choices to choose from.  Never seen so many salsas offered anywhere else and I'm sure I will make it through all of them with my many visits to follow.

Keeping the flavor of the area being on the edge of a very artsy neighborhood the decor is amazing.  Vibrant paintings all around and murals on the bathroom doors definitely makes this place stand out with style.

This place is a must see for anyone who likes great food and culture.  Take a deep breath before you walk in and inhale an experience I am sure you will remember.

The Yelp rating is what made me drive out of my way to pickup a late lunch. If I were just driving by this shop I would have never stopped. 
I ordered a three taco plate with three different tacos. I do not remember the names, but they were ALL excellent! I ordered a Quesadilla. It is different from the Americanized version but I did not care for it. Love all the salsas!

I'm not even sure why this place has so many reviews. I try to be nice about reviews cause I know how this effects various businesses. We went here on a Saturday night (group of 9); and before I even decided to rate this place.... I went around asking the entire crew what they would rate this place ... all of them either said 1 or 1.5 out of 5 stars.. When we got in, we had to wait for 45 mins to get a table... I mean that's understandable given the fact that we were a large group... once seated.... everything is just so slow. We ordered and the food literally took about 45-50 mins to come out. That's way too long. The waitress was nice. (only reason why I'm giving them a one star). I advise this business to give chips for free since the wait is so long. Anyways, overall ... not too happy with the service.. and the food wasn't all that at all. There's a lot better Mexican restaurants around!

We have been to Santisima several times. The food is very good and the salsa bar not only adds, but makes it fun, too. Drinks were tasty, and service is good. One point to improve would be that we almost always have a long wait for our food. Given that it's tiny, there might not be much to do about that...Maybe expand?
From my experience up to this point this place is hands down the best taco shop in PHX.  The salsa bar is awesome with a ton of options and their street tacos along with the gourmet tacos are great.

food was pretty alright.  the menu is quite extensive, it can overload people if they don't really know what they want.  I had to ask for suggestions since there was so much going on.  the hostess/server made a couple suggestions for me though, and i was pleased with what i received.

the organization with staff though really needs to be improved like others have said.  all the servers and hostesses appear to be college aged girls yet they don't seem to know what's going on when the place gets crowded.  after i had been seated, we still waited 20 minutes for someone to take our order and it wasn't even the server that's supposed to take our table.  it was the hostess that took our order and told us "our" server would be by with out food.

i like the food, not the disorganization though

Being from Los Angeles I pride myself on having discovered some great taco shops and trucks. La Santisima was a Yelp driven decision right before driving back to CA.  The food was absolutely amazing..........an explosion of flavor that is second to none. You can taste the attention given to the preparation and the quality of all the ingredients. I'm going to always make time whenever I'm in Phoenix to stop in.........however the food is so special that I may actually drive back every so often for a fix.

Every once in a while yelp is just flat out wrong and that is the case with la santisima taco shop.  Every review makes you think it will be amazing, but the reality is that the food is ok, but there are much better places to eat in Phoenix.  

So what is wrong with this place?  First off, what the heck kind of quesadilla are the making?  I am still not sure.  Why fry a tortilla and throw some cheese in the middle, it just doesn't make any sense to me.  I love quesadillas, but this one was not good.

Second, the "carne asada" was not good.   It just didn't have much flavor.  The only burrito that I liked was the shrimp burrito, although I didn't realize that it had mushrooms in it, which was disappointing. 

The salsa bar is very good.  The tortilla chips are ok.  The location leaves a little bit to be desired and so does the food.  

I am sure many will go to this place based on yelp, but I was not impressed.

Best tacos I've had during my week in Phoenix, with a literal buffet of well-made salsas to match. 

Busy and a little disorganized at lunch (they needed one more person to help handle the crowd), it's worth seeking out.

Get the horchata with fruits and pecans, too - it's great.

Came here after my boyfriend had done seen it on Yelp. It is not by any means a large spacious restaurant. However, the best Mexican restaurants are primarily a hole in the wall. 

We split the House Margarita. We had asked for no salt but it still came salted. It was good,  although I don't like salt on my margarita when I am trying one for the first time because I want to know what it tastes like without anything added.

I got a lot of food (because I couldnt decide what to get). I got the traditional Quesadilla which is ironically not a traditional quesadilla. It is a corn tortilla  folded over that has Oaxaca Cheese inside and its fried. Its kinda like a Calzone but better. If I had to pick a cheese that could possibly be my favorite cheese in Mexican cuisine it would be Oaxaca. The Quesadilla was amazing but it is HUGE. I was expecting something around the size of my hand.  Nope, one half was probably the size of my hand. We did ask for no crema but they still put it on there. I also got the Conchita Lonche, the meat was delicious but the bread was kinda hard. It does come with mustard, which I was not expecting. It would be a great thing to order for Lunch for anyone who works downtown (which I do).  My boyfriend got the shark taco but I was not up for trying it mainly because I barely eat fish tacos when it is cod inside. It did look good displayed on his plate. I didn't get to try the beans but the rice was good. I have a hard time judging rice because I still believe my Nana makes the best white rice. 

The service wasn't bad but the woman was the only one really taking care of tables and about 4 tables including us walked in probably within 5 mins. So she was running around taking orders, running food and then touching back to the tables to see if anything was alright.  

In the end, I definitely am coming back.
Great atmosphere, phenomenal service and fantastic food. I ordered the baja shark tacos and cabo shrimp tacos. Fresh and very delicious to say the least. A MUST TRY!!

Yum! I wish their space was bigger and had something further on the northside but that is honestly the only thing I can say negative about this place. I have never had anything that I didn't like. Everyone who's visited me has wanted to come back to Phoenix to eat these tacos. If you go during a normal meal time expect to wait probably at least an hour. But it's all worth it!

By far one of my favorite Mexican restaurants to eat at in Phoenix.  I recommend it every time i get the opportunity. Everything from their exceptional salsa bar to their Quesas! You will not leave disappointed.

One of my "go to" places in downtown Phoenix.  Food is very good, salsa bar is excellent.  Very creative menu, so you aren't stuck with just a single filling choice in your tortilla.  House special is a fave.
Place is very small, which can be an energetic environment for a meal.  However, it can also be a bit of a pain when you want to go to the salsa bar at the same time as someone else.

There is the salsa bar with around a dozen house made salsas.  I am truly amazed by this place. It is small so not recommended for big groups.  Maybe a second date if you notice a parking spot open as you are approaching.  Horchata with chopped nuts, fruit, and cinnamon for the win.

I first saw Guy Fieri's visit on TV. I have Family in Phoenix so I said I had to try it out on my next visit. I was just there with my Family this past weekend. I was blown away by the decor and delicious food. It was everything that Guy Fieri said on his show and more!! I can't wait to go back to Phoenix so I can eat there again!!

First off, the service was lacking. Our waitress didn't seem very attentive or happy towards us. She could have checked on us every once in a while...and maybe smile? 

HOWEVER, the food was delicious (which is why I had to give a least four stars). We ordered their carne asada tacos and they didn't disappoint. Their salsa bar has a lot of choices and yes, the horchata is good.

Excellent food. Kinda steep on the pricing, but the size of the tacos is by far one of the largest portions you can get. This place is great if you want to eat some good ole unadulterated tacos. The salsa bar is outstanding as well, a lot of different styles and heat levels.

The self serve salsa had a great variety and was a lot of fun. The margaritas weren't amazing, but the food certainly was. I enjoyed a few street tacos, but particularly enjoyed the refried beans. I was visiting Phoenix, but it is definitely the best Mexican food I've had in a long time.

We moved to Arizona about 4 months ago and had driven past this place several times, but last night we saw it on an episode of Triple D and decided its time to try it. This place was amazing! Who doesnt love tacos, especially for breakfast/brunch! But they do serve actual breakfast on the weekends too. We will definitely be back.

I had this restaurant bookmarked for a while after seeing it on Diners, Drive-Ins, and Dives. We were attending a show in Downtown Phoenix, so we went by La Santisima before that. It was around 6-ish in the evening when we arrived and there were only 1 or 2 small tables open, so we were seated immediately. Getting to the table was kind of like walking through a maze since the restaurant is small and crowded.

It was very obvious that they were super busy and there were only 2 people taking orders, delivering food, etc. It took a while for them to take our orders and then even longer to bring us chips to snack on & our drinks. When they did, however, we were more than happy to wait for our food as we were were enjoying all the different salsas with the chips!

The salsa bar they have is very unique. They had very flavorful salsas that I've never had before. My favorite was the peanut one. It was kind of thick and creamy with a bit of spice. Other salsas that both me and my boyfriend liked were the pecan salsa, the salsa roja, the guacamole, etc. There were a total of maybe 10 or 12 different ones, all that tasted great with the chips and also on our tacos. I'd come back here just because of the salsa bar!

As far as our food goes, I ordered the Tinga taco and the Cabo Shrimp taco plate with rice and beans. My boyfriend ordered the La Santisima Speciality tacos with chicken. Both the tacos I ordered were completely different from each other. The Tinga taco tasted good as it was served but I thought that the shrimp taco needed a couple of salsas to enhanced the flavor of the breaded shrimp. The La Santisima Speciality tacos were much like the Tinga taco in that there were a bunch of different toppings on them, so they tasted great as served. My boyfriend couldn't help but to add the delicious salsas on them anyways, however!

Next time, we come in, I'd probably skip both the rice & beans and instead order one more taco! It's not that the rice & beans weren't good, it was just that the tacos were SO GOOD! It's great that everything that can be ordered a la carte or as a meal. Some tacos are bit more expensive than other ones, but the whole menu seemed fairly reasonably priced.

Overall, like I've said, the food was great but the service is where there could be some improvement. We'd recommend this restaurant to others!

Mixed feelings about this place - the food was great, the salsa bar awesome, and the service really bad.  I really like the filling choices,  especially in a taco.  Their quesadillas are like a thick fry bread, I though they we're too greasy but everyone else raved.

Leave extra time to check out, it took longer than the meal.
Their salsa bar is very inventive, and tasty.  Food is excellent too.  I will definitely return.
It was good. The only thing we didn't like was the wait time. Come early if you want a seat. Taco's were really good. I highly recommend this if you are in the area.

AVOID this place is dirty and has a bathroom smell as soon as you walk in... waited to be seated and the server said wait a minute and never approached. Waited 10 minutes- looked at the food and said forget it. Not up to par with the restaurants from Los Angeles at all. If I could give a negative start review I would.

Awesome salsa bar and SHARK tacos!! You rarely see the words "gourmet" and "taco" in the same sentence, but La Condesa somehow makes it work. However, La Condesa isn't in the best part of town, and I'm glad we came here for lunch versus dinner. We tried:

-Different Salsas from Salsa Bar (Pecan Salsa, Pico de Gallo, Mexican Salsa, Sesame Salsa, Cilantro Salsa, Grilled Peppers, http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/la-condesa-gourmet-taco-shop-phoenix-2?select=ytgVAxv6hFuPzqsPxwQmhg#ytgVAxv6hFuPzqsPxwQmhg): I liked the Pecan and Sesame salsas although I didn't get much pecan taste. The cilantro was too watery, but the grilled peppers were really good (and had a nice spicy kick). The pico de gallo was solid, as was the mexican salsa. Their tortilla chips are really good, and thin and crispy, so make sure you try them!
-Tacos (From L to R: Mayan Cochinita Pibil Taco, Carnitas Street Taco, Baja Sur Dogfish Shark Taco, http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/la-condesa-gourmet-taco-shop-phoenix-2?select=ytgVAxv6hFuPzqsPxwQmhg#Wah_j9kHBXGf2NluqFZB_g): 
-Mayan Cochinita Pibil Taco (Roasted Pork Shoulder w/Achiote Rojo, Wrapped in Banana Leaves, Slow-Cooked Until Fork Tender and Topped w/Lime Marinated Onions & Salsa Habanera Maya): I ordered this since a lot of other people seemed to like it, and it was a "Yucatan specialty". However, it was just ok. The pork was a little dry, and the flavors didn't stand out. I wouldn't order this again.
-Carnitas Street Taco: Pretty good! The carnitas were very flavorful, and I liked how bite sized this taco was. 
-Baja Sur Dogfish Shark Taco (Corn Tortilla Stuffed w/Beer Battered Dogfish Shark): DELICIOUS! I've had shark meat before and am used to it being tougher and firmer than regular fish. However, there wasn't a big different in the texture, but there seemed to be more of a sweetness to it. I guess I enjoyed the "Baja Sur specialty" vs. the Yucatan. This is a must order if you go to La Condesa!

I only saw a small strip of parking available in front of the restaurant, but it is shared with a convenience store. I think street parking was also available, but I'd recommend making sure you don't have any valuables out! I definitely plan on coming back to La Condesa and trying their other seafood tacos, but will make sure it's during lunch. Dining in is the way to go so that you can sample all of the different salsas. The staff was nice, but weren't the quickiest.

My wife and I use this as our go to quality taco spot. But I could spend all my time just sampling the salsas. Great midtown PHX spot. Parking is somewhat difficult if you come during busy hours but don't let that deter you.

Amazing food! I haven't had quality Mexican food since moving out if So. Cal, but La Santisima is delicious! A plain chicken burrito is a bit pricey but anything unusual (shark or smoked marlin) is the same price.

I'm not a fan of what's annoyingly referred to as "Tex-Mex" food, at all. It gives me the idea of pseudo-not-fast-food like Moe's, or lame cantinas, run by people whose ancestors probably couldn't pronounce "cantina," that cater to the effete-minded "Margaritaville" crowd.

My wife, however, was attracted to the outside decor and lured in by the "gourmet" in the name.

Welp, folks, let me tell you: I'm really glad I went in this place. Their big advertisement is that they want to turn the tide of opinion on Mexican food/Tex Mex whatever from one of greasy, unhealthful junk to tasteful and thoughtfully-prepared fare- to the end of the latter, they did their due on me!

The woman and I had their take on quesadillas, which weren't the usual stupid flat flour tortilla cheese sandwiches with a pile o' salt and a not-pile of meat. In fact, these guys were made from homemade corn tortillas, deep fried (though not doused in grease) and filled well with your menu choice (In my case, al pastor; the wife got mahi-mahi). Folded over like a calzone and topped lightly with cojita sour cream, these guys are filled with flavor- flavor I've not experienced at any other Mexican joint in this city. The light crispiness of the tortilla really drives it home, and the quesadilla in all makes me think more of "tamale grande" than what you would classify as a quesadilla. (again, a boring flat cheese sandwich).

The price is kind of high; and while the portion is not *big* big as if you might get from a typical Mexican restaurant around here, let me tell you pals: It's well worth it.

Can't wait to try some new things here, sometime. In the meantime, go and try a quesadilla if you want to be flavor-blasted for the first time in Phoenix.

Small dining room and no waiting area, so hard to get in at peak times, but worth trying more than once to get in.  The meat is deliciously flavored and the salsa bar makes every meal fun and personalized.  Inexpensive, high quality food.

Best quesadilla I've ever had, I wish I could get it back home. It had that really fresh Mexican style cheese, between a very war and flaky tortilla.

You can never go wrong with a salsa bar, particularly one that has a creamy almond salsa, yeah.
Love the salsa bar and the burritos are always great... not to mention the house margaritas.  Only wish the wait wasn't crazy but that's what happens when a place makes great food!

I came here to eat with my co-workers at lunch time and it was packed!!!!! This was obviously a great sign, but know it's packed during the lunch hour. 

The place is small but seats quite a few people. You may also sit by the bar to eat (which is what we did since we didn't want to have to wait forever to eat). 

I had 3 carne asada tacos with rice and beans. The meat was well seasoned and they double up on tortillas so they def won't fall apart. 

The highlight for me was the salsa bar. Omg it was yummy! They have your traditional salsas, like salsa verde, salsa bandera etc, but also have very inventive yet delicious spins on the ordinary, like their salsa siete chiles (7 types of roasted chiles with red onion and it was super chunky) or another salsa made with a base of chopped radish.  

It was great that they also gave us a basket of super crispy chips to enjoy with all the salsas. 

The ONLY thing that I did not like was that I saw drinks poured at the bar and the bar tender grabbed the fruit out of the open bin with his bare hands. I had a bottled drink, but would have not asked for a drink if the bar were the only option. Just to be clear, the kitchen staff had gloves and you could see into the kitchen, which was organized and clean.

My grand finally in Scottsdale came the evening I went to La Santisima.   I wanted to some good Mexican food before I left the west coast,  so I looked this place up and based on the Yelp reviews I made the journey.   It was about a 35 minute drive from my hotel in Scottsdale,  but well worth the trip.     The place isn't that big,  but it's very clean and pretty traditional.   The whole time I was there I heard bob Marley playing.   It was odd,  but cool at the same time since I expected mariachi music playing.   Anyhow,  me and my friends placed our orders and came to the salsa bar.   This had to have had the most variety in salsa that I've seen.   Tasted a few salsas for my chips and ordered a few alcoholic drinks which were fantastic.   I tried the peach margarita and my friend had the strawberry one.   The food was also delicious!  I had the asada burrito smothered and my friend had the chicken quesadilla.    The quesadilla is pretty stuffed and filling.   I would definitely come back and have lunch or dinner here in the future.

Keeping this brief..


Went for lunch on Monday after a co-workers recommendation and was blown away by how good the Cochinita Pibil Burro was.  The pork shoulder is marinated in achiote, orange and a bunch of other stuff and was unbeleivably tender.  Great tortillas as well.  My Mexican buddy declared it some of the best meat he has ever eaten.

The salsa bar had some pretty interesting stuff in it and everything I tried was great, including marinated onions and two different salsa verdes.  A plus was the Pico was pretty spicy, with large chunks of Jalapeno in it.  

I will definitely be back.
The best salsa bar in life. Delicious vegetarian options, love them.
Small place but good authentic Mexican food. The tacos r bomb and different salsas at the salsa bar. Moderate price.
Definitely one of favorite restaurants ever. Everything from their margaritas to their burritos to their salsa is so awesome. Their speciality burrito is my favorite.

I'm a salsa fan, and this place must have had 20 fresh salsas just waiting to be enjoyed. I tried most of them and they were excellent. Five stars for the salsas alone. The tacos were great - mole, shrimp, etc..
A-freeeeeaking-mazing!!!! Everything's sooooooooo good!!! Seriously authentic and flavorful!!! Mix the pecan salsa with the chipotle salsa - it's bomb!
Specialty taco and margaritas are great. The Mayan taco is also good. Mole and Marlin were interesting but not as good.

So glad we finally got to try this place! The salsa bar is awesome and our tacos were so good.  The veggie taco had so much flavor.  The service was also very good. Two very nice attentive servers! Can't wait to go back.

By far the best mexican food I've found in Phoenix, and trust me, I've eaten at almost all of them :)  I tend to get their street tacos with either pastor or carne asada, but everything is good here.  They have an awesome little salsa bar with like 10 different kinds of salsa.  I live in Anthem and we drive out of our way 30+ minutes to eat here it's that good!

This place makes the best horchatas, we  had Their tinga, carne asada, and pastor tacos and they were dang delicious all the meats had so much flavor, if I wasn't so full I would have ordered 6 more tacos, I also ordered their house lonche. It's pretty much a torta. 

That one so good nice crunchy bread, and the Oaxaca cheese was so soft and full of flavor.
Will definitely be coming back for more 
Thank you guys for the great service
The salsa bar, the horchata, the veggie burrito, the fish burrito... SO GOOD. However, their tacos didn't do it for me (specifically the tortillas). Hey, can't win them all.

Went there with the whole family cause it was nearby. We weren't expecting to walk out so satisfied, especially cause we're all so picky. Highly recommend the quesadillas. They're filled with Oaxaca cheese and flavorful meats/veggies, folded over fresh maza then fried. The salsa bar is colorful, unique, and spicy!!
Amazing tacos! The seating and parking can be a little dicey, but the food is worth it.
Absolutely delicious. Fresh ingredients that don't hide under heavy sauces. Great alternative to the regular taco shops.

I was craving street tacos and this place is as close to the street tacos you will get in Rocky Point. It's a small quaint place but they have such a variety of different salsas I didn't even know existed. The corn tortillas were fresh and the carne asada tacos were extremely on point. 
I'll be coming back here sooner than you think just to get my taco fix!

I loved the food! It has great authentic food and it is all fresh. My only downside for not giving it 5 stars is the size of the place. It can fit probably around 20 people max. I think they need to move to a bigger location. Service was ok as well, give them a past because of the busyness.

Just really good salsa's and Tacos!!  Just had a late lunch with the wife...had the fish tacos plate and the pork tacos plate accompanied by housemade horchata...both tacos were really good...especially liked the salsa to accompany the pork tacos.  The beans and rice were good. The horchata had fresh strawberries and nuts in it, tasted like they had  just made it!   Salsa bar has a really good selection..especially like the avacado and the tomato chipotle.  Will be back for more and try their queso's or a burrito.

We flew into Arizona, jet lagged and hungry. This taco spot was near by and food network featured it. 
Outside the place looked a little sketchy, but inside it looked like a typical taco spot. We got fresh chips to start. And then we ordered about 3 tacos per person (all of them were good!). 
The best thing about this place is their salsa bar. They have everything from pico to strawberry to pecan salsa. Some were spicy, some sweet. It's insane. And delicious. 
Pretty cool and simple taco spot in Phoenix. Small dining area though, so don't get mad if there's a wait.

This place was so totally awesome and unique. My girlfriend and I are visiting from Colorado and this place was recommended by a local and damn did we get lucky. The food was amazing and our waiter Abraham was super kind and took great care of us even though it was busy. The burritos and the salsa bar were out of this world amazing!

I grew up in the SW but have loved in the NE for 20+ years. Also worked in a Mexican restaurant during high school and college. This was the best Mexican food I can recall. I had Queso Fundido with Choizo and Poblanos, paired with a 3-taco platter of Baby Shark, Tiger Shrimp and Mahi.

All I got to say that these were the best taco's I've ever had. Found this place by chance on Yelp by chance on a visit to Phoenix for the Pro Bowl. The salsa selection is good. Next time I'm in town I'll be there again.
Love the salsa bar!! Kind of a tight squeeze but worth it.

I have been here twice now and both visits were great. I love the Salsa Bar they have with fresh homemade salsas. Both visits I ordered Taco plates. I have had the Tinga Chicken and the Carne Asada. The Chicken was much better. I have also had the mahi taco and a shrimp taco. Those were amazing. Their Horchata is delicious as well as their rice and beans that accompany their Taco Plates. I highly recommend this place. I hear their margaritas are great too. I will be back.......many more times.

A great little taco spot hidden in Phoenix. The pastor tacos have a nice hit of spice, which contrasts well with the sweetness of the pineapple. Prices are reasonable. This place is seriously small, we went on a Tuesday afternoon and it was empty, though I can see La Santisima filling up quickly during the evening. Our waitress was reserved, but not rude.

It's not in the best neighborhood, which is kind of sad, because there's an elementary school across the street, but I feel like the best eateries are usually in someplace sketchy. Often, you must venture outside your comfort zone to experience the sublime.

Also, I neglected to try the salsa bar, I was so memorized by the pastor tacos. I'll definitely return on my next trip to PHX.

Fantastic. I had gaucho borro, was delicious but I should have added rice and beans. Margaritas were tasty too. Guacamole was from perfectly ripe avocados, which I really appreciated.

If you go at night, don't be discouraged by the total lack of lighting outside. Inside the food was great and staff was welcoming.

Tip: When it says 3.99 a la carte, it's actually only 1 taco. Only the taco plate has 2 tacos. We made that mistake and our bill ended up tripling in price. 

On a brighter note, the horchata was fantastic! This is the first time I've seen horchata filled with so much fruit and it was such a large size, perfect for sharing. We ordered the slow cooked pork taco and I thought it was a little too messy. I enjoyed the fish tacos the most, light and crispy.

Also loved the extensive salsa bar and the fact there is cilantro salsa!

the food is good, the service is not good sometimes. in fact sometimes the service kind of ruins the experience when i eat in so i always order to go. and even when i order to go i must wait 30 minutes for my food, even at times when they are not too busy. i have tried multiple times to call in my order ahead of time so i dont waste my time with this restaurant, but many times their phone just keeps ringing and they never answer it. funny tho, because when you walk up to the counter, there is their phone right next to the most encountered area of the restaurant. when i have the patience to put up with the lack of decent service here, i come and enjoy some good food.

We really enjoy the food here, but service was poor due to lack of adequate staff. They recently expanded the restaurant, which was sorely needed, but appear have failed to hire more staff and cooks, which makes for an even longer wait than usual. 
Would give this place 5 stars for cuisine, 2 stars for service. I would like aknowledge the staff in service since they tried their best.

Dude.

I love this place. It's walking distance from my house, that is baaaad news for my thighs. I've driven past it multiple times and it never caught my eye. Finally, I did notice their large statue thingy outside of the establishment. It was all lit up as I drove by during the evening. When I realized it was a gourmet taco shop, I knew I had to go asap. 

I went with my boyfriend and we both went to TOWN on their chips and assorted salsas. My favorite was the pecan salsa. Sweet and spicy! For our meals, he ordered 3 tacos and I ordered 2. The pork tacos were slightly bland and made me worry at first that I was going to be let down, but then came the chicken mole taco - oh my! Delicious! Sweet and savory, it was perfect. I know that sauce is difficult to make too, so, well done. Most of the tacos actually don't come with cheese - you know why? Because the tacos are so bomb you don't even need the cheese really. Their flavors are very carefully picked to taste a certain way. Save the cheese and salsa for the chips! You'll enjoy the tacos just as they are.

YUM!

Great food but boy..... the wait to get served is so long. And forget getting your appetizer before your entree. We waited 30 min for appetizer only. 

If they continue with this horrible service I'm sure they'll go out of business, no matter if they were featured in Food network.

Gonna keep it short(ish) and simple today.  Arrived at 6PM on a Sunday, and to say that parking is extremely limited is an understatement.  The restaurant itself is small, which explains why there weren't too many parking spots.  It was a 45 minute wait for a table for two so we ordered takeout instead.  A little crammed and loud with people talking over one another, but it was actually pretty cozy.  The staff were really nice, pleasant, and efficient even with the crowd and gave us little lids for the salsa, along with our horchata, after we placed our order.

Fast forward through standing around awkwardly in what felt like everyone's way for 20 minutes in the restaurant, we had our burros in hand - an Al Pastor burro and La Santisima burro (chicken).  The burros are pretty sizable and scrumptious.  The salsa bar is probably what sets this place apart from the rest.  It's fun and most of them have a little kick to it, so have a glass of water nearby.  I loved their horchata, it's a little sweeter than other horchatas, has more cinnamon, and the fruits (strawberries) are a great touch.  Definitely will be back, probably for takeout.

My co-worker walked in from lunch the other day with their horchata and I liked the bit I had so much I demanded to know where it was from. It took a bit for me to get used to the sheer number of salsas they had available, but once I got comfortable trying things (I was afraid I might burn my tongue off accidentally) I was hooked! 

I'd recommend the peanut salsa to anyone. It was some seriously good sauce.

Wow! 

I was pleasantly surprised when I stepped into this joint. The decor was fun, the restaurant was super clean and the food was so great! I am so excited that this is within walking distance of my home. 

YOU MUST TRY THE HORCHATA! It tastes like my mom's except better. Wait? Is that even possible? Yes! I swear to little baby Jesus that this is the best horchata in the universe. 

The Cochinita Pibil taco was great, the mole chicken taco was great and the salsa bar was killer. I tried 5 or 6 and they were fresh and uniquely flavored. 

The best part? Three people ate for 20 bucks! I could have eaten cheaper if I had not gotten the plate. I took half of the food home, if that is any sign of the healthy (but not overly large) portions here. One taco would have done it for me. 

I will be a regular at this place!  You should try it too! :)

I ordered the shrimp and carnitas tacos (both delicious!)  and washed it down with an ice-cold Mexican Coke (the only soda I'll drink).  

The salsa bar is GREAT - variety. The walls are covered with local art. 

Con: There is nowhere to wait if the modest sized restaurant is full. No one wants to wait in the heat during the summer.

Well we went back just to check and, sure enough, this is still the best mexican food we've ever had.  My taco with pork cooked in a banana leaf was uh-mA-zing.  And the margarita was too.  I think I just gained five pounds.

Yes. Just yes. If you go, do the carne asada tacos. They were delicious and very decently priced. The beans tasted like homemade, honest to goodness refried beans. The salsas were all really interesting and the chips were nice and crunchy. I will definitely return!

Edit: went back a second time with my husband's family and even though there was 6 of us, we were treated very well by staff and I'm assuming owner. Great experience once again!!!

Love, love, love this Phoenix gem!  I stumbled upon it when I was out house hunting & my husband learned about it from a co-worker, so we tried it one night & have been hooked ever since!  The salsa bar is awesome & the food is fantastic!  We are so happy to live just a few short miles from here & we go often!
Amazing! Cant wait to go again. Really great salsa bar, and lots of choices on the menus. Hubby was a bit apprehensive about going but he enjoyed it

Ok. This place was great. But I had some issues with my girlfriend here. She's an executive chef and is madly in love with Guy Fieri. When she saw the autographed poster she instinctively tried to climb on the table and smell it. I think she even tried to lick it. After the manager had to threaten to call the cops she settled down and after the shakes and sweats stopped, we were able to enjoy the best damn tacos we have had in a loooong time. The salsa bar kicks ass and we mixed a few together to get even better sauces. I do recommend this place to everyone, but not Guy Fieri. He's a dick and almost ruined our vacation.
Awesome food!! Really really good! Great atmosphere as well. Definitely recommend for Mexican food lovers!

My favorite place for tacos in all Phoenix! Try any meat or vegetarian "La Condesa style"... . Everything is fresh and tasty... Service is also friendly and quick...i highly recommend it if you have visitors from out of town.

It is the superlative bean and cheese burrito in Phoenix! Classic taste and the refried beans are not cooked in lard, which is nice for vegetarians to know and whatever oils they use give them a good savory taste. No bland beans here! If dairy is not your thing, the Ghandi Vegan burrito has fresh guacamole and black beans matched by no other. And if the entrees weren't enough, there is also THE best salsa bar of all time. The red chipotle salsa must have some sort of addictive substance in it, as I cannot stop at just two servings. 
The service is top notch and the atmosphere is mellow. 
My only issue is that it's kinda hard to see from the road. But you can see the sign pretty easy if you're looking for it.

Best horchata EVER!  The salsa bar is great, they have a huge variety to try.  The shark dog fish tacos are great...a MUST try.  The place is somewhat small, but if you come at the right time there is no wait.

I tried this joint simply because of the great reviews on yelp. I was not disappointed. There is an awesome salsa bar. The service was great. The staff was helpful and friendly. The food alone was worth the trip, but there was just so many wonderful elements. I had a steak and bean burro. The steak was seasoned perfectly and had a nice crust of season on it. The horchata is seriously the best I've ever had. I can't wait to take everyone I know to this great spot. Enjoy!
Place is a bit overrated.   Good salsa bar but tortillas for the tacos were pretty average and the meat on the arrachera tacos not particularly tender.  The fish tacos were very good.

Based on my first visit, I would have happily given La Condesa a 4 star review. My veggie tacos were delicious, and I loved all the fun salsas. I couldn't get enough of them! Really, the only negative was the cramped quarters.

My second visit, however, was not nearly as good. On the positive side, I got guacamole this time which was studded with dried cranberries and tasted great with the strawberry salsa. I was impressed with the service too because my friend's order came out the same time as mine despite the fact that we ordered separately 10 minutes apart. 

The tacos this time were awful. I decided to get the vegan tacos since the description of "no pintos, no rice" lead me to believe that the beans and rice in the veggie tacos weren't really vegetarian friendly. I'm a pretty strict vegetarian so I try to avoid food that's been prepared with meat-based stock. The vegan tacos come with black beans which were absolutely flavorless. I'm not sure these beans encountered even a grain of salt during their preparation. The tacos also had iceburg lettuce in them which tasted dreadful of course. 

So now I know I can't have their veggie tacos, and the vegan ones suck. No reason to visit again.

Hands down yum and fave taco place in town!!!!! Haven't tried the burros as I'm in love with the tacos... Love love the salsa bar as well! Cute inside, nothing fancy and a great place to take friends. If you like barrio, you will love la condesa (so will your wallet).
Amazing food!!! Great service!!! Loved it!!! I will go back for sure! The guacamole salsa was amazing!!!
First i wanted a quesadilla and they didnt have any cheese and then the waitress skiped our table and gave food to 2 other tables that got there after us.. never going back..

Not a fan. We waited 15 minutes for a table when the place was practically empty. They sat us next to the hot window (triple-digit hot day) when there was plenty of open tables all over the restaurant. The guacamole was weird (cranberries in guac?) and I hate those salsa bars that give you those tiny plastic containers that are too small for you to dip your chips into. The margaritas and tacos were good though. Just a warning...don't get the three taco plate...it's too much food. One taco was enough with the beans and rice.
Nice variety of salsas. I had the shrimp tacos and they were delicious. The place is very small and only had two servers for dinner. They were nice though. I would definitely return.

As someone who's travels to Southern California a few times a year, I sort of know my Mexican food especially as it comes to street tacos and such.  I do admit this place has more protein for your tacos than any other Mexican restaurant I've been in.  It can also be overwhelming the number of choices but at $3.99-$6.50 for a single taco, the prices are pretty high so I had some high expectations.  What I can say is that the al pastor tacos were dry, in fact tasted like tree bark in terms of texture.  The braised pork was good though but the tortas were very interesting, it came out on a toasted French baguette.  It was decent but I had to put quite a bit of salsa in it to moisten it up due to it again being very dry.  Imagine dry meat on a toasted French baguette.

What I believe does set this place apart is their amazing salsa bar, it's self serve and unlimited.  You get your first bowl of chips on the house, refills are $2.70.  The other thing that stood out was the horchata, it had fresh ground cinnamon, some oats and bits of strawberries on the bottom.  It was very interesting, but nonetheless, was very good.  We also had a strawberry margarita, tasted more like sugar water with a half shot of a tequila and very very sweet.  I believe the strawberry margarita was $9.00, so it was a little high.  If I ever go back, I think I'll stick with the horchata instead of their margaritas.  

They said an hour wait for two, we waited outside for 30 minutes and was called, so at least that's nice.  A tip is to write your name, party size and phone number on the waiting list, they will call you when your table is ready.  And no waiting inside either, all waiting is outside.

"Oh wow, what did I get myself into?" was all I thought as I pulled up to La Condesa.  I'm not familiar with Phoenix or the surrounding neighborhoods, so I was a little taken aback at first.  The business looks like an old house, as most of the businesses in the area do, i noticed lots of bars on the windows, and the majority of the business signs in the area were in Spanish.  THE ONLY reason I noticed this is because I'm unfamiliar with Phoenix and was traveling alone.

First impression, the restaurant is tiny! I would say that at capacity, the restaurant is pretty loud and I had a difficult time hearing my server. The tables were very close together, all the chairs were mismatched, and the lighting was really dim.  It was very difficult to get to the back of the restaurant where they put the salsa bar.  

The house margaritas were made with fresh grapefruit and lime, and that was perfect for me. Unfortunately, the food wasn't as good.  I had the shrimp burro, and it was really sloppy.  It melted out of the sleeve and fell apart while I was trying to eat it.  Plus, some of the tails were left on the shrimp... let me tell you about shocking!

The service was sub-par, in my opinion.  My server was inattentive and didn't ask how my food was.  I had to flag down the server like an air traffic controller in order to get my bill, and it took a while to get my bill back.  

This one is not a revisit for me.

A truly great casual and authentic Mexican restaurant with a gourmet twist. La Santisima sports great artwork on the interior. They have a salsa bar with a wide variety of interesting flavors. The food is delicious, unique and interesting. Less traditional, but flavorful and satisfying. So are the portions.

My friend raved about it so I thought I'd try it. First off, the place is SMALL. luckily we got there right when they opened. Seemed like as soon as we got seated, the place started to fill up. I enjoyed the salsa bar and the different assortment of salsas. As for my actual food. I didn't care for it much. To me, it didn't have much of a flavor to it unless it was drowned in the salsa from the salsa bar. Was going to order a strawberry horchata to go but every time we asked for something, the waitress took a while to come back (she only came back in a hurry when it was time to pick up the money), so I said forget it. I won't be back but at least I can say I went.

Saw this restaurant on diners, drive-ins and dives and am so glad we stopped here! We are in town for 2 days from Miami, on our way to Sedona! Service is amazing, food is OUT OF THIS WORLD!!! Great place! Horchata is the best I've ever had!

A plate with 3 tacos, a scoop of rice and a lick of re-fried beans was $15 dollars! I ordered a michelada after seeing the pictures of it here on yelp (which let me add that the michelada was not even on the menu) and that thing costs $12 dollars... for 1 beer and some clamato juice in it!

I saw of bunch of plaques on the well for "best of...." this and best of that, including a 2012 "cheap eats of phoenix". I interpret that plaque as something having to do with "low prices" however, it seems like the restaurant totally moved away from low cost!

taking away the cost factor, i think the food is good. i ordered a Marlin, Cochinita Pibil and barbacoa taco which were all great and my wife ordered a "lonche" with skirt steak which was also good. the salsa bar does have great salsas but they're watered down... it can't even be scooped, you can only "wet" your chips in it and if you add it to your food be ready for your tortilla or lonche to fall apart ... they might as well serve the salsa on a cup with a straw so you can sip on it as you eat!

There's one plaque that this restaurant deserves to have on the wall... the one that says "Best use of a small space" tables are so close to one another, it gets really crammed in there.

OVERALL Rating
Food is an A
Prices C
Horchata B+

Fresh chips and salsa with a temporary unidentified object in my "margarita tamarindo".  Our waitress graciously explained that this was a tamarindo in my drink, which gave the margarita flavor. I have been driving past this restaurant for years, admiring the beautiful sugar skull mosaic glistening in the Phoenix sun as I drove by.  Well tonight was the night. I pulled into one of the limited parking spaces located directly on 16th street, momentarily pondering how I will pull out later, but consumed with curiosity as to what was behind the big wooden door. I apprehensively opened the door, and was pleasantly surprised with what I found. A quaint mom and pop restaurant with a true southwest feel and experience. With the likes of a visit from Guy Ferari (?) And Best of New Times awards plastered on the menu, I was feeling pretty proud of my mystery choice.  My sister and I ordered and split the bean and Oaxaan cheese burro, mole chicken taco, an the al pastor tacos.  All were excelente!!
Ok, thats enough for now as I am feeling the nice mellow effects of my magnefico tamarindo slowly wear off.  We will be back!!

I liked this place but I dont feel like it's as amazing as yelp says it is. They do have a large salsa bar which is nice for people who like to try tons of different flavors. I found only a couple that I really enjoyed. The tacos were good, but not the absolute best I've ever had. Service was mediocre at best. I would eat here again if someone invited me. Decent food for sure. But the best I've ever had? No

Best Mexican restaurant in Phoenix manos down. Be patient with the service since it's soooo small but their food is the best. Their take on a quesadilla is delicious. Their salsa bar keeps my wife and I coming back time and time again. Just be careful not to get too full on chips before the meal comes out.
Killer tacos and the salsa bar is unparalleled. Get there early, nut if your late it's worth the wait.

We were excited to try this place bases on the reviews.  I am giving this 4 stars because it was kind of a long wait (35 minutes) and there aren't a lot of benches outside to sit, (also it was hard to get water refills during our dinner.) But once inside, it is totally worth it!  The salsa bar is very unique and I liked how I could sample so many different kinds.  I got the mole tacos and would recommend trying one and maybe a different kind.
Awesome street tacos. Best in phoenix and cheap! The place is small but the service and food is amazing. This is my new favorite place for tacos.
Love this place- only wish we didn't have to wait outside to get in!! That beau g said it's worth the wait!  We got tacos but saw some quesadillas that looked amazing- next time!

The tacos were amazing!!! When you step inside you'll think you are in Mexico. Everything from the art to the bar is authentic. The salsa bar has so many exotic selections that you will salivate over. The menu even caters to vegetarians. The tacos and burros are amazing. I will be a regular here and you should be too! Oh yeah and Alfredo makes killer margs!

La Condesa, you stole my heart.  Gourmet Taco Shop indeed.  Your saucy molé put me over the top.

You really know how to spice up a relationship with your many wonderful salsas.

I loved your warm decor and warmer service.

I can't wait to come back to sample your salsas and try more tacos.

I finally made my way here to meet some friends on a trip to Phoenix about a month ago, then I met another friend here on my most recent trip.

$3.99 gourmet street tacos.  Filling.  20 or so salsas.  Delicious.

The tacos are $4 a pop (I guess that's why they call themselves a "gourmet" taco shop), but they're worth every cent. I came here twice and tried much of the taco menu. My favorites were: cabo shrimp, fish, mayan pibil, arrachera and guacho. This place has the best salsa bar I've found in Phoenix so far, too. Great house margarita as well!

Almost missed this place, because Yelp still shows no alcohol, and a mexican meal without a beer or margarita is not complete.  Glad I went!  We split the shrimp, veggie and pork tacos.  This is the only place where I would consider ordering a veggie taco over the meat ones.  The grilled vegetables were packed with flavor, and the cheese was perfect.  Add an awesome salsa bar and mexican beer, and you have the perfect meal for before or after the ball game.  I would have given 5 stars, but the pork tacos didn't wow me.  Don't get me wrong, they were good - but just above average.

I enjoy both authentic Mexican tacos and excellent variations of the originals. The restaurant offers both. The simple and delicious street style tacos are as good as the ones cooked on the carts on the side of the streets in Mexico. The shrimp taco was also divine. The salsa bar was a treat. The chips were just ok.

I won't beat around the bush. This was hands down the best Mexican food i've had in Phoenix so far. The salsa bar was incredibly varied and interesting, the street tacos at happy hour were delicious, the house margarita was perfectly balanced and the handmade quesadilla destroyed any preconception I had of what a quesadilla was supposed to be. Highly recommended. On top of that, staff was attentive and the atmosphere was unique, and unpretentious.

One of my favorite taco shops in Phoenix, with a vast variety of salsas and menu items, new school and traditional tacos, and a deep-fried quesadilla. Yes, you read that correctly. Surely you'll have a heart-attack immediately after, but it's worth it. I almost think it's time for them to update locations, and get into something bigger since it's a nightmare to try and eat there around the lunch rush time, also its sort of rustic appearance doesn't quite match how good their food is. If it wasn't for recommendations from friends previously, it's the kind of place where you'd walk in, take a quick look, and walk out. Needless to say, don't allow that to deter you from exploring their menu, you surely wont' be dissatisfied.

Great find! This place is a little whole in the wall and not the "cleanest" environment....but the food was great! Best margarita I have ever had...and that was only the house margarita. Can't wait to come back for happy hour when they are only $3.00. I had the shrimp and carne asada tacos while my husband had the burrito with carne asada, bell peppers, avocado. Everything was delish! The salsa bar was great! So many different choices and all were excellent.
The table behind us had the guacamole and quesadilla...both looked yummy..they were very loud about how great it all tasted too! :)

I will definitely come back!

Hands down the best Mexican Food I've had in AZ! Not your typical greasy, heavy Mexican food. Everything is so fresh and delicious. They have a huge salsa bar with a variety of salsas. Their margaritas are delightful. I highly recommend if you're craving something a little south of the border.

This is hands down one of my favorite taco shops ever! The restaurant itself is pretty small inside, but it is always packed because it is a local favorite. There is a salsa bar with around 15 different types that you can sample for your chips and dinners. Every time I go I get two fish tacos, and they always hit the spot. The different alcoholic drinks look amazing, and I will have to try one of those the next time I come! I have tried taking every person I love here just to share this favorite of mine with them!
The burrito I had was the best burrito ever. I'm here on a 6 hour layover and was told to visit this place.  Very good food

My coworker and I stopped here for lunch today. The selections on the menu are plentiful and overwhelming. I was impressed with the variety of vegetarian options. I had the gaucho burrito, and my coworker had the Azteca Tinga burrito. The food was amazing! Make sure you get the horchata. It was the best I've ever had. There were strawberries, apples, and nuts in the drink. You will be mad at yourself later if you don't order it. The salsa bar is also ridiculously good, but your burrito will need no condiments.

This was my first time here. I will definitely be returning soon! The horchata was the best I've ever had. Not too sweet but comes in 32oz portions. The casadillas are insane! More like a deep fried calzone. Delicious. Gaucho Burrito was also incredible. 15 salsas to choose from. Parking a little tough but don't let it hold you back from visiting this gem.

Oh. My. God. This place is so amazing, even the rice is delicious!!! We had the shrimp with veggie tacos ( I can't remember the exact name of the dish), Sonoran Carne Asada Taco, and al pastor burro. Every bite is better than the last, and my cousin and I had takeout! I can only imagine what it would've tasted like fresh out the kitchen. We also had strawberry margaritas (non-alcoholic to go), and we added our own tequila at home :-) An amazing last dinner to our weekend trip to Phoenix!!

I ordered the arrachera and the mariachi tacos. I feel the hype was too much. The arrachera tasted like it was seasoned in a pound of salt. To me, it wasn't such a pleasant taste. The mariachi tacos tastes like they were missing salt. One of them seemed like it even had way too much oil. However the beans and rice were real good. Aside from an angry lady behind us, the atmosphere was pleasant and really really enjoyed trying all the different salsas that they have.

Tremendous food that has only gotten better over time since the restaurant opened a few years back.

The tacos are the best item on the menu, and the quesadillas are a close second, in my opinion.  This is not the typical Az-Mex quesadilla.  It's deep fried and incredibly delicious.  I'd go with anything including arrachera.

The salsa bar is as good as hyped here on Yelp.  My personal favorites are the cilantro, the pecan, the peanut, and the strawberry (when they have it).  A couple of great typical molcajete blends are there too.

Don't miss the house margarita.  The happy hour price of a few bucks is a total steal.  It's a ruby red grapefruit blend, and it's absolutely delicious (and well worth it even at the regular price).

You can eat like a king with a huge helping of food, great salsas, a quesadilla to split, have a margarita, and walk out for $15-20 per person including tip.  Delicious food and one of the best places on Calle 16.
Hidden gem. Hole in the wall with the most unassuming store front but delicious salsa bar with great authentic Mexican food!

What more can you ask for from a legit Mexican restaurant? La Santisima has the tacos and salsa bar that make up Mexican food euphoria, and even offers serious vegetarian options. 

My friend and I had dinner here. Driving from El Paso to Los Angeles, we had become sick of Chex Mix and energy drinks. I didn't realize La Santisima had been featured on Food Network's Triple D, but the Guy Fieri memorabilia gave it away immediately. In a fantastically awkward moment made possible by fourth generation cellular technology, we watched the restaurant's Food Network VODs right as the server came to take our order. The server let us finish watching.

There were more tacos available at the restaurant than its online menu currently displays. The veggie tacos I ordered were a classic guac, black bean, pico, and lettuce combination. They also offer a grilled zucchini type side for those that are looking to avoid eating rice. The food was fantastic. The freshness was palpable and the flavors were balanced. With so many salsas to choose from, I felt like a child in a candy store. Did I mix salsas? You bet I did. Maybe people should start saying, "I felt like Chris at a salsa bar."

The restaurant had an odd atmosphere. Maybe it was the mermaid skeleton with dollar bills clipped to it. La Santisima wasn't quick - despite being an odd hour in the afternoon, our food took quite some time. They also charged for every basket of chips past basket numero uno. I'm sure the United Federation of Restaurants that Proudly Serve Chips and Salsa was furious at the first member restaurant to offer unlimited chips - that restaurant set a ridiculous expectation!

La Santisima was pretty tasty, and I would return for the salsas and tacos. I'm excited to see if Los Angeles has similar options.

This place is AWESOME! My husband and I were in the area and decided to stop simply because of the Yelp reviews, it didn't disappoint! The service was great - we were immediately greeted and our drink orders taken right away. We both ordered the horchata - wow! Such a delicious twist to the already yummy drink. I ordered the mole quesadilla and my husband had a pastor bowl, both delicious, seasoned perfectly and pretty darn close to being authentic Mexican food. This place is a must - parking is limited as is the seating space inside, but worth it. I'll be back!

Waited for 10 minutes at the bar without so much as a hello from the staff here. I understand being busy, but to not even be acknowledged while waiting is pretty rude. I didn't try the food because I tired of waiting and left. Probably won't return.

My mom and I were referred to go to this place for some tacos and so when she was visiting me in Phoenix, we finally went to check it out! We pulled up and were very skeptical by the look of the outside, but we were greeted right away to pick a table. We both got the Cabo Shrimp Taco and a steak taco and it had this amazing fried cheese in it. And the salsa bar was amazing. I think the Cilantro salsa was my favorite. The beans and rice were also to die for. The shrimp in my taco were so delicious. I couldn't get over how amazing this place was. We happened to go for happy hour and got $5 Grapefruit margaritas as well. BEST MEXICAN FOOD EVER. I wish there was one in California. 

P.S- Everyone around us ordered a quesadilla because they are stuffed inside their homemade tortillas and deep fried. Can't wait to go back and try these. 

The service was awesome, too!

i have been to this place a few times now.. in the beginning it was amazing but last time i was a little disappointed.

the salsa bar has lots of great flavors, but the best was the guacamole which used to be free.  now they charge $3.75 for a tiny container..!

the quesa (although tasty) can be VERY greasy.. took it to go last time and it was literally swimming in the container by the time i got it home.

the art on the walls and bathroom doors is lovely and tricks me into liking the place more than i would otherwise, i think.

not bad.. but not good.

This place was ok...

Parking was slim, but there was space on the street. 

It's a nice, friendly place.. small, but welcoming to our large group.

The salsa bar was nice.  There were a lot of different ones to choose from and everyone was able to find ones that they enjoyed. The chips were free (there were some reviews saying they were charged for chips..)

i had the taco/burro combo.. I got the shrimp taco and the gaucho steak burro.  The shrimp had a lot of breading.  It had good flavor, but the shrimp was a little dry. I also found that the steak in my burro was a little dry.  Again, it had good flavor, but i was disappointed in the meat. The grilled squash that came with the plate was good though! 

I decided that I had to try the horchata because of all the reviews.  It was pretty good, but I didn't care for the chunks of fruit.  It was difficult to drink through the straw towards the end, and I ended up wasting 1/4 of my $4 drink... 

Pricing is higher than noted.  My plate was $12ish and the horchata was $4.  After tax and tip, it was over $20.  

All in all, it was a decent meal/experience, but I probably won't go back.
Love the salsa bar with so many different varieties from sweet and fruity to hot and juicy

Diner's Drive-ins and Dives location...  known for their tacos and salsa bar.  Everything was tasty and the prices were good.  Service is basically counter service, but good.  The place is small, but they seem to move quickly.  Don't be surprised with a wait for a table.

Make sure to try as many salsas as you can.  The tacos were very good - I had very high expectations, and while I wasn't blown away, they were very good.

So I went to lunch here on a Friday and the place was full, but then again it isn't all that big. The interior is fairly nice for a Mexican food joint and what first caught my eye was the salsa bar. At least 10 different kind of salsas for the taking. This is a good omen. Gourmet Taco's feels incredibly insincere. It is like when MacDonald's have "a la carte" on the to of their back lit wall menu. It becomes a joke. 

I had the shrimp tacos that comes when ordering some cheesy slur that most surely contains the words 'baja' or 'cabo' or something silly to that nature. I also ordered the horchata to go with my lunch. The order is two decently filled tacos with both double corn tortillas. The shrimp wasn't the long monster that I expected but instead three minor in each taco. This was OK. Then it was filled with some kind of cabbagy mass that was completely raw and tasteless - but would look good on a  picture. This was not OK - tasteless filler is pointless. The horchata was tasty, but way too much ice in the glass. The salsa bar did not disappoint - they have hot and mild and spicy and seasonal, in this case some strawberry salsa that was strangely tangy. But I love the variety. 

I liked the food. Not all of our party did enjoy their meal, but I did. But it is too pricey for Mexican food.. because it isn't that spectacular at all. The price would be the discouragement for me, when it comes to my return factor. I have had better tacos for cheaper. that is the bottom line - but it wasn't bad. Not at all. 

In summary; meal was good but too expensive.

Oh My Goodness!!
Husband is Mexican - we're from Chicago - have NEVER had such fabulous food outside of Mexico City! Were there on vaca and went one night - loved the tacos (the Tinga chicken was SOOOO tasty!) and the salsas are so fun and interesting and tasty!

Had to go back one more time before we left and ordered the DEEP FRIED QUESADILLAS!!! O.M.G. pas deaux - it was AH MAY ZING!!! One of the best fried foods I have ever tasted - and the cheese, and the chicken tinga..... mmmmmmm - 

Booking another flight to Phoenix as I write this....

We waited way too long to check this place out!  I had the Baja Shrimp taco and Fish Taco with rice and beans..... all delicious!   Wifey got the Maztalan taco and we enjoyed sampling almost everything the salsa bar...something for everyone. Will be back soon to try some more!

I love the food here, ans their salsa bar is always kept stocked and clean.  Every time I have visited the restaurant there is a bit of a wait time, but it is worth it.  Portions are pretty well for price of food (which is reasonable).   I live closer to their location in Glendale but will rather drive to this location due to better service, food and cleanliness.

I came here because my coworkers were all talking about how good this place was. I also heard that they had shark tacos that my bf really wanted to try. The place is super small and kind of divey. They have a salsa bar for you to enjoy when you first sit down. The strawberry salsa was my favorite. Sweet but a little bit spicy. They definitely get you on the chips though because there are no free refills like most other places. Another basket of chips is almost $3. I got the chicken mole quesadilla. Their quesadillas are definitely not like your typical quesadilla. It's almost like a deep fried calzone. The portion is huge though, I could only eat half of it. My bf got one shark taco to try and it was kind of disappointing. It tasted like cod and there wasn't very much flavoring. The taco just came with a tiny bit of lettuce and some green sauce. We got the guacamole and it was delicious. They put raisins and some other fruit in it. At first it sounds strange but trust me, it's so good. Wish we saved some chips to eat with it since we ate most of it with the salsa. The service is friendly and the food came out pretty quick. I'm glad we tried it out but don't know if I would be dying to go back.

Food and drinks were amazing..I enjoyed the black mole` taco.  The salsa bar had a variety of flavors and spices...The guacamole was rediculously hot, but yummy!  The service was a little rough, it was very busy and i think they were understaffed.  They forgot to set our table and once served did not come around often to check on us.  If you dont mind waiting and sub par service come check this place out...The good food definitely outweighs the bad service.

If the food and salsa weren't off the hook incredible, I would have given just 1 star.  Apparently I went to LCGTS on a really bad night.  But they pulled off a tasty miracle.  My pal and I went to LCGTS on our way to see Cheech and Chong at the Dodge Theater.  So we were up for some good Mexican food munchies.

We walk in and there is a line... okay no big deal.  BUT there were no forks (we had to eat with spoons and fingers).  There were no napkins, and the salsa bar was bone dry.  I mean the salsa trays looked like they had been licked clean by a starving dog.  They were able to replenish the salsa but they completely ran out of forks.  We got no chips and no drinks.  We had to beg the poor, nice girl who was completely stressed out.  They were a tad understaffed.  It was a "trip".  

But somehow they managed to bring out my dish.... a Chicken Mole burrito and a Carne Asada Steak taco.  OMG were they amazing.  The flavors of those dishes and the flavors of the AMAZING salsa were just super.  The meat in that taco was cooked to perfection.  Crusty bits of steak that had a crunchy sear but were still very tender on the inside.  I didn't mind not having a fork.

While we were there, they LOCKED the door, just like Cheech Marin did in the Vampire den in "From Dusk till Dawn".  We were locked in as prisoners.  Apparently they were closing down at 6:45 p.m. due to being understaffed and not having forks or more salsa.  Luckily, my buddy and I were the last people to be served.  I will definitely go back.
Delish. Cool Salsa bar. Packed.

We were so impressed with this place and so surprised we had never heard of it!

Salsa:
There are something like 20 different salsa to choose from in their salsa bar but our favorite was the salsa mexicana which was nice and garlicky with chopped cilantro. You scoop the salsas into little plastic containers similar to what you'd find in a taqueria but this is definitely a cloth napkin type of place. Luckily, there are free chips with which to try the many salsa so you can pick your favorite before you food arrives. 

Food:
So fresh, warm, and just plain delicious. We split the Santo Plato and Traditional Quesa. The Santo Plato comes with your choice of burro and taco with a side of calabacitas. We chose the fish taco which conveniently came with two pieces of fish and two tortillas so it was like having two tacos! It was traditional fried fish "Baja" style but it was light and crispy instead of greasy and came with a savory white sauce. The La Condesa Veggie burro was filled white Mexican-style rice (but not that orangish "Mexican rice" you see at fast food joints), Oaxaca cheese, mushrooms, spinach, poblano pepper, onions and fresh garlic. The burro is grilled after its assembled which enhanced the mouth feel. Crispy outside, soft inside. The calabacitas were just grilled green Mexican squash, nothing special. The Traditional Quesa was unlike anything I'd ever seen. They're made with a THICK, dense corn tortilla, stuffed with Oaxaca cheese, and then grilled for a nice crunch. These bad boys are HUGE and have so much cheese which made me relieved to be sharing. You have to eat it with a fork and knife but it was amazing with different salsa varieties drizzled on top. 

Drinks:
Try the Horchata! Best we've ever had. They put real fruit and pecans in it. There was some sort of strawberry syrup in the bottom but it was not overly sweet. The serving size is 32oz which was a lot bigger than we were expecting. We didn't get any alcohol but I overheard the guy next to us tell the waitress his margarita was amazing. 

Atmosphere:
Be prepared because this place it TINY! We got there at the right time because when we were leaving all of the 10 or so tables were full. People didn't have room to wait and some turned around and left as soon as they came in and saw how crowded it was. There is an itty bitty bar that a few people chose to wait at. The decor is cute but the custom made chairs were a bit fragile as I had to switch mine out due to the bottom falling out. 

Overall:
We know Mexican food and this may be the best we've ever had. We'll have to go back for a few more visits to be sure but for now we certainly left smacking our lips with the delicious flavors we had just tasted on our lips and on our minds.

The food was amazing, and so many choices. I had a al pastor street taco which is probably one of the best ones I've ever had. I also had the pacific white fish taco, two big pieces of fried fish, very crispy and tasty, and my friend and I shared the poblana quesa quesadilla, very untraditional but so good. You get chips when you sit down and theres a self serve salsa bar with a big variety of all kinds of salsas. Limited seating but we got a table right away. Can't wait to go back!

Worth any wait,  ours was minimal.  Horchata and salsa bar were great highlights! 

Loved the decor and character of the place.  Dia del morte all about including cool mosaic tile art. We walked right up past the bar to look up menus and wait on a table.  No tables available.  I was directed to use the men's room.  Which was decorated yet cluttered with a music stand,  stool,  and supplies.  I couldn't open the slider lock easily and had feared they'd have to break the door down but I got lucky and got out.   By the time I got out,  only a few minutes,  my friend was seated.  Tunes were good,  Even when I couldn't understand the music I was grooving. 

Menu was a bit overwhelming with so many choices.  Got the best horchata ever with strawberries, cantaloupe, and pecans.  It was mammoth. 

Settled in on a fish taco and Mahi Mahi,  both grilled.  They were hot to handle,  and a bit over filled.  Nice because good value,  but the bottom tortillas were soggy. 

Only got two bites of this delishness in,  because I filled up on chips and fun salsas from the salsa bar.  The horchata contributed too. 

The peanut salsa was the hottest,  and the salsa de albor was my first experience with this fruity hot Mexican Chile.  The jicama was nice and refreshing and cooling but very hard to get on the chip as by its nature wasn't saucy.  However the cilantro was too soupy so I could only pour it on.  The pecan wasn't spicy like the peanut and was therefore nice against the heat as well.

So I finally got off my yelpn butt and made it on over to La Condesa for lunch today. I got there around 1045, so I was that creepy taco stalker in the parking lot for about 15 minutes. I ordered teh La Condesa Shrmip Burro and the Oaxacan Mole chicken Taco. As I waited, I was able to check out the 8 or 9 different salsas they had there. Great stuff, I only packed up four. My fave, by a mile, was the creamy cilantro salsa. I wanna bathe in that stuff, like now. My food was ready pretty quick and I was in and out, which is nice.The taco was great, I really liked the flavor in the mole. I decided to add some of the peanut salsa the had, which was pretty good. I do have to say the Burro did fall a bit flat for me. there were tons of ingredients in tehre, but somehow it seemed to be a bit bland without adding any of the salsas to it.
