Kiinda like that girl you see at the club, and y ou get home and...well, you get the picture. It was a good burro, but the shrimp were somehow flavorless and the bacon was non-existent. Not that I'm total food snob but when you tell me there's bacon in that mug, I wanna taste me some bacon. Overall my meal was good, I'm going to go back another day and try some other things on the menu, like the dogfish taco. Two thumbs up for the creativity on the food and the salsas, it's hard to stand out in teh Phoenix Taco/Burro scene.

Nice small restaurant for street tacos. Had the carne asado tacos which are fresh and tasty.

The thing that stands out here is the salsa bar with the different varieties of salsa to choose from. Fresh and home made with a great opportunity to experiment and sample all kinds.

Very small place with old tables and dawn of the dead motif if that is your thing. Service is good but they dont have much to do with you. The parking is limited and may need to park along a side street.

You order at the counter and they bring the food to you. Simple and easy

Recommend to try their tacos if you want real tacos and something different

I went here at about 11:15 today for lunch. There was a line. that had already formed. Its a very small venue, no bathroom, so make sure to wash your hands and do your business before you get there. Only about a dozen or so tables on the floor, and the cashier is also your waitress delivering food to your table. If your expecting great service, forget about it, you focus strictly on the food here. Their is barely any parking. Everyone that seemed to come in was new to this place checking out other patrons food and asking them what it is and how they like it. Im sure they were all fellow yelpers as well considering where this place is and how everyone appeared to be new to this place.

The address is a little confusing with the map being shown on their website. Its off 16th street as the address implies, and the crossroad is Palm and 16th. There is a sign for another business there that says FAT PAD which is easily visible. Blink and you will miss this restaurant. The inside has a lot of cool mexican art. They also have a fresh salsa bar.

Wow this has some very flavorful food. Its not greasy or fatty at all. You can really taste all the ingrediants. I ordered the Dog Fish Tacos, the mahi mahi burrito, and the Carne Asada Taco. Everything was absolutely delish with lots of flavor! I liked the Dog Fish taco best. 

Make sure to get there before noon. They do take a while to make it, so be sure you have the time, especially if they are busy. You can call ahead or fax your order in as well.

I am beyond picky when it comes to Mexican food, having grown up in Phoenix. I eat here weekly since I work down the street. The meats are seasoned perfectly, the salsa bar is amazing (try the creamy cilantro), everything including the guac is fresh and the price is right. Waitstaff is very pleasant. Eat here.

I love this place!!  As other reviewers have pointed out, the salsa bar is insane.  Do yourself a favor and sample each variety.  They're not labeled to indicate how spicy they are, so be forewarned.  The cochinita, gaucho, dogfish, and shrimp tacos are my favorite.
Seriously outstanding tacos.  Not sure why we waited so long to come here.  Will be bringing everyone that comes to visit us in Phoenix here! Thanks!

It is in the weirdest area!  But the food, good!  Had the shrimp and carne asada tacos, the beef was a little tough, but the shrimp tacos were yummy!  Best part, eating all the guacamole they had out, yummy!!  It's worth going back ::-)

Been driving by this place for some time, and finally I decided to try it. I was skeptical at first because the parking isn't very inviting. The restaurant is somewhat small but yet quaint. I was very excited to try all the salsa's but was utterly disappointed when the chips they brought us were hard, stale, and just not suitable for eating. I think they were some of the worst chips I have ever had, I had one.. I requested another basket and they kindly bought another basket of chips but they were the same, Stale, hard and dull. I ordered the Aztec Tinga Taco, and they were very good. The salsa's were all great. The service was great, and the waitress apologized for the chips, and stated that they had ran out and had to buy some etc, etc.. Overall tacos were great for the money, just disappointed with the chips.

We tried this spot last night for dinner. First impressions were not good. The lighting is horrible. The restaurant layout is over crowded and the lack of ambience is just sad. Now with all of that said, the food was delicious! The salsa bar was a lot of fun. We enjoyed trying several types of salsa while we waited for our food. Unfortunately, the waiter did not put our two courses in properly, so after waiting an hour, everything came at once. This was only after we asked about it. The waitress apologized and did comp our beverages. We are our entrees and wrapped up the first course to eat the next day. We will try it again and hopefully they won't be as busy or their kitchen will have their act together.

Their quesas are the bomb.com!  They're very big, so you can totally split one with a friend.  The salsa bar was great and had different varieties of salsas and guacamole.  We went there around 11:30 and it was pretty busy, but that's not surprising for a place that has really good food eh?  I'll definitely be back to try more! :)

Very, very good "real" Mexican restaurant. This is not in the high-income part of Phoenix, but certainly the area is safe. The restaurant is positioned between a piñata shop & an empty store, but you cannot miss the signage! Everything that our group of five ordered was excellent. I had the chicken quesadilla; it was not like any other quesadilla I have ever had, with the shell a unique experience. Great place for informal dining with a different version of Mexican food.

Over hyped I think. To me the tacos actually lacked flavor. Had a combo of 3 different types and thought they were all somewhat bland and lacked real creativity. Basically its taco truck food (not a bad thing) at probably triple the price (a bad thing). Now the salsa bar is awesome and this is where this place shines. Lots of unique flavors and it is clean and well presented. The chef/cook came out to check on orders so i think they care but the price does not justify the food....

La Santisima is a taco oriented Mexican restaurant located in a blue collar neighborhood of Phoenix, which offers an impressive happy hour menu and a delicious variety of tacos.

I ate dinner at La Santisima on a Thursday. I arrived around five and was seated quickly. I did not receive any service quickly though. The restaurant was clearly understaffed. It took a long time to get a drink, a bowl of chips, and my ultimately my check. It was never clear who my server was either.

The food was excellent, but the service was overwhelmed. I would try La Santisima again, but hopefully the service will be better next time.

I'll echo the sentiments of other reviewers that the service here is horrendous; staff is completely rude and aloof. 
Phoenix has tons of great mexican joints, no need to frequent this one. Overlook the hype and take your business to a resturaunt that actually appreciates your business.

Lots of options, cool/hip smallish place, great vibe....

Salsa bar killed it, and service was quick.  

Just what you want.
Slow service, but we'll worth the wait! El pastor street tacos are AMAZING!! Salsa bar is also very good with some really unique salsas. Rice and beans are nothing to brag about.

Recently some of my colleagues from Spain were visiting and on their last night in town, I offered to take them to dinner.   They immediately told me that they NEEDED to have authentic Mexican food and they really wanted tacos.   After searching through pages and pages of Yelp and Google, and polling my friends on facebook...I finally chose La Condesa over many strong recommendations of Los Dos Molinos, Barrio Cafe, Aunt Chiladas, and many more....   Now, I realized that never having been there myself before I was taking a bit of a risk...but my fellow Yelpers surely couldn't lead me astray, right?!   

Happily, they did not!   The food was delicious.  The four of us all ordered different kinds of tacos and we all loved our dishes!  I had the Mayan Cochinita Pibil Taco, which I DEFINITELY recommend!  The flavor was amazing! a little heat, a little citrusy....mmm mmm mmm!!   Two of my co-workers had the Carne Asada and they both raved about it the whole way home. we all shared an Horchata for dessert -- wow!  very good too!  It's a big drink, so I do recommend sharing - it's totally worth it!    Their bellies were content before the long flight back to Espana!   

The portions were good.  Not too big, not too small.  Two tacos were filling - I always like to know what to expect.  Nobody had any leftovers, so I think the portions were just right.  

Of course, the salsa bar is a key feature of this place.  I think we only made it through 5 or 6 kinds and I liked them all.   The mango one was one of my favorites, which is a surprise b/c I'm not usually a huge fan, but I loved the sweet and spicy combo - it was done just right.   

I've already sent the link to my foodie brother in law - the whole fam will be visiting for the holidays, we will definitely be going back!   This will be a MUST visit place for my future recommendations!  

Yeah!

We were looking for some mexican food and I stumbled upon this place.  What a treat!  The food was really good, especially the Quesas and Tacos.  They have a great salsa bar as well and Real Coke.

The parking is a little tough and we had to wait 20 minutes for a table, but the food taste and quality was well worth the wait.

Tacos are authentic! Salsa bar is awesome. There can be a bit of a wait but when you get to your table they already have chips there waiting for you ! Burritos / burros are huge and they grill the tortilla, nice touch. Servers are awesome but a little short staffed.
Try the tamarindo margarita!!

Wow! What a great surprise, You can definitely taste the quality in the food! Great selection of salsa and the menu has a variety for all. The good isn't over done to the point where you can't finish your plate. I will most definitely be coming back here.

The place is a little small so we had to wait a bit for a table. The food is fantastic. 

Steak asada tacos were perfect. Nice chunks of meat with shredded cabbage. 

We also had the black mole tacos. Also outstanding. 

The selection of self-serve sauces is the standout.  They have maybe 20 sauces for you to sample. The variety and quality of the sauces is excellent and should satisfy any palate. 

If I'm ever back in Phoenix I will definitely be back.
I've been all over the web to find out how much you charge for your fancy tacos. Can't find your prices..code for toooo high for me. Sorry.

Came here with a party of 10 and had an awesome, awesome meal. The waitress was so on top of things, and made sure that everyone had drinks (relatively) quickly, and always had full water glasses. (I say relatively because one margarita took a while and it took a few tries to get my coke, but again, we were a party of 10, so it wasn't a big deal). 

While we waited for our food, we sampled the salsa bar, which has 16 flavors of salsa. The waitress brought baskets of chips as soon as we sat down. Each one tasted so different, and while we didn't love all of them, we had so much fun sampling and comparing the different flavors. 

I had the fish tacos, which were awesome. Everyone on yelp raves about them, and they were totally right. So flavorful and the tortilla held up well. I also had a quesadilla - most places make their quesadillas with flour tortillas, so I was ecstatic to see that they made theirs with corn (extra points for being gluten-free-friendly!). They let me sub out the pork for the steak, and the quesadilla did not disappoint - stuffed with cheese, steak, and some veggies, this this was awesome. 

Wish I didn't live so far, because I would absolutely become a regular here. 

Good for: cheap dinner, night out with friends, date night, any time you're feeling hungry!

Sometimes, Yelp is right on.  I was looking for a great Mexican restaurant in the neighborhood to take my wife to (it was date night).  This place had far more stars than most, so we gave it a go.

Upon entering (we visited on First Friday last month) it was so loud that it was like bombs going off.  The decor was unusual and had an interesting botanica vibe going on.  Service was a bit slow but they were so packed that I wasn't surprised.

Their salsa bar had more flavors than I've ever seen at a restaurant anywhere--and I've been to a lot of Mexican Restaurants.  As for the food itself, there was nothing "traditional" about it, but everything was so bursting with incredible flavor that I was savoring every bite.

Holy sh*t, that was good.  My burrito was loaded with CHUNKS of marinated steak--not ground, not shredded, but chunks.  I was blown away.  Next time, there's a SHARK burrito on the menu that I can't wait to taste.

If you're in the mood for something "traditional", I still point people to Mi Patio in Phoenix.  However, if you're looking for something other than the same old Mexican taste, may I recommend this landmark.  It's just a few blocks north of McDowell on your right hand side.  You won't regret it.  The place is small and can sometimes be packed with noisy gringos, but the taste is unforgettable.

I was in Phoenix on a one day business trip and found this place on yelp. I'm glad I did. The restaurant is small at first but has a variety of home made salsas at the salsa bar. I didn't get a chance to try them all but the ones I had were very good. They have really good service with a friendly server and prompt service. I had the mahi fish taco which was grilled and I also had the chicken taco. Both were excellent with the rice and beans. They give you soft drinks in a to go cup so that was convenient to take with me in the 100 degree weather. 

The food was really good and was better than similar tacos in CA. I'm glad I chose this place for my one meal in AZ before my flight home! One more thing the price was very reasonable and the location was only a couple miles from the Sky Harbor rental car center. Will go back if I'm in AZ.

I've had nothing but good experiences with the food at La Santisima, and minor frustrations with a particular attendant can be easily overlooked when the cuisine was that good. 

My real love for this venue is from their simple, lovely drinks--including the best horchata I've had in Phoenix.  Chopped fruit and walnuts? Are you kidding me? Delicious.
I would say what a great find, but it's already been found.  Some of the best Mexican food I've ever had... And I've had a lot. Definitely give this place a try.

Do yourself a favor and start eating here (if you're not already a fan).

#1. Hands down best salsa bar on the PLANET!!!

If I can help it, I eat here at least 2x/week. I literally order the same thing every single time and it never gets old: veggie tacos and horchata, both of which have ruined any other Mexican restaurant for me... nothing comes even close to their glorious flavors, and it's always fun picking and mixing the different salsas with the food.

The super chill and friendly staff and unique atmosphere are also worth mentioning.

Seriously, I hesitate to leave Phoenix because of this place.
Oh, I dream about the salsas here... I love all the different combinations, and could very easily make a meal with those alone. Love the tacos and the horchata as well.

Amazing Mexican food and sauces!  I never have experienced such diverse foods. They have pulled recipes from all over Mexico and excel at reproducing some amazing food. If you love Mexican food you must go here. Their salsa bar is like no other. Pecan salsa, peanut sauce etc. And they have a good tequila selection!

We were taken aback by the decor, waitstaff, the patrons, and classic rock playing, because it appeared filled with hipsters,  an all male staff, and an interior with a very confused identity.   HOWEVER, I will be returning, and I will tell you why.....
       1. Salsa bar, simply delicious.  All of them. From mild, to smoky, to hot, there's a peanut and pecan salsa, jicama, guacamole, Pico de gallo, and several more. 
       2. Great menu choices, not your typical American/Mexican options.  
       3. The street tacos! !! We chose Al Pastor,  Carne Asada, y Cochinita Pibil with rice and beans. Uhhhhh-mazing!  

From a white girl who used to never eat Mexican, who is now married to a Mexican.....
I was totally impressed. My husband said 4 stars, because he's got a picky palette. 
Thoroughly enjoyed my meal! Can't wait to return for a Horchata, and to try the Mole!

This was a great find! We enjoyed the homemade horchata which was bursting with flavors like cinnamon, nutmeg, fruit and nuts.  Equally as delish was the guacamole. This is not your typical guacamole. It was more chopped than mashed and had dried cranberries in it. Very tasty. I had the cabo tacos and the beer batter was too thick for my liking, but my fiancé ordered a chicken taco and it was much better. When I come back again, I will try non-beer battered tacos!

I have to admit that it is a great restaurant. Its service attitude is not only very friendly,the taste of food is also very delicious. The environment is so clean that I have a warm feeling. I recommend you go but DON'T be too late because it might take you some time to line up.

Nothing more than average at best. Other than the Awesome and extensive salsa bar , it was pretty mediocre..especially for the 4 1/2 stars they have. 

We had two burritos and they were decent! You could taste the individual ingredients and the vegetables tasted fresh, which I liked but it wasn't a BURRITO. It was more like a wrap you would get from Whole Foods. Not to mention, it was way, way, way too small. It was similar in size to a McDonalds snack wrap. I legitimately left lunch at La Santisima and had to get a bite at another place...Mexican joints are supposed to fill you up!

Either way, the place has a lot of potential and it could be very good but I wasn't a fan.

If you've ever been to Lucha Libre in San Diego, it's very similar in style, just not as good in my opinion.

Very small dining area - we arrived at 5:30 and it was full and by 6:30 10 people were waiting - had street tacos they were good - salsa had a good selection but they weren't all great - service was average very friendly but not proactive - better than average - won't be going back - too many other great choices in the area

All of these years I've been living downtown just down the street from here and I haven't been until today. Everything here is amazing. Amazing. Amazing. Except the service. In their defense, the restaurant does warn you that the dining area has recently expanded and they are relying on a small kitchen. Too bad our food and drinks were out right on time. Our server was hard to find and not very friendly. That's a shame. 

Now that we've gotten that bad stuff out of the way let's talk about the fun stuff. First, the salsa bar. Oooo girl. There's something like 15 salsas and sauces here. They're all amazing but I'd recommend the pecan salsa. You do get a free bowl of chips, but it is 2.70 for another one. A little disappointed about that since there's so much salsa to try but that's okay. 

Second, dranks! We ordered the blue devil margarita, which was full of fruit and sweetness almost like an amazing marg-sangria hybrid. My table also got a huge michelada and some other regular margaritas. All were absolutely delish. 

Last, but not least, those tacos tho!!! There are just too many to list here but out table ordered some of the best looking ones, mahi al pastor, baby shark, tiger shrimp, battered and fried avocado, cauliflower, and Barbacoa. The Barbacoa was certainly the least exotic but my favorite. The tortilla was softly fried and just tooooo good. The vegetarian and vegan choices were numerous if that's your kind of thing. Much appreciated to see a restaurant that serves lots of options for those with dietary restrictions other than just another damn salad! 

Get here now because you are missing one of Phoenix's greatest hits!

I absolutely adore this restaurant and thought it was time I gave a review. The Santisima shrimp tacos are to die for - simple as that. Everything I've ever had here has been flavorful and uniquely delicious, and the homemade salsa bar is the icing on the cake. The only criticism I can offer is that they're a bit on the slow side in terms of bringing out food, particularly for to-go orders if you don't call ahead, but I can't blame them for being busy or successful!
Absolutely amazing tacos. This place has the best tacos in town. Great value great quality. Very very impressed. Can't wait to go there again.

I was so hyped on my way here, I brought a coworker to order for the whole store. It was so busy, everything looked great. I said I've never been here and I'm starving. He ordered for me and it literally ended up being a beef burrito with only retried beans and nothing else. I'm sure everyone else enjoyed there's but man was that confusing
Omg I love this place! They have the best tacos and salsa bar. Oh and the humongous horchata is to die for!

I read alot of reviews and had very high expectations of this place. The food was good but nothing that made me say "WOW". Out of the 4 tacos that I tried, the CABO shrimp taco was the best and would return for it.  The salsas and chips are a good way to down down some beers before your meal. I'd say give La Santisima a try and make your own decision.

Been here a few times now and this place is amazing.  Like many, I am in love with their salsa bar which has at least a dozen different options for dunking your chips in.  While I wish they would provide bigger containers to fill your salsa in, it is meant to be a sampler and not a meal.  The choices are great to have and everyone will find something they like.  What keeps me coming back are the amazing tacos.  I order the shrimp and the mahi fish street tacos each time and they are some of the best in town.  Really great flavor and healthy portions.  Can't wait to eat again!!

A few particulars - this is a very small little place on 16th with mostly street side or residential parking, no actual lot.  During peak times, good luck finding a seat and the line at the register where you must order will leave you waiting a bit.  It's worth it for the taste, but just be prepared.

WOW!!!!  Arizona already has the best Mexican food around, but this place is truly a gem.  All the sauces are homemade and present a wide spectrum of flavors.  My favorite unique items from the salsa bar were the peanut salsa (spicy, most likely has habaneros in it), pecan salsa (similar but very mild with interesting flavor), strawberry salsa, and jicama salsa.  Everything was incredibly fresh.  After sampling everything from our group, I would recommend getting one of their mole dishes (the mole is stellar) or the mahi mahi fish tacos.  Also, their house made guacamole was amazing; very unique and chunky with lots of different veggies in it.  I will be back again and again.

After moving from San Diego, CA I found the best Mexican food here. Vegetarian/Vegan is just awesome. Food quality is great, clean and variety of sauces excellent. They just need to improve their setting chairs. It's very old and foam coming out.

Great  salsa bar
Gaucho taco and burrito are the best
And the Mahi Mahi 
Horchata is also pretty good
Definitly coming back

One of the best Mexican restaurants I've been to. The taco bar was awesome...we went crazy over it! Special mention for cilantro, pecan, guacamole salsa. Th e main course was also really good. Tried the fish taco and I wasn't dissapointed and hubby was happy wi th his chicken taco. Portions are generous and best part about this place is that they have a lot of options for vegetarians.we will be coming back here for sure :)
Great tacos.  Burrito was good but bit salty.   Doesn't look like much from outside but we had great lunch there.

This place is awesome, and I am deciding is my favorite Mexican food restaurant (restaurants-both locations are pretty much the same) in the Phoenix area. I have eaten here (and at the Glendale location) a total of 4 times, and each experience has left me wanting to come back. 

The salsa bar is the best I've experienced with an amazing variety of tastes, fresh ingredients, and mild to moderate spice. Order extra chips straight away if you love chips and salsa.

The food is outstanding-from their pibil to their arbol, to their beans and rice. They use very high quality fresh ingredients with KILLER flavor and spice. While there is a very strong Mexican feel to the restaurants (no gringo influence that I noticed-Thank you), there is also a modern feel to their menu. So I've started out with the more popular dishes/recipes, but I am excited to try out some of their other offerings that appear more modern.

Their margaritas (I've only had the house) are the best, period. End of sentence.

Finally, you should be aware that the physical spaces are pretty different. I'm going to guess the owners are young and without the resources to afford something more expensive. But don't be put off by the space. I love that they have more modern art, and the food more than makes up for any misgivings one might have about the space.

If you really love Amazing Mexican food, you must try this place. I can't imagine you will be disappointed.

PS, I don't think their prices are reasonable/not expensive.

Damn, you want some awesome tacos, burros, quesadillas, or tortas?! This is your place! Ever since Guy Fieri stepped foot in this place, it gets really busy now. It's a small place, so expect a wait unless you go during off times (avoid lunch and dinner). The salsa bar is incredible, so many different variety of salsas from cilantro, pecan, to a delicious jicama or a bomb pico de gallo. The quesadillas aren't your typical ones, they fry them entirely that it almost looks like a empanada/quesadilla hybrid but they're so good! It's true about what they say about the horchata, it's the best I've tasted. They put pecans and chopped fruit in the horchata giving it some extra flavor a but its so delicious. My favorite tacos are the Shark tacos! Try them! Only reason why I give them 4 stars is because the service is alright. Sometimes they are not staffed adequately and it takes forever to get your order in, other than that, it's a great Mexican food joint!

Love this place! Not super close to my house but always worth the drive, or a fun place to stop by if I'm headed to the Ranch Market. You have to be looking for it because it's in a tiny strip mall and could be easily passed up. I love the decorations inside it's Dia de los Muertos themed and all the art work is super cool. They have a salsa bar with tons of different salsas you can try out which is fun and gives you a good variety of spice and flavors (try the strawberry one!). All of the tacos I've had have been delicious but if you do get the plate with 2 tacos and rice and beans you're going to be really full or have half of your plate to take home. I haven't been for the happy hour tacos or whatever it is so I will have to make it by 6 one day for the deal. Highly recommend this place.
Great food, very slow service.  I can't imagine what it would be like if they were busy.
Husband introduced me to this place yesterday and I was totally impressed. Donot pass up the cilantro or pecan salsas!
EXCELLENT!! Regular sized tortillas, really authentic and tasty! $3.99/taco. 2 Taco Plate  w/rice & beans $8.97 plate.

I've had some delicious Mexican food here in Phoenix.  But this place trumps all.  A stocked salsa bar, delicious fish tacos.  Seriously, what isn't good here?  I'm going to keep going here and trying a different menu item every time just to see if something is subpar here.  I'll put my savings on it that there isn't a single thing that isn't good here.  I'd probably go here just for the chips and salsa if Mexican food isn't your thing, but your coworker or spouse or some guy or girl you're going on a date with insists on La Santisima.  Just go.  No excuses.  Nothing.  And order the chips and salsa.  Try every salsa.  I don't care how strange pecan salsa or strawberry salsa sounds...trust me, it won't disappoint.
Customer service sucks!!! Waited 15mins just to get the menu. Food is good tho

It's a small location but HUGE in flavor. 
Make sure you try the quesadillas with carne asada.

The wait can vary due to its small size. I have waited for almost an hour. It was definitely worth it.
Best gourmet tacos around with really interesting flavors. Salsa bar is so good. I crave the pecan salsa!!
this place was ok not as good as people make it seem one thing I like is salsa bar. dislike the location.

I can't believe I haven't written a review for La Condesa yet.  I have never been disappointed here.  Ever.  

Here is the deal:  

-you start with a side of chips.  And then you get to feast on the humongous salsa bar.  My favorites are the pecan (creamy, thick, and with a kick at the end), cilantro (thinner but delicious), and the tamarindo (sweet and spicy).  Sadly, the tamarindo one seems to be quite elusive and is not always available.  You could spend hours trying all the different salsas.  I agree though with Iain, the peanut was the weak link.

-next comes the real food.  I have only had the tacos, but I imagine everything to be of the same quality.  So these tacos come with double tortillas to hold all the ingredients.  These aren't skimpy by any means.  Two should be sufficient for most people.  The Cabo Shrimp is amazing.  Huge shrimp beer battered with a creamy sauce on top.  The chicken mole taco was also great with that special chocolately flavor to it.  Today, I tried to Mayan Cochinita taco and it was stuffed to the brim with tender as can be pork.  I have had the rice and beans before with a combo and I would say the beans are better than the rice.  Though in my opinion after four or so visits, it's best to come enjoy the chips and salsa and then indulge in two tacos.

This place is really hard to find, but if you find Palm and McDowell, it's right there with a few parking spots along the street.

If you like tacos, you need to come here.  It's just that simple.

My wife and I found this place when our friends moved to the area. We love it! It's small and a little cramped but the people who run the place ( I believe it's family-owned) are always pleasant to us. Being Caucasian, this isn't always the case when we go into other Mexican restaurants. I love El Goucho Burro. The salsa bar is fantastic. I like that they bring you a glass bottle (about a liter) of water at the beginning of the meal. My wife is pregnant so we usually go a little early so we don't have to worry about seating but when normal dinner hours role around the place gets pretty packed. Great food - my mouth is watering as I write this. 

The could probably splurge to fix their front door. It does slam when people go in and out.
Steak tacos are awesome. ..so is salsa bar! Make sure you come by early, for no wait.

I'm visiting from San Diego where we have the best Mexican food . The menu , I didn't really get so I ordered the soup which was great ! A little bit of direction on where to order would be good . The line was long the people in front of me didn't know where to order, they just passed me a menu . I stood in line hoping that that was what I was supposed to be doing . My star rating is for the salsa bar , I'm very impressed. It's hard to find places that offer a hot salsa

Really awesome tacos here. I ordered the black mole and the conchinita pibil tacos. One of each and a steak queso. I didn't expect everything to be so big so I really over did myself. The queso I figured was like a quesadilla but it really isn't anything like that. Closest description is a calzone sized gordita. And not the taco bell version. The cheese was gooey and the undercooked parts of the masa were delicious. It was awesome. I broke out the plastic utensils and went to town. Daunting none the less. But I managed to put down half of it before the coma kicked in 

The mole taco was delicious. The chicken was sliced and covered in red onion. The sauce was spicy and not sweet at all. And the whole thing melted in my mouth. The corn taco shells are soft and made to order. The conchinita pibil taco was full of flavor and dripped juices all over the basket. Delicious. 

The horchata is unbelievable. Full of fruit and pecans as well as cinnimon and nutmeg.

the salsa bar is epic. there was at least 12 different salsas to try. the cilantro was really good. and i normally hate raw cilantro because i burp it. but this was excellent and really brought out the flavor of my food. also the strawberry salsa was hot with a hint of sweet and freshness. and the salsa peanut was very tasty. very. very.

I'm buying a bike just to ride here.  A lowerider bike with two 20's in a trailer. So I can rock all the way there.

for now condesa....you are in my top 10.

Stopped by for a quick lunch - the salsa bar was superb. Lots of selection - none were very hot though including the "de arbol". It took a while for the server to take my order and even longer to get a drink of water. I I ordered the Sonoran Arrecheta tacos and they were delicious - basically carne asada with cabbage. The server let my food sit in the window for a while and never came back around to fill my water. So because the food was ok but the service was terrible on many fronts it gets a two star review.

So recent trip to Phoenix and I was craving Mexican food.  Turned to YELP and they pointed us towards this little gem.  Uber took us out there....ummmm a kind of sketchy area but what the heck.  Put our name in and waited about 45 minutes to get seated (place is small). Once seated we ordered margaritas and had chips with the amazing salsa bar!  There have to be 30 salsas freshly prepared.....from mild to OMG that's hot.  My favorite was the Pecano......sooo yummy. 

        Ordered food and I chose the Mole (Black Oaxacan Mole) in burrito form.   I will say that was a damn good Mole.....probably in my top 2 that I have had.  Burrito was big and I love that they make the tortilla crispy by flattening the burrito on the flat top.  Wow soooo good. Came with rice and beans.  A wonderful plate for sure.  

       So if you go it's tiny.....there will be a wait BUT it is sooooo worth it.  I'm from San Diego so I do know great Mexican food and this was GREAT.  Inexpensive as well.  Give them a shot.....you won't be disappointed.
Fish tacos were amazing but two waiters for a jam packed restaurant. No bueno. Horchata was as nasty as it the name sounds.

Salsa bar had so many delicious choices and flavorful options that I was beside myself with excitement! The street tacos were so tasty and unique flavors has me come my back for more!!! Can't wait for my next trip back to this restaurant!!!

Really good Mexican food. Very friendly service. Couple of things you should know. 1- you don't just sit down and wait for order. You need to go to cashier and place it then it will be brought to you. 2- park on the side of the building, easier to get in and out. 3- make use of the salsa bar. Very good and probably different from what you've had in the past. Food was very good and had great flavor. I did order a drink that took a long time to come out but the manager gave it to me on the house. Can't complain. No big deal and the mint drink was delicious. We enjoyed this restaurant
This place is delicious. Everything tasted fresh, service was great and tons of salsas to choose from. This is my go to spot when I'm near downtown!

Great little gem for authentic Mexican food tucked away in a small building on 16th Street.  They have great service, a comfortable atmosphere and an amazing salsa bar! We tried the smoked Marlin and El Gaucho tacos. Yummy!
Another hidden treasure in the valley of the sun. I went there for lunch and it was packed,  food was great as always.
The tacos are excellent and the salsa bar is fabulous.  Need to continue to go and the staff is friendly and helpful.

The praise here is warranted. This is the best Mecican food possibly in the world. 

Service and ambience are awesome. 
You can tell that the salsa bar is clearly insane. I actually wasn't a huge fan of any, but I combined the peanut with some other chipotle salsa and the tomatillo with another green salsa and made two amazing new salsas.

The food is indescribable. You can only understand if you eat it. I've had the carne, pibil, pastor, and mole tacos. The only one I didn't like was mole but it's an acquired taste and I think if you like mole you'll love it. The beans are also super flavorful and the rice is pretty good. It's closer to an Asian fried rice than the Mexican rice I've had, but I'm not complaining! 

The horchata was also like nothing I've ever had. It had cantaloupe, pecans, And strawberries and somehow it still worked out?? You have to have it if you come here.

I have absolutely nothing bad to say about this place except that I wish they delivered to where I live (NY) hahaha

We recently moved to Phoenix and were excited to try all the new culinary wonders around us. Unfortunately we found this place first and were HOOKED! We have been there 3 times in the past week. The mole is delicious as is the Aztec Tinga Burrito. Even the veggie taco is scrumptious and is not missing meat in the least! The horchata is really, really good as well. Keep it up!
Heaven,  the way Mexican food should be! Dogfish tacos are the bomb! Salsa and guacamole are great too.  If you want true tacos this place is a must.
Had the mole burrito (and of course mucho chips and salsa). Have nothing negative to say at all. Definitely more of a quick, cheap, and easy type place.
Simple, best shrimp taco's! Love this place!

Just. Brilliant.  This place puts Barrio Cafe to shame.  There isn't a bad thing on the menu.  The food is amazing, the atmosphere is warm and fun, and the service is spot-on.  Oh, and unlike Barrio, the prices are very reasonable.  

Forget the Barrio Cafe hype, THIS place is "The real deal."

The Guisados of Phoenix. 

Order the smoked Marlin tacos they are amazing. You will easily forget that you are eating fish. 

The salsa bar selection can be a bit overwhelming. You want to try everything but at the same time are afraid to because you don't want to make the wrong taco salsa combination. Ahh the paradox of choice. 

Horchata lovers will be enticed to order the house Horchata which goes for $3.99. The specialness of that drink all float on top in the form of pecans, diced cantaloupe, and strawberries. A girl walked in solely to order the Horchata to go.

Food was very good, actually. The only thing I didn't care for was that the salsa bar wasn't very full, and they didn't pay much attention to it. They were busy though, so it wasn't a deal breaker. I still enjoyed my food, though.
If "10" were an option, I would have picked that as a rating. This place was off the charts!  Highly recommend the Spicy Margarita. Oh, and bring an appetite.

Best Mayan Cocinita Pibil this side of the Border!! I've been coming to this place since they served tacos on wax paper in plastic baskets, and though the atmosphere has changed, the food has not. Solid menu, great salsa bar, delicious albeit expensive margaritas, and very friendly staff in a cozy, genuine atmosphere. Be prepared to wait -this place is small, with only a handful of tables, but very worth the wait!
Went here for lunch - it was packed but service was quick and we were able to share a table with another group. Taco selection is excellent. Highly recommended.

This is the first time I have tried horchata, and it was delicious. I love the cinnamon taste of it. They serve the drink in a plastic cup, so you can conveniently take it togo. 

Before the main course, they give out complimentary chips you can munch on. The chips are quality chips - they're not the thin ones like from Rubio's. The best part is the salsa bar! They have a wide selection. Watch out for the extra spicy ones. I'm definitely returning to this cute hole in the wall place for good tacos and horchata.  

A heads up that parking in front of the restaurant is limited.

I ordered the el pastor and carne asada tacos, and they were great. The wife got the shrimp tacos. They had great flavor, but the shrimp was a little small with a lot of batter. Unfortunately the batter became a little soggy and diminished the great plate. Overall, good food. The freshly made horchata was the most amazing drink I have had in years.....a must have every single visit. The dinning room area is really small, few seats which means it fills up fast. Service was mediocre, not a very personable experience.

I can't believe I haven't reviewed this place.  Shocking.  I LOVE this place.
Their quesadillas are doughy cheesy heaven.  HEAVEN.
Their tacos are the stuff dreams are made of.
Their salsa bar proof that there is a god.
Well, that may be much, but still, awesome place.
And guess what kiddies? They finally have beer!
Decor is nice, room is a bit small to contain all this awesomeness though.  Its cozy.
let me recommend  the Mayan Cochinita Pibil Taco.  That pork, tender, so very very tender.  Amazing in the quesa as well.
The dogfish shark and shrimp are great too. 
I haven't been disappointed yet actually.
Order one of everything! (maybe two of the pork)

Popped in here over the Labor Day weekend after reading the Yelp Reviews.  One word....WOW!

The tortilla chips were fresh and not soaked in grease, the 20+ salsa's were fresh and flavorful, the burritos and street tacos were some of the best we ever had.  To top it off, our server was wonderful.

It's a small place with 20 or so tables, if their busy I urge you to wait it out.  They turn the tables quickly and it will be with the wait!

My friends love this place (seriously one of them has gone there like 10 times within a few months) and I have to say, it was pretty good. I love their salsas. There is this one, I can't remember the name of it, but it was so delicious.  If I remember correctly, The peanut one was not tasty at all. Their tacos was unique and tasty. I also got a burrito, it was good too. It is a little pricey, $$ for sure.

Everything here is delicious.
Best salsa bar in town. The pecan salsa is my favorite. Mexicana and pico are second favorites.
Horchata is a must.
Beware the cheezieness of the quesos!

Wife and I came during vacation and arrived about 10 minutes after opening. There were already 3 parties there at 11am. Promising.

Orders were taken at the cashier, then sat down with a number. The menu was a little confusing with all these caveats and pricing schemes, but at the end of the day, we got some tacos and we liked them.

*** FOOD ***
They allow you to create "meals", so we got two - one with 2 gourmet tacos and another 3 street tacos. 

Cochinita Pibil Street Taco (5/5)
Mouthwatering and delicious. Pork was super juicy and well worth it. You'll see this in many other reviews and there's a reason for that. 

Al Pastor Street Taco (2/5)
I have a habit of always trying my favorite meat everywhere even if the reviews suggest otherwise. Wasn't really a fan, flavor was a bit lacking. 

Baja Sur Dogfish Shark Gourmet Taco (4/5)

Cabo Shrimp Gourmet Taco (4/5)


*** DRINK ***
I have two categories of Mexican places. Places that serve horchatas and places that don't. (The latter contends with Taco Bell.) However, living on the east coast most of my life, I haven't seen anything other than a normal horchata... I had a pleasant surprise here.

Fruit & Pecan Horchata (5/5) 
Topped with strawberries, pecans, and a healthy dose of cinnamon, this had enough body (i.e., not watered down) to take on the sweetness delivered by the fruit and still taste like an horchata. It was novel and delicious. Highly recommended.

*** BOTTOM LINE ***
Check it out. It's worth it. Get an horchata. And one to go.

We tried this place due to yelp.   We were impressed with the atmosphere as it has beautiful art hangings and the place is clean.  I ordered the guacho burrito and the horchata due to the yelpster's recommendations. I usually don't go for beef so I wasn't crazy about the burrito, but it was good.   I was freaking crazy about the Horchata though!  I am a salsa snob so it takes a lot to impress me.   Rule number one - it must cause burn or don't call it salsa.   The seven chiles was so good that there wasn't much left at the salsa bar.   What was left, I took!  Second best salsa was the salsa peanut!  It was creamy, hot, flavorful and the best salsa peanut I have ever had!  So happy that they serve real salsas. My only recommendation for them would be to improve on the chips.   The chips are a bit thin, but cover them with salsa and all will be alright. When in Phoenix-go to this place.   It's a bit small, but hang in there and grab a seat and set your tongue on fire then cool it down with the horchata!

Lunchtime is very hard to find a seat, but once you do you're treated with a great selection of unique and well-known Spanish staples. Worth the drive for lunch or dinner if you're not from the area, check out the shark tacos!

I went there for the first time with family and friends last Saturday. We all got something different and delicious. The salsa bar was really fun to explore and we ended up sampling all the different salsas. The guacamole was delicious and chunky and you could see all the fresh ingredients - no fillers here. 

There were so many different burritos and tacos to try and you could even make things into bowls. While not everyone in our party was a vegetarian, we had two and I'm vegan. They had multiple menu items for both, which was amazing and extremely rare for an authentic Mexican restaurant. I tried the cauliflower taco and Gandhi taco (black beans and more) and they were delicious!

We'll be back again to continue exploring the menu.

I'm so disappointed and sad.  Saw this place on Check Please and saw that the Yelp! reviews were raving, but I can't give a great review. 

1.  Service - poor.  Had to ask for a menu, way too long of a wait time for every.thing., did not get attention I expected, such as a water refill..., had to ask about my food (which conveniently "just finished", but it had been sitting based on the cool temperature of the food).  Literally there for over an hour on 1 plate order.  

2.  Food - mediocre.  The rice was good.  The tacos were nothing special.  The salsa bar is impressive, especially the pecan salsa, but unfortunately there is only so much salsa and chips you can eat.  Plate was less than $10, but I wanted gourmet tacos.

3.  Atmosphere - not enough room.  Someone actually took my tot's seat when we went to the bathroom...?

I'd like to assume this just wasn't my day...
Off the charts delicious and menu is extensive and unique. Best occixicana tacos ever. Can't wait to come back.

Salsa Bar is still on point. I feel like with the expansion its not as cozy and the music did not match the restaurant any more. Food was still great and the Horchata is still MVP. Service was still great, I just personally enjoyed the place when it was smaller. The air conditioning was a bit to cold even though it was 115 out! All in all not a bad place to grab a bite.

Great sign.... Um couple of the salsas were ok.... Chips were spot on...Service was great! Food not so much. I think there trying too hard to be like barrio cafe and honestly fall short. Guy Fieri was too nice. If you like a gringo taco u will love it. I prefer real flavor and authenticity.

Great service- server was friendly and attentive. Small place, will probably have to wait if you could at a typical busy lunch or dinner time. Food was on point, even a few options for vegetarians! Good sized portions, not overly pricey. Love having the salsa bar there!! The jicama drink was similar to a berry juice, was a little too sweet for my liking but once it was watered down a little, it was delicious. Will definitely come back here next time!

Warning : this place WILL knock your socks off so either wear flip flops or proceed cautiously with your toes curled.   Really can't go wrong with any of their tacos. Probably my favorite is the LA Santissima specialty taco with the toasted cheese on top. The shrimp taco is also really good.   Their burritos are delicious. Salsa bar has huge selection and some very unique flavors. Beans and rice are also top quality. Prepare to leave absolutely stuffed because good luck holding yourself back from eating their generous portions. And after it's all said and done make sure you try their horchata (perfect end to a fantastic meal!)

Food quality is incredible. The flavors are exceptional! They are very busy but despite that the service is still very fast and efficient. Margaritas are delightful as well; we will definitely be back!

I saw 450 plus reviews and almost 5 star rating. Well here is another 5 star. The menu is a little overwhelming at first. So I tried the Cabo Shrimp taco. Amazing. Then the smoked marlin taco. More amazing. Then the tinc a chicken taco. OMG. The salsa bar is extensive all made from scratch. I tried six of them and they were all terrific.  The salsa peanut and salsa strawberry really stood out.
Great food and service. Huge salsa bar with so many options. Will definitely be back many times!

As many have mentioned, this place is freakin fantastic.  I vote for La Condesa Shrimp tacos as my fav.  Best horchata I've ever had and eating the fruits and nuts when your done is a tasty dessert.  The Rabano (radish) Pibil salsa was so amazing I almost killed their supply of little cups going back for more.  That's one I'll be trying to recreate at home forever but will never get quite right.  Slightly sour, slightly hot, it's like a Mexican kimchee . . literally, I just drooled on myself thinking about it.  Viva La Condesa!

La Condesa was the final push to convince me to sign up for Yelp.  I've been using Yelp for years to find everything from local cuisine to family doctors but now it's time to share.  So here goes...

La Condesa was excellent.  From the moment we entered through the heavy spanish doorway, to the smart and humble decor - we knew we had found something unique.  

Our server was polite, engaging, and insightful.  We've been searching for the ultimate Baja-style Fish Taco so we chose a-la-carte tacos this time and will return later for the full meal.  What we did experience this time was a dream come true in the land-locked state of Arizona.  The two pieces of fish in each taco were huge, hot, and crispy, wrapped in a light corn tortilla with a liberal covering of cabbage and white sauce.  With the first bite I was instantly taken back to memories of lounging beach-side in Mexico, or more recently the taco shops of Southern California.  My second and continued bites were adjusted to new heights of flavor with the plethora of home-made salsas available.

I can't wait to return and plan to bring friends!

Troy.

I'm not one to review very often, but this place is hands down my favorite restaurant I've ever been to in my life. I'm an arizona native and like to think I know a thing or two about Mexican food and this place has perfected it.

Must try: cochinita pibil taco 


Their whole menu is great but that taco alone I could eat every day of the week. 

Don't pass this place up!

If I could give this place 10 stars, I would. This place has the best tacos that I've ever had in my whole entire life, ever (seriously, they're THAT good). I also love that they have a variety of self-serve salsas, so you can try as many as you'd like. The place isn't huge, so it can get get packed pretty easily. It doesn't look like much outside, but that's okay because all of the magic happens inside. You should definitely check this place out!

Yes! Yes! Yes! ....
I've been here a few times now and every single time I come I ask myself "now why don't I come here more often?" I do live close by, but then their long line reminds me why lol. 

This place is so freaking delicious! First of all their beans are perfection. And their salsa bar is like its own tasting station lol. 

I've had their bullet burrito, azteca Tinga burrito, shark tacos, shrimp burrito, quesas, guacamole, and their veggie burrito. Everything was great I have no complains. 

If you love horchata you have to try theirs. I promise you will love it! I can go in there for just that a bullet burrito and chips with salsa. LITERALLY.  

It is a very small place so I wouldn't suggest coming during lunch/dinner hours. You will just stand there looking at everyone enjoy their food thinking to yourself "ok can you please hurry and swallow your meal, because it's my turn to sit and swallow mine". Lol 
I usually come here before busy lunch hours and dinner hours so I can get a table asap. 

Customer service is always great. Their menu is to the point, my kind of menu!

Was very excited to come here after all the good reviews.   Overall, our experience was quite "meh".  The menu was inspired.  I loved the idea of having a taco to represent the cuisine of so many different latin american places.  I also loved the salsa bar with its dozen or so unlimited salsas.  However, the food its self was nothing to write home about.  We tried six different tacos, and none of it seemed particularly fresh or interesting.  Had to rely heavily on the salsas to revive the tired tacos.  Doubt I'll be coming back.

Margaritas are amazing!

Tacos on point. Baja shrimp a must. 

Gourmet tacos are your thing it place is a must in Phoenix

I was so disappointed by our meal! :( I really wanted to give this place a chance..

PROS
The salsa bar is very extensive and you can tell that it is all homemade! Great selection and favorites were the salsa verde
Cheap beer - Modelos were $3
My favorite taco was the Al Pastor, added pico and extra lime

CONS
Very small place, we got there early to avoid the wait
Seating by the window can be VERY warm especially during these summer months
Music was static and scratchy it was annoying while eating
The chicken mole taco was such a disappointment - the flavors were not right
The rice was non traditional was just plain with no cilantro or salsa/seasonings

Did we eat most of our taco platters? Yes.
Did we think service was a little spotty and can be improved? Yes.
Do we think that our divey place in Downtown Chandler is levels above this "modern/more pricy" version that is out of the way location wise) for us? Yes.
Had a sample of tacos. The mole is amazing and so is the tinga!  The salsa bar is amazing with many delicious and spicy options. Don't be fooled by the guacamole...it is spicy but delicious.

Great food. I had the smoked Marlin burrito and the La Samita taco with shrimp.

The waiter was pretty awesome, he brought us samples of the different meats to make our ordering process much simpler. The salsas were great. The tomatia salsa was my favorite. The strawberry salsa was surprisingly good as well. 

All in all a great experience for $20 with tip. The burrito was enough to eat without the taco but the two together we're very filling.
I could go there just to eat chips and salsa, very good! The tacos are really good too. Small little place with great service and great food.

Great, cozy ambiance. Great service. Complex, unique, and absolutely delicious flavors on everything that I've tried (tacos, quesadilla, salsa, margaritas). The quesadilla is unlike any other I've ever seen or tasted, and absolutely the best. The margaritas are the best I've had in the valley, and the happy hour price for them is amazing. 
Their menu is so awesome too, so many things that are unique and not commonly found.

Hot food hot. Cold food cold. Yep, delicious. Horchata was full of delicious fruit and nuts. The place was very clean. Sat at the bar and saw the food come thru the little window. No rush, no fuss, just cranking out quality grub. Salsa bar would take a couple of trips to truly savor, lots of choices.

Finding someone who can make better mole than I can deserves 4 stars.  My absolute favorite is the chicken mole burrito.  The chickens mole burrito is just that- loaded with lots of shredded chicken, minimal rice in a flour tortilla.  The burros are gigantic and the drinks are gigantic.  I cannot comment on any other items as I am extremely satisfied with the mole and don't venture far from it.  I think you can order chicken mole tacos but I am unsure.  The salsa bar is tasty, too.  

Apparently there is a Happy Hour on weekdays.  I noticed Tequila behind the bar but didn't see any beer and am unaware of what the Happy Hour entails.
The best Mexican food I've ever had. The street tacos are the best. Good friendly service too. Small though so hard with big groups.

Stop reading and just freaking go there NOW!

It's the best place for street tacos... by FAR!  From traditional carne asada, pollo asada, carnitas, to exotics like fish and shark tacos... it's FANTASTIC! The price is fair and their menu is pretty large.

The place is definitely not Scottsdale. It's a small place and looks kinda dirty.  They have the whole "Day of the Dead" theme going on.  It's an odd looking place but trust me, these are the kind of places where you will find the most authentic food.

They also have a small bar to serve up some nice cocktails and beers.

Their chips are very good and they have a salsa bar with over 14 different salsas. I'm glad my friend recommended this place to me.  I look forward to visiting often.  It's sure is a LOT closer than driving to Mexicali for the same tacos! :)

Advise:  The seating is limited, so if you arrive at the traditional week day noon lunch rush, expect to wait for a table.  It's first come first serve.  I usually visit around 1:30pm or on the weekends.

I reserve 5 stars for meals that are  exemplary. This "gourmet" taco shop is truly that. Every bite is a flavor party, including the array of succulent salsas ranging from chipotle to creamy cilantro. The spicy jalapeños are truly spicy, turning me into a fire-breathing dragon for moments after I ate them.

This restaurant does justice to vegetarians, all veggies are sautéed with care and attention to spices. The mole nearly made my partner dance, dark and intricate like a Spanish tango. My Santisima quesa was a revelation, full of flavor and topped with Mexican crema, a thick corn crust that managed not to be greasy.

And the horchata? It's the real deal. We shared a margarita that tasted natural and refreshing, not a bottled mix in the house.

I have heard so many great things about this place (It was on Diner's Drive-Ins & Dives!) and we finally decided to get our taco-loving booties over there to try it! Ohhh my goodness, I am so happy that we did!! 

They have the most amazing fresh salsa bar with at least 10 different salsas made daily. Being a sauce lover, this was a complete dream come true. I recommend getting the two taco plate with rice and beans. I got the Aztec Tinga Taco (Shredded Chicken, Tomato, Onion & Aztec chipotle sauce) and it was SO juicy with the perfect combination of spices. I also got a Carne Asada taco that was delish! The restaurant is small and I hear it gets busy so I would recommend dining here during off days/times. We went on a Thursday night at 7:30 PM and it was perfect!!! We will for sure be back, i've been daydreaming of their fabulous salsa bar ever since we left!

Ya'll don't understand.  This is it.  This is the place.  This is as good as it gets.

When people say, "Know any real Mexican restaurants?" take them here. When you have people fly in from out of town and say, "Take me to a hidden hole-in-the-wall spot" take them here. When you want to impress a date, your parents, or just have delicious meal... take them here.

If you go at prime dinner time it'll be a 15-30 min wait.  But it's so worth it.  You sit down.  They place a complementary basket of chips and you look to the back where there are 10 different salsas.  Yes ten.  And not this made-in-a-bag BS.  Real fresh stuff.  So you get to experiment with these while you wait for your food to come out.  Next, order the Horchata.  Get only one and share.  They are huge.  Their margaritas are also good. Finally, get something with the black mole and/or oaxacan cheese.  

I cannot overstate how amazing their mole sauce is.  All of their food is excellent but the mole... I have no words to describe it.  I have had their black mole tacos, their black mole sandwich and the heavenly Oaxacan Black Mole Chicken Quesa which is more like an empanada. 

I am from the Midwest originally.  Before I moved here, I swore off Mexican food.  It was greasy, disgusting, and tasted like hot and salty mush.  This restaurant is probably my single favorite place to eat since moving here 3 years ago.  Treat yourself to this place.  You deserve to know happiness.

I want to say don't go here... Why? Because my wife and I loved it so much on our first visit to La Condesa that we selfishly want to keep it a secret from others.

The food was really good and such a unique sampling of traditional Mexican food dishes, with a twist.  The mole was to die for and the shark tacos were amazing.  The rice is also so tasty and I am not usually a rice kind of guy.  I always forgo ordering the traditional side of rice & beans and initially I did the same on our visit.  But my wife ordered the rice with her meal and after seeing and tasting hers, I actually added that to my order even though we already had received our food.  Everyone has already mentioned the amazing salsa bar so I won't repeat the accolades other than to say what a journey of amazing and unique concoctions, coupled with a few of the standard salsas.  Have to recommend the cilantro salsa if you go and be prepared to order more chips if you want to take the salsa adventure and try them all!!!

Gets pretty packed during the standard rush hour periods but worth the wait and if you plan accordingly (noon or early dinner meal), you can avoid the surge.  Definitely one of my favorite taco places in Phoenix.

Ray

Their salsa bar is the best I've seen in Phoenix... I love them ALL. The Al Pastor burrito is my favorite... The burritos are HUGE here. I've tried almost every type of taco they have here and they are all great. Be prepared for a LONG wait if you're not going at an off time because they only have a few tables but it is seriously worth the wait. The prices here are unbeatable, too. They only have 2 servers usually who double as bartenders so you have to kind of grab their attention sometimes but like I said, there are only a few tables and it's very small inside so they can always see you.

I mean, it's whatever. At 1500 reviews, who cares at this point. 

We're never in the area and decided to stop in for lunch this past Saturday afternoon. Bad choice. We were completely underwhelmed.

Pros:

Food. The salsas were great (our chips were stale though...), the tacos were outstanding. I had a chicken tinga taco (so juicy and topped with my favorite: picked red onion), a steak/veggie taco (topped with some sort of fried cheese...HELLO!) and a battered fish taco. I finished most of it, but I should have stopped way earlier. #fatpants

Cons:

Literally everything else. They were clearly understaffed (which by reading the reviews...is a trend? What?) and kept a wait, even though tons of tables were empty during our meal. 

Bussing: We finished our chips and I piled the empty salsa ramekins, used napkins, etc. and pushed it to the side of our tiny table. You'd think our server would remove it when she set our plates down. Nope. WTF? I had to flag down a bus boy to put in his tub. Our table was so small and we needed the real estate to eat comfortably. When we were clearly done and asked for our check, she still didn't bother to pick up our plates and clear the table.

Wait: I get it. I worked in the service industry for way too long. I do understand. However, I've never been so close to walking out of a restaurant before. It took about 40 minutes for us to get our lunch. Our server walked by and told us "Oh, your food is about to come out." That was the midway point, as we waited about 20 more minutes. Why would she just say that to us when it wasn't clearly ready? It felt like bizarro-world

The dining room was pretty grimy.

Truly, the food was amazing. But, we won't be back.

Talk about a salsa selection! Don't even get me started about their Horchata! 
I take my friends from out of town to this place. Try it. You will not be disappointed!!

since I cannot show my face in Gallo Blanco ever again, this has now become my fave gourmex establishment where they will trade food for $!

the tacos are good. the salsa is better. the only downfall, is NO ALCOHOL! ...which may be why I am still able to show my face in here...and perhaps why the hairspray is not sticky... NO ALCOHOL!

It was good but they only serve tacos, quesadillas, and burritos.  I did go with the fish tacos and they were very good.  My son had a steak burrito and was disappointed because it had beans in it.  He  considers beans a cheap filler to provide less meat and he said the beans ruined the flavor in his opinion.

My second time here and the food had been fantastic both times!  I got the Jamaica Rose Shrimp and La Nueva Ensenada and my husband got the shark taco.  We enjoyed everything very much and the service was speedy and friendly.  We also love the many selections at the salsa bar!

The BEST in Phoenix:
Fish tacos (beer battered with cream sauce)
Horchata (contains fresh fruit and pecans, yum!)
Salsa bar (includes peanut and strawberry salsas)

The owner is this cute little lady who is always very nice
Been twice. Authentic, high quality & great price for what you get. Salsa de Chile de Arbol was the best!! Loved the decor. Orchata tasted fresh, which is a rarity in most Mexican Restaurants.
HORRIBLE SERVICE.  The food is good but the terrible service killed it for me.  It appears as though the waiter didn't know the menu very well!  Won't go back!
This place has the best horchata!!!!! You have to try it, but it only comes in one very large size so it is best to share. They also have a great salsa bar and good vegitarian tacos.

Gourmet Tacos at it's best!  The lovely lady behind the counter was the owner that served us. My friend John and I decided to check this out this evening, and all I can say is it's the bomb! I ordered the deep-fried shrimp quesadilla with ooey-gooey cheese! ( I know it sounds unhealthy, but I had to have it) It was enormous and succulent!   John and I both had the pecan horchata, and it did not disappoint.  We went there around 8:00 pm when it's slow, so our service was stellar. They have a lot of great sounding items on their menu, so I am looking forward to returning.

Food - OK. Had cochinita pibil tacos with beans and rice. I found bone and thhe flavor wasn't all that great. Husband had a quesadilla - way too greasy. Napkins couldn't soak up the grease fast enough. Salsas available, because some were empty were quite tasty.
Ambient- sound bounced of the walls and couldn't really have a talk with out contributing to the already loud room. Lighting not great. Beautiful mexican culture inspired art. Loved it.
Service- not good. Sat us down and then disappeared had to stop them and ask any of the employees to put in our order, refills, and our check. The worst part was... there wasn't that many people.
Other- loved there terra cota plates. Cups were paper cups, and they had nice silver wear. Couldn't figure out whether it was nice dinner restaurant or just a dive.

So good! So good. A must try taco shop if you are in Phoenix. I ordered 3 different tacos and was able to turn them into 6 since they put a lot of fillings and 2 corn tortillas. The mole is so delish and you gotta order this taco. I ordered the steak and it was good too, but my fave...the carnitas taco. The pork is so tender and flavorful! I also love all the salsas! I just wish they didn't run out of some of them...there were so many to choose from it was hard to decide what to try so I relied an a regular to steer me in the right direction. The margarita was ok, but I would definitely go back for the mole and the carnitas!

Food: very good...  authentic and worth visiting.  Maybe better to go. 

Service: SUCKS.   Incompetent people who don't know how to operate a restaurant.   When I walked in, there were 10 people in line - many "couples".   There was an open table for two at the front of the restaurant.  I approached the hostess (incompetent) about the table she said, "we are not using the table" followed by something about not wanting to overwhelm the wait staff.   Then, 5 minutes later she went back and talked to a waiter about the table.  She then proceeded to have a party sit down.  Really?

Overall experience:  I was there for over an hour just trying to get two tacos.   Food came out lukewarm probably because it was sitting in the kitchen waiting to come out.  Overall, service with waiter was pathetic.   The people here don't know what they are doing and should go to school to learn how to run a restaurant like a business.  

My (Hispanic) friend always says, "Mexican restaurants are not known for service".  This restaurant epitomizes this statement.

Since it's already a well-established point that this place has delicious food at an excellent value, I'll simply provide a few bulleted remarks:

Great Original Paintings
Sweet & fresh faced Guadalajaran transplant at counter
Amazing Strawberry Salsa (WTF -- who knew?) 
New favorite pinto beans in town (sorry America's Taco Shop)
Not a fan of the Dogshark taco
Chicken Mole & Conchinita were T'Asty
Generously portioned $6.99 2 taco combination entree is UNBEATABLE

I went in at 1pm, and the place was empty.  With all these great Yelp reviews, where are all the sophisticated, bargain hunting peeps with a hankering for delicious Mexican in a town notoriously lacking in this?

I LOVE La Condesa.  What more do I need to say? The salsa bar is amazing! I really like their carne asada.  They do but beans in the burrito, which, at first I wasn't sure how I'd feel about it, but after a couple, I really like it.  I've had the pork and shrimp tacos also.  The quality is always top notch.  I did the artwork too!  Two negatives...The music can sometimes be loud, and sometimes they are REALLY packed and parking is a bit tough to find.  Other than that, I HIGHLY recommend!

Literally,  the BEST burrito we have ever had! The La Santisima burrito with chicken was absolutely incredible. You come for the food, not the service. They are a little slow, but the food is great! Completely worth it ! 

The mushroom quesadilla was also great! 

Small restaurant,  self serve salsa bar. 

10 tables and a bar. 

Highly recommended!

Los peores tacos de mi vida, yo soy de México en específico de la Ciudad de México y vaya que conocemos de tacos los de la ciudad y en lo personal yo como muchísimos tacos.Desconozco que calidad tengan el resto del menú pero en lo personal los tacos no fueron de mi gusto en lo más mínimo el suadero no sabe a sudadero, el pastor no sabe a pastor en fin etc etc.Tuvimos que esperar un poco pasado de 1 hora para que nos entregarán la orden de 6 tacos 4 para mí y 2 para mí novia que por cierto está vomite y vomite y con mucho dolor estomacal.En lo personal no volvería jamás
Great gourmet tacos! Recommend the brisket one on the street taco menu. The pecan salsa is very tasty as well! Classic margarita-phenomenal! Wonderful lunch spot.
Unbelievable food, friendly and helpful staff, great vegan options. This place seems to get packed so plan ahead but I think it's well worth the wait.

Driving down the rough streets of north phoenix, I have never really taken the time to look at the many restaurants that adorn the streets. I thought north phoenix was really only pawn shops, tire shops, and smoke shops, but my gf had heard of this place so we made a special journey out to La Condesa. After checking to make sure our doors were locked 4 times, we entered this "gourmet" taco shop...and boom all my misconceptions were erased.

This place is extremely clean and friendly. The tacos I ordered were overflowing with flavor and ingredients. I was thoroughly filled after two tacos.  I had the Shrimp tacos - not the cabo ones, i think they were simply grilled and guess what? that's right, no diarrhea afterwards. Also had the the sonoran carne asada tacos....which were arrachera steak marinated with fresh garlic & olive oil, charbroiled with mesquite charcoal. The tacos were amazing and the salsa bar was mind blowing. The yhave about 12 salsas to try from and I had to try them all. My personal favorites were the cilantro, chipotle and the surprisingly  yummy peanut salsa.

I REALLY wanted the horchata, but they had just run out..i won't ding them for running out because we did come in 5 minutes before closing. Can't wait to go back here, you gotta give this place a try.

We had a few hours before heading to the PHX airport so we stopped by La Santisima for lunch. Being Mexican from SoCal I know good tacos. This place does not disappoint, everything we tried was good. Plenty of taco options and an awesome salsa selection (strawberry salsa my favorite). The only disappointment was that they didn't have any horchata when we arrived. Had the following. 
 
- Sonoran Carne Asada Taco
- Aztec Tinga Taco
- La Condesa Veggie Taco
- Mayan Cochinita Pibil Taco

I'd definitely go back and recommend it to anyone looking to get a local meal near the airport (about 5 mins away)

Hands down best tacos! They have quesadillas and burritos as well (I think they added sandwiches recently but I don't know for sure). Anyhow, the quesadillas are fried, so if you shy away from fried food, don't even go there. The salsa bar is the best I've ever seen and I enjoy mostly all of what they have available. I like the arracherra taco, the tinga taco and the guacho taco. Perhaps I have spelled those incorrectly, I'm not sure but whatever you get it's going to be good. I do not however, like the beans. I don't know what it is or why, I just don't like them. I do like the rice with the corn in it but generally speaking I just get the tacos a la carte. OH and the Horchata? OMG, get it I promise you even if you don't like Horchata you will probably like this. It is huge though and has fruit and nuts and wow, it's just good. I like the Jamaica (sp?) juice too, but who doesn't :-P... Obviously, I don't speak spanish sorry for my awful spelling. Everyone should try it here, but they are small and get busy so try to find a time not everyone will be going to eat.
Some the best taco I've had. I had the Al Pastor (pork), Carne Asada & Chicken mole. The service was friendly and a salsa bar was amazing with 13 different salsas.
I always bring friends and family here to have good real Mexican tacos. They always  want to come back here. The horchata tastes the way my mom and grandma make it.
Loved this place! I asked the cashier to order me her favorite thing and it was absolutely delicious!
love the salsa bar but service can be WAY slow during peak hrs. THEY NEED MORE HELP!! Food is fantastico!! Try it but avoid peak hrs.

Delicious food - had the different veggie tacos and the cactus taco. A plethora of vegetables cooked just right. The rice and beans were the best, THE BEST, I've ever had. Also, One outstanding veggie quesadilla. What !!!

I'm not even a fan of Mexican food but this was pretty damn good !

So many colorful unique flavorful sauces and salsas helped a lot. Really really delicious.

The chips were good too, not greasy at all 
Hot hats drink had nuts and fruits in it which I ate with a fork afterwards...

Service was good. There were two servers and they handled it well. Alan took care of us and he was friendly professional and nice and efficient. 

When we came in, the place had three tables. By the time we left it was packed and there were people waiting outside on the bench and inside at the bar. 

We parked around the corner in the white spaces.
The place has a cool exterior and a cool interior. 
I'll add a photo of two

Enjoy, folks, this one is a winner...

This is my first time in Phoenix and decided to try this place this evening due to all the yelper reviews. I was not disappointed. The salsa Bar had many different flavors of salsas-- yum!!! I was really pleased.  So many varieties and all complimented our meals very well. I got the al pastor bowl (perfect low carb option) and I was absolutely delicious! The kids had a chicken quesadilla and they were very happy. If I'm ever up this way I just may come here again. We had a wait for 30 minutes to get a table and we also had to wait 30 minutes for the food to come. It is fine except for little kids having to wait was not easy.
Amazing fair with a laid back atmosphere. Love the salsa bar!

Love how their menu basically blasts TexMex as giving Mexican food a bad representation. Now this is authentic Mexican food. Not some heavy just because we're Americans portion. 

Ordered a lonches. Because they wanted to be different from a torta. But even in the mindset of what a standard torta is, these lonches are WAY BETTER. Bread sustains itself to the fillings (instead of falling apart or soaking up stuff like a torta bread does. Ordered shark. So that was different. There was a freshness to it due to a cucumber to give it a nice crispness to each bite. Brother ordered the al pastor lonche and he thoroughly enjoyed it as well. Girlfriend ordered the mole quesadilla. And yes yes yes! Delivered on the multiple layers of spices within the mole. Man, have I always only had flat moles (such a sad fact). Now, I can imagine not being able to order mole from anywhere else ever again! Eeeek! But do give it a try. Oh, and this quesadilla looked more like a dessert. But nope. A nice balance between the spices of the mole, meat (chicken), and cotija cheese that's sprinkled over it. 

Also tried their horchata. Once again, flavors up the Ying-yang! Theirs nuts, melons, freshly mashed strawberries. So definitely not your typical Americanized Mexican restaurant. 

Tip: don't park in the front. It's extremely difficult to back out into the busy traffic street. Especially if you're alone. Somewhat more doable if you have someone standing outside the car giving your a thumbs up.

Remember: food adventures are out there. So eat 'em up!

This place is probably paradise for my white/non-hispanic friends! I was born and raised in Mexico, so I know La Santisima is NOT authentic mexican food. But it is tasty food and for a good price. Yes, they have a salsa bar with about 23,594 different salsas (ok, maybe I exaggerated a bit) but only about 2 are pretty tasty. 

I say this restaurant consists more of "Mexican-American" food. But if you're hispanic and want to take your non-hispanic buddies to a "mexican" place, then La Santisima is the perfect spot where their minds will be blown thinking they're eating "authentic" mexican food and at the same time you'll be satisfied too with the tasty Americanized version of a torta or quesadilla.
