Gonella brand Italian bread is what most places in Chicago use but it's impossible to find in the west and cost prohibitive to ship. There probably is another brand of bread that's available around here that's more like Gonella which would boost the authenticity rating up a notch or two, but with all of my nit-picking aside Windy City is a great choice, and in my opinion even better and more authentic than both Rossatis's (pizza pub) and Al's (which is supposedly a Chicago tradition and recently closed up after 2 years of business in Las Vegas)

My husband wanted to try this place. We got my son a simple hot dog he ate it. My daughter ordered a tamale (it came in a sealed plastic wrapper) she didn't like it at all. She thought she was getting a real Tamale LOL. My husband and I ordered a Reuben Sandwich.  It was probably the best we've had. Great flavor!!!!  After our meal I purchased the spicy popcorn and the hot mixture thing they sale. Very good customer service.  My 3 year old son went up and bought a drink and the lady was so sweet. Before we left they offered our kids sherbet ice cream on the house! Love this place we will be back
Nicest people you could ever meet.   Food was like Chicago. Had a combo beef and sausage.   Brought me back to my childhood.   Please come here.   It is worth it.

Was on the way home and remembered to finally stop by this joint and take it off my "To Do List".....thank God I did!  It was 10:45 am and I wondered if they would be open.....they were, lucky me!

I was greeted by the owner and his Wife.....at least it appeared as if they owned the joint.  They were very friendly and welcoming.  It's a casual restaurant with 10 or 12 tables inside and 8-10 counter seats near the grill.  There's also a few tables outside with umbrellas if you like to dine outdoors.

I browsed the menu and was getting excited with every item I saw.....Vienna Beef Dogs, Beef Sandwiches, Iltaco Pizza Puffs......WAIT, Pizza Puffs?!  Holy $hit, that changes everything....I love those things!

I couldn't control myself, so I ordered a #2 Two Chicago Dogs w/Relish, Pickle Spear, Tomato, Hot Peppers, Mustard, Onions, Seasoned Salt....and Fries ($6.00)....plus I ordered a Pizza Puff ($3.50) and washed it down with a bottle of Coke Zero.  Dammit, there goes the diet!  The lady asked for my name and asked if I was dining in or taking out....I told her dine-in.

I saddled up to a table and anxiously waited for the food.  While I was waiting I noticed a man with his Son sitting at the counter.  They were eating Chicago Dogs and he was telling his Son how a Chicago Dog is made and how it should taste....the owner, who was grilling it up was there telling the kid about how to make the Dog....it was awesome.

After a few minutes my order was ready.  The lady brought it out to my table....I unwrapped both Dogs and the bag of Fries and put them together on one wrap so I could eat it uninterrupted.  She told me the Pizza Puff was still cooking so it would be a few minutes....that's pretty standard to wait for Pizza Puffs, so I didn't care.  The Dogs were covered in Mustard, which is how I like it.....if you don't like too much Mustard on your Dog, I suggest you tell them ahead of time.  The first bite was an explosion of Awesome on my taste buds....it was sooo good!  The Vienna Beef Dog was full of flavor and the combination of toppings was just how I remember the Dogs in Chi-town.  The Relish is the atomic green colored stuff you find in Chi-town.  This place is legit!

The Fries were piping hot and seasoned with a Salty seasoning....if you don't like your Fries too Salty, then I suggest you either ask for them plain or tell them easy on the seasoning.  I liked it.  It complimented the Dogs just right.  The Dogs were average size.....not too big, do don't expect a 1/4 lb Dog with the #2.  I think they offer larger Dogs with other combo meals, but not with the #2.

The Pizza Puff came out shortly after I started eating.  I waited until I was done with the Dogs before I moved over to that bad boy.  It was wrapped in the traditional Iltaco Pizza Puff wrapper.....those of you familiar with Pizza Puffs know what I'm talking about.  I bit into the greasy, flaky, doughy Crust and mmmm.....yeah, it's the Pizza Puff that I've grown to love.  Inside of the flaky, doughy Crust is a filling of Pizza Sauce, Sausage, and Cheese.  Dammit, these things are addicting and I just discovered this place....I have a feeling I will be here often.

The owners were very attentive and asked if I was ok and needed anything.  After I was finished, they asked how I liked it....I gave them the thumbs up and a big smile.  They were smiling too and said "See you soon Peter!"......I love family owned businesses who pay attention to their customers.  While I was there 6 or 7 people came in and they knew all of them by first name.  I hope I get to know them better too.

Will I return?  This place has won my clogged artery Heart....you bet I will!  Now, back to the gym to burn off these calories.
Great place to grab a bite to eat.  I have been here time and time again and have always had a great meal with good service.

Gerat Beefs great dogs and amazing decor! I will go back to this location every time I find my self in Las Vegas. Two things you must see the Las Vegas strip at night and this Italian beef at the south end of the stop must do

My wife is in love with all things Chicago so I decided to try Windy City Beefs-N-Dogs and was pleasantly suprised.  Windy City Beefs-N-Dogs has its strong points and its weak points.  One thing I do like about this restaraunt is that they use very high quality ingredients.  I had a beef and sausage sandwich and the beef was fresh and juicy and the sausage was huge (no dinky small sausage around here).  I also liked this relish like substance they put on their sandwich, which is a combination of carrots, peppers, and onions.  The Au Jus was delicious.
   One thing I would say though is this is not a place to go if you are trying to monitor your cholestrol or even lose a few pounds.  Everything is greasy and fattening, but this is not necessarily a bad thing if it is done right (and in this case it is).  The only complaint I had about my sandwich is that it might use some more seasoning as it was slightly bland.  It is possible though this is a more stylistic attribute of the Chicago style food so I can't complain.

All in All Great place.
My wife and I enjoy the dogs at this restaurant!  They are consistently good.  Much better than that dump on Rancho.

Originally from Chicago, I crave the Chicago Vienna dogs at times. 

We went across town in search of the Chicago Dog for me, and the Italian Beef for hubby. We were greeted as we walked in the door by two very friendly and outgoing people behind the counter. The Italian Beef was ordered 'wet' (whole sandwich dipped, bread and all) and with the spicy jardiniere. 

We took a seat and waited while everything was made fresh. I loved all of the posters and pictures on the wall showing the Chicago stadiums and teams. Made me feel like I was back in Chicago for a bit. Hubby loved the Italian Beef, and made a great mess of himself while eating it. If the juice is running down your arms, you are eating it properly!

This was definitely a fun place to visit, with super friendly staff and great food. I give it 4.5 stars since it seems a bit pricy. Not too badly though. I was torn between 4 and 5 stars.

Wow!! A taste of Chicago in Las Vegas, awesome food beef, Chicago dogs, Italian beef, pizza puff n fries :)
Great flavor in a family owned business.  
They have a chicago themed diner.
Dude. I got a Italian beef and sausage sandwich, dipped. It was glorious. It was delicious. It was messy as hell. I loved it.

The food is good as long as u like Chgo food. Prices are high.. The young staff are friendly & the orders are always correct but the 2 Lady owners (sisters) are RUDE RUDE RUDE!!!! 
I don't like their treatment towards their customers. You can SAVE money & shop @ Glaziers. Same Vienna hotdogs, beefs & Supreme Hot Tamales for 1/2 the price..

This is my first spa experience so I don't have anything to compare it to. I came in for a for:
Microdermabrasion
Swedish Massage
Rhassoul Wrap

They were all amazing services. I even booked the 30 minute jacuzzi suite rental at the end which was fabulous, I needed that alone time after being touched so much! lol. 

The use of the steam room in-between each service was fabulous. It so relaxing. And the staff were knowledgable and sweet.

My only thing is during my facial the lady who was doing it left when she was finished and didn't even tell me. I wasn't sure whether to just lay there and wait or get up, leave and wait for my second booking. I wish there was more communication. It was my first time and maybe I should have mentioned that but then again they shouldn't assume you come there often.

It was my first time at Hammam, and I booked a 60 minute massage and then asked if they had an open pedicure appointment for my awful feet and they said yes! Hooray! The place itself is pretty, and the hustle and bustle of King West disappears as soon as you walk down the stairs. The changeroom is average, but has everything you need. They offered up the steamroom, but that's not my "thing", although one of the other customers I was speaking with said it was amaazing! The lounge area is small, and my biggest pet peeve was the creaking coming from the floor upstairs; it was impossible to relax with that sound, along with the chatty employees. However, once I was lead to the massage room, relaxation ensued. My male masseuse was unbelievable, and the massage was the best massage I have ever had..and I've had plenty. He paid attention to those areas I had asked him to, and finished the appointment by showing me stretches I could do to help with my tense muscles. I felt like a new person! My pedicurist was also wonderful, but the employees doing pedicures on one another nearby while gossiping about a colleague made that part a tad frustrating (but my toes looked great!).

Overall, the services I had were awesome but the atmosphere needs some serious work, as there's far too much chatting and noise going on for a spa..even one that's downtown!

I see a lot of reviews here on how it's amazing here. And yes, it's very beautiful on the inside but the staff is NOT beautiful on the inside at all. Selene is the cruelest woman I have met to this day, I just don't understand, they work at a SPA, SHOULDN'T YOU BE CALM AND TRANQUIL? Unbelievable, there are better spas in Toronto with amazing staff. If i could give this no stars, I'd find a way to eliminate the star-rating and just stamp it with a BIG RED PHRASE SAYING "SHITTY BITCHES"...phew I got THAT out of my system :)

I have used Hammam Spa in the past and the spa services are decent.  The steam room was fine.  The facial was fine.  However, the spa itself is noisy, both within and from the noise upstairs.  The Turkish bath/massage is a joke compared to the experience you get in an actual Turkish style bath/massage (and I have had in Turkey, as well as Morocco and Budapest).   

I am giving Hammam Spa one star though because of their repeated poor customer service and condescending and arrogant attitude.  

First, you cannot get through to anyone at their phone number - you are directed to the website or you can leave a message.  That is not helpful customer service.     

Second, on several occasions, I have left a message and have never received a return call.  That is not helpful customer service.  

Third, their specials are highly misleading.  For example, their January 2014 special says "20% off any service when you book online...use promo code 2014".  I purchased a gift certificate online for two specific massages and entered the promo code.  I understood the special would have applied to this, especially since the online purchase page had a box where the promo code could be entered (which I entered).  The 20% was not taken off the purchase price.  I left two voicemail messages for Hammam Spa asking them to call me back to give me a credit for the difference.  I never heard back from them.  Finally, after I had to email them (again, it is not helpful customer service if I have to spend a large amount of time chasing you down) Hammam Spa called me back today to say that gift certificates purchased online are not covered by this special, notwithstanding I was purchasing gift certificates for services.  I suggested to her that the special should specifically set out in the future that it does not apply to purchases of gift certificates for specific services and I believe she agreed that would be helpful (duh!).  I asked if there was anything she could do for me to which she repeated that gift certificates are not available.  Her tone was arrogant and her refusal to do anything reinforces for me that Hammam Spa has very poor customer service and a condescending and arrogant attitude.  

For these reasons, I will not use Hamman Spa in the future personally nor purchase gifts for others there.   I urge everyone to instead consider all of the fine spas in and around Toronto other than Hamman Spa: http://www.blogto.com/toronto/the_best_spas_in_toronto/.

I've visited in the past and enjoyed. Today was the first day after their renovation and I expected a great experience. Instead I was horribly disappointed. I wish they had called me and just cancelled instead of getting what I got

I should say that the massage therapist who l saw was great. The  treatment itself was pleasant. But Hammam be brands itself on being more than just a massage treatment. 

The steam room was cold. Ice cold in fact. Just not ready yet. There were contractors walking around still working. Including one that walked into a toilet stall on me, which by the way didn't have a lock installed on it. 

The showers don't even have doors yet, there was no shampoo or soap nor was there any hot water. I must say. A great massage was very quickly ruined by an ice shower that I couldn't even wash up in. I hope they shut the doors for a few more days and finish up before inviting clients in. 

And the $25 gift card for my inconvenience did not do much to make up for paying $125 for such a negative experience.

Just like most people seem to say here, the rmt massage is actually decent - the professionals know what they're doing (my deep tissue involved trigger point and passive muscle activation). But! My lady was not able to get into my tight neck/shoulder muscles. I own a massage clinic and my rmt is wayyyy better at getting into my neck. There left something to be desired. With the prices they charged (45mins massage $110), I expected a sensational steam experience which they advertise as their main selling feature. I did not particularly enjoy it with water droplets intermittently dripping from the ceiling and flashing colouful lights that just made it seem so tacky. It was also coed, which could be uncomfortable for some as no dress code is really enforced (when asked about what i should wear in there as i brought a swimsuit, the lady nonchalantly said theres a wrap in your locker..). The hallway was so dim it seemed dirty. I did enjoy the cold minty towels and did wonder about the turkish suites, however I dont think I would come back just on that account. I didn't enjoy the music throughout - I thought it eerie and the whole experience before the massage didn't relax me. The space at the entry is a bit awkward for spacing and there is too much product being advertised - it felt like I was in a store. The cleaning staff must be a bit disorganized because there were water cups left on a table in the reception and the bench where you sit to fill forms was dirty with crumbs of something scattered about.

I'm a massage queen. I used to get them regularly but due to my travel schedule not as much. My preference is a male masseuse and typically walk away if there is none available. 

I just got back from a 2 week vaca, while I should  have come back relaxed my back was totally stiff! I slept on the worst bed and airplane seats make for a backache. 

Due to year end, it was virtually impossible to schedule a massage anywhere. Thankfully Hamman is close to my office. Someone canceled and took me in. cami was my masseuse (female). In my condition I had no business being picky.  I asked her to only focus on my back. She was AMAZING.. absolutely amazing! I literally died and went to heaven.. 

I'm in Toronto every other month and plan to make a regular visit to Hammam. Two thumbs up.. Thanks Cami!!

As far as Toronto day spas are concerned, my best experiences have been at Hammam. I find scheduling can be an issue, but that is probably a reflection of their popularity.  I had a wonderful RMT where other spas have offered massages that always leave much to be desired.

Especially accommodating of couple pampering. 

Recently went to Novo Spa and it PALED in comparison. 
Will be going back to Hammam and soon.

WARNING: Weekends book 2 to 3 weeks in advance, especially for couple activities.

My husband and I came here for the hamma turkish baths. This was our first ever turkish bath experience and we were pleasantly surprised.
As son as you enter the spa, the aromatic eucalyptus smells gives it a nice relaxing feel. Check in process was smooth. Upon check in we were given a quick tour of the facilties as it was our first time. The locker and shower areas were clean and in immaculate condition. 

For the hammam treatment, we first used the steam room. By far one of the best steam rooms, I have ever been to. It has nice soft lighting which chnages with the music. Yes the steam room has music!! What I loved most was the bowl of ice and washcloths that are provided for you to take inside the steam room if you need to cool down a little. 

It was then followed by our Turkish bath. The ladies that helped my husband and me were very professional and did an amazing job. The marble stone remained hot and we were never uncomfortable/ awkward at any time. What I loved the most was the couples turkish bath is on the same slab of stone, which allows you to hold hands, talk and actually enjoy the experience together as a couple. It was a really fun experience for us. After the baths, we could either relax in the tea are or use the steam room again. Both me and my husband were extremely happy with our scrub downs, our skin has never felt softer and cleaner.

The tea area is nice and cozy and has plenty of magazines, juices, water, tea, nuts, cranberries, fruit for use between your sessions. It has a nice fire place as well where you can sit and relax with your tea. 

As mentioned earlier, the showers were nice and clean, they have plenty of towels, bathrobes and sarongs if you need to change them out. They also have basic things like hair bands, deodrant, hair spray and hair brushes.  The only one thing I wish they had were better hair driers but that was no big deal. 

Overall, we both loved our visit to hammam spa and would definitely book a bath again. If any of you want to enjoy something as a couple together, the turkish baths are highly recommended.

I've been to Hammam Spa 3 times now, all of which have been during promotions (they have new ones every month) and for facials. I have a hard time justifying paying the full premium here vs. a joint like Pure + Simple, as well as not just paying an extra $20 or so bucks to go to a nicer spa in the neighbourhood (e.g. at the Ritz or Shangri La).

Hammam is pleasant. It's a nice little retreat at the northwest corner of King and Portland, with little being the operative word. The amenities are limited to a tea room and their steam room, or "hammam". All amenities are available to men and women. You are provided a wrap, a robe and flip flops in the locker room, to walk around in. I would recommend wearing a bathing suit underneath if you want to use the steam room, as the alternative is spending the rest of your time there in a damp wrap.

The tea room can comfortably seat perhaps 10 people, before it starts to feel cramped. There are apples / dried cranberries / almonds to snack on, and water, juice and tea, alongside a selection of predominantly lifestyle magazines. The star attraction, the hammam, is of a similar scale and is included in your stay if you spend over $100. Otherwise, I believe the charge is closer to $50 for entrance, which is not justified in my humble opinion. 2 out of the 3 times I was here, the face towels in the ice bowl outside the steam room were completely depleted (literally was a bowl of ice with a sign saying "enjoy"). Sometimes there are big towels available for you to lie on, depending on your luck. The hammam is eucalyptus scented and quite hot, but not very relaxing given the side conversations which always seem to be happening in there. It's no fault of the spa, but it's hard to zen out when you can hear the couple beside you talking about the coworker they hate.

There are no clocks anywhere (which can be stressful for type As...). Your attendant will come find you when it's time for your appointment. The treatment rooms are nice, and the facials I had were fine. I prefer the dermalogica facial over the skincetuicals (which was more mask-oriented). To be honest, I've received better "extras" (e.g. the hand / foot / shoulder massage) at cheaper places like Pure + Simple. I am 80% sure that during one of my treatments, when a mask was left on, I received a brisk scalp massage and then could hear the cosmetologist texting. . . I digress. What I do like about Hammam, is that they have never pushed product on me (contrary to some other reviews I have read).

Bottom line: a little bit more "spa like" than your standard no-frills joint, but not even close to the range and scale of amenities available if you pay a little extra (or even a little less at the Elmwood Spa, which offers a hot tub and a pool). 4 stars, because there is nothing offensive about the experience to deserve lower.

A friend and I decided to take a pampering day today so we booked individual treatments for early in the afternoon.  I had requested a 60 minute Swedish massage.  The massage itself was just ok - I've had better.  I normally get a massage every month so I know good massages.

The ambiance was ok.  When we got there (2:00pm) hardly anyone was around so our expectation was that it would be a nice and quiet afternoon.  

We changed and headed to the steam room.  Yes it is dark but not as dark as I had imagined from what everyone is writing about and I thought this added to the relaxation.  As we waited in the tea room for our treatments, this is where I was most disappointed.  You could hear people walking across the floor from overhead.  It was loud and continuous.  Then there were random guys dressed in street clothes that kept walking by.  They obviously weren't there for treatments and looked like construction workers.  It was a bit creepy seeing as we were sitting there in bathrobes.

Overall, I think this place is over-priced and too hyped.  For the amount that I paid for the massage, I could've had the same treatment at Elmwood (my fave spa) and had a mani pedi done.  After we paid for our services they didn't even provide an RMT receipt for the massage (which is standard nowadays). I won't be returning to this spa anytime soon.  My BFF was lucky - she didn't spend a penny for this experience since she was trying to use up a gift certificate for her service.

This was a pretty disappointing trip - not like my last one at all. The girl who gave me a massage last time was very good, best I have had. Apparently she is not coming back, so I went with a guy who really did not do a good job. It was not enjoyable, and I am in pain today (next day).  

The steam room was "redone" but look the same as before. The staff opens to door for a good minute or two in order to find their next appointment. This happened too many times in half hour and the steam room got very cold.

I have not decided whether or not I will be back, I think I would try another spa first and then decide. They should really have the best of the best on their staff, and it was disappointing that I paid $160 for a massage that I did not love.

The steam room is good but overpriced.  If it was half the price, Id use it way more often.
The massage was good but overpriced and you could hear people walking around and talking while being massaged.  I've had better RMT for 50$ less than what I paid here for 1 hour.
I live nearly across the street from it and I am not that sold on this place, mainly because of their prices.

I am a spa lover. I consider visiting the spa a reward for all my hard work. Visits aren't cheap by any means but if the quality and the service matches or exceeds the price, then I leave a blissed out camper.

So Hammam... what do I say about you? I can't say many good things.

We booked a Couple's Package which comes with a steam room session in the communal steam room, a massage and a facial in room which accommodates you and your partner. 

The steam room was...steamy? I really enjoyed it. The steam was naturally scented with eucalyptus and some other herbs/plants. I felt calm and relaxed. The kinks in my muscles melted. It's important to keep hydrated when you're in the steam room and the spa has water pitchers and glasses right outside the steam room. The boy... well he didn't enjoy it as much. He found it too hot (duh). 

The couples massage was okay. The massages were supposed to be done in the Swedish style but frankly, the pressure was so light and we didn't really feel the benefits. 

The facials or "facials" weren't that great. It was rushed and all they did was cleanse and slap a mask on. I could've done better at home.

So did I leave Hammam blissed out? No... and I won't be back.

I love this spa.  I've never had a bad massage here... the RMT's are the best in the city!!  The only 'beef' I have with this place is that it's pricey, but I suppose that's normal for a spa located in King West.  

It's my little escape when I need some good 'me' time.  Highly recommended if you've got some extra cash to spend!!

I can not express how much I love this place. I specially love the Turkish bath and steam room. Such a cozy, and relaxing setting. I had done a multitude of services there from waxing to, mani/pedis but I would mostly recommend the massages and definitely the bath. The staff are very friendly and professional. The space is always clean and organized. I love this place.

My experience at the Hammam Spa completely ruined my day.

I'll start from the beginning:

I arrived half an hour early, as requested in the confirmation email, to "fill out paperwork". The waiting area was freezing cold, and the paperwork consisted of a sheet with merely 5 questions on it. I was then escorted to the change room, which was awkward and completely open with only a small table to sit down on. I changed into my robe and PLASTIC flip-flops and proceeded to wait in the "tea room" for my treatment provider to call me in.

The "tea room" is a lounge-type room, more befitting of a trendy club - not a spa. There were basic refreshments and food, including apples, water, and juice - I couldn't be bothered to have any. The waiting room was probably 16 degrees - I was absolutely freezing! I couldn't feel my toes.
 
My esthetician was 20 - 30 minutes late - I was honestly about to get up and leave when she called my name. She was young and spoke with me as if I was a student in school, bossing me around and not speaking in a calm, soothing manner at all. She seemed impatient as she waited for me to spend a few minutes in the steam room. The steam room was unbearable - too hot, too dark, too wet. It seemed like a cesspool of bacteria. Gross.

On to the treatment. I opted for the Turkish Bath Treatment - considering this was a Turkish style spa, it seemed like the best option. Basically, I had hot water THROWN on my body multiple times, then the esthetician scrubbed my body down with an exfoliating mitt, then THREW hot water on me again, and then poured soap on me, and then THREW hot water on me again. I felt like a dog being punished in the form of having some awful sort of bath. My esthetician made the treatment feel rushed, like she hated her job and couldn't wait to get out of there. The room itself had thin, see-through walls, and I could hear other people talking in the rooms next to me and see them walking around (can they see me? I'm practically naked!). And again, the room was COLD! The entire experience was very noisy, not at all relaxing. And the water everywhere made me feel like I had to pee. The entire treatment lasted maybe 30 minutes - and cost $125.

When the treatment was over, i was sent back into the tea room, wet and freezing cold. I was told that I would have an assortment of teas and treats waiting for me. What I found was a glass of water and three dates.

I am never, ever going back.

I've been going to Hammam for years for one thing and one thing only:  facials ($130 plus tip) from Ashley.  I've been to a lot of spas, and she is as skilled as they come.  I love the steam room when it's not full of chatty bitches and gross men sighing and groaning like they're at the Oakwood men's only Steam Bath, if you catch my drift.  And the towels have shrunk over the years, which makes things a little more exciting than they need to be.

The spa itself is gorgeous and smells like eucalyptus and freshly bathed babies, although the change room floors are sometimes a little dirty/hairy which freaks me out, and is really kind of unacceptable at these prices.

I went for a facial and I'm now concerned that there is so much product in my hair that it won't wash it for weeks. She proceeded to do a head massage that had her rubbing all the product from my face in my hair for about five minutes. I really wish I had asked her to stop.
They also are very very aggressive about selling  you product.  The first 20mins of the facial were spent trying to convince me to buy product at the spa, despite multiple attempts to divert conversation without being ride. 
The overall spa atmosphere is okay but there are many nicer places in Toronto, particularly for the price. 
I would not recommend this place. The hammam is coed and is so dark you can't tell whether it is actually clean or you're stepping in a big puddle, which happens frequently.  To be honest, the steam room at my gym is more pleasant as it has lights.

I absolutely love this place!!! Went there with my friend and we each had an awesome massage! Amanda is the greatest! :)
The place is clean and welcoming. Change room/locker/showers are super clean as well and there's a nice steam room. 
Staff is friendly and we will definitely go back!

I went to Hammam Spa on the 21st of December...I was finished work and this was my first day of vacay until Jan 4th 2010, what an amazing way to start a vacay...other then jumping on a plane and flying to a hot country with a hot man. 

I had purchased the gift cards in a charity auction at work, so I had a good amount to play with. It took me a few days to think about what I wanted to do and I finally settled on an hour massage (so I could write some of it off) and an algae wrap. As you all know, I'm a self confessed spa snob....and with all of the places I have been to I have never done a body wrap.....well....what a treat. 

My day started with getting there early, I wanted to take advantage of the full spa, and since I was on vacay I had nothing else to do. The staff was very sweet and checked me in right away. I was taken on a tour, told where to change and given a key for my locker. 

I wasted no time in filling out the forms, changing and making a mad dash to the traditional Hammam steam room. It was very dark, and very beautiful. Built of slate the cool tile was a nice break from the warm sent infused steam. 

When it was time for my wrap, I was gathered from the steam and taken to the room. I must admit that it was a weird but very cool and relaxing experience. The lady preforming my treatment, Shelley, was so sweet, and very wonderful. She explained everything and made sure I was comfy when the actual wrapping took place. Next I was off to my massage with Emily and that was just as amazing! If you happen to get the same treatments that I received, try to get these ladies. 

To finish off my day I headed back into the steam for a bit. In total I was there for 5 hours and it was well worth it. I will admit that the prices can be a bit steep if you're used to other places, but I think that it's due to the area where the spa is located....it is King West after all.

The services in the spa like massages are great however I went for a manicure pedicure and the whole experience was a disappointment. They used shellac which didn't dry well and when I formally complained they said they could re do the color at no cost - that mean removing and putting it again and no reimbursement. The second time the application was better but results were not as great as I get in other places. They also confused my name and sent me a cancelation for my service. Terrible customer service for complaints etc.

I love love love the steam room. I got the steam pass which gives you one month unlimited usage of the steam room and lounge. Turkish steam rooms are my favourite and this one is a beauty. The smell of Hamman spa is so relaxing. Im not sure what the other services are like but the steam room is amazing.

The scrub "Hammam" was amazing the room & treatment 
The massage was ok 
The down fall of this place was the noise it was not a relaxing place

The steam room is so peaceful. The size alone is wonderful not to mention how relaxed you feel after. The authentic Turkish feel is refreshing after so many other spas look the same. They did a great job renovating and its well worth a visit to unwind. Nice and close to the Thompson hotel, so if you're in town its an easy visit to the spa.

Hammam stands alone in Toronto by offering a co-ed turkish-style steam bath plus spa services.

The steam bath is an oasis from the city's hustle and bustle.  The essential oil scented steam fills a dark, restful grotto where bathers enjoy the reguvinating effects of steam therapy.  The steam bath is by far my favorite - I would go here once per week if time permitted.  Go, spend a few hours and emerge renewed (and your skin will be amazing).

Hammam also offers spa services.  I have had a deep-tissue massage that was perfect.  

Facilities are VERY clean and guests are well attended to.  Hammam is a great spot.

I visited this place a couple months ago as birthday treat to myself. The steam room alone was worth the price of admission. The lighting, eucalyptus oils made this steam room divine and utterly relaxing. They give you sarong to switch into as the stream room is quite HOT!

I didn't feel impressed with the massage while it was happening. I prefer a deep tissue but I thought pressure was kinda light. Regardless, about an hour later.. My body was in the most relaxed state ever. So I suppose the masseuse was doing something right.

The only other minor pet peeve- it was a bit noisy with all the construction going around.

The spa is on the pricey side but I would go back for the steam room alone.

A massage therapist who's name was different than my receipt... makes me wonder who is actually doing my massage and if they are actually credentialed as an RMT. Based on the pathetic massage I received, despite clear instruction for firm deep pressure, I am really wondering who they are hiring. 
Creeky floors above the tea area. 
Difficult to breath in the steamroom. The changing lights make for a somewhat scary psychedelic experience. 
Oversized bathrobes.  

The only thing going for this place is their music which is downloaded onto an ipod. Not worth $200... thank goodness for insurance coverage or I'd be livid.

I had a really nice day at Hammam.

I bought the Rest package for my mother for her birthday and joined her for a massage, facial and manicure. 

The locker rooms were clean, but a bit on the cold side. 

I really like the renovation. The moss on the walls gives the place a really earthy feel, and the manicure area has beautiful plants along the back wall. 

We arrived early and used the Hammam steam room before our services. We were the only ones in there, which was really nice.  

We had: 

Swedish massage, facial, manicure. All of my services were excellent and the attendants were friendly knowledgeable. Also, the person who booked us put us in a couple's treatment room at no extra cost, which we both really appreciated. 

Hammam Spa is nicer than the casual places, and more casual than the ultra-luxurious spas. The prices are reflective of this. I think our package was extremely well priced at $339 each, taxes in. 

I will definitely return to Hammam!

Took advantage of an AMEX delights special for some well deserved pampering.   I thought I would use it in the deep dark depths of winter but as is common with these coupon things, you tend to forget.  By fate or fortune I called  on the very last day the voucher was supposed to expire luckily, Hammam was very accommodating and allowed me to make an appointment for a couple weeks after.  

The Spa itself is beautiful, warm and offers a surprisingly serene respite away from the hustle bustle of King Street despite being in the lower level of the building.  Decor was comfortable and very well appointed.  Kudos to the designers for creating such a comfortable space.  It's chic without appearing too "feminine" and modern without being stark.  Men and women alike would feel right at home in this environment.  It is kept impeccably clean by a constant attendant making sure that all towels are not left strewn about, the floors are clean and everything is tidy.

Reception and the staff were all polite and very welcoming.  

My voucher included a 1 hr massage, manicure and pedicure as well as use of the steam room.  

The massage was good, not the best I have had but in fairness I do have a regular RMT whom i am convinced is the best RMT in world so anyone else have to have magical hands to better him.  That being said, the RMT was professional, accommodating and i melted into the hour.  

My manicure and pedicure were equally good.  She was terrific, cleaned and clipped my nails, hand massage followed by a dip in parrafin wax.  My feet and hands never felt smoother or cleaner.  The scrubs and lotions that Hammam uses are top notch and smell almost good enough to eat.  

Hammam's steam room is co-ed but nice and hot, the steam is perfumed with eucalyptus and other herbs and is lit by a ever changing LEDs.  Just be sure to keep yourself wrapped up to avoid embarrassment.  

I would rate Hammam a bit higher were it not for the sky high prices of their services.  I was grateful to have had all that pampering for a not unreasonable $200 but I would be hard pressed to have paid regular price (amounting to almost $400).

The staff are great, the spa is beautiful.  Hammam is a Great experience overall.

Have been wanting to visit for awhile and managed to make it here on a Sunday at 6 pm.  We didn't realize that they close at 7 and so there was no opportunity to try the steam room.  As other reviews have mentioned, the customer service needs a little work.  As first time visitors a health form was required to be completed before the massage.  We completed the form and we were shown to the waiting area.  We were confused as usually you get into a robe and slippers before a massage.  We asked again and the woman who showed us in told us she thought we were there for pedicures.  Seemed strange but however.... We were now running later and had to quickly change as our massage therapists were waiting for us.  The massage was great!  No complaints at all about the massage.  45 minute massage was $130 which is quite pricey.  The decor is nice and the massage was great.  Overall it was an ok experience.  It probably won't be my go to location fir a massage though.

I could get used to this kind of luxury. 
The spa was very nice, they have a nice spot for you to go read magazine and drink tea or water and have fruit. Gorgeous. The steam baths are crazy cool, too, though if you go at a peak time like after work, they get pretty crowded. 
The massage was solid, though not as strong as I would have liked. 
I wish I could afford coming here more often.

First of all, I'd like to observe I didn't have any "spa service" there. I went for a shellac manicure just because it's across the street from my work - super convenient. 

It's a beautiful, super clean, well decorated spa. They will treat you like a princess. Everything smells like paradise. I was waiting in a beautiful room for my manicure, who asked me if I wanted standard shellac or this new "gellish", which she preferred, because it lasted longer and the results were awesome. I was sold. I want that, now. 

Then, paradise suddenly disappeared. The manicure chairs were not so comfy - I am small and had to bend over the table for her to reach my hands. The amazing fantastic gellish polish was just not amazing, and after two applications in both hands, and lots of " trying to fix this", she finally agreed that it was awful and the amazing gellish she was using was not of good quality, and she had to remove it. Fallback to standard shellac, simple, fast application. But I spent one hour and a half there. And the most expensive manicure of my life.  And didn't even get a hand massage!!!!! 

Not coming back AT ALL. For 50 bucks,  they should have covered me in gold! This must be a joke!

I have always loved this place! I feel instantly relaxed the second I walk in, I feel so pampered in the robes they provide and love the opportunity to relax ahead of time in their gorgeous steam room, and the massages and customer service are always amazing. 

I didn't think it could get any better, but this weekend they outdid themselves. I bought a gift certificate for a friend's bday, and somehow between there and home I lost it. I was absolutely devastated at the thought of spending all that money again. I called nearly in tears to see what they could do and Ferelith was an absolute angel. She calmed me down, and said she would cancel the gift card and issue me a new one since she had all my info on file. By the time I showed up she had everything ready for me. I could have kissed her she was so kind to me. Now that's what I call service. I loved this place before, and is now my only spa of choice! You have my forever loyalty Hammam.

Not the best around for $135 / 1h massage.

Perhaps Hammam Spa was better when it opened; but the interior is beginning to feel and look tired and run-down. 

The lobby / entrance feels and looks dirty. It is difficult to tell if the light coloured bamboo floors are just dirty or stained from years of use. Either way, it detracts from the overall first impression. Not the end of the world.

The men's washroom / changeroom floor suffered from the same dirty/stained appearance (not pleasant when you're walking around in bare feet). The washroom area again, looked either dirty or stained from years of use. Clearly, the fixtures and finishings are tired and worn. The showers are dark, claustrophobic, and grimy feeling. The shower door frames had clearly been welded backtogether following a failure; but the sloppy weld job and exposed cracked tiles were signs that this place needs some serious investment. The hot water suddenly ceased to flow during the shower, leaving me in fridgid water for about a minute; pleasant! The shower faucet was covered in some kind of grease or gunky soap scum. I feel like the lighting was intentionally dark, not for ambiance, but to hide the decay.

My massage was ho-hum. I feel like my tiny RMT was overwhelmed by the amount of effort requried to work out my kinks... perhaps my fault for not requesting someone stronger. You do not get to choose your music (Bob Marley covers done with a sitar?) nor your massage oil. The RMT was nice enough to to bring water / tea at the end of the massage. 

The co-ed steam bath is ok? I feel as if Hammam is trying to pass this off as a feature simply because they do not actually have enough room for separate facilities. 

The reception staff were friendly and courteous. Though during check out, only one staff member was present and apparently she was getting and earful on the phone from the owner. I felt bad for her as she looked incredibly apologetic to the line up of customers waiting to pay; but probably felt as if she couldn't tell the owner to shut up for a minute. (Where was the other cashier??)

Not sure I'd go back. 
For a few more dollars, Stillwater offers a much more pleasant spa experience. 
If you just want a massage without the spa add-ons, avoid this place - just have your SO do it.

This has been my go to spa for many years. I am always very happy with the costumer service, the decor and the facilities. The two main reasons I keep returning - my fabulous massage therapist and the steam room. The renovated steam room is beautiful and I have had no issues with temperature.

I would probably be considered one of those "chatty bitches" that the reviewer below is referring to. Well, not in a rude way, because I maintain spa etiquette but if you go to the spa with a friend, you tend to chat.... Anyway....

My best gal pal and I went to Hammam on the weekend because my hubby got me a gift card for Christmas. Hey, I spend my days chasing around our busy little 11 month old. I deserve it. He booked a Turkish bath for me and a signature pedicure so my friend booked the same and we requested a couples room for our bath so that we could do it together, which is more fun. 

I've been to spas before, but of course, but never a Turkish one. It's very pretty inside but if you look closely, you can sorta see the "basement-y" thing going on. The change room was excellent, very clean with everything you need there for your skin and hair if you forgot. Great plush robes and slippers are included. The spa has a pleasant scent as well, very incense-y. We hit the steam room and it was WAY way WAY WAAAAAY too hot for me. I'm not one for heat intensity like that but my friend convinced me to not turn around and walk right out so we sat down (and were probably "chatty bitches" at this point) and it wasn't too bad. Until the light turned red. They have this slowly flashing colored light, blue, green, yellow and then red. The red is AWFUL! It literally makes me you feel like you're in some kind of inferno! NOT RELAXING!!! Then my friend joked that a serial killer could lock us in there and that'd be it and that was it for me! Buh bye steam room! It's just extremely hard to breathe in there. Good to warm up in, that's for sure.

We started our bath. They had us lay down together on a marble slab. It felt great, very relaxing but both of our backs started aching from laying on the hard stone. They splashed us with water from bowls for an hour and then did a scrub, then soap, then finished with oil. It was definitely a fun experience but I can splash water on myself at home. For much cheaper than what this cost. But, overall, it was cool, fun, and felt good. 

Next they took us to the tea room and gave us some snacks--dates and halva. Apparently the snacks are only for the people who do the bath. We had some yummy tea and I started to get colder, and colder... and colder.... it was VERY chilly after being in the heat. Not so good. They did not time manage well and we ended up waiting probably 45 min between procedures. That's ok if you're not pressed for time. 

I have to give the pedicure 1 star. That's it. It kinda sucked. My friend's pedi also sucked. 

It was $75 and the Vietnamese nail salon that normally does my nails did a 100 times better for 1/3rd of the price. They didn't do much for the skin on my feet here though the paraffin was ok. She barely did the foot massage. For that amount of money, I expected more. The polish selection is excellent and she applied well but my friend's polish didn't dry! We sat under the dyers for a good 40 minutes and her's was still sticky and they ended up giving her 50% off the price. 

Overall my experience was positive was but not extraordinary. We had a great time and felt great afterwards too but the day cost about $250 (including tip) per person and we only had two treatments. I didn't feel it was worth that price at all. It's certainly not bad here but certainly not amazing. 3/5 stars, middle of the road. I would probably not go back unless I got another gift card in which case I'd definitely try a facial and massage instead. I must compliment the staff here in general though because they are very friendly, very accomodating and they make you feel like a queen, no matter what treatment you're doing. Everyone who interacted with us was very, very nice.

Oh and BIG THUMBS DOWN for not being wheelchair-accessible. That's inexcusable.

Having been to Hammam Spa many years ago and remembering the great experience; my lovely beau and I decided to check it out again on my birthday last week. We treated ourselves to a Turkish Hammam bath treatment as it seemed fitting to bring in my new year feeling cleansed, relaxed and purified.

We arrived an hour prior to our appointment to enjoy the hammam and were greeted by a lovely receptionist who gave us a quick refresher of the spa. Since our appointment was on a weekday mid day we pretty much had the whole spa and hammam to ourselves, which I loved. 

I didn't know what to expect of the bath since we've never had a Turkish bath before but it was a nice experience to share with my love. It was a lot shorter than the 1 hr 10 mins. it was suppose to be so I doubt we'll try it again but the attendants were very informative during the treatment.

Although I loved the way it made my skin feel afterwards we won't be returning. Some of the reviews I read here turned out to be true even though I was really hoping it wouldn't. The hammam did smell funky at some points and we both ended up sick a day after. Coincidence much??

I've had multiple services now and feel like I can write a review. The spa itself is beautiful, and with prices that reflect some of that luxury as well. For the price you pay for some services they are definitely not worth it:

Manicure : regular manicure . Very disappointing both mine and my friends chipped the night of, and within one day chipped so much that we both had to take it off. Don't know if it's the products or cream that caused it to do that but for that price I expect it  to last a bit longer than 24 hours . She's called the spa, took pictures of her nails and is waiting to hear back . 

Massage: great massage each time regardless who did it 

Paraffin wax for feet : felt nice, made my feet feel smooth 

Facial: okay. Felt that while masks were drying, no one was attending to me . I've been in places where at that time someone massages you etc I also usually need lots of extractions, and I know those were not done as attentively as they were in other places . I expect a bit more for that price . I had this done twice now with similar styles 

Steam room: excellent 

Atmosphere : great relaxing 

Would never get a manicure here again. Some of the other services I might consider going back as I do enjoy the steam room or if I get receive it as a gift 

Update: Management reached out to me and gave me a credit on the manicure which is very impressive on their end. I went back to get another facial during their promo in March and it was definitely worth the time and money I spent. Great job Hamman spa - I felt the services I received were well worth it

My girlfriend booked a couple massage, which was OK, but not spectacular. Well, actually she really liked hers, said it was the second best massage she ever got (I guess the one I gave her was the 1st best :). I think I may be more demanding, so I would only give mine 3.5 out of 5. Also, it's a little on the expensive side - price was $125 each for 1-hour RMT massage. 

On the good note, the steam room (which is included in the price) is fantastic - the decor, the amount of steam, the temperature, the scent - everything is perfectly balanced and puts you into blissful tranquility if you're able to relax in a coed environment. The water decorated by citrus, the large silent TV screen and clean elegance is a nice touch.

I just DON'T GET IT!
ok, this is my 2nd time here and I hated both experiences.

Disclaimer: I hate spas or any type of salon that requires someone you don't know touching you.  The most acceptable form of touch I will tolerate from a stranger is a high 5 and I give those out generously and graciously.
That being said, I still feel like I am somewhat qualified to rate this spa because I have been forced to endure these types of events through friends, "girls days" & dates- despite my protestations that they are an offensive waste of money for an experience I despise.

Things I generally want from my spa experience (not unlike a date): 
1) I want you to be nice from start to finish.  Be welcoming, speak w/ me and not at me.  
2) Ask me what I enjoy instead of assuming whatever you have planned is what I'm up for.  
3) Offer me tea, coffee and something delicious or sweet.  You have no idea the additional bonus this provides when you just offer someone some nice tea.
4) Be clean and don't ever make me question the cleanliness of your premises.
5) Allow me to be me.  Don't force it upon me that I have to be in a specific "zone" of meditation or whatnot.  I will be as quiet or as loud as I please in your establishment and you have to deal with it.

Ok, onto the review- the First time I went was on a girlfriend date where the boyfriend booked a package and we enjoyed it on his dime.
It included a steam, couples bath, and couples massage.  It was a romantic gesture but to maintain a friendship we skipped the couples bath : )
I do believe this package cost somewhere in the 500$ range... yeah..spendy.... and it was meant to be "enjoyed" over 3 hours.
First of all the place was clean but not particularly inviting.  The staff are pretty meh.
They ask you to change in a very nice clean changeroom and then you sit in a side room where they have self-serve tea/coffee, cucumber sandwiches and fruit.  It was alright.
We tried the steam room but I have to say that was the most UNENJOYABLE steam room possible. It was super dark, SUPER hot and impossible to see more than an inch in front of you.  YES, I UNDERSTAND how steam rooms work.  But this one was just ridiculous.  I felt like this was a horror movie and I was going to be attacked any second.  I also questioned the cleanliness of such a room because I can imagine people contaminating it with their public sex.  Honestly..someone could have been having sex RIGHT beside me and I wouldnt' have known becuase it was SOOOO dark in there.
Then we were introduced to our masseuses and they were very gracious.  
The massage was ok but nowhere during the time that I lied down to the end did he ask me how it was going or what type of pressure I enjoyed.  The entire experience was PAINful.  If you enjoy deep tissue massacres I would highly suggest this place.  But if you are more into a nice backrub this is not the place.

Finally, they let us relax and chat in the room...but when we got too giggly (as we do when gossiping) they came in and SHUSHED us.  
Seriously..really?
really?

REALLY?
I don't think so.

ok, so second time I was here happened just recently on a third date with a person I THOUGHT I liked but will likely never go out with again due to all disregard of LISTENING to me and reading the type of person I am.  Really, if I say I don't like spas...don't think a spa date is going to be a wonderful surprise that I will enjoy blindly.
He had already planned the whole day and was super excited (he loves getting manssages) and I had minor protestations but like...he had planned the WHOLE day already.. And I love people who plan.  But it was just a poor choice if you knew me....

So I went along with it.

He booked a special lunch at the spa w/ different gourmet coffee and coffee inspired food.  
Then he booked a coffee scrub for me and a seaweed wrap for himself.  
I looked it up and it seems like they were 120 and 140 respectively.
We had a huge convo about "detoxing" etc etc and thought it would be a fun treat- I got to enjoy my own room and it was nice and soothing, although I must say that the rooms themselves are nothing special except for clean, dimly lit rooms with a lot of White.

The coffee scrub was incredibly uncomfortable and confusing.  I have never got a fully body treatment where they lather you up in types of edible or inedible things that you have to promise NOT to eat..but this experience was just as bad as you might imagine for someone who hates spas and general touching.

The smell was divine but basically I felt like I was a baby resisting bath time and, honestly...was even kind of squirming around like a baby with my limbs resisting the treatment.
The person wasn't especially chatty and wanted to like, put me in some sort of yoga-zone w/ stupid "eastern" music that made me want to write an additional chapter of Said's Orientalism...
The entire thing ended quite unceremoniously with me w/ me wanting to take a shower.

never again, Hammam spa..never again

I had a wonderful time at this place . I booked a 30 min massage for myself and my friend since I lost a bet in a game of scrabble. We came about an hour early as traffic was light on Sunday and the reception kindly greeted us, they even offered complimentary use of the Hammam steam room even though it was not included in our services. Inside the spa we were given a tour of the waiting area where you get fruits, cranberries, walnuts, cranberry juice and water. A selection of lifestyle magazines are also available.The change room is stocked with amenities like hair dryer, hair spray, gel, towels, flip flops, the digital locker inside contains a robe and a wrap for each guest. Overall the showers and change-room is very clean. Afterward my friend and I went to the steam room which is across from the Turkish baths. The steam room is hot and steamy , and the ice cold towels made it super soothing and relaxing. Interestingly we had the whole steam room to ourselves which was really neat. The massage was awesome too, my masseuse was on point throughout the whole massage. By the end of the massage it felt more like 45 minutes have gone by instead of 30 minutes. Overall I had a fantastic experience and would look into the Hammam Turkish bath experience.

I have to say I've been here quite a few times and it seems like the service is just going down the hill. I've always had the Turkish bath and used the steam room but lately from the rude attitude of the employees to the shower not working properly or just filthy and the towels being dirty you wonder why all the bad reviews. The last time I was there was Oct 24th, and received rude welcome and goodbyes, shower not working properly and just dirty as well as doors not being able to close. The worst part is, my '60 minutes Turkish bath' was 35 minutes, how do I know that? Because I timed it!!! I've noticed the last few visits have been at the most 40 minutes treatment. Although she was good, I have to say, I felt ripped off. I don't think I will ever come back or recommend this place.

I booked a facial at Hammam in the midst of going through some very hard times in my personal life. I wanted to get the most of it so specifically booked Hamman so I could relax in the steam room first. My facial service was incredible. I forget the name of the amazing therapist, but she was blonde and had hipster tortoise shell glasses. 

It was a blonde girl at the front desk who completely ruined the experience for me and upset me for the rest of the day. What  I thought was a 1pm facial, was actually at 130pm. When I checked in and said "I had a 1pm facial" I was not corrected. So I planned my visit accordingly and was waiting in the tea room at 1pm for my service.  By 115pm I had not been retrieved so I went to the front desk to inquire. I was told fairly rudely that my service was at 130pm to which I replied I thought it was at 1pm, no one had told me differently...to which I was told to go sit down and wait. I asked that they tell my friend, who had a massage at 1pm and would be done at 2pm, that I'd be a half hour later, to which they said no problem and then did nothing about.

Like I said, the actual facial was incredible but when I went to pay a young woman at the front asked me how my time was and I admitted I was a little annoyed that the time of my service had been messed up... that's when this blonde woman (not dressed in their traditional black so perhaps she is a manager, in which case she should be fired for not knowing how to speak to clients) started barking at me that "she remembered taking the appointment and it was at 130pm...."  and so on...to which I said ok and that I felt that she was attacking me, but in return did not receive apology from her or anything after her uncalled for outburst.  I did not go to Hamman to be attacked by the front desk staff and if it was the case that I did get my times mixed up, customer right or wrong, that is NO way to treat a client, anyone should know better.   I  was distraught for the rest of the day, unsure why this "manager" or whoever she was would yell at me as she did when my visit was to relieve myself of stress not be treated to more. 

There are many good places to get a facial in the city and unfortunately after this experience and being treated so rudely by the front desk staff, one woman in particular, there is no reason why I would return.

Went here with my best friend today, best facials experience in my life! Reception/Administration seemed a little disorganized, but service as a whole was good! Awesome steam room and nice that it is coed.

Decided to come here for my bday, had a massage and a facial. I wrote a feedback letter regarding my facial, and how time was cut short, hand/foot massage was skipped, another concern was she came to get me 10mins into my appointment which had nothing to do with me, left me for long lengths of time to have me change which I already was and to get product. Once she started the service everything she put on my face was quickly removed. This is not my first facial I know how long it feels and I've never felt so rushed. 
Totally disappointed never coming back! especially after spending over $300. 



This is the response I got back from the spa 


Hi Kelly,
 
Thank you for sending us your feedback, I am glad that you've had amazing experiences with us. I have taken the time to review your feedback regarding the facial service that you received yesterday.
 
With regards to timing I checked our security cameras from the hallway outside of the treatment room to verify service times. I did notice that the length of times that your service provider left for you to change and to dispense products were normal periods of time for the service provider to leave, 2 minutes to get settled into the room and 4 minutes to dispense product. I understand that it can feel like a longer stretch of time. I did double check and the overall treatment time was 53 minutes. The facial is listed as a 60 minute service but there are a few variable minutes depending on the clients skincare needs.
 
Regarding your concern about missing the hand massage and hot towels I will share your feedback with the service provider when she returns tomorrow in order to discuss improvements.
 
Thank you again for your feedback.
 
Sincerely,
 
Victoria

Don't understand some of the negative reviews on here. This place is amazing and the staff are nice. 

I had a one hour Swedish massage and a Turkish Bath. Let me tell you that massage was heaven! I got a full body massage by a male RMT (forgot his name) and he gave me the best, most relaxing massage of my life! As for the Turkish bath, omg, my skin is still super soft and hydrated from it four days later. I've never had one before so it was a new experience for me. You basically have do lay down on a marble table looking thing and the lady will dump water all over your body, followed by an exfoliation of the whole body, then puts these huge bubbles on you (this part is really cool), and then rubs you down with black soap, and finally, pours water on you again. After that you turn around on your stomach so she can repeat the same process for the back. My lady's name was really nice (I believe her name is Michelle, sorry I forgot again). And I don't want to forget the steam room--it's definitely the biggest and most beautiful steam room I've ever been in. The relaxing coloured lighting and the smell of aromatic scents  really sets the tone and relaxes you; just don't forget to stay hydrated. As I mentioned early my skin is so soft still! Like I don't even have to wear any lotion so my skin won't dry up and crack, it's just that hydrated. 

And while waiting in between each service there is a tea room which is basically a lounge area where you can sip on tea or lemon water and fruit juice, and munch on snacks such as apples, almonds, cranberries. There is also a bunch of magazines to choose from that you can read to kill time. 

This is a luxury I definitely could get used to once a month. I'd definitely come back and I'd be happy to recommend this place to anyone looking for a couple hours of relaxation

Incredible.  A piece of heaven in downtown Toronto.  I cannot believe I have lived in King West Village for a year and not found this place.  The steam room is incredible, the customer service stupendous and the massages fabulous.  I also rescheduled the massages same day a few days ago due to an emergency and it was rescheduled without charge. Wow.  I found my new favourite place.

Nice atmosphere. Service left a bit to be desired.
For a tea room- would be nice if someone brought you tea, or there is tea to choose from? I just saw water and a juice.

Facial- The lady who performed the facial was very nice and friendly. I would've liked to know the products she was using on me, usually a facialist will say "you have oily skin so I am using X.... There was also very little extraction, which is the main reason I get facials. She only did my nose. The massage was also quite weak, and lasted about 5 minutes.

I asked the facialist if I could have a robe, so I could go from facial to steam room, without having to get my body lotion all over my clothes. She told me to get one from the front desk. I ended up just getting dressed and leaving. This is a small detail,but it would've made my experience 10X better. 

As I paid, she gave me a sample bag of product for "older" skin, at 25 with oily skin, that is hardly a concern, and would've liked product that worked for my skin type.

I don't think I would return, for the price, there are much better places for facials in Toronto

I just had a fantastic experience here and felt I need to share. First off, the place is very pretty. I just felt good as soon as I came in. Nice music and decor, lovely music, and very clean. I arrived a bit early for my appointment and was shown to a relaxing waiting room, equipped with refreshments. 

Once my appointment time came around, the esthetician showed me to the a comfy seat where she was going to give me a pedicure. Before she began, I was offered more refreshments. 

She was very gentle with my feet. The massage felt like heaven. And the wax treatment was phenomenal. By the time she was done, the awfulness of winter had melted away from my feet. They felt soft again, and my nails looked amazing. Definitely beach worthy.

When I went under the nail dryer I accepted her second offer of refreshments, and asked for water. It had a hint of cucumber; very refreshing indeed. 

I plan on returning to try out other services.

My Honey thought it great to send me off for a day at the Spa. Very thankful  unfortunately for the price the experience was not great. Massage was great ,all the loud talking and noise throughout the rest of my time was in no way relaxing. I do prefer a little privacy while taking all my clothes off to put on robe. No privacy
Turkish bath was amazing. More focus on feet as well next time. Will be back forsure . What a treat

Low rating because mediocre customer service. Unfriendly receptionist and masseuses. Went for couple's massage. Massage was just average as well. The only friendly people were the filipino workers, whose vibe already felt friendly without even speaking to them, but the receptionists really seem cold and even if they try to act polite, you still feel like it's not genuine. The place itself is nice, steam room is nice but could be hotter. Lounge room is cozy. Changeroom is alright, not as fancy as other high-end spas but still okay. What killed the experience was the unfriendly staff. Management should do a better job at hiring genuinely friendly people. Customer service makes a big difference

This place is AMAZING!! My boyfriend and I got a couple's Swedish massage. My massage was so relaxing (although my bf said his massage was painful). The steam room which you get to enjoy before and after your massage is incredible. I really enjoyed my first visit and will definitely be going back.
The service at the desk here was horrible and rude. Simple thing like paying for a friend massage was complicated! Nothing to say about the therapist but service at the front should be improved.

This place seems quite polarizing based on previous Yelp reviews, so I wasn't sure what to expect. But I came here mainly wanting to check out the hammam experience. This place has been around for a long time, but I never came before because the prices seemed way too high. But they are offering 20% off all online booking this month, so I decided to use my insurance RMT benefits and try it out. A 60 mins. Swedish massage came to $112 instead of $140. Yes, it's expensive but with any service over $100 you get free access to the hammam.

I had a really relaxing experience here, despite it being a busy Saturday. There were a lot of people but it somehow never felt crowded, I never had to wait for a shower, and there was always room to sit in the tea lounge. There were a few instances were people were talking loudly in the changeroom, but generally, I found it much quieter and more relaxing than Body Blitz. It's also nice that it's co-ed (but it means you have to wear either a bathing suit or the wrap they give you... I brought my swimsuit because I think the wrap would still be kinda risque).

From start to finish, the service was excellent. I was given a walk around of the place and the facilities are really clean. Staff were constantly walking around clearing used towels, empty cups, etc. Everything smells amazing too! Eucalyptus oil everywhere... The change rooms have lockers and you can set the code (i.e. no having to keep track of a key). They provide robes (which are enormous, but I have never found a spa where they have small size robes) and slippers (which thankfully come in S/M/L/XL). There are rain showers and all the basics -- blow dryers, hair straightener, body lotion. But bring your own hairbrush. 

After taking a shower, I went to the steam room. It was a lot larger than I expected. It is very steamy and you can barely see in front of you, but there's lots of room to sit and enjoy. It might be too hot for some people, but I loved it. I have been to hammams in Europe before and this was similar. In the hammam area, there are also showers to rinse off, a fridge with cool towels and cucumber water, and 2 suites (for if you buy a package that includes gommage scrub). I went back and forth between the steam room and the tea lounge (which has hot and iced tea, fruit, and magazines). You don't need to watch the time for your booked service, because once you arrive the staff know you are in the facility so they will call your name either in the steam room or the lounge. I thought that was nice, but it still would've been useful to have a clock somewhere. 

My massage was with Connie, and it was great. Some people find the service rooms noisy (you can hear people walk by), but I was in a room that was farther away and it was fine. Connie checked in a few times to make sure the pressure was good. I didn't have any particular area of focus, but found the massage really relaxing and almost fell asleep... The massage table is heated too, which was nice. 

Overall, this was a great escape in the middle of the city and the only reason I wouldn't give it 5 stars is because it is so expensive (I wish we had a hammam experience in Toronto that was more social and affordable enough that one could go regularly). But it is definitely a nice treat!

Staff was great as there was a mix up with the bookings. They were able to call in a back up therapist and have him start within the hour. They also gave me a gift bag of goodies which was unnecessary but an excellent touch. The baths were great - super clean & beautiful. Maintenance staff was very attentive- love the fresh fruit waters. My Rmt was excellent, incorporating a variety of massage styles into my treatment to ensure I left feeling great!

I wasn't going to write this review.
I find writing negative reviews take up a lot of emotional energy, But, after a bit of thought, if I can save someone else from a shitty experience, it's the least I can do. 

So here it goes.

I live a block away from this spa, so I was hoping this would be a good alternative for when my usual go-to is booked up. Plus, I'm a big spa junky.  

I booked my DERMALOGICA CUSTOM FACIAL online. Super convenient, and I could even request a reminder via SMS. Great. 

I arrived 15 minutes early, and opted out of the unisex Turkish bath room. 
I was guided to the change room by an uninterested girl who worked the front desk. She pointed at a locker at the very entrance of the change room and told me I could undress, and then go wait in the tea room. I had to ask where the tea room was. This was my first visit, which she was aware of, as she asked me when I checked in. 

The change room was noisy, and cold. and there was NO privacy. There's a circular seating cushion thing in the centre of the change room, and then rows of lockers.  I tried to back up into a corner to remove my clothing, just to get a bit of privacy,  and then realized I was backing up into a full length wall mirror. Awesome.  
I slipped on a massive, one sized fits no-one robe, and then realized I didn't know where the flip flops were. ARE there flip flops?! I asked a naked lady in the change room, and she showed me where they were. 

I wandered out of the change room (with very little under my robe), and realized I was standing in the main hallway, steps away from the reception. More, open, and COLD. I quickly walked down the hallway in the opposite direction, hoping I was going to the right spot, and found the tea waiting room. It reminded me of a nicer VIP lounge at an airport. Circular chairs, with magazines. They had a set up of boiling water, and tea .. and water, glasses, ect. 
I just sat there. Waiting. For what? I wasn't even sure yet. I just hoped they hadn't forgotten about me ...

Out popped a very loud lady from behind a partition,  who turned out to be the one doing my facial. Her name was Tanya. **Word of the wise, don't get TANYA if you don't like LOUD TALKERS. :(
She shook my hand, introduced herself, and I followed to my treatment room. I was disappointed of the location of the rooms. They're at the end of the noisy, drafty hallway. I could very clearly hear people chatting and talking that were in the tea room, and even at one point, heard laughing from the reception area. 
This is a very busy spa. Very high traffic.   
I heard lots of flip flops and people chatting & giggling as they passed our treatment room, heading to other rooms. Again, noisy and distracting. It also didn't help that my facial lady left the room 3 times. I'm really detail oriented, and I couldn't help but time her 'departures'. The first she left, she was gone for 11 minutes. The 2nd time, 8 minutes, the 3rd, 10 minutes. She didn't tell me she was leaving, nor WHY she was leaving. I'd hear the door open and then slam shut. Damn. I'm laying on that table, pretty much naked with a sheet covering barely my boobs, and she's opening and closing the door ... people passing by, and a draft of cold entering the room each time.
 
She put some stuff on my face (again, she didn't tell me anything) and when she didn't talk to me, she asked me what I did about those 'black hairs' on my chin. Lovely. Way to be sensitive.  She told she forgot her tweezers, so she couldn't remove them. I had NO blackheads for her to remove. Literally, nothing to squeeze. Hm .... 

She did another wash, and she was really rough. By the end of my facial, my little nose ring was all red from the tugging and pulling she didn't even seem to realize she was doing. It actually really freakin' hurt. She was whipping her hands around in a sloppy application. The mask she did ended up in the corners of my mouth. She had no idea, and I had to use the edge of the sheet to get it out of my mouth. 

Maybe I"ve been REALLY REALLY REALLY spoiled by the beautiful facials I get at my usual place, but it made me realize what a difference a sensitive touch can make. At one point, she was moving around, running water harshly, flipping around her flip flops .. I had no idea what the hell she was doing, but I literally jumped because she put something on my face and I had no idea she was at my head again. UGH. Not relaxing. 

When she did talk, it was to tell me about the mask I was getting for free, promo of the month, and in the same breathe, she started telling me I should book another appointment with her in 3-4 weeks for one of the $75 treatments. WTF. I wasn't even done my facial. I have to emphasize, this lady was LOUD. Really really loud. And she kept repeating the costs of everything. (??!!!??!?!)

I've run out of Yelp comment space (!) but you get the picture. That lady is INSANE if she thinks I'd be rebooking an appointment with her. I'll never return to Hammam again

This spa is sub par and should really take a second look at its delivery. I'm surprised its received such reviews. I've been to many spa places in the city and this one is by far the worst. 

One star off because the massage itself was just okay. We had a couple massage, I had an aromatherapy and my partner had a deep tissue. Even upon a little instruction by us the RMTs failed to adjust their styles - frustrating. This is especially annoying when the place charges WAY more than it should for massages. Is this a cash cow kind of place?t
Another star off, The place is terribly used for space. The male washroom was small. The faucets were broken and slippers were way to small. Is this place only for small people?

Another star off because the space is terribly used. Its small, does not remind one at all of a true gamma experience besides the pictures on the wall. Not even a small bit. The steam room was nice but really the LEDs lights were over stimulating. In fact, the music was like a club - probably to suit the demographic of the neighborhood.
