                  9:00am-3:00pm Saturday

This post office does a fairly job, I like them since they quick and smile at me often.

I needed a certified letter to them help with and they did, thank gof!

I was soo happy they wer able to help and make sur they helped out.
One of the worst post office I have ever been to. The wait is crazy. With 2 people waiting on you. And moving at a very slow speed your better off going to the main post office.

Pretty much have no one has any idea what is going on. I have been here five times in the last three weeks have no mail and no key to get my mail. I have all my receipts yet they have no idea what the status is on getting a key and why my old mail key doesn't work. I am positive I have mail to pick up but yet they don't know where it is. I don't know how this place is still operating. Good luck getting answers out of this place.

I liked this post office until today. This is the closest post office to my home since I live in Southern Highlands. Two days ago I sold an item & went to this location to ship it. I have my 9 month old in my arms and the nice gentlemen at the end assembled the box & taped the label since he could clearly see that I had my hands full. He kept a smile on his face the entire time and was super polite. 

I go in today to ship something & don't even get greeted by the woman who ends up helping me... Or not helping me. She quickly had a horrible attitude when I set the box, my item, & the label on the counter. She rolled her eyes when she realized that it was a paper label and would need to be taped. She told me I would have to assemble to box away from her section, BUY tape, and then go back through the line. I politely told her that the gentlemen two stations down helped me last time and definitely didn't make me buy tape. She quickly said, "Well, I don't have tape here." That same sweet gentleman offered to bring tape to her & she declined. So wait..... Someone is WILLING to be nice and hospitable and you say no?

I asked her nicely to please help me out that I was on my way out of town & she told me that I'd have to wait in line again and see if I got someone different.

Look lady, I get it. It's Friday & you're counting down the hours before You get to walk out that door and go play Bingo, but for the love of God, if you can't at least put a smile on your face... Go away. Retire. Quit working with the general public.

If I could give zero stars I would!!! WARNING! DO NOT waste your time, breath, or energy here!! The management is unprofessional, eradic, and by far one of the worst experiences I've ever had dealing with customer care service. I was trying to explain my situation over the phone, and was rudely hung up on mid sentence! I was trying to locate my missing mail, and because on their end it said "delivered", that's all they can "justify" for. All staff members have been rude, unhelpful, unorganized, and UNPROFESSIONAL 100%. Two of the employees I can call out are Mark and Mayra. Do not trust them with any of your shipping! There is a reason why UPS and FedEx are in better standing with customer service and care! Again, I am warning you!! The people who work here are rude and unprofessional people!! SHAME ON YOU USPS FOR NOT SERVING YOUR CUSTOMERS & RECTIFYING GUEST COMPLAINTS!!!
I thought priority mail is 2 days guarantee.. Now i found out its bs.. There is no guarantee for delivery.. Absolute bs..

I dont know if I am always going to the post office at the worst times or what but there is always a long long line!  They had hardly any packaging envelopes or boxes out.  I did not stand in line, I went to the do it yourself computer. much faster.

For the fact that it's a post office, which is the mail equivalent to the DMV, it's pretty well-run. I've never had to wait more than 5 minutes to get anything done here. Maybe I just luck out at the random times that I go. I was in and out just now in less than 5 minutes, and the majority of that time was making myself sure everything was packed correctly and I wrote down the correct address. Woohoo!

I know going to any post office is a pain, but that is rarely the case for me whenever I go to this location. This post office tends to be busy while it is "open" more often than not, but there is always one or two parking spaces available so I can park. As soon as I enter, there is a long line for the counters with employees behind them, but fortunately, I rarely have to deal with that line. Most of my business at a post office is either picking up mail at the PO box, waiting in the much shorter line to pick up a large package at the half door, dropping off letters inside, or using the machine to print postage labels so I can easily drop off my large packages to the left of the machine.

Because my business rarely needs a live employee, I never have to worry about what time it is because this post office is "open" 24-7 if I don't have to go to the counter with the live employees. I deal with the machine if I need to or I drop off mail in the slots. In and out of the post office any time during the day or night and I like that flexibility.

Rude doesn't even begin to describe some of the employees here.  Came for a simple money order and there wasn't a long line (bonus!).  An older man came in and asked a postal employee what type of mailing envelope he should use to mail a DVD he wanted to send to his granddaughter.  The lady snapped at him, "You'll have to wait your turn and when you get to the counter someone can tell you." Really?  Um actually you pick out the correct mailing envelopes before you get up to the counter.  That's why they sell them right next to the line so you have time to fill out the proper info.  I told the man he could do a small bubble mailer and the DVD would be protected.  The lady snapped at me, "Well that might not be the cheapest way." Instead of making a scene I politely smiled and said you work here so you would know.  The only reason this place gets 2 stars is the postal employee who helped me at the counter, Imelda, was very nice and thanked me for coming in.
Quick response to a question I posted on USPS.com led me to the Pebble Rd location. Once there, I found the staff to be very friendly and helpful.

What poor customer service!!!!
I sipped a box priority (2-3 day delivery) via Pebble Post Office on the 8th. As of the 11th, the package was not delivered. After the weekend, I returned to the Post Office to follow up on my package. Once there, I was told there was no way to find it without a receipt. Ok. The package returned to my home on the 17th; over a week after it was to be delivered. 
I call the office and spoke with Cheryl, the supervisor, about what happened. She was of no help. I came to the office directly  after speaking the her. How convenient, she was out within 10 minutes of our conversation. The staff were of no help. Soon as I got into the car, I called them post office to speak with Cheryl. She just happened to be available. What game are these folks playing?? 
Not only do they not want to speak to customers, they don't want to accept responsibility for there terrible service they provide. We pay taxes for that? No wonder the postal offices are closing. These "people" don't care about service, only a pay check. Save us some tax money, close the useless postal service.

The customer service is bad. I feel like the workers hate their job.  Every time I go in one person is at the counter and there is a long line.  No one   acknowledges that another line needs to be opened unless the customers start to complain.  One of the workers was arguing with her coworker and said bitch out loud.  Other than the HORRIBLE customer service this post office is convenient.

The absolute best place to waste your time. How many people does it take to find a package? Anticipate adding at least 30 minutes or more to your visit, no matter how empty or how packed the place is.

Horrible...grrrr went to mail a certified letter walked in at 4:59pm and Amber Green said they were closed. And asked her was there another PO that closed later she told me the nears one. I walked outside and on the door it clearly states they close at 5pm. I went back in and she said "no mamma I block this side off at 5pm" I showed her on my phone and it still was 5pm so how could that be? She said were closed. Asked to speak to a manager. Manager did not won't to come out and talk to me. So Amber says she said were closed. I'm sorry can I speak with her? She's right here. She was helping 2 other customers so I waited. When I finally get to her she tells me I told her to block it off 5mins til. I said but I was in here before 5pm. Well they are closing their register so.... SMH. The managers name was Roxiann Enno. Federal Employees are soooo rude. And its sad to say its nothing we can do about it. I wish I could give a big fat 0 for their rate

I experienced one of the worst customer service here!  I had a package that was missing the my street name. They were unable to deliver it. I called the 1800 number to usps and told the lady the tracking number. She told me the package was at the pebble facility still and I should call them to tell them the street name and have it delivered. The experience gets bad once I call the pebble office. I Call the pebble and one of their rude employees answer and I told her the situation. She asked for the tracking number and I began saying it and she cuts me off saying it's a fedex tracking number so she can't help me. I asked her so what do I need then? And she said I need the usps tracking number. I said how can I get that and she said she "I have no idea". She was incredibly rude. I called fedex and asked how can I get the usps tracking and the young lady told me I just have to put a "92" in front of the fedex tracking number and it becomes the usps tracking. Upset,  I called back and the rude women answered again and I told her I had the tracking number. She put me on hold 3 times,  and finally she said " do you want to pick it up?",  I answered yes. I go there to pick it up and they cannot locate my package. That employee did not do her job and didn't put my package to be picked. Nor did she correct the address that she said she would do. She was rude and very unhelpful. It's incredible that the 1800 number was able to locate my package with the fed ex tracking number because she knows how to do her job. That employee was the worst and I wish I got her name because she basically sabotaged my package into being sent back to the shipper!   Horrible customer service!
This place is the worst.  The majority of the staff are the most miserable-appearing, empty-eyed people I have encountered in quite some time.  The customer service is severely lacking.

This post office sucks! I walked in on a busy day and I walked up to the store section to ask for some tape and before I could even say something the older man that was working the counter said, "If you want to be helped you need to stand in the back of the line."  There was no line for the store portion so I replied to him, I was wondering if I could get some tape, and he answered with an attitude, "You need what?!" So I told him can I get some tape, then he replies to me again, "For what?" Then he starts walking away.  I was so irate that as I was walking away I said, if you don't like your job then you should quit and I called the post office the minute I walked out to make a complaint.  I don't know what it is with some postal workers but they need to learn to respect their customers. I do not care if you are a federal worker, to gain respect, you need to give it!

This Post Office was near the airport which made it convenient for my wife and I before we flew back to Cali.  All we needed to do was grab a flat rate box and ship it out.  We went inside grabbed the box which was easily acceptable and went out to the car to load it up.  

I love that if it fits it ships, and we made it fit.  After we made it back inside we were waiting in line when when a nice old lady needed help with a piece of registered mail.  Since all the employees were busy my wife who works in a law office helped her out.  

While my wife was helping that lady, an employee asked me if I wanted to use the self checkout computer and I looked over and there was a lady using it.  I forgot to say that I was next in line.  So I asked the employee, isn't someone using it, and she said no I can help you.  So I don't know why but I believed her and we walked over there and she said ok just wait behind this lady.  I then asked why would I want to wait when I was next in line so I walked back and the girl that was behind be was being asked to come up to the counter.  

All I could do was laugh and I took my spot back in line and was then helped by a very nice gentlemen who got me out the door very quickly.  

The place was very clean and I would use it again if I ever need to ship something next time I am in Vegas.

Waiting in line of about 10 people, it's 15 minutes till closing time and there is two windows open for helping out the customers in line, until now, they shut one down putting up a window closed sign!!!! Seriously!!! It's only 15 more minutes till closing time!! You couldn't have waited! And it's sooooo hot on here. There is one helpful lady in here working down the line trying to help people out. But leaving open the second window would've helped us in a tremendous way.


I hope a supervisor reads this ....I first went to the self mailing station, put my package on the scale and went to print the postage, the price was $4.95 for regular first class, I went to get my debit card, then realizing I forgot it at home. So I head over to the line and wait, once I get to the window to pay, the price is now $6.95 for the same first class!!!!!!! So I waited 15 minutes in line to pay $2.00 more to use cash!!!!! WOW just wow!

Yesterday I opened my locked mailbox and found a package cut open and empty. It was delivered this way. There was no damaged note with it. 

I brought it to my closest post office (this location) and had little hope of getting my items. After speaking with a friendly manager there, and describing my items to him, he remembers seeing them!! He said sometimes the machine can rip a package open. 

I was so grateful when he walked back upfront with my two lost items. He saved Christmas for me. 

I just wanted to say thanks to the management team there again! I didn't get his name but he was the tallest manager I saw that day. Thank you sir!!
This place is hell and slower than a turtle. Avoid this place at all cost. Not worth the drive over to this location.

idk what's going on!?! but waited over a week for a package and it's says it's been at this location for 6 days and says just departed, when the package is priority with 3 business day maximum wait. idk who working there.  but either they need new staff or some really management because I've never seen such laziness from one location to another. the manager here and staff suck as workers.

Its a post office... what do you expect

At least they have an automated system for self serve for those that arent totally retarded and know how to follow basic instruction. 

Never had an issue here with service
Worst post office in Vegas. Don't bother coming, itll take all day, whatever youre trying to do.

This post office is always so busy! Surprisingly the line moved rather quickly today.... Maybe because they had three postal workers at working at the service desks... The mail pickup line on the other hand, was long and people were getting impatient and just leaving their place in line... I normally go in after hours and use the self-serve kiosk... Less stress then waiting in line with people invading your personal space... Common courtesy people! We don't need to be breathing on each other's necks! Thank you!!!

Wanna hang for 30+ minute each and every time just come here...Grab a PS Vita, make sure u got internet on your phone or just bring a friend for chit chat...Been living in the neighborhood for 6+ years and this place is terrible from day one..

This post office is a great place to meet fun people in line!!!!! The staff is great as well and everyone is professional! However, the lines can take a while to get through and I feel bad for anyone in a hurry!

i cannot wait for the day budget cuts force this place to close!!! you are going to wait an hour to send a package because there is one teller open and four managers watching her!?!  so you and the 40 other people get to wait all day, i will gladly pay the extra for ups/fed ex. and they actually deliver your packages. unlike this post office. they will let them sit in the office for 20+ days because "oh we forgot to deliver it"

FOR THE LOVE OF GOD SHUT DOWN THIS OFFICE!

Unfortunately there always seems to be a long line. But the other reviews on rude service don't seem fair. I've always had pleasant or at the minimum straightforward professional service. That says a lot considering how many grumpy customers these agents handle after the long lines

I've lived in this area approximately 6+ years and I've used the kiosk at this post office many times. I love the efficiency and ease of use. 

However in the past two weeks I've had to go inside three times and interact with the USPS staff. Goodness! Many of them are doing their job, that isn't necessarily the issue. First thing is most of them seem miserable. I mean these people all seem so genuinely unhappy. The next is that on every one of my most recent three interactions, a customer was unhappy and/or frustrated. All three issues were different, but all three customers complained that someone else used to let them do this or someone else told them the could... It just seems like some of the people enjoy saying no. Almost everyone I interacted with was slightly rude or at the least very abrupt.  Two of the young guys working in the back to get your packages are both very nice. Although the woman working back there was very unfriendly. Going forward if I need to speak to a person I would try to go to a different location if possible.

Giving it one star cause i have too. Don't ever drop off mail or packages or anything at this post office. The people who work there steal the mail. I've had many cards never get to where they need too and i've had people send me things to this location and for some reason they always go missing. The manager don't do anything about it either. Avoid this post office if you can.

I have been in line 20 minutes without moving. The service speed would be equivalent to a snail carrying a brick trying to crawl 50 feet. It is really, really bad. I came to pick up a package, I will drive the 20 minutes next time to the next closest post office
Worst post office in Las Vegas. Do not come here for any reason other than dropping off a package. Worst customer service ever.

Okay #1 - they need to hire more staff! 2. I was standing in a line of about 10 people waiting to pick up mail. The girl behind the door was helping a customer. A man came from behind the desk and walked to the line. He helped the man in front of me only, but guess what? In front of the man in front of me was a Latino man, an Asian woman, another ethnic man, and a Latina woman. Behind me was an Asian woman, a Latin woman, and the list continues. The man that was helped was the only Caucasian male in line. Not sure if this was done intentionally, but it sure was rude. If you're going to help customers, start from the front, not the middle! Also, don't only help one person; assist multiple people. Not only that, a man asked to speak to the supervisor. The lady behind the door told him to wait. He waited for 15 minutes! Then that same guy from behind the desk told him that he could not find the supervisor. What the heck?! If I were that man, I would be really mad. Anyway, I've been standing in line for 40 minutes. Wow! I still haven't been helped yet. Luckily, I have the time to spare, but you can see how this is ridiculous. Spread the word please ;).

DO NOT COME TO THIS LOCATION! These people are the rudest most unhappy people in Las Vegas! You can tell they hate their jobs and don't know what customer service is. If I could there would be 0 stars given.

If I could give them less than one star, I would. I constantly schedule pick ups for our customers online orders and they never show up to get them. 3 or 4 days in a row. I receive emails saying they completed the pick ups but they never did. They are lazy individuals, most of them have bad attitudes and they're even worse at job performance. The government should close it down.

Waited in line for 45 mins to renew my daughters passport. Only to get to the front of the line and be told they have to take ten people before me!! Oh and it's their policy!! Then she says there are other post offices that I can go too!!  No wonder people go postal!!

This place is a joke. They don't even deserve one star. Apparently my package was received at their restarted facility and sent back without even an attempt to deliver. Every time I call it's a busy tone and the lady that did answer is honestly a moron. Clearly she speaks no English and has no idea what she's doing. Well with this kind of service usps will go out of business. It's just a matter of days. They steal your packages and say it's lost without even caring.

I don't understand the bad reviews this post office gets. 
The staff is always very friendly and helpful. I have not once had a bad experience there. Yes, the wait can be really long sometimes. But that is not the fault of the staff at the post office. It's the fault of people who come there and ship things that are not boxed up, they don't have the paper work like custom declarations ready, etc. They bring their babies and they are crying etc. The staff is always so patient, friendly and helpful to people who didn't prepare their stuff right. I go there often, and I have never had a bad experience. 
I like to compliment the staff there for their patience with people. I hope that people who read this think about their attitude towards the post office employees a bit, and hopefully appreciate their work a little more.
I like how there is always an employee asking what we need when in line. That speeds up the entire process and helps. I also like the kiosk. It works well for me.

My experience at this post office varies. Sometimes there's no line so you're in and outta there in 5 mins, other times you can barely move with how many people are inside.

If you have a prepaid label you can just go inside, drop off the box in the drop box area, and leave. If you're really paranoid about your package, you are free to wait in line to get a receipt. If you need them to weigh it you have no choice but to wait in line until its your turn. In most cases, someone steps out from behind the counter and uses a hand held device to speed up the process.

They can also take your passport pictures here. I got my picture taken here though and I turned out orange in the picture. Im not sure if the person that took my picture was inexperienced or their camera really just sucks. Either way, this is your warning! Make sure you check what it looks like on their camera.

As far as service, some employees are cheerful and some are just blah.

worst post office ever , they changed our mailbox locks with out giving us a key then put our mail on hold. do not go there if you can avoid it.  it makes sense why the us post office system is losing money.
They only carry flat rate priority boxes...& I am not waiting in a line of 20 people just to buy a darn box I should be getting for free.

Unfriendly Staff........It takes a Supervisor to get anything accomplished! Just another trip to this location where nothing gets accomplished ....I want to move to a different distinct to avoid this place!

This place is awfully. Global Warming is faster. This is fifth time at this location and it keeps getting worse. It does not matter what time of the day. The speed of service is the same - glacial.  

I have never written a review in my life - until today. This location prompted me to action. I feel it is my duty to warn others. I use to think that snail-paced, apathetic postal employees were an urban legend. The service I experienced in both Denver and Tampa was outstanding. There if a postal employee saw a line forming they would call their co-workers for help. Here, if these people see a line and they run to the back. Or they have conversations in front of you, pretending that customers do not exist. 

Find another location or try Stamps.com. I signed up on-line, while waiting in line. After this experience, I plan to do as much business as possible on-line. The Internet has not ruined the USPS business, their slow service and indifferent attitude is what has killed their business. I understand that they will stop delivering on Saturdays, the retail locations are closing and rates are going up.  Less service for more money.  If I ran my business like this, I would not have a business. It's time for competition. Run to another location. It's got to be better than this one.

I moved into a condo about one mile from this P.O., I made sure everyone had my new address since you cannot rely on the USPS to forward anything.  These idiots stamped "return to sender" on all my mail, pay checks included and returned everything back to sender.  I have retreived several pieces, they are addressed perfectly. 

I've been here five weeks now and not even a piece of junk mail yet.  I cannot wait until this worthless organization is disolved and turned over to someone capable of getting out the front door without it hitting them in the ass.  The USPS is by far the biggest failure in the history of US Government. Your days are numbered, I hope and pray.

The "manager" of this post office - Cat Phan is extremely rude and degrades customers in front of the whole lobby! Not to mention the long wait just to talk to someone! He refused to refund a guaranteed next day priority mail express that took two days to get 4 hours away. I paid $18 for next day and it took as long as normal delivery!! He needs to be fired!

Waited in line for about 40 minutes to pick up a package only to be told that it wasn't there. My USPS tracking clearly said that it was left at the post office waiting for me to bring the slip left at my door and brought there to pick up. Their solution was "we just have to print this out and give it to your carrier to find". What. The. F***. For them to find? It was brought back at around 1PM on a Saturday, and given that the post office was closed Sunday and Monday (Presidents' Day) how could it have gotten lost or misplaced in a matter of 4 hours or less...I would give 0, but the woman who was trying to assist me wasn't rude.

first time we went and they told us we needed an appt.  waited almost a month to get this appt and completely aggravated as we waited one hour even tho we had an appt. for a passport. on top of that we did not have copies of our driver licenses so she told us to go to a store and get copies and come back?! after waiting one hour???
and not to mention the slowness 
next will be our third attempt to get a passport for my little one. who knows what it will be this time?

I live right next to this place, so I come here a lot. They don't pack stuff for you, but up can get your needed supplies on site. The lines are usually long, but I think the service is pretty fast. There's usually 3 people servicing the main mailing area. There is an additional person helping get your mail for pickup. Staff is generally friendly, except this one younger lady. They have a great range of stamps at all times which is great if your a collector. I really am surprised at how negative the reviews are. The dmv is way worse.

I go here alot.  The line is usually always super long and some of the workers are not too friendly.  If you go at a not too busy time, then you can get in and out fairly quickly.  They do have a self serve machine if your items are quick and easy to mail.

Freakin horrible.  Every Time a package is dropped off into one of these parcel lockers,  the key given to me never works!! Get that shit fixed!! The fifth time already.  And when I try calling your office no one answers.  Hello customer service?? I moved into a new house and this is the first time I have ever had trouble getting a hold of MY mail.  WTF?

A post office is a post office...but the other day I went there to pick up a package and as I had my 9 month old in tow, I was a little scatter-brained and left my ID there. I didn't even notice until several hours later. There was a knock on my door...and it was the woman who had helped me and she was returning my ID. I was so shocked and happy. I still can't believe that a person would go out of her way like that. Amazing.

This is BY FAR THE WORST POST OFFICE IN THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA! The box clerk, Bette, is literally insane and needs to be not only fired but institutionalized for the criminally insane! Usual scenario. 10 people waiting in line at the service window, wondering if a staff member is actually going to open it only to disappear again for 5 minutes while she works on a consumer need.

15 people waiting in line for the counter. Only two clerks at the counter who are as slow as molasses.

1 lady complaining to the floating clerk and asking to see a supervisor who is told to wait by the office door. Nobody come to help her so now she still has to complain even louder now.

Poor management. Under staffing. Tenure laziness.

horrible horrible horribe customer service.  They also sit on packages way to long and in some instances loose a package all together.  I wish they would just destroy this location and allow the other locations to properly handle mail.

Rude employee "Anacita" told me and 2 other customer we couldn't come in because they were closed, except it was 4:56pm not 5:00pm. I needed assistance about a package delivery that kept having issues getting delivered to my place. So I went there to attempt to pick it up from the office but it wasn't there. So they gave me a card to call them back around 4pm to check on it cause they close at 5pm. I called the number and the damn number didn't even exist anymore. Really???

I don't come here too often but when I do, it's usually just to drop off a package. I usually go onto their website and pay and print my postage that way I don't have to wait in line. And you do get a very small discount by printing a label with postage at home. The few times that I did have to wait in line, it wasn't too bad, and the staff was nice and friendly.

I like that their lobby is open 24 hours, so you can go in and use their automated postal service instead of waiting for their counters to open at 8:30.

Customer service agent I spoke with barely spoke English and didn't seem to have any idea what I was talking about regarding a simple mail hold and address change. It's a very time sensitive matter, and she promised me a call back after she could "check the system," but I haven't heard from anyone. 

Impossible to reach anyone to begin with, the phone is permanently busy it seems. 

Service is slow and inadequate in store as well. 

But, what would you expect from a government run agency?

Is there really no way I can give less than a star? If you've ever seen the DMV scene in Zootopia where the facility is run by sloths, you'll have an idea of what this "post office" is like. Only this joke of an establishment is worse!

I am usually pretty lucky in terms of wait time when I need to conduct any transactions requiring interactions with a USPS postal worker at this location. (There, just jinxed myself for all future visits.) But the wait time and length of the line is always more manageable than the Rainbow/Spring Mtn location I typically go to.

I moved recently. Back to an address I used to reside at. So I've getting emails from my bank and such alerting me my statements getting returned by the Post Office.

Now typically, filling out one of those change of address forms is pretty straight toward. But I wasn't sure in my case, as I have not had to fill out the form for my situation. Luckily there was an elderly postal worker at the package pick up window that was not currently occupied at the time, and he also faced a similar situation, so he was able to give me the clarifications I needed.  Awesome!!!

Now I just need the roughly 7 business days for the update to go into effect.

As far as parking, never been an issue for me. Of course I can imagine it could be an issue around busy shipping season like Christmas, but that's why it is best to be early with shipping off those holiday cards and packages.

This location also has a lot of real estate dedicated to PO boxes for rent. Although I am not sure about current availability.

For me the only confusing part of using this postal location on my first visit, is where to start lining up. Typically there is a clear rope and cordon setup to help you navigate to the right place, so you can avoid upsetting people that might think you are cutting them off at the other USPS locations. Since the arrangement of this Pebbles location has counters on both sides of the center aisle, where you can find the usual forms you might need to fill out for registered mail and shipping labels, it confused me since people were on both sides.

Anyway, friendly inquiry from people working there or other people there to use the USPS services will quickly resolve that minor quandary.

4 stars.

WTF?

I recently sold an item on eBay and came here to send the package. The staff placed it on the scale, weighed it, typed in the delivery address zip code, printed a sticker for postage and it was sent. All was fine until I got an email several days later that the post office on their end demanded $ for insufficient postage. 

First, if there's insufficient postage, return the damn package. Second, I physically went to this post office to mail the package, how is it possible that it's insufficient? So someone screwed up somewhere. And how could they hold the package as collateral until the insufficient funds are paid. WTF??

Oh, and when I moved to my place and requested to have the mailbox key re-keyed. It took this office 2 months to rekey the mailbox and issue me a key. I went back there 5 times to remind them, and they completely ignored me. Talk about bad service!!!

The hours at this location are just about as terrible as possible for me (M-F 8:30am-5:00pm).  The Seven Hills location is open 9:00am-5:30pm which would at least allow for a few more people like me to be able to stop by after work.  I don't understand why they don't just open 9:30am to 6:00pm or something.  The way it's set up now just forces this location to have a HUGE weekday lunchtime rush.

Today during the weekday lunchtime rush there was ONE person working at the counter.  ONE.  Ridiculous.  Usually it's only understaffed by having two employees at the counter (which is still about two less than they should have working).

To make things worse, the kiosk was broken today.  Although, even when it is working it doesn't help the lines much (more of a commentary on the customers than the business though).

The employees are rude and unprofessional.  One time when I was at the counter I could hear the employees in the back calling each other "n***er" and "motherf***er".  Unbelievable.

Worse customer service! Management is rude and so is the staff.
Wish they would close this location & get rid of everyone all together!!

I got here and immediately Eric says "We're closed." I saw people in line and said okay Can I drop this in the package drop. He said yes. I asked for a small piece of tape, and he said we don't provide tape anymore. Literally I needed two small pieces of tape at most for the shipping label. What happened to good customer service? I asked if I could buy one and he said no I can't sell you any tape after 5pm. So now I have to drive all the way to the Sunset location (where they're actually nice) to ship my package. What an inconvenience. I won't be coming here again.

It's a friendly, laid back shop staffed by people who know and most importantly care, about what they do. You get advice from people who live and breath cycling and all that goes with it. Highly recommended.

It's true that the people who work here are enthusiasts who know their stuff, but the after sales service is very poor. Having purchased a BMX bike for my son we got it home to find that it hadn't been properly prepared (spokes loose, handlebars loose, crank set loose etc), so had to take it back to get things sorted. 9 months later we were charged £35 for a service (the first service) and got the bike home to find that once again work had not been properly completed. Took the bike back to get things put right and was charged another £20 to have a puncture repaired. Pre sales advice and service was great; after sales service was very poor (and expensive) - we won't be returning...

If you're the proud owner of an expensive or high end bike and you are looking for high quality and most importantly reliable parts or upgrades for your bike, this is probably the best place to come for these.

The prices here, whilst value for money when you consider the quality of the items you are buying, are too high to justify buying these parts for a cheap bike.  There is no point putting expensive parts on a cheap bike, but there is also no point buying an expensive bike and then putting cheap parts on that.  If you are after cheap parts then my best recommendation would be to visit Bike Station instead.  If you do have a good bike, instead of diminishing it by putting on cheap parts come here and get the parts the bike deserves.

I went to Leo Orchid nail salon for two reasons. First of all, I've been looking for a new nail salon in my neighborhood and secondly I really needed coffee and it is located in the same plaza as the Xtreme Bean. When I entered the salon everyone seemed relatively friendly, and while there were clients in chairs the place was not busy by any means. I had stopped at Magen nails first (they've changed owners and the place was filthy) so I bee lined out of there in hopes of finding some place that had some semblance of sanitation. 
 Leo Orchid is decorated...interestingly. I'll give them an A for effort because most nail salons are so tragic and 90's looking. I was impressed by their rather "fancy" pedicure chairs, which are adorned with glass bowls and varnished wooden arm rests. The pedicure bowls have whirlpool action so it feels like constant hot water is constantly being circulated which is a really nice touch.  Their massage option on the fancy chairs is terrible, and didn't seem to work well. The chairs, despite having some great features are lacking cup holders which made things awkward and inconvenient. I picked a color and sat down, with the intent of relaxing and enjoying the ride. I was immediately robbed of any relaxation by the rather insistent woman preforming my pedicure. "You want this color?" she showed me some terrible bronze monstrosity (if you dig bronze, bully for you, but I'm just not that kind of girl) "No, I picked out OPI red." I was totally stunned by the fact that in a matter of ten seconds she'd been able to lose the color I'd placed on her tool cart. We found the color, and just as I picked up my phone in an attempt to thwart further contact she began badgering me about flowers and rhinestones. I tried to politely refuse her efforts at first. I'm not the flowers and rhinestones type, I like things very classic, very clean. Finally, after approximately two minutes of being pressed for a flower or rhinestone I told her i was sure she'd do a great job, but I think that they're tacky. She acted like I'd slapped her in the face, and continued mumbling about how she would do a great toe flower. Then she asked "What you do?" like maybe I had the stodgiest job in the world and that's the reason I wouldn't want a flower on my toes. I told her I was pre-law at ASU. "Ahhhhh" she said, like I'd summed up the universe for her. I went back to what I hoped was some semblance of silence, playing words with friends because there wasn't a magazine in sight. She struck up a conversation again. This time asking me if I did my own hair. I understand that culturally, somethings are lost in translation and that there are language barriers. I told her the name of my stylist, probably a little more shortly than I could have, and she finally took the hint. She then proceeded to give me the shortest and most painful foot massage ever. I was thankful when it was over, it was like she was pinching my legs instead of rubbing them. Finally, she broke out the hot stones, and my god were they hot. I don't know how she managed to pick them up. Maybe she was seeking revenge because I'd robbed her of her opportunity to prove me wrong about my decision to go flowerless. I looked down and my toes were almost done. My nails really could have used a manicure, so I looked at my toes and decided that maybe, just maybe she'd get it right with my manicure. Wrong. So very, very, wrong. I told her I'd like them shaped "sqoval" my natural nails are really healthy, and were quite long, and already filed, she just needed to even them out. I now have tiny pointy stubs for fingernails. After telling her that she had done my nails unevenly and incorrectly, in the most polite way I possibly could, a gentlemen co-worker got involved. He managed to mess up my nails even more, so there I'm trapped, one hand to the mean flower witch, one hand with the old man in the plaid shirt, feeling completely helpless and in desperate need of escape. I looked at them and said "we're not communicating very well, the manicure was a bad idea. I'd just like to leave now." Even though they were having a $17.99 special, I gave them $25, begged for a pair of paper flip-flops and waited what felt like an eternity for the man to put them on. The pedicure wasn't worth $17.99 and honestly, they probably didn't "deserve" a tip, but I believe in good karma and I just wanted to throw money at the problem and get out of there alive.  The two women clients in the shop kept on looking at me like "Are you okay?" "What's going on?" 
It was one of the most awkward transactions of my entire life. 
The moral of the story, is go ANYWHERE but here. I'd trust the mad doctor from the human centipede before I'd go back to Leo Orchid nails and spa. Seriously.  Mani/Pedis should be relaxing, indulgent, and decadent. This was stressful, painful, and distressing. Save your time, money, and patience. I cannot stress this enough, go ANYWHERE but here.

I needed a mani pedi, and a coupon had come to the house. So I thought on my way to the doctors I would stop in and get a mani pedi.
There were 2 males working here.  The younger one said, Hello, what would you like to have done.  I said mani pedi. He said, pick a color.  Then the older guy had me sit in the chair for my pedicure.
All in all not too bad, but I noticed none of the instruments were sterile. But the worst part was he took a hot hand towel out of the microwave looking thing and wiped my legs down. Ladies you know what I am saying.
Then when he thought I was not looking he put it back in there for the next victim. 
I am not kidding that really happened.  They are supposed to go in to be laundered!

I never let them use cutters on me and this is one of the big reasons why.
Cutting corners like that makes my skin crawl.
Honestly where is the Health Dept. on these places.
Well no surprise , a few days later my toenail polish started to peel off.
I could not wait to get all that stuff off me ASAP!
I agree with Angela on those other reviews. Unless they have just recently gone down hill fast, I do not know how they have stayed in business this long.

Umm.  Stay away.  I went there because I liked the old location.  I should have walked away before I opened the greasy fingerprint stained door, but I gave them the benefit of the doubt, knowing they were relatively new to this location.  Dirty, dirty, dirty!  Now I have an infection in my toe that i can't seem to get on top of with alcohol wipes and hydrogen peroxide.  Sorry, but they need to close.  They just don't care anymore.

wear your snow boots, decided to be a re-peat customer and go back for a pedicure/manicure.  Boy, what a month's difference makes.

T, who is the manager acted like he didn't know me.  The problem I have is, another guy did the service, he had a nervous hand, overcharged for a "buff" when I didn't get charged the first time.  I won't go on, and on, just get ALL the pricing up front.

I have never felt so uncomfortable in my life and I beg all women reading this to never go to this salon. I ended up alone at the salon with a man who started talking to me about how American girls are freaks in bed and while he was giving me a manicure he asked me if I liked having my hair pulled and getting spanked during sex. When he looked down and saw my wedding ring, he started asking me questions about my sex life with my husband. To top it all off, he asked me to hang on for a minute while I finished watching a TV show...which was playing on Hulu and could have easily been paused until he was finished with my manicure. It was an uncomfortable and unpleasant experience. I should have just walked out.

My nail tech had horrible nails himself, very unclean. Played games on his phone intermittently and smoked his e cigarette! While working on calluses he was just brutal and kept bending my toes in ways that just hurt. Got bruises from my leg massage. His long greasy hair kept getting stuck in my toes during my bruising as well. Gross!!! He answered calls during my pedicure too. I asked for a basic French pedicure, he kept watching the tv show they were playing while painting. The massage chair was broken, looks like they are remodeling or have never cleaned the whole place. There is trash everywhere. Didn't let my nails dry before putting my shoes on.

Bike parts scattered in the back of the salon along with a motorcycle and bicycle.  My nail tech had dirty nails himself, Ewwwww!!!  Did a below average gel mani.  Color was not even when done.  I pointed out specks in polish before curing.  He said it was fine then he tried to file them off.  They were still there.  Had bubbles in top coat.  Massage was very quick & could have just spared me wiping oil into my forearms and hands.  Told me if I wanted lotion it was in front of me.  I thought I would try this place for s second time being close to work but I got the same manicure result the 1st visit.  Where are all the GOOD nail techs?

So having very little time and desperately in need of a pedicure I stopped in to Leo Orchid Nails.

I am truly convinced that the two high marked reviews must have been planted or paid for... Or maybe the reviewers just have never had a quality pedi because my experience was something I would not wish on anyone.  I wish I would have followed my gut and walked out half way through the pedi.   I have to agree with Whitney the two men are just creepy!

This place is cluttered and dirty... Disgustingly D-I-R-T-Y and the staff is extremely pushy and RUDE. How are you going to clean the tools in the dirty water that my feet have been soaking in and then put them back for the next person? Ewww! Gross!

Let me tell you I came straight home and scrubbed my feet... still have the heebee geebees!

There are way too many places where you can get a much better pedi for the same price.  I have learned my lesson and will drive the extra miles and make the time to go to Ken's Nails from here on out!

As a side note - this is the same people that used to be in the shopping center on Baseline between Lakeshore & Rural (between Big Lots and Classic Pizza Kitchen). Now located in the Walgreen's shopping center on McClintock and Southern.  Had I realized that prior to sitting down I wouldn't have bothered... Last year I had gone to the old location once... Horrible pedi and I kid you not it lasted exactly 1 day... I wore closed toes shoes the next day to work and when I got home the polish had rubbed off of my toes... never had that happen before. I spoke to a friend who explained that it happens only when they use 1) cheap polish (I only pick OPI products) or 2) they thin the polish down too much.

Either way... I know my money is better spent @ Ken's (Sorry I deviated Ken & Amy!)... sure hope the health dept shuts them down soon!

Meticulous, thorough job on the pedicure - and great massage!

Seriously got what I think is the best brow was I've ever had (and I have gone to a lot of really nice places) for $10 - SCORE!

Leo Orchid - I approve. :)
First time here and I received excellent customer service.  T  has a great variety of nail designs, the place was clean and the ambiance is just right to sit back and unwind.

I went here for the first time recently and won't be going back - my gel mani polish is already starting to come off after just a few days. I haven't done any activites that would warrant the wear this bad other than washing my hands like normal.

the place is just two brothers as the workers - they are perfectly nice but I don't think it was a job well done. The hot stones for the pedi aren't even hot and he rubbed them on each leg for about 15 seconds. In addition the massage you're suppose to get with a pedi was about 30 seconds with no pressure - basically just like someone is touching your skin. and no hand massage with the mani.

To make this place a definite no-no, when he pulled out the light thingy for the gel manicure, it was super dirty and all crusted with dirt or who knows what, on the inside. I felt so dirty and gross sticking my hand in there and just kept telling myself that I would sanitize my hands as soon as I got out of there. No telling what else was unsanitary that he used on me.

I meant to go to the nail place at 3320, but this one is in the same corner complex and ended up here at 3360 by mistake so watch out - avoid this nail salon by cold stone unless you are just looking for a quick cheap mani/pedi that you don't mind chipping after a couple days and can handle the uncleanliness of the products that will be touching you.. definitely wasn't worth the money.

Really used to like this place. However the past two times I've visited my favorite friendly lady has been replaced by two creep men. The older one likes to rub my hands and arms while doing a manicure. (Not in a professional way). I just feel the quality of work has gone down. This tends to happen when nail salons get busy and start to feel greedy. 

It is an outdated place with runny nail polishes that are obviously thinned down. There has to be a better place in Tempe...

I've gotten my nails done here multiple times and each time it has been wonderful. I am very particular when I get my acrylics done. I like mine a particular shape and good quality to me means not breaking or lifting. This is the only place that has been able to keep me coming back due to the great prices and quality. I am very lazy when it comes to getting my nails done, I like to wait three to four weeks! (Yes I know that's bad, but when T does my nails they actually last that long!) overall I'm a very happy camper coming here! Unfortunately, I move to the Bay Area for law school and have been unable to find another person to do such quality. Also, his designs are the best!

This was are first visit ,we had no small kids with us .Is more for smaller kids I guess.They are understaffed .The people that worked there where friendly. We enjoyed the Corn maze .I think the prices are high.

Definetely a place I would visit if you are in central Illinois for just the fun of it.  There is a corn maze there which is totally awesome.. totally affordable at $6/person!  And they have other things like reindeer and hay rides.  And only one exit up on 57 from UIUC.

This place is sooo cool!

I was visiting Illinois for family reasons and we came here for one of the events. I got to feed the reindeer (there is a fee), and there is a pumpkin canon, and hay to crawl around on, and lots of things to look at in the gift shop. There is a dining hall where we had a group dinner, that included all kinds of good wholesome food.

If I ever go back to Illinois, this is a place I am going to visit again.

Hardy's Reindeer Ranch wasn't super exciting, but could be fun if you have kids.  I was mainly curious to see a reindeer in person.  They are just kinda lounging around in a few fenced in areas.

There is a corn maze, which was around $6 person.  You could also pay for a reindeer tour, which meant that you get to feed crackers to a reindeer.  It didn't really seem worth the extra money, since you can just look at the reindeer for free without feeding them.

They also have cut your own Christmas trees and Christmas-y gift shop.

Smooth visit, a mere 4$ to take the reindeer tour. They have several things out for photo ops including the reindeer. Came with the wife, sister and parents. Easy way to kill a couple hours and do something you don't get to do all year round. Would gladly return as the staff was friendly and attentive.

Our family has made a Christmas tradition of visiting Hardy's Reindeer Ranch. The $3 tour not only allows you to get up close and personal with the reindeer (you feed them graham crackers and pet their noses), but it supports a portion of their care throughout the year. The gift shop is cozy -- a good place to stop in from the cold. You can sit around a potbelly stove sipping cider that's for sale, browse through the lodge and country decorative items, and then finish up by buying a Christmas tree. The pre-cut tree selection has been a good one in year's past. The guys will trim it, wrap it, and get you on your way. Or, you can cut your own if you prefer. There's a little cafe on site that has very limited hours; my husband likes their chili. Plus, it's a pretty ride out into the country.

My fiancee and I had yet another great time going through the corn maze this year! These guys are always doing something different. This year it's in the shape of a train! They have an awesome selection of things to do for kids as well like their go carts, pellet gun range, and playground. They also have a pumpkin cannon that they shoot off periodically. My fiance and I have been coming here annually for the last 3 years and plan to continue :)

Their gift shop has all shorts of neat items as well. And they have pumpkins as well you can purchase. This was our first year buying pumpkins and they were in great condition. I even attended a wedding reception in their recreational building. These guys offer just about anything!

Looked forward to taking my three year old grandkids to Hardy's.  We took the "Reindeer Tour" which consisted of standing in a small corral to "feed" the reindeer while the owner doled out a cracker at a time to people.  We paid three bucks a head (including the children) for this experience.  The cafe was not open, though it is part of their ads, and no one there seemed apologetic about that fact.  It was a cold day but there was no fire in the potbelly.  My son-in-law treated us to a "hay ride" which consisted of driving around harvested fields for about five minutes.  Items in their gift shop were all overpriced, too.  Not a very pleasant experience.  It was interesting to be up close and personal with reindeer, who seem to be nice critters, and my grandkids seemed to enjoy them, but the reality of Hardy's Ranch did not live up to the ads.  Be forewarned.

So, uh, I went to a reindeer ranch in central Illinois....and enjoyed myself.  First off, the idea that there are a bunch of reindeer just chillin' on a random farm that also grows Christmas trees is so surreal it has to be believed.  Then there are  kitschy Christmas items in the gift store, pedal powered racing carts, and a gigantic corn maze.  You can spend your money as well on snacks or paintball shooting.   It's literally a nonstop kitsch fiesta, but as a one time lark, it's worth it.  They also change that damned corn maze every year, but it freaked me out that I think it was a one time only thing for me.

I have never written a Yelp review but after my experience today I felt I needed to not only to explain my situation to the staff who was unwilling to listen to my side (let alone let me finish a sentence) but also for those of you who may be thinking about making a trek, as we did. I apologize for the length but this is for management to read as well. 

-------------------------------
THE QUICK STORY
-------------------------------

Hardy's has a place where you can grab a wagon and saw, and then two different entry ways into their tree farm. All of their signs near the wagon and saw said nothing about cutting down anything under 4 feet tall. 

There was a small sign on the left entryway that said you can't cut anything underneath 4 feet tall. There was no sign anywhere near the right entryway. 

After reading all the signs near the wagons and saws, and proceeding to enter the tree farm on the right entryway (with no signs) we were scolded pretty harshly for cutting down a tree less than 4 feet. 

After apologizing and agreeing to pay, I was rudely interrupted numerous times while trying to explain that the markings may not be very clear if you are entering the park from the right side. I was also scolded for not talking with someone before taking a wagon. How was I supposed to know I needed to check in with someone??

The employees were VERY difficult to talk to and although the manager lady wasn't too bad to talk to, she definitely didn't allow me time to suggest to her that maybe her signage wasn't very effective. 

When we pulled our car up to pick up our trees, there was another gentlemen who was having the exact same issue we were, so it was a recurring problem. They ended up pulling the sign out of the ground and moving it to where the other signs and wagons were...probably where it should have been in the first place. 

I don't even care that I had to pay $40 for a tree that was 2 feet tall. I am disappointed that I was treated so poorly as a customer and listened to so little. 

_________________

THE LONG STORY
__________________

My girlfriend and I went to Hardy's two years ago and it was a pleasant experience. We dealt with the owner (a male) and he was very kind and helpful. This year was a different story. 

We arrived and walked up to where they keep the wagons and saws. Our favorite part is cutting down our Christmas tree and we drove 2 hours to do it (we live in Chicago). Yes, there are closer farms but I had liked this place the previous couple years. 

I would say my girlfriend and I are a bit nerdy, in that we are pretty careful to do things correct in really everything we do. This involved reading all the available signs around the wagons about the size of trees, cost, etc. We did this, didn't see anything funny, took a wagon and saw, and went on our way. 

There are two walkways to enter the tree farm. One to the left, and one to the right. We took the walkway to the right so we could see the Reindeer. 

We cut down one big tree and one small tree. 

After arriving at the tree shaker we were met by two very rude employees who intended to scold us for cutting down the small tree. "There are signs everywhere telling you not to do this! You will have to pay full price ($60) for this 2 foot tree!) they said. I apologized and told them I was sorry and I hadn't seen any signs. I was reminded they are all over. 

While my tree was being shaken, we walked around and again read all the signs to see what we missed. We still couldn't find anything that said we couldn't cut a tree down that was smaller than 4 feet. 

I went back and asked the lady nicely "do you mind showing me where the sign is? We cant find it" She says rudely "there are signs all over"

"I understand" I say. "But since we can't find them, we'd like you to show us where they might be". She answers with, "well did you talk with one of us before you grabbed a wagon and axe!?"

"No", I say. "Was I supposed to? I didn't know there was a requirement to talk with anyone. I figured it was like a pumpkin farm and we could take a wagon and go, since I've been here before a couple years ago"

"If you've been here before, then you know you can't cut down a spruce shorter than 4 feet". 

"Ma'am" I say..."I live in Chicago. I dont even know what a spruce is amongst the others, let alone that I'm not suppose to cut anything down under 4 feet. The only sign you have posted about this is on the left entryway to the tree farm. You have no sign anywhere near the right entryway to the farm"

"Well I'll give it to you for $40 instead of $60 like I should. Merry Christmas" she says sarcastically. 

I was really looking forward to this but these employees really ruined our experience. We won't be returning and we won't be recommending this place to our friends anytime soon. 

Shame on you Hardy's. You shouldn't make your customers feel bad when it's your fault for not labeling your directions and rules properly.

I just stumbled across this place while doing a google search for a kid or family attractions in central IL. I was looking for  place to stop with my 2 & 4 year old to break up our 5 hour road trip. This place was perfect. They played in the sand, climbed the straw bales and could have cared less about the reindeer. We did not take the tour and from what I saw, the reviews are pretty accurate. Still we loved the hay ride. But again my kids are young and the resident dog, huckleberry,  came along for the ride and that helped. Afterward we got to witness the pumpkin launcher in action. Only one pumpkin though : / we are spoiled and used to at least 3 when one of those launchers are fired up.  Overall we had a nice time, it was better than a park.

I'm sorry Hardy's. Don't be fooled by the Reindeer Tour.  For $3 (or $12 if you're a family of four like us) you are entitled to the experience of standing in a crowded pen with several other families whie you feed graham crakers to the reindeer for about 10 minutes.  But first you'll have fight your way through to the man with the crackers, as he gives them out 1/4 of a cracker at a time, and there will be at least a dozen other people in there with you.

If you and your kids simply must see reindeer this holiday season, which is admittedly a cool sounding thing to do, please save your money and stand outside the pen and look at the reindeer.  The reindeer are interesting to see - their antlers are pretty incredible.  But uh, the experience as a whole left us rather underwhelmed.

For another $3 a person, you and your kids can ride the pedal cars around the little track.  Unless your kids are under the age of 5 or 6, because they only have 1 car small enough for littles, and it's broken.  Most of the rest of the cars have flat tires, too, so . . . .

Some hay bales to jump on.  A sand box with some broken digging tools.  And some tire swings.  My kids enjoyed the tire swings the most.  Next time I'll just take them to the park.

This place is SO cool. The reindeer are gorgeous and extremely well-natured. The tour was a mere $4 and worth a lot more than that. I really don't understand how anyone could rate this less than 5 stars. Reindeer!

The staff are extremely friendly and helpful, as is (the dog) Huckleberry.
Great fun! Kids and adults will love it Nice gift shop too..

I had a much more detailed review but yelp shut down and didn't save it so I lost it.  Guess I need to look into reviewing them.  Anyway the reindeer ranch was a lot of fun.  Family owned and oriented.  Our kids, 8-13, really liked it.  The reindeer tour really isn't a "tour".  Just a feeding and petting area.  The corn maze is a treasure hunt type event which is really entertaining compared to most.  Allow at least 2-3 hours with kids.  No complaints on our part.  Great way to spend the day and totally worth the two hours we drove to get there.

I think the best thing going for this Tim Hortons is the convenient location and possibly their hours, I believe they are open until at least 11pm, possibly 12am regularly. The location is big with quite a bit of seating, but I find it to be pretty dark and I personally wouldn't want to sit and stay here. Customer service is below average. The only reason it isn't a one star is probably because I don't have high expectations for the Tims experience and I have never had any major issues - I wouldn't go out of my way to stop at this location by any means.

I'm not sure any Tim Horton's would get more than a 3.5, but this one is definitely below average.

The staff and fellow customers are on the surly side.  The staff seem to be always new and not so happy to serve you.  Not sure why this location attracts such a rough crowd, but it does.  You can basically expect to be hassled on the way in for money.

The coffee is totally bland.  The food even more flavourless.  I'm not sure how an everything bagel can taste like nothing, but they've succeeded.  

The only thing getting it it's second star is that it's cheap and my expectations were low to start with.

The General Manager is very disappointing and rude to customers.
He would swear (very rudely) at employees if they make small mistake.
Managar name is:  Maroun Atallah
Terrible staff, lazy, not so willing to work, confused, got there on a Saturday at 8pm, two cashiers banging their heads not so willingly trying to make customers satisfied

This is the best subway I've been to because of the great service! !!!! I pass three others on my way home and this is the one I will always go to. ... I'm tired at the end of my day and it is nice to have fast professional service.  Apparently one employee has been there for 12 years and for all the time I've been going here he is always very fast and courteous. ... thanks!

Yeh I must not have caught the team on a good night cause they were mean. I'm not gonna go into detail but I will never return their again. And Annie or Andrea whichever one is her name I'm not sure, she should be fired. She has some problems and she needs to learn to not bring them into work with her. Oh and the issue had to relate to her forcing me out pretty much and threatening to call the cops on me right at 9pm most likely due to some personal issues of her own and needing to be out ASAP which being mean to someone and threatening to call the police on them isn't a way to handle that if you ask me. And I'm a nice guy and did nothing to deserve the kind of treatment she gave me. Here is what is written right on the subway workers manuel to that I found online, "- Employees must be willing to stay past their scheduled time at times when the store does happen to get busy", and "All customers must be greeted with a "Welcome to Subway" greeting as they walk through the door. Customers must be treated in a professional manner, be patient with customers, even if they are giving you trouble. Last but not least, remember that the customer is always right. She did say Welcome to subway, but that is about it.
The staff working tonight was very friendly. The only thing missing is Cherry Coke.

There are another two Subways that are closer to my house, but I make it a point to come to this one instead. The staff are friendly, and some make very neat and tidy subs (I think that some of them are still new and the sandwich can be a little messy, so that's the reason for only 4 stars). I only come in about once a month, but certain employees recognize me and are friendly and open to small talk.

I really like that the prep surfaces and the overall store is clean. I seldom notice food debris on the prep surfaces or trash around the store. The other Subways within a few mile radius tend to be messy and never have prep surfaces as clean as this one's are, at least not when I've tried them.

I just got home from Sweets N Beats and I already want to go back for more candy and vinyl. 

This place is a small shop specializing in music and old school candy. They are nestled between The Trunk Space and The Bikini Lounge.
I found lots of great records ranging from Talking Heads, various ska bands and a Rudy Ray Moore album. Good selection of yummy candy like squirrel nut zippers (a chewy, nutty candy), lemon heads, cherry heads, bubble gum cigrars and cigarettes. 
They also have a selection of books, t-shirts and novelty items. 

Definitley check Sweets N Beats out. It's a great addition to the downtown area and it's owned by two wonderful people.

Cash only here folks, so bring the green. Everything is pretty cheap, so you can walk out with a bag of candy under $3.

Maybe I'm completely biased because the people who own this place are friends of mine, but I think I'm being pretty honest. This is a great record and candy store with lots of odds and ends, rarities, and local art. My pal Stacy makes hand puppets and things for them and a couple other friends also make healthy home-made dog treats, too. A great addition to the Grandevelt block next to the Bikini Lounge and of course, the ever-wonderful Trunk Space. Go support awesome local businesses, guys!

I've never been so intrigued and cheered up by a store before. 


This place is so...miscellaneous, so I'll try to break it down.

Candy: A wall of Haribo products that I didn't even know existed, a long with a boatload of other sweets that I haven't seen since childhood. Major nostalgia points.

Toys: A variety of faux fireworks, like 'snakes', sparklers, or those things that pop when you slam them on the sidewalk. Nothing mind blowing except the selection and arrangement, which gives you strong impulses to purchase them all and go on a rampage of immaturity.

Books: Made me LOL more than anything else. My buddy picked up Postsecret for only $12, and as I perused the books, one stood out. It was by some author by "Mr. Pottymouth" and had some crude drawing on the cover with contents that may or may not be appropriate for a Yelp review.

Records: A decent selection of 70s and 80s music. I picked up a Rick James vinyl for $2. It said "special prize inside!" and when I poured out the contents there was a condom. Queue immediate laughter.

One day, I'm going on a shopping spree to recreate a long summer day of my childhood. There will be lots of little knicknacks flying around and popping in every direction, while my parents listen to music from the days they were allegedly cool. Another Yelper described this place as a "yard sale"...I wish yard sales could be this awesome!

I don't think I've seen such a strange mix of items ever before. This place has a lot of weird and off the beaten track sort of things for sale and it's really one of those places that just make you perplex. It's only fitting that it's next to the Bikini bar. Anywhere else and would have felt completely out of place. 

The store has plenty of records to sort through, a couple of tables full of strange candy. Book shelf with a lot of odd books that, well are really beyond strange. I found one long time out of print book "How To Be Italian", Let me tell you, with a title like that and the dry wit and comedic satire found in that book, it had me cracking up and was the perfect gift. 

This is also where I found my plastic lobster. They had a table in the middle of the room with $1 plastic lobsters. Now you're probably wondering what function a plastic lobster would have in your every day grind.... The truth is that it has none. 

Zero, no use, nothing of value. It's really actually a waste of resources as I'm sure that plastic could have gone towards making a pace maker or some sort of container for orange juice. But you know what, it's a fucking plastic lobster for a dollar. I LOVE IT! 

Who can say that they went to Phoenix and came back with an Arizona Lobster? Ha! Not many at all. I'm sure I'll get a lot of confused faces when I do say that I have an Arizona Lobster.. but let's face it, this plastic lobster is from there. So yes, I have an Arizona Lobster. It'll be something I have around. 

The store owners were also really really nice to us. In admiring their autographed picture of Adam West (I dare say one of the BEST Batmen ever) they told us a cool story about when they met him. Now, I'm going to name drop here, but I have met Adam West before.. We're in Hollywood, after all.. That sort of thing happens often, especially when you hang out where I'm usually at daily (on a studio lot) But to hear this couple's story about how awesome it was for the to meet Adam West, it was really nice. I dug it. 

So big ups to them, big ups to this location. It's really a place to find just about that strange gift for that one friend who has everything or likes a good comical joke gift.
Yummmm ... I likes candy! I think they have a better selection than Smeeks ... lots of stuff from my childhood. Yum

Thank God for mustache combs.  My Boyfriends beard can be unruly at times, and sweets and beats had the remedy!   My Friend bought one for her fiance as  well(along with some pop rocks and gummy treats of course! How could we resist!) This shop has a great atmosphere, not to mention fun candy, records, books, records etc.  I wish I could peruse this establishment more often!

I was terribly disappointed.  This place has nothing on Smeeks.  We weren't even acknowledged as we walked in the store despite it being mostly empty in there.  That was rude.  The candy selection pretty much sucks and none of it was anything I hadn't seen before.  Prices were fine I suppose, but this place just left me underwhelmed.  I don't do vinyl, so I can't say anything about that, and there were some shirts there too, but again, I came in for candy so I left empty handed.  Sadly, this place just reinforces my belief that Grand Avenue is full of businesses that just don't care.

What a great concept!  What poor execution!!  This place is rubbish.  It is literally like a yard sale inside a building.  There is no atmosphere, no color, no style, no substance.  The record selection is minimal and the candy selection is actually worse than Smeeks (which I didn't think was possible).  I have no idea how this place pays rent but it should be closed.  At least then homeless people would have a place to stay - providing more value than it does right now.

Sweets & Beats is amazing! Plenty of cool/weird/unusual stuff to look at, besides the records...I find something I want everytime I go. This is unlike any other store you'll find in AZ.
The candy that foams in your mouth is awesome....I highly recommend.

This garage is my go-to when I am visiting the North Shore to have dinner or to PNC Park.  I like the quick/easy in & out access and paying is a breeze.   On an evening when there isn't a ballgame or football game.. parking is usually $5.00  Sometimes it hard to get into the other parking lots in the area.  

If you park at this garage its just a few blocks away from PNC or other nearby Restaurants.   One of the reasons why I frequently visit the garage is because I rarely have cash on me.   This past weekend was heading down to the Pirate Game and was surprised to see a sign "Cash only" .  So disappointing but will visit the garage again.

I recommend this garage but be prepared it could be cash only on a weekend.

Reviewing a parking garage?  Really?  Sure, why not...this is my favorite garage to park in down by the stadiums.  Whether I am going to PNC Park, Heinz Field, Stage AE or any of the restaurants down there.   It is a parking garage that also has some bathrooms in the lobby.  They have several pay stations in the lobby (if you did not pay on your way in).  

I really like this parking garage because it offers very quick an easy access to the HOV lanes that lead to the North Hills.  You pull out of the garage, hand a right, move over one lane, through the light and you are on your way.  It is quick and easy.

Is it pricey?  Oh yea, but it is the same price as all the other lots.  If you live in the North Hills and want a fast and quick get-away, this is your place.

This is a great place to park when going to Stage AE for a show. I'm sure it is more expensive during Steeler games but Saturday night it was almost empty. Only two blocks away from Rivertown and Stage AE, $4.00 to park for the evening is a real savings from event parking at Stage AE $10.00.
The location is great for games, events and visits to the Warhol museum, especially on weekends. But during the week days it's full.

I have been taking Mojave (8 year old Aussi/Cattle mix) here for at least 5-6 years. 
The staff is kind, & prices are on target.

Mojave always comes out smelling great, her nails trimmed and she always looks stylish in her bandana or bow!

There are a ton of groomers much closer to me, however it's worth the extra drive for Mojave to feel comfortable with the ladies she knows. 

Thanks!

Not only do they take good care of my dogs, but, today, I found out that they close in remembrance of the lives lost on September 11, 2001. If ever I questioned whether or not this is the right place with whom to do business, that has stopped.

I love the Barking Lot--we have a long haired Shih Tzu who always looks amazing after being groomed.

Miss Tika, who just turned 14, has been going to the Barking Lot since she was a puppy. Marissa takes such amazing care of our Fur-Baby and everyone is always nice and professional. 

Highly recommended!!!

Today was my puppy first time and let me tell you they are the best. My baby is a Yorkieepoo and is 1. I always took him to someone that could never cut hair around his face because he didn't like it and I was always unhappy on how the cut would turn out. So I advised them on what I was told prior and I advised them what I wanted. When I picked him up a few hours later I got what I wanted. A full cut, with a Mohawk if you are on the east side of town this is the place to go. Thank you

I brought my 2 boys here March 1st for the first time and had an excellent experience. My German Shepherd looked beautiful and my little rotti mix looked great as well. They did an excellent job. You can tell they love what they do. They treated my boys with care and that's something that I appreciate and look for in a groomer. The prices were reasonable especially for my Shepard since his fur is on the longer side. I will continue to bring my babies here. Thank you Barking Lot for making my boys look great!

They cut my dog's ear badly and charged me full price before they showed me how bad it was. I was told it was a nip at first. After they took my credit card ran it, them they brought her out and told that she was taken to the vet and had to have it super glued. Her cut is a mess, on top of the gash on the top of my babies ear! I posted a photo of her ear to show that this is no "nip".

My Girl loves taking her little puppy to this place for a bath and a nice grooming. The women here do a great job. Her puppy comes out really cleans and all cute with a nice trim. They even gave her a little bandanna wrap around to keep her warm.

I recommend you try them out if you live in the area.

This great business has taken care of my kids through generations ! Bubba was first !  Beautiful male black lab mix that lived in & out of the pool year round as well as in & out of the house always wet & stinky so we decided to see how a shaved Bubba would work out, and we haven't stopped since.
