Can't forget Jodi one of the servers!! Don't walk by this restaurant, walk right in and they will make you feel like you are "home"....We haven't missed a Friday night here since they opened.
Fabulous location for a private party, room in the back that can close off from the rest of the restaurant, service was impeccable, food was out of this world, they went over and above to make our group of 14 very comfortable as well as the birthday girl turning 80!

I have been very excited to try all the restaurants in the Scottsdale Quarter. After looking at all the restaurant's menus I decided to start at Parc Central. BIG MISTAKE

I went with my mom on a Friday at around 6pm. We walked in and were immediately greeted by a very bubbly woman at the front. She handed us off to another gentleman to lead us to our table. I was able to sit but he stood in front of my mother's chair as he was listing the specials, so she had to stand next to him during his entire spiel. A little strange, but alright. 

The next part is what really irked me. When our waiter came to take our drink orders he was very friendly and warm and made lots of eye contact. As soon as we revealed we weren't ordering wine or a cocktail you could tell he was almost less excited to be our waiter. Then when we ordered our food and didn't order any of the dishes that were 35+ dollars he almost dismissed us. He refilled our waters pretty consistently but he said maybe 3 words to us after that. He never smiled and never made eye contact after taking our orders. 

Just because we weren't having the most expensive dinner doesn't mean that you can treat us poorly. It wasn't like we were looking to buy the cheapest things on the menu. We just ordered salads and water! Not abnormal.

Side note: I had the Parc Central Salad (Field greens, walnut-whole grain granola & strawberry-brie dressing). It was fantastic. Very fresh and light and refreshing.
This is a beautiful, new restaurant in Scottsdale Quarter.  The decor is chic, the service was great and the food was delicious!  I highly recommend checking this place out.

Myself and 2 other people had dinner here Friday night.  It was about 7:30 and the place was pretty crowded but not totally packed.  I've never been here before so I made a reservation earlier in the day but I don't think we needed one.  Better safe than sorry I guess.

Everything about this place screams coolness.  From the decor to the waiters to the people there.  The place is pretty swank but not so over the top that it is a turn-off.  Anyway, it is a super cool and chill place to hang.

As for the food, here is what I tried:

* Black Truffle Hummus = I thought this was just ok.  You could definitely taste the truffle but I found the truffle/hummus combination a bit odd.
* Panko Crusted Goat Cheese = Also ok but nothing special.  Basically just fried balls of goat cheese.
* Grilled Wedge = This was excellent and unique.
* Parc Central Burger = This was tender, juicy and delicious.  It was perfectly cooked and of a decent size.  The fries were also very good.

This place is a bit pricey but not too over the top.  Everything was quality and combined with the "coolness" factor it was worth it.  I don't know why this place needs it, but I would definitely recommend getting a Local Dines gift certificate (http://bit.ly/dfR4eQ) to save a few bucks.

As you enter, you will certainly be impressed by the stunning decor.  Unfortunately, that is the last and only thing that impressed anyone in our party.

Service is appalling.  It took nearly an hour to get our waiter to take our dinner order, and that happened only because we threatened to light road flares to get his attention.  With wine in hand, we could have passed the time recreating the last supper, but were told that serving bread was something that the kitchen might start in the future.

And while the attractive hostess who visited our table momentarily distracted us from the notion that the delay in preparing our ribeyes may have been caused by the chef chasing down the cow on Scottsdale Road to slaughter it, her asking "How was your meal?" only further showed that she too was clueless that we had not even been served our food.

2 bottles of wine and 34 games of gin rummy later, our food arrived exactly two hours after we were seated.  All but two people at our table remarked that their food was ice cold (Those two said the food was luke warm).  The culinary frigidity was the one consistent thing in our dining experience.  Everyone wondered if the food prep area was in an alley behind the restaurant on the cold winter night which we dined.

Unfortunately, it's not possible to offer an opinion on the taste of the entrees or dessert as, after biting into the ribeye-cicles, we got up and walked out.  We settled for pizza around the corner.  It was far less fabulous, but far more satisfying.  Most importantly, it was served piping hot in a mere 20 minutes.

Had an office lunch here last week and boy was I impressed.  

The first thing I always look at - even when I am not drinking - is the cocktail list.  If a place cares about their cocktails, then they must care about their food.  This is, I think, the first place in Scottsdale I have seen a cocktail (actually several) listing Absinthe on its list.  Boom - I am impressed.  Plus all these beauties are actually included in the happy hour deal - not like some places where you get the crappy Sky vodka or Absolute cosmo for 5 bucks but the better drinks are still 12.  Anyway - love them for that.  

The place is super cool, I love NYC and the huge art on the wall showing central park definitely got me in the mood.  The bathroom even smelled like the tropics - I felt wierd coming back t the table and saying to my work mate - "oh my god, you have to go to the bathroom - it smells so good in there!"  ha ha!!

I had the blackened salmon salad - forget the menu name.  A touch over cooked, more on the side of full medium as opposed to medium rare, but the salad dressing (passion fruit) was lovely.  The beet chips are amazing for sure.  

I definitely want to go back for happy hour and try that black truffle hummus and a fun cocktail!  So far my favorite place tof all the new joints in the Quarter.

I know that the management of this establishment has hired at least one server and not paid them for their time.  If the management team has this type of integrity, I can't see myself eating here.  Shame on you!

Wir waren am Montag mit Freunden zum essen dort, der Service war gut und wir mussten nich lange auf das essen warten. Das Essen war sehr lecker und von den Portionen her in Ordnung nur der Preis war etwas teuer. 

Um sich die Zeit zu vertreiben kann man mit Wachsmalstiften auf den Tischunterlagen rumkritzeln was sehr Spaß macht und einem die Zeit vertreibt:)

Die Cocktails waren auch lecker und wenn man in der Happy Hour kommt auch vom Preis her ganz in Ordnung. 

Wir kommen sicher wieder auch wenn es ziemlich laut zum ende hin wurde.

Ich kann mich hier nur einigen Kritiken anschließen. 
Das Joe Penas ist zwar in einem "südamerikanischen" Stil gestaltet und somit auch wirklich nett, aber im Joe Penas ist es einfach viel zu laut - man versteht sein eigenes Wort nicht...Und den ganzen Abend schreien - da ess ich lieber in einem der umliegenden Restaurants, wo ich anschließend nicht kurz vor der Heiserkeit bin. Das Essen ist soweit ok, aber die Portionen werden auch immer "überschaubarer". Die Cocktails hingegen sind sehr lecker und zur HappyHour auch preislich ok. Die Bezahlung könnte anschließend ein wenig schneller gehen...einmal habe ich über 45 Minuten (und mehreren Reklamationen) auf die Rechnung gewartet... 
Ein Erlebnis hat mich allerdings veranlasst, das Joe Penas nicht mehr zu besuchen (neben der Lautstärke): Beim letzten Besuch habe ich ein Dessert bestellt ("Verführerische Zimtcreme") und ich dachte, dass dieses Dessert wirklich lecker klingt. Dies bestätigte der erste Bissen leider nicht. Ich weiß nicht was bei der Zubereitung schief gelaufen ist, allerdings schmeckte das Dessert richtig komisch. Und ich meine wirklich richtig richtig komisch (eine nähere Beschreibung des "verführerischen" Geschmacks lasse ich lieber...). Nachdem mein Freund diesen "komischen Geschmack" (und das war kein Geschmack wie eine "verführerische Zimtcreme" schmecken sollte!) ebenfalls bestätigte, wurde mir vom Personal gesagt, dass in diesem Dessert spanischer Manchego-Käse verwendet wird und man das Dessert gerade probiert und für "gut und lecker" befunden hätte?!? Naja...wie auch immer, so richtig glauben konnte ich die Antwort nicht. Was macht bitte Manchego-Käse in einem Dessert (und wenn es so wäre, dann sollte dies mit auf die Karte als Info...). Man bat mir dann an, ein anderes Dessert zu wählen - leider scheint man im Joe Penas wenig kulant zu sein. Selbst auf Reklamation wurde auf die Bezahlung des zweiten Dessert (das erste "Dessert" wurde gnädigerweise nicht berechnet) bestanden... Anscheinend wird es nicht für nötig gehalten, dass Kunden nochmals das Restaurant besuchen. Schade... Jetzt haben wir uns eine gute Alternative zum Joe Penas gesucht und außerhalb Esslingens auch gefunden.
Vielleicht war dies nur "ein Ausrutscher", aber leider prägen solche Erlebnisse die Eindrücke zum Restaurant...

Allgemein
Ganz ok. Etwas mehr habe ich erwartet. Wir kommen aber wieder, da wir hier in Esslingen keine große Auswahl an mexikanischer Küche haben.
Bedienung
Das Personal war ein wenig gestresst und durcheinander, dennoch sehr nett.
Das Essen
Nicht schlecht. Nur dass die Teller überfüllt waren sodass man den Tisch dreckig gemacht hat.
Das Ambiente
Die Inneneinrichtung könnte etwas mexikanischer sein da es so sehr kahl wirkt
Sauberkeit
Im Großen und Ganzen nichts bemerkenswertes. Unser Tisch war anfangs ein wenig klebrig aber die Bedienung ist sofort gekommen und hat es gereinigt. Das Frauenklo könnte auch gepflegter sein.

Super leckere Cocktails, für die harten würde ich einen Hausgemachten Chili Tequila (aber Vorsicht sehr scharf) Das Essen kann ich nur empfehlen. Bedienung gut (könnte manchmal aber auch mehr hinterher sein!). Das Restaurant ist  immer voll, egal an welchem Tag-deshalb besser reservieren!
Sehr empfehlenswert  
WIR WERDEN WIEDER KOMMEN

Im Grunde kann ich mich dem Urteil der anderen Schreiber anschließen.
Aber letztens sind wir (8 Leute) TROTZ Reservierung an der Türe wg. Überfüllung abgeblitzt - das sollte auf keinen Fall passieren!
Es gab nur Schulterzucken und keine Entschuldigung - geschweige denn einen Gratis-Drink als Trost


 Die haben es eben nicht nötig


 Dafür gibt es von mir nun 2 Punkte Abzug!

Ansprechendes Ambiente! Leider ist das auch das einzige positive was wir feststellen konnten. Die Kellnerinnen und Kellner waren äußerst unaufmerksam und teils auch unfreundlich (haben knappe 2,5 std dort verbracht und wurden nach dem Essen nicht einmal gefragt ob wir noch etwas trinken oder ein dessert wollen)Die Preise für das Essen sind übertrieben da die Gerichte weder nett zubereitet noch vom Geschmack her überzeugend waren. Die Ventilatoren an der Decke lassen sich nicht einzeln regeln, so dass es an einigen Stellen extrem zieht!
Alles in Allem ein äußerst entäuschender Abend in Joe Penas in Esslingen

Typisches Tex-Mex-Restaurant mit nettem Ambiente. Die Cocktails sind lecker und auch das Essen ist nicht zu verachten. Leider ist das Joe Penas nicht gerade günstig, aber wenn man zur Happy Hour kommt lohnt es sich wirklich. Gerade für einen netten Abend mit Freunden ist es zu empfehlen. Wer Montags in Esslingen Cocktails trinken möchte geht am besten in Joe Penas.


 Negativ fallen im Joe Penas leider die Unfreundlichkeit des Personals und die Wartezeiten für Cocktails auf. Es ist klar, dass wenn das Restaurant voll ist alle gestresst sind, aber teilweise wird man nicht nur unfreundlich sondern wirklich unverschämt behandelt. Die längste Wartezeit bei einem Cocktail lang bei uns bei über einer Stunde...

Ein wirklich tolles Restaurant! Kommt schnell super Stimmung auf und die Getränke und Speisen sind wirklich zu empfehlen. Teilweise finde ich die Musik zu laut  aber das ist auch schon mein einziger Makel. Bin gern mit Freunden im Joe Penas und verbringe den kompletten Abend dort  ist halt auch immer was los da ;-)

Allgemein
Beste Steaks und Co ever :-) Alle Fleischzubereitungen und auch die Burittos Nachos und so weiter sind ein gaumenschmaus...wir sind und waren nicht zum letzten mal dort
Bedienung
Die Bedienung war dieses mal sehr besonders und sehr lustig...auch die andren male war es immer o.k. aber diesmal war es wirklich perfekt
Das Essen
Wir hatten diesmal das 500 gramm Rumpsteak für 2 Personen medium auf Niedrigtemeperatur gegart...und es war ein Traum.....mehr brauch ich nicht sagen..als Beilagen hat man immer 2 zur auswahl von baked Poatao,Steakhousfrites,Gemüse oder salt..dazu bekommt man noch einen Maiskolben und Barbecuesauce...einfach lecker
Das Ambiente
Das Ambiente ist ein Traum...zwar durch die gut besuchte Masse an Menschen sehr laut aber mich stört das eher weniger...Musik immer Mex Style
Sauberkeit
Alles sehr sauber,gibt nix zu bemängeln

We went here on Saturday with a few friends 23 to be exact and we all loved it. Happy hour is from 5pm-8pm !! I've never in my life had a mojito so good. It was very strong and the flavor was on point the waiter recommend it! The chip and dip tray was amazing great appetizer. The nachos were also a hit ! I ordered chicken fajitas they were seasoned so well. The kids had Texas chicken from the kids menu they loved it. Everyone at the table enjoyed their food. The only reason I gave it 4 stars was because around 7:30pm it was so packed and the waiter forgot my drink and my friends dessert. But it was super packed and the customer service was very good. They have specials daily we will go there again. I heard at 11pm they have a DJ I'm defiantly going to check it out.

Ein nettes Restaurant mit leckerem Mexikanischem Essen, einer großen Cocktailauswahl, passender Musik und einer tollen Atmosphäre. Es empfiehlt sich einen Tisch zu reservieren, da es fast immer voll ist.

Die Cocktails sind wirklich super und das Barpersonal geht auch gut auf eigene Wünsche ein und berät einen, wenn man sich völlig unsicher ist, was man trinken will. Das Essen ist OK, es gibt meiner Meinung nach aber bessere Mexikaner in der Region Stuttgart. Zum Cocktails trinken also sehr zu empfehlen, wenns um super mexikanisches Essen geht, dann bevorzugen wir einen anderen Mexikaner.

Wir sind um kurz vor  20 Uhr angekommen (hatten auf 20 Uhr einen Tisch für 4 Personen reserviert). Wir mussten einige Zeit auf den Tisch warten und er war so "in die Ecke gequetscht", dass wir nur sehr eingeschränkte Beinfreiheit hatten. Getränke wurden bestellt, kamen nicht gleichzeitig, sondern mit etlichen Minunten Unterschied und erst nach Nachfrage. Das Essen wurde bestellt - einmal OHNE KÄSE (Vegetarierin), einmal mit Hausdressing anstatt mit Käsedressing (Allergie gegen Käse) und einmal extra scharf. Nunja, als das Essen dann endlich kam war das eine (Vegetarisch) mit Käse überbacken, der Salat mit Käsedressing und das extra scharfe kein bisschen scharf. Die zweite Runde Getränke musste erbettelt werden und wurde nach und nach (nach mehrmaligem Fragen) von drei Unterschiedlichen Bedienungen in zeitlich recht großen Abständen gebracht. Beschwerden wurden alle kopfnickend hingenommen, keine Entschuldigung, kein Preisnachlass oder sonstiges.
Dort werden wir nie mehr hingehen und dieses Etablissement auch nicht weiterempfehlen.

Wie immer super leckere Cocktails, fast schon etwas zu stark- aber ok, dann braucht man nicht soviel:-)
Essen immer sehr lecker, Bedienung gut (könnte manchmal aber auch mehr hinterher sein!).
Laden ist immer voll, egal an welchem Tag-deshalb besser reservieren!
Einziger Nachteil ist die Lautstärke im Restaurant. Es hallt alles sehr..
tolle mexikanische Küche, suuuuuuperlecker wie ich finde!!! tolle Musik, für einen lustigen lauten Abend unter Freunden oooptimal!

Das Essen ist zum Glück wieder besser geworden, ne zeitlang war's echt gar nix.
Mit mexikanischem Essen hat's nicht so viel zu tun, aber hauptsache es schmeckt :)
Ein gutes Restaurant, das aber leider nicht an die Stuttgarter Filiale herkankommt - was wohl teils an dem Personal liegt, und wir auch einfach Pech gehabt haben könnten...

Das Joe Peñas ist eigentlich immer einen Besuch wert. Tolle Atmosphäre und Räumlichkeiten.
Sowohl das Essen als auch die Cocktails sind immer lecker gewesen. Am Wochenende empfiehlt es sich einen Tisch zu reservieren da es sonst gut sein kann das mein keinen Tisch bekommt oder recht lange warten muss. Ein witziges Gimmick sind die Tischdecken aus Papier die man mit den vorhanden Stiften bemalen kann.

Wieder einmal mehr besuchten wir das Joe Pena's in Esslingen.
Parken ist direkt im nahegelegenen Parkhaus möglich oder mit viel Glück auch (fast) vor der Tür.
 
Wir hatten reserviert, jedoch fand die Dame am Empfang diese nicht und machte dann einen sehr verwirrten Eindruck. Schließlich bekamen wir dann doch noch einen Tisch zugewiesen.
 
Als Vorspeise bestellten wir Taquitos Estilo Joe Pena's (Tortilla-Röllchen mit Hühnchenstücken mit Cheddar-Cheese-Dip). Jedoch kam es uns vor als sei am Dip etwas verändert worden, er war nicht so lecker wie sonst. Vielleicht auch nur ein Versehen, wir werden das bei Gelegenheit nochmal testen.
 
Die Hauptspeise bestand aus dreimal Sizzling Fajitas (ein Bastelset bestehend aus Tortillas, Fleisch und Gemüse aus der Pfanne und einem Beilagen- Teller) und Soft Enchiladas Estilo Joe Pena's (Weizentortillas mit Putenfleisch und allerlei Beilagen).
Das Fleisch, bei uns Garnelen & Huhn, Rind & Garnelen, Huhn & Rind war leicht scharf, aber angenehm.
 
Meiner Meinung nach ist diese Bastelei nicht jedermanns Geschmack, da es sich doch recht umständlich gestaltet und immer mal wieder was aus dem Röllchen herausfällt.
 
Das Einzige was uns hier immer wieder negativ auffällt, ist der Lärmpegel. Wenn das Lokal voll ist und das ist es eigentlich immer, dann ist es hier auch dem entsprechend laut.

Update März 2009:


 Personal unaufmerksam und oberflächlich; Essen langweilig und lieblos angerichtet; versalzene Chips verderben jedes Gericht totaler Reinfall!


 Freunde, so geht's nicht: Wenn der Waiter bei der Zubereitung der Guacamole am Tisch eher nach seinen umherlaufenden Kollegen schaut als nach der Schüssel und den Gästen vor ihm, dann hat er was nicht verstanden. Und wenn das gesamte Pesonal deutlich zeigt, daß die Gäste eher stören, dann läuft was schief und dann ist der Laden auch keinen Pfifferling mehr wert (geschweige denn 5 Sterne): 
Joe Penas sucks.


 --


 Mein Original-Artikel von 2006:


 Auch wenn's weh tut: Das Joe Peñas in Esslingen (Dick-Areal, beim Bahnhof) ist das beste mexikanische Restaurant in ganz Stuttgart. Ja, ich weiß, Esslingen gehört nicht zu Stuttgart - es gibt aber auch keinen wirklich guten Mexikaner in ganz Stuttgart (so lange bis endlich auch ein Joe Peñas in Stuttgart aufmacht :-)
Sehr leckere junge mexikanische Küche (Cross-Over mit z.B. Cajun) und grundsolide Klassiker (Fajitas) mit Herz und Verstand zubereitet. Vergesst Enchilada, Cantina & co: SO muß mexikanisch schmecken!
Anspieltips: Die Guacamole - am Tisch frisch zubereitet! Und: Alle Fischgerichte!

Joe Peñas is perhaps one of the best Mexican restaurants in Esslingen am Neckar. Menu of the restaurant offers really wide choice of traditional Mexican dishes such as Mucho-macho Nachos, Fajitas, Enchiladas, etc. Moreover, every day during Happy Hours 17:00-20:00 all cocktails cost 4.50 euro (except for Mojito and Juleps).

Nachdem wir ( mein Freund und ich ) gestern einen enttäuschenden Abend im Dockseven erleben mussten, wurde mir heute wieder klar warum ich gerne ins Joe Penas gehe. Die Cocktails sind lecker, die Mitarbeiter freundlich und gut gelaunt, allerdings ist das essen nicht immer top. Nichts desto trotz werde ich in Zukunft weiterhin ins Joe Penas gehen, wenn ich in Esslingen bin und mich nicht mehr im Dockseven verlaufen.

Das Joe Peñas ist ein wirklich sehr empfehlenswertes mexikanisches Restaurant. Das Essen schmeckt ausgezeichnet, die Portionen sind reichlich und dabei nicht zu teuer. Das Ambiente finde ich in dem Esslinger Joe Peñas sogar noch um einiges besser als beim Stuttgarter Joe Peñas. Zudem ist es noch um einiges Größer. Freitags kann im Esslinger Joe Peñas ab ca. 22:30 Uhr Salsa getanzt werden. Dazu werden im vorderen Bereich die Tische bei Seite geräumt, um eine ziemlich großzügige Tanzfläche freizugeben. Unter den Tänzern findet sich alles von Anfängern bis absoluten Profis. Also keine Scheu mal vorbei zu schauen und mitzutanzen. Gie Leute sind echt nett und zeigen euch auch mal gerne ein paar Schritte. Donnerstags gibt es übrigens im Stuttgarter Joe Peñas auch einen Salsa-Abend ab 21:30 Uhr.

Wir gehen immer wieder gern ins Joe Penas. Das Essen ist sehr lecker und frisch. Die Kritik, dass es zu teuer sei, kann ich nicht ganz nachvollziehen  8 Euro für einen großen Salatteller (und hey, man bekommt ihn in so einer lustigen Nach Schüssel!) finde ich eigentlich recht normal, ebenso wie die anderen Preise. 

Das Highlight sind natürlich die Cocktails, die zur Happy Hour nur 4,50 kosten und wer möchte, kann Freitagabends Salsa tanzen.
Was mich total nervt ist aber, dass die Musik an den meisten Plätzen so laut ist, dass man sich nur mit dem direkten Sitznachbarn unterhalten kann. Das ist schade, wenn man in einer größeren Gruppe hingeht. 

Uuuuun: Ernsthaft Leute, nur zwei Damentoiletten für einen Riesenladen, indem man ständig einen neuen Cocktail in der Hand hat? ^^

Wir haben unsere Weihnachtsfeier dort ausgerichtet. Das Essen war in Ordnung, manche von uns waren begeistert, andere weniger, zufrieden waren aber letztlich alle. 
Nur dann gab es ein Problem: An den rustikalen Stühlen schauten Nägel raus - und riss ein böses Loch in den neuen Pulli meiner Kollegin und meinen 3 Tage zuvor gekauften Pashmina-Schal.
Wir wiesen die Bedienung darauf hin. Diese verwies uns an die Geschäftsführung.
Zunächst wurde uns spontan die schnelle Regelung des Schadens versprochen, dann verzögerte sich das aber mehr und mehr: Sie wollten noch Fotos vom Schaden + die Kassenbons für die Versicherung. Wochen und wieder einige Nachfragen unsererseits später hieß es, man werde doch nicht über die Versicherung abrechnen und wir sollten uns das Geld bar abholen - Problem ist nur, dass wir nicht in Esslingen wohnen oder arbeiten - es kämen also noch Fahrtkosten hinzu. Wir baten um eine Überweisung und warten immer noch auf's Geld - nach 3 Monaten!
Sorry - aber selbst wenn das Essen toll gewesen wäre - so geht's halt nicht!


 PS: Nachtrag vom 07.04.:
Letzte Woche haben wir das Geld nun bekommen. Essen gehen werde ich da aber trotzdem nicht mehr...

Ein authentisches Ambiente, super Mexikanisches Essen, perfekt gemixte Cocktails und ein schneller und freundlicher Service. Das beste Mexikanische Restaurante, welches ich bis jetzt besucht habe. Ich war schon mehrfach dort und wurde kein einziges mal enttäuscht. Ob zu zweit oder als Gruppe, es war immer ein tolles Erlebnis. 

Meine wärmste Empfehlung, ich wünsche eine heiße Nacht im Joe Pena's

Im innenraum Wird Man in eine mexikanische Welt entfuehrt mit guter hintergrund musik.gutes essen Und sehr Gute cocktails (mit viel eis). Tipp: rotwein mit dem stier uns dazu ein steak fuer 2 personen, angerichtet Am tisch. Draussen kann man Auch gemuetlich sitzen. Reservierung unbedingt notwendig.

Wir waren Wochenends dort, hatten vorher natürlich reserviert und bereits dann wurde uns gesagt, wir würden nicht direkt im Lokal u hergebracht werden, sondern in einem "Aussenzelt". Bei dem Sturm der draußen wütete war ich erstmals nicht begeistert. 
Jedoch was das Zelt sehr stabile, beheizt und der Lärmpegel war wesentlich angenehmer! Es störte, dass die Gäste von innen zu ins raus kamen um zu rauchen, dies taten sie aber nicht direkt neben uns am Tisch, man könnte es also "übersehen". 
Beim Reinkommen und Heimgehen(wir sind durch das Lokal gegraben) fiel uns allen aber auf wie Laut es dort war, wir waren also froh im Zelt gewesen zu sein. 

Das Essen war genau die richtige Menge, mehr hätte ich wirklich nicht vertragen. Die Dessertkarte war mir aber etwas zu mager. 

Die Margaritas waren super lecker! Und das Personal sehr nett(gestresst, aber freundlich)

Der beste Mexikaner bei dem ich je war! Super leckeres Essen und top Service! Klar ist es etwas teuer aber Qualität hat eben seinen Preis außerdem hat es ein top Ambiente. Auf jedenfall einen Besuch wert! - wer einmal hier was wird wieder kommen !

Eine Location lebt von der Atmosphäre und die ist sensationell.


 Außerdem kann man die (Papier-)Tischdecken mit vorhandenen Wachsmalstiften bemalen (falls es mal länger dauern sollte oder einem doch langweilig ist).

Das Restaurant ist gut und die Cocktails sind super. Wer zur Happy Hour kommt (bis 20:00 Uhr) kann an der Bar sitzen und bekommt noch ein paar Knabbereien zum selber holen umsonst dazu. Mexikanisch gibt's bei uns ansonsten eher selten.
Wer später kommt oder gar einen Tisch möchte: reservieren!


 Montags ist komplett Happy Hour und dementsprechend voll.
Die Atmosphäre leidet etwas unter der Lautstärke, die sich gegen später entwickelt. Die Decke ist zwar hoch aber es hallt ganz schön. Zum Unterhalten ist das Joe Penas kaum geeignet. 
Das Personal scheint nur im Ausnahmefall freundlich zu sein.
Ich bervorzuge das Juleps um die Ecke.

Waren Sonntagabends dort und kann die Kritik meiner Vorredner nicht beipflichten: War mit meiner Freundin zum Essen, vorher telefonisch um 16:30 Uhr auf 18 Uhr einen Tisch reserviert. Am Empfang freundlich begrüßt worden und von der Dame, die nichts anderes macht als die Reservierungen zu koordinieren, an den Platz geführt worden. Ambiente schön, Kellner (so ein ganz Großer) super freundlich und zuvorkommend und das Essen sehr lecker! Tisch-Stuhlhöhe stimmt nicht, da gebe ich recht, aber wenn manche bei Holidaycheck schreiben das Algen im Meer waren, dann interessiert mich das auch nicht. Also wir kommen wieder.
...außerdem steigt freitags immer eine prima Salsa-Party mit DJ Tony Gomez.

wir waren zum wiederholten Male im Joe Pena's zum Essen. Mittwochabend gibt es hier ein umfangreiches Buffet. Das Essen war ok, die Auswahl reichhaltig. Die Preise bewegen sich im akzeptablen Bereich, z. B. 15,80 Euro/pro Person für das Buffet. Wir gehen wieder hin.

Das Essen bestand ausschließich aus vorgefertigen Industrieware. Es hatte NICHTS mit mexikanischem Essen zu tun. Und war in jeder hinsicht ungenügend. Z.B.: schlechte Grundstoffe, schlechte Zubereitung. Eine völlig enttäschende und absolut überteuerte Systemgastronomie. Will man die mexikanische Küche genießen, sollte man unbedingt wo anderst sein Glück versuchen.

Im Sommer 2012 war ich mit meinem Mann mehr oder weniger im
Joe Penas. Das Restaurant machte einen rustikalen Eindruck, war spärlich
beleuchtet und rammel voll. Wir gingen wortwörtlich in der Masse unter. Keine
Bedienung war in Sicht, die uns einen Platz zuteilen konnte oder wollte, also
nahmen wir eine andere Gelegenheit war, um gemütlich speisen zu können.

Letzten Montag wollten wir dem Restaurant eine zweite Chance geben. Die
Bedienung ignorierte uns erneut und fühlte sich nicht im Geringsten angesprochen,
als wir das Lokal betraten, also sahen wir uns alleine nach einem Tisch um. Die
Plätze waren im gesamten Lokal noch nicht einmal zur Hälfte belegt. Seltsam,
dass die freien Tische allesamt reserviert waren und das um 18 Uhr
an einem Montag! Schien mir sehr nach Platzzuweisung nach Laune des Kellners.
Da dieser allerdings lieber an der Bar verweilte, als sich nützlich zu machen,
verließen wir erneut das Restaurant. Das Ganze passierte uns wohlbemerkt zum
zweiten Mal. 

Anhang: Alle guten Dinge sind bekanntlich drei. Nach diesem Motto gaben
wir dem Joe Penas eine dritte Chance. Die Spannung auf die dort servierten
Speisen, überwog die einst gemachten, negativen Eindrücke. Etwa eine halbe
Stunde nach abendlicher Öffnung des Restaurants, fanden wir uns erneut im Joe
Penas ein, in der Hoffnung zumindest diesmal einen freien Tisch ergattern zu
können. Das gesamte Lokal war leer. Einzige Gäste waren ein Pärchen im
Nichtraucherbereich und einige Herren an einem Bartisch. Nach kurzer Zeit
erschien tatsächlich eine Kellnerin, im Sinne, uns zu empfangen. Dem
Himmel sei Dank, dachte ich mir vorerst, doch als diese behauptete, dass alle
Tische reserviert wären, kamen wir uns geblendet vor. Also hakte ich nach, ob das zu der gegeben Tages und Uhrzeit denn überhaupt möglich sein
konnte. Ihre Antwort fiel klar auf ein Ja, aaaber sie könnte so freundlich
sein, und uns einen Tisch für eine knappe Stunde zur Verfügung stellen. Da wir
nun schon zum dritten Mal dort waren und nichts anderes, als das Essen
probieren wollten, sagten wir dem fraglichen Angebot zu. Auch wenn das
überhaupt nicht unseren Vorstellungen entsprach, denn von Fast Food,
war nirgendwo die Rede. Schlimmer geht es jedoch immer, wurde mir klar, als die Kellnerin
uns zu einem Tisch führte. In diesem Moment stellte ich mir die Frage, ob das
ihr Ernst sein konnte. Tatsächlich wurden wir willkürlich an den Nebentisch, des
jungen Pärchens verfrachtet, welches gerade unüberhörbar ein Date hatte
und da man aufgrund der dicht aneinander gedrängten Tische zwangsweise ins
andere Gespräch mit integriert wurde, brach sofort peinliche Stille aus. Keine
angenehme Situation. Die Karte wurde gebracht, wir blickten hinein und
verstanden nur spanisch. :) Sie schien mir zwar sehr ausführlich zu sein, und
zwar so ausführlich, dass das Ganze einer Kurzgeschichte glich, jedoch nur auf
Sprachen, denen wir nicht mächtig waren. Auf gut Glück bestellen, kam für uns
nicht in Frage, denn immerhin ist dieser Spaß nicht umsonst. Fakt ist, dass man
in einem guten Restaurant selbstverständlich ein gewisses Minimum an
Kundenfreundlichkeit erwartet, die hier bedauerlicherweise absolut nicht geboten wird. Schnell kamen wir auf einen Nenner und verließen dieses
Restaurant zum letzten Mal.

Man muss nicht viel zum Ambiente eines Joe Penas schreiben: Toll, extravagant und immer herzlich. Ich besuche jedes Joe Penas in Europa, wenn ich zufällig in eine andere Stadt komme: Augsburg (auch sehr super), München, Berlin, Frankfurt - das lohnt sich immer und es gibt fast nirgends bessere Cocktails als hier !!!
Am 19.9. hatten wir eine Geburtstagsfeier im Joes in Esslingen. Wir waren mit 25 Freunden da. Das Servicepersonal war wie immer ausnehmend freundlich und das Essen könnte besser nicht sein (normal mag ich die mexikanische Küche gar nicht - aber im Joe`s kann ich blind bestellen).
Zum Schluss war es zwar etwas teuer, aber das Trinkgeld haben wir sehr gerne bezahlt. Vielen Dank liebes Joe Penas-Team. Bis bald
Cocktail Auswahl ist groß und lecker. Das Essen ist Geschmacksache aber durchaus ok. Für ein feucht fröhlichen Abend mit Freunden lohnt es sich alle mal

Ich Weiss garnicht warum ihr meckert...
Wunderschönes lokal tolle Musik und nette Menschen
Ich kann's weiter empfehlen 
Ich finde es so schade von den Leuten die immer nur was zum meckern haben!!!
Wie gesagt ich kann's nur empfehlen! Bin gerade im Joe und genieße mein essen

wenn wir Besuch aus Südamerika haben, scheuen wir uns nicht, den ins "Joe Penas" einzuladen.... und denen schmeckt es!
Gibt es ein größeres Lob?
Natürlich ist es eng und voll und man muss vorbestellen, aber was ist das im Vergleich zu den Drinks und dem Essen.... vorallem, wenn man schon in der "happy hour" (17-20 Uhr) mit Cocktails beginnt ;-)


 Ach ja, noch ein Tipp: Die Vorspeise (Mais-Chips mit Dipps) für 2 Personen reicht locker als Vorspeise für 8! Leute, sonst seid ihr schon satt und könnt nachher nicht mehr richtig beim Hauptgericht zuschlagen.

Echt leckere Cocktails zu normalen Preisen. Das einzige Problem: Bei Specials (Mittwochs glaub ich) ist es sehr schwierig ohne Reservierung einen Sitzplatz zu ergattern Ich habe aber die Erfahrung gemacht, dass man wenn man nur bereit ist lange genug zu warten auch ohne Reservierung einen Sitzplatz zu bekommen.

Waren bisher vier mal Freitags zum Salsa tanzen in Esslingen, einmal haben wir auch gegessen. Das Essen war richtig Klasse, die Portion reichhaltig und der Preis absolut angemessen. Die Tische fand ich etwas ungünstig platziert, aber es geht im Grunde nicht anders.
Das Ambiente ist, wie in Stuttgart, sehr urig, ganz so wie man das erwartet. Auch hier viel dunkles Holz, eine noch grössere Bar als in Stuttgart, angenehmes Licht, insgesamt eine schöne Atmosphäre zum wohlfühlen. Auch hier sind die Cocktails sehr lecker und werden optisch sehr ansprechend serviert, die Barmänner sind richtig nette Burschen.
Nun zum Salsa, der DJ legt einen knackigen mix aus vielen verschiedenen Stilen auf, hauptsächlich natürlich Salsa. Highlight hier, am DJ Pult liegen diverse Percussion Instrumente von denen auch reichlich gebrauch gemacht wird, Klasse!
Die Tanzfläche ist gut gefüllt bis proppevoll, die Stimmung kocht, vor allem wenn gegen später noch ein paar bekannte Gesichter aus der Tanzschul- oder showszene kommen. Das Joe Peñas Esslingen scheint auch bei den Kubanern mit am beliebtesten zu sein, man könnte auch einen ganzen Abend lang nur zuschauen (und ein wenig neidisch dabei werden wie gut die tanzen ;-) ).
Das einzig störende ist dass drinnen geraucht werden darf, sonst gibt's nichts auszusetzen.
Auch hier habt ihr mich nicht zum letzten Mal gesehen.

Ich gehe seit Jahren immer wieder ins Joe Peñas, wenn ich in Esslingen bin und muss sage, dass die einfach die besten Cocktails haben. Es gibt keine Cocktail Bar, die diesen Mojito machen kann. Und ich trinke häufig Mojitos in ganz Deutschland. Was mir auch gut gefällt, ist das Stammpersonal. Obwohl ich schon seit Jahren nicht mehr in Esslingen wohne, sind immer diese die gleichen Angestellten da, die mich auch immer noch erkennen und begrüßen! Ganz klarer Fall: 5 Sterne plus!
Ridiculous that if you have a kid you are punished and can't sit on the patio. Will not go back

I only gave it a 1 star as it wasn't possible to score it less.  We stopped there for dinner, they weren't very busy, not unusual since it's Tuesday.  We ordered a small house salad, with grilled chicken and a personal pizza.  It took over 30 minutes to get the salad.  We finished the salad and was told the pizza would be out soon.  I was drinking ice tea.  The waitress re-filled it, and when I took a sip it wasn't tea - it was coffee.  I told the waitress about it, and her response was they don't service coffee, and got me a fresh drink. At one point a server stopped by to ask if we had our pizza.  Forty-five minutes later I went to find her to tell her to bring us our check for the salad, ice tea and soda as we were leaving.  Before they brought the check, the pizza arrived - in a to go carton.  I told them we didn't want it, and then we had to wait for the manager to deduct it from our check.  Manager never came out - they said they were slow because they had a new cook, yet other, larger tables were being served in less time.  Ironically, one of the handicap parking spots in front of the restaurant had a 15 min parking limit.  Not sure you could get much in that amount of time.  Don't waste your time or money on this place.  You have a choice when you go out to dinner -don't chose this place.

Walked in, awkwardly sat myself after no one greeted me. Waitress came and took my order (a beer), and then I sat there for about 15 minutes watching her serve everyone around me. Finally just walked out. Not sure if anyone even noticed. So, yeah...that happened.

The suicide sauce is legit.  Pizza leaves a lot to be desired.  I do not recommend this place for a pie.  Soggy, undercooked, cheap crust, etc.  Server was pleasant enough but not quick on the refills.
We did not eat but everyone around us did. It smelled and looked great.  The happy hour was a great deal and the wine pour were generous for the cost

Oh. My. YUM!!!!!

I had a coupon for a free pizza (thanks to a Yelp event) and have never been to this place so we decided to make the drive and check it out. Sooo glad we did! 

I wish I would have gotten our waiters name, he would have gotten a 1 star. We were seated and sat and sat and sat. It was a Thursday (5/24) at about 6pm, there were maybe 3 other tables with people. NO ONE acknowledged us for a solid 10 minutes. We finally flagged down a bus boy who went and got our waiter. The waiter was not personable at all. Whatev. Although twice a lady brought our food out to us, she was so super nice and we had even said to her that we wished she was our waitress, very personal and nice. 

We ordered several things to try since it was our first time. We did an order of wings, an antipasto salad, the mozzarella and then a pepperoni pizza.

I don't eat wings, so I cant say how they were, but they were the biggest I've ever seen and the guys really liked them a lot! 

The antipasto was fresh and tasty! We will for sure be ordering that again. Note a small is big enough for 4 people! 

The fried mozzarella was super tasty! Very different! Loved it! Not the best I've had though, that award goes to Lo Cascio, but I will for sure order it every time I go! 

The pizza was HUGE! A large will easily feed 5 people. It was so different, loved the amount of cheese on it, though I do wish there was slightly more sauce on it, the sauce is soooo tasty! 

This will for sure be a repeat place for us!
My favorite pizza place in n phx.  Great atmosphere and the food is spectacular!   You won't be disappointed.
Was really excited to try this place but should of read the reviews about no kids on the patio before we stopped by.  Bummer.

We live right around the corner from Upper Crust, and if it weren't for the high prices, we would probably eat here once a week because of the high quality and freshness. The pizza is fantastic and the wings are the best I have had. We normally get takeout and the service is always quick and friendly.
Always a good meal!!!  The ingredients are fresh and they make their own mozzarella! The price is right for the great quality and quantity.

This place has the best pizza.
We usually eat in and that is a good thing as the take out can be cold before it gets home.
They have a decent selection of beers and wine and the service is good.
As a family dining place we like to bring our out of town families and friends!

Very good! We stopped in after a Costco run and were really pleasantly surprised. The pizza was delicious!! Super thin crust and very tasty. We had the pizzoki for dessert, also very yummy. Our server was just ok, but food came out quick and hot. We will definitely be back. A place we consider one of those hidden local gems. Glad we stopped in.

I'm compelled to write this after having dinner here last night.  I ordered the house blend but was informed they were out. I said ok let me have 2 glasses of wine X. On my second glass they came back and said they were out of that wine also. I said ok give me what you have of the Pino Nior.  Now the problem I am having is that the bill comes with prices for wine that I had no intention of purchasing when I arrived. I asked if they could adjust the bill downward a little to offset the cost a bit.   I was informed that they would check and returned telling us that there was nothing that could be done. This is where I have a problem.  There was no possibility of taking anything off the price or as I suggested was to give it to us at the price of what they ran out of?  This apparently @ 830 pm new years eve half hour before closing was to much to ask for. Paying $72 + tip for a pizza, salad and a few glasses of wine is excessive for me and my wife. Pizza was good. Just can't handle the nothing I can do for you..  In this day and age, there is always something that can be done to get your customers to return. Now not so sure. Arena's would have taken something off the bill. Call me picky.

I'm not sure why this place is rated as high as it is. I just placed an order to go and these guys are NOT organized or efficient. To pick up your order you have to go into the bar area and ask one of the bartenders to get your to go order. I think a bar tender is better suited to serving drinks rather than helping with to go orders, don't you? As a restaurant owner I would want them pouring drinks. First, they couldn't find my ticket. And you have to understand how busy this place gets. It's BUSY where they have you picking up to go orders. It's right where the waiters put in their orders and also the kitchen is RIGHT there. It's just a very high traffic area and there is nowhere to go when the waiters are trying to bring out food from the kitchen, so you have this, excuse me--cluster F, of a situation. Then more people start piling in to pick up their order and it's just a big mess. 

So on the way out I had to put myself back together again because I'm carrying this 14" hot pizza box, my purse, my debit card and my wallet and there's no place to set anything down. I stop by the front entrance near the hostess stand and sit down to collect myself. At the hostess station there was, what I would consider to be either a host or the owner, I'm not sure which...In any case, exasperated, I exclaimed to him that the to go order pick up process was inefficient. You would have thought I'd told him his hair was on fire and he was wearing clown makeup...Total deer in headlights. Didn't give a CRAP that his customers have to jump through so many hoops to get to their food. In addition, many of their servers are pretty grumpy when I see them. If you don't want to be there, go find another job.

I don't think I'll order take out from them again after this experience.

The food is legit, don't get me wrong, but we sat outside and asked what the happy hour specials were. Our server listed them off and then said he would be back with our waters. We put our order together and waited for him to come back. And waited. And waited. After 2 cigarettes, we figured he didn't want our money and left. As we left, he was standing at the bar hanging out with the other staff. We came in prepared to spend money. Oh well.

We had a coupon so that's what lead us to Upper Crust in the first place. 

We ended up sitting at the bar during happy hour on a Thursday night. The two guys behind the bar are really what ruined our experience. They weren't very friendly and were somewhat abrasive.

The Caprese Salad was excellent! We loved it. The pizza was also very good. Not my favorite pizza in the valley, but it was definitely better than average.

Their patio looks quite nice, but it was too hot for us to sit outside. I'd like to go again when the weather cools off. The bar has a bunch of TVs and would be a great place to watch a game. This place does have potential so I think we'll try them again this fall.

The food is really good! Don't complain about service or how long it takes to get water & a kids lemonade from Tammy, because she will come to your table and argue with you about it. Thank you to the gentleman who fixed the situation.

The last several times we've eaten here it's been more or less a disappointment. The quality of food has definitely gone down hill. (The service was never very good, and tonight was no different). Our server acted as if we were inconveniencing her by being there. The spinach dip was the highlight of the meal. The pizza was fairly soggy and the house salad was less than desirable- a small was, however, enough for two people to share. But we were charged a dollar for dressing?? Really? WTF?! I think we'll skip Upper Crust next time around....

We've been here quite a few times and its always been great pizza.  They make everything in house, fresh cheese, fresh sauce and fresh crust...oh the crust!  In my opinion its the crust that will set you above all others, and this crust is fantastic.  Try to go on Tuesday for the special $10 one topping large pizza, we usually get pepperoni and its not greasy like most pizza places.

Been here twice and thoroughly enjoyed the food and wide selection of drinks. Have to give it only 4 stars instead of 5 because we have had the same waitress both times and she is slow and doesn't check up on tables. Had to go to the bartender to ask for things a few times.

Let's start from the beginning, came with a group, everything was going fine until the end. The food was good, no doubt, but it was the service that was "sketchy". When we were done we asked to spilt the checks, our waitress was having a really hard time with this common core math, , and got real snappy with us when she couldn't get it right. It took her around 1/2 hr or more to figure out the checks. 1/2 hour later she split the checks but had doubled everything. It was painful. Even tho we told her what was on who's,it really was not that hard, and there were only 3 tables at lunch time. She was acting very strange and was twitching a lot. She was all over the place. We got there at 12:30 and left at 2:10. I had my toddler and he was about to lose it because how long it was taking her. To the owner the food was fantastic, it was the service that makes me not want to return.

Enjoyed everything about the bar.  But the lack off staff means service was slow.
Roomy rest rooms, spacious dining area, OK beer selection.  Loved the pizza.

Great Pie! The small pie is perfect for two people -awesome date place.
Stuffed mushrooms a great added bonus to the meal. (the artichoke, and Italian sausage made those mushroom oh so yummy!) 
If you can ever make it there for happy hour you should, and not just for the pricing but to try all the other small serving items on the happy hour menu. Such a great way to start the evening and end it with their desserts! 
Fantastic food and fantastic service.

Stopped in today after reading Yelp reviews.  Happy hour is only in the bar-that alone means we likely won't be back.  HATE restaurants that do that.  We always have our kids with us and like to enjoy a HH beer while out.  Waitress seemed annoyed to be at work, and the place was EMPTY.  Pizza was good and the housemade mozzarella was amazing.  Place was expensive too-$78 before tip!  If I ever patronized them again it would be for takeout.

AMAZING place for the perfect dinner! The food is absolutely delicious and the staff is incredible and super fun! If you get Nikki as a waitress you're in for a huge treat! By far one of the best places I've ever been and I can't wait to return! :)

Enjoyed Happy Hour here last night. The $3 house red was great, as were the bruschetta and small pizzas. Server was extremely busy but still personable and provided good service. It was a nice place to spend a Friday evening.

The pizza here is top notch.  Family style Italian food which is all good.
Have a decent selection of beers on tap and the wine selection seems varied (not a wine lover).
Has a NY type feel and the staff are friendly.
Decent size bar and a patio for the cooler weather.
-1 star for a pizza we got to go that was cold.

I  have been there a dozen times and I'ved lived in the hood for 12yrs. The food is always fabulous! Orgasmic in my opinion. Apparently it's a pre-rec to hate customer service and your life to work there. Not pessimistic, just a happy realist.

This was our second visit to Upper Crust.  It's located at the SE corner of Cave Creek & 101 in a nice suite that seems to be cursed for some reason...  First, there was Native Yorker (serially successful in the Valley across many locations)... After a few years, they gave up here and Brick Yard (a nice sports bar) took over the spot.  Just a few months later, that was over.

In the last year, Upper Crust moved in.  Our first visit, shortly after they opened, was not great, but showed promise.  The wings were average, and the pizza was straight up soggy in the middle.  However, you could tell the ingredients were good and it was reminiscent of Grimaldi's (same style, almost the same crust...).  The salad was... well... FRIGGIN' AWESOME.  Simple romaine, tomatoes, cucumbers, red onions, and kalamato olives topped with nice feta tossed in a simple vinegarette.  I'm not sure what kind of olive oil they use, but it was just perfect.  Just the right amount of dressing with a perfect balance of the buttery olive oil and tangy red wine vinegar.  Maybe a bit too much feta, but damn... it was good.  The pizza was much improved.  The center was still just a bit on the soft side, but as before the ingredients seemed top notch and the sauce was just right.

Happily, we can say that the kinks appear to be working out.  Tonight, we had a couple beers, a small Mediterranean salad (they say it serves 1-2, but as a first course, it's more like 3-4), and a 16" w/ onions, mushrooms, and sausage.  

The atmosphere is casual, but a bit on the quiet side (sad to say, it was probably because the restaurant was about 1/2 full on a Saturday night).  They retained all the TV's and sports programming from the Brick Yard/Native New Yorker days, but don't crank up the volume, so it's a bit unique, but cool.

The service is pleasant and earnest (admittedly, our server seemed a bit inexperienced and awkward, but effort was all there).

We'll be making an effort to visit more often (gotta hit the neighborhood places a bit more...).  

Really, this place is just an over upgrade away from being right on par with Grimaldi's and the prices are bit better.

This is a pretty cool little pizza place to come have a beer and watch a game in the bar room on one of their many flat screen TVs. They have a good happy hour 3-7. Their pizza is ok. The boneless wings are pretty bad. Nothing you would find at a Buffalo Wild Wings. The rest of the food is pretty good tho

We are frequent diners at Upper Crust, as the restaurant is less than five minutes from our house. We love the buffalo chicken pizza, which is topped with buffalo chicken, blue cheese, and celery. The crust is on the thinner side, which I like, and it's nice and flaky. The fried mozzarella is our favorite starter. They make the mozzarella fresh in-house, and it is lightly coated in their pizza crust and served with marinara sauce. The wings are great as well (we like them a little spicy, so we get them in medium), crunchy on the outside and not too heavily battered.

Based on food alone, I'd give Upper Crust five stars. However, service can be hit-or-miss. It is usually fine, but every few visits we'll have a waiter seemingly forget about us.

The first time we went, the place had been opened for a week. Food was average. Nice neighborhood joint. We had a server that was clueless and ruined the experience for us. I gave them some slack because it was opening week, but the server had no idea of the beers they served. We decided to give them another shot a month later, the service was great, but the food was still not that great. For some reason they season the food with quite a bit of salt in everything, which really ruins the flavor. We tried two pizzas which came out undercooked and the lasagna which was ok minus the insane amount of salt and being burnt on the bottom.
Great ambience for a drink, but the pizzas, pastas are not that great.

I'm lazy. I'm lazy and I like wine. What I really like is to be lazy on patios that I don't have to clean up while I drink wine. Therefore, I have found a new happy place. 

Ironically, we didn't sit on the outside patio as we had my daughter with us and the patio is 21 and over. I was bummed out but am sure the euphoria that will be induced by lounging with wine sans kids anywhere near me at a future time will make it all better. 

Our waitress was adorable and explained that she can take our order with her iPhone and that, no, she wasn't texting. Cool technology, people. We ordered the fried mozzarella after she explained it wasn't like lame fried pieces of string cheese. Oh, she steered us down a happy path. The mozzarella is fresh house made and it was wrapped in thin pizza dough and fried. If I could married it, I would have. The marinara dipping sauce was spicy and tasty. My kid hogged all the cheesy goodness. Damn her. 

Next, the three of us shared the small fettuccine with meat sauce with a few meatballs thrown in for good measure. Didn't feel like pizza but that looked REALLY good. The pasta was a little over cooked. More mushy than al dente. That's why they only get four stars. The sauce was yummy and the meatballs were freaking awesome. They had great flavor and held together really well. Personally, I would have dunked them in sauce and then served them. Just serving them baked, no sauce, made them seem dry. 

Boyfriend and I had a glass of Pinot each and the bill came to $40, and we had a $10 off coupon. Pretty sweet. Perfect amount of food. We'll definitely be back. The staff is lovely and so is the atmosphere. Looking forward to some unpretentious wine patio lounging.

I was a little shocked at the appearance of the pizza. Granted, I got it to go. But it had white cheese and was super thin. It tasted "ok." I'm sure I'll go back bc the have a great pino...but I'll probably order the wings.

Nice place and staff. Went in after our courthouse wedding and the server we had still remembers us years later. Good service and they bring the kids crust dough so they can make and bake a little appetizer while they wait.

Pizza is great and a fair price, but I always have trouble with the takeout service.

Almost every time I go to pick up a pie, I have to fight to get the attention of the bartender to get my order...even if there no one at the bar. I get weird looks when I ask for a side of ranch and the staff isn't generally friendly.

I had given this place a great review previously, but I had to edit it because of the lack of customer service and disappointment.
It's very upsetting that I booked a party of 7 (only 6 people had eaten) and was charged an added gratuity of 20% without being made aware. I called to ask for a manager and they passed the phone to someone else. I explained the situation and asked what their policy was for automatic gratuity and I was told  it was for parties 8 or more and to call back when the other manager was there. 
I sent an email to the Upper Crust via Yelp with no response. I then emailed the actual Upper Crust's website via their contact information and also received no response. I called once again and the gal who claimed to be the manager stated that it was the "servers discretion." Granted, I should have looked at the bill closer, but we were a bit focused on the bottle of wine that was charged to our tab that shouldn't have been on there. It's very disappointing that, for #1, the hostess didn't tell me that I would be charged a 20% gratuity for a party of 7 upon booking (again only 6 people were eating) and #2 the server (Claire) didn't make us aware that she added an automatic gratuity. There were three tabs at our table. The total tip that I gave Claire ended up being over $80. For the entire table, Claire made at least a $130 tip. I would have expected at least an email back regarding our disappointment.

We just had the best service from Miranda. Truly top notch! We came in around 10:15 for some pizza and never once did we feel rushed to get out by 11. She was polite, attentive and just plain delightful. 

We ordered theFried Mozzarella to start and oh my golly! I think they make it with rainbows and unicorn tears. Thick slices of fresh mozzarella wrapped in thin pizza dough and flash fried to a crispy, not greasy, crust. Pillowy pockets of cheesy heaven. It was delicious! As far as pizza, we orders a small (which is an enormous 16") half cheese, half pepperoni. The crust is thin and crisp with a perfect chewy bite to it. The sauce is light and fresh and not over powering. Somehow their cheese to sauce ratio is perfected. 

Our drinks were always full and our dishes were cleared in a timely manner. 

If you are thinking of trying it, you will not be disappointed. Very delicious!

If there was a 3 1/2 star, that is what I would select for this place. The first time I went during happy hour, it was fantastic. The other two times, not so much. The personal pizza for $4 plus $1 per topping is a good value. They make fresh Mozzarella cheese and you can definitely taste it. 

The wings are also pretty good. Honey Hot is how I like em. They have a nice beer variety and $3 house Merlot during happy hour is a nice offering. If it was more consistent, it would get a 4 star rating. The pizza sauce seems to vary in flavor from sweet to a tad spicy. Not sure why this is the case. 

The layout and flow is nice and the patio for outdoor lounging is nice when the temperature is below 90 degrees.

Went with Ashley L. and another friend.  We got seated right away and enjoyed our pizza.  That fresh mozzarella is great.  I didn't like the way they take orders, via iPod Touch, but I think that is just how things are changing and eventually it will be the norm.
This place has some damn good pizza, could not believe the size of the personal pizza , there was enough to definitely take home and the staff is good, friendly, and fast highly recommended!!!!!!!!

Upper Crust has AMAZING fried mozzarella!! We always go for that to share for an app, a medium pizza, and a bottle of wine and four of us are STUFFED.  The crust is SO good to and the pizza is even good 3 days old in the microwave!

I had Grimaldi's pizza the night before and really hoped this could rival or beat it, as Upper Crust is a good 15-20 minutes closer to my place.  Definitely not bad (the cheese definitely tasted fresh), but the sauce seemed a little bland and the pepperoni seemed to be just the generic, thin sliced kind you can get pre-packed at any grocery store.  All this considered, the crust was so good it elevated the whole to a pretty decent pizza. I was on the cusp of giving the restaurant 4 stars, but I had to wait ten minutes beyond the time I was told the pizza would be ready.  I'd understand if the place was packed when I got there, but it wasn't.   All in all, I liked the pizza enough to give this place another shot sometime in the future.
Really good pizza, wings and wine. Lots of tv's for your viewing pleasure and a real neat outside seating area to enjoy the spring weather.
Great fresh sauce and spicy pepperoni.  Mozzarella tasted handmade and crust had the right thickness.  Good pie.

My wife had to literally drag me to this place, mainly because I didn't expect there to be a decent pizza/wine place away from Old Town/Kirland/Desert Ridge areas. The place blew me away! Delicious food, friendly service, and a comforting atmosphere. 

Atmosphere: They really spent the extra cash and attention in the build out. Three sides to the restaurant, family dining area, a sports bar area, and a patio. Since college football was in play we sat in the sports bar area. There were a dozen or so TV's to catch all the games that were on. The atmosphere here was clean and inviting. 

Food: Good selection of wine and beer. Since we were watching football I thought it only natural to go with a cold beer. Was nice to see they had beers on tap that is typically not found around town, gives me another reason to go back there. Like I said before, I had low expectations going in so when our appetizers came out it blew me away; THE best stuffed mushrooms I have ever had. Next, we tried the wings, not the highlight of the meal but still fantastic. For our entree we shared a ceasar salad and pizza. If you are expecting to get a $10.99, 3 topping pizza from Dominos, with greasy cheese and crust, this isn't the place for you. The pizza is higher end with fresh topping and higher end cheese. Not the type of pizza that makes you want to gorge after, it was light and delicious. Reminded me much of Grimaldi's but with better toppings.

Service: Very friendly staff. Couldn't decide on the beer I wanted so she offered us a couple of samples. Really gave us a fantastic experience, THANKS LAURA!!

This is by far one of my husbands and my FAVORITE spots.  Living up north off of Cave Creek there are not a lot of options.  Many restaurants have occupied this space all of which we hated.  Amazing lounge area with lots of TVs, free wifi and  great staff.  Matt or Kevin usually wait on us in that area and we now actually consider them friends were there so much!!!  Only bad thing is you can not sit in the lounge area with kids...which is awesome now but will be annoying once we spawn. Gluten free options for me and when we feel like cheating delicious artichoke dip!   Patio was nice in the spring and were looking forward for the cooler weather to sit out there again.  YUMMIE PIZZA, BEER, WINE  AND SALADS and a good spot for watching sports!

I am so disappointed in the experience myself and friend had last night. He was so excited about taking me here because he said the pizza was some of the best he had ever had and he knew how much I like trying new places. 

We arrived at around 9pm and it wasn't busy. We were greeted nice enough and asked if we wanted to sit in the main seating area or the bar area. We choose the bar area so that we could also watch highlights of the game. We got a booth, the waiter in the next booth over saw us sit down so it wasn't like no one knew we were there. A waiter took care of a table two tables behind us and another waiter took care of a table that was seated one table to our right. Again nothing. We even watched as 3 waiters congregate around a table to chat it up but again nothing. After 15 mins we decided to leave. Yea we waited 15 mins. My friend was more disappointed then I was only because he felt that he had talked them up and he felt like he let me down. I told him no worries as it was there loss. I was there to hang out with him anyway. The pizza would have just been a bonus. 

Will I be back?  Probably not anytime soon. I wish I could say that it was because they were so busy. Oh well.

Review is for Lunch only.  We've had dinner here and regularly been pleased.  But the last 2 times for lunch, there have been order mishandling and errors that I'll spare the details of here.  The reason for 2 stars is that both times, management attitude has been policy over customer satisfaction.  I'm truly easy going, maybe that's the problem.   But each time I've talked to a manager, I've ended up paying full bill and walking out the door dissatisfied.

AVOID lunch!  Enjoy dinner here.

The husband and I went here for dinner (after wanting to come here for years...literally since we tried them at the Yelp Pley date...whoa) on Friday night after a not so good happy hour somewhere else. We were pleasantly surprised by their amazing service...they were on top of their game, friendly, helpful, attentive. The place was SO busy! I couldn't believe it. Despite this, we were seated fairly quickly. The food was good, we split a 'personal' pizza and the appetizer meatballs. The meatballs are really good, very juicy, and topped with house made mozz... yummy. The pizza was thinner than I expected, but it was tasty...you know what made it better? Putting some of the meatball on it...so good. Here is the weirdest part....their pizza was even better as leftovers...seriously, microwaved leftovers....it got crunchier and just was awesome...that is a good thing to note since leftover pizza isn't always so good. I would definitely make the trip out here again.

I used to be here 1-2 nights a week a couple years ago then stopped going for no real reason. Went back tonight and the place has slipped for sure. Bartenders never asked if we wanted peppers/Parmesan with our pizza then automatically gave them to the couple next to us and they had to be waved down every time the glasses were empty. Smh. Not a bad place but not great either. Costco is next door and I may just have their pizza next time.

Just wanted to add that over three years later, the pizza is still amazing.  We ventured outside of pizza and ordered the calzone, which is also quite tasty, and sometimes order the mediterranean salad to go with the pizza or calzone, which I am now addicted to.  The stuffed mushrooms and wings are also noteworthy.  To top it off the service is always consistently great.

Order To Go...12 mild wings, 12 bbq wings, great tasting. However, i will go with medium, needs more fire. 
The only thing i want to mention is, their are the drumettes and wing parts, right? 
out of the 24 wings, there was 5 drummettes and the rest was wings. I eat the wing parts and my Alex like the dummettes. We perfer it to be more equal since we are sharing. 
We have never eating here but the ambience on the patio looks very comfortable.
Maybe next time we will have to try that before it gets to warm out.

The pizza was really good. The beer and wine selection had some nice options. Im glad I tried this place I am always looking for a good pizza place.  The only thing I can suggest is maybe some customer service training for servers something is a little off with the staff.

Good prices. Horrible bartender (Mike). See picture. Sooooo inattentive.  Maybe that's why it's empty at HH. He's also Dropping f-bombs talking with clients. Checking cell phone instead of filling drinks. 

No HH menu/price list. Heard servers and bartender try to explain to customers, both here and over the phone, what the HH prices were.

Men's room missing soap dispenser and has graffiti on the mirror.

Dinner was fantastic! Waiter knew his stuff pairing a great wine and suggested beer flavor to a great pizza and salad. 
Pizza was a tomato less sauce. The basil pesto and garlic sauce set our taste buds into a spiral of greatness. Dinner prices are so very reasonable. Eating outside on a comfortable couch is again very relaxing.

Went 1-4-17 for dinner with my daughter.  Read all of the reviews prior to leaving the house so was hoping for the best.  Laura was our server - EXCELLENT service - thank you, Laura.  Had the meatballs (very tender/tasty), the anti pasta plate (it was per the description so can't complain there, but a variety of meats and cheeses would have made it a great plate), fried mozzarella (unique way to prepare mozzarella), and spinach dip (very flavorful).  All in all, this is a neighborhood gem.  It's not, nor is it meant to be, some 5 star Italian restaurant.  It's just good food, with excellent service, and a relatively good wine list for the type of restaurant it is.  Also, Wednesday is 1/2 price wine day - all day.  I will definitely return.
One of our favorite pizza places!  We usually take out, but the times we have eaten there have been enjoyable as well.  Their Pizza and Salads are very good!
What a nice find. Gluten free for the wife, and half price wine on Wednesday night for me!  The pizza was excellent and prices seemed reasonable. The wife said the gluten free crust was excellent b

Fantastic pizza - thin, buttery crust,  not swimming in cheese or sauce! Speaking of sauce, theirs is a simple tomato sauce with seasoning added on top of the toppings. Made for some awesome bites - mild seasoning or simple sauce, or both - loved it!

Hubby and I shared their "small" Mediterranean salad.  Excellent dressing, not overly seasoned,  letting the olives, tomatoes, cucumbers,  and red onions show thru with that yummy feta cheese!  Well done! 

Plus,  hubby was happy, they serve Sierra Nevada!

LOVE THIS PLACE!  My girls and I love coming here (close to home).  Andrew is our favorite waiter, he recognizes us, knows our favorites and treats us awesome!  We come back, always...and will continue!

I have been here a few times now, and it's been usually great!

I love the patio and the fact that the patio is only for age 21 and up.  On a nice night, it's great to sit out there having a drink and eating their delicious pizza!  I also love that they have one of my favorite beers, Ace Pear Cider!  Not many places carry cider, so this is a huge bonus!  

There were still seats available at 6:30 in the evening, so it wasn't too full.  The wait staff has always been pleasant and nice.

I do love their pizza!  I'm from Chicago and I feel like I am a bit of a pizza snob, but I love their thin sausage pizza!  They use such fresh ingredients and I love their mozzarella.  So fresh and delicious!  I also like their Mediterranean salad.

I have ordered pizza to go from here twice, and both times I wasn't super impressed with it.  I think once I got it home it was cold and just not as good.  But I know I love it when I'm there!
I was very  disappointed in the restaurant due  the fact that it was freezing  and couldn't enjoy my meal and told the waitress a few times to put up the heat. Won't be back

My family and I came to Upper Crust after receiving a free pizza card from Yelp's playdate.  It was a pretty long drive for us, but well worth it.  We had good service.  We asked the server what she suggested and she said that the mozzarella was a must.  I always ask for suggestions, but normally still order what I originally wanted.  This time I listened.  I am so glad that I did.  The fried mozzarella was wonderful!  I would order it again.  It was sooo fresh!  We also ordered the mushrooms which were ok.  The pizza looked beautiful, but it tasted ok...it needed a tad bit more marinara.  I would go back.

Hands down the worst service. Owner could care less and outside of Alan, no one in that restaurant cares about the customers. With way too many places to patronize and spend your money on average food, I'd suggest you venture elsewhere.
I love this place best pizza and wings in the valley by far. They have a great drink selection too!

Weve moved here from back east, and thought that we'd never find pizza we loved as much as back home!  Well, WE FOUNT IT AT UPPER CRUST!! Best Pizza I can remember having, crust was perfect, flavor was out of this world, and they even gave us a private area for a family party.  Wish there was one in MY neighborhood :)

This is one of our to go spots but today early Sunday afternoon my husband and i walked in to catch a game and spend some together time and we sat at the bar for about 7 mins or so...it seemed long..and we waited for bartender to greet us...he then stood in front of us making a drink for someone else no eye contact with us or a  hello ...he tended to others and mind you it was not busy...we waited another minute passed us up again so we left. Really disappointed.  All he needed to say was be right with you but we got nada!  Food is great...but guess today was an off day.

Food was tasty, This place has a great wine and beer selection. It has anchor stream on tap. Menu needs expansion though. I would like to see pre made combos on the pizza menu and a kids menu. I think this place has potential though if it expands its menu as the pizzas are excellent.

My Fiance and I have become regulars here for happy hour after moving to the area. I can't get enough of their wings, they are the best and I am addicted to them now. They also have a great house white wine for $3 on their happy hour menu. We occasionally get pizza, which is delicious. The thin crust kind that is only is good hot so eat it quick! When it's not too hot we love to sit on their little patio. I wish it wasn't next to the parking lot, takes away from the ambiance a bit but it is still comfortable. Inside has a nice laid back feel as well now that it is too warm for outside. A lot of people's reviews are low due to no children in the lounge or patio. As an adult with no children who wants to relax at happy hour after work I really like and prefer this. They don't extend happy hour to the family dining area, which I think maybe they should. 

Only reason I gave it four stars instead of five is because it can be hard to get the waitresses attention to come serve on the patio when you get there since it is open seating. Service can occasionally be a tad slow, but the waitresses are always friendly to us. 

All in all I love this place as my go to spot. Definitely worth checking it out!!!!
Really nice place to eat pizza. Friendly staff, very knowledgeable. Atmosphere is very relaxing. Pizza is very good. But this place can get pricey. I will be coming back with family and friends.

i had some issues at AT&T recently which required me to spend time in the shopping center in which Upper Crust is located. I decided to take some time and check out Upper Crust. I was stressed out and needed to regroup. I walked into the door and the immediate sense of calmness was in the air. I decided to have some food and beverages at the bar. 

The ambiance was  of being invited to a best friends house for dinner. Perfect lighting, perfect receiving, perfect welcome. I sat down and had the most incredible appetizer that was simply tomatoes covered with mozzarella cheese, oil and spices. WOW. I felt like I was in Italy! 

I left Upper Crust with a calm sense of the inevitable. Back to AT&T to finish my business in a peaceful state of mind. 

Thanks Upper Crust.

Our first visit was on a Saturday around 830pm The place was not busy and it took awhile for someone to seat us. The service was ok. The pizza was very tasty and the wings were amazing! The second time we meet up with a friend for happy hour; enjoyed the 5 dollar pizza but no drink specials . Definitely will be back for the food!
I absolutely love this place!!  They have an amazing happy hour (till 7pm) and great lunch specials:)  Thank you Michelle for introducing me to this fantastic place!!!  The pizza is top notch!!

Very excited to have another restaurant in the neighborhood.

Ate here last night with some friends. Pizza was very good but the wine is way over priced. 

$42 for a bottle of Petite Petite is crazy!  I don't think they can classify themselves as a wine bar.  The wine selection is not of wine bar quality and the atmosphere does not allow them to charge as much as they do for the wine.

I will go back for the pizza but will not make this my neighborhood wine stop.

This place is as much Italian as Pizza Hut.  Server was very nice but the food is bad.  They want $12.00 for a small Linguine "dinner" that includes nothing.   I asked for a side salad and I got a few pieces of lettuce in a bowl right out of the cooler for an additional $2.50.  I asked for bread and they do not have bread unless I want to order it off the appetizer menu.   WHAT REAL ITALIAN PLACE SERVES A MEAL WITHOUT BREAD!!  If you like Pizza Hut stye food this is the place for you.  I am staying far away.

Tucked into the shopping complex this location can be easy to miss if you aren't looking for it. We ventured over here since it was close to our place at the time and we were hoping for good eats close by. The inside has a definite New York style feel to it when you go it. We were seated right away and had our drinks quickly.

The menu is a variety of what you'd expect from any Italian eatery - pizza, pasta, calzones, etc. The food was tasty and the ambiance is nice if you are looking for a good date night spot. They offer a variety of weekly specials, so check it out to see what may be happening when you go.

Overall: A
Good eats, easy going vibe and nice staff.

Have frequented this place several times and felt it was time to give a review. 

 I have noticed the last few visits that my pizza is burned black around the crust and/or doughy and limp in the middle so inconsistent baking here folks!  Ordered a calzone last night and it was bland, no garlic AT ALL and the dough was limp and the filling all kept falling out - not a true calzone!  

My biggest gripe about this place is the revamped pick-up and take-out process. You have to walk into the bar, jump up and down to get noticed to let them know you are there to get your order, be made to feel like you are interrupting the staff be being there, play cat and mouse trying to stay out of the way of everyone while you are backed up to a wall next to the bar waiting for an ungracious server to bring you your meal.  Then you play a balancing act trying to hold the bill and pen in hand to sign the receipt which you can't see because you are in a dark corner. I've decided not to return after the rude manner in which I was treated by the staff last night and I know they get a large part of biz from take-out.  Better re-think this part of the process there, I'm sure other patrons do not return for the same reasons.  Go back to bringing take-out the the front hostess stand on the restaurant side of the place like you used to and make even your PAYING take-out customers feel appreciated!
Upper crust has great pizza and wings. Also take out and just the same when you get it home ;) wish they delivered !

My second home, no seriously , its that good! Cant say I was ever in the place before so I wont be making any comparisons. 

Dough!- The pizza is perfect! I always get the personal size, with italian sausage and ricotta cheese. Its big for being a personal , I usually share it with my main man and it fits us perfectly, however I think for most people its not for splitting. Its thin crust , sorta similar to Grimaldis but better! and not as pricey. They seem to use a similar style bread on the spinach dip too and it melts in your mouth! noms!

Friends behind the bar- I have only been at the bar seats, but the servers are all friendly and happy to chat with you even when your not at their table. Bartenders are super awesome. All are fun and talkative. Making drinks quick and having a good conversation is hard to find!!

Wine bar?- The sign says Patio and wine bar, soooo it is.. but its very unpretentious , so if you are just getting into wine or are not at all , dont be shy come on in.. its not pricey and the guys are here to help! Plus a good selection of draft and bottle beers! If you like good wine, get in here! I you are a beer drinker, get in here! If you just like a goo place with good friend and soda, get in here!

Break it down Jess- All in all its a great place, half price wine bottles on Wednesday, and a great happy hour. My only thought that if you go to this wine bat for a bottle of wine with friends for a quite time, dont go during any sporting events as there are tons of tv's( which is great) but could easily turn into a guys bar during those times. But I love this place!!!!!!

See you there!!!

My review is on the take out service. I have not dined in yet. I always crave this pizza. It is the best in the area, hands down. Great togo service. The lady even asked me if I wanted plates. I think she read my mind! (I was low on plates and just ran the dishwasher) great little place. Keep it up

Went there the other night, had Pizza and wings.  The pizza was ok-good, really not the style I like, so if I were you, reading the review, I'd take that wiht a grain of salt.  It was large and very thin.  Like 1/2 as thick as a Rosati's.  The good news is the price is much mroe reasonable than Rosatis.

Now to the really good news.  The wings.  Very, very good, like a 14 out of 15 on my proprietary scale of wings.  Would have been 15 out of 15 if they had left them in the fryer a few moments longer.  they bake the wings ahead of time, then fry them quickly to crisp them before adding a perfect, thin sauce (not the ketchup like stuff you get at some "wings" palces".  These are, in my opinion, some of the best I've had in Phoenix.  Let's give it another shot to ensure they're consistent... and ask them to drop them in the frier a little longer!

The other reason I gave them 4 of 5 - and if they ONLY did wings they'd already have a 5/5 - was I don't care for the happy hour policy.
