If they need some real Mexicans to help with getting the cooking straight, we have plenty in California we can send!

The food overall was pretty good. We went late on a Monday night, and they were still pretty fast. They were out of one of the burritos that my dad wanted. I would however recommend that you go mad Mex, which is close to Don Pablo's

We went here a couple of weeks ago and didn't have the best experience.  We waited over ten minutes to be greeted.  (we were preparing to leave when we were greeted) and they were not busy.  There were perhaps 15 tables all together, and there were at least 5 waitstaff there that I counted.  The waitress was polite when we're being waited on and the food for the most part was tasty. A bit cold but not the worst Mexican food that I have had.
It's chain Mexican food. Not much more exciting than that. Server was attentive and at the table almost as much as the fruit flies were.

Went there with a group of men from my church.  The service was excellent.  Unfortunately, I forget the our server's name to give her credit but she was fantastic.

It was all you can eat fajita night last night.  We all got our money's worth.  The fajitas were quite tasty, especially the steak ones.  We polished off quite a bit of food.

But the most delicious thing was the desert.  One person ordered one, and I don't even know what it was or what it was called, but it was like a fried tortilla with a honey-type sauce on it and powdered sugar.  Oh my, was it absolutely delicious!

So we wanted to try somewhere new and landed on Don Pablos- not the best decision we've ever made.  Not the worst, either, but certainly not the best.. or even second, or third, or 10th best.  Anyway, we walked in and the theming I thought was pretty cool.  The fountain in the middle, the decor, the music, I thought it all was pretty good which made me  pretty pumped that we had chosen a good place.  WRONG.  Our server had zero personality.  Our food had zero flavor.  So there was really nothing that made us want to go back.  The prices were good, but as they say, you get what you pay for, which at this place is very little.  The portions were pretty big, but you could give me mountains and mountains of food, and if it doesn't taste good, who cares how much there is?  And speaking of prices, I asked for guacamole and my husband asked for sour cream (who doesn't automatically serve sour cream with EVERy dish at a mexican place, anyway?).. after she forgot my teeny tiny little dish of guac and I had to ask again for, we get the bill and they charged both of us!  The guacamole, I kinda get, but sour cream??  Thats like places that charge for ranch.  What is that about??  Anyway, to sum it all up, if you're looking for low prices and big portions, then this is your place.  But if you're also looking for decent service and food that you actually enjoy, you may want to reconsider.  You've been warned.
Horrible!! if you have 4 hours on ur hands to wait then this is your place, horrible food and service! and  thats not just from one visit its been 3 ( i thought i would give another chance

Walked into the establishment tonight with my two cousins.  There was a wait and tons of people waiting while there were multiple booths and tables open.  We asked our hostess that since there were high-tops available in the bar area if we could eat upstairs.  She said sure there is no wait to be seated in the bar area.  So off we went!  We we claimed an empty table and asked for it be cleared and cleaned.  We were then attacked by the waitress that "This table is reserved for waiting people"  We then tell her that the hostess told us it was OK for us to sit up here.  Well the waitress insisted that we couldn't sit there since it not open.  So she and her pissy attitude stormed off and went to belittle the hostessing staff.  While she was gone.... another waiter came over and basically said the same thing to us.  Needless to say... we stood our ground and claimed the table for the remaining of the evening.  We were so blessed to have to miserable soul as our waitress for the night.  My cousin ordered her dinner with special requests and when she got her food.... none of her requests were fulfilled. We asked multiple times to have our chips and salsa refilled and that was so as molasses. Me along with my cousins were in fear of asking for refills or additional special requests. As we were eating our dinner we witness our "table situation" happen again to another party that sat at another high-top.  Both waitress yelled at the customers and then SCREAMED at the hostess staff in addition to the waiter belittling the customer as he did to our party.  At the end of the evening our "princess" waitress came and asked if we needed checks.  I said yes but I am separate from my other two cousins.  Just make me separate and I requested a drink to go.  She so nicely rolled her eyes and *sighed* at me like I asked her to change a tire on my car.  When she came back... she had separated ALL our checks and slammed my to-go drink down in front of me. We did talk to the Manager on Duty about our issues and she said she would look into it and have a talk with our selected staff we had for the evening.  What I didn't understand was why there was such a huge wait of people lined up in their hallways especially when they had TONS of empty tables and booths open.  Personally with the economy being the way it is.... I would think that you (as a waiter/waitress) would want to fill the table for more chances of getting good tips.  I felt like my business was not wanted and they just wanted an empty bar area for the night.  How would  you make money off an empty room dumbfounds me? Just IMO.

The complimentary tortilla chips were the best chips I have ever eaten. Worth going there for the chips alone!
Sad to see it go from the Robinson location!!

The food was okay. The ones we used to go to in Cleveland closed so we took the opportunity to try this location. The food was not as good as we remembered. Our waitress was great but way too much drama from some of the other waitresses and bartender. They seated us by the waiter station where they were constantly bickering and complaining about each other. Even dropping expletives at times and our family could hear everything they were saying. Not at all what should be happening in front if customers. We asked for the manager and told him what's going on and he just said he was sorry. He looked shocked and didn't know what else to say. Didn't offer us anything. We even ordered dessert and they didn't comp it. Very disappointing experience.

I have been here several times.  The problem with this place is that nothing is consistent.  Sometimes they totally nail it.  Sometimes the food is off.  Or sometimes you get rotten service.

Even the rules vary from visit to visit: things that you always get will all of a sudden be an "extra charge", or drinks suddenly become available by the pitcher only.  

When everything is good, this place is great!   But you just can't count on that with every visit.
Love love love this location!  I always stop here and take advantage of their great lunch specials when flying into the Pittsburgh airport.

We go here for lunch all the time.  Quick service and the queso is yummy. Try taco Tuesday.  Unlimited tacos.  The tortilla chips are made right there.  

The only problem is the rest rooms are not as clean as I would like them to be

I've been going to Don Pablos for years. I grew up in Virginia and would always go with my family. Now, living in Pittsburgh I've gone to this location probably about 10 times. The quality of food as well as the service seems to be getting worse every time I go. 
Tonight, my boyfriend and I went for dinner. Right when we walked in, we stood at the host stand patiently for about 5 minutes...After the same employee/server walked by us about 4 or 5 different times, he asked if we've been seen yet - We just politely shook our heads no as he walked away to go get the hostess. After that, it took an additional 3 or 4 minutes for her to come out and actually seat us. 
Once we were sat, it took about 5 minutes for our server (Lindsey #561) to come over and introduce herself. We ordered soda and Border Dip. Once the Border Dip came out, it was only warm as though it was waiting in the kitchen for a while. She forgot the tortillas that were suppose to come with it which I brought up to her and she seemed annoyed that I asked for something that was suppose to be included in the appetizer to begin with. Once I got my dinner (Combo - Pick Two) which was two crunchy beef tacos with a side of sour cream, there was so much grease from the taco meat that I didn't even finish one of my two tacos. A puddle of grease covering the entire bottom of my plate - the tacos themselves made me sick. I had to ask for my side of sour cream 3 separate times before she actually went to get it for me. Our server didn't stop by even ONCE to ask us if we needed anything or how our food was. My drink was completely empty for an entire hour and never actually got a refill. The sad part? They weren't even busy. This was the worst service I've ever had. Worst $40 experience for even worse food and service.

We were a party of 6.  4 adults and 2 children.
I have been to this restaurant many years ago and did not have a good experience.
Thought we would give it another chance.   I dine all over the country and  Don Pablo's is not up to my standards,  
Ice tea has no taste, lemonade weak, guacamole appetizer dissapointing. Small scoop, tasteless and the chips underneath were soggy.  My stuffed burrito which I ask for white queso cheese came cold and hard looking like plastic oner it.
Grilled Chicken salad had water in the bottom of the bowl.
Qusedia were cold with no taste. 
The salsa that come to the table with the chips taste like you open a can of tomatoes to make spaghetti sauce.  Absolutely no taste.
I have no intension to return knowing that I can get my Mexican fix elsewhere and enjoy it.
Worst service i have ever experienced. Waitress forgot an order, messed up our check and never refilled drinks. Food was average-typical chain mexican food. Won't go back to this location again.

Went for dinner and was pleasantly surprised with the food.  

My brother had the beef and chicken fajitas and it was a good portion.  I had the Chile rellenos and taco.  It's hard to find a good chile relleno here in the north and this place had it almost spot on.

Service was okay.  I did have to chase the waitress down to get my brother a few more soft tortillas because three was simply not enough for the amount of food they served.  Probably if I didn't have to go find her, I would have given it four starts. They weren't that busy and they had enough staff on the floor that I shouldn't have had to go get her.

Over all, it was good food for what we had and will be going back again.

If I could give it 0 I would. Bad food, bad service, restaurant is dirty and not well maintained.  Specifically, our server was not familiar with the menu, I ordered an Arnold Palmer and there was black mold in the drink, fruit flies everywhere, shells in my shrimp fajitas and broken bathroom stall, broken hand soap dispenser and the other hand dispenser was empty of soap. How are severs and cooks washing their hands?!?! Overall disgusting and I will never go back. I should have known better when it's 615on a Saturday and the restaurant was practically empty. Don't waste your money- go to mad mex instead or el campesino.

The food is especially yummy, some of the best Tex Mex you can get on the East Coast I'm sure. (I'm from Texas.)

The service? Absolutely horrid! I've NEVER had good service at this location and with it's closeness to the PIT airport, I've been here plenty of times. However, the food is the reason I continue to go back - I'm consistent with eating fajitas here and they've never gone wrong. Tender meat, even the steak here is more tender than other places' chicken. If you don't like the prices, try their weekly specials. I know that Wednesday's are $8.99 fajitas, and they have several other pretty good deals.

Came back home to the burgh for a couple of days. Decided to come here cause it was close to the hotel and we were starving. Have been here before and had one bad experience with service, but that was a couple of years ago. Never had any prob with the food. Ordered my dinner, think they called it the texas two step. A few ribs, BBQ chic breast rice and beans. Food was good. Only complaint is that it coulda had some more BBQ sauce on it. This time the service was great. Drinks always full, food served up fast and hot. If anything was needed, their manager was out walking the floor making sure every need was taken care of. Still full.

A total waste of calories.  Ordered hard tacos and the waitress brought out soft tacos, but with some hard tacos (unfilled) on a plate. She said that I could switch them out (?) at the table or she'd take them back to the kitchen and have them do it.  How about just bringing the right stuff in the first place? The LAST thing i would do is send them back to the kitchen to be "fixed".  Also had refried beans...inedible as they were too salty to eat, and the tilapia in the tacos tasted like dirt.  I wouldn't eat here again if somebody gave me a gift certificate......WAIT!! someone did give me a gift certificate!  Glad I didn't have to pay for this meal.

I really like this place.  Being that we are transplants from AZ, it is hard to find authentic Mexican food that is good.  Their food is yummy and they also show the caloric count for each item on their menu.  Very helpful!  We will go back for sure.

Kleines vietnamesisches Imbissrestaurant (hat nichts mit Thai zutun)!!! Das essen ist ok, aber nichts besonderes. 
MfG
Leckerer Schnellasiate, nette Bedienung. Ich empfehle die gebratenen Nudeln mit Garnelen.
Schlichte Einrichtung aber schnelles und gutes Essen. Sehr empfehlenswert.
Große Auswahl und sehr lecker! Die Einrichtung ist einfach, die Bedienung bzw. Angestellten sind sehr nett. Es geht schnell, auch zum Mitnehmen absolut zu empfehlen.

This small restaurant is not just selling Thai food but also Vietnam and Chinese food. I ordered 3 of my Vietnamese food but unfortunately they are all tasteless. I will try Thai food next time and maybe Thai food is their specialty. They don't accept any credit cards at all.
Jedes Mal ein super Essen. Absolut zu empfehlen! Es gibt jeden Tagesessen mit Suppe dazu. Die Angebote gelten auch abends.

This has become my go-to late night dinning place. As you walk in you order directly at the counter. They have English menus available and accept cash only. Decent sized portions for a low price. Expect to spend less than 10 euros. Service is quick and of good quality. I normally take my dishes to-go. I recommend the breaded chicken with vegetables. This place is nothing to write home about, but good for a quick cheap meal after you are sick of kebabs.

Being that it's Easter weekend, every store and most restaurants are closed, except for the Asian ones. Lucky for us, this was open. 
You can order to go with their cheap lunch boxes or dine in. Their entrees are all under 10€ with most under 8€. I decided on the fried duck with peanut sauce and this was pretty amazing! The duck was perfectly fried to a crisp and the meat was tender and juicy! The sauce itself was a hair too salty but I guess Germans like it this way. Hubs got the pho. The broth was not quite salty enough but the noodles were spot on and the flavor was perfect. Just needed more of it. The spring rolls were a hit as well. Served with a spicy sweet sauce, it's the perfect cheap appetizer, with two pieces at 3,50€. 
Will definitely come back!! Lucky for me it's about a 20 minute walk from my apt :)

This location I happen to like because it's in the mall! Well I give it 4 stars. They have a few managers who work at this location. If your a size 20-22 you can find clothes to fit your beautiful curves & be easy on your checkbook.

I love this Lane Bryant. Yes, mostly because of it's location too.

For those unaware, Lane Bryant services the big beautiful women. Sizes 14-28 women. This location offers a wide variety of clothing and has the Cacique line in a separate section of the store, (big enough that it has it's own entrance too).

Now, why do love this store so much more opposed to others in the valley? I know Lane Bryant is a corporation and their items do not vary much store by store but they do. Because boulevard is urbanized I feel that this location has a younger, hipper selection to it's clothes. 

I have gone to other Lane Bryant's in the valley and felt like I was shopping for my grandmother or something. It just felt old and retired. 

This location steadily has a huge clearance section of clothes. Worth searching through, especially right when the season changes over. You can definitely find some good deals.

The staff that work here almost always plus size women and yes, that makes me feel comfortable. To know that another woman of my stature can relate to how I feel and look in clothes makes it that much better for me.

Want an item of clothing that they do not have in your size at the store? They will order it on-line for you and have it shipped to the store for free. 

The dressing rooms are spacious and well lighted. Not those funny dressing room mirrors that make you look good and then as soon as you go home and look in your mirror, you are like what the heck was I thinking!?!

Don't let my one check in fool you. Before my yelping days, you could easily catch me here on pay day. I have never ever had a bad experience here and if something started to go south, an associate quickly fixed it.

I am loyal to the Lane Bryant brand and the stores associates have always provided great customer service but this place takes the cake!  I was attended to, informed of deals, made me feel comfortable, went above and beyond to find me the items I was looking for and was not pushy in any way like other places.  Thank you for a great shopping experience!

Being that I'm the first Pittsburgher to review UUBU6, it pains to me rate this typically superb restaurant with only 2 stars. But unfortunately last Saturday night, my lofty expectations fell well short of what we had experienced here before. We arrived early for our reservation at this funky spot up the hill on the South Side, and decided to have a drink at the cool bar of what used to be the Workingman's Beneficial Union No. 6 lodge (somehow they get UUBU6 out of all of that). I was excited to see a large beer tub full of one of my favorite beers, Blue Point Hoptical Illusion, and quickly ordered two for the guys. Our ladies each decided on a pomegranate martini which were so strong even I had a hard time taking a sip. The four of us were seated in the grand main dining room with the yellow and green checker board ceiling and the dramatic yellow drapery. But unfortunately after we sat down, the staff forgot we were there. We waited almost 20 minutes until a server approached us and asked if we were ready to order. I said "we would be happy to order if we had menus." You can see where this night was headed. The server apologized and quickly returned with our menus.  UUBU6's menu tonight looked nothing like the menu on the website (it does say "menu subject to change upon the Whim of the Chef" ) but I have to say we were very disappointed with the night's offerings. The entire first page was a Lenton menu ( this was a Saturday night) with 8-10 seafood specials. But the biggest disappointment was the fact that there was only one appetizer (asparagus frito misto) to go along with 3 or 4 salads. Are you serious???   The app selction on the website had so many different choices and our only option was asparagus which also happened to be the vegetable of the day?  Fortunately I saw a very attractive cheese and fruit plate on the dessert cart next to our table and we decided to order it for our appetizer. The waiter obliged and it was actually a very good selection of a Maytag blue, a brie, a borsin and a smoked Gouda to go along with the grapes, strawberries, crackers and bread. The wine list is extensive and is attached to every menu, so after finally settling on a bottle of wine, we were sorry to learn that it was unavailable. Our server suggested a similar California Red from the $20 bottle list. I was confused because none of our menus had this value list. So he returned with another menu and we were lucky to have a very good Cali Pinot Noir.  The salads were just okay with a blood-orange vinaigrette.  Nothing to get excited about.   But  my seafood bisque was very flavorful and hearty. My lady ordered the Hangar steak with mustard sauce and sweet potato fries. Our server informed us that he thought they were out of it so he asked her for a plan B in case it was unavailable. After another 20 minutes, we motioned to our server to see if she was getting the hangar steak and he informed us that there indeed was one left. We wished there hadn't been because the steak came out a little overcooked, but drowning in mustard flavor. But her biggest disappointment was that the accompanying fries weren't sweet potato, just plain ordinary steak fries. She wouldn't have ordered the steak if she had known they were out of sweet potatoes and our server again neglected to mention this to us. As for my dish, I went in ready to order either a duck or a lamb dish from the website but of course neither were on tonights menu.  So I decided on the soft shell crabs with spring onion and tomato relish. I chose poorly.  The "salsa" on top was just that, chopped tomato and sliced green onion.   But that was the least of my entree's problem. The soft shells were so salty I could feel my blood pressure rising with each bite. It was almost laughable but by now I was too hungry to send them back. Apparently it was contagious, because the accompanying asparagus also seemed to be inflicted with this same salt problem. In fairness, our dining companions enjoyed their dishes, I especially liked his Angus beef tenderloin (we like to try each others dishes) but his wife's salmon dish was a little on the dry side. The dessert cart (again, none of the desserts on the website were on the cart tonight) sells itself with the elegantly arranged trays of small cakes and pastries. The ladies' Chocolate flourless cake wasn't very awe-inspiring but a strawberry Napoleon with whipped cream was sublime. All things considered, and because of my $50 gift certificate (thanks WPXI Just Pay Half) our final tally came to $65 per couple.  All things considered, UUBU6 can give you a pretty good bang for your buck with the $20 wine list and also a $30 recession buster prix fix feature.   So as you can see, you can get pretty good value here.   As long as the kitchen and waitstaff  rekindle the commitment to excellence that I had come to expect when UUBU6 first ascended up the slopes of the South Side.

Good food and unassuming location.

I've eaten here twice and thought the food was excellent. They don't have many choices at any particular time, but everything put on the table has been good. 

The Valentine's special menu for $66 per couple including a glass of wine, shrimp appetizer, salad, filet, crab cake, vegetable, dessert and coffee was by far the best deal on a meal I've had in years. The three couples left wondering how they could serve so much for $33 a person.

What is particulary appealing is low-key, quiet nature of this place. You can hear the other people at the table without shouting.
Great little hidden place...friendly staff...great food! Diane (waitress) takes the cake though...she's hysterically awesome!!!

Perfect day to check out the Underground City since it was wet and rainy. I had planned to walk the entire thing, but halfway into it, I was getting bored so we ended up leaving and walked around Chinatown instead.

The place is filled with lots of shops and eateries. There's quite a food court (didn't eat there) there and it links malls together as well as takes you to the Metro. It's clean and there are places to sit and rest your feet.

It reminds me of the underground tunnels in Houston, TX which serves as an underground network of shops and eateries for locals to escape the harsh conditions of the Texas heat. I imagine when Winter comes, people are more apt to travel in the Underground City to get their errands done or to get to the Metro.

If it had better food and store selections, then I'd give it 3 or 4 stars. I was expecting more and was underwhelmed. Maybe I hyped it up in my head too much. I'm sure if I was there in the winter, I'd be seeking refuge there, but above ground in Montreal in the summer was too pretty to miss!

A great way to explore the city during cold winter months. It is more like an "Indoor" city than underground. Most of the paths are clean except patches which are not completely insulated or as clean.

I love the Underground City in Montreal!  It reminds me of the Underground PATH in Toronto.  When it's raining outside, super cold or super hot, underground is the way to go!  

What I love most is that if you take the train into Montreal and you're staying in one of the downtown hotels, you can probably walk most of the way underground.  

The Underground City connects to all the big downtown malls.  So you can go from the Central Train Station, through Les Halles de la Gare, to Place Ville Marie, through this corridor (I don't know what the name is, but it has shops and restaurants), to the Eaton Centre, then if you go west you go to Place Montreal Trust, to Carrefour Industrielle Alliance, to Les Cours Mont-Royal.  If you go east from the Eaton Centre, you go to Complexe les Ailes, then Promenades Cathédrale, which then connects to La Baie.  We're talking 8 hour shopping marathon all underground, no need to come up for sunlight, haha!  

Signage is pretty good throughout the Underground City too.

I think the most impressive part about RÉSO is its sheer magnitude. It's pretty much an underground mall that spans over 20 miles. If you're a shopaholic, this is the place for you. Otherwise, it's just a really, really, REALLY big mall. 

There are lots of great things to do and see in Montreal, but if you're looking for a way to kill 30 minutes or so - just enter RÉSO through one of its many entrances throughout the city and try not to get too lost.

Pssst!  Where is the..."Underground City?"
Montreal's secret shopping paradise, 
often called the "Underground Mall," 
is a MUST for shopping when it's cold out!

SHOPPING: Although it is a mall, of sorts, it offers 
SO much more than simply shopping. The underground city 
is one continuous group of tunnels that connects buildings 
to 7 metro stations in downtown Montreal Quebec. 
NOTE: It's easy for tourists to get lost down under,
despite the signs pointing to main streets and metro stations.

WEATHER: Canada suffers LONG, COLD WINTERS, 
and this Underground City is a world of warmth.
It's also a fun way to get around the downtown area.

DINING: The food courts here offer fabulous, fresh options, 
many of which can compete with the area restaurants.
You can even open a bottle of wine with your dinner.

THE DEAL:  Their winter art festival is also held here!

Neat to be shopping underground at this massive mall which reminded me of Tokyo Central station where everything's underground and there isn't a tremendous amount of natural light and you have to follow the signs to get to where you're headed lest you take the wrong exit and end up halfway across Montreal!

Lots of retail shopping options, tons of restaurants of all sorts and prices.

I wasn't planning on buying anything and I managed to stick with it. But it was a close call.

I was very fascinated by this place. The underground city is one continuous mall that spans 7 metro stations in the downtown area. Famous for its endless shops and boutiques and a sanctuary for those who seek to escape the unforgiving summer heat or the bitterness of winter, the underground city is an interesting way to get around the downtown area, great for grabbing some quick eats and window shopping some famous stores. Admittedly, it is very easy to get lost in here - once you've ducked into the maze that is the underground city, it's hard to tell where you'll end up. Although, there are semi-helpful signs posted everywhere to point to essential streets and metro stations to make sure you don't stray too far from your destination.

What an amazing feature in this extremely cold city in the winter. I went to Montreal in February 2007, and while many people said I was crazy, I knew about this underground city while researching my trip.

Montreal's underground city is directly underneath this amazing city. It is 19 miles long, and it links many major buildings and shopping options.

This underground city is spotless! As a New Yorker, I walked through this tunnel, and was amazed by the cleanliness of the passageways.

So many restaurants, stores and other things to do while walking around the city below Montreal. My hotel, the Fairmont Queen Elizabeth had an escalator outside its lobby door that brought you down to the underground city.

I was amazed by the extent of this place. At first I thought it was just an underground shopping mall, but quickly realized that it's function was to cut out passage through surface streets altogether in the winter time. The large atriums let plenty of light in, even if you're subterranean. There are numerous food courts and plenty of good shopping. 

The passageways connect you to hotels, conference centers, subway stops, cultural centers. 

It's supposed to be 2 miles of passageways but feels longer. We walked all the way to one end, at the Westin to reach old Montreal without stepping outside. Amazing.

Smart Idea. When it's cold outside, create an indoor mall.   Not only indoors but underground.  Some areas are free to enter, some you have to pay.  Best to ask the information desk for details and map. 

Walked around and it was pretty packed.  Montreal can get really cold. 
Also ate at the food court. Tried the french savory crepes, Korean bbq beef, mediterranean fried fish, and a nutella crepe.  All were pretty good! 

The place can be like a maze, so best to carry a map.  there are some exits that lead you to the outside.  it's very exciting!

Inside, it looks just like a mall. But what gives it its charm is that it's underground! I felt like I was exploring an underground city that thrived after some horrific disaster that occured above ground. For a few seconds, I thought 'Waterworld' meets "Blast from the Past". There really is no logic behind it, but that's what I felt, and what I feel is a result of my feelings. That makes sense.

There weren't many chain-retail stores (they were all above ground, those snooty bastids), mostly off brands and family-owned businesses. But browsing through mom-and-pop shops made me feel warm inside. Some of the shopowners tried their best to push merchandise, and I was a victim of their puppy-face guilt-trip sales pitches. But no worries, I needed another pair of faux-shearling-lined cowboy boots.

I think I was expecting too much. I heard it was an underground city. If someone would have just told me it was mostly just an elaborate mall I think I would have had a more realistic idea of what I was walking into. 

If I lived here I think I would have a greater appreciation for being able to shop and walk around without having to step outside. However, I was here to see Montreal's sights and shopping centers don't really do it for me.

I actually expected more... I don't know - maybe some flea markets? But this was literally an extended version of NYC's subway system - several tunnels leading to an entrance to either a subway or a mall...

RESO definitely worth a solid 3 star if it is cold and freezing and snowing or raining outside... 

Great place to get lost... Gee, why am I going around in circle... I just want to walk South.... Don't follow me, I am lost!!

The stores can get a little boring if you are into shopping,,,.. I just want to have a break from the freezing cold

I end up just going back on the street... just walk South, a little cold but at least I find my way back to the hotel.

A local's delight, a tourist's nightmare.

One late rainy Montreal afternoon, my family and I decided to play a little game of "Lava Rain". We started from the Place des Arts and challenged ourselves to stay underground all the way 'til Eaton. We may have cheated and followed employees passing through after work. We got halfway-ish to Place Bonadventure, where we were met with a choice of stairs, a tunnel to a restricted door, and a split level of escalators. I was like F-this and took to the sidewalks. Even with a map, it was confusing figuring out how to get back underground once we made it to the next building. Signage was minimal and not visitor friendly... it makes me wonder why is this on everyone's must-do list? We passed by fellow frustrated tourists wondering where all the action was. For a stretch, it's just tunnel. In other areas, you'll see some budget boutiques, people picking up at the dry cleaners, grabbing a bite in the food courts and stalls. Not much in the kitsch-factor, but a huge utility for locals. 

If I lived and worked near here, I'd probably have more of an appreciation for the Underground. For now, I'll stick to Montreal above ground.

A mole-like world...who knew, right?  Miles and miles of subterranean pathways and shopping, fountains, and plantlife (???) so that you can avoid the extreme weather of Montreal (very hot or very cold).  A very interesting place for one who doesn't live in Montreal.

La ville souterraine de Montréal est à voir au moins une fois dans sa vie, parce que bon, faut reconnaître c'est quand même quelque chose! La plus grande du monde quand même, ce n'est pas rien! Et puis il faut reconnaître que c'est quand même bien pratique l'hiver quand on se les gèle trop ou encore au printemps quand la pluie n'arrête plus de nous tremper les os. Généralement je navigue entre la partie Eaton et les Ailes qui est bien pratique et aussi pas trop compliquée à trouver. Bon certes, ce n'est pas la partie la plus jolie. Mais pour ça je vous recommande les visites guidées de la ville souterraine qui permettent de la découvrir  autrement que comme un simple (et gigantesque) centre d'achat. Parce que sinon, honnêtement c'est vraiment ce que c'est : des centaines et des centaines de boutiques qui s'alignent les unes derrières les autres... Pratique pour les courses de Noël donc, mais à éviter si vous êtes claustrophobe ou si vous n'avez pas le sens de l'orientation!!!

La partie la plus animée du "RESO" est le centre d'achat .. il y a des connexions souterraines entre certains station de metro mais pas evidentes à trouver et souvent desertes.. des fois on retrouve des expositions mais c'est les couloirs vides sont plate par bouts .. donc il y a de la place à la amelioration surtout quand aux signalements pour bien se retrouver..

This place was NOT marked well so anyone looking for it for the first, second, tenth time would've missed it! It was full of places to eat but dark and gloomy inside. Bathrooms were hidden down a dark lonely hall. I was forced to use the mens room since for some reason the womens room was pad locked with a punch code. I would recommend this place if it was snowing/raining and even then with detailed directions and a map you'd only find this if a rouge bus caused you to dive into an unmarked doorway on accident.

I recommend visiting the Underground City to tourists especially if 1) It is cold when you are visiting 2) You tend to over-eat on vacation, like I do, and need some moderate exercise. 

The Underground is something like 18 square miles underground--air-conditioned in the warmer months and heated in the colder months.

Shops, shops and more shops. And the biggest, most diverse food court I have ever seen. 

Visiting Montreal during the dead of winter, we walked a good portion of it. It's pretty amazing that something like this was built. I can't imagine a city like Chicago having a system like this....our pedway is pretty sad compared to the Underground City and often under construction.

Free health care and the Underground City? Color me impressed!

More like underground mall. There's nothing city about. It's a bunch of shops and places to eat, and just happens to be bellow ground. If you want a good mall, sure check it out. But if you're looking for something more, this is a waste of your time.

Underground City of Montreal.  Some say it is the largest in the world.  We did not have enough time to explore this part of downtown Montreal.  It must be very convenient to go down to the Undeground City during the cold, harsh, winter months.

There are so many shops here.  If you are a shop-o-holic, you will enjoy discovering the shops here.  It is also a great place to exercise.  You can walk for miles here.  There are about 20 miles of walkways here.  These walkways connect complexes both above and below ground.  I read that there are more than 200 restaurants, 1700 shops, and 30 movie theaters in the Underground City.  That is a lot to see and do!!

It is free to enter the Underground City.  There are more than 120 exterior entrances to access the city, and it is connected to 10 Metro stations.

I look forward to spending more time here during our next trip to Montreal!  Still much to explore and discover here!

This place is worth it especially in the middle of winter. It sure beats walking outside in the cold and wind freezing your butt off. 
A good way to get exercise too. It just goes on and on, mile after mile, store after store, metro to metro.

A fun way to explore Montreal in the winter.

I don't see the city part of it-- it's an underground mall with many exits. I tried the poutine (poo-TEEN) for the first time in the food court, it's pretty good. French fries with cheese curds covered with brown gravy, delicious!

First off - I found this place bloody difficult to find!  Maybe I just didn't understand the concept but I thought that I'd be able to zip down after a visit to the museum and at the point on my map where it said there was an entrance, I'd be able to pop underground.  Well, I spent nearly 2 hours looking for the ruddy place!  I was finally headed back to the hotel when, by lucky chance, I found an entrance!  Yay!!!

I was more interested in the Underground City as, well, an underground city than I was interested in it as a mall.  The concept fascinates me and I wanted to see what it was like.  But unfortunately, once you're in it you forget that you're underground and just feel like you're in a mall.  The concept still amazes me, and I'm glad that I checked it out (and I think that you should too if you're in Montreal) but I'm not sure if it would be someplace I'd make a point in putting on my itinerary again.

I can definitely see this being a benefit in the winter especially if you could use it as part of your commute so you could walk without having to trudge through the slush and freeze your toesies off!

The Underground City, or Ville Souterraine, may not be a tourist destination per se', but it is quite a feat for Montreal, a very convenient system for Montrealers who work in or frequent Centre-Ville, and something that a tourist might just want to check out because it's so unique.

The Underground City is a system of tunnels that extends some 20 miles, albeit in a fairly compact area.  This means there are a lot of tentacles and spurs to add up to those 20 miles.  Not only that, it connects many modes of public transport, such as Metro stations, the central train station, suburban train stations, and bus stops.  This doesn't even account for the access provided to shops and eateries in the tunnels proper, not to mention shops and eateries in large shopping centers right above the tunnels.

While navigating them is considered confusing, the system looks like a big "U" that cuts a swath through Centre-Ville's key nodes.  The system would form this "U" from metro stations at McGill, then south to Bonaventure, then east to Square Victoria and Place d'Armes, and then finally north toward Place des Arts.  That said, overall, the system is much more cohesive than the underground tunnels in downtown Houston TX which are smaller and don't have as ample of a merchants' presence.

Montreal's tunnels were principally built to keep people in a climate controlled setting during the harsh Quebec winters.  Minneapolis MN has overhead walkways above street level meant to accomplish the same thing, as does Calgary AB.  On the other hand, Houston's tunnels are geared toward keeping people in a climate controlled setting during the long hot and humid summers.

I knew the Underground City existed, but I never clearly saw how one would enter the tunnels from street level.  I am sure there's a way.  However, I stumbled into one, and kept walking and walking, after having disembarked at Gare Centrale, Montreal's main train station.  The tunnels are wide such that people can walk abreast, the atmosphere is mostly nice, and, even in the tunnels themselves, there are shops where you can buy most necessities and eateries spanning many types of cuisine.  Needless to say, it shouldn't be too far to stumble into, or up to, a Tim Horton's.

I lived in a one bedroom unit on the first level at Hayden Park for a year and a half.  The location was great.  Close to Old Town and convenient shopping, pretty close to Tempe Marketplace, and within a reasonable distance for working in downtown Phoenix. The grounds were kept pretty nice. Occasionally there would be trash left outdoors by the younger crowd from a previous night, but almost every morning I saw one of the guys out picking up trash first thing. The office staff were always very friendly and timely with any questions or requests. I was impressed from the start that they remembered my name and which apartment I lived in from the beginning. The maintenance guys were also great and responded to me quickly. The layout of the apartment is what I liked most. It was great having the high counter in the kitchen and the sliding door looking outside. Having two closets in the bedroom was a real luxury. One of my favorite features of the apartment were all of the mirrors. I like bright and open-feeling spaces, and the mirrors added so much to a space that could have otherwise felt small. It was not a very big apartment, yet for being just a one-bedroom, it felt very spacious with all of the light. To give you a more complete picture, I will add that this wasn't by any means a "fancy" upscale apartment. The buildings are not new, and my unit had not been remodeled. Occasionally there were things that needed to be fixed, just like one experiences anywhere they live. I thought the cost of the apartments was reasonable for the location - I explored other complexes, and I really felt this one offered the most bang for my buck. Of course I would have liked it to cost less. who wouldn't? But for the area, it was fine. Overall, I had a very positive experience and highly recommend this apartment complex.

Hi im john i just renewed my lease for the 4th year im very happy to live here.It feels just like family here ...Dan and Dana the mgrs that run the complex are always very helpful....Dan the mgr went out of his way to make sure i got a new oven when my other one stopped working his fast attention is what i look for when i live in any apartment .I Totally recomend this  place,you wont be dissapointed!!!!

I have lived in a lot of apartment complexes but Hayden Park is definitely my favorite. The grounds are always spotless and I love that there are so many trees and the grass is always green. Danaan and Dan in the front office are always so nice, helpful and actually know every residents name. I have never lived in a place where all the neighbors are so nice and friendly. I lost count on how many people introduced themselves on the day I moved in and offered to help with anything I may need. I can not recommend this place enough.

I was just there on a one year lease in a two bedroom apartment recently, and I actually really liked it! Maintenance was excellent and timely on requests. Dan and Robin were excellent in the office, always taking care of the residents there. Dan was exceptionally friendly since day one of meeting him and getting a tour of the place. He   had incredible, genuine customer service! (Another rarity to find among apartment complex staff members). 

There was one incident I had where my apartment flooded a bit because my bathroom sink would not turn off. (It may have been my fault since I could not find the emergency shut off switch... lol) And regardless, they took care of everything and did not charge me at all for it! They were very reasonable about it and fixed it right away. 

My only complaint is that it may have been a bit overpriced, but it is Scottsdale after all. You pay like $150 more just to live in the city regardless of what apartment complex you are at. 

It was a very quiet apartment complex and I literally never had a single problem with my neighbors or any suspicious activity going on (which is what you expect from a lot of apartment complexes these days... lol). 

I would recommend this place to a friend any day!

I never write reviews but I lived here for almost 5 years ever since I left my home state in Wisconsin! My apartment had multiple leaks through it in the years and the parking lot floods BADLY every time it rains hard!!!!! The parking got so bad with water that it flooded INSIDE my car which the complex dismissed!! Then when I moved out I cleaned the apartment from top to bottom (except the tub that for whatever reason wouldn't get clean) and they charged me up the ass!!!!! The apartments are nice but they are VERY overpriced!!!!

I feel shamed to have taken so long to write a review about this place... I have been a resident of Hayden Park for 6 months and had to say that I am very happy with my overall experience.  

I've lived in Scottsdale for a few years and know there are many luxurious apartments around.  I've lived in one of them and yes it was a nice experience...BUT still attracted right out the college people who loved to party at night by the pool.  And customer services were not that great.  

Hayden park is an older property, yet you can request for an upgraded room for an additional cost if it's available.  Price is very reasonable for the location.  I gave 4star because of two things. The one thing that I wish I had in my unit is more storage space... I literally don't have a place to put away any extra boxes or even vacuum:(  And another thing would be that the door that connects from a hallway to the bathroom and one the connects from bedroom overlap.  So you have to make sure one of them is closed before you open if that makes sense.  

Other than the feedback I've given, I love living here.  I have a fireplace in my place, which makes the room cozy and home.  Most importantly, the staff here, Danaan and Luke as well as the maintenance team (Mark and one another) are AMAZING!!!!  They are so quick to take care of any issues you may have and SO caring.  Thank you Danaan and Luke for creating a great experience!!!!!

I took a tour of Hayden Park a while back, and I absolutely loved it!! The front office staff is super friendly, the grounds are beautiful and well-maintained, and they have a ton of different options which I appreciated. I've never been on an apartment tour before where random residents were so friendly and recommended it! Plus the location right by the greenbelt is awesome. 

I ended up choosing a complex closer to where I work, but I still recommend this place to everyone I know that's looking for a new place to live.

I have lived in a lot of apartments in my life and this is one of the nicer and affordable complexes I've lived in. There is a year round pool with a hot tub and a work out room. They let me use the fax whenever I need to for free.

The apartments are well built.  Washer and dryer in unit is nice (and being from Chicago, not something I've EVER experienced before).

The layout of the apartment is acceptable, although it is a bit odd having a bigger guest bathroom than a master. 

Since moving in, my experiences have been very consistent, honest, and pleasant. I'll most likely stay here until I buy a house in a few years.

I've lived at a few apartment complexes in my life, and Hayden Park puts all the rest to shame. Was my stay perfect? Nope, but what is in life? I don't value perfection, but I do value people who work hard to keep my satisfaction. 

Folks, Dan and Daanan are the best in the industry. These guys were always quick to help with any issue that ever came up, and they always did it with a smile and a friendly demeanor. Same for the service guys. They were quick, efficient, and always helpful.

Why else should you live here? Hayden Park is located right in the middle of the fun part of Scottsdale. You can walk to great restaurants and bars. Old Town is an extremely cheap fare away. The neighbors? Quiet as a retirement home. Loved it! 

Another awesome aspect is that HP has many options for apartments, including one-story residences. 

So if you're sick of incompetent staff - or if you live in BFE and are tired of traveling to do anything fun, you should definitely check out Hayden Park for your next apartment home.

Just finished a year lease here.  I know it's really popular to bag on every apartment complex on Yelp, but this place is solid.

Pros:

The office staff is excellent, which I can very rarely say - Dan and Robin do an awesome job, have maintenance out immediately after you request it, and will help out it dire circumstances.  
I once gave a friend coming into town the wrong key when he dropped by my job across town to pick it up, I called the office and asked them to let them in and they walked down and opened my apartment for my friends (after verifying my identity via email).

The community is quiet.

Prices are very reasonable.


The cons:

The apartments were built in the 80's, and look like they were built in the 80's, but have been maintained well.  You get what you pay for, neither super cheap nor luxury.

Just moved in about a month ago and I am impressed with the apartment. I live in the Casita floor plan and so far the apartment is clean, very spacious, and is pretty quiet. 

I am glad I chose the 1 bedroom Casita floor plan because nobody lives above me and the unit has high ceilings. Haven't had any bug issues or noise issues and maintenance office has been pretty responsive towards any problems, if any. 

One downside to this apartment is that all the windows are single paned. I am curious to see what my SRP electric bill will be for the month, but everything seems to be good so far. No problem with parking or neighbors. Can't say this is one of the best apartments in South Scottsdale but is pretty decent if you are looking for a good apartments in this area. I can tell the unit is very well maintained.

I have lived here almost 16 months and I have nothing but good things to say. The property is well-kept and the Property Managers are exceptionally kind & helpful. Great location - love Old Town! No plans to move out anytime soon!

I've had two different apartments in this complex the first time I lived here I loved it! And this second go around is horrible! I've had multiple problems with the leasing office Damon gives attitude left and right and accuse you of doing things that didn't happen. And management doesn't do anything about it. If this is how they treat their residence now I won't be renewing my lease or referring anyone to this complex. Poor job
Great community, Good Location.  I have 2 apartments in this community.  The pricing is great, and the staff is better.  Anytime I have had maintenance issues Dan/Dana gets its handled promptly.

I love living here! It is quiet and the staff is amazing. Anytime I've needed anything, they've taken care of it on the same day. There has been no turnover and it's been great working with the same people consistently since I've lived there. They always go above and beyond; in fact, when I needed a jump for my car, a staff member was right there and ready to help. I would recommend this complex to anyone!

I've lived at Hayden Park for over 3 years now, and I highly recommend it to any prospective residents. The apartments are about the same size as the ones at San Tropez right down the street, except you're going to pay a fair amount less at Hayden Park for essentially the same amenities. You really can't beat the location either. You have plenty of restaurants and stores within walking distance, and a couple bars too. It's right near the greenbelt, and close to Old Town and all attractions in that area, and it's a 15 minute drive the airport. I've never had any issues with my neighbors, and the staff is super helpful whenever you have any issues, or need maintenance done on your unit. Though I've never borrowed any up to this point, they also have free movie rentals at the office, which is pretty neat, and I don't think I've ever lived anyway that had that before. I also like being able to have my rent check come out of my account automatically every month. They have free pest control once a week if you ask for it, and you can replace your air filters free at any time. You do need renters insurance to live here, but even when you factor that in to the price, it's still more affordable than most places in the area. I don't have a pet, but plenty of folks do here, and everyone seems to clean up after their animal for the most part, and the landscaping around the complex is very nice. I don't see myself leaving here any time soon, unless I have to move out of state or something like that.

While living here in 2015 we counted down the days until we were out of here. We are constantly woken up at 2am due to people sneaking in and screaming at the pool. The pool hours are from 8am to 10 pm and in summer 7am-11pm. We have told the office staff on numerous occasions about this problem and they continuously do nothing about it. 
After one of the storms a tree branch broke and send gardeners out at 6:30 am on a Saturday to fix the tree. The tree branch was broken for about a week. We lived on the 2nd flood and one of the stairs broke while my husband was on it. We told them about it. The apartment manager wasn't in, so I reported this to the the manager's assistant at the time. Her response was uncaring and didn't have any urgency to get the stair fixed. When I told her she said I won't be able to get this fixed until after the weekend because maintenance isn't in on the weekends.

As far as the apartment itself. There is plenty of closet space throughout the apartment, including each room has a huge walk in closet.  The sink is shallow, so whenever I wash dishes by hand water gets everywhere and the dish washer is on the smaller side. The oven they provide you with has no ability to view what you are cooking. In the "upgraded" apartment there is a washer and dryer in unit. If you don't upgrade, you run the risk of not getting this luxury unless you get lucky. The property has plenty of space to walk your dogs but there are only 3 location to get poop bags.

One good thing about the apartment complex is its proximity to old town. This allows for quick travel to popular destinations and cuts down on traffic. During spring training the whole area gets overwhelmed with tourist and can cause long waits at your favorite restaurants.

I have never written a review for apartment complexes before, because apartment complexes are normally something of a headache that you just learned to deal with. Although I was very excited to move out of Arizona, I was actually really sad about leaving such a great apartment community and I have never had a positive experience like this with an apartment complex. 

The office staff is always very responsive and professional, and I really felt that they were truly understanding and customer-oriented. To me the true integrity of a business is not necessarily the lack of any problems ever, but how they handle the problems. 
I did have some maintenance issues such as my stove stopping working and ceiling leaks, but Hayden Park handled all requests with pleasant professionalism, and I was more than happy with the results. I also had some difficult requests for the office since my job required traveling frequently, and they were always eager to cater and make my living at Hayden Park easier. 

I recommended this place to my coworkers and friends back in Arizona, and I would recommend this place to anyone looking for a good, solid place to live where you can be trusted to be really taken care of by respectful, kind and professional staff.

Nice. Semi quiet. And the guys at the front office are always Nice and helpfull.  But be careful paying rent on line. If anything goes wrong, there bank carges you $50.00. Maintenance is not very good.

I lived here for two years and didn't have any issues.  I rarely needed to call maintenance, and when I did call the guy came out pretty fast.  Office staff is friendly and the neighbors are great.    The units aren't new so don't expect high end brand new amenities, but for what they have it's a bargain.  Would recommend.

i lived here 5 q/2 yrs ago for 6 mo,, i never had to call maintenance,  its very small apt but laid out well, very efficient, my only bad comments, was  1 leasing guy, i forget his name, great location, groceries nearby, downtown Scottsdale beautiful park nearby. but apt was squeaky clean when i moved in, id recommend this apt to anyone

I lived at Hayden Park for the last two years. I am moving out of state for work, but would recommend Hayden Park to others. Location is perfect, right next to the greenbelt, and with an easy drive into Old Town or to the 101. Management and maintenance techs are friendly, the complex is in good shape, and the price/value is competitive with anything in the area. I especially like our large walk-in closets and amount of storage space. The walls are also very thick; I've literally never heard my neighbors. This place is worth a look!

Called them to open a line blockage that was causing backup of the laundry and kitchen line. They did good work to fix the problem as requested, but what I was charged initially seemed a bit high but I paid it, given dirty dishes and laundry with 2 kids. 

To my surprise I get a call from the owner Chris a few days later to discuss the price I was charged and he offered to rectify it. Will definitely recommend this company for plumbing needs.

What a great company! They kept me informed every step of the way and did a wonderful job! Highly recommend!

I will always recommend Chris & Pink Plumbing....highly professional, really kind and kept me inform via text every step of the way.  Thank you Chris, I appreciate you!

Quick response, amazing service, quality work, and great price. Chris was a amazing and very knowledgeable. He was also super helpful from the moment I called. I will be referring him to my family, friends, and neighbors.
Fast, dependable and honest. He even took the extra time to discuss my repairs with my insurance company. I am to have found my new plumber!!  Give him a try, you will not be disappointed!
Super helpful, quickly fixed our plumbing issue. Will definitely refer them to my friends.

I called Chris about a second opinion on a sewer repair and he spent plenty if time on the phone with me making sure he answered all my questions. Then he came out and got the job taken care of for cheaper than the other guys wanted to charge me! Fast work and great clean up. I will definitely be using Pink Plumbing for all my plumbing needs! Thank you again!

Efficient, quick, and knowledgeable!

Thanks again Chris!
Great service! Told me they were going to come out between 2-4 and were here by 1:30 very knowledgeable and we're also quick

Friendly service. Explains everything plainly, patiently, and in plain English. Does competent, reliable, quality work and stands by it 100%. Competitive pricing. Properly licensed plumber.

Maintenance-free for 10 years, and worth every bit of the up-charge for great quality home water.

When you need plumbing...Think Pink!!

Called Chris on Sunday after discovering sewage coming up the bathtub.  Chris answered the phone.  I explained the issue and he came right over. I went in for my first ever lash appointment on August 1st (as I was going on vacation and didn't want to deal with mascara) and tried out their first time client promotion for $80. It was amazing ! I went in for my second appointment today for a classic refill and they look just as good as the first time. Mami has the touch of a feather and you can basically fall asleep while she works on your lashes. I have yet to be worked on by the other tech but I'm sure she would be just as good ! Overall, this place is top notch. Pricing is comparable to other studios but they do have first time client promos as well as friend referral promotions. DEFINITELY try this place out!

My favourite lash place!! Not that I've tried many but I know what I want and when I find it I'm a happy camper :) 

So my biggest reservation prior to visiting was the location. living downtown I have the downtown syndrome of not wanting to leave lol. I got past that because of their very professional video and awesome pictures on their website and decided to try it out. I've been twice now. If you are looking for a professional place that treats you really well with impeccable results, look no further! 

From the initial discounted visit with a full consult (they have a form u fill out to pinpoint the exact look you want), evaluation of your lashes and explanation of thicknesses, shapes, post care and expectations, I went into a separate room. the bed is super comfy and the blanket is a nice touch! What impressed me was her meticulous hygiene throughout the procedure. 

The result - nothing but fabulous. It's so hard to find a place that does natural lashes so well - I've seen so many bad jobs on my friends. The lashes are so flexible and soft and long lasting.. 1 month until I went back for another set! These ladies are all professionally trained and experienced - the tech I had was trained in Japan. They book up fast.. you really have to book in advance of 1-2weeks.. waayy worth it. Please note they take their time.. expect to be 2.5hrs for a natural full set!! (The first time I wasn't prepared for that so I got mighty hungry).

I've been going to Divine Lashes-- Naoko since she was at her old location and she is by far the most educated and experience eyelash technician I've ever been to. The environment is extremely clean, inviting, bright and relaxing.
At DL they educate their customers on the process before actually proceeding to do it. They even take into account your everyday facial/makeup routine so ensure that your lashes will fit into your personal lifestyle. They also have an amazing eyelash video that explains what they do and how they do it. At the end of the visit, they gave me an eyelash shampoo to help clean and maintain my lashes. Such care and thought! 

EYELASH EXTENSIONS: (main reason why I return)
Very clean-- all the technicians clean their hands prior to starting to process, they place this pad over your forehead so their hands are not resting directly on your skin.
The process itself is very tedious, they all wear magnifying goggles to ensure that they are placing each extension onto your natural eyelash. And after the process you can visibly see that each eyelash was carefully placed onto each individual lash. They don't use any harsh glues/chemicals that sting or irritate your eyes in the shower. The result is a beautiful enhanced natural eyelash look that doesn't look fake or too over the top.

Cons:
The only thing I would mention is that their prices are quite steep! I definitely prefer a fuller lash look, so I go about every 2-3 weeks to maintain and upkeep the look, however it's about $120/visit! While comparing to other eyelash boutiques (although not as good), DL is extremely expensive. 
I would also offer that her fellow associates are not as skilled/experienced as she is, however at DL they charge the same price whether it is Naoko, Mami, or Kaoru providing the service for you...
Naoko is definitely by far the most experienced (DL is her company), and she is the only one certified at DL for the Russian volume technique-- I just don't find it fair to be charging the clients the same price for their associates work, who obviously don't do as good of a job. 

BOTTOM LINE: I will be retuning to Divine Lashes

I recently moved to Atlanta and make monthly trips home to Toronto to see Naoko... she is amazing and always does a fantastic job on my lashes ... 

I have been going to her for about 2 or 3 years now and have never ever been disappointed!

I recently decided to try a new place to get my eyelashes done, prior to this I've been to Keiko's on Dundas and another private/home eyelash stylist. The original reason for leaving Keiko was because she was getting more busy and the job got a tad sloppier, although for the price she was definitely more affordable. 

I tried the 3D volume lashes here at Divine lashes and had them for 3 weeks before I had a refill. They stayed on great and lash separation was amazing, (sometimes stylists clump two lashes together). If you take care of them properly(wash them, comb, blow dry cool) they'll last you a lot longer. I opt to go for the natural flair with C curl. My stylist was great, we have a consultation first and she explained to me my maximum length (30% more than my original lashes) would provide me with the longest wear. She was very carefully in understand what look I wanted and told me we could keep changing it as we go on, which I did upon my refill. I decided to try the D curl this time, which was more curly and made my eyes pop more. 

The facility is small, but clean, and professional. The little things I notice them do that drives them over the top for me is that they carefully clean your lashes before application, provide you with eyelash soap, and keep track of your eyelash status. I typically have more lashes on my right eye and she would try to match it up with my left so that both sides looked even.I highly recommend coming here if your budget allows for it.

I've been to several lash places... Richmond Beauty Bar, Be Fabulous Spa, La Belle Femme...and this is hands down the BEST lash service I've ever received!

There are several reasons why I would give this place 5 stars (or more if I could).  Let me this them below:
1) Cleanliness:  The space was clean and bright!  You're asked to take off your shoes when you enter, and they provide you with slippers and offer you a drink if needed.  The ladies were masks and have good hygienic practices.
2) Thoroughness:  This is the first (and only) lash place that asked me about my skin care routine and my makeup routine.  This helps them provide you with recommendations to make your lashes last as long as possible.  For example, using an oil free cleanser, and a lash shampoo (that they provide free of charge), extends the life of your lashes. 
3) Instructional video:  I've never been to a place where they have an instructional video on lash extensions!  They provided examples of some work they did to save lashes (like mine!) and how to clean your lashes.  
4) You get exactly what you want: Mami (who did a fabulous job BTW), had a binder with several 'looks' that you could go for.  eg (.---'---,) depicting the different length of lashes (eg. 6 mm, 7mm, 10mm).  I went with the natural flare.  Most other places just ask you what you want, but doesn't delve specifically into what they'll do in terms of length, and what it'll do to your eyes.
5) Precision: 1 lash to 1 lash.  They wore magnifying glasses so they can do this! They take their time to make sure this is done correctly so you don't damage your lashes.  

Out of all the places I've been to, my husband says this looks the best on me (he likes it natural).  They feel great, just like my natural lashes.  Although I wanted to find a cheap lash place, I realize that sometimes you get what you pay for. It's a bit on the pricey side, but it's a worthy investment for fantastic looking lashes.

AMAZING! first time getting lash extensions....and Mami was awesome. She put me at ease and showed me how to care for the lashes. The extentions went on with a light touch...I could barely feel it, and these look beautiful....I can't stop marveling at them! Thanks Mami....I'll be back!

*Message me if you want to take advantage of the referral program!*

Best eyelash extension experience I have ever had:).

These people really know what they are doing. I have been to a couple other salons before but they all caused irritation on my eye. Divine is different- they provide a cleansing kit for your lashes and a detail tutorial video to teach you how to clean and maintain the lashes.

I went in for the first time as a new client ($80 package). The whole process took 2 hours and my technician really takes the time to understand what I need and what suits me. I will definitely come back again. They also have a great referral program! Make use of it ;)

I've been here twice now even though it is not in my neighbourhood, but it is worth it! There is free parking which is great. I was afraid the lashes would be too high maintenance but it's actually quite easy with the soap and comb they give you. I had mine for three weeks before getting a refill and I was able to choose more of a curl this second time. At three weeks I actually had quite a few lashes left - more than I expected. It's a very relaxing experience and they take great care in their art. I am more confident not wearing face makeup with these lashes.

This was my first eyelash extension experience; some friends told me that if I were to cry at my wedding, than this is better to have over the glued strip lashes and lots of mascara. I was also initially afraid to get these done because I've heard some horror stories from friends who said all their real lashes were gone after the extensions came off!

After watching the Divine Lashes video and hearing positive testimonials about Divine - I decided to give it a shot. It seemed like they had a better technique on how they're glued and better quality extensions. Most importantly, it seemed like they really do care about their clients.

So I had the "natural" set done on Sept 20, 2014 - the girls at Divine wanted to ensure I didn't have any allergic reactions before the wedding (which was Oct 5) so this was like a trail set before they added the volume/drama set put on the day before the wedding.

I LOVE them! Such a huge difference in photos and they look so natural! Best of all, I can see my real lashes are still there, growing between the fake ones.
Attached is a photo taken yesterday before bed - I took good care of them (as instructed on the video), except the fact that I sleep on the sides of my face sometimes which probably rubs them more than a regular back-sleeper. There are some gaps, but it can be brushed out to look full again. Considering I got the first set done over a month ago, this is not bad!

Something to note also: before they added the drama set, they warned me that if I noticed lashes coming off more than 5 pieces/day, to come back and get them removed because some people's lashes can't handle the weight of the fake lashes (I think it was a 6:1 ratio between fake and real lashes). Obviously, I took the risk because I only get married once, but I appreciate the fact that they warned me and had my best interests at heart since I could've just taken my business elsewhere so someone who makes false "guarantees."

Needless to say, I will go to them again if I want to get them done again and I have referred many friends to Divine. These girls wouldn't put a crazy number of extensions on you if your real lashes aren't healthy enough/can't handle it - I think this is great company moral because this is better for the clients' lashes long-term.
Thanks Divine Lashes for making me look beautiful on my wedding day - and the weeks before and after the wedding! ^__^

I have been getting my lashes done for 5 years at various establishments but this is by far the best job! I will look no further!
