The next day, now nearly 72 hours after drop off I was told there a was a pin that was not working and given a quote that seemed pretty high (later confirmed by calling around). I asked to pick up my equipment and was told I could. I drove to the their store only to learn my hard drive was not there but was off site somewhere. Wasted trip number one.

Alex offered to bring it directly to me and set up a time to do so, which was an incredibly nice thing to do. However, he was well over an hour late and by the time he did show up I was on my way out (I was now late for where I needed to be). However he forgot my cables to make the hard drive work. He promised to be back in 15 minutes with the cables and would leave them in my screen door. He never came back.

This began a cycle of three weeks of calling and asking when I could pick up my cables, being told Alex would drop them off at the store for pick up in an hour, by 5 PM, by 1 PM, etc. I must have been told over half a dozen times when Alex would drop off the cables but he didn't. I dropped by the store for at least 2-3 more wasted trips.

Finally I was told Alex had dropped them off at the store. I called the next day to confirm they were there and then drove down after their lunch break. BUT the cables were not there. According to the employee, Alex had grabbed the wrong bag and it had my cable is there. Yet another wasted trip. This time I was livid because I had specifically called to confirm.

After nearly a month I was able to get my cables back but it was a lot more frustrating than such a simple exchange should ever have been and I was flat out lied to multiple times about the timing of everything which resulted in a lot of wasted trips and time.

Price alone gave me second thoughts about this place. Some of the crappiest customer service I've ever gotten deserves the lowest rating possible.

Updated review. I have been dealing with this company since longer than 2013, I bought few computers from them for my office and they have backed up their service 100%. I recently had a problem with an HP computer I bought from them, warranty was for 1 year but with the manufacture, they asked me to allow them to handle the service to contact HP to speed things up, they were able to get my laptop repaired through HP within 1 business days for the cost of NOTHING. They wanted to help me out since I've been a long time customer, this is what I truly call a great customer service and great to their customers, Local family owned shops are the best!

I love Saigon Sandwich, I work a couple blocks away so try to get down there about once a week.  The sandwiches are great, the meats are very good, I recommend the combo, and the other toppings are all fresh and flavorful.  I recommend getting it with everything, as long as you can handle a little spice, there are jalapenos, but it isn't super spicy.  Service is super fast, and the prices are very good.  One sandwich is $4.75, which should be plenty for most people, similar to a 6 inch sub from subway, but a bit bigger.  If you are really hungry, get two for $9.50, it is a lot of really good food, and is bigger than a foot long at subway.  I mention Subway because there is one just down the street, and why anyone would pick subway over Saigon Sandwich is beyond me.  So check out Saigon Sandwich the next time you want something fresh, tasty, and not too filling.

My only complaint is their limited summer hours, but that is hardly a complaint.

Let's be real here, the UW Campus is basically a wasteland when it comes to good ethnic food.  I know people rave about Mediterranean Cafe and Banzo, but when those places are your bastion for "good ethnic food" I can't help but shed tears of anguish.  

Fortunately, there is a food truck called Saigon Sandwiches that is my go-to when I really want banh mi.  If you don't know what banh mi are, they are Vietnamese sandwiches with a heavy French influence.  The nice thing about the food cart is that they have pens and little pieces of paper that help you customize what type of meat you want (or tofu) and the toppings/condiments.  It is kind of like Subway, except Saigon obviously has much better tasting food and none of that goofy feeling like you're on a conveyor belt and need to rush through everything.  

It is true that you can probably get banh mi sandwiches in the big cities for 4.50 or so, but 4.75 for one of these is still a good deal especially when you consider that a similar-sized sub at Jimmy Johns or Potbelly costs about the same.  And of course, these Vietnamese sandwiches are much better.  As far as the options go, I always get the special combo.  The meat is always tender, the pate has good flavor, and their bread is nice and soft.  Last week, I cut up the roof of my mouth eating chips, but couldn't resist getting one of these sandwiches.  As terrified as I was of the expected pain, the bread was crunchy but also soft enough so that I wasn't screaming uncle thanks to the cuts on my mouth. 

I'm usually here once or twice a week.  I tend to avoid going around noon because that's when everyone and their mother is lined up for their lunch breaks.  I would definitely recommend stopping by if you are near Union South.
The sandwiches are made fast, inexpensive (under $5!!) and very tasty.  I highly recommend this place if you can make it down there.

This is literally the best food cart in Madison. No other cart comes close. (Caracas empanadas is the second best cart in Madison). Excellent ingredients and great options for sandwiches. Efficient service. Good value. I wish I could eat here every day. I SHOULD be eating here every day.

Saigon sandwiches is amazing! I went right as they opened so it wasn't too busy and I got my food quite quickly.  The sandwich overall was great.  Like others have said, it is very fresh, and very flavorful.  Every bite I took out of the sandwich was bursting with flavor, either from the meats or the radishes.  The best part is that the overall bread to filling ratio was very satisfying.  I never felt like there was too much bread or too much filling.  I did take away one star because I expected the baguette to be crisper.  Don't get me wrong, the bread was great, but seemed too soft to be a real baguette.
This is the best-value food truck in Madison. A fat, great sandwich for $4.75. I recommend the Vietnamese meatball.
Super cheap food that is quick and delicious. I'm glad they have vegan options.  Make sure no fish sauce is added.

I've had this same sandwich (my fav- special combo with everything) 3 lunches in a row and didn't feel tired of it at all.. it is that good. Sometimes, I wonder how a sandwich that simple can taste so good! The combo special has roast pork and steamed pork roll. I also recommend including pate in the sandwich. Very friendly customer service too, and the speed they make these sandwiches is crazy fast.

I love this food truck for many reasons. First, it's cheap as in it's around $5 for a sandwich that's almost a foot long. There are many meat options and it's topped with fresh herbs on a crisp bun. Secondly, it's strategically placed in the middle of the bustling campus for hungry college kids like me when I attended there. Although I remember many times looking for it and being disappointed that it wasn't there. This is one of the treasures that I miss about being on the UW campus.

I work around the block and find the sandwich perfect for lunch. It's cheap ($4.95), fast, and a short walk (South Union cafeteria takes longer usually). You can pick so many kind of vegetables / topping (no extra charge) to go with it. I have tried a couple of them, My favorite is banhmi (grilled pork and chicken) sandwich.  The only thing that I complain about is probably the baguette is not as crispy as I hope it would be. Coming from New York, I have pretty high standards for my vietnamese sandwich crust! Otherwise I am happy and have been back so often since I have my first bite.

My favorite to-go lunch spot on campus. If you go before noon, you can avoid a line. All sandwiches are $4.75, and they have veggie options. Sometimes the meatball filling can be too fatty/greasy, but the special meat combo has never failed me. I always get all the toppings, but you can customize your own when you fill out the order form at the counter. The ordering system is a little chaotic; there's only ever one person working there who takes orders and makes the food, so sometimes you have to wait a while to put in your order. Sandwiches are about the size of a 6 in Subway sandwich.
It's very good. I always have meatball sandwich and love it. Very convenient on campus and good price for lunch.

We were driving by and saw the food truck at the corner.  I tried the banh mi sandwich with shredded pork and chicken. The bread tasted fresh and crispy. The pork is the dry shredded pork found in other Vietnamese dishes.  I'm not a fan of the pork.  Next time I'll try the banh mi dac biet.

I had this sandwich the other day and it was just average really. The ingredients seemed fresh and the speed of service was fast. Good price.
But the bread was awful - just a Midwestern, white bread, sub-style soft roll. A bahn mi sandwich is supposed to be on a baguette. With flavor. With a bit of crunch.
I am a bit confused as the pics here on yelp show sandwiches on baguette - so maybe the day I went - they missed their bread delivery and went to Copps for horrible, boring rolls?????
Also, the carrots and daikon (radish) were shredded, and in the pics the veges are sliced thinly.

Maybe they have a new cook? Maybe I will give them another chance.

Menu says all sandwiches are 4.75 but I was charged 4.86, and it came out to 5.16. Wish he would change that because the sandwiches are good. The raw jalapeño is extremely overpowering, if I could change something I would suggest that he substitutes a different kind of spice, like sriracha. Got the pork chops. 

Edit: ate here again a year later, paid with cash, was charged 4.75. So that's good. Didn't get jalapeño this time. Got BBQ pork. Dank

My favorite food cart in Madison. The sandwiches are great and the price isn't too expensive. Every single time I see the cart behind the chemistry building I always stop for a minute to see if I have enough cash to buy one.

When you are craving banh mi sandwiches this is the cart to go too Madisonian.  Fresh ingredients...love the pate, I wanted 3 yesterday could only get 1:-( By 1:30pm, he was sold out!  My only complaint, fyi  the lemonade was water down.  I'll be back for more sandwiches.  See you soon.

This place is a gem. Their sandwiches are made using French baguettes, with delicious pickled veggies and your choice of meat (and much more). The meat options are cooked asian style and are very savory. The best part is that a sandwich only costs 4.75! You can't find that kind of deal easily now. Just come up to the cart, fill out an order form and hand it to the guy inside. It's conveniently located at the corner of Charter and Johnson, across the street from the bus stop.

I LOVE coming here for lunch. In fact, I crave these sandwiches pretty often, like about as often as I crave sushi (I'd eat it every day if I could afford it - sushi I mean. These sammiches are quite affordable!). I work down the street too, so it's really quick and convenient. You show up, write down what you want on paper, hand it to the guys in the cart, and then wait for your sandwich to show up (with your paper on top - it helps if you make your name really big if you're like me and can't see far away..).

Everything on the sandwich is fresh and flavorful (I usually get ALL the toppings). I have a very high spice tolerance, so I never find the jalapeños too spicy. There are usually 5-6 slices on each sandwich. The bread is perfect for Banh Mi. Nice crisp crust that's soft on the inside and gets nice and soaked with the picked deliciousness and flavor from the innards :). I also like that there's a tofu option - it's flavorful too!

The only reason I'd give one less star is that they're not out there when the undergrads aren't around. Too bad there must not be enough business from everyone else. So Spring/Winter break I have to go without my Saigon Sandwich! #TheStruggleIsReal !!
This food truck has the best banh mi Madison has to offer. They are clean, fast, and have fresh ingredients. And the price is unbeatable.

I am surprised that no one has reviewed this cart yet, so I am taking the lead. 

Saigon sandwich offers very delicious and inexpensive ($4.75) Banh Mi, which is the baguette sandwich that introduced during French colonial period. While colonialism is a ugly history, the culinary cultural exchange certainly created some most interesting food in the world. Banh Mi belongs to this category. 

There are five choices of meat--veggie tofu, bbq pork, chicken, vietnamese meatball, and combo. You can also choose what fillings to be put onto your sandwich. The subway idea on a Vietnamese sandwich. The jalapenos are super spicy, be careful. I have tried bbq pork and chicken sandwich. Both taste good. 

The cart is operated by a team from Pho Nam restaurant. I am happy to see it in the corner of Charter and Johnson. A great place to grad quick lunch if you're in the south side of UW campus.

Like many Americans, I'm a big fan of a well-constructed sandwich. There are some key things to a great sandwich - flavor harmony, texture variety, uniform layering, and good ingredients. Let's start with flavor harmony. Depending on the ingredients that you decide to add to your sandwich (I usually get all of them), the sandwiches have a good mixture of sweet, spicy, savory, and acidity. This is a very good thing as it makes each bite interesting, complex, and rich in flavor. Another good thing - the ingredients have a variety of textures with a combination of raw, crispy, and soft. Third, the sandwich makers at Saigon do a pretty good job of layering the ingredients. In most bites of the sandwich, I am able to find all ingredients present. The final point is where Saigon falls slightly short of expectations. While the bread and supplementary ingredients are all fresh, the meat seems to be of a lower quality. However, this does not deter too much from the sandwich. For the price and speed, you get a lot more than the $5 that you paid. Overall, this is a great spot on campus for a quick and flavor-packed meal.

Since I moved to Madison this place has always intrigued my boyfriend and I. We moved here roughly three years ago from San Jose California. There is a huge Vietnamese community, so I love to eat Vietnamese food. This place makes a mean sandwich, had to go back for seconds. Very fresh ingredients and they where quick with the point of service. Definitely will be back. The bf loved the meatball sandwich. I could eat a million of the BBQ pork. Check it out for a cheap lunch

Hmm I ve never been so confused about writing a review before. This place is scabby, the coffee I was served was cold filter coffee. Though I think this is the whole idea about forest cafe, an Edinburgh CBGB's more poetic rather then punk rock. There is a tension in the air here, a political and spiritual tension. I feel a lot of sadness, frustration and anger at the forest and I can't say I felt very comfortable here but can see how people feeling the same seek out each other to fight internal struggles and injustice in the society. 

They say that a messy room is a messy mind, maybe some passion to make good drinks and food would do good here, after all it is in human nature to seek out good food if we can. Though this is just my opinion.

Only after seeing Peter S's review pop-up on my feed was I reminded of the Forest Café, and also of how little I genuinely liked it.

I love the idea of it. And I tried to like the old one (near Bristo Square). But at that one I ordered a falafel salad. The falafel was so dry I had to order coke to go with it (I never drink coke), but then as one of the servers walked by she knudged by coke with her hip and it spilled into my falafel salad. She just looked behind her, muttered "oh oops" and didn't offer anything, even help to clean it up, let alone more dry falafel.

So with that memory of the old Forest Cafe as the only comparison point I had for the new one, I went along here when it first opened to meet a friend. I admit, I like the space. It's on a corner, all glass, near the Meadows but overlooking Tollcross. They've done a nice job of decorating the ground outside with chalk patterns.

It's probably worth knowing that I went through a two year 'hippy' phase in my youth / pre-teens. I listened exclusively to music pre-1980, wore vintage levis flares, watched the 70s version of Jesus Christ Superstar on a monthly basis, wore tie dye, started a school World Wildlife Fund group, started donating money to save the gorillas. (I didn't say I did the hippy phase very well. It's a sliding scale. I still washed, shaved, and worked.)

Anyway. I have a nostaligic love of all things eco-hippy. I still engage in more spiritual matters -I practice yoga, I try to meditate, I still do my bit to help endangered animals, I use ecover products where possible. But I've grown out of my dreadlock-crush and the 'image' of it all. Because really it is an image.

I'm not trying to bash on anyone. All I'm saying is, I should in theory love the Forest Café. The idea of it appealed to my inner eco-warrior. 

But when I found it cold, the tables dirty, and as Peter S also said, serving cold coffee with very non-engaging or friendly staff, you realise that whilst some things are nice in theory, when it comes to running a business and serving customers, there's certain standards that you just shouldn't let slip. Like smiling. Or serving coffee in clean cups.

I *might* give it another go. Their advertised mexican coffee sounds good. And it's got more romance than the previous venue. But I just can't trust it to be reliably good...

Been here many times to get some lunch. Falafel meal is nice, vegan chilli is great, a variety of food. Really love the place although sometimes the wait can be a tad long. Really hope it'll last a long time, and maybe even expand. The decor and furniture are colourful and cosy, plus sometimes there's free bread. Looking forward to the many times I'll be back :)

'If you turned lesbian, I'd turn lesbian too..' The tone was set by the band's opening line at the Forest Cafe. It's all a little strange. And quirky. And hipster. I am partial to all these things. On Valentine's day they have 'My heart goes boom, boom, ribbit, ribbit - love for frogs.' It said so on a poster. I have no idea what this entails but it sure adds to the mystery that the Forest Cafe exudes. I think I'd quite like to sit here with a tea when I'm in Edinburgh. It's all very creative and artsy. But 3 stars because the service was exceptionally slow and I think the live music (if as silly as it was when i was there!) may have you wishing for a quieter spot to drink and chat.

First time visiting in this location and found it to be as cheap and cheerful as expected. People seemed oddly fascinated by a Dansette record player but otherwise all pretty normal. When coffee's this tasty you don't need it tarted up.

Great community here- they host all kinds of activities from documentary film releases, to inky fingers writing groups, to whatever people want to share with others.  Just sitting there for any fingers to fondle are three typewriters, glinting with invitation to let the mechanical sound remind the writer how much machination goes into their own work.  

I had a drip coffee, which was eh, but I hear the food is nice. They happened to be making a soup and cutting onions, which I am allergic to, so my eyes were burning and I could not keep them open.  I don't usually like to cry in public, but this was unavoidable, as my eyes were running trying to get the noxious fumes out.  

It is also run by volunteers, so thank to the lovely folks who make this possible!

It's clear that the earnest-feeling Forest Cafe is trying to do something different and meaningful, and for that I want to support them. And yet I don't particularly want to return. 

This is one of those funky hip cafes with "freeshop" shelves of books, board games, boxes of knitting supplies, that sort of thing; lots of mismatched wooden chairs and stools, handpainted creaky tables, slightly torn throw pillows. And I see the appeal of Forest Cafe in principle. The problem? It's run by well-intentioned volunteers who don't actually seem to know how to run a cafe. The food just isn't very good and the service is terribly slow. I had a reasonably priced (I think around £5.50) bean burrito, which was enormous and came heaped with a couple of side salads. It was pretty bland. 

Other issues? Besides the very slow service, you need to bus your own dishes, which always annoys me. There's not enough light to read comfortably, which certainly is a design flaw considering their seeming target demographic of environmentally-conscious students, and the entire place is just a bit grimy. The coffee isn't great. Nothing too objectionable, but I won't be returning.

Simple and cosy
It's a simple small cafe, dedicated to a environmental cause.
The coffee is regular, the carrot cake was vegan and very good. 
It has a great atmosphere.

I have been here a couple of times and each time have felt right at home! I loved the whole vibe of the place, reminiscent of places I used to go to in California (bay area.) 

I also love supporting a non profit vegan/vegetarian cafe. Its artsy, experimental and the food is really tasty! We hung out in it for a good while at lunch today, my toddler completely at home dancing around to depeche mode. The funky ambiance, toys, games, free boxes full of clothes, random objects. I loved that the guy next to us was creating this glittery poster and glueing together a wee ceramic duck. 

The space is just so open and embracing to whatever you may need. You have the guy doing the art next to the dude on his laptop doing his thing and us doing our thing all at the same time in complete harmony. I really enjoy these types of places and feel sad that there arent more of them.

We headed here on Sunday as, since it's opening, we'd wanted to check out the new incarnation.

I was a fan of the old Forest Cafe for free gigs and somewhere to bring cans from Tesco (I'm mad classy, I may have mentioned this before...) My first year here, I popped in and out but never really became a 'local'.

I have no intention of becoming a 'local' to this incarnation... first off because I think I've outgrown it but also....
It's cold! Oh so cold! Granted, I was near the door, but brrrr! Concrete, linoleum (I think) and giant windows do not suit Edinburgh. Speaking of linoleum, the floors were dirty which I could deal with if it didn't look like weeks worth of dust. The staff were friendly but, and I'm going to sound awful here, the service was bad. we ordered a tea and a coffee and were told it would be brought over to us. The drinks arrived, no milk or sugar in sight so we go back up, with our drinks, to get the essentials. There weren't too many in when we went so I couldn't really get a feel for what it would be like on a Friday night.

If this was anywhere but the Forest Cafe it would be one star. No question....but....I like the idea. I like the 65p to come drink your own cider in a place that isn't your living room. I like the local drama workshops. I like the free space for artistic expression. I think it's necessary to have a place like this. Also, I think they've learned a few lessons from the last place and the running of things has slightly improved. Based on those points I think Forest Cafe deserves a bit of leeway...

I want this place to work! I really do, but I think the volunteers maybe need to step up their game a bit and have more pride in what their doing....just the opinion of a rambling mad-woman though....

So I had a good hour to kill before a play (OK, a musical) in the nearby King theatre, and I was tired of walking all day. I literally couldn't find any café which is still open on a Saturday at 18 (never happened to me before, even in East European capitals). Anywho, was a bit desperate and not at all picky, which should be the new name of this café if you ask me. You should go and order but they will bring your food to you (after a while, and without cutlery). I had a soy hot chocolate and a vegan date pie. Paid £3.8 which is OK I guess although I had better chocolates and pies before. The service was OK- waitress wasn't super nice, wifi was down. As I said, low expectations and a bit of desoair is key here. Looks and feels incredible hippie, hipster and other words used to descibe semi dirty low quality food and drinks in a one-small-lamp-for-an-enrite-place Institute. Noticed people leaving food, toys, books etc. here as donations, that's nice, though I've seen about 20 homeless people in Edinburgh today, so why not just give it to them rather than to hipsters/students/hippies?

I had a Mexican Chai coffee when I visited the new Tollcross-located Forest Cafe for the first time. And it did work. It was really tasty actually, and just the milky-sugary hit I was looking for at the time.

What I do like about Forest Cafe is that you never know quite what to expect when you arrive - the people hanging out here are and always have been a distinct bunch, and it does always feel chilled - and actually, every time I've been here I've got quite a bit of quality writing done, which must mean its artistic leanings have prodded my procrastinating typing fingers into action somehow. It's good to be in an environment where you feel like (almost) anything goes in terms of what kind of a person you are and where your interests lie.

I think it might just need a bit of time to grow into itself (much like a blossoming forest......meh......) and to develop more of a buzzing atmos. Sometimes it just takes a bit of time to find a banter balance that works, and I'm sure (and I hope) that'll happen, because I do like it here. I will return for more sweet Mexican goodness soon.

Nice idea, poor execution. I like the idea of a volunteer run, enviro focused place, however there are some basic cafe requirements people tend to look for:

-Good coffee
-Reliable wifi
-Space to work/lounge.

Forest is trying on points 2&3 but does not hit the mark on any.

This ALDI has been our go to for some time now. Walmart has gotten out of hand with some things. Not all of ALDI products are good but that's kinda half the fun trying them out. We get probably 80% of our groceries here and get the other 20% at Publix, Harris Teeter and Walmart. Some items you just gottah have what you want (ex. Heinz Ketchup). I can't and won't do ALDI brand ketchup.

Though sometimes not the healthiest or the best types of food it is definitely a cheaper and different place to try. I wish there was a longer fruits and veggie section instead of the overall one lane of snacks and junk food. But again this is a lower end grocery place. The brands are the generic never before heard of brands but some are good to try and some are... Cheap knockoffs. Tried it once and for me it's like a cheat day grocery store. Love the dollar lunchables haha!

Good cheap snacks and fruit! Can't beat that. Not having bags and having to use a quarter to get a basket is a bit annoying especially with my hands full with two busy toddlers.  Good prices though so worth a little hassle

ALDI is a great alternative to the higher end grocery stores and even the Big Box grocery chains.

You can cut your entire grocery bill basically in half by shopping at ALDI compared to the aforementioned other stores.  They do carry a decent selection of name brand items, but focus mainly on other "not-so-well-known" brands to help keep your bill low!  They do carry a selection of non-grocery household items as well.

ALDI is becoming increasingly popular in the Charlotte area, with new stores popping up constantly across the region.  Including this store which has been open for just under a year.

With this store being open less than a year, it is still very fresh and clean inside and very well maintained.  They usually only have one register open at time (another cost saving initiative) but will not hesitate to open a second when a long line develops.  If you are unfamiliar with ALDI, you have to insert a quarter into the shopping cart lock box to release a new cart.  That is to ensure you return the cart to the appropriate carousel.  That again is another cost-saving measure so they don't have to hire someone to chase after the carts.

They also carry a selection of alcohol.  Including a small inventory of beer choices and a fairly larger selection of wine.  Of which is unavailable for purchase at this particular location on the holy bible belt Sunday.

It's cheap, cheap.  Give it a try!

Update: this week's theme is car items. I needed a battery booster box because one of the cars died. Bought the box here for $40 and it is better than some I have seen at $100. It even has a USB port to charge your phone or computer!

Inexpensive food shopping of brands that you've probably never heard of. If you're looking to save money and not shop at the nearby Wally World, then you'll likely be here at Aldi where they trim costs by getting you to put in a 25 cent deposit for a shopping cart and you'll be bagging your own groceries in your own bags. There's nothing wrong with that!

Groceries, dairy, some meats, some deli, lots of frozen. You'll not find more than one or two choices of brands in each item, but I've been fine with the quality overall.

Speedy shop, slow check out. They're not big on staffing of the registers at Aldi. That's part of how they keep costs down.

Remember to bring a quarter and remember to bring your own shopping bags!

This Ibis hotel is really close to the old town, that was one of the main reason we chose it. Although there is another one even much more closer to the St. Giles cathedral. It was full booked when my hubby and I were doing the booking online. We didn't mind to just walk about 5 minutes more.

I remember when we just got to the hotel and doing the check-in process like usual. One thing really gave me a really good first impression was the staff. They all seem really friendly, and the one who assisted us was particular nice. She was super friendly and also happy to recommended places to visit in city. We did have our own plan, but great to listen to what the folks say about the city.

The room we were staying was also quite nice, a bit the standard style of Ibis. Not much different, just a bit smaller. I was more surprised that since like they had the same paintings across national, hanging on the wall of the bed side. Interesting.

I like the breakfast here as well, quite international choices, but all tasted good. The place is quite big, cosy place to have a meal. We also got our welcome drinks here. 

There is a bus station not far away from the hotel. It make this really easy to get around. Overall, I like this place, we both had a good staying here.

Wir wurden sehr herzlich in Empfang genommen. Nach dem ausführlichen Check-In bezigen wir unser Zimmer und richteten uns entsprechend ein. Als wir am späteren Abend ins Zimmer zurück kehrten, fielen mir erst dann zwei Unannehmlichkeiten auf. Diese reklamierte ich am nächsten Morgen an der Rezeption. Die Behebung der Mängel wurde äußerst kompetent vorgenommen. Das Frühstücksbüffet war "very Scottish", was mir wirklich gut gefiel und schmeckte. Das Personal war stets freundlich, zuvorkommend und hilfsbereit. Wir kommen auf jeden Fall wieder!

We arrived on Monday afternoon, even though no room was ready for us. The personal on the front desk called the house keeping but nobody answered their calls. 

I had ordered separate beds, instead we got a single bed. I will figure this lack of communication out with my booking portal. The room was clearly for on person, indicated by the number of towels and hangers. We had to ask for a separate single blanket. 

Tuesday we returned from out sightseeings so early that our room was not cleaned, I catched up with a guy from the housekeeping to get new towels at least. 

Wednesday I noticed that the single blanket was full of staines. 

Thursday, again we came back too early for the housekeeping to clean up the room. Even though 3 house maides where around on our floor and we left again, nobody cleaned up our room. We asked for a new towel, our wish was noted at the front desk. Nothing happend, so we helped ourselves by getting a towel from the ironing room. 

As this hotel is really great for sightseeing and all museum around open between 9.30 and 10 cleaning could start earlier. Perhaps, like in other hotels, a sign "please clean up my room"  would help to find out, which guests are already off to start the process. 

One star for the great location, everything you want to see as a tourist can be reached by foot. 

Another star for the great breakfast, continental and classic British breakfast, always fresh.

The rooms are great. Service is wonderful. The downside is that it is hard to get to your rooms. Overall this hotel is pretty good. If you have a family of 4 or more book 2 rooms because each room holds up to 2-3 people.

Hotel Ibis is modern with efficiently designed rooms, something out of an Ikea catalog. Tricky floors and navigating through the hotel, but the customer service was excellent, providing a quick tour of the hotel. Clean, modern, and no carpet in the rooms (always a bonus for allergy sufferers). Excellent location near all the good sights and pubs.
Absolutly correct. Good sleep, maybe a little bit too loud. But you have too know it so close to Royal Street. Fantastic breakfast.

If you came to go out at night and sleep in, this hotel IS NOT for you. 

I am currently staying on the fifth floor and the staff has decided to roll around a dolly and make loud operations prep noises beginning at 6:15 AM! 

He location is great, but the customer service at check in was awful and unfriendly. The rooms are smaller than advertised. And the noise caused by their own staff is horrendous. 

I will not recommend this location even though the physical location is convenient.

It's official... bridal stores are either amazing or horrible, and although I was initially on the fence with this place today proved to be the straw that broke the camel's back!

I ordered my bridesmaid dress back in June for an October wedding and was told I'd get it  mid September. I literally had waited for the last minute to order the thing, but since I only needed minor alterations, the person "helping" me said I should be OK. 

Speaking of "helping", I find the people who work here utterly useless and generally inattentive. It seems that unless you are bringing a truckload of bridesmaids with you or are a bride willing to spend $$$$ on their selection of generic dresses you are SOL. I've been here on a Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday and it's the same every time....
No one to assist you in the fitting room, no one to provide you colour swatches and no one to answer your questions.

I was surprised to get a phone call Aug 11 to tell me my dress was in and ready for pickup! Usually bridesmaids dresses can take up  to four months to come in, so I was super happy to see that it was early.  The message stated that I could pick the dress up any day except Saturday or Sunday.

I came in and told the woman at the cash I was picking up a dress. She asked me to write my name down on a piece of paper and then proceeded to help someone else. In the meantime, the other woman at the cash ignored me; I waited for 10 minutes until she realized that no one had helped me.

When I finally got my dress, I was told that I would need to make another appointment for the alterations. I have no clue why this wouldn't have been mentioned on the phone message would have avoided me yet another trip! As I waited to be rung through, there was an uncomfortable silence.... no music, no sales clerk small talk, NOTHING! I honestly don't recommend this place, what a disappointment.

Where to begin? My fiancee and I came to pick up her dress, and the following happened:

1) Sales associate on the floor assumed we were just here to "look at accessories" instead of asking us what we needed, then took quite some time to call anyone to help us
2) Had an associate (actually, this may have been the owner) come to help us eventually, then treat my fiancee so condescendingly that I had to step in. This sales associate also could not locate my fiancee's dress, and claimed we gave her the incorrect name information (it was given to her in a 'lastname-comma-fullname' format, written down--what's to not understand? Why the attitude?)
3) Treated so rudely throughout to the point where if we hadn't already paid a deposit, we would have been out of there without paying. 

Hey, guess what, Best for Bride? We were both going to do our alterations (two dresses = more $$$) there and buy accessories. You just lost out on that business. Would absolutely not recommend.

Made an appointment online, was greeted right away and shown around by Bonnie. She is a very warm and welcoming woman; makes you feel at ease and excited about your search for the perfect dress. Their selection is massive and they have TONS on the clearance racks. Unfortunately many of them are damaged in some way or on the larger side (size 10 and up). If you are looking for discounted dresses and don't mind paying a little more to fix it up this is a great choice for you! I didn't find my dress here but was really pleased with Bonnie's customer service!

Of all the bridal shops I was intent on visiting, this one was the one I was most excited about.  The reviews online made it seem like a dream, and that the perfect dress waited just for me. 

When I walked inside a woman was at the counter arguing with the saleswoman about how her daughter's dress was picked up from the seamstress terribly wrinkled, and she wanted Best For Bride to pay to have it steamed.  Apparently it's pretty pricey to have that done, but even if it wasn't, that seemed like a pretty reasonable request, if you ask me.  

The woman flat out refused to help or offer any sort of information and said it was the seamstress's responsibility and that the woman would have to "deal with it on her own".

At first I thought, okay, this woman took the dress to her own seamstress to have it altered.  It's entirely possible Best For Bride has nothing to do with this.  I browsed through the selections, which were okay.  They had some nice designer dresses, and their clearance rack, though small, was pretty amazing.  $400 for a Jasmine dress!  

However, buttons were missing, the side was ripped, and I just didn't feel like that was okay.  When I was trying the dresses on the same saleswoman explained to me that they'd send the dress to their seamstress to have it fixed, altered, and etc. 

Fearing some impending awful customer service experience based on what I had just seen, I skipped it.  Boy am I glad I did.  The dress I did end up going with was fantastic and the saleswoman INCREDIBLE, but that's for a different review!

We came in here today for 3 bridesmaid dresses. We made the error of not booking and appointment (none of us has done this before!) Despite this the lovely ladies here made time for us and even found us an associate to help out. Erin did a fantastic job helping us pick out dresses. My friend also had her 1y/o son with her and Erin was great with him. It was not an issue at all to have the baby and stroller with us. She asked good questions to find out what we need in a dress and then pulled some cute styles for us while we looked around for things we liked. There are tons of dress options available so it was very helpful to have Erin there.  She was able to help us getting into the dresses and quickly found prices, style numbers, and options for the dresses we liked. In the end, her favourite is the one we're going with. We had a great time here today and have beautiful dresses in the colours we need. Everyone from the manager to all of the associates were friendly, helpful and way more accommodating than many stores would be. I can't say enough good things about this place!

My experience with Best for Bride spans 3 long visits and ended with one very happy bride... 

I first came to Best for Bride about 8 months before my wedding with the intended purpose of trying on dresses I could later find online for less because I was on a budget. It was sneaky and I felt bad when I saw how helpful and down to earth my sales rep Gordana was. I was also pleasantly surprised at their selection, esp. of size 14 and 16 dresses (though they have tons of each size) and at Gordana's polite honesty cause I hate it when sales clerks tell you you look good even when you don't just to get a sale. When I got home, I was annoyed to find that any website that had my top dresses either had bad/mixed reviews, multiple complaints with the BBB or didn't offer much of a discount. I didn't want to risk it after all and found myself browsing physical bridal stores in the GTA again. 

I returned to Best for Bride 6 months before the wedding for another look, this time with my mom and maid of honour and tried on a LOT of dresses in every style. Gordana helped us out again and she was incredibly patient and light-hearted, making us all feel really comfortable. We narrowed the search to fitted mermaid gowns and selected a first, second and third choice (two of which were under $800). Unfortunately, I didn't act on anything and shelved the purchase due to an income interruption.

3.5 months before the wedding, feeling cynical and stressed over putting it off this long and wondering if anything can still be done in time, I came back to Best for Bride knowing that if I'm going to love a dress anywhere, it would be there. I was happy to see Gordana assigned to me again, but disappointed to find out that my first choice dress from before (of which they had a size 8 sample) would not come in in time for our wedding date and I had to choose from samples. Gordana cheered me up and helped me go through their entire stock looking at every sample mermaid dress in my size that was in good condition. I tried on a bunch and was almost ready to settle for my 2nd choice when by some strange miracle, we found my first choice dress in my size! My mood changed within seconds and I knew it was meant to be. Just when I thought I would never have that "this is THE dress" feeling, I had it. It was awesome, and I couldn't have done it without Gordana. *happy dance* 

Knowing that I was budget-conscious, Gordana explained all options to me: buying vs. renting, etc. and I paid my deposit on the spot. I am sooooooooooo happy and relieved and excited. I'm definitely looking forward to the big day where I get to finally show off my selection. 

I would recommend Best for Bride in Etobicoke (and especially Gordana) to any bride. If you're looking for a place with a relaxed atmosphere, helpful knowledgeable no-pressure staff who offer really great and honest advice, a huge selection and good prices, this is the place. I used to think David's Bridal had good prices and variety, but the quality of the dresses there pales in comparison to those at Best for Bride. Stop reading reviews and just make an appointment, already! :-P 

To any bride considering the online option (as I did for a long time), just be very careful and do your homework. If it turns out to be a dud, make sure you can return it and when you do, get yourself an appointment at Best for Bride!

It was my first bridal shop and they made it so enjoyable. Jan was super helpful, funny and very nice that the whole visit felt very relaxing. She listened to what we wanted, was able to answer all our questions and absolutely did not put pressure on us buying the dress

I had made an appointment online with Best For Bridal, but when I phoned multiple times and could not reach them I was beginning to think they went out of business.  When I was there I realized that they just let the phone ring while helping people in the store - handy if you are the one in the store but not so great if you are the one phoning.  Going in there was intimidating, being told to pick out dresses in a sea of white, but eventually my helper finished with her former appointment and picked a few, one of which ended up being the one.  The change room was crowded with all the dresses hanging there and it was awkward having a curtain for a door when there was a man sitting with another group just outside, but my helper was friendly and helpful.  I thought I got a great deal on the dress, but waited until I went to see a seamstress before writing my review just in case - I'm glad I did.  I had taken a quick look at the dress to make sure it was ok and the workers did not mention any problems except that it was a size big but could be taken in when it was fitted to me by the seamstress.  When I went to the seamstress, taking in the larger size turned out to be more complicated than the other store had indicated.  She also found other problems to fix that I had not noticed in the sea of white:  there was a four inch rip below where the dress ties and a bunch of missing beads, that can be fixed for a price, and some pulls in the fabric that cannot be fixed at all, which I'm starting to worry about.  My reasonably priced $600 dress will be approaching $1,000 when the seamstress is done with it, and it may still have issues.  I understand it is caveat emptor and I should have looked more closely at the dress, but it is hard to see problems in that volume of fabric, and the store employees gave no indication that there was any damage to the dress, which should have been visible to their expert eyes and should have been obvious to the person tying my dress up at least.  Had I known they were selling me damaged merchandise I would have requested they show me something similar that would be made new and presumably perfect, I was not looking to save money like that and never indicated that price was a factor.  So while I was initially going to give four stars for friendly service and good prices, for sleazily pawning off their damaged goods for $600 they drop to two stars.  Try to find an honest dress shop instead and avoid buying lemons from Best For Bride!

Although I didn't find the dress I wanted I enjoyed my experience here. The first time that I tried on dress was at Best for Bride. Bonnie was my sales person. She was really nice and friendly and I was able to try on a variety of styles to figure out what I wanted. Bonnie paid attention to my budget, and took note of what I didn't like. 

The store is big. They have lots of room and I felt special here. They don't overbook like some places where you are fighting for space with other people. I recommend going for morning appointment if you can get one. I love the 360 camera that allows you to see the front and back of the dress. They have a large variety and range of wedding dresses. Their bridal selection is better than their bridesmaid selection.

If you go here ask for Bonnie and you won't regret it. She's lovely and very knowledgeable.

I'm only giving BFB a 4 out of 5-star rating because it was the only dress shop I went to so I have no other shops to compare it to. However, I did not leave disappointed.

My mother and maid-of-honour flew in this past February after one of the worst snowfalls so far this winter, which meant that the roads were in poor shape, at best. Since they were coming from out of town and I had booked the appointment, we (including my future mother-in-law) decided we were going to make the trek from Brampton to Etobicoke regardless of the weather. I'm glad we did!

I made sure to read tips on how to try on wedding dresses (strapless bra, shapewear, put some make-up on, bring heels, put hair up, etc.) in order to make sure my experience was less stressful. 

We showed up right at 10:00 a.m. on a Saturday and were one of the first groups in. It turns out that we were the only people who had a reservation to try on dresses that morning (the others were trying on bridesmaids dresses downstairs). After taking off our jackets and putting on slippers (as is customary of bridal shops) we were introduced to our consultant, Lucy, and given a small container of yellow binder clips to put on hangers of dresses I liked throughout the store. I was a little worried I would be overwhelmed, but it actually went a lot easier than I thought.

Here's the trick: don't bring too many people and don't bring people with FAR different tastes than your own. Thankfully, my group was open to all suggestions and even picked out a few contenders.

So, I clipped about 8 - 10 dresses and headed towards the large change rooms to get started. Lucy brought my dresses over and helped me into every single one, and even showed my maid-of-honour how to do up the corset back. 

I almost could have stopped at the first dress - it actually turned out to be the runner-up. However, after 8 dresses, I found THE ONE. A $1,200 Mori Lee illusion neckline dress from the 2013 Spring series. I LOVED it. I decided to go ahead and put the deposit down right then. Which is great because they have a deal where you get $100 off your dress or $100 worth of accessories when you buy the dress the day of. 

My mother also found her dress and it looked great. For $400 a gorgeous dark grey dress with jacket. Very sharp looking - my mom looked great.

I even got to pick out my bridesmaids dresses too - a black, cocktail-length Mori Lee lace number that matches my dress. At a great price too!

This shop is very clean, spatious and well-tended to. While I lucked out on a day where it was essentially empty (thanks to the storm), I could only imagine what it would be like on a busy weekend. They even have "interns" to assist the consultants to ensure that everyone is well looked after.

I would definitely recommend this shop to friends and family after my experience. I have no critiques of this shop. Great work, ladies and THANK YOU LUCY! :)

I can't wait to go back in June for my first fitting!

Vanessa

While I did not walk out with a dress, I certainly had a great experience here. Yes, I am still in the market, but that's because I'm notorious for having buyer's remorse, and promised myself that I will not be an impulsive shopper when it comes to my wedding dress. 

I came here last weekend with my bridesmaid Jessica and we got Bonnie as a sales associate. Bonnie was incredible, she was so much fun to have as a consultant. I showed her a few pictures of the dresses I liked, and off she went. In the hour I was there, I tried on 6 different dresses. I really liked 2 of them, but again - I promised myself I will give myself time to shop around and really find THE dress. I was the last appointment of the day so the store was pretty quiet, but I didn't feel rushed and Bonnie made it an enjoyable experience. She's the type of consultant you want working with you! 

The store is large (there is a whole section of bridesmaid dresses in the back I never got to see yet), and very clean. Note: bring socks, no shoes allowed (like many other bridal shops). 

I gave this review 4/5 stars because I did not buy a dress yet and so I cannot comment on the service i.e. on time delivery, fittings, alterations etc... What I can say is, just by my short visit - I would be happy to buy my bridal gown here. I still have a few stores to look into, but there are definitely prospects, and I may be back.

Worst experience ever at a bridal shop !! Dirty inside and terrible staff!

Came in during my scheduled appointment to pick out a wedding dress. The environment was rude and hostile the moment we came in. The sales associate was very rude and told us to take off our shoes and leave it at the door in a terrible manner. 

The sales associate Golda stood there as I was looking for my wedding dress. She was unprofessional and didn't offer any help. She said I can pick anything from the entire store to try on. I went to a rack, the sales associate yelled at me saying I can't try the dresses on that certain rack on because they're new. 

At this point she was not only rude to me but also gave attitude to my bridesmaid. She didn't help me much in terms of my dress selection and didn't know what she was doing. The dresses were all in the wrong size and Colors. I had told her my preferences and she didn't care. 

At one point I wanted to try on more dresses, the sales associate seemed annoyed and told me there's no more dresses in my size and preferences. I even told the sales associate I don't have a budget and she treated me horribly. 

I recommend future brides to not waste your time and come to this store. You will be shocked at how disgustingly horrible the customer service is the moment you walk inside the bridal shop.

Can't really critique this store, but from what I saw. They emphasize cleanliness o the store that the women took off their shoes before entering the floor. They have a tremendous staff and very attentive to all customers. Good job staff.

I am a big fan of Fat Burger. LOL I was craving it and I got there at 9:27 at night. I looked it up online and made sure they closed at ten. When I got there they had the open sign still on and the doors locked. They just starred at me as I shook the door handle. I was pretty disappointed. The next day I still wanted to eat there. I went there during the daytime. The staff is a mess. They are so unprofessional everyone is running around, laughing and playing. So many people backed up waiting on their food. I couldn't even figure out who was managing the place. I don't think I'll be eating at this location any longer.

I'm writing this review as I just sat down to eat, I was craving a turkey burger, so I thought this would do the trick. So I order, and go to wash my hands, this bathroom was so disgusting, I've been in cleaner gas stations than this. Graffiti on the diaper changer thing, the floor was repulsive and I won't even speak about the toilet. As I come out to find a table, I notice all the tables are dirty, and the seats. I'm starting to lose my appetite. Since the grill is open I'm trying to asses the situation behind the counter to see how dirty things are. Should I stay or should I go now? Ask for my money back and leave? Ugh decisions. 

I decide what doesn't kill you makes you stronger (I was really hungry) and I gave the turkey burger a try. Was pretty tasty.   

The ambiance, not so much, between the thoughts of a dirty restaurant, and the guy behind the counter making burgers singing mariachi music, and the day workers in the home depot parking lot, I'm positive I won't be coming back here.

Burgers are good.  But really thin patties.   Really not much meat at all.  As with most places you get way more bread and bun then meat.   If your carb conscious opt for lettuce  instead.    They do have some killer shakes though
First off, the food is always great. It's so good. But what made this experience wonderful is JAMIE. She was very nice and professional. Made our dinner well worth it

FAT BURGER CORPORATE ALERT: BRAND BEING TARNISHED! Ive loved Fat Burger since the first day I enjoyed their turkey burger with egg and Mr Pibb. This is the only Fat Burger I've seen look this bad.Do not think this is how all Fat Burgers are operated. Everyone I've been to was nearly perfect.  What happened to corporate quality control? Neon sign broke, dirt building up from neglect, no one greeted me and manager rushed order, TV broke playing nonsense. Trays of old food sitting out, chairs, straw wrappers, and other stuff all over while employees walking by with no care to clean it up. Only the manager and lady working not sure but looks like they are trying to save money but its going to end up costing them customers. Food was good but more care could have been put into stalking the burger so it was even.  It's sad they don't care anymore...

My girlfriend is a fan of Fatburger, so I decided to go to this location to surprise her with some food. I quickly discovered, however, that Fatburger, this location in particular, is a very mixed bag.

First and foremost, the biggest flaw: NO DRIVE-THRU WINDOW. In this day and age, I didn't think they were still making fast food restaurants that required you to get out of your car. It doesn't take a rocket scientist to know that this is a big mistake.

Secondly, the service is very hit and miss. One time I asked for the thin/skinny fries, and they put the larger steak fries in my bag anyway (which if you ask me, aren't as good.) One time they tried taking my order when they weren't even standing at the register, and needless to say I wound up repeating it several times. 

Another thing that is really weird about this location is their jukebox. It brags about free music, yet the LCD appears to be covered up. On top of that, it even has money/credit card slots. Seriously? Having access to free music would be a great way to kill time while waiting for my order, but it looks to me like this damn thing doesn't even work.

And another big flaw.... the PRICES. For a medium burger and a small  order of fries, its TEN DOLLARS. And this is WITHOUT A DRINK! The food at Fatburger is excellent, and I believe they would be justified in asking slightly more for their items.... but this is ridiculous.

If you MUST eat at a Fatburger, go to one with a drive-through - and be prepared to pay more than you might want to. This is a place that has the potential to be great, but this one needs a drive-thru, improved service, and lowered prices before I give them anything above 2/5.

I would rate this place 2.5 stars. food was delish, but service sucks balls. 

We went here for dinner on Friday night, a quick stop for "fast food" on the way to the airport.  Is Fat Burger fast food? because this place was anything but fast!

There were 4 people working, 1 cashier and 3 ppl prepping food. It took 15-20 minutes for our order (2 burgers, shake, drink, fat fries) to come out.  The server brought us our food and I asked "will my shake be coming out?" and the chick gave me a blank stare and walked away muttering "I don't even know what's going on."  Really?!  Did I just witness that?  My shake came out...5 minutes later.  My burger with cheese and chopped up bacon was bomb-tastic btw. So freakin good.  Too bad the service here sucks though.

I love Fatburger and this location is one of the better and bigger ones in town. The dining area is really big so there are always comfy tables or booths. And the rocking jukebox is FREE so play some tunes while you eat. 

I usually get an XXL (double cheeseburger) with grilled onions, pickles and all-beef chili. I'm a low carber so I'll get it served in a dish with no bun. I love the beef here and I love how it is cooked in all of its own delicious burger grease. Sit at the counter and talk to the cooks while they prepare your dinner, and order a soda that you can keep refilling yourself at the self-service soda bar (this location has Coke Zero and Gold Peak brewed tea, both make my tummy happy). 

I love Fatburger's handmade milkshakes too (and their skinny and fat fries) but I've had to give those up due to all the carbs. But if you can, try their skinny chili cheese fries, they are the best. They melt shredded cheddar on them which is the key to good cheese fries. There are also a long list of possible toppings you can get on your Fatburger from relish to fried eggs to bacon and grilled onions. They also make grilled chicken and veggie burgers too, and both are good. You can also get your burger on a whole wheat bun or wrapped in lettuce.

Everything is cooked to order here so once you order you are given a number. They'll deliver the food to your table. Plan on spending about $25 for 2 people; it's not exactly cheap but it's convenient and the food is always fresh, hot, and served with a smile. The bathrooms are usually pretty clean here too, and they have FREE wi-fi so you can work through lunch.

I gave a bad feed back because the dinning are and tables are always dirty. Salt and pepper shaker and discusting all covered with black gums till the new management took over. Guess what not a thing changed and didn't take long same disgusting place to eat. The cooking are you can see over the counter is dirty as it can get. You will run out of you see it. Just walk up to cooking area and see it through glass....Never again..!!! Move along to better and cleaner place to eat. In & out is your better choice and not too far.

One of the few fast food chains that offers a veggie burger option. They use the Boca patty which is not my favorite. 

Pros
-Staff is friendly
-Offer a veggie burger, turkey burger
-Skinny Fries (not diet food but they are cut thinner than steak fries)

Cons
-Burgers don't taste that good. My veggie burger was very very lackluster and my friend's beef patty was apparently not a home run either
- Price : 11 dollars for a fast food  meal (burger, fries, coke)
- Not really fast food if it takes 10 min to get the food

It's going to be a long time before I go to FatBurger again. Not impressive but edible.

If I could give them zero stars I would.  Fatburger has great food. That being said, this location is horrible.  They can't get an order correct and the fries are always burnt to a crisp.  Customer service is nonexistent and they have an "oops" attitude when they forget food in your order or give you someone else's order.  Don't waste your money or time. Go to a different location.
Service was great. Got my food fast, how  I ordered it. Place was clean, even though I ordered to go but I was satisfied

A regular cheeseburger, regular fries, and regular soda for $12.50?!

First, I have to acknowledge the cashier, Shanae.  She was excellent.  Helpful and outgoing to everybody in the restaurant.  I was so impressed with her service that I looked on my receipt for her name.  

The cheeseburger is good.  The fries were decent but not worth $2.99.

I gave it a shot because I use to love fat burger. It was the only place I could get a child burger in Vegas years ago. I was starving so, here I am. They don't take the on line coupons here. Its $30 for me and my kid. The food is not the Fat Burger I've had in the past. The burger is super greasy and the fat fries are hot but, soggy almost as if they were microwaved. 

I'm eating and all I smell it a dirty bathroom. How can I eat when I smell sewer. I'm disgusted. I'm not eating I'm leaving. 

I'm never coming here again. The smell is overwhelming!!!!

I'll go to Tommy's and get a real Cali style chili burger and not smell shit!! Never coming here again

Called them to see if they were open and the guy said yes. I said great I will call you back with an order to go. Called back 3 minutes later and went to voicemail. Waited a few more minutes and called again still went to voicemail. So I called from my husband's phone and wouldn't you know, they answered. I said I was calling to place an order and the guy straight up hung up on me. Can't tell you how much I love Fatburger, but this definitely pissed me off. Definitely not going back. Called 5 guys across the street, 10 minutes before closing and they happily took my order and had a smile on their faces. Love spending my money on places that deserve it! Bye bye Fatburger.

Just paid $14 for a turkey burger fries and soda. Could have gone to McDonald's.  Used to love this place.   Won't be back. Just by tasting one fry I can tell they haven't changed their oil in a long long time.

For some reason I'm on a Fatburger kick lately.  I was in the area, so I stopped by and ordered a Large Fatburger with Cheese and Skinny Fries. 
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/5jTmjxb1X34EfcY1gos4tw?select=GHXXu6KUhAB1WgvXVovFBg
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/5jTmjxb1X34EfcY1gos4tw?select=nuXk9K_k26TXuwTqscisEA
I like this location because the restaurant is always clean and there are plenty of seats and tables.

The food took a while to come out.....it's Fatburger after all.  The Fatburger was very good, as usual, and the Fries were cooked just right.  I couldn't finish the order of Fries, next time I'll pass.  Solid 4 Stars ()

Return Factor - 90%

I've been to other Fatburger's in the valley and this one is by far the worst. 

Came in here at 5:50pm to order two burgers to go, one medium and one large, with cheese and no tomatoes, and some fries. The cashier was very nice, however don't be fooled, a nice face does not mean a sense of urgency. My order was punched in at 5:59, and since I know the burgers are make to order, I expected the food to be out in about ten minutes.

Wrong. The female cashier and the male cook had absolutely no teamwork whatsoever. They were all over the place and were literally falling apart, with only 4-5 orders on the screen. There was food just sitting under the heat lamp for a good ten minutes before she decided to grab it and hand it off. At the 20 minute mark, I was getting impatient, because an elderly woman got her order (two burgers) before me, and she ordered after me. I politely asked where my food was, and the cook said it was coming right up, and that if I had a complaint, it wasn't their fault because they were short handed. 

That's a load of BS in my opinion. I manage a high volume restaurant and any competent staff can handle multiple orders, ESPECIALLY when the whole menu is essentially burgers and fries. Even with two people, with proper teamwork, sense of urgency, and a sense of priority, they should be able to handle a work load, especially since it is what they are trained to do. 

6:34 comes around and I finally get my food, along with one other woman that was waiting for her orders to come out, which had a long ticket time as well. The cashier went up to me and said if I came in next time and said they botched my food, I would get a replacement. I don't want a replacement. I want to go into a food establishment, and get my order within a reasonable time period. 30 minutes is not acceptable ticket time for two burgers that weren't even made properly. 

Other locations are good, just this one needs some serious improvement.

I see this is a pattern at this location. I already am leery of fatburger due to the food poisoning I've received at another location. When they made our order (take out) the service was pleasant. When we got home to discover one of the burgers was wrong (three is a much higher number than 2 and therefore hard to count to) we packed it up and drove back. They told us "They would prepare us a fresh order, but didn't want to get in trouble with their manager. Well, I WOULD return to the place, but I ate cold, soggy hamburgers that cost me over $20, for just the burgers. With this location in the hub of Five Guys and Fuddruckers, I do not feel that I should have to pay that kind of money for poor customer service AND just a burger. I can go to a full service restaurant in the area and receive CUSTOMER SERVICE, and that's even if I choose to just have take out. Luckily, since they do cook everything fresh (at least half of our order), I had plenty of time to type up this review and post it to several review pages.

Awful.  Place smells like garbage and the service is poor.  I could get over the garbage smell since I didn't eat there, but the burger just was just not very good.  Place was empty and the employees seemed annoyed that I came and they actually had to do their jobs. 

Fat burger used to be a place to grab an above average burger in my opinion, but this location defiantly is not.

went in to try their famous XXXL burger, their soda machine was down so they were offering can sodas and promised free refills with the soda purchase, asked for another can of soda and the cashier was like annoyed by me for asking, they messed up my order and put all kinds of things on it that I did not ask for, every bite was smothered in mustard and relish. the 3 employees were like hiding in the back you'd have to wait a while before anyone would come to the counter for anyone needing help. horrible service extremely dirty restrooms that appeared to not have been cleaned up for a long time.

If you've been to a Fatburger before, you know what to expect.

The food is on par with every other restaurant in the chain that I've visited, which is to say incredibly greasy and fattening --the way an item named "Fatburger" should be.

I've never had a bad experience here, but it could stand to be a little cleaner and the food is still only a notch above standard fast food fare.

I know, I know... I'm supposed to keep my food consumption controlled if I am to either lose some of this weight or maintain.  I couldn't help but try out Fatburger again after the whole discussion between In&Out and Fatburger.  I wanted to make sure that my choice between the two were correct.  And, hands down I will choose In&Out over Fatburger.  Sorry Fatburger fans.

I chose this location just because of convenience.  What I like about Fatburger is the fact they take call ins, the patties are fatter and thicker, and the choice to have an egg in your burger is available.  Mmmm, such a delight to have egg in a burger.

Downfalls are that the meat is somewhat hard and dry, the relish on the burger doesn't do anything for my pallet, and the taste just doesn't do it for me.  There's just something missing.  I thought the onion rings were good but all that oil just lost me.  

Staff were great and awesome.  Lady calling out names when the order is up seems cheerful and willing to go above and beyond.  I liked her enthusiasm.  :D

Gave 1 star because the guy on staff that took our order was nice, polite and smiled a lot ..Cost $30 for 2 of the smallest cheeseburger meals. Floors were sticky all over the store. Tables not. Leaned. Bathroom was in terrible Gross shape. Soda machine was out of syrup. Napkin dispensers were empty... the 7 employees I saw were all hanging out in the back by the cook. Not once did any of them come out to the lobby to clean up or do anything that resembled work. Got our food and the buns were so old I literally checked for mold... all on a slow Sunday afternoon. No leadership. Can't imagine how dirty the kitchen is since the soda machine looks like it hasn't been cleaned in over a year.. just bad.. could have spent literally half the amount somewhere else and not had to worry if I was going to get e-coli poisoning.. #nevergoback

I love fat burgers but last time my families order was not right and ever time it gets dirtier and dirtier.  It is so unclean that I stopped going.  For example, go to a smash burger on Sahara and compare the inside and the cleanliness.  I like the taste of FB better but I don't want to eat some place that is dirty.  Imaging what the kitchen, that we don't see, is like.

When I feel like having a good old fashioned hamburger, this is where I go.  It's just a good, juicy hamburger, and they do it right.  Love that you have a choice between steak fries or skinny fries, and both are good.  Their chili is also decent, and goes well with their fries or on their burgers.  I like that they give you a list of everything they put on your burger, so that you can pick and choose.  Also, handmade milkshakes, yum.

Now I have eaten at several FatBurgers and this location has got to be the worst! My burger was the driest, thrown together burger I've ever had got home took 2 bites and was pissed!!! My fries were cold as ice! I will Never go back

We Went to see Nashville unplugged a country concert and then went to eat at Fatburger, the burger was okay, but we got fries that was cold and 2 drinks  the bill was over $30 for 2 burgers for what we got and the price was charged it is not worth it and we will not be back!

We stopped in here today for lunch. Definitely not the best dining experience we've ever had.

First of all the young girl taking our order seemed very bored with her job. No enthusiasm at all.

We both ordered a burger and fries with a drink. I assumed they'd give us our drink cups at the counter. When they didn't I assumed our drink cups would be brought to us at the table. They weren't. We went back up to the counter to get our cups.

There was some smell emanating from the restroom that smelled like spoiled air freshener if there is such a thing. My girlfriend said it was almost overpowering in the restroom. It was a really sickly sweet smell. I'm not sure what it was but it didn't make the burgers taste any better.

Here it is several hours later and I'm a little bit queasy. Not sure if it was the burger, but I haven't eaten anything else today. 

If it comes back up I'll change my review to a 1 for now I'll stick with my 2 star review.

I'm so surprised at how low the rating is for this location. I've always had great experiences here and the staff is very friendly! The restaurant is clean and the atmosphere is fun. I admit the burgers are pretty pricey (my husband and I can easily spend $25 for both of our meals), but the food is delicious!

Fatburger and breakfast? I never really saw myself eating here on a lazy Sunday morning, but a quick and casual breakfast craving brought me here. Plus, seeing that breakfast is served all-day, I can see a breakfast fanatic (me) frequenting this place on more than one occasion.

Don't come here expecting extravagance. You get your typical breakfast sandwich: a bun packed with a sausage patty, cheese, and a fried egg on the bottom. The fried egg was a nice touch, which gave it more a homemade taste that you don't get in most major fast food joints. It's not a gigantic sandwich, but it's a good enough size to get my fill. Although it doesn't specify in the menu, the sandwich comes with a side of tater tots too.. score!

I'd skip out on ordering the OJ. Turns out, it's the bottled concentrated Tropicana stuff. Does not taste fresh squeezed, nor does it taste fresh. Reminds me of the sour OJ sipping sessions during depressing hospital visits. Definitely gonna roll with a coffee on the next visit.

Prices more than reasonable for the breakfast menu. I got my sandwich, tater tots, and OJ all for under $5. I end up spending almost twice that much getting something off the regular menu.

P.S. - Free Wi-Fi is offered here!

Great food. Worst service of all time.  They rarely get it right. Root Beer float ordered 3 times in 3 visits. Meal came without float twice got it 15 minutes later after asking. Once float came without meal. Had to request meal 15 minutes later.

Apparently they have new owners and want to charge for everything individually.  Bring the cost of a reg fat burger meal to over $13.  Yea sorry fat burger your dreaming of you think you can charge that for your burgers with 5 guys right across the street.  Fat burger you FIRED!  I doubt this location and its owners will be here very long. Bye Felicia !  5GUYS HERE I COME

Its the worst burger i ever had, the meat was so dry and salty, Service was slow, the place is so dirty.and top of that you pay almost $12 fir a burger you're expecting to be a good one but its very disappointing.. I never recommend this place

I'm not sure what more one could want if a fat burger with the works, American cheese, bacon and a fried egg doesn't do it for you.  I can tell you that's the only way to go.  Add a chocolate shake if you game.

I really like coming here. The food is always good and consistant. Its made right in front of you while you wait. It takes a few minutes, but is worth it. The staff is always friendly as well. We had more than exceptional service this evening from Natalie and will be back!
So very, very, very dirty.  People were nice but disgusting EVERYWHERE! I honestly don't know how they're able to stay open.

My boyfriend and I came to this location for lunch because I remembered LOVING fat burger when I was a kid. When we walked in and I went on yelp and saw all the bad reviews. I thought "whatever I'm sure it'll be fine" I thought wrong. We walk up to order and the cashier was having problems with her register, no big deal. After I had finished ordering and was about to pay I asked for no pickles and relish and she got flustered because she didn't know how to go back on her POS, and said she would just let the cook know herself. We sat down and waited probably 25 minutes for your food... THE PLACE WAS EMPTY! After we got our burger I looked and there was relish and pickles on it. I took it back to the woman who had taken out order and she replies, "oh yea you're right, so you want a new burger?" DUH! After waiting another 15-20 minutes for a new one it came out with cheese that I did NOT ask for. At this point I was over the top angry. I haven't ever asked for a full refund before but there was no way I was spending my money on this service. I asked for a refund and the fry cook and cashier got an attitude with me. The casher then refunded me for the burger only and not the fries. I had to show her my receipt and she said, "oh you want me to refund the fries too?" She refunded me the fries and we got the hell out of there. I will NEVER go back again.

Don't go to this Fatburger unless you're prepared to endure disappointment after disappointment. 

It began with ordering our food. My mom ordered a burger without the bun, which isn't anything outrageous these days, but for the woman taking our order, she had to go back and get the manager to assist her in completing the rest of our order. In total, we were up at the counter for over five minutes. 

After ordering, we sat down and waited...and waited...annnnd waited...annnnnnnnd waited. I'm not exaggerating when I say we waited 20 minutes for our order of three burgers and two fries to arrive at the table. And it's not like the place was packed; we were the only people there, other than a party of five that walked in about ten minutes after we arrived. 

Once the food arrived, the manager apologized as one of our burgers was incorrect, but we didn't really feel like waiting an additional 20 minutes for a new one. There was definitely some temperature consistency issues as well, since our food was hardly warm by the time it arrived, most notably the fries. 

After bringing us our food, the manage went outside to smoke, as she was sitting right outside the window next to our booth. Another large party walked inside and started ordering. Once again become frustrated with the ordering system, the same employee who originally took our order when to the door and shouted to the manager "Get your ass back in here!" 

Overall, I don't mind Fatburger for its food, it's okay for what it is, but I probably won't be back at this specific location. The entire experience was unpleasant from the get-go.

This is a tricky review to write as I do enjoy Fatburger products but the service is inconsistent. Often times they forget to add the extras that you order for your burger. On several occasions I have ordered bacon on my burger and have gotten home to discover no bacon was ever added. About half of the time something is wrong. The staff is friendly and helpful but many of them are not properly trained. Often the credit/debit machine is out of order. Compared with In-N-Out Burger the wait time is very long.
