An okay place to stay, just don't get stuck eating here.  You are better off going to Wendy's in Terminal three than subjecting yourself to the dubious food, indifferent service and ridiculous prices of the Gateway restaurants.

I ate two poor to mediocre dinners here, both with tabs in excess of $50 including tax and tip.  Gluey soup, microwaved bread, pizza crust reminiscent of cardboard. (Worse than the frozen pizzas you buy for your five-year old.) The spicy pretzel mix at the bar was the culinary highlight of my visit.

Our surreal experience in this factory-like hotel is worth recounting. But first, the review:

Pluses: great bed, well-appointed room, great shower and bath. Good ventilation and soundproofing, and the entire hotel is non-smoking. The front-desk staff were attentive. We got our room via hotwire.com for about $84, including all taxes.

Minuses: The sound of diesel engines in the background is constant, from buses and service vehicles in the terminal. Our third floor room was next to the monorail, which was quiet, but it was disconcerting to see a train flash by periodically. Internet access costs over $7 for 30 minutes! 

Housekeeping left the alarm set, so we were rudely awakened at 7am, after arriving at midnight from a long flight. Then housekeeping knocked on our door at 7:30am (on a Saturday!)  But the best was yet to come.

The fire alarm went off at 10am.  This is of course just an accident. However it kept chiming for 35 minutes, off and on, louder and softer, until the staff finally announced the all clear. This mostly motivated us to get our stuff packed and get out of the hotel as soon as possible.

The in-room Starbucks coffee was horrible.

Honestly, I've stayed in one-star hotels that were more comfortable and relaxing.  With free or reasonably-priced internet, no less.  Hotwire rated this four-stars...I don't think so.  The best thing about this hotel is the convenience of staying right in the airport.

Not cheap, best rate I could get was $150.00 for a 9 hour stay between flights, but if you're ok with that money (I was), you won't find a better location for YYZ airport.  Connected to Terminal 3 via a short walk and Terminal 1 by a 90 second free train ride you'll never be late for your flight.  Huge rooms with very comfy beds and a great shower.  Widescreen TV's were nice, even if small for the distance.  Staff was very friendly and helpful.

We arrived at 11:30 pm and it took us almost an hour to get to our room! The shuttle train to Terminal #1 was down and the signage said to go to column #27 - we could not find one. A Airport Employee sent us to column S5 where we began asking for a shuttle to the Hotel. There was much confusion. Finally one unrelated shuttle driver took pitty on us and took us to the Hotel. Not good considering we paid more to be right at the Airport. We should of stayed at at a Airport strip hotel and shuttled - it would of been more reliable and less costly.

stayed here for my quick trip to toronto. luckily.. my flight landed in terminal 3 so it was super easy to get to the hotel. there are signs to help you find your way to the hotel so it's pretty straightforward. 

the staff is super nice and the lobby is beautiful. upon check in.. we were advised of all our transportation options.. but we felt the front desk was trying to steer us in the more expensive mode of transport because they probably get some money from guests who take the hotel "taxi" since they only stop at hotels. in the end we decided to take the bus/subway option and it was perfectly fine.

the rooms themselves are okay. nothing spectacular. for the club level i would have expected nicer rooms. the sheraton gateway in burlingame which is now hilton was much nicer than this hotel... and i think much cheaper too! i was a little disappointed. the rooms just look a little worn down. 

the LG flat screen TV was nice.. and the rooms were spacious. thats about the only positives i could say besides the lobby. i think in the future i would book here on my own only out of convenience.. especially now that i know how easy it is to get downtown.

tip* if you plan to take the bus/shuttle into downtown, exchange your money for tokens at the exchange booth in the airport. instead of paying 3 dollars each way you pay 2.50 and get a token. one token is good for the bus ride AND the subway including the transfer so it's super easy. no fumbling around for your transfer or token after the bus. one token takes care of you the whole way :)

Recently stayed at the Radisson kitchener, and the Grand in Toronto which set my expectations at level the Sheraton failed to meet. Thus they did not meet my expectations.  1st off the line ups for SPG members, so if your in line and about to be served but a SPG member comes up they get served before you. Creates a sense of social class disparity for members and non members. thus don't expect equal treatment for customers. Additionally WIFI costs $15. fortunately for me this is the only place I have stayed in this decade that doesn't provide free access to wifi. Lastly also no breakfast. Overall if you want to spend more to make yourself feel special over the those who don't this is the place for you. If you are against being nickel and dimed not the place for your. There is another hotel at the airport I will try next time. I have no intention of going back to the Sheraton I do not recommend it. However, I have had worse experiences it was clean, and the room was nice despite not having a view, but I doubt you should expect that at any hotel airport.

I am a platinum guest with Starwood hotels.  Love the brand and for the most part love the service offered by all Sheraton hotels.

I have stayed at this hotel many times and they have virtually zero platinum recognition.  It all starts upon check-in where the spg preferred guests are ignored and preference is given to flight crews and other guests from the regular line-up.  

My most recent visit I actually called ahead to tell them I was arriving at 6AM and would only be staying for 3 hours to catch up on sleep - I paid for the full night.  Not only was I not given an upgrade I was put on the louder side of the hotel.  Furthermore they were cleaning the room across the hall from me at 6AM!  Seriously who cleans a room at 6AM? The hotel that is trying to double sell a room to airline crews does that!!  No worries that the noise will be inconveniencing guests at that hour.  

Upon leaving today I am carrying 2 coffees and my bags out the front door and was having difficulties with the door and the door man stood and watched while he chatted on the phone.  My colleague who was picking me up saw this from his car and noted he had been on his phone for over 15 minutes.

I will give the morning staff in the club lounge credit.  They are over the top friendly and offer fantastic service!  Take note of this as this should be the standard for the entire hotel!  

I have complained to the hotel management on numerous occasions and apparently  it is falling on deaf ears as nothing ever improves.  If anything it gets worse!!

Unfortunately there are no other choices attached to the airport otherwise I would have switched long ago!!

I had a late night flight into TO so I called both Sheraton's to see how much a room cost.  They were very similar in prices so I decided to stay at the one that I could stay indoors in the whole time.  There is a connection from Pearson terminal to this Sheraton so I came over here.  When I arrived I got quoted a different price but they were "willing" to give me another room at a discount slightly above the original price they mentioned but had to go through a cleaning because someone had smoked in it.

Thanks to the jerk-ass on the phone for not telling me this when I called.  I would have went to the other Sheraton.  I was exhausted so I stayed but the room stunk of smoke.  The room was very large and like most Sheraton's you never feel like you get your money's worth for the stay.

Here to assist in the executive meetings for my company, and I have to say the Service staff here has been great. They are professional, timely, and friendly. They follow the instructions that we have given them and they have been very helpful whenever we needed something. GREAT SERVICE.

While I cannot comment on this hotel as a guest, I feel it is noteworthy that I review my experience here.

I am a meticulous-OCD traveler. I have itineraries, addresses, phone #, hours of operation etc. with me everywhere I go. Rome may not have been built in a day, but I got us through Rome in a day!

Fast forward to the one time I did not get down to ONE detail on a vacation. Weeks before the trip, I download app after app so I could be well prepared. When our plane landed in Toronto, I turned on my iPhone and realize it doesn't read AT&T on my phone anymore. Why?! Because we are NOT IN AMERICA and did not plan ahead with our carrier that we were going outside of the country. Our phones were roaming and basically useless. 

After going through the airport and getting vague directions from staff there, we walk outside of the terminal and I notice there is a hotel literally at the airport terminal. We decide to walk over and ask if we can use their wi-fi (we clearly did not know the airport had wi-fi) so we can plug in the laptop and try to figure things out. We needed to accomplish two things: 1. get to an AT&T store  2. get to our hotel.

Upon walking into the hotel, we were greeted by Flavia at the front desk. I told her about our little embarrassing situation and had to be an unfortunate representation of a product of American public education. Instead of giving us wi-fi, she took matters into her own hands and feverishly searched on her computer for an AT&T store and when that could not be found as they do not exist in Canada, she got us their customer service number so we could call them later when we got settled into our hotel. She also went above and beyond and called our hotel to let them know about two stranded guests, asked if they provided a shuttle to/from the hotel/airport and what was the best/easiest way for us to get to the hotel and to ask if we could check in early as we would be there in an hour or so. She wrote down a ton of useful information for us and sent us on our way. 

While we were not guests, Flavia's service truly stands testament to this hotel's customer service. Having been my first impression in Canada, I was humbled by her act of kindness. Flavia was extremely kind and efficient, what she did was far beyond the call of duty as she was helping non-guests. She really took control of our situation and made sure we were taken care of. I am so thankful for Flavia's generosity and the Sheraton is very lucky to have her represent the company at the front desk. I am going to contact the hotel and the company to make sure they know she provided outstanding service!

Thank you Flavia!

Landed at 11pm and had another flight at 7am, so naturally we wanted the easiest, convenient sleeping option, which = this hotel as it's the only one actually connected to the airport.

Check in was a breeze and we opted to go straight to the bar to grab a late night bite to eat. 

Bartender was friendly and made some suggestions on the menu.  Hotel pricing, but we managed to get two glasses of wine, a soup and a pizza for about $50.  Food came out relatively fast, and found it was decent.  

Room was quite nice, and the shower head had some amazing pressure. 

Nothing too special, but perfect for getting a few hours of sleep.

Woke up with giant, swollen bed bug bites which I did not notice until 12 hours later (and took 3 weeks to heal), after I got home and stripped off my clothes. Fairly traumatizing experience actually - I used to say that you can trust SPG hotels at a minimum not to have bedbug infestations but that is not the case. The hotel later confirmed it was bed bugs. I asked for 200,000 points and they gave me 20,000 (and $250 from the insurance company). They said they felt this was fair compensation for what I went through, but I disagree and this experience has really tarnished the brand for me.

Sleepless night in this hotel. 

PRO: it's located attached to the airport 

CON: Rooms are dated and old.  Carpet is loose and ragged.   Shower is fitted with old, 1970 's faucet and head with very little consistency in water temp during the shower.  A/C (loud) would run for 30-45 seconds and cuts off for about 2 minutes and then back on for 30-45 seconds... All night in this loop.  The whole time it was hot in the room.   Sheets are marked up with a Sharpie noting "King" and other notations that I guess make it helpful for the cleaning logistics.  Hair in sink. 

Overall, just seemed like a Days Inn with a fancy lobby.   I'd opt for a close hotel in the future.  The benefit of staying so close doesn't out way the issues with this tired property.

Stayed here many times. Rooms are very nice and quiet. Well kept and of course close to the Airport as you are in it pretty much. Good lounge in Lobby and a restaurant. You can literally walk out the door and catch the Shuttle train free to go to your appropriate Terminal. Unless your flight is at Terminal 3, then you are already there.

The Toronto Pearson International Airport, Terminal 3, has this Sheraton hotel literally connected to the terminal.  So, if you don't need to travel into the city for any reason and convince your meeting host just to utilize a conference room here, then you are in luck.  You could literally just wander around in your pajamas if you wished.

Now, the downfalls are exactly the same as the positives in that you are nowhere near the city itself (relatively speaking, i.e., you cannot from your hotel out onto the streets of the city and explore).  As a result, you are confided to room service, the hotel restaurant, or starvation (or I suppose airport food)... and then there is always taking a taxi into the city - which sort of defeats the purpose of staying here, I think.

The hotel is very clean, the rooms are spacious and acceptably maintained, and you are not going to come away with "the pox" or any other malady from staying here.  You are also very safe and secure.  Additionally, since this is probably a concern, the rooms are amazingly soundproof.  You will absolutely not hear the planes coming and going around you - which is pretty phenomenal.

Anyhow, you might as well give the joint a whirl.  In the end, it's a Sheraton (not a W, not the Ritz, etc.) so 3-stars seems fair.

Not my favorite place but okay. A little dated and the parking situation sucks because it's right at the airport.  You have drive to the top floor (5th) of the parking lot to park at the hotel.  The gym is okay and the SPG lounge is actually pretty good - the selection of breakfast and happy hour items was definitely more than I've seen at most sheratons.

Toronto Pearson Airport is literally surrounded with hotels, but only one is located within the actual airport itself! If you're flying to/from Toronto and don't want to to deal with the hassle of taxis, finding your way around an unfamiliar city, or have to leave for an early morning/late night flight, the Sheraton is located right inside Terminal 3.

Driving to the hotel was a bit of a mission - the roads leading up/around the airport are a nightmare so it took us 4 laps around the airport before we found the hotel. You have to drive through the parking lot to the top floor in order to get to the hotel entrance. Parking is $30 a night, but there's a value parking lot just a short distance away. Access to Terminal 1 is also super easy, as the hotel is connected to the terminal link monorail train.

The reception was absolutely lovely. I'm part of the Starwood Preferred Guest program because I travel quite often, and was upgraded to the Prime Minister Suite!  This is more of a business executive type of room I'm guessing, so it's great if you're on a business trip or need a conference area. The bedroom has a king sized bed, a bose sound system, a large dresser, a desk and a large flat screen TV!

The room itself is on a private floor and has a lounge area with buffet - the food is great and there is always a supervising attendant.  There's a Sheraton Club lounge located by the elevators. Sheraton Club hosts hors d'oeuvres until about 8:30PM, so we popped by for a light evening snack.

In case you're wondering about the noise - the hotel is located at the airport, so that means non-stop airplanes overhead right? This was a concern of mine until I learned that the windows are double paned so you don't hear anything!

Overall, I had a lovely experience at the Sheraton Gateway Hotel! I highly recommend it if you need a place to stay while traveling in/out of Toronto Pearson Airport. The staff were friendly and helpful, the rooms were clean and spacious, and the location is super convenient! An all around winner, methinks.

Location is ok if you're already at the airport. Bathroom was literally rusty and not very clean. More noisy than usual. Parking was expensive, $28/day. Stayed here because the deal was $50 cheap than any other 4 star. Staff was nice.

As a hotel attached to an international airport you should review your policies. I flew in on a red eye and wanted to land, book a room and get some rest from my jet lag. Your front desk agent told told me he could not check anyone in at 6am so I had to come back at 9am. Terrible service for business travelers

Very nice place to stop in if going to Terminal 3.  This hotel serves multpile purposes.

In one case, its a hotel.  As in, you need a place to rest your head for the night.  As far as that goes, its a fine hotel, and if you are on the club level its a nice little bonus.  Nice lounge, edible food, nice drinks, really cant loose for a hotel club level lounge.

It is also a great place to park and walk through if you are picking someone up from Pearson.  You can park at the hotel (there is a fee), and walk through to find your person, the arrivals are near the hotel, and then go back out through the hotel.  You can do the same by parking at the airport, however, this is very easy and it may be faster in the long run as well.  

If you have to wait, there are nice restaurants and a bar in the hotel itself.

The third nice thing is they have a deal, if you spend a night here you can leave your car for a reduced rate for a week or more if travelling overseas.  This is terrific.  You can of course stay here on the way back as well.  Your car will be here, covered parking if you want and its all just easy.

3 stars because it is a hotel at the end, comfortable, nice beds, fine rooms, easy parking, reasonbale food.  The 4th for the ease of the airport as a result of the hotels location.  But if the hotel were just "another hotel" near the airport, it would be three stars.  Its the parking, the airport access from the hotel that give it the extra "umph".

I stayed here for one night on an SPG free night reward. Unfortunately, I was given a room which was directly across from the YYZ Link train (airport shuttlle), which significantly impacted my ability to get a good night's rest. Running all night long, the noise generated by Link train was loud enough to become a major annoyance. 

For the most part, the room itself was modern and clean, although the bathroom could have used some renovations. 

If you are looking for massage therapy, you may want to think twice about the "Vaccaro Spa" on the main level, as it provided the sketchiest massage I have ever had. The rate was $105 for one hour, even after receiving an airport employee discount. A receipt is provided for insurance purposes. Upon requesting a massage treatment, you are instructed by the therapist to follow her up to the 2nd floor of the hotel, and all the way to the end of the hallway to a hotel room. Inside the room are two massage tables and a cheap stereo playing relaxing music. If after receiving your treatment you wish to shower, you must use the room's shower in the bathroom, which is FILTHY, and contains half-used bars of soap for your convenience.
No free wifi! Rooms are nice, clean and comfortable, and corridors are quiet. Couldn't believe they charge for wifi on top of the fee you're already paying to stay at a Sheraton!

If you find yourself walking around in your PJs outside your hotel and you're in terminal 3 of a major airport, then you must be in in Toronto at the Sheraton. 

Super convenient if the plan is to have local sales force pick the geeky marketing guy from the airport for customer visits. If you don't need a car for the night, staying here would be Option A. Where else can you fling open your window curtains and watch a few Boeings and Air Busses drift by?

The staff is super nice (except when you talk about the Leafs and the Sharks) and the lobby is nice during check in. Whether you're going back into the clouds or you'll talk about cloud computing the next day, this hotel offer lots of transportation options and the rooms are fine for a biz trip.   

Whether you're the type that wears pink PJs with little hearts or the type that sport fluffy bunny slippers or you're like me, sleep commando when you go to bed,  remember to not thoughtlessly rush out of your hotel to buy something out of drugstore--- you will have terminal 3 as an audience.

Rude front desk.
Slow check in.
I'll forever go the extra miles and stay somewhere else & I recommend you do too.
Safe travels
Not great value but worth remembering when you are stuck in Mississauga for meetings. Good food quality if you order sensibly.

This hotel is handy if you have an overnight connection... certainly beats the Toronto traffic!

That said, the amenities were generally poor, though that isn't entirely the hotel's fault -- aside from the hotel lounge, there were few choices for dinner, etc.

This is probably the best feature of YYZ, but that's not saying much...

It most certainly was not on-par with a Renaissance (YEG) hotel nor a Fairmont (YVR).

The hotel is convenient for my layover on the way to the Dominican.
It is a bit of a walk to catch the train from Terminal 1 but faster than taking shuttle to another hotel around the Toronto airport.
It was a bit expensive for only a 4 hour sleep before catching the next flight.
Room was large and clean.

Definitely one of the better airport hotels I've stayed at (I think the other one was at Paris CDG). Very clean, friendly staff, pool and hot tub, steam room (looked a little sketchy).
The best part is that it's in terminal 3 right were American flights depart.

Check-in was seamless for our 1 night stay. Which technically was 7 hours since we were catching a connecting flight early the next morning. Staff at front desk was friendly. Our room was clean and average size. Nothing that makes you say "wow" As a Starwood member, I would expect an upgrade but since it was such a short stay, no big deal. Would have been nice, but hey it didn't happen.

I like the convenience of staying here, since it's located in the airport and no need to go outside. Grab your bags and go over the pedway/walkway to the hotel and vice versa back to the airport.

The problem I have with some hotels, is ones that charge for Internet/wifi. This isn't 2007 anymore Sheraton. Get with the times. When we finally arrived to our room, I was not able to get Internet on my laptop or IPad? After a call to the front desk, found out I could pay for it for $20? For a person who needs to access her emails and respond to somethings for maybe an hour max, this isn't something I was willing to pay for. Sadly, I had to go down to the lobby and work from there since Wifi is free in the lobby as well as the airport.Not ideal when you just travelled for 6+ hours and its almost midnight.Fail.

Checkout wasn't ideal. As I mentioned, we were at the hotel for less than 7 hours before catching our early morning flight. When arriving to check out, only two people were in line. Since its check out it should be a fairly quick and seamless process....right? Not so much! Only one person was working at the desk and it was obvious, she had no idea what she was doing. When we finally had our turn, she printed off our stay/bill. I noticed two charges on there,that shouldn't have been. Our bill should only be our 1 night hotel stay, nothing else. Which I told her. She advised me there was two charges from the restaurant for lunch and dinner? Advised her that was not possible since we arrived after 11:00pm and were not even in Toronto for lunch or dinner? She obviously didn't believe me and thought I was pulling a fast one on her? No idea, but I was not impressed. Told Her I would not be paying those and to only charge my credit card for our stay. After all it's 6:00am and I am in no mood to get into an argument this early before my next flight. That didn't sit well with her and after some debate, I told her to look at our file since she should know what time we checked in at? "If we checked in that late, well it's well after lunch and dinner time". Yes, stating the obvious and trying to be a problem solver. Someone needs to be.

Long story short, paid for our stay and she would investigate the other charges. No apology or friendliness on her part. It's obvious it's Sheraton's error. She stated she would charge the credit card for our stay and if the food charges were really not ours, it wouldn't be charged to the credit card. I was firm and told her, it better not be since we were not even at the hotel when these charges transpired or even in Toronto? We have been back home for two weeks and no other charges showed up on my credit card so I will assume they figured it all out? No idea. Was not overly impressed with this or the Internet situation. Next time we will stay at another hotel at YYZ airport.

The times I did stay at this hotel, I was actually stuck in Toronto on way to wherever else.  And that seems to happen quite often.  This hotel is literally right outside Terminal 3.  Anyways, this is a great hotel for those frustrating moments.  The staff was always friendly, patient and helpful in any way they can.  The hotel is kept quite clean and nice but the staff definitely makes this place a wonder to stay at.  I'm sure it's because they've dealt with many, MANY stranded travelers!   The hotel bar's last call is at 1am...and that was very important when I couldn't find a soul inside the airport to answer my questions!  If you are ever stranded in Toronto airport (not that I would wish that onto anyone!), just head here.  You will feel relieved that someone cares!

Nice hotel and very convenient. Rooms are well appointed and generally in good repair. The bathrooms are getting a little tired, but are still in reasonable condition. 

Parking is a little confusing, but once you find it, it's very handy.

Nice hotel in a very convenient location. My flight got cancelled, so I walked over to this hotel. The gym is very nice, compared to most other hotels. They have a lot of equipment and it's well maintained.

First of all, this is NOT a 4 or 5 star hotel as it is ranked on many travel booking sites. The rooms are nice, a little tired as some other reviewers have noticed. Fine for a 3 star but if you are really expecting more than that you will be disappointed.

Pros: 
*Easy to access location
*Friendly staff
* Decent sized rooms
*Clean rooms
*quiet rooms-easy to forget you were at the airport.
*Onsite store-pricey but good if you are snacky

Cons: 
*Parking is very expensive so if you aren't travelling on business (ie can't      expense it) and have a car, reconsider.
*They overcharge on room service. Yes, I get room service costs more but they add two separate fees not including taxes on top of the already grossly inflated food prices
*Want internet? It is free 50 ft across the road at the terminal but they'll charge $20 a day for it here. It isn't 2005 anymore Sheraton..stop charging for internet access.

I might consider staying here on business if it suited my plans. But if I am footing the bill I'd rather go to a nicer hotel that includes a little more with its rates.

At Pearson Airport in Toronto it's your only choice. There are tons of cheap airport hotels a short shuttle ride away. But waiting for a shuttle late at night in minus 20s is not very nice. Some of the hotels even charge for the shuttle. This one is attached to term 3 and a short train from
Term 1 (where you're likely to be). Pricing is terribly variable (from $100 to $400) pretty much reflecting how much you want the room. If your flight (and everyone else's) just got cancelled then expect the $400 panic rate. If you can get $129 that's pretty good. 
It's clean and nice enough. There is a pretty big bar that's open late. Food is terribly expensive and (I'm a slow learner) after multiple samplings must be said to terrible. Beer is also expensive but fortunately not terrible. Note fish and chips which is really oversized fishstick cr@p is $22 which is quite a lot more than  in the designerist of Philly designer pubs (dandelion of course). That's really silly.

So if you have an early flight out of TO or if you get in late and don't want to drive AND you thought about it it in advance and got a reasonable (vs panic) rate, then this is your place. 
Do not eat at the bar. It's not worth it. I wish I could say something humorous but I'm staring at half a plate of fish cr@p and cardboard chips.
I stayed here for one night for my flight was cancel.  The breakfast was OK at the restaurant.

Look...its an airport hotel....so take it for what its worth.
The rooms are large and clean, bathrooms are small and tired. Nice big flat-screen tvs but the system sucks.....its a cheap cable system with a limited and pretty lousy choice of channels...you are never sure what program you are watching because there is no program title/info, its sort of like being back in the 1990's..over half the channels are unwatchable due to out of focus,snow....this has been a continous problem for all the years I've stayed here during my travels. The food is fine,not 5-star but more than adequate. Lobby bar is your typical airport hotel bar...but a very good variety and choice of booze.
Its attached to the airport so its biggest plus is the convenience between flights,especially for those really late arriveing or really early departing flights.

I hate living here. These are horrible quality apartments. Every time I walk to my car or back to my apartment I can smell marijuana and cigarette smoke and all of the tenants are rude. They charge you almost 1200 (water/sewage included) a month for 2 beds and 2 bath with 1 parking spot?! Almost everything has broken at least once (washer, dryer, toilets, garbage disposal, door handles, cabinets are falling apart) Can't wait to get out of here feels like a overpriced ghetto. (Don't be fooled with the nice offices) at least the repair guys are nice. I WILL NOT BE RENEWING MY LEASE.

I'm giving Park meadow 5 starts because I've lived here going on 3 years at a pretty damn good rate for the area. I've never had any issues with parking, dings in my door, loud neighbors or bad management. The few appliance issues were fixed pretty quick as well. What else could you want from an apt complex. Convenient affordable and upgraded options. Nicest apt you can get in Gilbert before you get into mortgage prices, in which case, buy a house.

I've lived here for almost a year and a half. I would NEVER move back to this complex. The office doesn't open until 9am but they send all the landscapers & leaf blowers to start at 7am --  ridiculously early. And to top it all off, at 7AM this morning they sent a group of guys to cut up the sidewalk RIGHT BY MY BALCONY. It's extremely loud and when I asked the maintenance guy why this was happening he literally said too bad. We can't wait until 8 or 8:30am? Really, 7AM? 

Also - kids play all over the parking lot and ride bikes/scooters up and down all the sidewalks. They also take trash from the dumpster and play with that too. One morning I woke up to what looked like my car being keyed, with a 2 foot long scratch all along two panels. I took it to the body shop and they said it was probably a handlebar from a bike or scooter. GREAT. When I called the front desk all I got was "sorry that happened."

The younger girl at the front desk has the worst phone etiquette, attitude, and ability to handle any issues. Literally, your water could not work and it's 4pm and she'll tell you "maybe tomorrow." Um..... Nope, you're sending someone now to fix it. When I first moved here I loved this place, now I just can't wait to leave.

I toured the apartment homes with a Rebecca.  She was very informative and kind.  She had a great attitude the entire time and helped me out tremendously, being that I am moving from out of state.  This place seems amazing and in a great location!  I will definitely be renting here when I transfer from Ohio, thanks for the great customer service:)

After living in these apartments for a year here is what I discovered:

I really like the area around here. I was able to walk to Freestone Park which was really nice, it is walking distance to a pretty good sushi place & a couple other restaurants, and there are lots of things in the area that make living here convenient. The apartments themselves are not much to speak of. The kitchen countertops are white and made of a material that absorbs ANYTHING wet that gets on it. Stir a cup of coffee & put the spoon down - stain, if your counter happens to be slightly wet and you put a grocery bag on it the ink from the bag will stain it, fruit stains it, some vegetables stain it, just about everything stains it. So if you're the kind of person who actually uses your kitchen for cooking then this may not be the place for you. The bathroom countertops are the same way. The carpet looks bad despite taking my shoes off on the tile entry and being very careful. I think it's just really cheap carpet. I've had water in my storage closet for about 6 months. They supposedly fixed the issue but I know it has not been fixed. I told them but nothing happened. I only keep a bike in there thank God or otherwise all my belongings in the closet would be destroyed. One day a maintenance person was walking around and asked me if he could look in my closet and I let him in. He said the whole wall needed to be knocked out. He said he would do it the next day and it wouldn't be an issue. Well, it never happened. So my mold-infested wall is still there, getting moldier. I also do not think there is a playground in the complex. If you have kids you may also want to rethink this place. Unless you don't mind them playing with the other kids in the complex who ride their bikes and scooters in the parking lot (be careful if you plan on using the parking lot to drive your vehicle in because they do not look out for cars), and who climb on the dumpster and the wall surrounding the dumpster. When I called to inform the office that there was a safety concern with the children playing in the parking lot WHERE CARS DRIVE I was told there was really nothing they can do about it.  I'm no genius, but I thought maybe they could inform the parents that their children are in harms way by riding bikes where 3000 to 5000 lb vehicles drive (some of which whip around the corners pretty quickly).

I would give them zero stars if possible. I am so glad that the manager can take time to respond to negative Yelp reviews but can't be bothered to return a tenant's call about an important issue. This complex is no better after ConAm took over from Equity Residential. All they care about is getting your money.

Park Meadow Apartments leasing office has the worst customer service that I have ever encountered.

When a tenant calls with a serious question about poisons being sprayed in my apartment for the 6th time and they can't even be bothered to call me back as promised, it doesn't feel too great or reflect well on the company.

Since taking over from Equity, the leasing office staff has been nothing but incompetent. My husband and I had to go to the leasing office 3 different times to sign lease renewal papers because the office staff could not manage to print out the correct paperwork until the third attempt. This is really annoying when you have to leave work early to make it in during office hours. And did they even apologize? Absolutely not, they just laughed at their mistakes. But this wasn't even the real issue.

The rear building of Park Meadow has a roach problem that began in 2010 shortly before my husband and I moved in. Within the last few years of living there, our apartment was fogged with roach poison 5 times. This means that we had to pack up and seal our whole kitchen, linen closets and bathrooms, wipe up the poison as best as we can and try to put our home back together. We have had to do this 5 times, despite the fact that our unit is kept clean and no roaches were found after the initial fogging. There was never an apology and never an offer to pro-rate our rent for the continuous inconveniences. Shortly after the last fogging in Spring 2012 my 6 year old cat started experiencing acute renal failure. Because he is so young and this shouldn't happen to a healthy cat, our vet said it was possible the chemicals used to fog the apartment had something to do with it. We managed to save him after several months of treatment, $3,000+ in vet bills, and coming close to death. No matter how much you scrub and vacuum, some residue from the poisons will always remain in the apartment, especially after 5 treatments.

So I was reasonably concerned when I received a notice that the apartment was to be fogged again, especially when our lease is up in the next month. I spoke to Kathleen in the leasing office and she assured me that she understood my concerns (which she didn't) and that the manager would be calling me the next day, which was Friday. I did not hear anything from the office and nobody would answer the phone when I tried to call. My husband went in to the office and again he was reassured that someone would call us. Again, they didn't bother to contact me on Friday or Saturday. I was willing to discuss the possibility of using nontoxic means to deter the roaches, but they office staff didn't even give me the time of day.

I understand that they are in the process of remodeling the office but that is not an excuse to provide poor customer service and ignore the concerns of the residents. I am in the middle of moving out of state and actually had to cut short a trip to visit family to come home and deal with this problem that management continuously fails to solve. The building has German cockroaches, a species that has a higher rate of reproduction than normal roaches, making it easier for them to build up tolerances to certain poisons. After 5 foggings, I have a feeling that this has happened at least to some extent. And the chemical that is supposed to sterilize the surviving roaches has no effect on the German roach larvae which stay safe on its mothers back. Also, fogging only the units just scatter them into the walls. No treatment has been done to ensure that no pipes are leaking to provide water for the roaches and no poisons have ever been used between the walls where they go to hide and reproduce.

I know ConAm management company took over in the summer of 2012, but there is at least one staff member who has been here the whole time that I have been resident, so they should know the history of the bug problems in that building and should have done more to solve it, rather than just scattering the problem for several months.

I am disappointed and disgusted with the lack of respect and concern the Park Meadow apartment leasing office has displayed. I will be sure to spread the word in person and on the internet because I do not wish this stress and hassle on anyone.

DO NOT RENT FROM THESE PEOPLE! The old management was awesome but the new management is inept and idiotic. First off i made a deal with the old manager to pay a couple days later than normal because I was going out of state from early into the month to 2 days later than rent was due.  I am always on time and pay early even so she agreed that we would be ok and just pay when I returned. I got back and the management had changed without notice and they refused to honor the old managers deal because she was not a Manger anymore so our deal was worthless according to them and charged me a late fee of 200$ that I stupidly paid. So with a bad taste in my mouth i had decided i was moving out of state anyway so had to put in my notice.  I went to get out of my lease and signed the paperwork and left the office. A couple hrs later my fiance gets a call regarding my son needing to sign to get out of the lease... he is 1 yrs old. So I returned to the office with my son on my hip to explain that he will not be signing any termination of the lease for what I thought was obvious reasons. They then started arguing with me that all persons in the apartment needing to sign to get out of the lease.. kinda laughing I told them he can't even talk yet. He just learned how to walk since moving in a couple months ago! They then asked if he could make a mark and  assured me if he could hold a pencil than he could make his mark and that would suffice. I refused to let my son sign any paperwork. They then asked me what would happen if he stayed to fulfill the lease while I left.. staring blankly at him with my babbling child in my arms I told him that would be child abuse and how would that even work? Would I just leave him with a bowl of cheerios and wish him luck in his new apartment?? They then looking at one another tried to hand me a paper for my son to sign again and once again I refused to entertain this idiocy. They then decided they would call their bosses and get back to me. Luckily there boss has appeared to be reasonable because I have yet to hear back. 

Update: ok we put in our notice on January  14th and were told to be out by March 14 and that they would send us a final bill so we pay all of it on that date. No problem seems reasonable. We move out Feb 1st. Give the man running the desk our keys in an envelope marked with our apartment number and both of our names. Saying here are the keys we are moving we gave him our new address to send bill. He says we might even have some money coming back because we have moved out so early. Perfect! Fast forward to March 10th we get a call saying they are taking us to collections for not paying March rent and our lease end. We explain we are happy to pay but we need a bill to know the total and that we were told when we returned the keys we would have some money back and they would send us a bill after the 14th with all of our expenses. They claim we havent even returned the keys!! Finally after a lot of discussion they agreed to send a bill. We wait patiently for our bill. 5 days later we get a call saying they are taking us to court and tried to serve us papers at our apartment! We vacated that apartment more than a month ago! We tell them that we have left the apartment and returned the keys, but now they claim we never returned the keys and are suing us for squatting! We ask about the total and explain the bill scenario and they won't give us the total of the bill so we can pay it! They promise to call back later that day with the total but never called. The number we call back won't go through so now I'm getting taken to court for a bill they won't give me and I have no way to reach the lady who I talked to. These people are awful and I would never recommend living here!!!
The ribs here were disappointing to say the least. The sauce was not good they were chewy and just plain gross. The tiny pathetic corn on the cob was not fresh but frozen. Will not return.

Today was sad for me went into Toms BBQ to celebrate their birthday I got the pork Sandwhich 7.50 combo and a crispy chicken Sandwich. I came home and noticed a skimpy piece of chicken in my Sandwich  usually it is a nice piece of juicy chicken .This was sad maybe next time guys

We gave toms BBQ another whirl last night and I'm so glad we did . I had a chopped beef Sammy , my bf had pulled pork and a side of mashed potatoes .we shared a combo basket of fried pickles , zucchini & mushrooms it was to die for yeah!! We will definitely keep this place in the weekend restaurant rotation

Came back tonight for dinner- even better than the last time

Lunch on Saturday, turned out to be quite disappointing.  I had the Brisket platter, this is not BBQ, it was all dried out and the so called bark was nothing more than a thick salty like substance on the outside edge.  The BBQ sauce was nothing more than tomato paste/sauce with sugar.

The restaurant was 83 degrees inside and when I asked one of the people working there is they could turn down the air 1 or 2 degrees she claimed it was the best it's going to get.

We will not be going back to this wanna be BBQ restaurant .

As former Tempe, AZ residents we had enjoyed Tom's BBQ when we lived there.  We are in Sun Lakes now and we were very happy to discover their new location.  We really love the pulled pork sandwiches.  The employees are all very welcoming and kind.  We even got to meet "Tom" a the Grand Opening.  If I had one request it would be to improve the corn on the cob.  Not sure if they keep it warm in water or what but it lacks flavor.  The BBQ beans are to die for!! Love them.

The main reason I ever go here is because they have fresh cut fries. Their food is so-so for me and the BBQ sauce is not very enjoyable. I always hope I am remembering the quality of the food wrong but end up being disappointed again.
Tom's BBQ in Chandler is amazing.  The food is excellent.  And they have great weekly specials. The staff were very friendly.  We will definitely be back.

This place is growing on me. I usually eat here once a week as it's close by my job. It' no Joe's BBQ in Gilbert, but it's still really good. The owner and staff does a good job at being friendly and there are a lot of sides to choose from. The sign on the pink pig van in the parking lot says it's Chicago style BBQ. Tip: Take advantage of their rewards program. Points add up fast and I'm always getting free side dishes.

Stopped by Toms BBQ for lunch, I ordered the rib tips with curly fries and it was super yummy!!   The place was clean and the atmosphere was friendly.  It was pretty cool to use the bar code scanner on my new smart phone with the little review card I was offered that took me right to this link! Will be back for sure!

The food is great, a little pricey but what BBQ isn't! I love the sauce and the service too. The location is great at Alma School and Queen creek. The place is always clean, and you never have to worry about parking.

They do great at carry out and always offer different deals around the holidays like smoking turkeys etc. 

Love it!
Cashier was annoyed when I asked if they had gluten free options. He told me they don't so we left.

Tried this place out with a Restaurant.Com coupon.  The food was quite good.  The brisket and pulled port were both solid with the pork being some of the best I've had in a long time.  I don't like the fact that they cover it in sauce but that's easy enough to rectify during my ordering next time.  The side dishes were good and they have daily specials ($9.99 pork dinner, etc).  For a filling lunch or a casual dinner, it's a great option.  The interior of the restaurant isn't very appealing but it'll do.

It was alright. We did takeout. Waited inside the restaurant, the atmosphere was definitely lackluster. Felt a little cheap. What I really care about is the food... which unfortunately, was just OK. 
Ordered the pulled pork and the brisket, neither really tasted fresh. The BBQ sauces were awesome, however. 
I'd give it another shot, but won't go out of my way for it.

Location: plenty of parking and the restaurant is super open, clean and spacious. They even have few TVs on the wall. 

Food: I came here to try the beef brisket last night. I agree with other yelpers, it is just average and a bit dry. Their corn bread is too sweet and wasn't the type that I am used to. Service is excellent. I believe the owner/manager was a lady and she was super friendly to check on everyone. 

I might come back here again to try something else.

There wasn't much in the phone in order that they got right. They forgot to give us buns with the family meal, they were out of corn bread so they replaced it with Mac and cheese, they gave us a small Mac and cheese instead of a large (although the kids didn't like the mac and cheese anyway), and they forgot to give us the large beans we ordered. Very disappointing.

Ordered the pulled pork, it was very fatty and the pork was overcooked to mush.  Mc & cheese was comparable to velvetta boxed stuff.  Coleslaw was ok, nothing to get excited about.  Unfortunately not worth the money in my opinion.  Joe's BBQ on Gilbert Rd is way better and everything is home made,
Straight fire  you pay for what you get. It's hard to leave hungry. Onion Strings are a must have IMO. Fish is always good.

So delicious! I love that this location opened up because I would drive to the Tempe location from Gilbert just because it is so delicious. I order the pulled pork with jalapeño mac and cheese almost every time. My mouth is watering just writing this review. You can get hot or mild bbq sauce depending on your taste and there are pumps with extra in case you want to drown your meat like I do. The people working are always super friendly and treat you like you've been friends for years. Love it and it's definitely one of my favorite bbq places ever.
Stopped in for a quick lunch. I had the pulled pork and my husband had the brisket and it was all great! We will definitely be back!

The chopped  beef sandwich was only so-so, but the fries were out of this world -- I'd  go back just for them! Also, I usually ask for sauce on the side and I forgot this time so the sandwich was slathered over with BBQ sauce. Next time I'll try the pulled pork.

Was a bit nervous going here after seeing the mixed reviews.  Went tonight with my roommate and we were both very pleased!  Restaurant set-up is simple and decor is all new-looking.  Staff was very nice and helpful even though the main employee seemed very frazzled since it was a bit busy - he was still very kind and attentive!

Food came out within 5-10 minutes of placing our order and was brought directly to our table rather than having to go back up to the counter to get it.  I got the rib tips dinner with corn on the cob and cole slaw.  The portion was absolutely huge - I needed help to finish it!  Cole slaw was creamy with just the right amount of mayo and the corn was sweet and not overly buttered.  This was my first experience eating rib tips and I was not disappointed.  The pork was tender and had phenomenal flavor.  It was not excessively fatty as some people have said.  The sauce was very tasty - sweet and brown sugary but with a little tang.  My roommate had the pulled pork sandwich with the spicy sauce and the baked beans.  He loved it all and raved about the baked beans.  Desserts looked good but we were way too full.  Overall, I would definitely recommend this place!

We tried Tom's BBQ for the first time.  Not the best BBQ I have ever had.  Not the worst BBQ I have ever had.   The ribs were ok but not a lot of meat on them.  The rest of the meat was salty.  Corn was terrible as also the mash potatoes and gravy, real bad.  The rolls were fresh and the BBQ beans were very good.  The Lady who took our order was very pleasant.  The place itself is bland but they do have a tv with sports.  I have to agree with someone else's comment, how do you smoke meat in a strip mall?  If I was at the strip mall and hungry I might go back, maybe for a hamburger but I would not drive out of my way for the BBQ.
Great service, price and quality! Hard to find real BBQ, this place is great!
The staff is really nice here. In addition to the #BBQ options here are plentiful. If you are looking for a place to take the family or a great date night, this is your place!
Great Chicago style BBQ in AZ.. The pulled pork is a must... And say yes to their spicy sauce... It truly is just like Chicago...

Just OK

I have been here twice and it is OK

I cannot say it is great or exceptional or that it is bad... 

It is just alright...

The bathroom was tricky to find behind a hidden door! Funniest part of eating there!
Simple store layout. Food was very good and portions were sizeable. Best cornbread I have ever had as was so moist.

Love this place!  Just found it and tried the fish fry tonight.  You can order white fish or catfish, all you can eat.  It's the best fish yet! We'll definitely be back for fish as well as try other menu items.   The staff is very friendly as well.   I highly recommend it!
I stopped by on Monday and picked the Monday Special, pulled pork dinner with 2 sides and a roll for 8.99.  It was excellent! The service was fast and friendly.  I would definitely go back.

I will not be back. I am offended that I ordered Catfish and was sold Basa (Swai). Born and raised in Chicago and lived there 44 years until 2 months ago when I moved to AZ, and I feel cheated that I wanted catfish and ribs but was sold Basa, which costs less and doesn't taste the same, not even the same texture and quality of fish. Disappointed! I guess if you don't know better, you would know the difference. They offered me a different meat, to which we took ribs but I'm turned off at the fact that they advertise catfish but give you something else. Basa is not Catfish! When you buy it in the store, they are not the same and they don't cost the same! I find it tons issue of ethics and false advertising! Just stick with the whitefish! Corn meal breaking does not make it Catfish!

This was my first visit and after hearing nothing but great things about Tom's BBQ, I realize why.  Wow, their great selection on the menu, the special requests they will create, fantastic  customer  service and their enthusiastic interaction with the guests creates a wonderfully unique dining experience.  Today they are taking orders to smoke Turkeys for Thanksgiving.  Who knew, I have to try this next year.  
A new favorite spot.
Fantastic BBQ. Local family owned business providing great service and food at very reasonable prices. Try the beef brisket, it's amazing.

Houston? Steak? That sounds like it would be an excellent experience ... Negative ...

Ordered a bloody Mary, nasty

Ordered steak sandwich... Dear Lord, I don't think they know what a steak is!. What I got looked like cat food between two buns dripping with excessive amounts of grease, seasoned with Taco Bell spices.

$18 sandwich.. You can have the same experience at Taco Bell for $1

"Dude, it in is an airport"

Don't expect anything too great BECAUSE this restaurant is in an airport!!!! One shouldn't expect a 4/5 star experience. One should expect to eat edible food, to drink a decent drink or three (depending when your flight is departing), and to read which ever random magazine. Oh, you can read the lips of some morning shows from the U.S.  

I ordered some eggs over easy with bacon and potatoes. Was it the best breakfast I had - No. Was it the worst - No. It was simple food for a small-moderatly sized airport. The service was fast and friendly. I will say that the prices are a little steep but that is the case in many airport restaurants.

It is extremely frustrating for a customer when there is a massive line up of people waiting for a table and many empty tables ready to go with no one being seated and a hostess that doesn't seem to know whats going on. I hope someone from management reviews these comments. These people are all trying to grab a bite to eat at your restaurant before catching their flight and many are walking away frustrated and hungry because the staff are incompetent...translates to a huge amount of lost $$$ for you.

Food was almost inedible... ordered the Californian salad and the greens were wilted and the dressing was disgusting (also, I was starving coming into this restaurant, and I'll eat almost anything when I'm hungry... well I could NOT eat this salad). Other food at the table was mediocre at best. In addition to terrible food, service was poor. Our waitress never came around to check in, took 40+ minutes for food to come, and all meals came at different times.
Pleasant ambiance, friendly service, very slow food preparation, mediocre-to-barely adequate food. The usual high airport pricing; roughly 50% higher than outside the airport.

Poor service, fair food and airport ambience. 
Houstons was recommended by the ticketing agent. The place was packed when we arrived, necessitating a 5- to 10-minute wait to be seated (luckily, we were not in a hurry). After a semi-reasonable wait our server arrived, but the drinks didn't come in a reasonable time. 
Our appetizer was calamari, the best part of our dining exerience and the chardonnay from California was nice and buttery. Our entrees arrived 2 minutes into our appetizer; the server mumbled that it was the kitchen's fault, served it anyway, and apologized repeatedly. 
We thought our food could be worse. My ribs tasted like it was water infused and the fries had good taste, the "seasonal side" never arrived. The salmon was slightly over-cooked and rice was "ehhh." Broccoli and green beans were al dente--good!
Due to the full house (we suppose), our service was lacking. Our water was never refilled, the waiter never checked in,  and it took forever to pay our bill.
My advice--consider a different place to eat if there's a line (we were there at 3pm on  Monday). If you eat here, ask for your check when the meal arrives.

Our group ordered sticky chicken, chicken tenders, and a salad. Took over 40 minutes for the food to come out!  This is an airport​ and people expect for food to arrive in a timely manner. 

Our plane was boarding so we asked for our food to go. By the time we rushed to our gate, we realized they did not include utensils or napkins.  Food ended up tasting terrible. I should have done my yelp research beforehand, listened to the other reviews, and stayed away at all costs.

If I could take away stars, I would but unfortunately yelp will not allow me to rate less than 1 star.
Avoid at all costs. Customer service was good..not great. The food is awful for the price. Take your chances if you want too. Been warned.
This is bad even for airport food. Very long wait, very expensive prices, very bad food. It's the perfect storm of bad restaurant experiences. Stay away!

The food was average but consistent. Have eaten here a few times due to limited sit down options at the airport. The service is very slow. I don't think it is the servers fault but the management. They are under staffed which creates the issue.

I come here often. Food isn't bad for airport food but management needs to help their servers. They are so nice and work so hard but too many times I have waited 10-20 minutes to find they didn't have what I ordered. Most times I have to skip lunch because I have to catch a flight....
I graded this on its airport food. If outside the airport the stats would have fallen. We ordered the poutine and the steak sandwich. They were ok. Decent for airplane food.
Too slow.  Took them over half an hour to make me a burger.  In the end I gave up and went to board my flight.

First, I was told the steak sandwich was not available, then it was available so I went ahead and ordered it.  It was terrible.  The bread and tomato were fresh, but the "steak" was a moist, sticky, and tasteless paste of indeterminate protein.

I sent it back and ordered the Houston burger which was better, but not great considering the delicious ingredients.  Part of the problem was a burger they had to cook well done (because, Canada), but still a poor showing.

Terrible selection of beers for a restaurant with a full bar.

The service was actually pretty great.  Our waitress was nice, polite, understanding, and fully intent on making our visit a pleasant one despite the circumstances. 

I would not ever go back here, though, because it is a waste of money overall.

Rude staff. Rushed waitresses. Horrible dry food. Cold fries. Tasteless high priced 18 dollar burgers. Coke is undrinkable. Tastes like coke syrup mixed with flat dish water. They should be embarrassed to serve this stuff at such prices. A microwave burger would be much better. Tastes like grade school cafeteria lunch. But worse.

Only place near my gate that had nice place to sit (other takeout places close buy had a few tables nearby that are first come, first served). Was not too busy on a Monday at 12:30 pm. Had the crunchy chicken taco (3 pcs with choice of salad or fries) which was supposedly a Houston special. The chicken was not crunchy at all. Had a reddish breading that reminds me of General Tao's chicken. I found it a bit salty but otherwise just ok food. Had a glass of chardonnay and wished it was chillier. Next time, I would try the other takeout places nearby.

2.5 stars

Really slow service even with their call system on the table which could have potentially been a good idea.

Food was underwhelming and def overpriced. Granted it's airport food which is always overpriced but you expect at least decent food. 

The sticky chicken was salty and sauced over until the chicken was super soggy. The Houston burger was okay. We came here cause I was starving and we were desperate for something to eat close to our gate. Otherwise, do yourself a favor and try another restaurant.

Food was just bad  - soggy,  almost cold vegetables and fries served with mediocre steak.   Only virtue is that I think it's the only sit down restaurant after you clear US customs in Montreal.  Would have sent it back in a normal restaurant,  but cut really take the time when you have to run and catch a flight.

Houston not Houston's like in the States and a very different experience. To be honest, we found the food to be fair. Lots of different options from healthy to unhealthy (poutine!). But the service was very very slow. I mean very very slow. We went at around 5 pm on Sunday with 1.5 hours to go before boarding and they appeared very understaffed. Lots of folks waiting to be seated would give up before even making it into the restaurant. We were proactive and flagged someone down to get seated. Then we fetched our own menus and placed our orders for everything at once. We also asked for our check when we placed our order. I think that without those precautions we may have missed our flight. Perhaps that was just an off night when someone didn't show for a shift but be warned.

The service was good but the food was overpriced and flavorless.

Chicken tenders: greasy and bland.

Steak & Frites: both bland.

Who doesn't like an airport bar? This one is nothing to write home about on a MTL postcard. 

They have two local-ish beers available. Show some pride in your beer culture people?! Rickards White and Red. The red was kicked. So the white it was. Otherwise Coors light ('MERCA!!) and Heineken (Netherlands for those not in the know). Where's the Labatt and Molson Canadian at?!

Rickards White with an orange slice it was. It was ok. Not my favorite white of all time but got the job done. 

I conversed with Canadian and international travelers as I waited for my Poutine (see photo). It was a half ass effort, to be honest. Cheese curds not melted. Not enough gravy. And not enough cheese. The meat on top was akin to not warm enough shaved steak from the steak sandwich I got from the cafeteria in elementary school. The potatoes were potato wedges that might as well have been microwaved. Definitely had potential because the flavors were on but the effort wasn't there. 

If this is your last taste of Canada before leaving the country I would describe it as a sour taste. Take some pride in the food and drink and show us why Montreal is such a great place to visit. 

Conclusion: it's the only real option in the terminal so you should go but don't expect too much. Sigh.

This review is in line with all the others who have had the misfortune of eating here.
My potatoes were cold, the "veg omelette with spinach & sun dried tomatoes" was a plain omelette with a few spinach leaves and about 10 microscopic pieces of sun dried tomatoes hurriedly thrown on top.

Unfortunately there aren't too many eating choices in this part of the airport ... at least you've been warned!

As a frequent traveller to Montreal for business, I usually stop for a glass of wine at the bar. The bartender Giovanni is awesome;  he always remembers me and my drink of choice, gives excellent customer service and makes me feel welcome. The food is hit or miss here, and he is always honest and helpful with recommendations.

This is the worst Houston's I ate in. The service was pathetic!  The hostess was rude and impatient. She was doing us a favor. We ordered burgers. They were really bad. Hated paying a $100 bucks for a bad meal! Even the Diet Coke was flat!

If you happen to be unfortunate enough to be delayed several hours at Montreal airport and begin to feel hungry, you will find yourself in a predicament of epic proportions - a wasteland of bad food options.

This steakhouse, to my dismay, is no different.

Because I categorize airport food into two categories: sub-par but edible and sub-par knowing my little cousin could make something better.

I'd say this place falls somewhere in between those two categories. With dry meat, flavorless chicken, and undercooked fries being the highlights of the menu, there really isn't much else to write about.

Went there to grab a bite to eat.  We missed the breakfast menu by about 5 minutes and were  told there was no way to get 2 eggs over easy  and toast.  So at 10:35am we ordered  mini burgers and a club sandwich. It took about 30 minutes to get our food when the place  was only half full. The club was average,  the salad it came with was wilted.  The mini burgers were hard, cold and clearly  had been from the night before.  Very disapointing.  It's not the waiters fault and we could clearly see he was apologetic.  We will  probably not go back there.

OK place to grab something and use table as your work desk till your boarding time.  Food portion is good but don't expect anything more. Burger buns are dry and fries are luke-warm...   No cocktail menu so we asked simple martini and it was 19 CAD!! What a ripe-off! 

Nacho might be the best value item. My club sandwich came with chicken salad.. 
If you choose, sweet potato fries, you get half portion of the regular fries.

Service is good.

There is nothing of the Houston restaurant experience you are accustomed to in town at this airport's US departures location at YUL.  The staff are curt, "you order-we serve" and the menu is overpriced for the quality of food.

I ordered the grilled chicken salad and about thirty minutes of a long wait later, I got a plate filled with arugula, a shake of Parmesan and four strips of chicken for $17.99; quite the rip-off.

I'm in a hurry to take the flight and won't remember much of this place; not worth anyone's time.

I always stop at this restaurant when flying to the US.   The Salmon is great!    also a very good spot for breakfast for those early morning flights.   Service is quick, so if you only have 30 minutes, no worries.
We waited half hour to order, and half hour for a chicken caesar, and steak-ish sandwich, both only ok. Not crowded. No excuses. Fortunately, we weren't in a hurry. If you are, skip it.

Overall a good place to stop for a bite while waiting for a flight into the US.  I've been here twice, once ordering a burger and once getting a sandwich.  There isn't a whole lot to say about a restaurant in an airport terminal that I assume is part of a chain (I don't know for sure, but it certainly does have that feeling of "decorated by corporate committee"), yet the food was good and the turnaround was quick enough that it won't leave you sweating your departure time.  Service sometimes seems to be a free-for-all.  On my second visit a waitress took my order, someone else dropped off my food, another guy refilled my water, the manager took my credit card, either the food guy or the water guy gave me the receipt, and the waitress said goodbye as I left.

Food was barely passable and grossly overpriced. Decor is that of a nice fast-food restaurant. Servers are remarkably poor, uninterested and ridiculously slow, especially in an airport! The delis available just 50 ft away are a vastly superior option.

If there was a 0 stars option I would do that. I ordered pad thai and it was not even remotely close to pad thai. They need to take it off the menu. I basically got a ball of angel hair pasta that had 3 pieces of broccoli, tofu and some egg with some kind of a coconut sauce. No flavor whatsoever. I was starving and I have a fligjt to catch so I did not have the option of sending it back. My server is not the best either. He forgot to give me silverware and never once came by to ask if I needed anything. I also didnt enjoy watching him pick his teeth with a toothpick by the bar that is directly in front of me. I will never come here again.

Had bacon and egg breakfast before a crack of dawn 6:00 AM flight as this was the only breakfast place (other than fast food) that seemed to be open.  Breakfast was so- so.  Bacon didn't taste as fresh and came with your usual potatoes.  We sat at the bar and service was quick and attentive.  Would I come back here?  I would try other options as it wasn't anything memorable!

My flight was delayed and I took the time to have a little dinner. It's an airport restaurant so. My expectations were low. I ordered the sliders which come with a side of sweet potato fries. I also had a glass of the Pinot Noir.

These sandwiches reminded me of grade school burger day,  dry and really tasteless. The fries were unremarkable. The wine was okay. Staff was flat. The chairs were comfortable. 

Bottom line:  Dig deep down into your bag and find that granola bar you've been avoiding. There is nothing for you here.

This place is something else.

Half the staff are OK, other seem like they care about nothing at all. Food wise, they just really don't know how to cook stuff for the general public. Burger by default is well done, so make sure to specify beforehand.

Fries came dashed on the side with BBQ sauce, just sloppy. First time I've ever had a warm salad (clearly they put it too close to the kitchen heat for a while).

Starving? Sure, it will fill you up. But needs new or at least involved management to get this place to glory.. it's not too late. Staff seem even unhappy with each other sometimes. And the floor can be sticky under the table.. plastic glasses don't belong in a upscale-looking place either.. kinda strange.

The food was good, service though isn't the quickest.  I had the ham omelette which was good: ham wasn't too salty, onion and tomato tasted fresh and eggs was decent.  It came with some potatoes, toast, 2 pieces of fruit and a small bowl of beans.  Didn't eat the beans as I usually don't eat it for breakfast.   

All in all, something before the flight.

As others have noted, the prices are high for what you get ($15-25) for burgers and $10-20 for glasses of wine.  The atmosphere was nice if you can snag a booth, more cozy than the sports bar further up the concourse.  The burger was a bit overdone, as were the panko chicken tenders.  BBQ sauce is the sauce of choice.  The wines were of acceptable quality, at least if you are going to pay a high price you get something that is OK.

Traveling with three other colleagues and we all had roughly 18:00 departure times affording us some dinner time since there is no meals on our respective flights home.  There are a few places to chow down but this one had real seating unlike the fast food type cafeteria sitting.  As usual airport sit down restaurants are not the fasters due to the number of diners and their carry on luggage.

Our servicer was maxed and tough to get his attention and no doubt he was worked to the max.  I had the steak with some brown gravy and fries.  Cooked to medium rare as I asked, it was pretty tasty especially since this trip I didn't have any steaks.  

Overall I think if they had more servers and our poor server didn't have to jump from table to table I think service would have been more than fine.  We ended with ordering their 3 small slice cheesecake plate which was as expected good enough to satisfy the sweet tooth in all of us.

If I am back in Montreal and hungry before departure, I will give them another try hoping that staffing issues will be resolved.

Hostess was accommodating of my request for a larger table and the waiter was very nice but the food was not good. I  have a Plain Jane palate but literally nothing had any taste. Shrimp cocktail...no taste. Burger...no taste.  Fries...no taste. Even the bacon on the burger barely had any flavor. I know it's an airport restaurant but for the prices charged by airport restaurants we should at least be able to enjoy some of the meal. 

On the positive side, it is relatively spacious and comfortable so a good place for drinks but recommend avoiding the food.
Outdated overpriced menu ...could find anything interesting that would be healthy... After trying TWICE to get the attention of the server, I decided to walk out elsewhere.

The other reviews have pretty much crystallized my thoughts. Skip the fancy food on the menu, this place is only good for a beer and some bar food. Service at the bar was average, I was offered beverages promptly but it took a really long time to get an order of calamari (which was a tiny serving), maybe that's a ploy to get me to order another beer :)

I didn't see many other decent options at YUL, but this passed the time.

Stopped by for a quick bite while we waited for our plane. Our waitress was super nice and pretty attentive, but that my be because there were only like 2 other tables eating at that time. It's a pretty spacious place and I didn't feel too cramped like some other airport restaurants.

We shared a salad and steak sandwich. The salad was ok, nothing special. The steak sandwich was really greasy and the meat was low quality. The only thing that was good were the French Fries! 

So... bottom line it's not that great, but it's a place to chill if you have time to waste before your flight. Or you can just go sit at the gate...

This airport has few choices and we decided upon this location as they were busy but there was no wait.  We were seated quickly but then it took forever for anyone to approach us regards our order.  Good thing we had the time waiting on our flight as the service continued to be very slow and forget needing a drink refill.  The lettuce on the burger was 25% brown, fries cold and bun stale.  Not impressed with the food nor the service.  The airport needs other choices as I wouldn't eat here again.
This was not good. Rubbery calamari with cream cheese and a tiny dry burger. Not to mention it took 40 minutes to prepare this $50 delight. Go get sushi to go and a beer at the bar down the hall...

Solid airport restaurant. The prime rib dip sandwich was juicy and tasty, it even came with horseradish. Beer was cold. Prices were comparable to most in the airport and a good sit-down meal option with friendly wait staff.

Is there less than a 1 star? If there is, this place gets it. The service sucked, I got my food 40 min after I ordered it and I sent it back. Server threw a place setting at me for no reason. I told the waiter to get me a manager and he flat out ignored me. Perhaps because I didn't speak francoise? Don't know. When I was leaving I said I wanted the meal comped and the waiter looked at me said 'you wanna go?!?! Go!' Then gestured something my way. I ignored it and got on the plane. This place sucked and I'm not stopping with a Yelp recommendation. I'm going full tilt on this place and calling corporate.

Okay so you don't expect an airport to really offer great food but here take the great French dish steak frites and within 5 mins ruin everything that chefs around the world have created. 
Step 1... Unlikely that onglet steak was used, couldn't tell as it was ordinarily resident in the UK 
Step 4... Frites add that dumb seasoning that I bet trump likes... 
Step 5.. Serve.

The one saving factor that got the stars was they used good salt, great crystalline structure with a crunch on oh yeah cold broccoli and greens 

Beer was okay with the dish so altogether a great place to waste that 45mins of time at an airport.

Oh the barman had a top knot thing in his hair ..:

The most important thing to note about this restaurant is that the service is not good nor quick.  As others have noted, make sure you have ample time before your flight.  If you do, this is a great place to relax while you're waiting for your connection.   

Food quality is not great.   I chose this restaurant over Burger King and actually regretted my decision afterwards.  Pluses are: the good atmosphere of the restaurant and the cold beer, which helps, especially when your plane is delayed by a few hours due to weather.  

Overall. I rate this two stars based on the service and the food.
good location in the airport but the food was sub par.... not houstons like the hillstone chain...

Ordered mushrooms on burger and fries, it arrived about 60 seconds later, Luke warm with cheese unmelted.  Meat so tough the knife could hardly cut it.  Sent it back for an order that was hot, got it but totally disgusting soggy fries and meat like a piece of leather.  Had it with a tomato  juice.  Came to $30 with tip!  The worst I've had at an airport and that's saying something.  Macdonald a would have been better.

Very disorganized!  Took forever to be seated. Then had to ask for utensils. Then another long wait until we were greeted; so, I made sure we ordered at that time. Surprisingly, the food was served fairly rapidly - Breakfast. It is hard to screw that up. My coffee was served sans cream or sugar. Luckily I take it black. Our server ignore us until I asked for asked for a coffee refill and additional jelly. The place was not that busy. Oh yeah, the rotund guys seating everyone and busing the tables dropped his cleaning cloth on the floor and THEN USED IT TO WIPE DOWN MORE TABLES.
Don't expect much.  Keep in mind it's in an airport.  They bartender was nice and service was quick but the food was average at best....but if you have a couple hours to kill it works fine.

Awful burger that was overpriced and took forever. It was overcooked, dry as a bone, and not even warm. The beef had that characteristic livery flavor of cheap meat, and a strange bitter crust on it. Service was pretty much nonexistent.
We saw servers, but all they seemed to do was hang out at the wait station. They certainly weren't coming by our table. I really wish I had read the other reviews of this place before coming here.

To be fair, the waitress did comp the meal even after we ate the burger (which we only did because we were starving).
Located past the security checkpoint and close to the departure gates, it's a nice place to sit down and have a meal or a few drinks while killing time to board your flight.
