Can somebody please shut this place down? The only reason they are still in business is because it is the only restaurant in the terminal. The front staff need training in customer service. Words like 'Thank you' or 'You're Welcome' are not in their vocabulary. Not to mention they cut off customers when they are trying to walk by. The food was absolutely horrible and the service as well. If you are hungry or need to kill time do yourself a favour and find somewhere else to spend your time and money.

I am going to be blunt... the food I had here was terrible. It took 20 minutes to prepare a 'hot' sandwich, that finally came to the table nearly cold and missing parts of what it was to be served with. The sad thing is there aren't many options in this area of the airport. The experience was so bad they didn't bother charging me for the order. This location is part of a chain and I assume this means either the entire chain makes bad food or this location is an embarrassment to the group it's apart of. I would give it half a star if it were possible. I didn't have a drink... that may be all this is good for. But I exhort everyone passing through the airport to avoid dining here.

The venue was fine for an airport, service was fairly quickly however the food was not great. I had a veggie omelette, nothing was mixed in except for a lot of cheese, it was very oily and didn't taste that great. It was also pricy for what it was.

Been to several Houston's before and the experience was always good.   I'm seeing a low rating on this location and not sure if it's all warranted but here goes with my review. 

This was my first time and I went with a simple meal, chicken strips and fries.  It was about 11am and there was no line and I was seated immediately.    The strips were decent but not spectacular for $18.00.  (Not for 1/2 that actually). The Fries were
Decent too but only mildly warm.   

Fortunately, my server was fairly quick so I didn't have long waits and poor service like so many others mentioned but then the place was only 20% full.  

Overall, it was a 3 star experience.  Decent but if your right on cash I would have just went to one of the many delis just 30 seconds away.  

Enjoy!

Food is ok, there is no lots of others place for lunch.. staff is lazy and arenot customer oriented.
Well just good because you have almost no choice.

Wouldn't recommend this if you're in a rush. Very slow service. We waited over 30 minutes for eggs and the people next to us had to leave before their food arrived because they were going to miss their flight. Also, warning: the omelet are made from a pre-mixed egg formula and are completely disgusting. We sent ours back. All in all, I would not recommend.

Terrible service, probably the worst I have ever experienced. I actually saw a patron next to me get his bill before his food arrived. All he had was a glass of water!  His face was priceless!  If you must eat here, make sure you have plenty of time. 
As for the food? Okay.

Drink a beer or two, eat some "bar" food. If you come here and order a steak or complex entree, that's your fault. That's like ordering Sushi in Bangalore...(You got food poisoning? Hmmmmm, that's weird). 

Their burgers and tap beers will do the trick, then get on the plane and go. Just go.

When you're the only restaurant in the terminal, you simply don't need to give a flying f*ck about quality. And at Houston that's their modo! Overpriced frozen dog feces on a plate. Go to the grab and go counters for decent food. 

we ordered the steak sandwich and the chicken salad club. Both "meats" resembled what you'd get in a pre-made, week old, gas station sandwich. The poor guy next to us ordered their $55 "steak". Don't think he was too happy when it arrived and looked like it came from a Hungry Man TV dinner meal pack. 

Avoid like the plague, simply not worth it.

The Coffee Table has been open in Wesley Chapel (Weddington) for about five months. It is the brainchild of John and Melissa LaTour. John is the executive pastry chef. I was finally able to find my way over there today to check it out, and I was very glad I did! 

This is MUCH more than your typical coffeshop, such as Starbucks! They have something for kids and adults of all ages and tastes, and not just beverages! Sure they have many different coffee, espresso etc. drinks, hot, on the rocks and frozen. They also have teas, chai, homemade fresh lemonade, hot chocolate, Italian Creme sodas, and much more. 

They also serve Tony's premium ice cream, bagels (direct from NY), pastries (see reference above to pastry chef John LaTour), cookies, specialty breads (more like cake), sandwiches, soups, salads, etc. 

Danielle had the Coffee Table Club, and they happily subbed American cheese for the Swiss, and I had a special, the roast beef and cheddar panini... hold the red onions, easy on the horseradish. Danielle's club was also prepared panini style. We each loved our sandwiches! Make any sandwich a combo with chips or cookie and coffee, tea, or lemonade for a buck more! The cookies looked delish!! 

Both of us ordered chocolate malts to go with our meals, and they were simply decadent!! So rich... from hand dipped ice cream... none of that shake mix out of a machine!! They offered some much more creative and exotic options for shakes, but we're old-school chocoholics! This was our fix, and satisfied that jones! 

I read on John's blog several days ago that he had experimented with something apple-praline... I had to know what it was, and he told me at the time that it was an apple cake with praline topping... and they apparently go through it pretty quickly. I inquired about it when we visited, and luckily John had just baked some more this morning, and had not yet topped them with the praline. We stuck around until he had, then made off with two of them. 

I dropped off one of the apple praline creations with a friend who lives in Weddington, as a Christmas gift, on the way home. I am saving the second one to make kicked-up French toast on Christmas morning. I almost can't wait! 

Free Wi-Fi for customers, and a VERY comfy cozy "living room" area with TV, bistro style tables and a European style outdoor cafe area for when the weather is warmer. 

I wish the Coffee Table was in Park Road Shopping Center, near my house #pout#! John is a long-time Union County resident, so I don't foresee them moving to satisfy my selfish desire. I guess I'll have to trek out that way more often in the future. 

If you live in Monroe, Matthews, Weddington, Waxhaw, Indian Trail, etc., you've got to make this place a regular stop!! You won't regret it, and will probably become addicted. Maybe its a good thing it isn't closer to me. I'd probably be there every day!

I'm one of those weirdos who does not like hot coffee - and I have to say, they have the BEST iced coffee in town.  Much better than Starbucks, which is much too bitter.  Friendly owners and staff, free wifi, great relaxing atmosphere - try the ham and swiss croissant, it's excellent!

The best staff, the best coffee, the best pastries and food, the best atmosphere. Why go anywhere else? The Coffee Table is locally owned and operated- unlike the competition. When you come here, you can be confident that you are getting a fresh pastry, with NO PRESERVATIVES... baked the day you get it (maybe the day before), not frozen and good until the apocalypse. When you order your coffee- be confident it was roasted just a few days before, all of 7 miles away from the shop's front door. It wasn't roasted 6 months ago and vacuumed packed and sent half way across the country, already ground. The Coffee Table is quality at its finest, John and Melissa did their research- they are professionals and take great pride in all they do.
Competitive pricing and way better than Starbucks. Free wifi. Good relaxing environment.

You are the key to your success, and many of you that left these drastic negative comments most likely are not successful which explains why you are struggling to make ends meet.

Let's cut the bullshit, do you have passion for cooking?  Or, is it that you are looking for a genie to grant your every wish?

Face it!  Yes, you will have to start from the ground and work your way up.  That goes for majority of the professions out there.  And, that same rule goes for most college students graduating with degrees.  Unless you are Donald Trump's child - YOU AREN'T GETTING SHIT HANDED TO YOU.

Le Cordon Bleu LV tuition plus fees is about 17,000 for the entire program. If you are hands on, which I might guess most people who have in interest in cooking are, then this school is amazing.  You will have more than enough opportunites to whip up some amazing dishes. 

Besides covering the basics, fundmentals, and productivity, once you graduate you are welcomed to use any Le Cordon Bleu campus to take FREE refresher courses and utilize student services.

I find it funny how majority of you stated that as long as you can pay tuition they will let you in.  I bet you are some of the people that had to re-take the entrance exam.  

I found that when going through the interview process that Le Cordon Bleu asked me lots of questions about me and why it was that I wanted to attend the school.  Of course they would ask questions regarding how I was going to finance my education. DUH!!! 

During my interview process I discovered that my passion really wasn't for cooking but for business management.  And, it was their interview process and their rep that discovered there was no match for me and the program.

Even when I had the financial aid and payment plan taken care of, we just weren't a fit.

I have witnessed success from Le cordon bleu through my sister in law who I shared the program to.

For those of you enrolled - best of luck, and become your success story.  For those of you interested in the program - get an interview and take the tour it won't hurt getting the CORRECT info you need.  For those of you who have graduated - rock on and be proud that you committed and acheived.  If an employer cannot recognize that then they are not worth your labor.  And to the rest of you - quit bitching about a CHOICE U MADE.

I am a graduate of this school and I agree with Stephanie 100%! 

As long as you pay the tuition, YOU'RE ACCEPTED. During my job hunting adventures, most places that I applied to in Las Vegas during my schooling and even after I graduated, LAUGHED at the fact that I went to the LCB in Las Vegas. The NAME "Le Cordon Bleu" is world renowned, not the Las Vegas school. 

The school also fails to mention to you, after you graduate, you're not a "Chef" as soon as you graduate, qualifications are based on experience not the school you attended. Although, during your training, they make it seem as if the LCB name will open doors for you- HA! (Exactly what Chefs said when I told them I attended there! lol) 

As far as a comparison to CSN? The tuition there is a sOoOo much more affordable than the price that you pay at LCB and they cover, the same, if not more at CSN. Private schools want money. Most of the credits, if not all, are not transferable to another school. I tried transferring my credits to make a career change, since I was getting more laughs than praises regarding the LCB name in my current career choice, and the school told me most of the credits are NOT transferable... WTF?! 40 grand in tuition that I am still paying off and the credits are not worth diddlysquat at, of all places, a community college! 

And about the student body, they're all the same at any college that you go to, "World Renowned" or not. 

Now, the instructors, *SIGH*. There were a handful that are GREAT! Then, there are the rest of them that seem to hate their jobs or hate the students and there were also the perverted ones as well- EW! There was a particular incident that happened, not going to name names but there was a married couple that were baking & pastries instructors for part 1 & 2. For whatever reason, there was a misunderstanding with B&P1 Instructor and a few of my classmates... The instructor became so upset, stormed off, left the classroom and never returned. Well, this instructor went crying over to the B&P2 instructors class, the spouse's class... Because of the "drama" with the first instructor, the dirty looks we'd receive from the B&P2 instructor and to avoid any "issues" in B&P2, the school had to rearrange the schedules and provide us with another instructor for B&P2... It'd be a lot easier if I could put out the detailed information but I won't but it was quite hilarious, immature and unprofessional of the school and instructors to handle the situation like that. 

The ONLY good thing that I can say about the school, is that the campus is small which allowed for easy parking. Very convenient unlike CSN, other than that, my suggestion is to either attend another LCB in another city that has a better reputation or CSN... Especially for the amount of money that you pay for the classes.

I showed Medical Documentation for an excused absense. I completed the entire course except 2 weeks of back of the house restaraunt rotation. Purchased a travelzoo voucher for 2 people for $99 for a master chef cooking class (the title of this class is extremely deceiving). My friend and I of course waited until the very last Saturday before the voucher expired, so the class that we attended was "fall harvest" it was learning to can stuff basically. The class was scheduled from 10-1p and it started out with a tour of Le Cordon Bleu (probably could've skipped this, wasn't interested) then we were taken to a large kitchen where the students do the cooking for the restaurant and class. It was very clean, but freezing, definitely wear long sleeves and closed toe shoes. We were each handed 7 recipes cards, I was under the impression we all would get to make each one, but there was 7 people in the class, we were paired up and given one recipe, started out learning how to properly sterilize the mason jars. In the end, we each were given a jar that each team made, we were also given a apron to take home. Don't know if I'd go back before trying some other cooking schools in town. Mama will be so proud.

Total waste of a drive out here, but - oh - what a bullet that was dodged that day. My girlfriend expressed interest in going to this school to further her education as an aspiring chef, so we drove all the way out to this place in Summerlin from the Tropicana and Pecos area of town. The recruiter showed us around the place, and it LOOKED like a decent learning institute... then, this walking leather handbag with short white hair sat us down in her office. I started getting suspicious once she showed us that a two-year Associate's degree would cost over $40,000 (before the disgusting amount of interest would ultimately accrue, making it somewhere between $60,000-$80,000) and started making condescending remarks about my girlfriend's former employment as a baker at Glazier's in addition to my academic pursuits. Yeah, sorry the career I'm going for DOESN'T involve preying on naive kids and purging them into debt for years to come. 

Anyway, something did not feel right about this whole "prospect", so I went online on my phone while we were sitting there, saw the horror stories about Le Cordon Bleu Las Vegas not only on here, but on numerous other Web sites (Ripoff Report, being one of them). Then, I excused myself out of the office, instructed my girlfriend via text NOT to sign anything, and told her exactly why. From what she tells me (I was not in the room for this), when she informed the recruiter that she did not want to put anything in writing that day, her demeanor IMMEDIATELY changed and she got incredibly pushy. "Well, whaddaya mean you don't wanna sign anything today?! Don't you wanna start having a future already?!"  All doubt was promptly removed on what kind of place this truly was. The funniest part about all this is that on our way out, the recruiter lady looked like she was genuinely pissed off at me. Aw... sounds like someone's upset she didn't get her big fat commission.

Underneath the hollow promises, buzzwords, and presentation factor they try to "wow" potential applicants with, this is nothing more than a "for-profit" rip-off school. LCBLV has been on the receiving end of so many class-action law suits, it is outright shocking. College of Southern Nevada might not be the greatest learning institute, either, but at least they offer the SAME education (if not better) for a small fraction of the price, most of their credits actually transfer, and potential employers don't flat-out laugh in people's faces upon telling them they paid to go there. Honestly, I'm starting to think that most of these positive reviews are fake. That, or the people who posted them either don't know what they're in for yet or just don't want to believe they got swindled horribly. Also, I find it a little strange that entire pages worth of 1-star reviews ended up in the "Not Recommended" section. Just saying: It kind of makes me wonder...
it was a great program very good teachers great staff very personal i love it ! i found a great career by choosing LCB

The worst move I could have ever done. Now I am stuck with a school loan debt. When I got to Foundation 3 that's when I decided this whole thing was a joke. I am better off learning off you tube for free than to have a teacher who is not even into teaching. I have so many bad things to say about this so called college and to think I had many interventions but I didn't listen.. SMH!

I graduated in 2007 I have never once mentioned my school as a LOOK AT ME kind of thing. They help you get a job if and only IF YOU TRY!   Proving your worth is 100% of why you took classes. So if your washing dishes and the head chef says hey make me an omelet  you can and maybe even become a line cook from that. This school doesn't make you THE BEST CHEF IN THE WORLD.  YOU make you the best chef in the world. Tons of Chefs have been working in the industry for YEARS! and now you think that because of your achievement in learning the basics Makes you Better then them, YEAH they are going to laugh and throw it in your Face.  I don't know who told you that if you read about it then you are the Master at doing it.  I loved all my classes and Yes some of the Chefs were meaner then others but honestly if they saw you putting your heart into it they treated you decently.  They are not there to babysit you and hold your hand. You are an Adult!

Perhaps I'm a bit early in writing this review as I've only recently started here however I can already tell there are several things in previous reviews that SEVERELY differ from my current experience here and I felt the need to provide some feedback against them.

First of all, the loans/tuition/etc. The first day of the school year - orientation, the president of the school took about 20-30 minutes to talk to us. He had us examine the reasons as to why we were in the school and VERY emphatically told us to make sure this was exactly what we wanted because it was a huge amount of money to spend on something and that if we weren't sure, he encouraged us to rethink it before Monday when we started classes. When we started our classes that Monday, our Chef Instructor told us we had three days to decide we wanted this before we became financially responsible for the amount of the loans/tuition. He made sure we were aware we would NOT come out of this school as a "chef" and that we needed to work from the bottom and earn our way up the ladder whether we went to school or not. When Career Services talked to us during Orientation, that made sure that we knew there was NO guarantee of employment when we graduated, that they were not there to GET us a job but to HELP us find one. They told us what any grown, sane adult should know already - only we can get ourselves jobs, having a degree guarantees nothing in life. If you have a piece of paper that says you know how to do something but you're still unprofessional, unreliable don't interview well etc, you're not going to get hired, end of story. You have to be able to partner your own resources and capabilities WITH the degree to get employment. One additional thing - we've had several people from the school tell us about the scholarship opportunities the school offered and assistance with finding grants and other forms of aid we would NOT have to pay back. So hopefully that makes sense in regards to all the people who complained no one got them a job or said all the school wanted was our money.

Second - the school teaches us the terms, techniques and other basic material we all need to START a culinary career. Anyone who thinks attending 13 months of schooling will get them to executive chef levels of knowledge and capability is delusional. I have a friend who went to the CIA, one of the most prestigious culinary schools in the country, if not THE most prestigious - he's currently an Executive Chef but he didn't come out of school AS an EC, he started as a station cook and worked his way up through the kitchens. The best way to gain experience to supplement your education and make yourself more attractive to employers is to complete the volunteer events they provide us with to show we have experience with actual working kitchens, catering events, being able to take instruction from chefs, etc. 

I've been interested in cooking/baking/food for half my life and I've been wanting to go to culinary school for almost as long. I follow every food program out there, read hundreds of cookbooks, magazines, websites and blogs on cooking and baking. I have learned more in the first two weeks of school than I thought possible. My chef instructor is a graduate of LCB himself and knows what we need to do to make it afterwards. I'm sorry that people went into this with unrealistic expectations so I'm here to tell you that if you go in with the right attitude and you know exactly what you're gong to get when you come out, than you're really going to enjoy this experience. YES it's expensive however I'm not sure where people are getting 40k from, the program is $19,500 for the year. But if you want to invest in your future than 20k seems like a small price to pay if you start young and have a long career ahead of you. 

One more thing - I realize this school is in Las Vegas which is one of the culinary mecca's in the United States. Which is precisely why it is completely unrealistic to expect it would be EASY to get a job here right after graduating. Chefs who have been working all over the country (or the world even) come here to advance in their careers and if a restaurant on the Strip has the choice between someone who just graduated from ANY culinary school vs someone who graduated years ago and has been working in the industry for a few years, who do you think is getting hired? Which is precisely why when I graduate I plan on leaving to find a job. If I want to work in Vegas, I'll come back after a few years when I have more experience and more leverage.

I graduated from this school in '07 and it has proven to have been a grave mistake. They are preying on people's hopes and dreams. This school is FAR from selective, both in regards to student body and staff. You will only learn THE BARE MINIMUM there, and chef's laugh in your face and deny you an opportunity just hearing the schools name. I have accrued over $50k in debt, and could't afford to cook for a living to pay it back. Several other student I know including myself have had to resort to taking on completely different career paths just to pay for this mistake. This school is a gimmick, shame on them for taking advantage of  so many people!
Also, I know exactly who Joanne below is referring to. There has been drama in those baking classes since 2006....SMH.

I have to disagree with the other reviews.  I can see they were very unhappy because they were not sous chefs as soon as they graduated.  I am sorry but that is the same with any culinary school including the biggest ones (cia and johnson wales).  Culinary school teaches you the basics so when you graduate you have a better idea of what to do than other people who have no experience at all. YOU STILL HAVE TO WORK YOUR WAY UP THE LADDER LIKE EVERYONE ELSE!!! 

I graduated from LCB Las Vegas in 2005.  I had several years of experience before I went to school.  It was hard to advance to a sous chef before I went. After I graduated I became an Executive Chef in less than three years.

So take your sour grapes and make some WHINE!!

Fun times! Le Cordon Bleu classes are a great way to do something new around Vegas. Especially in the middle of the summer when you don't want to be outside.

There are a ton of different classes and workshops so you can find whatever interests you or something you want to learn more about. Besides cooking they have numerous technique courses such as knife skills, etc. 

What may turn people away (or prevent them from finding it in the first place) is their website. It is not very user friendly and rather difficult to find a straight forward listing of what classes are available. If your patient you'll eventually find it. Keep in mind that some 'limited time only' classes aren't shown but will only be displayed as you delve further into signing up.

Cost is also a factor since they're not cheap. But I will say you come away with a ton of food to take home! So weight that when you make your assessment. 

I went to the Hundred Foot Journey class which, like the movie, is a theme of French and Indian with some overlap (cardamom crème brulee). The instructors were friendly and helpful and gave good tips. The students who helped clean, set-up were great too. That class was overbooked sadly so we had to team up with a partner. Which was fine but you also end up with half the food you'd get on a few of the things.

Try it out!

I attended this school from '09-'10. From the start it was hectic to put it nicely. I visited the school and was taken on a tour. They gave me a list of the current curriculum and didn't let me know that it was going to change before I attended. I decided it was a decent school to go to and signed up. I was from out of town so I decided to go with the school's housong program. Instead of providing the single room I applied for and was promised in writing, they tried to put me in a shared room for more money. When I got my single room they raised rent yet again and no where near the agreed upon original rate. As for the school, they changed the curriculum's butchering class from a six week course to a 2 day stint somewhere in foundations 3. I should have demanded my money back right away but decided to stick it out. Despite many complaints from myself and other students, a certain student who constantly fell asleep and coughed into everything (after failing safety and sanitation several times) was allowed to remain in class and the school. He was also allowed to move on no matter what. Other filthy students,  who didn't know how to shower or wash their uniforms, were allowed to remain in classes. After an altercation with my restaurant intructor, he cornered me in the kitchen and threatened me while yelling two inches from my face, I was allowed to repeat the course  without the possibility of a new instructor because he was all they had for that course. The finance office was never there and when they were had no clue  how to do their job. The staff included chefs who admittedly hated their jobs and others that had only 2-3 years experience or none at all. Career services helped absolutely nobody and were rude to anyone who came in their office. Overall the experience was poor. I got most of what I could from a few chefs: Chef Bruce, Chef Labahn, and Chef Watson. They and a couple other chefs were the only chefs who cared enough about teaching t thehw correct ways of  preparing foods.

My favorite place throughtout my day. I love to come here and learn to cook the way my favorite chefs cook. Vast amounts of knowledge roam these halls under a chefs jacket and hat! If you love to cook savory or baking & pastry and you want to be the next hot shot chef, this is the place to come and learn!

My first review got filed under the "not recommend" section along with a dozen other 1-star reviews. Be sure to read those reviews and save yourself $40,000. My recruiter told me I had to sign up right then because it was the last class for the rest of the year. I enrolled and then found out they have a new class starting every 2 weeks! Very pushy for totally unnecessary schooling. Graduating from Le Cordon Bleu will not further your career. It does not impress restaurant chefs. In fact quite the opposite. I had a chef tell me they would not hire me (despite graduating with a 4.0 GPA and a letter of high recommendation from my instructor) because their experience with Cordon Bleu students has been negative. She said we were lacking in experience and self entitled because of our "degree." Waste of time and money. Save yourself. Please!!!

The staff here is great! And even though I haven't started classes yet, it might be a bit premature to say that I already think the most of it. Everyone there has been very helpful in directing me through this process. They made it easy for me to get my health card and my financial aid in order. And I'm so looking forward to orientation and uniform fitting. They are very straight forward and letting you know that jobs do not come along with the program. They just gives us the tools we need and I as the student are responsible for getting the work done in school and looking for work with their guidance. Of course I am older in age so I have experience in the work industry and knowing that no job just lands on your lap. It'll take work and if it's something a person is not willing to do, than this program is not for them. Only for the passionate culinary student like me..:)

Terrible customer service. 5 employees stood around joking while I waited to be helped.  Them fought in front of me about who had to help me. Awful!!! They obviously don't care about their customers. Never coming back.

Great pizza for a great price.   They have a wide menu, and everything is made to order right in front of you with fresh ingredients.   People are nice and friendly.   Unlike many pizza places,  everyone looks nice   Not all the tats and piercing.

I was contacted by the Owner the following day. She was extremely apologetic & expressed her corporate vendor concerns about the quality of lettuce. She asked for pictures to forward in order to get problem resolved. I am happy with outcome & will give this establishment another try.   
Original Post-We have been getting pizza from this place for quite a few years now but not sure we will be back. Tonite we decided to also try their Cobb Salad. What a horrible mistake. Before I took the lid off, it should have been a red flag - the Sell By Date had been changed or written over. The lettuce inside was mostly pink and limp. I thought it was just a couple pieces on top but, as I dug down it only got worse. The turkey meat was even slimy & discolored. The bacon bit pieces were mostly a flesh tone color.  
We are now concerned about the lack of quality ingredients & health precautions taken and  used for their pizzas. 
I called to make sure they remove any remaining salads that were for sale & to report the problem. I never asked to speak to a manager but was immediately told one wouldn't be available for 3-4 days and to call back then. 
There was my answer as to what's going on - This business is being run by minimum wage earning kids and without any supervision. 
Please be careful eating at one of these establishments. Young kids can only do the best they can. Shame on Management for expecting kids to run their business!

Tonight I went into this location with my father and we are absolutely appalled. As frequent customers, we were under the impression that we would walk in and get the exceptional service we usually do; this was not the case. Not only were we ignored by the two ill-tempered, eye rolling employees, we walked into a filthy unattended lobby. After repeating our order multiple times to the absent-minded cashier, she still managed to enter it incorrectly. Once our pizza was in the process of being made, my father had to stop the other employee to verify his order. After multiple scoffs and dirty looks, my father had to pay a separate time to fix their mistake. Instead of apologizing for the miscommunication, the cashier rolled her eyes once more and walked off annoyed. Now that our CORRECT pizza was finally being made, I noticed that the employee in charge of creating these "masterpieces" didn't change her gloves she used for condensing Cambros full of raw meats. Violating a direct Food Safety and Environmental Services law especially in front of customers is not only repulsive, but a rational reason for me, a former manager in the food industry, not to return.
This was the best customer service we've ever had any Papa Murphy's this will now be my new location.

This Best Buy is usually well stocked with helpful staff. One time I had been one day off on a warranty and they honored it in a roundabout way. It's always nice when customer service is of actual service. However, I did have issues with this Best Buy mobile location but eventually it was resolved. I find this location not as crazy as Yonge & Dundas nor the Warden location.

Worst customer service.  I was in the market for a TV however ONLY if it could be installed by the weekend.  Hassan looked in his computer, said there were no appointments available for installation in such a short time.   Thats fair so I said no prob thanks and was ready to walk away until he pulled out a magic phone that he used to call someone and he said "OK we can have it done by the weekend"  that should have been my first clue there was something wrong.  Long story short - no one showed up to install it and I had to go back to return everything.   Waste of time.   The worst part is he was there when i was returning everything and smiled and said "sorry it didn't work out"     Won't ever go back.

Store has amazing service. When returning a product you purchased, it is very simple to return the item. They will accept returns no questions asked.

In some areas, the store lacks knowledge. They don't know very much about Apple products or the musical instruments. Other than that, great service.

The location is great for Toronto- but the customer service needs improvement. I have been having countless issues with a laptop and brought it in today for a repair and the Geek Squad manager was quite rude to me. He did not seem to be on my side and kept questioning if I was being honest about my warranty policy and issues.  It was a bad experience. You would think that the employee would want to help you resolve and issue, not question if you're being honest. The Geek Squad manager is the reason I will not be returning to Best Buy at Leaside.

I went to this Best Buy store on three consecutive days. On the first day I went to buy a DVD/VCR. Not being able to hook it up effectively, I returned to the same Best Buy store on the next day. That day was a Saturday and it was extremely busy. I waited 20 minutes for "customer support" from a lady in the Home Theatre department. I told her that I hadn't been able to effectively connect the DVD/VCR properly and I felt I was missing a cable. I asked repeatedly if I needed another cable for the machine and showed her the DVD/VCR I had bought from the same store. Again the customer service lady said I didn't need a cable. I left without purchasing anything. The next day I asked someone to take a look at my connections. This person confirmed I needed another cable and told me which one I needed. I went back to the same Best Buy and found the cable on my own. Now I know mistakes happen, but I took huge photographs of the hookups for my cable box and television to the Best Buy store, in the hopes that having customer service see the current hook ups would get me correct information. That obviously didn't work. Also, the attitude of the customer service lady left a lot to be desired. For instance, I asked if she frequently got this question about this machine. She haughtily said no and that "most people" can figure it out by playing around with the cables. As a female I hate to say this, but avoid the short female in Home Theatre unless you are a technology pro.
Decent course. The small cookie cutter houses on the course are not what I want at a $70 a round course. I wont go out of my way to play here again.

One of the best courses on the south side. Always in great condition and never terribly crowded. Not the standard tree lined course for which northeast Ohio is known. Some dunes and tall grass separate the holes and can come in to play on several occasions. The greens are decent speed and the breaks are mostly as they look with a few exceptions. Not very steep or sloped but decent man made undulations considering the terrain they had to work with. 

The GPS on the carts work well but if you get near a green or tee expect total cart shutdown. The practice range is small but good for a warm up or to work on a fault post round. 

Holes 16-18 provide a fun and challenging finish and lead to a newly built clubhouse and grille which are pretty darn good; although I've only eaten here once. 

Top 4 public course in the area for me behind Boulder Creek, Fowlers Mill and The Quarry.
One of the best golf courses in Northeast Ohio.  More challenging than it looks, and very well maintained.

Sat at the bar and had some good drinks and delicious lasagna. Steve and Madison working the bar were awesome. We had great conversation and some good laughs. Steve makes an excellent watermelon martini (which Madison recommended) and he had good knowledge of the wine offerings. I will be back next time I am in town!

Wow. We decided to try Rush on a Saturday at 11am. So, when we arrived they did tell us that it would be 35 minutes for food, so we were prepared that it would be a little wait. Well, we waited nearly 50 minutes for food, which, by the way only included 2 poached eggs and 2 pieces of bacon that required actual cooking, my husband had a toasted bagel. While we were waiting an eternity for our food, with our 9 month old baby, someone doing maintenance in the ceiling actually asked if we could move so he could put his ladder where our table was. Um no. We cannot. Finally when our food arrived, my husband said to the server "wow, that took forever", to which the server responded "yeah, man." Now I know why they ask for tips up front. We won't be returning, obviously.

Can we say slo-mo expresso? Very slow service with staff members who don't listen well or ask enough questions. Also very limited pastry selection for 11 am on a Sunday. Latte was pretty but mostly foam.

First two shots at a Cuban with an Italian!  The Owner (Wife) made for me two different versions (two techniques) for a Cuban Espresso.

My description is that the flavor was more complex than most.  Unsweetened it grabbed my attention!  Sweetened I almost fell in love, which would have been easy to do with the crowd of cools in this place and the Espresso was real good too!  

It is still Italian ..."illy" is GONE... LavAzza is here now and I could not tell a difference because I did not drink enough "illy" before!

This place makes it look REAL Easy to get on my "Lookalota" list!  I have been here Late, Early and In Between - This place is NEVER amiss for who I'm talking about and talking to... Maybe my heart will Break... I'll RISK it!  With plenty of outdoor seating and a Cool Modern Interior, it is plenty Romantic and fun even if I'm alone!

My friend asked:  Who drinks Coffee at 9:00pm, and on Tuesday Night?  We were in this almost full shop at closing time!  Some places make it easier to fall in Love.

I have never written a review about a coffee "house" - but RUSH warrants them, and only the best. We happened upon RUSH after moving within walking distance in Ballyntyne. I'm very fussy about my coffee, and my husband and I agree their coffee drinks are just the best! Anderson who seems to manage the shop takes great pride in his work there as he gets to know customers and surprisingly remembers people's names (well, he remembered ours after one or two visits). The light fare served at breakfast and lunch is delicious. We're hooked on the Mocha Lattes - YUM!! Full coffee flavor and just a touch of chocolate sweetness (not one of those overdone iced coffee drinks loaded with all those unnecessary extras (aka, I'll pass on whipped cream & a cherry). Simply delicious, and fun to relax and people watch on their outdoor patio.

I have been to Rush several times and have given them many chances, but I am finally done giving them my business.  The staff here is the opposite of friendly and they couldn't care less about customer service.  Many different times I have ordered and paid for a certain size drink and received one size smaller "by accident". Then, when I mention the fact that the drink is the incorrect size, I am accused of being incorrect and the staff gets annoyed at me for having to fix the drink. Lets not forget that coffee here is not by any means cheap. I also very rarely get my latte made with any amount of foam on the top, which is a pretty common signature of a latte. Whenever I come in at busy times, I am rushed through the line in a way that makes me feel as though I am an inconvenience, and my drink is made in about 20 seconds (which is why it tastes awful). On another occasion, I hurried over to make it in time for happy hour (3-4) and paid for my drink at exactly 4:01, only to be told I missed happy hour. Talk about customer service! Overall, I am just not impressed with Rush in terms of the quality and taste of drinks, the attitudes of the workers, and the prices. There are way too many coffee shops around Charlotte for me to keep giving my money to Rush. This place is overrated. If you are looking for awesome coffee and a friendly vibe, check out Javas Brewing, Mugs Coffee, and Fabo Cafe!
Love this place for breakfast and some great coffee. Tonight we tried it for some wine and charcuterie which was good, not as great as it is for breakfast though, had some nice live music.

The lattes are great!  They have a really cute menu for breakfast and lunch and a ton of drink choices.  They even do that cute thing on lattes and make the foam into an image which I always love.  The people are really nice and the ambiance is like a real coffee house/cafe not like Starbucks.  They don't pressure you to leave or anything and there are plugs for you to use if you decide to do work there.  This place is great :)

Wow. Great atmosphere and so glad to see some bicycle memorabilia on the walls!!! First time here and will be back- staff super friendly and offered some recommendations. So glad to see a coffee house in Char-town. Will be back and can't wait to try the food!

Edited review because Rush continues to be AWESOME after becoming a quasi-regular there at the Ballantyne location.

The only downside is the wait on some days.  Every selection I have tried from the breakfast and lunch menu is tasty.

The coffee options remind me of a high-end Italian sidewalk cafe.  Worth the drive. Full-on five-star experience.

Rush Espresso is in the former "Dilworth Coffee" location in Ballantyne Village. They've given the space a more modern look since Dilworth Coffee moved out.

They give you the option of either having your coffee drink in a mug (if you're staying there to enjoy) or in the now traditional to all coffee purveyors, the cardboard cup. I personally enjoy being able to get my coffee in a mug since it seems a lot less common at most coffee shops.

In terms of the actual coffee, they use "illy" coffee and of the half dozen visits I've had to "Rush Espresso", the coffee has been great!

I'd definitely recommend them.
Ate here for breakfast twice this week while visiting from out of town. The yogurt crunch and light start were both excellent. Also tried a latte and a chai latte. Both were phenomenal.
Good food, great coffee, decent prices. Is becoming my "go to" local coffee joint. Laid back atmosphere. Sometimes it's a bit of a wait for food, but otherwise no complaints.

Are you fucking kidding me, Rush Expresso? This morning I fasted before my physical and decided to treat myself to breakfast here. I ordered a Egg and Avo Burger with bacon. I waited for 30 minutes before they realized that they never placed my order, and then, ten minutes later, I was handed a lukewarm lemony, watery mess. No bacon. No apologies.

I loved this place for their vanilla chai, but honestly, this was the worst customer service experience I've ever had. A 40 minute wait during morning rush hour for an incorrect order is completely unacceptable. I wish I could give negative ratings.

Rush Espresso is our new "go to" coffee hang in Ballantyne Village. Paul pulls a fantastic espresso, or any other drink you want to order. The atmosphere is modern and chic, and a cyclists dream hangout. In addition to coffee, their panini sandwiches are delicious, and the Australian Sticky Cake is to die for as a late night dessert. 

If you're tired of the suburban Starbucks and you wish you could get better coffee in a place with a more authentic, European feel, I highly recommend Rush. And if you walk by and see Paul back there making the drinks, you owe it to yourself to go in and try a latte. His are the absolute best you'll ever try!
Best coffee near the office. Their pastries are local and staff is friendly. Parking can be a pain but there's tons of space inside with the wine bar open

Basics first: coffee is good, speciality drinks are good, bakery items are GOOD (give the espresso muffin a try -- thank me later).  

Beyond the basics, I love this spot because the atmosphere is great. The staff is always upbeat and helpful, guests are all very polite and generally interacting.  What actually keeps me coming back beyond all that is how amazingly the environment is conducive to productivity.  Every time i go in there I plow through work that I have been putting off.   Caffeine + wifi + upbeat environment ...  adds up to something I can get into.

Chai Latte is the best item on this. 

The service is great and it's so nice to sit outside. Great place, friendly service. Had most of their teas, which I really enjoyed, but will particularly recommend Fruit de la Passion. 

Owner is very friendly and originally from Australia. 

Highly recommended. Great place.

Parking is very easy.

Asked for gf breads on all sandwiches. Got it on one. Person who took our order was very distracted during the order process. Our kid doesn't have celiacs, thankfully, so we said her sandwich was fine, but mine showed up with no bread at all. I said, there is no bread and she says, you said no bread. I said no feta, gluten free bread. She says I didn't ask for gf bread for mine or my child's in a very defensive way. She takes my plate and brings it back with the gf bread, not toasted and no pesto on it. Ok, I let it go, but 9 bucks for a lousy sandwich is, well, not worth it. We won't be back here. Anyone want my punch card?

I have now been here twice... Rush Espresso came very highly recommended and I now know why!! I came here on a Sunday morning and the girl working there was super nice and the coffee she made me was amazing!! Blows Starbuck's out of the water!! I could have drank 3 more rather than the 1 I limited myself to lol.  

I came back in a few days later after work. They do close at 6pm and it was probably around 530-540ish when I walked in . They had already closed the kitchen so I couldn't try anything there and the guy working didn't seem thrilled about having to make me a drink.  It definitely was not as good as my first one, and he forgot the Hazelnut that I asked for. It was still good but I was disappointed. I know it's because he was in a hurry and wanted to finish cleaning up so they could close up (even thought there were many people still sitting in the store). I will obviously be back again and hope to get the girl I had previously :-)  

All in all I recommend this place highly. Everyone raves about the food and the sweets that they have there and their coffee is a really great quality and tastes fantastic!!

I was pet sitting in Fort Mill and this was the closest option for coffee that wasn't a Starbucks. I go to the Uptown location almost every day since it's by my office, which means I knew I'd like their coffee. 

All that considered, it seemed an obvious choice to go here and boy am I glad I did. This location has a breakfast menu with very basic but unique choices. I got a panini with turkey bacon, egg, and Indian chutney. Yum! I also got an iced coffee for a change, vs hot. 

The service was really friendly and the vibe of the place seemed comfy and inviting. A nice little gem in Ballantyne, if you ask me.

I Wasn't too impressed with this place, the coffee here is great and so is the ambience.  The three stars are mostly for that.  We ordered a few things off the menu and unfortunately all of them were very dry.  Maybe I will come back and change the review after trying it again, very open space to get some work done.  It seem like they do have Live Music as well, we went in the afternoon.  Coffee is good, the wine collection looked good.  A place that can be tried again, but I would be very wary of ordering any food.

Not living or working in Ballantyne, I don't get by Rush often enough. But having been here a few times recently (twice in the last week alone!), I thought I should leave a glowing review.

Almond Chai Latte - get it! You won't be disappointed. I finally found another coffee shop that makes them exactly the way I like them.

I've been pleasantly surprised by the food options. The chef (can I call him that in a coffee house? I think he's earned the title) even stopped by my table to ask what I thought of the sundried tomato melt - I assured him it was delicious & proved it by ordering it the next time I visited.

For a local shop with stellar coffee & food, I think the prices are reasonable. 

Parking at Ballantyne Village continues to be a hassle through no fault of the store owners. (Google the drama about the former BV owner who kept the parking lots & won't allow customers to park there... ) Rush has been busy, so I'm very happy to see customers supporting the stores there.

If you're uptown, check out their new location in Latta Arcade. I haven't been by yet, but hope to trek a few city blocks from my office soon. I'm sure it will be worth it.

This place is weird. I do not feel comfortable eating here. I don't get the impression that food safety and cleanliness are priorities. The cashier who is always there is strange and covered with tattoos. She acts like the coffee shop is her own personal living room (notice I did not say kitchen) and that she prefers her own squad to visit her there. You can't call ahead to place to go orders (I've tried 4 times) because she/they always take their off the hook. 

Update:
The defensive response from Paul M. to my write up of my experiences at this coffee shop validates my opinion. He insults me rather than taking the opportunity to make improvements. I have given this place 4 chances and was let down each time. The first time the pastry I got was dried out, the second time the waitress got pissed because I asked her about a Nutella dish, and the last two I had to sit and wait because the phone was off the hook and I couldn't order in advance. So in short, the food, customer service, AND management are lacking. I have other options and will not give this place a FIFTH chance. I have been more than fair! Go kick rocks Paul M.

Still love it. Still a regular. But wanted to add that the food is AMAZING. I had the Power Rush the other day for breakfast. Delicious. Avocado, cheese, turkey. I actually might go get one today... Continuing my Rush love affair.

Me and my boyfriend dig this place! On an average, we go here 7 days a week, sometimes twice a day! In winter I was hooked onto their mint mocha. I also love the Fruit de la Passion tea that my boyfriend orders, which has a very pleasant Passion Fruit favor (I never order herbal teas at cafes myself, but steal my boyfriend's all the time).
I particularly love their chai though, Vanilla more than the Spiced. I always order them with 2% milk so they froth more. This place is just amazing! And it is a lot of fun to sit outside, watching the life at Ballantyne Village.
The servers as well as the owner are very sweet and friendly too!

Amazing little place. A place that I would dream to own! It's coffee place and wine bar. I've been only getting ice coffee from here because it's been so hot but last night I had a chance to order a hot caramel latte. My husband had a slice of cheesecake that was good. Our friends said they have great breakfast. We have yet to try but can't wait to go!

Love this place!  Great stop for a coffee, breakfast or lunch. Parking is getting better but still a little tough. Food, service and quality makes this a must stop if you live and work in the area. The sandwiches have a great taste and creative flair.

We came in for late breakfast on a Saturday. I had pouched eggs on wheat toast with a side of fruit and my wife had muesli with vanilla yogurt and fruit.
Both were well presented, fresh and tasty.
The service is friendly and our cappuccinos were excellent as well. 
I'd recommend this place.

Rush Espresso is fantastic! Love to support locally-owned, non-chain businesses so was very happy to discover this place. The front patio is lovely and the atmosphere is relaxed and casual. I ordered the sausage and tomato frittata and it was amazing... not to mention the out-of-this -world hash browns! They have the best spiced chai in the area and cinnamon rolls are to. die. for. I'm not a coffee drinker but my friend raves about the lattes and espresso. The staff is super nice, helpful and friendly.

Rush espresso never fails to serve wonderful coffee and amazing food. The delicious cappuccinos always make my day. My real complaint is that they have a small, ugly, and uncomfortable restroom. At a coffee venue you should be able expect a pleasant restroom to use after your morning coffee. I might also add that the fake plants should be replace with real plants to add to the over all decor of the new location.
Ordered a chai latte based off some reviews and holy. smokes! It was delicious!! It's pricier than some coffee places but I would gladly pay $5 for that bomb drink again

Rush Espresso is a great place tucked into the Ballantyne Village. I feel like I'm in another great coffee house in Seattle. They serve such well made and exquisite coffee and tea. You can tell they take pride in what they do. This is the best coffee I've had in Charlotte.

So... Maybe I just got the wrong thing? But I got a salad, a large, with chicken. It was $10.75. It's roughly the size of a side salad from Harris-Teeter which would run me about $4.50. It's also got gross brown lettuce in it, so I've got that to look forward to. Plus, the sign out front that says $5 Express Lunch should probably be taken down since there is no such thing as a $5 express lunch. The only thing on the lunch menu that's $5 is a side salad, which I'm guessing would be maybe a cup of greens and a tomato? Not gonna lie, I'm crazy disappointed in this. Maybe their other stuff is better.

Best coffee, atmosphere, service, and value for coffee in South Charlotte. Go for happy hour while they still have it. Tables are not super-comfy like in Panera, but that's the point! Sleek, trendy... You'll forget you are in Suburbia within minutes.

Great cappuccino! Quality coffee with expert execution. Takes me back to traveling in Italy. Amazing that the owner is Australian?????  but he obviously knows how to make great coffee beverages. Hope they expand to many locations in Charlotte.

We came for a little birthday party on Friday night with some friends what a pleasant surprise!!
Live music from Scoot was excellent.  Very up beat and fresh feeling over all.   Food was great! Ordered Pimento cheese assortment (With Bacon was my fav!!) and guacamole was excellent too. Others at our table had pasta, risotto a huge cheese tray and everyone raved how good it was! The wine list was great. I thought liquor prices were very reasonable. Staff was on it!! We did not wait for anything! I would highly recommend this place for a fun night out!! Or even a date night. I can't wait to go back!! Thanks Rush

This place is a nice alternative to big box coffee shops like Starbucks or Caribou. They do offer ample table seating with Wifi.

In the evenings they do offer live entertainment, typically a small band or guitarist. The coffee offerings are what you would expect.

It's rare that I ever desire to review a place. It's additionally rare that remember to actually complete the review two months later.

It's safe to say that my first impression two months ago was impactful.

I had the Australian pie and goat cheese, potato and onion tart. The seasons and flavor... perfect.  There are lots of options (but not to overwhelming) and the servers are friendly and helpful if you can't decide. 

The only thing they leave you wanting at the end of your visit is a location right down the street from you. 

Needless to say my best suggestion would to open a location in Mooresville or Huntersville/Cornelius. 

Keep up the good work.

This place is adorable. I am a coffee addict and especially love a good locally owned shop. I came in here early before class to grab a quick study session. There are probably ten to twelve tables but they do have a wonderful outdoor seating area that is a pretty decent size. 

They have great food and coffee (duh!)  I came in and had the power bagel. I think it was called that. Anyways it had ham, Swiss, avavado, tomato, spinach, an cream cheese. What a great way to start the morning! I have had coffee wise two different drinks. The vanilla latte which was so amazing. They serve their coffee drinks in clear glass glasses and do a beautiful little design on top of the foam. I have also had the chai tea latte. I found the chai tea to be a little more sweet than I typically like it so I didn't finish it. They have a choice of vanilla spice or regular spice and maybe I had the vanilla. The location is great and seems to be convenient to everything!! Love this place and look forward to trying every drink they offer!

Went here for the first time this weekend after driving by. Very clean and the employees were nice. You order inside and they serve you, if you're dining in. We sat on their patio due to the nice weather. The coffee was rich and bold, and the first refill was free. The breakfast was delicious and the servings were large for what you pay. I got  eggs Benedict and fiancé got some sort of breakfast croissant sandwich. We both enjoyed our meals and coffee for $20.
Service is beyond the charts and the coffee is great too!!!  I have never been to a coffee shop like this where they actually come over and ask you if you liked your drink!  WOW, will be back often!!
Honestly service was a little uncomfortable at first.. but please order the Vanilla Spiced Chai, literally heaven. If you order it around 3-4 you get it half off and it is super cheap and amazing.

Fav place for an espresso. I'm almost hesitant to review it because I feel like it's a hidden gem and I do t want the masses to figure it out! 

The large party room they have is super weird though. It feels like you're in an entirely different place and it's so empty when you talk it just echoes really loudly and it's awkward.

I love Rush Espresso.  When I came back to Charlotte after being gone for a year, I was very happy to see the business still open and seemingly doing quite well.  I visited the establishment every day while I was in town and the espresso drinks and breakfast was on par with just how I remembered it.  

If I had one criticism of the espresso drinks at all it would be that the lattes really lack a discerning espresso flavor.  I really like a nice balance of sweet and espresso, and I detect more of a cream and sweet flavor when I drink my latte from Rush.  Maybe it's the barista making the drink, or perhaps it just the type of espresso used in the drink, but nonetheless, it's my two cents.  Having lodged this criticism, what I will say is that the flavor is consistent...  So they do have that going for them.  

I would encourage everyone to support this coffee bar.  The owner is doing a hell of a job and I want it to stay around for my future visits to Charlotte.
There is not a better coffee place in Charlotte...quality and service is impeccable.  Just wish there was one in the Promenade.

Rush Espresso! Che bouno!
 
Love that they use Lavazza. My Café Latte was so delicious, smooth and creamy. Sorry Starbucks but this was awesome. Great house blend too!
 
When I ordered an éclair and apple turnover, I did not expect them on a plate with syrup drizzled and puffs of whipped cream = nice presentation. Great! The pastries were so good though, they could have easily stood on their own. 

 Looks like they have a full breakfast and lunch menu. Would have been a five star visit but service was less than friendly; the cashier barely interacted and seemed either sleepy or like he wanted to be somewhere else. The products here are excellent though.

Went here for a cup of coffee after reading rave reviews on Yelp and I was not disappointed in the slightest. I love espresso and Rush's was the best Americano I think I've ever had. I liked the decor and searing options. The padded benches and low picnic tables are definitely great for a group of friends though. Maybe a board game or two?

 I'm only in Charlotte for another month but I'll definitely be back.
I've never been more impressed with an owner of a business. It shows! Amazing service - perfect lattes - food is prepared with excellence!

Went here looking for a place to get a coffee, some breakfast, and work for a couple of hours. Started off with a cappuccino and the "Power Rush", which is a bagel w/ham, avocado, and...other stuff I can't recall. Very happy with both orders. Ended up working a few hours, and having a cup of the green/mint tea, also good. Friendly staff, good seating, good vibe.
My favorite coffee shop in town.  Great cappuccinos, great atmosphere.
I love good Italian coffee and it's done well here. The owner is really nice and remembers your order fairly quickly which makes for great service!

Rude owner! When I went in I sat at wine bar and it was my first time there. I waited ave waited but nobody came over to greet me! I finally walked over to the coffee area and ordered. Won't be back 
Overpriced and just not that great!
Great Coffee and fresh wonderfully prepared food. The new wine bar addition is alot of fun, with a casual but upscale neighborhood vibe, especially on music nights.

I thoroughly enjoyed my first visit to Rush, and I'm sure it won't be my last. With Adam R's affinity (addiction?) to coffee and that fact that he now works in the area, I imagine I'll be returning.

With Charlotte awash in restaurants and coffee shops that revel in their French coffees, a place that specializes in Italian coffees is a fresh change. While Rush very clearly advertises that they use Illy coffees and machines (a well-established provider of Italian coffees and espresso machines), they are still a locally owned, private business - don't let the branding fool you, it's an original.

The coffee is pretty dang awesome. It's light and has just the right touch of bitterness. You can see the owners' little hints of their native Australia mixed into the menu - all of which seems like a pretty good value and branches out beyond just the traditional baked sweets. The names of the menu items are straight-forward and very easy to order.

The interior is very sleek and trendy-modern with lots of stainless steel and bold colors. The patio is spacious with at least as many tables outside as inside.  Can't wait to try them again!

Friendly, intimate feel and service! Great choices of beverages and food. Only drawback was that they didn't get my order right. Though, I appreciate the quality of ingredients and products. For a quick stop it would be my second choice to Dean & DeLuca.
Wish I knew this place was closing.  Rode up. No longer there. And I was just here Sunday.

There are a number of good things about this place but my last visit left a bad taste in my mouth. The drinks are good but decidedly small. Although the menu says the size of a large drink is 16 oz the actual size is actually probably half that if you get it "for here". The "to go" sizes are closer to the menu but still don't match. Make sure you look at the sample cup/glass sizes in front of the register, rather than the menu, to tell what you're getting. Had the barista acknowledged this when I asked about the discrepancy, I'd probably feel better about my experience right now. But he didn't ... Nonetheless, I'll probably return here at some point because it's one of the few coffee houses in the area that isn't Starbucks. I'll just be more strategic in my approach to ordering!

When Dilworth Coffee closed and Rush opened, I admit, I was a little turned off.  I spent almost every day working from there, hosting meeings and chatting with their staff. After giving Rush a fair chance, I was very pleasantly surprised.  The spot got a complete makeover and is now a European, trendy vibe.  The layout is much more conducive to meetings and getting together with friends and the seating is comfortable and stylish.  I would say that Rush is a little pricier but the quality of the food and coffee is definitely worth it.  I'm very glad to see a locally owned coffee shop again rise in Ballantyne!  Paul, the owner, is incredible - Such a personality and is truly grateful for his customers.  He may be running in and out but he always takes a moment to say hello to his customers and thank them for their business.  I give it 4 stars because the barista's are not as friendly.  I'm notorious for going into a new place and asking what servers, barista's etc., suggest and at Rush, I sometimes get a strange look for doing so. I have had wrong orders delivered a few times. I think those are kinks that will work themselves out but all in all, I'm a proud regular!

Hi, I have reviewed this cute space before. However, now that I am a regular, I wanted to give some credit to the employees there. Many times we are quick to review poor experiences and not the good ones. There will be both because we are not robots and you can not be "on" every single time you work. With that said, I noticed a fella with a beard and silly mustache, maybe his name is Alex, always bustin his buns. He is always professional, attentive and pleasant. There is also another fella with a hipster bun, don't hold that against him, who does a great job as well. I would love to say the same for the females but they seem to what to spend their time giggling and pretending not to see customers.  Overall, this place is good and I enjoy when I am helped by either of the gentlemen there. Its hard to fine good workers and honest people, so when you do, hold on!

Awesome place. I like a good coffee and starbucks is not the place to get one. I was recently visiting Charlotte and stopped in to have a coffee and use the WiFi to plan my day. The vibe is great here! The staff is pleasant and friendly in a great way. Everybody new my name within minutes and that was something they practiced with everybody that came in. The Music is hip and cool but not blaring and distracting. They have a great food menu too. Had I known I would have had breakfast here, Most important my medium decaf late was delicious. Big props and I highly recommend this place.

This place has delicious coffee.  Their cappuccinos and lattes are perfect I would recommend ordering a large so because the mediums are kind of small.  The owner is from Australia and he seems to be very dedicated to his business

This place is a hidden gem, I love it!!!

The coffee is second to none, and the hollandaise sauce they serve on their eggs Benedict is the best I've ever had in the whole of America... 

All the staff are super friendly, and the owner is a ripper bloke, top notch in my books, you won't be disappointed!!!
Very nice atmosphere, friendly service. Good place for a chat with friends or your significant other.

There is no better place to be in Ballantyne on Wednesday night than Rush. They have a great list of wine/beer selection that pairs with the cheese/meat board. All the while with live performance in the background as you sip and snack. Do get a cheese board, and they don't skimp out in giving the cheese or other pairings!

If you want a full dinner, they have the option as well - amazing short rib sliders, burgers, tacos, and crab cakes that will easily fill you up. 

Don't skip out on the dessert either - the molten chocolate cake is cooked to perfection - warm and moist that balances awesome with ice cream.
Great coffee, very busy but cashier seem to keep things moving alone very quickly with a smile

Rush is my go-to coffee spot when I'm at the office and can get away for a little while. When you walk in, you immediately notice the modern, European aesthetic: lots of sleek black and metal accented by splashes of red. Most coffee shops tend toward the cozy, which is not a bad thing, but Rush's approach is welcome.

Fortunately, the coffee is high-quality as well (and also European). I have to admit, I didn't really care for the brew when they were serving Illy, but LaVazza is a much better label according to my taste buds. 

Two more things I appreciate about Rush: the loyalty punch-cards and the fact that the owner remembers my name, even though I am sure he has customers who are much more frequent visitors than I.

If you're in Ballantyne, Rush should be high on your list of coffee options.

I was visiting from out of town and couldn't believe my luck to find a coffee shop that has not only good coffee but almond milk! Add to this amazing find, they also had gluten free bread. I swear I died and went to heaven. I visited often while in town and found the staff friendly and helpful and loved hanging out here.

I always enjoy having coffee when it's not from the green lady people and Rush does an excellent double espresso. Just as good? The lemon cheese pastry with a side of sweetened cream cheese. Delicious!

I sat here at Rush for about an hour and used a good amount of their wifi while drinking my coffee and eating that pastry. Mostly decent music played and there were several interesting conversations going on that kept me entertained.

Cold morning, so the outside seats weren't occupied and there were still a couple of two-tops available inside. I liked this place!

I have been a regular here during the week since August and would never go anywhere else for my morning coffee. Their latte is second to none. The atmosphere is very inviting and clean. Paul, the owner, is one of the friendliest people I've met and he is often the one making your coffee. If you make it for breakfast, I recommend the breakfast panini, it's a favorite of mine and my girlfriends.
One of the best place for good coffee. The price are reasonable, and very friendly staff. The owner very good guy. Best time to go at Tour de France...

Looking for a traditional European Cafe complete with the accent then stop by rush espresso located in Ballentyne.The shop has a cycling theme and gasp the Tour De France was playing on the tv. I almost fell over at the mere sight. Not common in Charlotte trust me. This place won me over the minute I stepped in the door. Not the mention the Aussie accent when the coffee is served. Now on the the more important things yes the coffee. This is the best place so far I have been to for coffee. The cold press is smooth and non-bitter as iced coffee should be and the hot coffee is perfectly prepared. I should mention happy hour is from 2 PM to 4 PM where you can get the Java jolt of your choice for half price! That gives me an excuse to sneak out of work and head over to Rush for a quick afternoon break. I have not sampled the foodies but I can say the coffee is awesome. I am a coffee snob and none of the shops I have been to have stacked up to this place. As far as the atmosphere goes the servers are pleasant and you get the periodic how is everything are you satisfied Mate? There is a modern decor similar to some of the shops I have frequented in Europe. I just wish they had those little Italian pastries to complete the package. The only downfall I can see is that they are located in Ballentyne and not close to where I live bummer. Otherwise I would become a permanent fixture similar to the time trial bike hanging in the shop! Oh well guess I can't have good coffee and a close location to where I live. Sigh...

Stopped in for a mid afternoon pick me up on our travels. We tried the caramel frappe and the iced coffee. Loved the smoothness of the coffee. Not bitter and not watered down by the ice. Definitely a step above Starbucks if we had to choose.

This is my first review so here goes. I really love this place. The prices are reasonable, and every drink and food item I have had has been amazing. (Iced coffee and pancakes during breakfast are my favorite.) You can order to go if on a time schedule but stick around if you can. 

The service is wonderful and the staff is friendly. The owner, Paul, converses with the customers and will also be the first to get behind the counter and help when it gets extra busy, which I admire as not all owners will get their hands dirty, so to speak. 

There is outdoor seating available and I enjoy sitting outside as well as inside. There is a wide variety of foods to choose from and I have yet to try all the things that look good. Whether you want a meal or pastry with your coffee (or smoothie) they have you covered. 

I also really love that it is a local place. The atmosphere is very modern yet cozy and not too loud. There are plug ins scattered around for those who want to get some work done on a laptop or tablet. I always feel like I belong there and I love the experiences I have had, so definitely give it a try!

After a Friday dinner elsewhere, my wife and I developed a yen for a latte and immediately knew where to go... Rush Espresso! They have a newer, more expansive location and it is quite an improvement over it's old tiny space. One thing that hasn't changed however is their great lattes.

The place was packed with diners and those there for the live entertainment. It was a festive and enjoyable environment. Will definitely be back.

I've come here a couple of times and every time is a joy, everyone is so nice their place and drinks are perfect specially on this cold weather. If you are not trying to spend too much money then definitely come here. It is a place you can come with friends to catch up and have a great talk.

Great coffee but often out of chai lattes which is my daughter's favorite. They've been out of it the past 3 of 4 visits. We do love the location and quality of coffee, as well as the shopping/spending local aspect so we'll continue to go but do wish they'd beef up their supply of chai because after leaving I still need to take her to Starbucks it's the her only drink of choice

Update: after the owner personally reaching out, I am so impressed that I am updating my review. The coffee here is delicious and our only request was that they hopefully increase their stock of chai. Personally responding to a concern is a great example of why we love to visit local businesses. Also to clarify, our visit occurred a few weeks ago and point taken that I should have been more specific. Thank you for caring about your customers' experience!

I love this place! Stopped going to Starbucks after I found out about this place.
Also the happy hour rates, everything for half. You can't beat that. I think the timings are 2:00pm to 5:00pm.

Their new location is a lot roomier with lots of seating options both indoor and outdoor. 
I ordered the breakfast guacamole benedict and a cappuccino. The benedict was pretty tasty - there are 2 poached eggs on top of guacamole and spinach on sourdough with baby tomatoes on the side. The best part is when you break the egg and you soak up the yolk that runs down the side with the bread. It's definitely pricey for the portion ($12) but it's a good option for a healthy, light breakfast.
They bring your food out to you but they call your name once they make your coffee and you have to go to the counter and get it. Coffee tastes similar to what you would get in Europe, but sizes are smaller also.

I went up the road to have breakfast and coffee at Rush Espresso. I've been to plenty of coffee shops/breakfast cafe's and this was by far the most friendliest place. You wouldn't think a place located in Corporate park would be so friendly and comfortable, but it was. The owner pulled a chair from our table, sat down, and began to chat with us. He wanted to know where we were from, what brought us to Charlotte, and all about our coffee/breakfast habits. It was really refreshing to see an owner of a coffee shop so engaged in his costumers, involved in the kitchen, and outgoing. I thought that was really classy.

I'm not only coming back because the owner was so nice, but the food was really good, too. Plus it was super cheap. I ordered their low fat yogurt granola & berry parfait.

My roommate and I split their ham and cheese croissant. It was melt in your mouth heavenly! 

I also ordered a latte on the side and it was so good. They make their low fat milk so smooth and frothy. The espresso was strong and smooth!

There is a glint of hope for south Charlotte! A non-chain coffee shop! We're saved! 

This place has great ownership. I've met them before, but can't remember their names. Pretty sure one guy is from Australia and boy is he friendly!

This place serves some high-end product. They recently switched from only selling blends from illy coffee (one of my favorites of the commercial world) to a more recent brand called LavAzza. Pretty good stuff. 

On occasion, I've even seen a bit of latte art come out of Rush! Not sure who the baristas are, but some of them can actually make you something special. Nice to see in yuppyville. 

It's so nice to see some baristas who can actually tamp, pull and pour a decent espresso in south Charlotte. These places are few and far between from Ballantyne to Uptown. Definitely worth asking for something daring, folks. Step away from your cozy and boring triple shot, venti frappucino. Or whatever. This place knows how to make you a cafe latte. 

Definitely worth venturing and trying some of their teas as well. They carry a great brand of bright and flavorful teas to choose from. 

The vibe inside is a little pretentious but that's a bit expected. It's a little too clean and overrun with non-hipsters. Can't be too choosy, though. It is Ballantyne after all. 

If you're in the Ballantyne area, support this local business rather than one of the larger chains. Definitely worth the coin and much more love goes into their beverages. 

Get to know the owners as well! They have great stories.
