The last dish my wife and I shared was shrimp and scallops which came in a small casserole dish.  The scallops and shrimp  dish was okay, beside being made with cheap small seafood.  Overall a very disappointing experience.

Quite simply the most tender and well cooked Chicken Parm I have ever had. My wife had the Gnocchi and loved it as well.  Bread was delicious as well. Server said it was a garlic crusted and we couldn't stop eating it. No room for dessert even though it looked delicious. Server (Austin) was very attentive the entire time

This place has amazing food! I would highly suggest the pizza or pasta. I would recommend their salads as well. Their meatballs are HUGE. This place has true Italian and their presentation is perfect! Everyone needs to come eat here! PS: Sorry for the seemingly empty pictures, went late at night on a Thursday.

I got the warm mozzarella appetizer and the mushroom pasta dish... Not very good.

The mozzarella appetizer was good for the price but i would have to say that my pasta with mushroom and truffle oil was gagtastic. I seriously do not know why it tasted that way, but it got me nauseous and was extremely watery!

Probably never coming here again.... sorry!
Ordered pizza and ceasar salad. The lettuce was old and the Pizza was awful. Reminded me of middle school cafeteria pizza. Get it together Osteria....

I guess the best way I can describe this place is underwhelming. My dad had the margherita pizza and he said it was good. I had the Chicken Parmesan and was disappointed in the portion. It was one hockey puck sized piece of chicken and a cup of spaghetti. The pasta though was fresh and delicious--the best part of my meal. 

It's an industrial looking space--concrete floors and exposed duct work; it makes for a very noisy atmosphere. It was hard to have a conversation across the table.

On a pleasant evening, the outdoor seating is great, because the street next to it gets almost no traffic. The service was friendly, and the red wines were mostly blends, but were tasty and affordable. The gnocchi was pretty good, as was the ricciolina. A little on the al dente side, but tasty nonetheless. One thing I was pleased by--the portion size was actually reasonable! Not gigantic. A cute place we'll try again.

Out and about in the Strip District, and we decided to have a late lunch/early dinner at Osteria. Due to the non-peak time, we were the only ones in the restaurant and chose to sit at the bar. 

The bartender was very nice, though not up to speed on the beer info. The samples, however, were very healthy. 

We ordered the meatball and a pizza (1/2 pepperoni, 1/2 mushroom. The meatball had a kick to it, and we appreciated the real Parmesan! The pizza was overloaded with cheese, so I ordered a side of sauce to go with. The sauce was super bright, but it was needed to balance out the amount of cheese on the pie. 

After our meal, I asked for a taste of their homemade chocolate brownie ice cream. Thanks to the bartender for the healthy sample of that, too :)

I don't think we'll be back to this place, as other locations for dining in Pittsburgh have wowed us a bit more.

I don't quite get the ambience here -- it's part dive, part nouveau chic, part "authentic" Italian.  

No big deal there, but I have a concern about the menu, which has cheese weaved into nearly every dish.  This is not a practice you find in Italy.  It's an American, and especially a Pittsburgh thing.  Enough with the cheese avalanche.

Still, I was able to find one salad and one entrée without.  Both were really, really good.  The sign of an artistic chef.  I just wished I'd had some choice.

I read some reviews here complaining about the portions.  These are normal sized portions, and very typical of real Italian food.  This is about quality, not quantity, and the problem is with 95% of other establishments that seem to think it's the other way around.

Ehhh....I'm gonna give them a 3, a high 3, since I felt the entrees Kay and I ordered were too flawed to warrant a stronger rating. We came here prior to the Dio Disciples show at Altar Bar the other night (Hey, Ronnie Dio was Italian after all), and being that it had truffle oil in it, I just had to sample the Riccolina, truffle oil being something I'd been dying to try for many years. 

Fede pasta is a peculiar, long, fat macaroni that is solid instead of hollow inside. In this instance, it was al dente but had no flavor, the truffle oil failing to permeate the pasta. The arugala, however, absorbed it beautifully. 

What does truffle oil taste like? I'd describe it as a really robust olive oil. It's wild like an aphrodisiac or something taken from the pheremonal gland of a fantastical creature. I.E. I enjoyed it but realize that it either attracts or repels. Back to the dish itself...

The broth that collected at the bottom, something which also carried the truffle oil flavor fairly well, made me wonder if this was supposed to be a pasta dish or a soup. The caramelized mushroom chunks merely loitered. 

Not that the Riccolina was terrible, it's just that the truffle oil and arugala were the only things going for it. In fact, it was so lacking in flavor, I did something I rarely do at a restaurant since I feel it should be done before service; I used a salt shaker. 

My salad and dessert, on the other hand, both saved the evening, sort of. 

Wouldn't you know I ordered the Tomato and Mozzarella salad also? And wouldn't you know that it was a winner? The fresh mozzarella discs should be given out for Holy Communion as they were seraphic, delicate, "lighter than air" like the wizard in the Dio-era Rainbow song "Stargazer"...

 http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AIdxjegXKSw

The cubed tomatoes were fresh from a garden tended by a careful farmer as they were ideally ripe, juicy, berry-sweet, and dressed with a supradelectable house vinaigrette.

Each of our desserts were quality homemade creations. Kay had an individual coconut cream pie that was a flaky basket of custardy, whipped-up delight. My post-meal treat was a rich Cookies And Cream cake that held an Oreo cream filling and was topped with a fab, fudgy ganache, making it the most luxurious lunchbox pastry ever created.

Kay wasn't crazy about her Rigatoni, and after tasting the dishwater sauce, it was easy to see (taste?) why. Although, the sausage that wallowed in that sauce had a tenderness and savoriness that was beyond belief. 

The complimentary bread was also noteworthy as it came with a spice-infused olive oil for the bread to soak up famously.

Alyssa, our server, was attentive and polite. The decor was akin to a modern, swanky deli, and overall, the atmosphere was quiet, especially for the teeming Strip District. 

P.S. I came very close to ordering a sandwich.

P.P.S. My dinner, aside from sampling the meat in Kay's dish, was unwittingly vegetarian. Good on me.

P.P.P.S. I finally got to review #666! This is cause for celebration!

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eML6X8VfAfY

Opted to try the pizza take-out option at Osteria 2350 and loved it!  12" hand tossed pizzas with the perfect ratio of cheese to sauce.  The dough is crisp but not overly done.  I added arugula, ricotta and prosciutto to my pie and each ingredient was fresh and delicious.  As strip district resident these pizzas are worth the walk (or drive) two blocks for the freshness of this pizza.  Can't wait to return and try out the full menu in the dining room!

The prices are great, $5 house wines, $12 large pizzas, and the food is good.  I had the lobster salad and my sister had the caesar.  The caesar was delicious and the lobster salad had a ton of lobster on it for $7, but tasted like straight white vinegar.  Overpowered the lobster and the greens it was over.  We also all shared the meatball side and it was okay, but was only ground beef and i like my meatballs mixed with other meats.  Our pizza took about 30 minutes to come out, we ordered a white pizza, which was delicious, but the chef came out and explained that the first one came out terrible so he was making us a new one, he took it off our bill, so that was nice.  The crust was amazing, I don't typically eat pizza crust, but I forewent the bread and dipped the crust in the delicious garlic oil that came out prior to the pizza with the bread basket.  All in all its a great atmosphere, great prices, and I will definitely go back to try the pastas and other dishes.  Our server was great too!

I wouldn't call myself a "yelper" as I don't normally feel the need to go out of my way to post a review about a place either good or bad. However, something about this place "irked" me enough to do so. I have been to this place now twice, and both times the service was not only unfriendly but I would say rude as well. The first time I was there, I was the only customer in the place after the lunch rush, and the server/cashier was annoyed and not helpful whatsoever about the menu. I had never been there before, so I asked a few simple questions and it was like I was bothering her. The second time I was there- same experience except this was a different server (male). When you walk in the place there is no direction as to whether you seat yourself, etc- being that there is a large order counter, one would assume you order there and sit down like a Panera, so that is very unclear. I intended to sit there and eat my meal there, however per the confusion my food was made to go, and i just took it and left rather than make a stink about it. Lastly, I would say the food is very lackluster and overpriced. I had the Chicken Salad Sandwich the first time, which was just OK. I order the gnocchi on my second visit and it basically had no flavor. It could be a good spot, the ambience is kind of cool, but between the service and mediocre food, I'll take a pass.
Decent food, great atmosphere, wish there is a train passing by the railroad outside the place ;) That would be more fun.
Fantastic! Wonderful food, reasonable price (10-15), quick service, great decor and pleasant staff!

Osteria isn't high end or innovative, nor does it pretend to be.  What you do get is reasonably good homemade pasta at a reasonably good price.  The atmosphere is kind of industrial cafeteria, so not the place you want to go for a romantic dinner.  If you want higher end Italian in a more intimate atmosphere with a better wine list there are other options in town (Dish, Jos Tambellini, Stagioni).  There are also a ton of run of the mill mom and pop pasta joints that have a loyal, older following and serve ridiculously large portions - Osteria is certainly a cut above these.  You just have to go in with the right expectations.

This is the third time I have eaten at Osteria 2350.  Located next to Cioppino in the Strip District.  A parking garage is handy since on street parking is rare to find.  The tables are not squeezed together which makes conversation less intrusive.  Our service is timely, pleasant and not overly hovering.  The menu is not large but offers appetizers, salads, sandwiches and entree.  I enjoyed greatly the asparagus, arugula salad.  The asparagus was cooked perfectly, and dressing just right lemony and parmesan.    Hands down the beans and greens are THE BEST, in town.  Abundant beans cooked to a nice al dente texture, generous greens in a delicious garlic sauce.  This place is a winner.

Interested to find out that Osteria is owned by Cioppino (right next door).  But the service and food are inconsistent.  I like the prices here, the food is rather inexpensive, so you get a lot for your money.  We had a large party and waited a long time for our food, but Osteria was aware of that and they brought out a tray of free desserts.  They also did not charge one person for their beer.  So they are trying real hard to improve. Let's hope they can do better!  I ordered the seafood pasta.  It was okay, just not the heavy creaminess and rich flavor I was hoping for.

A group of coworkers decided to venture over to Osteria on Monday for a quick easy lunch. Quick, nor easy was on the menu for today's special. Several of us ordered meatball subs, one a salad and soup and the other a prosciutto sandwich. The bread for the sandwiches were hard as rock. The meatballs were just ok. The meat to cheese veggies ratio on the prosciutto was way out of proportion. No balance at all. One diner had to send her soup back as it was off the charts too salty. She also requested no dressing on her salad, yet the salad came out drenched in dressing. Even too much for someone who enjoys dressing directly on the salad. On top of the sub par food, the service was even worse. The waitresses that work there seem entitled and elite. Not attentive to the customers needs at all. Had to ask for refills on soda and water also had to go to counter to discuss the salty soup. I am not one to swear off restaurants, cause I understand everyone has a bad day every once in awhile. But this is a common theme at Osteria. As a side note, the quality of food for the price is not equivalent. There are too many other better options in the Strip to waste time and money at Osteria.

My girlfriend and I ate here for the first time last night and were both so happy with our experience that we agreed one of us had to write a review. We made reservations, though it wasn't crowded for a Saturday night. I'm assuming that's due to the the fact that the entrance is on a back street, not Smallman Street. Our waitress, Jen, was friendly and prompt. We ordered the antipasta plate as an appetizer, which was servered with bread and oil as well. My girlfriend ordered the gnocchi and I ordered the ricotto gnudi, both were delicious. We split a slice of baklava cheesecake and chocolate gelato for dessert.

We were both particularly pleased with the fact that our server held our next courses until we were finished with our current one. We've both eaten at upscale restaurants where they practically throw courses at you back-to-back in an effort to get you out in as little time as possible. It was a small touch, but it really made an impact. In total, we had two drinks, one appetizer, one salad, two meals, and two deserts for a reasonable $70.

Needless to say, this is my new favorite restaurant and we'll both be going back soon.

To say that I am obsessed with their riccolina dish would not do how much I love it justice. I've ordered that pasta dish the last 7-8 times I've been there, no lie. It's so good! I don't know how they do it with the truffle oil, mushrooms, and arugula, but it is just oh so perfect.

I love the laid-back decor of Osteria; the simplicity of it all really draws me in. Outside of the riccolina, I would have to give a thumbs up to the warm tomato appetizer, the spaghetti and the rigatoni. They are all super delicious. Only one of the pasta dishes have we tried that I would recommend you pass on, though I can't recall it now (I think it was a special).

I also tend to like the bread they serve prior to your meal. Yummy.

The menu is not extensive (as every menu should not be), but the items they have are quite tasty as far as the pastas go. I've only ever sat at the bar and the bartenders at first came off as kind of cold, but then we realized they just weren't chatty. Which is weird when you're a bartender, but oh well. I like this place.

In sum, the food was ALMOST okay. Save  your dough, order take-out SOMEWHERE else in Pittsburgh. I consider the pasta dishes along the lines of Pizza Hut. Basically,  it is bland and an insulting misrepresentation of Italian food.

I struggled to rate this. I considered giving them a 3. Merely based on the fact, the pasta they do not prepare in-house, the Fede pasta is local. Fede pasta is a pasta company located right outside the city of PGH. However, giving them a rating ONLY based on something they happen to carry and do not actually "make" seemed too gracious.

Can I also say what a major pain it is to have to get up from my table to walk to the other side of the restaurant in order to read the wine list.  Someone cannot type one up or use an etch-a-sketch? ((Yawns. This place very much underwhelmed me))

Overall, the establishment did not put much effort into a pleasant dining experience therefore, I will not put much effort into writing a review. I would not recommend anyone to eat here and I will not be returning.

Lets be honest, you cant come to Edinburgh without going on a ghost tour. As such, I have been on three tours now with various friends/visiters/family, and two of them have been with Auld Reekie Tours, which starts at the Tron Kirk at the bottom of the royal mile.

The reason I have been on it twice is because it is excellent. It can be scary, depending on the party you go with - with a real claustrophobic, supernatural fear as you enter the underground vaults. The tour guides are very funny and well informed, but they can be downright terrifying too. There is a lot of audience participation, and some jump out at you type moments. There is also a brief stop in a museum of hidious torture, which is good for a laugh, if nothing else.

Excellent, the best tourist thing to do in Edinburgh.
I did the vaults tour and it was creepy and fascinating.  The guide was knowledgeable and not cheesy at all.  Definitely a must if you're visiting Edinburgh.

We went on this tour with a small group off people from several different countries, and it was great,I think the guide can make a big difference to the enjoyment of the tour, ours was very good,s,I was not scared at any time, but the stories are good and our guide got us all involved.The vaults are quite eerie,and with a drink at the end what more could you want.

Auld Reekie Tours run ghost tours which lead you around the streets surrounding the Royal Mile. My friends and I decided it would be fun to go on one after a few drinks, and it did indeed turn out to be a good laugh. 

We caught the last tour of the night and we were the only people on it, so it all felt a bit private and special. Our guide, Rachel, was a great storyteller, but also knew her stuff in regards to the history of Edinburgh. She tried her best to scare us with tales of the grisly things that happened in days gone by, but it wasn't until we were led into the underground vaults that it got a bit spooky. You are led through various rooms which are supposedly haunted and teeming with ghosts, we didn't see any, but we did all get a bit of a fright towards the end of the tour (I won't give the game away). 

I'm not sure if we all would've enjoyed it so much with a bunch of pesky tourists there too, but it was an interesting way to spend the evening before hitting the pub.

Departing from the Tron Kirk, and descending in to the Niddrie Street Vaults, these tours are genuinely terrifying. With a quick tour and history of old Edinburgh the real fun begins with a stop at their private Torture exhibition and then its into the darkness of the vaults. Inside the vaults its scary, the stories and history that are told about make it all the more frightening. The final room that hosts the poltergeist has seen people faint, money fall out of pockets mysteriously, scratches appear on skin, torches and lights go out, and tour guides that were even too scared to stay in the room! Thankfully you emerge back in to the light within Nicol Edwards pub for a very welcome drink to steady the nerves!
If you like getting the fright of your life (litreally) this is for you. I went acouple of months ago liked the beginning likes the stories but when I entered i freaked out.

I went on the tour with a few friends from work and didnt regret 1 bit of it.
The tour was informative, interesting and rather fascinating.
I would definitely recommend it, and the free drink at the end is well needed I tell you!
Scary Stuff!

I really enjoyed this tour when I've been on it. The tour guides are what makes the tour, along with the dark dingy caves.


 The one thing that lets it down is that if you go on the tour more than once, the guides' stories are inconsistent. Which makes you have little faith in the place being hauted.


 Despite this, its a great place to take people visiting the city as the tour is full of history of the city.

Ghost tours in Edinburgh are apparently a must-do, and we were excited to try one out. We heard good things about this company generally, and it seemed to be one of the popular choices. We arrived shortly before 9 for our scheduled tour, and joined a group of about 80, yes, that's right 80! I was already a bit put off, but still hoped we'd be divided into smaller groups. No such luck. 

Our tour guide, who did do a good job, led us to the office where we spent time filing through and presenting our vouchers. It seemed some people were paying on the spot, and may had Groupons (jealous). The size of the group really did take away from our experience, and even the guide said several times, "If the group wasn't so big, we often go to X," or "With such a big group we can't Y." That made the disappointment even greater.

That being said, the tour of the Vaults was fine and spooky, and we got to hear some interesting history and facts about Edinburgh's seedier past. I think cutting off the tour max number to allow for a smaller group would only make the tour more popular. We left right after the Vault, skipping our free whiskey and shortbread, since we didn't want to fight the 78 other people filing into the pub to line up for theirs.

I went on the "terror tour" last Friday night, and I definitely feel as though I got my money's worth. It was entertaining, plenty of good stories, and an excellent experience of going through the vaults.

In fact, a lot of the stories he told us were a bit goofy and campy, not the horror stories I was expecting. Sure, I'd be horrified if the chamberpots were dumped on me of a night, but I was here for ghost stories and tales of terror, not stories about human waste which would fit better in a Three Stooges sketch.

Walking through the vaults was very, very cool. There's definitely a supernatural, spooky feel to it. But (you can consider this something of a spoiler alert - although honestly if you don't see it coming then you'll probably wet yourself on the tour anyway) the cheap spook at the end really ruined it for me. Up until that point I lapped up all the stories but when that happened, I remembered it was just a show - and it cheapened it for me, because then I started doubting the rest of what I heard.

Walking through those vaults and hearing the horrible stories about what happened under my flat was great. It costs the same as going to the cinema for a cheesy horror movie, and it's about as un-scary. But it's a lot more fun. 

Eerie? Yes, definitely. But terror? afraid not.

Judging from the other reviews on here, maybe I just had exceptionally bad luck, but I didn't have a good experience with this tour. We booked onto a 1 1/2 hour 'Terror Tour'.

Firstly, the tour guide we were due to have was ill, which is completely understandable, but they combined our (already quite large) group with a later (even larger group), which caused a few problems. It was raining, and the guide didn't have any kind of umbrella - so she decided after walking us round the block to cut off the 'street level' part of the tour. She then decided that because of the group size, she wouldn't be able to take us through the museum either. Instead taking us straight 'underground' - which is in fact not underground at all, but up a flight of stairs in the vaults built under (I think) South Bridge. 

A ghost tour is always going to be pretty silly, but to have a guide standing in front of everybody saying 'you can all see the woman stood right behind me, riiiight? or am I the only one who can see her?' is a little bit cringey. Her script was very well written to make people feel quite anxious about the whole thing (mentioning people crying with fear/ those stepping into a 'cursed circle' seeing faces in their wing mirrors and crashing - and then trying to sue Auld Reekie Tours/ children being attacked in the tunnels, etc), but the accuracy of the tour I'm not so sure of. 

I'm not a complete cynic when it comes to the supernatural, but I did get the feeling we were being somewhat conned. In the end, I just resigned myself to the silliness and decided to just enjoy being in the atmospheric vaults, and was glad that I got a half price ticket at £6 instead of the very steep £12.

Wow! This tour really scared the pants off of us. If you like REAL scares, and not some hoodoo voodoo made up "horror" rubbish, then by all means, do the Auld Reekie tour. They take you down to the Edinburgh underground, where it's dark and dank and full of malevolent ghosts (supposedly), and where hundreds died as a result of homelessness, indifference, fires, genocides and all kinds of evils. Even the hardiest soul will flinch when they get you in the cold dungeon-like atmosphere and tell you wicked stories of murder and pernicious hauntings. There was a crescendoing moment there when I was sure people were going to faint dead away or have heart attacks. After the scares, you're ushered into a neighboring pub which completes the spooky atmosphere...all in all, a pretty incredible piece of Edinburgh history, and well worth the price of admission.

We had a lot of fun on this tour. We like being spooked and we weren't disappointed. We went on the Terror Tour with Elsa as our guide. She was great, spoke loudly so all fifty (50!!) of us on the tour could hear her. She told some great stories and made the tour very interesting.  My only complaint is the size of the group. We looked into other companies and couldn't get a spot on their scariest tours, but we noticed those were usually limited to less than 30 spots. It took a long time to get from place to place with so many people. Other than that, it was great.

Went on the tour 18th October at 10pm, they walk you about the streets for 3/4 hour seeing nothing, there were 2 groups together (about 40 people) which was too much, the vaults were ok you were in them for about 20 mins couldnt see much as too many people, I would not recommend this to anyone and then after there was no complimentary drink as pub closed. Never again. Michelle Johnson

This was lots and lots of fun. We went for the Terror Tour at ten pm as we thought would be more scary.


 Started with a walk around the Royal Mile area with an interesting talk from the guide. He told us all about the area and there were things I just didn't know about my city.


 The main event was of course the Vaults - why else would we do the tour hey? Our guide was very skilled at building up the story and while I don't believe in ghosts I have to admit to being a little spooked while down there and there was no way I was standing in that stone circle!


 Doesn't take too long and it's an interesting way to round off a night out in Edinburgh.


 My only complaint was the size of the group - we had booked ahead and assumed there would be a limit on the number per tour - but that didn't happen. I think there were over 60 of us on the tour and that did detract from the tour. I think the people who run this should stop being greedy and limit the numbers so you get a quality experience.


 Oh and the pub you are supposed to go to for free drink has closed down - went into receivership I think!

When I moved here, I kind of felt like I had to do one of these haunted walking tours of Edinburgh, but the hard part was choosing which tour guide group to go with. As is usually the case when there are 15 of you, we went for the closest place, which happened to be Auld Reekie's big sign outside the Tron Kirk on the Royal Mile.

It was definitely a good shout - although the tour wasn't particularly scary, it was the most fascinating touristy thing you can do in the whole city. In fact, it's embarassing how often I hear myself repeating their stories to anyone who will (or won't!) listen. I'll try to restrain myself here, and simply tell you that you wander up the Mile to the former parliament, you go to see the spot where they burned witches, and then you go down into the vaults underneath South Bridge.

The tour winds up back at their Niddry Street office, which is conveniently located next to the oldest pub in the city centre, and supposedly the most haunted, where they give you a voucher for a free drink.

It'd be a pretty pointless thing to do during the day, as the atmosphere is so much better at night. If you haven't already done one of these tours, then do one. And do it with Auld Reekie's.

I have been different  SuperCuts locations but this one is my favorite. I usually get here early so I don't have to wait. The ladies are all friendly and like to talk. I will continue to keep coming here.

Whatever you do, do NOT let Connie cut your hair. I usually never go to super cuts but it was a last minute decision to add some layers in my hair. Went in and waited about 20 minutes. I get stuck with Connie, I tell her I just want to add choppy layers BUT KEEP THE LENGTH. My hair was down to my butt, and it had taken me forever to grow it. I made it very clear to keep the length. All of a sudden I look in the mirror after she was done and I wanted to cry. Like I was seriously so pissed. She must have cut about 12 inches off of my hair! It was just to my shoulders! Basically so short I can't even put it in a pony tail. Wtf was she thinking! Even the receptionist was like 'woah, why did you cut all your hair off' I told her I didn't want her touching the length! Whatever you do, don't go to her if you wanna keep your hair. She's scissor happy and my mom warned me about her too. She said she chopped all her hair off as well. Stay far far away.

Friendly, personable service but their rules for "appointments" are bull. If I'm waiting there 15 minutes and 5 people walk in with "appointments" meaning they called before they drove over they all jump me in line no matter how long I've been waiting. They need to change this policy to avoid pissing off people who forget to call.

I wish we could give zero stars, as some places truly deserve it. I went in this morning to get a haircut and was quoted 10-15 minutes wait. Well, during my 30 plus minute wait I first watched the staff order lunch from Port of Subs and than watched as they chatted up 2 young men who walked in and obviously werent interested in a haircut. My hair is already short and just needed a trim. We're talking 10 minutes TOPS and i sat there while 2 other "appointments" walked in and got their services done. 

I will NEVER be back here.

I used to go here often.  I was never really happy with them, but I had to go some place and the price was cheap.  Let me tell you about my last experience there.  Upon arrival I had my name put on the list and waited for my turn.  Another guy arrived and the hostess let him go ahead of me.  I complained.  She stated that he had a reservation.  When my turn came I was seated next to the guy.  We began to talk.  He told me that he did not have a reservation.  Basically, the hostess let him go ahead of me because he was younger and better looking than me.  I vowed to never go to any Supercuts ever again.  I know I should not condemn a whole chain because of the rude actions of one person, but that is what I have done.

You want cheap you get cheap service.

Walked in for a quick haircut. One customer getting a haircut and 3 stylists sitting around doing nothing but talking about their boyfriends and what time break is and what malls they shop at. After waiting 10 mins and not even being acknowledged I walked out and spent my money at their competition across the street.

What a joke this place is. They are not even interested in giving you service.

I stumbled in a few days before Christmas just to get my bangs trimmed up. It was busy, I was greeted right away, waited a few minutes and then sat with Shannon. That was just about 2 years ago now. Every girl in the shop has been doing hair at least ten years, they are one of the busiest salons in the chain. 

I was one of those girls who looked down on this type of establishment super cuts, great clips, etc. But I've been getting highlights, low lights, full color service, cuts and style here since that faithful day in December 2011. 

Shannon knows what she's doing and will not lead you a stray with any crazy ideas you might pickup from a magazine or tv show. 

I hope others will not judge and just give it a try as it was the best choice since I relocated to Vegas from a Orange County California. 

I don't even live near this salon anymore yet I drive 30plus minutes.

Don't ever go here people..... Unless you want to be told 10 mins tops then wait for 45 mins and have an entire family walk in and go before you because they called an hour ago. Are you kidding me?!?!? Plus they charge 15$ for a haircut when great clips cuts it for 12$ and offers out 2$ coupons so it's actually 10$. Oh and by the way great clips is across the street NEVER has a wait. And  THIS SUPERCUTS' stylist are complete Bi$&@s FYI.
$15 bucks straight up. Probably the fastest haircut of my life. Lady was very nice and did exactly what I asked. Didn't make an appointment. Just walked in. Waited about 10 minutes.
I've always like coming here except for the last two for my son and daughter. Today is exceptionally . I forgot their names, but thank you.

I just recently found out that the old manager Kelly no longer works there so I will not be returning. Especially after I went in for a haircut and waited 45 minutes for a terrible haircut, and to top it all off the salon was dirty. 

I really wouldn't recommend going here unless you want to wait 45 minutes for a terrible haircut.
Always a great experience.  Fast service,  friendly and knowledgeable staff. Clean facility.

Just had a super cut! Michele did a great job of explaining what steps she was taking and what the result would be. And it came out like she said. I had called ahead and my name was on the waiting list when I got there. I was in and out in 20 minutes. I will definitely be back.

Great location!  Well stocked, yet plenty of space to move around.  Friendly employees helped me with my selections and gave me tips for using the products I bought.

Great experience here, I'll definitely come back!
Rachel at this location is AMAZING! Today was my first visit to this location and I'll never shop at any other location.  Rachel was sooooooo sweet, helpful, welcoming !!!!!!!!!  Loved her!

I love this store and I love this location! I shop during the week so it's never busy when I shop. And I like the personal attention I get from the staff.

Love love love the sales!! Especially the scented candles and wallflowers.  I admit it, I spent a bunch a money. But I know it all gets used and our home smells lovely!

Great central location for the East Valley, but heavy sales tactics. Also, asked to have my gift items wrapped - even bought a gift bag. All the clerk did was put the items IN the gift bag. I could have done that! Over the top customer service would have been great, and would have balanced out the pushy sales clerk. Ah well, at least I like the gifts I chose.

I'm an avid BBW shopper.  Never had any problems using my emailed scannable coupons until I came here.  The girl kept saying she was looking for an expiration date??  Funny, I went to a different location a couple days later and they scanned the coupon with no problems.  Customer service must not be a priority at this location for loyal customers

ok i admit it i am a bubble bath addict. bath and body work has some good smelly stuff without breaking the bank. 

it's also located in the dana park village sqaure. in the same shopping center that aj's is located.  it's a nice alternative if you don't want to go to the mall.
 
the girls are super friendly, very motivated to help with any questions or suggestion's. the store smells great, clean, organized, convenient late hours.

overall, b&b works is not my favorite store to purchase bath products but it's possible i would return in a pinch.

After selling some previous items here and got a very fair deal I decided to come back.. I had some silver coins and some broken jewelry.. After selling about $9 in silver quarters I got $90 in cash.. I could not of been happier.. For the scrap gold I was more than happy for the price I got.. Thanks for your help David and Robert...

Amazingly rude. After we got done negotiating the guy turned his back on me and waited for a response from me. I don't know weather he was trying to rip me off and couldn't face me or if he was just being a jerk. Nevertheless I won't be back.

I went to sell some old unused jewelry and silver coins that I got from my grandparents after they passed away. To my surprise, it was a lot more valuable than I had thought. They didn't try to cheat me or take advantage of me. They were honest. The guy that helped me, Nate, was very knowledgable about jewelry and I know if I ever come across any jewelry I need to sell, I'll come back again. Thank you.

A friend and I bought a few bars of silver yesterday.  They sell their bars $3.00 per ounce over spot unless you purchase thousands of dollars worth.  Most places sell at $2.00 over spot for small quantities, but I've found several reputable sites online that sell small quantities for $1.50 or even $1.00 over spot. I was hopeful that by purchasing from this physical store outlet, that a relationship could be made to get better pricing on other items or a better rates on the fees when selling bars back, however, the fees to sell back are just as out of wack with the competition and the collector coins I saw were all twice the price as on the Internet.  The reason I give this review two stars instead of one is because the guy assisting us was fairly  pleasant.  I'll let you decide how much good manners are worth, but I don't think they are worth a fee 200% higher on each ounce.  It's a large store and it must have expensive overhead or something...hopefully...but from all the other negative reviews from customers selling jewelry far below offers from competing stores only blocks away, I'm leaning towards greed as the motive for all the overpricing.  I don't think I will be back.

I took my EGL certified diamond to possibly sell it if the price was right.  I am not naive so I went in with an open mind and knew that I would not get the retail price.  I bought the item at a jewelry store that was going out of business so I paid less than half of the retail price.  The gemologist looked at it under a miscroscope and I was able to see what he was seeing on a large monitor.  He told me that it was a lower grade than what the certificate states and said that if it was GIA certified, it would be worth more.  I think he assumed I would accept those factors as a justification of his very low offer.  NO THANKS!!  Again, I am not naive and know that GIA is probably the most consistent gemological lab out there.  But I had the ring appraised thoroughly (not the quickie thing this guy did) and he took the time to clean it, talk with me in detail about the it, etc.

I went there to buy a 1/2 gold coin. I was there, speaking to younger guy who didnt know as much, while the "real" coin guy was assisting another customer. The "real" coin guy finished and came over, said they only had a few things, got his calculator out, and went browsing. I wasnt finished, so I was sorta of just staring at him  like, "I want to see some other gold coins." 2 other customers came and he started helping them. Im like, I have $1000 to purchase this, and you're just going to annoy me like that? Needless to say, i went to sahara  coins and purchased there. Terrible service, I guess the dislike helping people and making a nice bit of revenue each day by acting rude. Whatever, I wont give my money to people like that, because there are plenty of fish in the sea. But, the reason it was 2 stars and not one, is because the guy who didnt know everything about it, but was trying to help, ALSO looked at the guy like, "you're going to help those other customers and not her?" He was dismayed too. Anyways, maybe they need to get a new guy. The rude one was about 5'6", short cut black hair, mid 20s. I hope he's worth the negative review for this store. These guys lost my business for good today. This place has given me 40 under spot during market hours and fifty off hours....the other gives 25 under all day every day. So lesson here....shop around for ppl willing to earn your biz.

The owner tried to rip me off. I had a 14k heavy gold bracelet and he offered $200 and I said no and then he said oh I quoted you 10K and offered me $300. I left and got $400 for it else where. BEWARE

Came in to this place today to sell some of my gold/coin collection. They offered me the most money compared to every other place in town. The staff there were all pretty nice. It was a really hot day and they offered me a cold bottle of water which was nice. I'll be back again I'm sure. They pay in cash, offer top dollar and are very easy to deal with. I highly recommend them if you're trying to buy or sell gold, silver or coins. Shout out to Nate and Avery for all of their help today :)
about selling my old diamond ring, got the best price after visiting 3 other stores in Vegas, very friendly, very careful never to take my diamond out of my site. I will recommend them to my friends.

Took my mom to sell a gold necklace she never wears and was pleasantly surprised it had some worth, also the service was courteous and friendly , I don't know much about jewelry but this place left a very nice impression and I would recommend them,

Best price i found for my gold. They had the accurate information on my gold every place i went to said wrong weight and karat. These guys are straight up. I recommend to stop by if you are selling your gold make sure you get the best amount.Staff is great i was helped by Avery great guy. I forgot to mention I actually felt happy after leaving here

It has been a long time since I sold any jewelry and I would have to say I am very disappointed in my experience. I asked how they come to that number but did not get a real answer. So I figured i would try another shop and just left.

The customer service was not great and they didn't explain how they got to the price nor looked at  the paperwork I had. I am not sure what this place is doing but it doesn't seem to be very good. I would strongly suggest researching this place more carefully and go to other shops.   Not only was there weird things going on here but I was offered over $1500 ($900 more) by 
another shop later on in the day. I am still going to shop around but I felt I had to warn people about this place. I will never suggest this place because they offer far lower than other shops and they were not straight with me. I would stay away

Stopped by because I saw the signs outside and my normal place was closed. So I thought I would see if they would offer me similar pricing and service. This was a mistake gave me a story about how my things were not 100% real and only one or two pieces were pure but yet wanted to buy it all regardless. They were not rude but far from very nice. I would not be back something is off at this place.

Hi Nevada Coin and Jewelry! I was there today to sell some of my old gold Jewelry. I did a little research prior to my arrival. As expected they low balled me (fat guy wearing 20 rings on one hand). I went the other day to get some of my jewelry appraised ...they didn't want to touch them...sent me to the other side of the store...this person with a bad attitude making me feel like garbage,and telling me that my jewelry worth nothing...I have the feeling that 80% of those "testimonials"  on their website are written by them...can you see the pattern? Ripoff place. They only wanted to give me 2k for a 13k ring. I guess they didn't know that I know what my ring is appraised at. Would not trust.

If you need to sell jewelry they pay Okay I got more elsewhere anyway I thought I could bring my coins and little jewelry to one place but it was not worth it went to super pawn with the jewelry and American coin paid the most for the coins because that is all they do and they do it good Nevada coin should be called Nevada jewelry and collectables LOL.

I went here based on some recent yelp reviews. That was mistake. The place was easy enough to find but the customer service had much to be desired. They did the normal song and dance explaining to me that my diamond was flawed and that I should be prepared for a low offer. So guess what they offered me low. BEWARE! 
If I could give them a minus 5 stars I would.. DON'T TRUST THEM! Shop around 1st... They are not there to help you... especially the guy on the commercial...REMEMBER! Shop around 1st...that's where we made our mistake by going to them first and them making us believe they were giving us the best price ...
Sent from my iPhone

I went in and spoke w Avery. Great guy. Asked about costume jewlery. He said to bring it in. I did the following day and was told by the person. Name started with an h that all I had was crap. Came to sell a few Tag watches and some diamond rings looked at and the owner wouldn't  even look at my rings. They were not large enough  diamonds.

I've always wanted to have them looked at and now that I am an "adult" and am in need of money for top ramen more than I need a bunch of collectible coins i decided to bring them in to be looked at!

I came in and Nate was super, super helpful! He was very patient with me considering I had no idea about anything he was saying. I definitely feel like they offered me top dollar and I will definitely be bringing in the rest of my stash to get it looked at!

Recently took some old gold chains and bracelets to them to see how much they would offer for them as they have sat in a drawer for many years and most were broken. Avery looked through what I had and came back with a very fair price. I explained to both Avery and Neil that I had about 40lbs of costume jewelry and they said they would be happy to go through it and would also purchase any I no longer wanted. Again, they offered a great rate on the gold and silver and even paid me for the costume jewelry I had planned to just throw away.

My husband died suddenly and Nathan and the staff at Queen of Heaven were fantastic. They made the transition to move him to another state for burial a smooth and easy process. I could not have asked for any better service from a funeral home on such short notice. Would highly recommend them. Their facility is just beautiful as well as the cemetery.

Just two months after my mother passed away in Chandler, AZ the next door neighbor succumbed to cancer. He and his wife had done a wonderful job of watching over my mother and including her in all their family events so that she felt part of a family in town while my brother and I were in TX and CA. Being a Catholic family, the services were at their church and he was buried here. It is a very pretty cemetery and is well-cared for.

Never in my life have I been to a funeral, catholic or not, where the cemetery staff tried to step in and refuse services to the family. The funeral director tried to physically stop a funeral mass mid-way through. She even threatened the priest.

Thank you Queen of Heaven for being so helpful and making everything so much easier for us. From the consultation all the way to the actual ceremony, we felt like you guys were there for us for anything. 

Great customer service and the grounds are beautiful. I'm so thankful we chose this cemetery to have our baby laid down to rest here. Thank You.

I was referred to this location by a friend and was able to pick up lease a new car from them.  There were no gimmicks or lies that most other dealerships would put you through.  Transaction was smooth from beginning to end.  Sales, Financial Manager and Sales Manager all responded to any questions I had through e-mail and text even after hours.

My car even had a big ass red bow on it when I went to pick it up.  Too bad I couldn't keep the bow lol.

The dealership is clean and well lit.  Waiting area had beverages, couches and tv for your wait.

I wouldn't hesitate to recommend anyone to purchasing a car from this dealership.

Went here for my A1 service and they were very accommodative because usually they don't do their "quick service loop"  on Mondays because one one tech is working, but they still took me in right away. Customer service is pretty good here, but the only thing i would recommend to the management is that you tell your customer when the service is done! My car hasn't been in the bay for 20 mins and I've been waiting for someone to approach me! When i asked they said it was done.

I was investigating buying a car from them and despite several attempts to contact then via email, I never received contact except by way of automated replies. Eventually, I bought the car anyway I paid for a year and two months of licensing and I got them to throw in a set of all season mats. After waiting a few days to receive the call to inform me about the mats being in, I called them and they were in and I could make an appointment. which I did. Upon arriving for my appointment, I proposed that they keep the licensing money and give me a key fob, given the terrible experience I'd had to date. Denied flatly by the GM. So, if you're looking for customer service of any kind, or honesty, or fulfillment of promises, don't deal with these scum bags. My sales person, John Baird was a good guy, but he is culpable to some extent since he didn't ensure that the agreed upon and paid for conditions were met. Completely unsatisfied. If I could have given zero stars, I would have because that is exactly what they deserve.

Been pushed back for grooming here. We had a family issue and needed to find a way to pick up our did from the groomers. They wouldn't work with us and the lady kept asking me to hold and just put the phone down. I could hear her chatting with someone else. This happened two times. I will not be going back here. Terrible customer service.

Done with Pet Club. You no longer carry Orijen. You are out of Red Barn Bones. Maybe if you would start paying your vendors you could get more product. It won't be long at this rate before you have to close all your stores. Great way to run a business.

I was exploring my new enviroment. I needed supplies for my cat. I decided to go to the nearby Pet Club. I was impressed upon entering. WHAT A BEAUTIFUL STORE!! So friendly, well organized, and great products. Prices were fair, staff was eger to answer any questions. I complimented the manager, Enrique, whom I can tell loves his job. He shared with me all the new changes made from previous management, and is proud of the appealing outcome. The hard work, and team players have earned a 5 star, and loyal customer. If you haven't been there recently...give them another shot. I really applaud this pet lovers store, they aim to please. Thank you Enrique!!! Judy La Chapelle

I generally order my cats' food online, but sometimes if they're out of food, and I don't feel like driving to Sprouts, I swing by Pet Club.

Overall, I like Pet Club. It's easier to navigate than some of the big box pet stores, and the staff has always been friendly. They also have a customer loyalty program that allows you to earn discounts based on your spending.

The only two drawbacks for me are 1) the prices seem a bit higher than what I've paid at other places, and 2) their cat food selection is pretty limited.

The staff is so friendly and helpful! Always nice to my fur baby too.  They had a sample of Avoderm products a few months back and our dog loved it. We only shop at Pet Club because of the knowledge staff and outstanding products.
Love the food there, especially the Pad Thai, even though I also enjoy the Pho as well. Great service, affordable pricing, cool vibe

Big disappointment...long wait...pho ordered wasn't to my expectation...not much in the bowl except for the salty n lukewarm broth.   The imperial rolls were very oily.  Not going back there as much as the owner was reassuring to correct the situation.

We had Pad Thai, Pho, Dumplings, and Spring rolls at this place and everything tasted amazing. As well, their service was fabulous. I would say the overall experience with food, service, washroom, and the ambience are pretty good at this restaurant!!
This place was amazing! So flavorful and perfectly seasoned. I would highly recommend. I had the grilled chicken soup and my friend had the vermicelli with chicken and shrimp... Both excellent!

I've had my fair share of pho (being Vietnamese!) and I am very, VERY picky with which ones I like! The pho here is absolutley phenominal!! Definitely takes the #1 spot. The broth is flavorfull, not too strong/weak. The noodles are cooked to perfection (a little chewy/bouncy, just how I like it) and the meat tastes high quality and fresh. I asked for a smaller portion of pho and the server was very accomodating and kind. I'm pretty sure he was the owner. 

Being a solo tourist, I always feel a bit uneasy about eating alone and being new to an area but my server made me feel very welcome as I entered the restaurant. He was kind, profesional and efficient. Definitely 10/10 service. The amibiance is also classy, dimly lit and comfortable. 

Would highlyyy recommend this place!! Hands down my favorite pho ever! Will definitley come back here if I ever come back to Montreal!

I think I'm general enough with this rating. First I ordered a small pho soup without the noodle. After trying more than 10 Pho restaurants in town, I know what i'm expecting for a delicious beef broth. The top criteria of a good pho restaurant goes to the richness of broth and how thirsty you are two hours after you have it (the more thirsty you feel, the more MSG the broth contains). So of course I wanted to try their broth. Very clear and light-colour, doesn't taste strong at all.  


For my main course I chose a vermicelli dish with grilled pork & imperial roll. I specified no salad at all except cucumber (which I always do in other places because I hate raw beans sprouts, carrots and cabbages). The waiter didn't ask me to clarify and he did not repeat what he understood from my order. usually the chef would simply replace the salad with a bit more vermicelli, which makes total sense. What I received was a dish with a bunch of salad, and no imperial roll. I returned the dish, asking to remove the salad and add imperial roll. The second time they brought me the exact same dish only with a roll  added on top; the salad was still there. Oh my lord!!!

The grilled meat already became cold by that time. 
So i was disappointed about the food.

Franchement mauvais.  A l'ouverture, c'était un petit resto qui se respectait mais maintenant, la qualité a tellement diminuer. A éviter. Franchement, se bâtir un clientele et les laisser tomber de cette façon, pitoyable.

Si vous aimez les assiettes remplies de féculents, c'est la place!  Pad thaï tofu légumes, 3 cubes de tofu 5-6 morceaux de légumes et des nouilles pour nourrir l'Asie;)
Service au comptoir très très long...

If you want to wait FOREVER in the drive-thru then this is the place to go. I have never been through this drive thru and had a good experience.  No matter the time of day it takes very long.

Worst McDonalds I've ever been to......Manager's are very rude and talk down to customers....go to McDonalds on 59th ave and Bell......AVOID THIS PLACE!!!!!!!!

Review for breakfast visits only.  After the remodeling a couple years ago this place got a lot more efficient. My orders are fast, accurate, and the food is always hot.  Drive-thru moves rather well in breakfast hours.
Love their fries or let them know? These fries must have been old and heated over again. Disappointing since I haven't had McDonald's in a year.

I am only giving one star because giving ZERO stars is not an option.   Extremely disappointed!!!  I understand this is fast food and you shouldn't expect much considering.....  I ordered an egg mcmuffin that was disgusting.  The cheese resembled hard plastic as if it should be something in a children's kitchen play-set.  The hash brown was ice cold in the center. Very rude manager/owner?went through the drive through and ate my lunch in the parking lot in my vehicle. Very dirty,not one clean table,floors are disgusting...never will be back..no wonder they're doing bad.

Terrible service, dirty nasty! Manager walking around behind counter people eating looking very unprofessional! Food on floor tables dirty! NO ONE CARES

"They always #$%@ in the drive through!"
Forgot my hash browns in a Big Breakfast. -4 stars.
Everything else was great.  +1 star.
Eggs were not dry or over cooked. 
Biscuit was fresh. 
Sausage juicy. 
Hotcakes fluffy.

This McDonald's have change for the worst. I went inside on a Saturday at 5 pm. There were two other persons in there so I though I might get in and out fast. Well guess what happen? I walked out after 5 minutes because there all the help behind the counter were making orders for the drive thru and I wasn't even notice. Well if i was notice no one said anything. I know for sure I wouldn't go thru the drive thru because there were 7 cars in line. Even after the 5 minutes I was inside the same car was still at the pickup window. Never again. Keep up the good work.

I thought that I somehow got magically transported to Tijuana when I walked into this Mickey D's. The place was filthy and I kept having to repeat my order to "Rosalita" because she could barely understand English. I left, without getting any food, and will never come back. 67th Ave & the 101 is not in the ghetto but I sure as hell felt like I was when I was here.

Mango Pineapple Smoothies - like crack... without the nasty side effects!!

This McDonald's is super fast... like lightning! Don't ever be afraid of a long line in the drive-through.

I honestly only ever go to McDonalds for a quick drink ^^see comment above^^... or while on roadtrip for the kids (nuggets are easy, no mess, finger food in the car).

In a pinch, this McDonald's is one of our go-to options for fast food.  We can always get our fries extra crispy when necessary and we actually don't mind waiting if they aren't ready yet since they will bring them out fresh to our car.  The person taking our order always speaks in a really clear voice and the on screen display is a good way to confirm the order.  We have been in the store a few times as well as no complaints inside, but we mostly use the drive through.  Their chicken sandwiches are excellent as well and set our standard for fast food chicken sandwiches with Chick-fil-a being higher (and more expensive) and Burger King being at the bottom (theirs is a fried "chicken flavored meat like substance, never going back to Burger King for a chicken sandwich).

We eat at odd hours so we never have to wait long to go through the drive thru.

What is going on here? Up until about a week ago this drive-thru was fine; orders correct, nice workers. Then suddenly it changed overnight. Now the workers are grumpy and orders are off. What changed???
Olivia is a fucking cunt and should be fired. Stupid bitch doesn't know how to do her job and had the worst attitude. Will not be coming back

Hate this place. Only buy from here since its 24 hours. Employees are rude. Orders are wrong 95% of the time and I have a severe food allergy and we address that at the order screen. My fries are ALWAYS stale. No joke. If this wasn't 24 hours, I'd never go here again.
Been coming to this location for a while and I guess it's under new management cause this place is trashy now employees seem to just hangout and very rude

Dirty floors after they've been mopped they didn't even move chairs because they were french fries on the floor where we were sitting tables were clean when we walked in at two in the afternoon I had to ask him to clean tables not too happy with this location in my own neighborhood!

one of the more expensive mcdonalds (they can all have different prices) not the fastest in town but the food has always been good- guess you get what you pay for! the inside is always clean so 3 stars it is. the remodel is nice.

I know that writing a review for a McDonald's is kind of pushing it, however, this one is by far the shitiest one I've ever been to. I waited over a half an hour just for two medium fries. I would understand waiting that long for a huge order but 10 minutes of that time was waiting for someone to ask me what I wanted. The customer service was horrible, the French fries were Luke warm even after coming out of the fryer and the manager seemed like she/he, (couldn't really tell), didn't care about me at all.

Came here for a nice lunch with my grandma. What we got was a nightmare. When we walked in, we almost coughed because of the extreme filth on the ground, tables, walls etc. how long has it been since you've used a mop? Months? It was supposed to be a nice lunch, not a horror movie. An employee finally came to the front after about 10 minutes of waiting. The food was terrible. The soda was flatter than a piece of paper. Felt sick afterwords. Had to shower as soon as I got home. Had to quarantine my poor grandma from our home. Almost died.

Great place. They are very honest and provide great service. I have had multiple services done here and I was given a honest, reasonable estimate before work was ever started. The work was done correctly and exactly as they said.

I totally trust Chill and his employees. He always tells me exactly what's wrong with my van and doesn't try to sell me repairs I don't need. When I go to pick up the van, he goes over the list of what he did and how much it cost with me. He is honest, reliable, and a kind person. If all mechanics were like Mr. Scardino, they wouldn't have such a bad reputation.
Chill &. His crew have taken care of a lot of vehicles for me with never an issue top-notch highly recommend. Trust worthy

Been going here for years. They have worked on all the vehicles in my family and they will always be the ones I go to! They have never run up a bill and this isn't the place where you go in for brakes and they tell you you need a new engine. Prices are maybe a bit more than other places but they are definitely fair and peace of mind is worth it knowing they aren't throwing parts at you.
Been going to Scardino's since 1987. I have no intention of changing that. No reason to. Completely satisfied.

I was referred to Scardino's by Network Alignment on Cavecreek road. I took my truck there to fix a motor mount issue that another shop caused. Chill gave me quality service at a great price. He fit me in that day because he knew I needed my truck ASAP. There was another new issue that had popped up that morning with my oil pressure sending unit. I had bought the part a few weeks earlier, but did not put it in because of difficulty getting to the part. He let me use my own part because it was a factory GM part. ( most shops will not let you do this). 
He also gave me some great advice on a few things that my truck needed that I could do myself. Sure enough it made my truck run much better and I saved a few more bucks! This will be my shop from this day forward. Thanks Chill, and I will be referring anyone I can!

Scardino's was recommended to me by my sister and brother-in-law.  I'm cynical about auto shops, having found more incompetent ones than competent.

Scardino's is an exception. They are knowledgeable, reasonably-priced, and absolutely HONEST! They will not only tell you what's wrong, they will give you the option of factory parts or cheaper after-market parts.  And they will never replace a part that does not need replacing just to jack up the bill.

To me, an honest auto mechanic is worth their weight in gold!

Our entire family now uses Scardino's, and I have referred friends there, too.

beautiful salon and spa, owner very friendly.  service by nail techs not always on par, sometimes good, sometimes bad.  owner willing to make up for it though, beautiful old home restored, wonderful atmosphere
Always has great deals going, jam up email service...not  big spa person but trying so nice to have a place close by

After an issue that stemmed from a Group-on purchase.  The owner personally contacted me to rectify the issue.  She has also explained the misunderstanding.  I appreciate her taking the time.

I have not yet checked out the facility, but look forward to what it has to offer.

We didn't really know what to expect when we saw the description of the Scrolls on the Kalendar Menu.

With the helpful reviews of some fellow Yelpers though, we were convinced to try.  Personally I had the roast beef and horseradish Scroll, and it's certainly something I would have again! Half was plenty, so only order a Full if you're famished.

My party of three also tried a Nannette, which is a decent app.  We had #4 with the havarti adn pine nuts.  Nothing mind-blowing, but not disappointing.

Without a drink, we paid about $25.  Not your every day staple, but a nice and casual night out.

Kalendar is the ultimate date spot. Quiet, dark tables inside or a lovely patio out front, and a menu that caters to vegetarians, meat-eaters, picky eaters, spicy food lovers, and for cheap/extravagant spenders. The appetizers all sound great: hummus/pitas/vegetables, soup, a lot of different salads - I've had the warm mushroom salad twice, and it's amazing - warm mushrooms, apples, etc.  On the lighter side of the menu are scrolls/naan-type pizza. Scrolls are like rotis but shaped like crepes. There were five different flavours, and they come served alone or with a side salad for around $10-$12. For around $16-$20, they have pastas, risottos, and meat dishes, and specials that change daily. The service was excellent both times I visited.

Great atmosphere, patio always busy on a warm summer evening so go at off-peak hours if you want to dine outside... very cosy inside in the winter. Some of the more adventurous menu items can be a bit hit or miss, but the scrolls are delicious.

Came here for winterlicious dinner ($28). For app, had calamari and soup. The calamari was good, soup was average. For mains, had salmon (overcooked) and veal with mushrooms (not a fan). Dessert was good - nice big slice of cheesecake, and I can't remember the other dessert we got.

A (young) friend & I had lunch here on a weekday.  This is a great place to meet up for a delicious fun food lunch in a quiet atmosphere.  We could actually have a pleasant conversation.

We both enjoyed our choices even though  we challenged our waiter with our food allergies and our uncompromising palate as we are both foodies. 

With the chef's help in modifying our dishes to accommodating food allergies, we shared a salad then C. had a Scroll  (wrap) and I a burger.

Great dining & meeting outing for lunch & brunch but may be too casual for dinner for my boomer generation

Cute decor!   Not a whole lot of seating.  Tables in the bar were tight and table was wobbly.  

Had pizza and salad that was good.

I've been here several times over the past year and I'm definitely a fan!
I'm vegetarian, so I can only speak for the veggie dishes on the menu, but everything I've had has been delicious ... (except for the Scrolls). I don't know... maybe it's just me (????) They seem to be a hit with everyone else I talk to!) :)

The Tortellini is A-MAZING. I highly recommend THAT!

The service is great too. Very nice staff, and always quick to fix any issues.
They seem like they truly care, which is refreshing :)

Definitely check it out!

Checked out this place in the winter
I loved it 
So hearty and filling
Had this roti wrap thing - forget name but well worth it 
Cozy spot
Sign outside states best date spot in Toronto for like the last thirty years!!

It was such a beautiful day I thought I would venture outside my condo and find myself a nice patio to do some homework and grab some lunch.

I was kind of bummed out that Kalandar's patio wasn't open yet but it was dead inside so I got to pick a nice table by the window. *does a little jig of happiness*

The service was great. My waitress was very attentive which is great because I needed coffee BADLY! Speaking of coffee... ORDER IT! 
The coffee beans have made sweet sweet love to cinnamon sticks in the kitchen, resulting in the most amazing coffee I have ever had at a restaurant!

I got a small hummus plate (which is NOT small by the way!) If you think hummus and apples don't mix? Shut up and try it... then thank me :-)

My large Kalandar salad is also amazing... that being said anything with a gratuitous amount of feta is fine by me!

While on a trip to Toronto my group and I stumbled upon this restaurant totally by chance. We read the menu posted outside and thought it sounded interesting enough to try.

I would describe the menu as Mediterranean/Indian fusion. Naan was present in most of the lunch offerings, and when I went downstairs to use the restroom (or the "washroom" as they call it in Ontario) I saw all the staff were of Indian ethnicity. (btw - the washroom was spotless)

The atmosphere however was not Mediterranean/Indian, it reminded me of a little restaurant one might find in Germany, and it reminded one of the people in my group of a place you might find in Belgium.

The food was spectacular. I had the Hummus plate which came with carrots, apples, pieces of Naan, and olives. The Hummus was delicious and creamy, and dipping apples in it was something I would have never thought of doing on my own but I loved the way the flavors worked together.

Other people in my group had Nannettes, Scrolls, Quiche, and salad. It was all pleasant to look at, and everyone enjoyed their food very much.

The service here was excellent. We were a rather large group but they did everything in their power to seat us together. They placed us on the upper level in a booth in the back corner. It was very cozy.

Being tourists we had a lot of questions about the area and how mass transit worked. Our waitress was a fountain of information and even went a far as marking places on our map to go see...just so kind and so polite.

I highly recommend this restaurant. The food is tasty, and the service is the friendliest I have encountered in a large city.

Also - Not everyone in my group had Canadian money but they accepted US money no problem(of course the exchange rate was 1-1 at the time of my visit so that could have been why).

I came here with my boyfriend for a mid-day brunch. Cute, friendly atmosphere..but I wasn't impressed by the service. I ordered a vegetarian quiche and my boyfriend got the burger. After ~25 minutes of waiting in the quiet, empty restaurant the server came and told us they were out of the burgers and said she should've told us earlier. My boyfriend reordered steak frites and after another 15 mins or so it came out...and my quiche was the salmon one. At this point I was too hangry to wait for a reorder, so I just ate it. It wasn't bad but I would've preferred the veggie one. My boyfriend ordered his steak med rare as well, and it came out med-med well. Could've been an off day for the server/kitchen but it was, nonetheless, a first impression. Probably wouldn't have cared as much if I wasn't fixed for time.

A charming and cosy little spot with dim lighting and rich colour schemes. The Parisian style patio opens to College St. and it is very good for people watching. The staff is friendly and efficient. The music during the night can be a little too loud. I had the Braised Beef Ravioli from their daily specials menu. The raviolis were large and beef filling was tender and succulent. I was quite impressed with the meal. Dinner for two and a bottle of decent Merlot went for just under $100.

Terrible service, even when the place is a ghost town. Food sounds good, but when it arrives its meh. 
I usually regret going, there are much better places along college.

I love this restaurant, and choose it when I am feeling too classy for most of my usual haunts. It's got a lovely atmosphere, dim and romantic, with cozy booths and just so happens to have a pretty creative and tasty menu.

The scrolls are made with (as they call it) "crepe-style roti", rolling its eclectic ingredients into some addictive sandwich wraps. My favourite is the roast beef and asiago cheese, a wallop of a flavor burst if I've ever had one. 

I've only had brunch there once, but want to have brunch there often, and get another chance with the fantastic mango, banana and cream cheese-stuffed french toast. Once again, a combination that I never would have really expected, and a very exciting result- oh! and speaking of exciting, the coffee is some of the best I've ever had, and I can't help but dream of it often- it had some sort of sweet spiciness that I can't put my finger on. My sister had the latte and it came in a gigantic bowl. That is all.

Oh, how I love Kalendars. I love their appetizers- the black bean dip with mango pieces is de-lish. I love their martini's- especially the Chocolate Peppermint one (and one is never enough). I love their nannette's- i always get the Smoked Salmon (fresh smoked salmon layered on top of creamy cream cheese and warm naan bread, yum). I love their location (Little Italy) and I love their ambiance. Seriously, great for brunch, a romantic dinner or a night out with friends. Best is in the summer when the patio is open and you can people watch or just chat the night away in the warm summer breeze.

*Note they do not take reservations....so if it is at peak time there will be a wait.

Cute restaurant with a wooden interior - classic but not grungy.
I tried Pizza Four, which comes on a flakey dough - simmilar to puff pastry dough. This results in a flaky texture but a limp pizza - I personally don't like limp pizza, I prefer to have it hold in my hand, but if you do like this I would definitely recommend the pizzas.
My friend had the seafood pasta and it was SO good. For the price, they do NOT skimp out on the seafood. It had mussels, giant shrimp, scallops and lobster. She got a cream sauce to replace the tomato which resulted in a really heavy meal, we both agreed tomato would have been better. It's served with two pieces of garlic bread as well - just in case you weren't full enough hehe.

Would definitely come back here, that seafood pasta is calling my name!

Kalendar is a wonderful restaurant. Nice candlelit tables, warm decor, they offer an abundant selection of quality drink and food. The restaurant layout has a seperate bar and dining room area.   

Everything we ordered was esquisitely prepared and tasted marvelous. Order scroll #6 beef filled naan, nice. (see pic)

I'd dine here anytime, anyday. Definite recommend.  C'est bon magnifique!

On a night out to the Royal, my lady and I popped into Kalendar, after our first choice for dinner didn't quite pan out.

This place is certainly a great date spot. Fancy without being snobbish, classy if casual, and the menu is very reasonably priced. Our table was small and intimate, plunked next to a huge mirror.

My girl ordered one of their pizzas, and I went with Scroll Four (parm, tomatoes, Italian sausage, carrots, mushrooms, onions and peppers). The scroll was delicious, and loaded! My girl also let me sample the pizza, and while it wasn't too different from your standard pizza, there was nothing wrong with it, and she enjoyed it, though our portions were both large enough that we were barely able to finish. I think with drinks, the bill came to around $50. Not bad at all!

I'd love to return to this place.

I was so lucky I walked into Kalendar when I did last night. After waiting 20 minutes in the rain for a southbound Bathurst streetcar that never came, my husband and I decided to change plans and have him come north to College. I walked west looking for a good place to dry off and grab a glass of wine. I skipped over Negroni, just not in a sandwich mood, and fortunately found Kalendar.

There were lots of seats at the bar, so I grabbed two and was instantly greeted by my friendly bartender. I perused the wine menu and he offered me tastes of as many wines as I wanted before choosing a bottle. He was truly a gem, and warmed my heart with his kindness.

When the husband did arrive, he was soaked. Turns out the northbound streetcars were also nonexistent and he had walked from King! What a trooper! Our lovely bartender and I ensured he had some red wine to warm him. All that was left was to decide on the food.

The menu has a lot of good choices. The naan bread appetizers looked really good, as did the crepe roti dishes. A few people near us were eating them, and I was sorely tempted. Instead we opted for some mussels in a deliciously spicy sauce (I had to opt out of some of those jalepenos, though!) and a warm mushroom salad. All the food was delicious.

This place gets crowded. After I had secured the bar seats, people just started streaming in. No one seemed to wait too long for a table, but be prepared, just in case. Kalendar is a popular place and now I know why

I was walking down College Street with my personal trainer clutching my arm telling me I need to do more arm curls (I already did 100 that morning), and we were looking for a cosy place for brunch. It was really hot out and we were trying to get out of the sun (also as per her advice). I hired her because she trains Billy Blanks and I had just watched Showdown. Anyway I instinctively asked Siri where to get the best brunch in Toronto, and she told me the Drake Hotel but after my last visit and that altercation with the man in the awful tank top who claimed to be Chevy Chase's cousin (bullshit, they're all dead) I decided to skip that and go to Kalendar. 

We got a reasonably decent table out on the patio however it was half in the sun and half in the shade (I of course gave the shade to my guest) and needless to say I was freaking out because I could feel the start of sweat pimples starting to form just from sitting there sipping on my second sangria (I chugged the first one). We both ordered the breakfast na'an. Mine had cream cheese, smoked salmon, capers, and a salad. Hers had who even cares. They were both delicious (I ate part of hers). I couldn't get enough. 

Our waiter was bashful, I tend to be very intimidating to wait staff, but courteous and timely. No complaints for anything really. Just stellar. If only they had fried chicken and waffles. Then I'd give them more stars.
Love this place. Great food throughout the entire menu and very reasonable with perfect casual atmosphere. Great service and good spot for a date
Only way to go is scrolls. Their pizza is pretty good. Salads were small and not great value. I don't really understand the consistent line ups.

Kalendar is a great spot on college to get some tasty food at a great price in a restaurant with a lot of atmosphere. My favourite thing about Kalendar is the seating - little nooks with intimate seating and soft lighting to set the mood. The waiters are very friendly and attentive and great at recommending a good wine with your meal.

Food wise, the menu is pretty eclectic. Lots of veggie dishes and a lot of Indian-inspired dishes. Their scrolls - which are  crepe style rotis, served with a garden side salad. I got the one with roast beef, caramelized onions and mushrooms. It was so tasty and warm and filling - I highly recommend it, especially when the winter kicks in.
