To sum it up: underwhelming.

I'd been here a few times.  I love where it's located in the Madison Square.  I love eating and people watching.  The food is always great and the service is always topnotch.

We had the Sausage Pizza and the homemade spaghetti. It was one of the best I have ever had.

We had a fantastic meal here one night and enjoyed some of the best people watching ever.  We started with the cheese plate and the caprese salad.  Everything was delicious, but there needed to be a better conduit for the cheese - more bread or crackers or something.  The waitstaff were teriffic, very attentive but not annoying.
There was a special richotta gnocci that night with chantarelle mushrooms and truffles - it was fantastic though the shaved truffles were ENORMOUS so a bit overwhelming.  Dave had the salmon and said it was the best thing he's ever eaten.  EVER. It did look amazing - perfectly cooked, crisp on the outside and served with these succulent julienned summer veggies.  Yum.  

The only confusion came from their website which made it seem as though there are two restaurants - a cafe and then a more upscale restaurant with a totally different menu.  They've now gotten rid of the restaurant menu and just use the cafe menu whether you eat inside or "outside".  I highly recommend Postrio for a fantastic meal and sit outside for the laugh riot that is the people watching in Las Vegas!

If there is one thing I despise in a server, it is defensiveness rather than service. I try to avoid carbs, and therefore asked for asparagus instead of potatoes with my halibut...just as my husband did. While my husband received a lovely portion of asparagus, I received three "flecks" and I do mean flecks of asparagus embedded in the creamy corn stuff my fish was on. When I inquired as to the whereabouts of the substituted asparagus, the first words out if the waiters mouth were "I don't control the portions." Next "did you want me to get you some more?" As though I were imposing on him with my question. All in all my halibut was flavorless and the service was disappointing. I expect more from a Wolfgang Puck eatery. Boo.

My mom and I actually had dinner plans with a big group of family at another restaurant, but we were tired and hungry from shopping so we stopped in for drinks and appetizers. Her pear martini was unbelievable: so fresh, not too sweet, and garnished with a slice of pear on top. I had a Moscow mule, which was tasty but nothing special. However, the real star was the appetizer. We went with the cheese board, and it was incredible (and $20): three kinds of cheese, apples, walnut toast, a few jams and some honey. 

The pizza also looked great, and the fries with garlic aioli. I wish we could have gone back for a full meal. However, be careful because the prices add up: our two drinks plus a cheese board was almost $50 total. A splurge, but worth it!

Don't let the fact that Wolfgang puck owns it tempt you in any way. Completely unmemorable. I can't say it was good, nor was it bad. Too many other good places to eat. The highlight was seeing Sigfried and Roy at the next table.

I'm reviewing Postrio after eating there two separate times.  If you are staying at the Venetian or at the Palazzo, this is an excellent option for fine dining.  My husband grew up in Germany, so he shares Wolfgang Puck's love and admiration for all things schnitzel, hence a return visit.  

Most people were eating in the "outside" patio, where you can enjoy the beautiful faux Venice ambiance.  The lighting in this courtyard area is truly spectacular.  But, it is really loud and you are usually subject to some "entertainment" on the nearby stage, which has terrible sound.  So, we opted to eat inside the restaurant which was sleek and modern and quiet.  I much preferred this to the patio option, personally.

Our server was prompt and knowledgeable; accomodating without condescention.  We were served several kinds of bread, including a remarkably light and flavorful foccacia. We started our meal sharing the apple salad which was, quite possibly, the best salad I have ever eaten.  The ingredients in the salad were all top-quality and the salad had a perfect balance of textures and flavors, featuring morsels of aged blue cheese and spiced marcona almonds.  The fennel was shaved thin and the apples were mandolined; both kept crisp in ice water until immediately before plating.  I highly recommend this salad as I have never had anything quite like it anywhere else.

My husband had the schnitzel, served with a warm mustard sauce.  The pork was pounded flat and the breading was uniformly crisp and not overly heavy.  It came with a very small amount of potatoes and roasted tomatoes, that appeared almost an after thought to the huge pork cutlet dominating the plate.  The waiter told us this is always on the menu as it reminds Wolfgang Puck of his Austrian upbringing and he does the dish proud.  I ordered the Cioppino, featuring shrimp, clams and fish.  It was good, not great.  The seafood had fresh flavor and firm texture and was not overcooked.  The broth was heavily scented from fennel and tomatoes.  I don't know Cioppino as a dish very well, but I would be surprised if this is as good as it gets.  

All in all, a good option for those visiting the Las Vegas strip.  It's pricey, but certainly not the most expensive option in a very high-dollar area.  And, the menu offers a variety for those looking for a break from the Italian and steakhouse options available elsewhere.

Good food and great ambience. A bit on the pricey side but otherwise tastes excellent. It's a great place to bring a date with the music playing in the background. For being in vegas and it's location it's not too bad.

Puck again hits a home run!  We have gone to several of his restaurants and have not been disappointed yet. 

We had brunch-the omelet was delicious as were the pancakes. Trevor was attentive and took great care of us. Omar kept the coffee flowing and this is important in Vegas in the morning!  Great views as it is close to the gondolas with faux sky and buildings. Very relaxing setting. We will be back!

Because I couldn't find Brasserie, we ended up at Postrio for lunch the other day.  I was impressed with the nice cafe atmosphere and the menu was smiple enough, so we gave it a try.

We were seated and it took a moment for us to get the server to acknowledge our presence after taking our drink order.  I'm not sure whether he was waiting for us to signal him down, but it took about seven  minutes from our drinks to taking our order.  I was a little frustrated at this, but wanted to give him a second chance and so we ordered our food and waited.

The salad came five minutes after he took our order, two Caesar's,  one without anchovy.  Their salad is baby romaine lettuce stacked on each other with grated cheese, tossed in the dressing and served with one crouton.  The flavors were good and a nice change from the tossed, chopped ones I get at Morels or Golden Steer.  that was 19 dollars.

The food took about 18 minutes after the salads to arrive.  I felt that this was quite long and was trying to flag a server down to ask if they could check for our food.  Either we looked too young to take seriously, or I caught this place on a bad day, but it is still no excuse for the lack of attention we received.  We ran out of water and drinks awhile back and no one checked up on us, so that was a bit frustrating.

When our food did arrive, it was presented well and the portions were a good size.  The large spaghetti was split between my niece and fiance in two separate bowls and looked like a hefty portion, so the 17 dollar price tag was understandable.  The pizza was large as well, about a medium pizza if you order delivery.  The lobster sandwich looked like a good size, too, but instead of a kaiser roll they use toasted grain bread.

Pepperoni, olive and tomato pizza with fresh basil: Good crust, nice taste to the dough as well.  the toppings were lovely and had a nice, salty flavor.  The olives were good and not cooked all the way through, but that was fine for me because I don't mind the texture.  Overall, the pizzas at any Wolfgang's are good.

Spaghetti with meatballs: Five dollars extra for those meatballs, just to warn you.  The pasta is made fresh there, and you can tell by the color and texture of the pasta.  It came roma tomato chunks and lots of cheese, so that was nice.  The sauce had that right amount of tanginess to it and spice.  The meatballs are very good and well flavored.  you still get the meat taste with a hint of Italian spice.  Quite a lovely meal.

Lobster sandwich: Good lobster, very sweet and succulent.  It's a cold sandwich, of course, so the mayo and other ingredients mixed with the lobster were really fresh and light.  The bread is heavy, however, so my husband took the tops off of the halves to avoid getting overfilled.  The fries and skinny fries and are your typical hotel fries.  Overall the sandwich had good flavor but we expected something more.  It almost felt as if this particular dish was missing something, but I couldn't place my finger on it.

For 160 dollars for lunch (I did tip 20% because the service went up from the meal, on) it was okay.  I am not a fan because of the initial service we received, but the food was good.  I like Puck's restaurants, but I won't go out of my way to eat here again.

If you like the cafe feel in Venetian and want something fair and fast, this is the place to go.  I know people are giving it five stars for food, but for my personal taste it wasn't exciting and lacked any "wow" factor that it should have for that price tag.  Still, it's fair eats.

In short: Delicious seafood (oysters and mussels) with fantastic pasta.

As I have been brainwashed by the cheese platter at Batali's San Marco right across the way at the Venetian, I had never noticed this place except that Wolfgang Puck has some restaurant in the corner.  Club Grazie sent me a complimentary dinner here so I checked it out with the GF this past Wednesday evening.

We were seated inside (would have been a 10 minute wait outside.  Inside is mood lit, clean, and less distracting which is great for a date and/or you're ugly (as in my case).  It felt more formal inside too, but the outside is nice if you want to see/hear the violinists or jesters, but you may also enjoy the crowd of tourists passing by.

Here's the menu: (http://www.venetian.com/uploadedFiles/The_Venetian/Dining/Fine_Dining/PostrioDinner0410.pdf)

Very friendly and accomodating waiter, simple wine menu (I like that). Also of note, the bread and butter comes with a crushed olive/basil/olive oil dipping sauce for the Italian bread that was really good.

We started off with a few of the kumamoto oysters which were phenomenal.  It's funny how you can get some of the freshest seafoods and meats in the middle of the desert.

We then split the caesar salad which had a nice deconstructed take on an old favorite.  It has a very flavorful white anchovie slice served with whole lettuce leaves which are tossed with the caesar dressing which IMO had the perfect balance of acidity and creaminess.  Great salad and it might be the first one where I've needed a knife to eat.

For entrees, I ordered the steamed black mussels in a white wine sauce and the GF got the spinach lasagna with meat sauce.  My one let down was the bearnaise sauce that covered the bread with my mussels.  It was too sweet, sour, and creamy for my taste, the GF didn't like it either.  The mussels tasted great, but I was not blown away, it was about what I expected when ordering steamed mussels.

The GF's spinach ravioli on the other did blow me away.  I recommend this dish to anyone who likes pasta in meat sauces.  I'll upload some of the iphone pics in a bit, but the pasta was perfectly soft and the meat sauce had great flavors of the beef and sausage.

For dessert, save room for the beinet.  Fried chocolate doughnuts with chocolate and caramel inside that melts in your mouth, served with coffee ice cream and a vanilla sauce... We got them on the waiter's recommendation and they turned out to be one of the best desserts I've had in a long time.

Next time I'll try the linguine in white clam sauce and the four cheese ravioli since the pasta was so good.  The pizzas didn't look special from the other tables, so I'll stick with San Marco when I want a pizza.

Perfect. Great service, great food, great wine, great food.

The lobster BLT impresses and the corn soup is outstanding.

Full of win.

A-OK. 3.49 Will have to go back to up it.

How to respond to the outdoor seating question I'm asked before submitting my review? I'm baffled given the faux-Venice atmosphere.

Burger was solid. It had some sort of tasty SECRET SECRET SECRET SAUCE on it. A little too huge for my preference. Fries were good, similar to Burger King in texture and cut.

Sat at the bar, service was excellent as is the standard in Vegas.
The tuna tartare was to die for!!.. I will come here again just for that!. We sat "outside" and the ambiance was nice to people watch and enjoy live music. Our waitress was nice but she was so slow.

Horrible experience!! Service is slow and food is not properly cooked. I order fetuccini pasta with steak and they overcooked the meat and brought it cold. This restaurant does not provide fine dining, I do not recommend this restsurant to anyone.

Really solid food with a charming atmosphere. Between 7-9pm, we still felt like it was daytime under the bright blue, cloudy sky.

Started with margarita and pepperoni pizzas. The margarita pizza was well seasoned and had delicious cheese. The pepperoni on the pizza was really great as well.

Entree was the stuff quail. It was delicious.

Overall I thought everything was finely executed.

Last night we went over to the Venetian and chose Postrio for the variety of food. I had a gluten free pasta they made me with a sausage bolgnase sauce. Delish!  At our table we also had two different pizzas and a spaghetti with meatballs.  Everyone loved their dinner and left nothing to take home. The waiters were good and decently attentive. We had wine refills and water, they took away dirty plates without being disruptive, and a nice 'fake' outdoorsy feel to the 'patio'.  They didn't have a specific gluten free menu but were very informed on what I could eat. It's so nice not have salad all the time when out with friends.
Don't come here.  The service was terrible.  It took 15 minutes just to get water and the portions are non existent.....

Went to Vegas and stayed at Palazzo... I was searching for a good restaurant and noticed this was a Wolfgang Puck restaurant, so we decided to go here, we knew we wouldn't be disappointed. I ordered the calamari (it was an appetizer, I chose to eat it as my main meal), it was ok... not much flavor, but there were peppers all over the place, which gave it some sort of taste. I've definitely had better calamari elsewhere.. wouldn't recommend it. For dessert... I ordered the chocolate beignet's... loved them- a taste of heaven! Rich, moist, and fresh, and the ice cream they served with it made it even better! So I would definitely recommend that for you chocolate lovers out there! The ambiance was nice... and we were seated outside (not really outside but  they considered it patio seating) so we got to enjoy the entertainment that was going on... which was probably the best part about dinner!

This restaurant is pretty amazing! Be prepared for the prices, they are a little on the steeper side, but well worth every penny. Great place to celebrate a special occasion or make reservations for a date night with the beau. It's tucked away inside the Venetian Hotel and Casino and although there's several shops and tourists nearby, the restaurant - even when you're sitting "outside" feels super elegant and cozy. The cocktails are great, the food is great, and the service was pretty stellar also!

The food here is always GREAT! This time, my the number of people in my party was 7 for lunch which forced us outside the normal enclosed dining area. Being outside the area, it was more difficult to get the same attention if we were inside the boundaries.
I realize the lunch period is always busy but this lunch took over 90 minutes which caused our customer to have to leave as soon as they were done eating.
I will eat here again but with a smaller party next time so we can be seated inside their eating area and not near the resort entertainment attraction.

We had a large party of 13 for a bachelorette party and they were so accommodating! The staff and service was outstanding and impressive. I loved that the restaurant was located in the Venetian by the canal shoppes. It has the open airy feeling of dining outside in Europe! The food was good, and I'm glad the portions were medium sized! My favorite appetizer is the tuna tartare, totally melts in your mouth and the flat bread pizzas. The fried risotto balls and chicken skewers lacked flavor and were least popular. I think that needs to get off the menu! I was adventurous and ordered one of the specials of the day, which was the peking duck. Delicious & creative! Despite our large group, the food came out on queue and we all had a wonderful time!

I had the prosciutto pizza which was pretty good.  It was listed as a pesto based pizza, instead of marinara, but I like the 4-cheese pesto one way better.  The location was nice and we were able to watch a live show going on next door in the Venetian.

I don't think Wolfgang Puck has every did me wrong. He knows how to run a great restaurant even though he isn't there and this place is no exception. I had the gnocchi and also ordered the blue cheese with truffle potato chips to start and it was so salivatingly good. I'm beginning to think Vegas is the new best culinary showcase city.

This is probably one of the most expensive restaurants in Vegas - My appetizer alone was $21.00 for some under cooked risotto (Wild Matsutake Mushroom Risotto, Parmesan Reggiano).  I can make BETTER risotto at home.  I did not bother to complain because I knew there was no point - I just had to survive through my next entree.  My husband had Ravioli with Ricotta, Spinach & Soft Quail Egg, Grilled Quail and Thyme Glaze - it was OK with alot of holiday seasoning.

My dinner entree was Grilled Prime New York Sirloin, Yukon Gold-Horseradish Potatoes, Cognac-Mustard Sauce - $54.00.  I can honestly say the steak was seasoned perfectly and the cognac-mustard sauce was excellent.  My husband had Slow Braised Beef Short Ribs, Creamy Polenta, Olives, Shallots and Natural Juices - not bad either...but then again, how can you screw up short ribs?? Just braise it to death and you'll be OK.

Service was exceptional - don't bother filling up on free bread, try to enjoy your expensive entrees because I didn't finish half my steak and didn't want to carry a doggy bag around :(  

A glass of wine really wasn't a "glass of wine" they poured short of 1/2  a cup a glass...but then again, foo-foo diners don't care when they are carrying wads of money with them.

Skip over to the Gelato stand right next to the restaurant for a cheaper dessert and PLEASE bring your American Express card for this place - don't leave home without it!

If it wasn't for my birthday - I would of gone next door to Enoteca ( I heard their food was great!).

Fantastic location (St Marks Sq), excellent service and great food. The roast beef panini was great. When my panini arrived I thought I might not be able to eat the whole thing because the portion size was huge. But it was so tasty that ate it all and all of the frys. I had a couple of glasses of red wine and an ice tea to wash it down. Great place to grab a bite. You are eating at a celebrity chef's restaurant in prime real estate inside venetiaian so expect to pay a premium.

I give this place 3.5 stars! .,.. the name was so confusing bc it had wolfgang puck in it buuuuut yelp notified me a couple days later i got it wrong ):

My friend and i were starving and trying to soak up fat tuesday alcohol with some food and we decided on this place ! We originally wanted to go to the restaurant next door/across the walkway, but the waitresses/hostesses were super snobby and rude there, so we came here instead, where the employees were incredibly nice to us. 

We had seen their happy hour everyday all day and was very curious in their small medium and large plates. Their prices even NOT on happy hour were very reasonable, especially for overpriced Vegas food and meals. We were seated at the bar for happy hour specials and were handed some complimentary popcorn from the bartender working there. After contemplating on the menu, we decided on:

-wild mushroom pizza ($16): loaded with lots of mushrooms, but it was alright. for a restaurant that also had a pizzeria, i thought it would be fantastic! but the crust was kind of hard and the overall pizza was kinda cold.... 
-homemade meatballs ($6): comes in 3 meatballs the size of half a fist, maybe smaller and a slice of bread. The meat was soft when you bit into it. You cant really taste too much of the beef(?) but the sauce was delicious
-garlic aoli french fries ($7): MMM this was the highlight of our meal. If you like soft or like yard house fries, you will definitely like this! They give you mustard and ketchup but you can really just eat it with no condiments. 

I would have given them a 3 stars, but the service was superb! The bartender checked up on us frequently and entertained us with questions and experiences about his trip to Europe. And when we packed the stuff to go, he gave us a cute little box for the pizza and an extra container of ketchup. 

Overall, i think this is a cute restaurant to go to for cheap food in Vegas! For under $30, you can feed two people for dinner! But then again, we had fat tuesday alcohol in our stomach and we're petite LOL
Not a good place for a group of nine.  Had to send one of guest's plate back twice - undercooked, items listed on the menu were not available, food was plain ... Not worth $750.

Being in the heart of the Venetian, I was sure this place would be incredibly expensive. However, the dishes came out to be about 20 dollars a plate, affordable for the place and ambiance this place offered. 

I ordered the bolognese here. Delicious! The pasta's texture was just perfect. It felt like it had substance. The spices in the sauce were subtle but tasty.

The best part of the meal was their chocolate beignets. They're not traditional beignets. The shape reminds me of a doughnut hole but the texture and taste reminds me of a molten lava cake. Creamy hot chocolate oozing inside covered by a crispy chocolate cake outside. We had two orders of that.

Service was on point here and they constantly came to check up on us. My friend didn't like his dish (some spaghetti dish) and they gladly took it back and gave him a new dish. That's service!

Found ourselves in the Venetian around dinner time, and between the three main restaurants in the St. Mark's area, this one seemed to be the best bet!

We didn't regret the decision, as the entire experience was both relaxing and pleasant. Instead of sitting in the weird outside vibes area, we dined inside, where it was dark but quiet. We even had a little fireplace by us, and it was eerie to see the glow of the fake outside world through the doors.

Despite service being a bit confusing at times (our main waiter was slow, and we had two other people asking us for our orders at different periods), things came out timely and well cooked. My boyfriend and I shared the creamy potato leek soup which was definitely creamy and not too potato-like, but still good when served with the crunchy bread. 

Vegetarian fare was plain & simple - homemade pasta with a mushroom cream sauce. I'm used to this. Still a classic dish, and done great with some mini onions and a myriad of different mushrooms. It was definitely not salted enough so I asked my server, who was a bit taken aback, for a bit of salt. My boyfriend went nuts over the meatloaf & onion rings dish! I was happy about his excitement! :)

The dessert menu rocked!! I don't even know where to begin. I was so confused - definitely a huge hardship for the night. I chose the lemon pudding cake with blueberry compote & blueberry gelato, which was maybe my only mistake - a little too lemony/sweet, overpowering. I wish I had gotten the sweet potato pie! Oh well :) A very great meal! Slow and delicious, definitely filing & reasonably priced.

I had dinner here with a large group and its a fun little place in the st marks square area of the Venetian.  The food is basic Italian done really well.  The service as great and the food is tasty.  Ask for a table outside by the square and take advantage of all the entertainment happening in the square.  It is not way over priced like some of the other options near by.

Postrio was fantastic!  They took great care of me and my wife when celebrating her birthday!

I highly recommend the meatloaf!

Service was simply incredible and well deserving of the five stars.  Worth it all the way around and a genuine find in the Venetian!

WAY TO GO WOLFGANG!

Wa
y overpriced for what you get. The menu is so mediocre as is the service and the portions are ridiculous! I know this is prime real estate but the empty restaurant should have been a warning sign. $30 will get you a teeny piece of FARMED raised salmon. The waiter was arrogant and we will not be in a hurry to return to this place!

Reading all the reviews, I expected to get mediocre service.. but I was pleasantly surprised. Our server was very attentive and very cool.
We ordered...
-the LINGUINI with CLAMS and PANCETTA was very tasty... the linguini was perfectly al dente which is hard to find with fresh pasta.
-my husband ordered the HONG KONG STYLE HALIBUT.. which I thought was ok, but he loved it... it was a little too tart for me. He said you have to have each component of the meal to balance out. I personally would never order it.. but he would totally order over and over again.
-they have a kids menu.... and my daughter got the cheesy pasta... it was simple and my daughter cleaned her plate. Too bad that you have to order each thing separately... we had to order her milk separately... which was like an extra $2.50 or $2.75.
-SANGRIA.. was really tasty. the apples were really crisp. The pitcher was only $25.. how can you beat that?

oh.. and the bread.. VERY GOOD... crusty on the outside and soft on the inside... and the olive tapenade that they serve with is.... mu-ah! I could just eat that ALL day long!

Overall... will definitely be back!

So I've never been a big fan of the Wolfgang and a lot of these celebrity chefs more because I believe they over commercialized themselves, but more power to them, I certainly respect them for getting to the top of their game.

That said, to get to the top of your game you have to know your craft and deliver the goods, which I find he does whenever I go to one of his restaurants and tonight was no exception.

I get that Vegas is what it is and appreciate that no where does it better. The spectacular Venetian "St Marks Square" location, offers al fresco dining without the elements but does offer great people watching, classical music performances across the square and a general nice buzz of people having a good time. friendly staff are pleasant, welcoming and professional.

I opted for three appetizers, a spinach salad with apple shavings, pomegranates, candied walnuts, fennel and blue cheese, which was perfectly balanced so all the unique flavors and textures both stood out and complimented each other.  The miniature salmon sliders were very well flavored. The chicken satay was juicy with a spicy peanut sauce that that really delivered a delicious flavor and burn.

Add it all up and once again Wolfgang and Postrio delivered the goods!

I've been eating here for years. Every time I go to Vegas I eat here. Last night my dinner was very disappointing. The cheese ravioli was soooo salty. My friend's salmon was above average, but not up to par with Wolfgang Puck's name. I bragged about how great the place was, but was not a good dining experience. The water was not cold. And the wait staff was blah. The mgr comped my meal, but I would much rather preferred to have great food and pay for it.  The mgr was deadpan like the wait staff.

Good food, great service, romantic setting...but as with every pricey restaurant, be prepared to leave hungry.  I  Ordered the seabass with a side of asparagus, a bottle of wine, dessert, and my wife got the wild mushroom Gnoochi.  Maybe we shouldve ordered more appetizers and sides, but our bill was already $130 not including tip.  So I do what I usually do at fancy places and just kept asking for more bread, which was good and filled me up.  Seabass was really good but not filling.  Mushroom Gnoochi was good, but the portion was so small my wife was starving after dinner.  After tip we spend around $150, and still had to find another place to eat afterwards just to keep our stomachs from growling.

Well the feel of this place is fabulous.  You really feel like you are in Venice when you sit "outside" the restaurant.  It is a fabulous feel.  I went here for lunch with a group.  For lunch I split a caprese salad and a lobster club.  Well the salad was unbelievable.  The heirloom tomatoes were amazing and the balsamic was aged and yummy.  The lobster club was just OK.  Nothing special for the price.  Someone at our table had a pizza which was UNBELIEVABLE.  I should have known being at a Wolfgang Puck restaurant to order the pizza. I  would go back and split the pizza instead.

My second time at Postrio though it's been a few years since our last visit.  This time we were supposed to be a party of 9 but at the last minute four cancelled out.  The hostess handled the change no problem and we were seated at one of the high tables.  

I went with the asparagus soup for appetizer which was absolutely delicious.  Others went with the grilled chicken skewers which were also delicious.   For the main course I went with the linguine with clams and pancetta which was just awesome.  Another in our party got the salmon and that was one of the best, most flavorful salmon dishes I've ever had.  Not sure what all was in the seasonings, but just delicious.   Another in the party got the Schnitzel and that was easily the biggest meal of the bunch.  We also had one pasta with their bolognese sauce which was also very very good.   All in all an excellent meal.

The waiter was very attentive to the fact two of our party had dairy allergies and checking on each item before serving.  Even not serving the peanut sauce with the chicken skewers because it contains cream.

Right off the bat we informed the waiter that we would all be paying separately and he told us no problem and at the end of the meal, he handled everything perfectly. So if you are a group all paying separately, just let them know when you sit down.  

Good beer and wine selection as well in a very relaxed atmosphere.  We were seated out on the "patio" where you're out in the open St Marks square area of the Venetian.  Live music was playing off in the distance which was fun.

It's been awhile back since my last visit to Postrio, I don't even remember what I had for dinner here, obviously it wasn't memorable enough.  But I'll never forget the doting service, delicious bread basket, attention to detail (wipe crumbs off the table and the waitstaff iron the tablecloths when it's changed) and that glorious chocolate souffle.  It's incredibly fluffy and soft texture kept my head in the clouds for a good part of my trip. It's at least a 30 minute wait for the souffle so place your order ahead of time.

Hubby and I liked this place.
Pizza was plain and simple.... a little drenched in oil but very good.
Porcinni Mushroom raviolli were soooo good.
We had a pitcher of Sangria it was soooooooooo good and cheap $25 bucks for a pretty big pitcher.
There is one thing that I am confused....
Why does  the cafe menu you can eat in and outside where the regular menu you just can eat inside and not outside?
I didn't get that.... wouldn't you think it will be the opposite?
Puck always delivers.  Nice portions.  Someone I came with on my last trip even ordered the burger lol, but it was definitely a cadillac of burgers.

Don't let those 20-25% off coupons trick you into going to Postrio. It lured me in (my Asian cheapness came out) and it was not worth it.  The faux-outdoor seating is charming and the free bread is good but the positives stop right there. 

The $18 pizza was very average. The $26 short-rib ravioli was less than average. I would have preferred Olive Garden's short-rib tortellini to the four chewy and stringy ravioli at this Wolfgang Puck restaurant.  

The  restaurant's Piazza San Marcos location reminds me of the real Piazza San Marcos - a tourist trap filled with overpriced mediocre restaurants.

One often hears a rendition of the famous adage to enjoy the journey rather than to rush through it, and this is one prime example of such great advice.
We were intrigued by the 1000 plus reviews for Bouchon, so our aim was to dine at this establishment for brunch.  However, i couldn't muster any more energy to walk that extra 10 minutes through the windy Venetian Hotel, so we ended up at Postrio instead.  MUST.EAT. NOW.  lol.  this was an amazing gem with prime real estate seating.  

LUNCH FARE: 

RICOTTA GNOCCHI with Sweet Fennel Sausage Bolognese ($25)
a soft ballad of flavors dance together with each bite.  so soft with potatoes oozing out.  each bite was outstanding and just the perfect portion.

TRIO OF HOUSE MADE SAUSAGES ($16)
Housemade Mustard, Pickled Vegetables, Grilled Country Bread, Baby Mache.  
yes, appetizer portion, but i knew i had to save room for dessert.  my ideal type of meal is usually 60% protein, 30% veggies, and 10% carbs, and this dish delivers exactly that.  executed so well, each bite was heavenly.  the sausage on the far right had pistachios, so pistachio lovers -- make note.  the fuchsia looking vegetable adjacent to the pistachio sausage is actually pickled watermelon.   it's not the typical watermelon that one would purchase at the local market.  this type of melon had the tight texture & consistency of a daikon or a radish, yet it was a watermelon.  

CHOCOLATE MELTING BEIGNETS were fabulous! ($12)
the chocolate beignets were oozing with warm chocolate filling and dusted with powdered sugar.  one proper spoonful of ice cream  was the perfect complement to the warm beignet.  the vanilla dipping sauce was just an icing to the dish -- it was great, but not necessary, but definitely did not hurt it at all.  for a dessert, everything was "not too sweet" either, which is always perfect in my books. 

for Mimi L,  they carry Banoffee, which is a banana & toffee cream pie ($9).  Other delectable treats include chocolate cream pie ($9), warm apple pie ($9), lemon cheesecake ($10), chocolate souffle ($12), and housemade ice cream or sorbet ($8)

****

SERVICE was impeccable.  Our server, Luigi, was nothing short of accommodating and awesome.  the pseudo "outdoor" seating gave us a great glimpse of St Mark's Square, where performers entertain passerbys.  the festive atmosphere and costume of the performers really enhances the "Venetian" feel.

lastly, love how the manager emails me personally to welcome me back to the restaurant.  i had received a similar email from Wolfgang Puck Bar & Grill at MGM Grand.  great personal touch.  definitely worthy of 5 stars =)  Mr. Puck, i'm starting to become a fan of yours.

Firmly squared in st. mark's square is this little restaurant. After all being in "venice" there's no better place to be. There is enterantainment and gelato nearby.

I had the house lasagna, which was pretty good. Nothing ground shaking, but indeed a solid course. Every dish my family ordered was indeed great.

However what stuck out to me, and would make me come back for more was the superb service. My grandparents are super 80+ and the waiter really walked them through and explained the courses to them. Its a nice pleasant touch, and done with the right spirit and its a winner.
Had lunch on a Sunday.  Not bad at all,  but don't expect anything spectacular.  Perfect Martini was great.  I up to 4 star for that,  otherwise average.

So after a day and a half, the staff working with us on this returned our phone calls to tell us that the waiter who committed this crime has been terminated from his job, all of the money we spent on our meal will be refunded and they were extremely sorry.  I appreciate that they took the time to see that this was an issue and handled it.

I may return again.
Incredible meal. Amazing cheese selection, phenomenal beers, great service!

I asked the waiter for his recommendation between a couple of entrees, and he highly recommended the meatloaf, so that's what I ordered.  Nice presentation but the meatloaf itself was kinda dry. The onion rings that came with it were outstanding.

Here's the thing, Prostrio does NOT play into the Vegas showmanship that surrounds it and that what's makes it a good restaurant.  

This is a simple, American bistro. Great salads and simple wood oven baked pizzas and entrées that are simple and approachable (meatloaf with potato puree mushroom gravy and buttermilk onion rings).  Its the kind of place that you can feel just as comfortable having a beer as a good glass of wine.

Eaten here many times and the food is consistently good.  Fresh ingredients used throughout.  There are no real standouts and that is part of the restaurants appeal.

Friendly service.

Very fair prices for a Vegas resort restaurant.

A great spot to enjoy lunch if you find yourself in the Venetian...

I like Postrio because it combines a good people watching opportunity with great cocktails.  The food leaves a bit to be desired, and coming with Wolfgang Puck's name on it, one automatically thinks it will be something it is not.  

The few times I've been here I always leave saying the same thing:  "Next time I'm just having drinks."  The cocktails here are fantastic.  Very creative and well made drinks are enough to keep me coming back, especially the cognac and lemon juice martini, mmm mmm!

Most recently we ordered:

Margarita Pizza - Straight forward mozzarella flavor, nothing developed or complex, very underperforming pizza.

Salt n' Pepper Calamari and Shrimp -  Perfectly light and flaky coating, good flavor, delicious sweet chili dipping sauce, just a good appetizer.

Chopped salad - What was he thinking?  This salad worries me, it shouldn't  be on the menu.  There are what I take to be pickled figs in here, which do what capers often do to dishes, overpower them.  This unbalanced bowl of greens is an expensive mish mosh of salad bar rejects.

Cesar Salad - Very crisp lettuce and a light dressing were a nice way to continue through our meal.  Think Cesar Salad's less chubby cousin.

Pumpkin Tortelloni in Brown Butter Sage sauce - Overpowering sage flavor, whoa!  The pasta itself was very well made, and I had no issue with the pumpkin in the noodle, but the sauce failed to accentuate anything on the dish.  It really just screamed Sage, and not in a good way.

Besides the good location, Namesake, and drinks, Postrio falls short of being a great restaurant.

Awful experience at  normally reliable restaurant.  Service was slow and inattentive.  Food was overcooked, undercooked, or came out cold or soggy.  Scallops were particularly bad-- texture was mushy like pre-frozen Costco fare.  I will never do dinner there again.  (Though I will be back for the lobster club at lunch. . .)

This was very mediocre. Let me say first that I even had a coupon for 25% off my meal and it was not worth it. I mean, anywhere else, I'd say meh... it was ok. But this is Vegas. And since this trip I only had 2 days, every meal counts. 

I ordered a sandwich (some sort of club) and the onion soup. The onion soup was sweet enough to be a dessert... imagine French onion soup without the saltiness nor cheese and throw on spoonfuls of sugar. Not very appetizing, right? The fries that came with my sandwich were also quite cold. I could literally see into the kitchen from my table. I saw my sandwich made, and it didn't take that long to come out. So why were my fries cold? They must have been from an old batch.

As far as service, it was decent. Friendly waiter, but not enough to save the whole restaurant. I sat inside (outside was a longer wait). The atmosphere outside (I say outside loosely...since it is in the middle of the Venetian) would probably have been a better experience. 

Not going to return, though, considering there were other restaurants in the same square.
A great dining experience in the heart of the Venetian waterway. The cuisine is a hybrid of American & Italian, but oh so good!

On the last day of our MDW Vegas trip, our group wanted to grab brunch together before we all left. We were lazy to leave the Venetian we were staying at so we decided to walk around the shops and find something to our liking... Obviously we chose Postrio! 

Their menu was divided into brunch, small plate, medium plate, and large plate options. I think everyone in our party chose something from the brunch section! Our waiter gave us fantastic service, I wish I remembered his name! I love that he always served the ladies first and tried to make pleasant conversation with us whenever he came to check up on the table. We also each got a complimentary mimosa with our entrees! Yummy ;D

Everyone was happy with their food :) The favorites were the eggs benedicts which you could get with either traditional canadian bacon, smoked salmon, lobster, or vegetarian. Mmm I got the lobster benedict and it was amaaazing with huge chunks of lobster. They definitely did not skimp out on me!

Great atmosphere, great company, great food = couldn't be happier!!

Of course the wide open restaurant in the middle of St. Marks Square is a must go! We were pleasantly pleased with the down to earth menu. I ordered the hamburger and wow! Yum! The seasoning was spot on, fresh tasting & huge! The bun was over the top no way was I eating this with my hands - fork & knife all the way! The service was good. A large bridal party was behind us and they were having the time of their lives! The vibe is FUN FUN.

After three years, went back to Postrio with my brother and s-i-l. It was just as good as last time. The caesar salad is my absolute favorite. Our dinners were superb. The prices are very reasonable for Vegas. All in all a wonderful experience. We'll be back.

Had Michael as our server, HORRIBLE service.

Our treatment versus others around us was atrocious.  After ordering and chatting up with my friend she pointed to tables around us.  I noticed he was putting bread baskets down on tables and when I asked for ours he said it was available during request.  A couple sat down after us and I overheard him offer them a bread basket, then he offered it to other tables that sat down.  

We bought a bottle of wine like we usually do and he was never around to refill our drinks, I got up once to do it myself and a busperson came over to do it for me.  I took care of him since Michael wasn't around.

And then another thing I overheard behind me, he told them the two specials that weren't on the menu.  Something about lobster and risotto I think, two of my favorite things!  We ended up ordering a filet mignon (alright), new york steak (alright), and the peanut souffle (damn good).  

If you dine here, do NOT risk your dinner experience with Michael as your server.  I still tipped him 20% because that's who I am but it'll be a toss up if you get shitty service or the stand in the middle of the restaurant where they place their order type of service.  Even the two managers on at the time weren't going around asking people how their meals or dining experience was going.  They seemed like an inseparable pair, always going off together and coming back to the podium together.

My husband & I had our wedding reception here and it was just PERFECT! Everyone & everything from the food, kitchen staff, front of the house, wait staff & manager Randy were all superb!! They were all professional and assured all of our guests were taken care of. I highly recommend this restaurant & the private rooms if you want an intimate party or wedding. I come to Vegas a few times a year and I can't wait to go back and just dine here!!!

Located conveniently (and beautifully) in the fabulous Venetian, where my two friends and I stayed, we decided to come here for my friend's birthday lunch. It was very typical food on the menu--salads, hamburgers, pasta, etc. I ordered a chinese chicken salad and ate about half of it. Maybe it was because I wasn't in the mood to eat, but it just didn't do it for me. Not sweet enough and just pretty mediocre. The atmosphere is gorgeous though, inside the Grand Canal Shoppes. I would likely not go back because of the food, but the location, speed of service and atmosphere makes up for it (almost).

I had the Roasted Mushroom Agnolotti with Black Truffle Butter and it was amazing, I wished I had saved some bread to soak up the last splashes of sauce.  My portion size was small to just enough, I left happy because it was rich and so delicious. Other members of my party got a pizza a largish portion for one person. They enjoyed the pizza but was not as wowed as myself. What my group got was that the sauces are the specialty so if you think the sauce sounds good than get the dish because it will be better than you imagined.

decent casino restaurant from the wolfgang puck family tree. service was ok as was the food but there wasn't anything that really stood out. the selection of wines seemed a bit limited and.. em.. top shelf supermarket-ish. not bad but there's certainly better, more challenging options out there.

I only ate TWICE in Vegas.

Not because I was on a mission to fit into my dresses. Not because I wasn't hungry. WHY THEN?

Because like always, we had NO time. haha. 

I was SO happy we got to roam around and tour at least one hotel. We picked the right spot. 

Margaritas were to DIE for. You could taste the fresh squeezed lime juice.

Bruschetta was perfection. $7 for about 2 small toasted crostini's and tomatoes is steep but HEY its Vegas!

Tomato soup was soooo good. I thought of Lily L b/c she always orders soup so I had to give this one a try. 

Soft Shell Crab sandwich has got to be the BEST thing ever!! So filling and delicious! Too bad I could only handle half of a half! 

Margherita pizza was the only thing that didn't blow me away. It was very oily. I was going to award 5 stars but it was very normal food that tasted very good in VEGAS. For the price, I could have gone to the best restaurant in SJ and had my world rocked.

*** Thx for an amazing lunch. ***

I was somewhat pressed for time.
All your tables were occupied but
I scooped an open stool at the bar.
The gracious hostess so obliged me.

My intention was to be quick in+out.
I had meatloaf since I skipped bfast.
The mushrooms and bacon were ;O!

Suddenly time became irrelevant so I
asked for the dessert menu.  Much to
my surprise, dessert was even better.

$19 Meatloaf
$10 Chocolate Beignets
$  4 Expresso

*** A serendipitous moment: priceless. ***

Great location and view within St. Mark's Square in the Shoppes at the Venetian, and I love that it has cozier, elegant "inside" dining as well as faux al fresco patio dining.  We were given an "outside" table, next to the bar.  

The menu looked good, and we had a large party so we ordered lots to sample.  I started with the Asparagus soup with Maine crab and black pepper creme fraiche.  It was excellent.   The chicken spring rolls were quite good - crispy, sweet and complex.  Unfortunately, it was all downhill from there.  I went pretty basic for my meal - spaghetti and meatballs.  I felt this dish was uninspired and pedestrian.  The meatballs were undersized and had a very soft texture which did not sit well with me.  The pizzas were better than average, but we more than once looked longingly across the square at Ottos which specializes in pizza.  The rigatoni with fennel sausage bolognese was a step above the other main dishes.  

One last note - the wine was decent.  The waiter recommended a bottle of syrah that was a fairly impressive syrah, and very modestly priced.  

Overall, I was expecting more from this restaurant.

I love the Venetian!  The painted walls and ceilings, the street performers...a little piece of Venice.  So naturally having lunch in this open space restaurant sounded like a terrific idea.  
The 20 minute wait was no problem, there are multiple restaurants around so we had a glass of wine at a neighboring bar.  Once seated we ordered our drinks, since I'm from Miami, whenever I order a caipirinha i take into consideration that not everybody understand what its suppose to taste like.  Unfortunately it was so awful that both me and my friend had to send our drinks back.  Then when our waiter kindly recommended the pomegranate mojitos, i nervously accepted.  Also terrible but I was not about to return two cocktails.  

So now for the food; boring.  Maybe I'm being bias because of my superb experience with the Wolfgang Puck Bar and Grill @ the MGM but the food was nothing special.  I was expecting a savory pasta dish and what i served was can only be described as ordinary.  

Very disappointing, you have all the right components, step up your game Postrio!!

Short ribs 80 percent fat. Salmon under cooked. Vegetables with the salmon were greasier then the fries. Caesar salad had too much dressing. A heavy hand in general. Drinks took too long to come. Not what I would have expected from a Wolfgang Puck. They did remove the salmon from the bill and give a free plate of cookies that tastes good.

After roaming thru the "Grand Canal Shoppes" at the Venetian, and visiting Davidoff's to pick up a few cigars, I arrived at postrio.

I initially walked away as the hostess was too engulfed in a conversation about herself with one of her colleagues. Taking a few steps towards my exit, I returned and interrupted the bloviation to be seated at the bar. Fortunately, the bartender/server (Erica) was spectacular - attentive, down-to-earth and very charming. Reviewing the lunch menu, I asked for her recommendation ... the Lobster Club. WOW! it was mouth watering to say the least. To end the meal, Erica suggested the Key Lime or the Chocolate beignets w/liquid center and macchiato ice cream; I had the latter and it was heavenly! Next time I'll have a glass of cab with the beignets instead of a double expresso.

Lunch was so good that I had to come back two days later for the lobster club before returning to SF.

One of the reasons I chose Postrio for our "fancy" dinner in Vegas was the lack of bench seating.  Seriously.  If I'm going to spend $30-40/plate I don't want to be seated with strangers ala McDonald's.  Postrio doesn't make you sit with strangers so they immediately got an extra star from me.

They offered us the option of sitting in St. Mark's Square or in the dining room.  My husband indicated that it was our anniversary and let the host make the choice for us.  He sat us in the dining room because it's a bit quieter in there and we could sit closer together in a booth.

I had a martini with hennessy in it (sorry, don't remember the name) and an elderflower martini.  The hennessy martini was delicious!  My husband had a beer - don't remember which one.

I ordered the pancetta wrapped meatloaf, and my husband ordered the Kobe beef.  After tasting both, we agreed that mine was better... although I really enjoyed the chimichurri sauce on his beef.  

For dessert we shared the souffle.  I like mine to have more chocolate/cream sauce than was provided, but it was definitely good.

The wait staff was attentive and accommodating.  They brought out a black napkin so that I wouldn't have to worry about white lint on my black skirt.  I would definitely eat here again.

I stopped in for a quick bite one afternoon and had the tuna tartar was excellent and the caprese salad was very flavorful. I sat at the bar and the bar tenders were friendly and the service was great. Next time I am in town and I am going to try this place for dinner.

I have gone hungry to this restaurant twice during happy hour! Both times had great service at the bar! The first time the happy hour small plates are deals but very small portions.  The second time my friend and I shared a burger and fires which was very filling and one of the most delicious ever.  They give you this tasty popcorn at the bar as well. I will treat at this restaurant again!

After much hype about the lobster club, we went for lunch last weekend.  I think it's overpriced and under delivered.  The lobster club and soft shell crab sandwich were $29 each.  Really?  A $29 sandwich?  I've never never heard of such a thing.  But my buddy had been raving about it and so I had to try it.  While it had a lot of lobster, it was completely bland.  The toasted bread was too hard for such delicate meat.  The crab po boy was also bland and forgettable.  I tried my friend's french onion soup and mushroom ravioli.  The soup was too sweet and the ravioli was under cooked. I love al dente but this was sticking to my teeth.  The best things we had were the lasagna, fries, and coffee.  The place has a nice set up but the food was amiss.

Friday night, got a table immediately at 7pm....
Imported beer (Belgian $14 )

opted for 2 apps and a pizza -
Short ribs were okay. Little on the fatty side.
Calamari - to die for. Lightly breaded with light colored flour and VERY tender. I live in FL and have had eaten many calamari dishes and these were far and away THE BEST we have ever eaten.

Pizza - okay, nothing special.

Service was superb....

Went to Postrio for dinner prior to a show.  Had reservations and sat on the patio.  High energy atmosphere in The Venetian's St. Marks Square, with Street Performer type shows going on in the surrounding square.  

Shared the Salmon and Seafood Risotto - Salmon was excellent but risotto was a little undercooked.  The server was attentive and professional.  Prices are moderate for Las Vegas.

Frankly, Postrio did not impress.  I expected a little more from a Wolfgang Puck restaurant simply from a food quality standpoint.  While I would suggest it as a viable option if staying at The Venetian. I would not return simply because of the vast number of options in Las Vegas, and would not recommend traveling from a different hotel to check it out.

One if the best meals of my life... And I've dined all over the world at Michelin star restaurants.. Perfect steak and appetizers, great wine list, and I would say one of the top wait staff service experiences I've had in my entire life. I had the steak sampler that included some wagyu, American wagyu and I think a New York steak... Includes a selection of sauces. This was the best steak I've ever had and came with really enthusiastic service. If you are in Vegas it's definitely a must eat if you like steak and have some money to spend.

Modern setting.  Nice classic rock soundtrack.  Professional staff.  Excellent steaks.  Try the Baked Alaska for dessert.  I like this place over other steakhouses on the Strip.  Would like to visit again.

I was pleasantly surprised at how much better the ribeye was as compared to CUT-Beverly Hills.  Service here was excellent and my steak was prepared perfectly and tasted way better than the one I had in BH.  The sides were also excellent.  Atmosphere is relaxed and enjoyable.   Would go back anytime though not to the one in BH.

By far the best Steak House experience I've ever had in my life! For starters I had the bone marrow, Flan which I thought I wouldn't like but it was quite remarkable and delicious. I would highly recommend you try it. For my entre I   Had the 14oz New York Sirloin and it was cooked to perfection and  the rub was delicious. Lastly for desert I had the baked Alaskan which is now my favorite dessert of all time!  I am not usually a big dessert fan but this blew my socks off.  I would even recommend stopping by just for this dessert if this Menu is out of your Price range. 

All of the staff was great,  even spoke to the GM and e was awesome. 

This place is obviously a high end,  expensive restaurant but man is it worth every penny.

Less than wowed by Cut at the Palazzo.

My experience was slightly better than the one in Beverly Hills, but overall this restaurant is lacking in quality of food and service.

Doesn't feel like a 5 star restaurant.

The steak is good...not great.

The chairs at the tables in the middle of the restaurant are literally like office swivel chairs which I found pretty tacky.

The hostesses were rude.

I'll probably just stick to SW at the Wynn next time...

CUT is in my Top 2 steakhouses of Las Vegas, along with SW Steakhouse.  In my opinion CUT and SW are nose to nose, with the next steakhouse a distant 3rd (I've been to several).

The only thing about CUT, is I only recommend you order the American Wagyu beef from Snake River Farms.  They have "lesser" USDA steaks that just don't stack up.  I must emphasize that my review is dependent upon ordering the American Wagyu.  They also offer True Japanese Wagyu that I'm sure is great, but I haven't had it.

There are 3 American Wagyu steaks to choose from, and I recommend either the 9oz Ribeye or the 6oz Filet.  I get them both medium rare, and they offer contrasting flavors that are excellent.   CUT does a char on the steaks.  At first I wasn't sure about their char, but I was hooked on it after one bite.  The filet is as tender as they come, while the ribeye explodes with flavor.  Some ribeyes at lower end restaurants are filled with fat, while the Snake River Farms ribeye has a perfect amount.  I eat every bite of the CUT ribeye, while I usually leave a large amount of fatty pieces at lesser restaurants.

Here is my recommended order:

Bread:  Pretzel (awesome!)

Salad/Appetizer:  None

Entree:  American Wagyu from Snake River Farms:  Filet OR Ribeye prepared medium rare.

Sides:  Yukon Gold Potato Puree.  They also have an amazing corn dish, but hasn't been available every time I've been there.

Dessert:  Chocolate Souffle.  Highly recommended if you have room for it!  It's big and should be split with someone.

Near perfect service and attention to detail. The best selection of quality steaks I have experienced anywhere so far. The drink menu is presented on an iPad and the sommelier was very knowledgeable and professional. I plan to return for my birthday dinner after watching Jersey Boys at the Palazzo.

Had dinner here w/ a few of my buddies.

Ordered the Wagyu Rib Eye.  I've been to a few high end steak houses(Maestro, Mortons, Flemings, Ruth Chris, Delmonico) and the cut I had is by far the most unique flavor I've ever tasted.  The outside had the perfect charred crisp, and the inside was perfection.  The texture was so different from other Rib Eye's I've tasted.  The inside had the consistency and texture of Sushi.  It was delicate and chewy, and would melt in your mouth.

This might be strange the way I'm reviewing the steak here, but its the only way I can describe it.  Its the best steak, in terms of texture, that I've ever had.  The sides were OK, but nothing to wow about.  I'd recommend saving $$$ by not ordering sides, and just order a larger sized cut.  Had a nice bold Cab to go along w/ the steak which only enhanced the experience even further.

The service was what you'd expect from a high end establishment.  Didn't have any problems, and the timing of the entree's were on the dot.  The decor is more contemporary and sleek, which isn't what you'd expect.  It was very nice inside, but didn't really match the food that they were serving.  Can't really explain it, just go and check it out yourself.

Overall, I'd come back again.  Well worth the $.

The hubby and I are thoroughly enjoying CUT in the Venetian/Palazzo hotel. The service is excellent. The house apple salad was superb. I had the 3 beef sampler with the Japanese Wagyu, American Wagyu, and the regular aged beef. I enjoyed all three. The Japanese wagyu was like butter, but the American Wagyu was my fav. Full of flavor and tenderness. A very nice blend of American beef with Japanese Wagyu.  I highly recommend you try this place.  Also the Mac And cheese was great (I'm not a Mac and cheese kind of girl)!!!



Very, very please
-Dr. A

Incredibly mediocre meal. In fact, probably one of the worst meals *for the money* I've had. I actually can't believe there are 5 star reviews of this place - it blows my mind. 

Decor: restaurant was active, well laid out, modern, and clean. 4 stars

Service: our table was not ready until almost an our after our reservation, which was already at 8pm. That said, we had a large party and required 2 tables side by side so this is understandable. Actual service at table was good, not great. 4 stars. 

Food: everyone got beef and everyone was VERY underwhelmed with the quality. The cheapest steak on the menu is ~$55 (a la carte) and they were fairly grisly, and honestly didn't taste all that good. For that amount of money, I should be able to cut my steak with a fork. The appetizers were good, not great.  Sides were also good. 2.5 stars

Overall: save yourself the time and money. I've been to many very, very good/nice restaurants on both coasts, and I am completely happy spending $230 on a meal, but this was absolutely not worth it. There have got to be better restaurants in Las Vegas. I will never be returning here and will be letting people who visit LV to avoid it as well.

Typical Vegas steakhouse. In every sense. 
I don't eat red meat, but I ordered this pork belly appetizer and soup salad an dessert. 
I was at a business dinner and our bill was about $900.00 I tasted stuff here and there 
Good service and atmosphere 
But not a place I'd recommend
Delicious food, great cocktails and amazing service! Locked and loaded is probably one of the best cocktails I've ever had! Everything we ordered was fantastic!

Over priced and under sized steaks. The atmosphere is wonderful and staff friendly and attentive. TBH, you shouldn't have to fill up on bread and sides to make up for the portion sizes of the steaks. I've eaten at many of the top restaurants in the US and just felt ripped off in the end. Better choices

Phenom service by Carlos, his assistant and the staff, fine dining... A to Z the dishes from tuna tartare, to cocktails, to apple & date salad, to waygu steak, to the banana dessert and freshly steeped organic mint tea was unbelievable... will never forget this experience and cant wait to go back!

Our table had the American wagyu, lobster, sea bass, and dry aged ribeye with some sides and appetizers. Ehh. It's alright. The only dishes that stood out were the wagyu and lobster (of course, the most expensive dishes). All the other dishes were unimpressive. We didn't even finish the sea bass or the ribeye. Service was attentive but rather indifferent. If you're looking to splurge and get blown away, try Delmonico's instead.

We went to Cut on Saturday night with a large group of people. The service was outstanding...waiters and other staff who truly want you to have a fantastic experience. Everyone is trained well and working hard.

The steaks were good, but not great. If you have ever tasted real Wagyu beef in Japan, you will see that Cut steaks are not remotely similar. However, they are good (just incredibly overpriced). That being the case, the other items on the menu were excellent. Great bread, especially the pretzel (house made) and the creamed spinach was the best ever. 

If I went again I would order a cheaper cut of beef or simply skip the beef and order a whole bunch of appetizers with wine.

To start, most the negative reviews I've read on here are written by people who don't know about high-quality steak. It's supposed to be marbled with fat -- that's where you get the flavor. And it's supposed to be charred dark on the outside -- it's not burnt but quickly charred to keep the flavor & juiciness in. 

That said, our meal at Cut was one of the best dining experiences we've had in a very long time, if not ever.

First, we got a great big booth, just the 2 of us, and the atmosphere is very nice -- modern, hip -- even the music is classic rock. I love the little pedestal sinks in the bathroom, and he loved the dining room chandeliers.

A breadstick basket with cheese sticks arrived -- delicious -- followed by the best gougeres (cheese puffs) I've ever had. They were made of/in puff pastry, which is unusual, & so good. Then, after we ordered, the bread tray with fantastic pretzel bread & focaccia, which we devoured, knowing damn well the meal would be filling. And, oh, it was.

He had the tuna tartare with avocado on top -- a healthy & delicious portion of both. I had thinly slices asparagus on brioche with a soft-boiled egg & bacon vinagrette on top -- oh my god, it was amazing. I absolutely devoured it. All the flavors came together and made for orgasmically explosive bites.

Then his dry-aged 16-oz bone-in rib eye & my pork chop. Both were thick, juicy, moist, cooked just right, and fantastic. Our onion rings on the side were a bit superfluous, but, dipped in panko, we had to eat them cautiously so as not to fill up on such deliciousness. 

Somehow, we made room for dessert, and good thing. Best chocolate souffle I've ever had -- served in its own little sauce pan. His apricot/blackberry crumble, with a shortbread crumble, wasn't so bad either. :)

As for service, it was perfect. It was timed just right so that we got our appetizers pretty quickly but had some time to digest before dinner. The servers were all attentive, and there were many of them, and the presentation was fantastic, very old-world steakhouse elegant with tableside presentation, dishes all served simultaneously, and everything presented just right. He also loved his martini with blue-cheese-stuffed olives. Both our wines were great. A little pricey by the glass, but that was no surprise.

We were a little hesitant to try Cut because a) it's not so cheap, and b) Wolfgang Puck has spread himself a bit thin over the last 10+ years, and some restaurants have suffered because of it.

Cut is not one of those restaurants.

One of the best steaks I've ever had. Got the 20oz Ribeye. Perfectly cooked and seasoned. Creamed spinach was the best I've ever had. Our server Carlos was fantastic. The bread they bring over (pumpernickel and pretzel roll) was phenomenal. Pork belly was also insanely good. 

My friend and I split one appetizer and one 20oz steak, three sides. We left extremely full. In retrospect maybe one less side was the way to go. We are both guys with big appetites so my advice would not be to over order as the portions can be aggressive.

Brilliant meal and service.  We sat at the bar to dine to save waiting for a table.  

You MUST order the mac and cheese, it's fantastic! I'd go back just for that...

I absolutely loved my experience at CUT during my last visit to Vegas. My friend had been several times before, and said it was a must for our last trip. I was not disappointed. We ate relatively early because we are on East Coast time and it was our first night, and the restaurant was quiet and relaxed.

Our waiter took his time explaining the menu to me, and offered helpful suggestions. I had the beet salad to start, and it was fantastic. Then, I tried the Tasting of New York Sirloin based on our waiter's recommendation. It included a sampling of American Wagyu from Snake River Farms in Idaho, USDA prime aged, and true Japanese Wagyu. Next time, I would just stick with my traditional filet and get the Snake River Farms filet. But for the experience, I'm glad I branched out a tried the sampler, even though I prefer filet.

For a side, I tried the field mushrooms with shishito peppers, and thye were phenomenal. Anytime I see shishito peppers on a menu, I order them. They are my favorite, and CUT didn't let me down.

Of course I was too stuffed for dessert, but I look forward to sampling some of them next time around!

Two of us came here for New Year Eve dinner.  We were sat in the lounge area for dinner.  Granted we were walk-in and the main dining area was full.  The food was good, but nothing too special.  It was expensive for what it was.  Given so many options in Vegas, I probably will not go back.

Went for a going away/birthday dinner in a group of 5. This was hands down one of the best dining experiences any of us ever had. The steak cuts/drinks and side dishes are all fantastic. In addition our service was impeccable. I would recommend this place to any one wishing for a one of a kind experience. Please keep in mind you will pay for quality though this dinner won't come cheap, but is well worth it!

This is one of the best experience I ever had in a steakhouse.
Stellar staffs!!!!!!!! Absolutely amazing service.
Bone marrow was my favorite. Tasty, not greasy at all.
Love it.

After seeing every steakhouse repeated from NYC we wanted something new so we settled on Cut. What a great experience.  The server was more knowledgeable then most I encounter in NYC. We went to order a particular cut of meat and the waiter said we would enjoy something better because it was to mineraly. Fantastic sevice, fantastic meal. Highly recommended.

This is the Wolfgang Puck steakhouse, and supposedly impossible to get a reservation at in LA.  So on a weekend in Vegas, we all decided to try this place out. Sure, it was expensive, but how often do you get to dine out in such a nice atmosphere?

The rooms were dimly lit, and tastefully decorated. We were sat in the inside room, away from the main dining room. Not sure why, but after about 20 minutes I was glad, because our group of 9 quickly became very loud and disruptive (read: drunk).

We first got a choice of maybe 4 different kinds of breads - I tried the onion focaccia and the pretzel, both of which were soooo good. I am a bread fanatic myself, and I have to say, these were amazing! The pretzel was more like a roll with pretzel covering, and it tasted like there was about a stick of butter in the dough - it melted in my mouth. And the focaccia was very flavorful, in just the right way.

The group ordered a myriad of different dishes, which was great because I got to try a little bit of just about everything. I got the porterhouse to share, medium rare like I always get my meat, and it came seared on the outside with a peppery rub, and delicately tender on the inside. It was cooked very nicely. I ended up scraping the meat off the bone... haha.

The scallops, albeit only 4 came on the plate, were exquisite.  I don't know if I would have felt okay with paying about $10 a scallop, but they were definitely the best I've ever had.  I had a bite of the American Wagyu, which was very buttery and definitely tasty.  The japanese wagyu ribeye was even more buttery. They had very high quality beef overall, but some of them came with a little too much salt rubbed on the outside. I don't know if I'd pay $200 for a steak, but it was definitely tasty.

I do have to say, I think my favorite dish of the night was the kobe sashimi - you get 3 thin slices of kobe beef sashimi in a soy sauce vinegarette or something - and it was so delicious. The sides, on the other hand, were just okay. The garlic steam spinach wasn't anything special - I think we would have been better off getting creamed spinach. The mushrooms were good, but then again, I always like mushrooms. We also got some potato side, but I don't remember which it was, and it wasn't all that good.

Most of the food was prepared and presented very nicely. Which is something you would expect out of an establishment like Cut. But service was a little slow and they ran out of the wine that was ordered (I didn't drink it) and had to bring out a different but almost identical one (why couldn't they just notify us in the beginning if they only had one of that kind?). They ended up giving us free dessert at the end of the meal, these teeny bite-sized squares of fudge, cashew, and lemon. The lemon was very tart and was my favorite.

Definitely a great dining experience, but I wish we had gone with a more intimate group. I'd give it 5 stars, but I just don't think there should be any drawbacks in your night when you're paying this much for a meal.

Straight good!  Had the American Wagyu Filet, melts in your mouth.  Cooked perfect, incredible flavor and just the right amount.  I've eaten here a few times now, and every time, everything is pretty incredible.  The bread is good, the salads are good, the sides are awesome.  What more can I say?  Give this place a try, you won't be disappointed.

The service in this place was very professional. Our server knew her facts about meat. Friends had the wagyu American filet mignon cut cooked medium and they weren't able to keep their "mmmm" comments in after each bite. I tried it- really does melt in your mouth, and was very good. I had the 14 oz. New York Strip aged 35 days and it was great, but I regret ordering medium well instead of medium. I was very happy with my side of mushrooms and peppers (sautéed well). Banana cream dessert wasn't as good as I had hoped. Dim lighting and romantic atmosphere.

When I came to CUT, we were celebrating a birthday and I felt like splurging. I ordered the Japanese Wagyu rib-eye with two extra ounces, which was the most tender piece of steak I have ever eaten. It was cooked perfectly medium rare, and I savored every bite of it. 

The sides are decent, but not spectacular. I do, however, like the long stick-like crackers that they provide to you. They taste kind of like Cheez-Its. 

It was a great meal, but dented the wallet quite a bit. What else was I expecting ordering a $225 piece of steak? Ack.

Came here with the bf and a friend. This place is good, but I think falls a little short of the 4 stars. 

The pretzel bread they offer is awesome. I like dipping it in the mustard offerings. I also like the onion foccacia bread. I like that they come around with a bread plate to give you as much as you like of any of the breads. Most places give you a basket, and it's never enough of the one bread you like and too much of the breads you don't like. 

The friend and I got the American Wagyu center cut ribeye medium rare. The flavor is incomparable. My bf got the 12 oz Omaha ribeye, which was also very delicious. The Omaha was more butter, but the flavor of the Wagyu was bolder. We got the sides of the wild mushrooms and potato puree. The mushrooms had shishito peppers in them that we all felt didn't really complement the flavors of the mushrooms. The mushrooms on their own were good though. The potato puree was decent. 

Service is stellar here though. They don't miss a beat at all. 

Overall, I was happy we came, and I ate a lot of steak! :)

I've tried CUT in Palazzo three times and each time my experience was worse than the previous. The first time, I thought it was OK... maybe they were off their game so I said I would consider trying it again. The second time, my experience was the same as the first. Not worse or better. I definitely couldn't understand the hype over this place. The service was fine, but the food was not worth noting. I promised myself not to return because I couldn't imagine them proving me wrong. This third time, I went unwillingly and my instincts proved right. My steak was overcooked. I feel that the mark of a good steakhouse is the ability to cook a steak perfectly. I just cannot justify the price for their quality... maybe all my money was going into the decor/ambience.

So torn between 4 and 5 here so, give CUT a 4.5.  Went there with a group for my birthday dinner on an early November trip and was really looking forward to it.  Overall, was not disappointed at all.  I started with the tuna tartare appetizer and it was really delicious.  Ultra fresh chopped tuna, topped with some thinly sliced avocado and pressed into a circular mold.  Not sure what exactly the sauce drizzled about the plate was but, it matched the tuna perfectly.  As I sampled tastes from everyone else's plates, it was clear that all the dishes were very well conceived.

There are a number of aged cuts of prime beef from a variety of sources.  I chose a 28 day (I think!) dry aged NY Strip from Nebraska.  While it was very flavorful, this is where the .5 knockdown comes.  Just a wee bit past the medium rare I ordered.  At these prices and with Wolfgang Puck's name attached one certainly expects absolute perfection and this was a very slight misstep.  Normally, I would have sent it back but, we  were trying to make a 9:30 show so, that was not an option.

Overall, I would not hesitate to return although I think next trip, I'll keep trying some of the other pricey steak joints in Vegas.  What the hey.... I like variety!
Don't need to say much. The service is perfect.. u have like 3ppl serve ur table and the wayagu steak is melt in your mouth.. what else can you ask for with a glass a red wine.. uhmm..

I've been meaning to write this review for awhile but never got around to it. I came here awhile back with my boyfriend and was hesitant, I figured it was going to be another one of those overpriced overrated dinners, I'm pretty sure I was a total brat when we first arrived as I wasn't looking forward to having another disappointing dinner (especially on vacation), when they brought this ginormous plate of beef out to the table and explained in detail the variations between them I thought "ok this is kinda neat but I'm still sure the food will suck"...I don't think I even spoke to my boyfriend for the first 15 minutes as I was throwing one of my tantrums lol...and then our dinner arrives...one bite was all it took for me to change my whole tune! OMG I have never had food that has tasted so good! Well worth the price! Only down side is now ever since this experience I think all other meat tastes like cardboard, can't beat the texture and taste of CUT! Will definitely be back someday!

Everything was pretty awesome. I had a party of 8 for a bachelorette and they were very accommodating! Our servers (all male, btw) were super knowledgeable in their cuts. I like that they come out and explain with the actual cuts of wagyu. 

Ambiance was very nice, I liked the feel of it.. very open and spacious. You aren't going to be seated too close to anyone here, which is a good thing. Even though they had high ceilings, this place wasn't that loud at all and was easy to talk to people across my table without yelling.

BONE-IN RIB EYE (med-rare) - very tasty, cooked really well

RIB EYE (med-rare) - this was surprisingly better than the bone-in! I've always thought the bone-in would be better since people always say it's tastier, but this rib-eye was reallyyyy good, juicy, and flavor was on point

CREAMED SPINACH - this was ok.. I'm not sure if I was too fond of this. The texture of the egg and the spinach kind of threw me off.

MAC N CHEESE - so good! I'm not huge on mac n cheese but this was one was quite tasty!


All in all, a great dining experience for a very special occasion!
Clearly hands down best steak restaurant anywhere!!!  Great atmosphere...lounge but classy.  Great service.  Never disappoint.
